Mermaid is a JavaScript-based diagramming and charting tool designed to help documentation keep pace with development by generating complex diagrams from Markdown-inspired text definitions. It aims to eliminate the friction and high maintenance costs of traditional diagramming tools. 

Main capabilities include supporting over 20 diagram types—such as flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, Gantt charts, pie charts, Git graphs, user journey diagrams, and C4 diagrams—alongside a live editor, version-control-friendly syntax, native GitHub rendering, customizable themes, and built-in security features like input sanitization and sandboxed iframe rendering. 

The tool is intended for developers, technical writers, and non-programmers who need to create and maintain clear documentation without relying on heavy graphical design software. Notable technologies used in the project include JavaScript, D3, and dagre-d3.

name: uv
description: An extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.
summary:
uv is an extremely fast Python package and project manager written in Rust, designed to replace tools like `pip`, `pip-tools`, `pipx`, `poetry`, `pyenv`, `twine`, and `virtualenv`. Developed by Astral, it delivers a 10-100x performance increase over traditional `pip` workflows.

Main capabilities include:
- Comprehensive project and dependency management featuring a universal lockfile and Cargo-style workspaces.
- Single-file script execution with support for inline dependency metadata.
- Python version installation and seamless version switching.
- Execution and installation of Python command-line tools in isolated or ephemeral environments.
- A drop-in, pip-compatible CLI interface supporting advanced dependency resolution strategies, version overrides, and reproducible builds.
- A disk-space-efficient global cache for dependency deduplication.

Intended for Python developers, data scientists, and engineers on macOS, Linux, and Windows seeking fast, reliable, and unified environment and package management. Notable underlying technologies include Rust, PubGrub for dependency resolution, and cargo-inspired Git implementations.

name: bitcoin
description: Bitcoin Core integration/staging tree
summary:
Bitcoin Core is an integration and staging tree for the official Bitcoin client software. Its primary purpose is to connect to the Bitcoin peer-to-peer network to download and fully validate blocks and transactions. The project includes an optional wallet and graphical user interface. 

Intended users include developers, node operators, and end users seeking a secure implementation of the Bitcoin protocol. Notable technologies and tools associated with the project include C++, Python (used for regression and integration tests), Transifex (for managing translations), and CMake or related build systems supporting Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. 

The software is released under the MIT license and relies on extensive automated unit testing via `ctest`, functional testing, and continuous integration pipelines to maintain security and stability.

name: system-design-101
description: Explain complex systems using visuals and simple terms. Help you prepare for system design interviews.
summary:
System Design 101 is an educational resource designed to explain complex computer systems, software architecture, and networking concepts using visual diagrams and simple terms. It aims to help software developers prepare for technical interviews and understand how large-scale production systems work beneath the surface. 

The repository covers a wide range of topics organized into categories including API and Web Development, Real World Case Studies, AI and Machine Learning, Database and Storage, Caching and Performance, Payment and Fintech, Software Architecture, DevOps and CI/CD, Security, and Computer Fundamentals. Notable concepts and technologies explored across the guides include REST APIs, GraphQL, gRPC, Kafka, Redis, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, Docker, AWS, OAuth, and various architectural patterns like microservices, event-driven design, and database sharding.

name: vue-element-admin
description: :tada: A magical vue admin                                                                https://panjiachen.github.io/vue-element-admin
summary:
vue-element-admin is a production-ready front-end solution designed for building admin interfaces and large, complex Single-Page Applications. It provides enterprise-focused application templates, permission authentication (page and directive-level), multi-environment builds, internationalization (i18n), dynamic themes and routing, multi-level tabs (tags-view), error logging, dashboards, and various built-in editors, tables, charts (ECharts), and UI components. 

Intended for front-end developers building enterprise admin dashboards and management systems, the project is built on Vue.js and leverages Element UI as its component library. Core technologies and dependencies include ES2015+, Vuex, Vue Router, Vue CLI, Axios, and Mock.js for simulated data requests.

name: hugo
description: The world’s fastest framework for building websites.
summary:
Hugo is a fast and flexible static site generator written in Go, optimized for speed and designed to render complete sites in seconds. It provides an advanced templating system, a powerful taxonomy system, multilingual support, and an embedded web server for real-time development. 

Main capabilities include asset pipelines for CSS processing, image processing, JavaScript bundling, Sass processing, and Tailwind CSS processing, along with Hugo Modules for sharing content, themes, and configuration via Git repositories. Hugo is intended for developers, content creators, and organizations building corporate sites, documentation, portfolios, landing pages, blogs, and resumes. 

Notable technologies used include Go, TypeScript, JSX, Sass, PostCSS, Tailwind CSS, and Git.

name: OpenHands
description: 🙌 OpenHands: AI-Driven Development
summary:
OpenHands Agent Canvas is a self-hosted developer control center and engineering team interface for managing coding agents and automations. It allows users to start conversations, generate reports, and automate everyday tasks like decomposing GitHub issues. 

The project supports running OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or any Agent-Client Protocol (ACP)-compatible agent across local, remote, and cloud backends. Users can execute agents directly on local machines, via Docker containers, across virtual machines, or through OpenHands Cloud and Enterprise infrastructure. It integrates with tools such as Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Datadog to run workflows on a schedule or via webhook events, and is compatible with any Large Language Model.

Agent Canvas is designed for software developers and engineering teams seeking an extensible, multi-backend control center for AI-driven software development and automated operations. Notable technologies used include Node.js, `uv`, Docker, REST APIs, and TypeScript.

name: awesome-for-beginners
description: A list of awesome beginners-friendly projects.
summary:
Awesome First Pull Request Opportunities is an open-source curated directory designed to help open-source contributors, particularly beginners and first-time participants, discover software projects that welcome new contributors through beginner-friendly issue labels like `first-timers-only` or `good first issue`. 

The repository indexes a wide array of prominent open-source software spanning multiple programming languages and ecosystems—including JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C++, C#, Java, PHP, Ruby, and Dart. It encompasses diverse project categories such as web frameworks, databases, game engines, development tools, mobile applications, cloud infrastructure systems, machine learning libraries, and documentation platforms. Intended users include open-source maintainers looking to attract new community members and developers or non-programmers seeking entry-level contribution opportunities.

name: Agent-Reach
description: Give your AI agent eyes to see the entire internet. Read & search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu — one CLI, zero API fees.
summary:
Agent Reach is a Python (3.10+) capability layer designed to equip AI agents with internet access across multiple platforms. It provides automated selection, installation, health diagnostics, and multi-backend routing for web reading, video downloading, semantic search, and social media integration without hardcoding single-platform integrations. 

Intended users include developers and AI agent operators looking to connect command-line compatible agents (such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, Cursor, and Windsurf) to external web sources seamlessly.

Main capabilities include:
- **Zero-config channels:** Instant reading and searching for standard web pages, YouTube transcripts, RSS/Atom feeds, GitHub repositories, V2EX posts, and Snowball financial data using tools like Jina Reader, yt-dlp, feedparser, and GitHub CLI (`gh`).
- **Configurable authenticated channels:** Multi-backend routing supporting platforms like Twitter/X, Bilibili, Reddit, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Boss Zhipin, Xiaohongshu (RED), and Xiaoyuzhou podcasts via tools such as OpenCLI, bili-cli, and MCP servers.
- **Semantic search:** Web-wide semantic search via Exa integrated through `mcporter`.
- **Diagnostics:** Built-in `agent-reach doctor` command to diagnose backend statuses and repair connection pathways automatically.
- **Security:** Local storage of credentials in `~/.agent-reach/config.yaml` with restricted permissions (mode 600), explicit permission flags (`--system`) for system modifications, and dry-run options.

name: gin
description: Gin is a high-performance HTTP web framework written in Go. It provides a Martini-like API but with significantly better performance—up to 40 times faster—thanks to httprouter. Gin is designed for building REST APIs, web applications, and microservices.
summary:
Gin is a high-performance HTTP web framework written in Go, designed for building REST APIs, microservices, and web applications. It features a Martini-like API powered by a custom version of `httprouter`, delivering high performance and memory efficiency with a zero-allocation router. 

Intended for developers building high-throughput services and concurrent web applications, Gin provides built-in capabilities such as extensible middleware support, panic recovery, automatic JSON request/response validation, route grouping, centralized error management, and multi-format rendering (including JSON, XML, and HTML templates). It also features a rich middleware ecosystem through `gin-contrib` and `gin-gonic/contrib`.

name: syncthing
description: Open Source Continuous File Synchronization
summary:
Syncthing is a continuous file synchronization program designed to synchronize files between two or more computers. Its primary goals are to be safe from data loss, secure against attackers, easy to use, automatic, universally available, and tailored primarily for individual users. 

The software is intended for individual users seeking safe, secure, and automatic file synchronization across common operating systems. It offers GUI implementations and background execution examples for Windows, Mac, and Linux, as well as support for running via Docker. 

Built using Go, the project features an easy source-building process via `go run build.go`, an automatic upgrade mechanism utilizing compiled-in ECDSA signatures, and GPG-signed release binaries. Code-signing is provided for macOS and Windows binaries. All code is distributed under the MPLv2 License.

name: odysseus
description: Self-hosted AI workspace.
summary: Odysseus is a self-hosted AI workspace designed for chat, agents, deep research, document editing, email management, notes, tasks, calendars, and local model workflows. Its main capabilities include local and API model support, MCP tools, shell integration, memory, a hardware-aware model cookbook, multi-step web research with report generation, blind side-by-side model comparison, a writing-first document editor with Markdown, HTML, and CSV support, an IMAP/SMTP email client with triage and reply drafts, CalDAV sync, image editing, web search, sessions, and 2FA authentication. The project is intended for users seeking a comprehensive, self-hosted productivity and AI orchestration platform. Notable technologies and protocols utilized include Docker, IMAP, SMTP, and CalDAV.

name: NextChat
description: ✨ Zero-config AI chat assistant. No API key needed — sign up and instantly chat with GPT-5, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, DeepSeek & 100+ top models. Pay-as-you-go saves you more. Available on Web, iOS, macOS, Android, Linux, Windows.
summary:
NextChat is a light and fast cross-platform AI assistant designed to support multiple language models including Claude, DeepSeek, GPT-4, and Gemini Pro. It functions as a web application, PWA, and native desktop/mobile client for Linux, Windows, macOS, and iOS, allowing users to interact with self-hosted or cloud-based large language models. 

Main capabilities include streaming responses, Markdown rendering with LaTeX and Mermaid support, prompt template management, chat history compression for long conversations, plugin support, real-time chat, artifacts, and local data privacy storage. It also offers an Enterprise Edition featuring brand customization, resource integration, admin-controlled permission management, internal knowledge base integration, security auditing, and private cloud deployment.

The project is built using modern web and desktop technologies, supporting deployment on platforms like Vercel, Docker, and Zeabur, with integrations for various provider APIs including OpenAI, Azure, Google, Anthropic, Baidu, ByteDance, Alibaba, iFlytek, ChatGLM, DeepSeek, Stability, SiliconFlow, and 302.AI.

name: svelte
description: web development for the rest of us
summary: Svelte is a web development framework and compiler designed to build web applications. Its core capability is taking declarative components and converting them into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM. It targets web developers seeking a new approach to application building. The project is open-source under the MIT license.

name: worldmonitor
description: Real-time global intelligence dashboard. AI-powered news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking in a unified situational awareness interface
summary:
World Monitor is a real-time global intelligence dashboard that provides AI-powered news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking within a unified situational awareness interface. Key capabilities include curated news feeds, a dual map engine supporting a 3D globe and WebGL flat map, cross-stream correlation, live Country Instability Index (CII) scores, a finance radar, and support for local AI via Ollama. It features specialized site variants (world, tech, finance, commodity, happy, and energy) built from a single codebase, a native desktop application built with Tauri 2, and multilingual UI support.

Designed for general users, researchers, agents, and developers, the project offers programmatic access via an MCP server, a REST API, a CLI tool (`worldmonitor`), and official SDKs for Python, Ruby, and Go. The notable technologies used include TypeScript, Vite, globe.gl, Three.js, deck.gl, MapLibre GL, Tauri, Rust, Node.js, Ollama, Groq, OpenRouter, Transformers.js, Protocol Buffers, Redis, and Vercel Edge Functions.

name: Scrapling
description: 🕷️ An adaptive Web Scraping framework that handles everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl! Don't be shy, join here: https://discord.gg/EMgGbDceNQ and follow here for daily tips and tricks: https://x.com/Scrapling_dev
summary:
Scrapling is an adaptive Python web scraping framework designed to handle single requests as well as full-scale concurrent crawls. It features a self-healing parser that automatically relocates elements when a website's structure changes, alongside fetchers capable of bypassing anti-bot systems like Cloudflare Turnstile out of the box. 

Main capabilities include:
- **Spiders & Crawling:** Scrapy-like spider architecture supporting concurrent requests, pause-and-resume checkpointing, streaming items, auto-throttling, robots.txt compliance, development caching, and built-in templates (`CrawlSpider`, `SitemapSpider`, `ShopifySpider`, etc.).
- **Advanced Fetchers:** Standard HTTP requests with TLS impersonation via `Fetcher`, dynamic browser automation via `DynamicFetcher` (Playwright/Chrome), and stealth browser modes via `StealthyFetcher`. It supports session management, proxy rotation, ad/domain blocking, DNS leak prevention, and background XHR capture.
- **Flexible Parsing:** CSS selectors, XPath, BeautifulSoup-style find methods, text-based searches, element relationship traversal, and similar-element matching.
- **AI Integration:** Includes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents, an Agent Skill for coding assistants, and one-line conversion of web pages into RAG-ready Markdown.
- **CLI & Interactive Shell:** Command-line utilities for extraction and an interactive IPython shell.

Intended for developers, web scrapers, and data engineers seeking a robust, high-performance scraping library. Built with Python 3.10+ using technologies like Playwright, Lxml, and asyncio.

name: Understand-Anything
description: Graphs that teach > graphs that impress. Turn any code into an interactive knowledge graph you can explore, search, and ask questions about. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and more.
summary:
Understand Anything is an interactive developer tool and AI plugin designed to convert codebases, knowledge bases, and documentation into navigable knowledge graphs. It targets developers, project managers, and power users seeking to comprehend large or unfamiliar projects through structural visualization, business logic mapping, and AI-assisted exploration.

The project uses a hybrid architecture combining Tree-sitter for deterministic static analysis with a multi-agent LLM pipeline to generate plain-English summaries, architectural layers, business domains, and guided learning tours. Key capabilities include interactive graph exploration, fuzzy and semantic search, diff impact analysis, incremental updates, and multi-language support. 

Understand Anything integrates natively with Claude Code and supports numerous other coding assistants and platforms via an installation script, including Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Vibe CLI, Trae, and Kiro.

name: laravel
description: Laravel is a web application framework with expressive, elegant syntax. We’ve already laid the foundation for your next big idea — freeing you to create without sweating the small things.
summary: Laravel is a web application framework with expressive, elegant syntax designed to ease common development tasks for large, robust applications. Its main capabilities include a simple and fast routing engine, a powerful dependency injection container, multiple back-ends for session and cache storage, an expressive database ORM (Eloquent), database agnostic schema migrations, robust background job processing, and real-time event broadcasting. It is intended for web developers and supports AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot through tools like Laravel Boost. The framework utilizes modern PHP, JavaScript, and unit testing, and is licensed under the MIT license.

name: mall
description: mall项目是一套电商系统，包括前台商城系统及后台管理系统，基于Spring Boot+MyBatis实现，采用Docker容器化部署。 前台商城系统包含首页门户、商品推荐、商品搜索、商品展示、购物车、订单流程、会员中心、客户服务、帮助中心等模块。 后台管理系统包含商品管理、订单管理、会员管理、促销管理、运营管理、内容管理、统计报表、财务管理、权限管理、设置等模块。
summary:
The `mall` project is a comprehensive e-commerce system that includes a frontend shopping mall and a backend management system. It aims to provide a complete e-commerce solution with features covering home page portals, product recommendations, search, displays, shopping carts, order workflows, member centers, customer service, product management, orders, promotions, operations, content, statistics, finance, and permissions. 

The backend is built using Spring Boot, Spring Security, MyBatis, and MyBatis Generator. It integrates Elasticsearch for product searching, RabbitMQ for messaging, Redis for caching, MongoDB for NoSQL storage, Logstash and Kibana for logging, Nginx for static resources, Docker for containerization, Jenkins for CI/CD, and MinIO or Alibaba Cloud OSS for object storage. The web frontend utilizes Vue, Vue-router, Vuex, Element UI, Axios, and v-charts, while the mobile storefront is built with uni-app and mix-mall.

name: awesome-interview-questions
description: :octocat: A curated awesome list of lists of interview questions. Feel free to contribute! :mortar_board:
summary: This repository hosts a curated list of technical interview questions and resources categorized by programming languages, frameworks, databases, caching technologies, operating systems, algorithms, design patterns, data structures, networks, security, and data science. The project is designed to help job seekers prepare for technical interviews and assist hiring managers in evaluating candidates. Intended users include software engineers, developers, system administrators, and data professionals across various experience levels. The collection references multiple technologies and tools such as Java, JavaScript, Python, C++, Ruby, ReactJS, Angular, Docker, SQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Linux.

name: devops-exercises
description: Linux, Jenkins, AWS, SRE, Prometheus, Docker, Python, Ansible, Git, Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenStack, SQL, NoSQL, Azure, GCP, DNS, Elastic, Network, Virtualization. DevOps Interview Questions
summary:
This repository provides a comprehensive collection of questions, technical exercises, and self-assessments covering DevOps, SRE, and software engineering topics. It serves as a practical study guide for technical interviews and professional skill development across numerous domains, including networking, operating systems, virtualization, cloud computing, containers, databases, storage, security, system design, and testing. 

The project encompasses questions and exercises across multiple technology stacks and platforms, featuring extensive coverage of Linux, Kubernetes, OpenShift, OpenStack, Terraform, Ansible, Prometheus, Grafana, Kafka, Elastic Stack, Go, Python, SQL, and NoSQL databases like MongoDB. It also includes study materials and question sets for professional certifications from AWS, Azure, and the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CKA). 

Intended for software engineers, systems administrators, cloud architects, and aspiring DevOps or SRE professionals, the repository emphasizes conceptual understanding and practical problem-solving. Content is structured into modular topics with community-driven contributions accepted via pull requests.

name: crawl4ai
description: Open-source web crawler and scraper for LLMs and AI agents: any website into clean, LLM-ready Markdown. Run it yourself, or use Crawl4AI Cloud with one key.
summary:
Crawl4AI is an open-source web crawler and scraper designed for Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI agents. It transforms websites into clean, LLM-ready Markdown for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and data pipelines. 

Main capabilities include generating clean and fit Markdown, extracting structured data using CSS, XPath, regex schemas, or LLMs (via integration with providers like OpenAI and LiteLLM), and controlling browsers with support for persistent profiles, sessions, proxies, and stealth mode. It also supports deep crawling (BFS/DFS), dynamic JavaScript rendering, and self-hosting via Docker with a REST API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support. 

Intended users are developers, data engineers, and AI agent builders needing programmatic website extraction and scraping. Notable technologies used include Python, Playwright, Docker, and Pydantic.

name: orca
description: Orca is the ADE for working with a fleet of parallel agents. Run any coding agent with your own subscription. Available on desktop, mobile and remote runtime.
summary:
Orca is an AI orchestrator designed for developers to run and manage CLI-based coding agents side-by-side. 

**Project Purpose:**
Orca serves as a desktop and mobile orchestration hub that allows developers to run multiple AI agents in parallel, track their progress, and review generated changes within a single interface.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Parallel Worktrees:** Run multiple agents concurrently, each in its own isolated git worktree, to compare results and merge the best output.
- **Mobile Companion:** Monitor agent progress, receive notifications, and send follow-up instructions remotely via iOS and Android apps.
- **Terminal & Editor Features:** Includes WebGL-rendered terminal splits, VS Code-based file editing with autosave, and direct file-dragging into prompts.
- **Design Mode & Computer Use:** Interact with a real Chromium window to capture HTML, CSS, and screenshots into prompts, or allow agents to operate desktop UI elements.
- **Native Task Integration:** Browse and open worktrees directly from GitHub pull requests and issues, or Linear project boards.
- **Remote & CLI Support:** Execute remote agents over SSH with port forwarding, and script workflows using the Orca CLI (`orca`).

**Intended Users:**
Developers and builders utilizing AI coding tools who need to manage, monitor, and coordinate multiple agents simultaneously across macOS, Windows, Linux, and mobile platforms.

**Notable Technologies:**
Supports any terminal-based CLI agent, including Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, Devin, and many others.

name: realworld
description: "The mother of all demo apps" — Exemplary fullstack Medium.com clone powered by React, Angular, Node, Django, and many more
summary:
RealWorld is a project purpose-built to provide a standard, functional clone of Medium.com across numerous frontend and backend frameworks. It aims to bridge the gap between simple "todo" tutorials and real-world application development challenges. 

The project's main capabilities include a standardized API specification, a shared CSS theme for identical UI/UX, an end-to-end (E2E) test suite for frontend validation, and over 100 interoperable implementations spanning various programming languages and technologies. Because all implementations adhere to the same API spec, any frontend can be combined with any backend. Notable technologies mentioned include TypeScript, Python, Nitro, Prisma, Zod, and Django Ninja. 

Intended users include developers, architects, and learners looking to compare how different technology stacks build real-world applications.

、attnvis：GPT2、BERT等transformer语言模型注意力交互可视化、CoVoST：Facebook发布的多语种语音-文本翻译语料库，包括11种语言(法语、德语、荷兰语、俄语、西班牙语、意大利语、土耳其语、波斯语、瑞典语、蒙古语和中文)的语音、文字转录及英文译文、Jiagu自然语言处理工具 - 以BiLSTM等模型为基础，提供知识图谱关系抽取 中文分词 词性标注 命名实体识别 情感分析 新词发现 关键词 文本摘要 文本聚类等功能、用unet实现对文档表格的自动检测，表格重建、NLP事件提取文献资源列表 、 金融领域自然语言处理研究资源大列表、CLUEDatasetSearch - 中英文NLP数据集：搜索所有中文NLP数据集，附常用英文NLP数据集 、medical_NER - 中文医学知识图谱命名实体识别 、(哈佛)讲因果推理的免费书、知识图谱相关学习资料/数据集/工具资源大列表、Forte：灵活强大的自然语言处理pipeline工具集 、Python字符串相似性算法库、PyLaia：面向手写文档分析的深度学习工具包、TextFooler：针对文本分类/推理的对抗文本生成模块、Haystack：灵活、强大的可扩展问答(QA)框架、中文关键短语抽取工具
summary: funNLP is a comprehensive and structured resource repository for Chinese natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs). It aggregates a vast collection of datasets, corpora, pre-trained language models, and specialized tools covering domains such as ChatGPT models, knowledge graphs, information extraction, text generation, machine translation, sentiment analysis, speech processing, and document parsing. The project serves as an extensive toolkit and reference library designed for NLP practitioners, researchers, and developers working on text processing, conversational AI, and machine learning applications.

name: cs-video-courses
description: List of Computer Science courses with video lectures.
summary:
This repository is a curated, comprehensive directory of university-level computer science and technical courses featuring video lectures, complete lecture notes, and assignments. Designed for students, self-learners, and professionals, the collection aggregates actual college and university courses from institutions such as MIT, Stanford, UC Berkeley, CMU, Princeton, and various IITs, while excluding basic tutorials and small MOOCs. 

The catalog spans a wide array of core and advanced computer science domains, including Introduction to Computer Science, Data Structures and Algorithms, Systems Programming (Operating Systems, Distributed Systems, Real-Time Systems), Database Systems, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning (Deep Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Natural Language Processing, Generative AI and LLMs, Computer Vision), Computer Networks, Mathematics for Computer Scientists, Web Programming, Theoretical Computer Science and Programming Languages, Embedded Systems, Computer Organization and Architecture, Security, Computer Graphics, Computational Physics, Computational Biology, Quantum Computing, Robotics and Control, Computational Finance, Network Science, and Blockchain Development. Notable technologies and specialized frameworks referenced across the listings include Rust, Python, C++, Java, R, Racket, and specialized libraries and tools utilized in modern academic curricula.

name: fzf
description: :cherry_blossom: A command-line fuzzy finder
summary:
fzf is a general-purpose command-line fuzzy finder and interactive terminal toolkit designed to help users select files, browse command history, preview data, navigate complex datasets, and build custom terminal interfaces and workflows. Distributed as a portable single binary, it provides high-performance search capabilities over millions of items with an event-driven architecture. 

The tool includes batteries-included shell integrations for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and Nushell, as well as plugins for Vim and Neovim. Notable features include flexible display modes (fullscreen, height, and popup windows), advanced search syntax with exact, prefix, suffix, and inverse matching, dynamic candidate reloading, external command execution, and built-in file previews supporting terminal image protocols such as Kitty, iTerm2, and Sixel.

name: deer-flow
description: An open-source long-horizon SuperAgent harness that researches, codes, and creates. With the help of sandboxes, memories, tools, skill, subagents and message gateway, it handles different levels of tasks that could take minutes to hours.
summary:
DeerFlow is an open-source super agent harness designed to orchestrate sub-agents, memory, and sandboxes via extensible skills. Built on LangGraph and LangChain, it provides complete execution infrastructure for AI agents to plan, execute multi-step tasks, manage files, interact with browsers, and retrieve knowledge.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Extensible Skills & Tools:** Progressive skill loading from Markdown files (`SKILL.md`), custom tool creation, MCP server integration (HTTP/SSE and stdio), and agentic browser control via Playwright.
- **Agent Orchestration & Sub-Agents:** Dynamic spawning of sub-agents with scoped context, support for batch tasks, session goals, and manual context compaction.
- **Execution Environments & Sandboxes:** Secure sandbox execution modes (Local, Docker, Kubernetes/Provisioner, and E2B) with workspace file management, artifact generation, and data retention.
- **Memory & Retrieval:** Long-term memory extraction via DeerMem, mem0, Honcho, or OpenViking, alongside private knowledge retrieval through RAGFlow.
- **Communication Channels:** Inbound task handling and proactive notifications across multiple messaging apps (Telegram, Slack, Feishu/Lark, WeChat, WeCom, QQ, DingTalk, and Buzz).
- **Client & Interface Options:** A full-stack web UI, a terminal workbench (TUI), an embedded Python client (`DeerFlowClient`), and a LangGraph-compatible REST API with support for Personal Access Tokens (PATs).

**Intended Users:**
Developers, researchers, and engineers building, testing, and deploying advanced multi-agent workflows, autonomous data pipelines, and research frameworks.

**Notable Technologies:**
Python 3.12+, Node.js 22+, Docker, LangChain, LangGraph, Playwright, and RAGFlow.

name: llm-course
description: Course to get into Large Language Models (LLMs) with roadmaps and Colab notebooks.
summary:
The LLM course repository is a comprehensive educational resource divided into three main sections: LLM Fundamentals, The LLM Scientist, and The LLM Engineer. It covers fundamental mathematics, Python, and neural networks; advanced techniques for building, fine-tuning, aligning, evaluating, and quantizing large language models; and production practices for creating LLM-based applications, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), agents, inference optimization, deployment, and security.

Designed for learners, practitioners, and developers seeking to build open-source models and applications, the repository features structured notebooks, articles, and community resources. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced throughout the course include PyTorch, Hugging Face (TRL, transformers, datasets, Hub), Axolotl, Unsloth, llama.cpp, GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ, EXL2, MergeKit, LangChain, LlamaIndex, vLLM, DSPy, Streamlit, and Gradio.

name: vite
description: Next generation frontend tooling. It's fast!
summary:
Vite is next-generation frontend tooling designed to provide a faster and leaner development experience for modern web projects. It features instant server start, lightning-fast Hot Module Replacement (HMR) built on native ES modules, rich feature enhancements, optimized production builds, a universal plugin interface, and fully typed APIs. 

The project consists of two major parts: a development server providing rapid HMR over native ES modules, and a build command that bundles code using Rolldown to output highly optimized static assets for production. Vite is highly extensible through its Plugin API and JavaScript API, and includes packages such as `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-legacy`, and `create-vite`. It targets web developers seeking high-performance frontend build and development capabilities.

name: lobehub
description: 🤯 LobeHub is your Chief Agent Operator, organizing your agents into 7×24 operations by hiring, scheduling, and reporting on your entire AI team.
summary:
LobeHub is a work-and-lifestyle space and AI agent platform designed to help users organize, hire, schedule, and collaborate with teams of AI agents operating 24/7. It serves as an AI agent playground and operational infrastructure for developers and general users alike. 

Main capabilities include an Agent Builder for setting up personalized AI teammates, Agent Groups for parallel collaboration via Pages, Schedules, and Projects, and Personal Memory features that provide continual learning and white-box editable memory. The platform supports MCP-compatible plugins, Function Calling, and an IM Gateway. 

Intended users include developers, design-engineers, and professionals looking to build, manage, and scale productivity workflows with autonomous AI teams. Notable technologies utilized include Next.js, Vite SPA, Docker, Vercel, and OpenAI LLMs, alongside companion packages such as `@lobehub/ui`, `@lobehub/icons`, `@lobehub/tts`, and `@lobehub/lint`.

name: lazygit
description: simple terminal UI for git commands
summary:
Lazygit is a simple terminal user interface for git commands designed to make version control more accessible and efficient for developers. Its main capabilities include staging individual lines and hunks, performing interactive rebasing, cherry-picking, bisecting, nuking the working tree, amending old commits, filtering views, using worktrees, creating custom patches, and undoing actions via reflog. It also features a commit graph, commit comparison, custom command support, git-flow integration, and GitHub pull request viewing through the `gh` tool. 

Intended for developers looking for an intuitive alternative to complex command-line git workflows, the project is built in Go and uses libraries like `golangci-lint`.

name: animate.css
description: 🍿 A cross-browser library of CSS animations. As easy to use as an easy thing.
summary: Animate.css is a cross-browser library of ready-to-use, "just-add-water" CSS animations designed for web projects. It provides a collection of categorized animations—such as fades and bounces—that can be easily integrated using npm or yarn. The project is intended for web developers looking to incorporate lightweight animations while maintaining accessibility standards, featuring built-in support for the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query to accommodate users with motion sensitivity.

name: ChinaTextbook
description: 所有小初高、大学PDF教材。
summary:
ChinaTextbook 是一个旨在促进义务教育普及、消除地区间教育贫困并帮助海外华人了解国内教育的开源项目。该项目集中并开源了中国各阶段的教育资源，重点提供涵盖小学、初中、高中、大学各年级的数学教材（如人教版数学教材、同济大学高等数学、线性代数、离散数学和概率论等）。

为了应对 GitHub 对单文件上传大小的限制，项目中超过 50MB 的大文件会被拆分，并配套提供名为 `mergePDFs-windows-amd64.exe` 的专用文件合并程序（位于 ChinaTextbook-tools 仓库）供用户合并下载的 PDF 文件段。此外，项目提及了 `tchMaterial-parser` 工具用于重新下载教材，并设有 Telegram 社区以便用户获取动态与交流。

name: rtk
description: CLI proxy that reduces LLM token consumption by 60-90% on common dev commands. Single Rust binary, zero dependencies
summary:
RTK (Rust Token Killer) is a high-performance command-line interface proxy designed to cut up to 90% of bash and command output before it reaches AI coding agents and LLM contexts. Implemented as a single Rust binary with minimal overhead (<10ms), RTK supports over 100 commands across file operations, version control, build systems, test runners, linters, package managers, and container tools. 

Main capabilities include smart command output filtering, grouping, truncation, deduplication, and failure-driven data storage for efficient LLM token usage. It integrates transparently with numerous AI tools and coding environments, including Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, and others, via automatic hook rewrites or plugin APIs. 

Intended users are developers and AI agent operators looking to optimize token consumption, reduce context overhead, and lower API costs during AI-assisted development workflows. Notable technologies used include Rust and ripgrep (`rg`).

name: FiraCode
description: Free monospaced font with programming ligatures
summary:
Fira Code is a free monospaced font designed for programmers that incorporates ligatures for common multi-character symbol combinations like `->`, `<=`, and `:=`. While underlying code remains ASCII-compatible, the font visually combines these sequences into single logical tokens to help developers read and understand code faster. Beyond standard programming ligatures, Fira Code features adjustable arrows, customized punctuation and letter pairs, character variants, stylistic sets, ASCII and box-drawing support, powerline glyphs, and dedicated progress bar glyphs. 

The project is intended for software developers and technical users writing code or mathematical documents across numerous code editors, terminal emulators, and web browsers. Notable technologies associated with the project include OTF, TTF, WOFF, Docker, and specific CSS font-feature settings.

name: hello-agents
description: 📚 《从零开始构建智能体》——从零开始的智能体原理与实践教程
summary:
Hello-Agents is an open-source, theory-and-practice learning tutorial developed by the Datawhale community focused on building AI-native agent systems from scratch. The project aims to guide learners from basic language model fundamentals and classical agent paradigms (such as ReAct and Plan-and-Solve) to designing multi-agent applications, low-code platforms (like Coze and Dify), and mainstream frameworks (like AutoGen, AgentScope, and LangGraph). 

It features **HelloAgents**, a lightweight custom agent framework built natively using OpenAI APIs, and covers advanced concepts including memory and retrieval, context engineering, communication protocols (MCP, A2A, ANP), agentic reinforcement learning (from SFT to GRPO), and performance evaluation. Intended users include AI developers, software engineers, students, and self-taught enthusiasts with basic Python skills and foundational knowledge of LLM API usage. Practical real-world projects such as an intelligent travel assistant, a deep research agent, and a multi-agent cyber town are included to bridge theory with implementation.

name: spring-boot
description: Spring Boot helps you to create Spring-powered, production-grade applications and services with absolute minimum fuss.
summary:
Spring Boot helps developers create Spring-powered, production-grade applications and services with minimal effort. It provides an opinionated view of the Spring platform for building stand-alone Java applications runnable via `java -jar`, traditional WAR deployments, or a command-line tool for running Spring scripts. 

Primary capabilities include a fast getting-started experience, embedded servers, security, metrics, health checks, and externalized configuration, all without code generation or XML configuration requirements. The project targets Java developers and Spring users looking to build web services and applications rapidly. Notable technologies and tools associated with the repository include Java, Gradle, Maven, and the Spring platform.

name: PayloadsAllTheThings
description: A list of useful payloads and bypass for Web Application Security and Pentest/CTF
summary: PayloadsAllTheThings is a collection of useful payloads and bypasses designed for Web Application Security. It serves as a comprehensive resource for penetration testers and security professionals, providing vulnerability descriptions, exploitation methods, and sets of files tailored for Burp Intruder. The repository is intended for individuals performing web application assessments and security testing. Each section typically includes documentation detailing the vulnerability, exploitation guides, images, and referenced files, with alternative viewing available via PayloadsAllTheThingsWeb.

name: d2l-zh
description: 《动手学深度学习》：面向中文读者、能运行、可讨论。中英文版被70多个国家的500多所大学用于教学。
summary:
《动手学深度学习》（Dive into Deep Learning，D2L.ai）是一个开源项目，旨在提供一本免费的在线互动教材与统一资源，帮助读者掌握深度学习的概念、数学背景、批判性思维以及实际工程实现技能。

该项目的主要能力在于将数学原理直接对应至可运行的代码，使读者能够修改代码、观察结果并获取实践经验，同时依托配套论坛进行技术答疑。项目内容涵盖深度学习应用的各个方面，并由社区不断快速迭代以跟进技术发展。

其intended users（intended users）包括希望成为深度学习应用科学家的学生、研究人员以及工业界研发工程师。项目作者包括 Aston Zhang、Zachary C. Lipton、Mu Li 和 Alexander J. Li。

name: MinerU
description: Transforms complex documents like PDFs and Office docs into LLM-ready markdown/JSON for your Agentic workflows.
summary:
MinerU is an open-source data-centric document parsing tool and local document library designed for precise document content extraction, conversion, optical character recognition (OCR), and agent reading workflows. 

### Purpose and Capabilities
MinerU parses a wide variety of document formats—including PDF, scanned images, Word (`.doc`/`.docx`), PowerPoint (`.ppt`/`.pptx`), Excel (`.xls`/`.xlsx`), RTF, OpenDocument (`.odt`/`.ods`/`.odp`), EPUB, OFD, HTML/MHTML, and CSV/TSV files—into structured outputs such as Markdown, HTML, LaTeX, DOCX, EPUB, PDF, and structured content lists. It features four processing quality tiers (`flash`, `basic`, `standard`, and `advanced`) supporting progressive page or block continuation, stable citation locators, local caching, searching, and batch conversion.

### Intended Users
The project is intended for developers, researchers, and AI agents requiring high-precision document parsing, layout analysis, table and formula extraction, and local document workflow automation.

### Notable Technologies
MinerU incorporates independent model configurations using ONNX, PyTorch, llama.cpp, vLLM, LMDeploy, and MLX. It integrates underlying tools and libraries including DocVortex, PaddleOCR, pypdfium2, magika, and TableStructureRec.

name: netdata
description: The fastest path to AI-powered full stack observability, even for lean teams.
summary:
Netdata is an open-source, real-time infrastructure monitoring platform designed to provide instant, per-second insights, zero-configuration auto-discovery, and machine learning-powered anomaly detection for systems, containers, applications, and logs. It targets system administrators, DevOps professionals, and organizations requiring distributed observability. 

Main capabilities include high-resolution metrics collection across 800+ integrations, edge-based machine learning, tiered time-series storage, interactive dashboards, advanced log management, and smart alerting integrations (such as Slack, Discord, and PagerDuty). Its architecture consists of the Netdata Agent, Netdata Cloud for centralized collaboration and RBAC, and the Netdata UI. The platform supports Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and Windows, while integrating with notable technologies and tools like Docker, Kubernetes, systemd, OpenMetrics, StatsD, Prometheus, and InfluxDB.

name: hoppscotch
description: Open-Source API Development Ecosystem • https://hoppscotch.io • Offline, On-Prem & Cloud • Web, Desktop & CLI • Open-Source Alternative to Postman, Insomnia
summary:
Hoppscotch is an open-source API development ecosystem designed to help developers create requests faster and test APIs efficiently. It provides a lightweight, fast, and minimalistic web and desktop application for sending real-time HTTP requests, WebSockets, Server-Sent Events, Socket.IO, MQTT, and GraphQL queries. 

Key capabilities include comprehensive request configuration (parameters, headers, authorization methods including OAuth 2.0, pre-request scripts, and post-request tests), response inspection, environment variables, collections, workspaces, and team collaboration features with role-based access control. It also supports Progressive Web App (PWA) installation, a built-in proxy mode to handle CORS issues, request code generation for 10+ languages, and a command-line interface (CLI). Notable technologies and protocols utilized include HTTP, GraphQL, WebSockets, Socket.IO, MQTT, and JavaScript for scripting and testing.

name: ghidra
description: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework
summary:
Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the National Security Agency (NSA) Research Directorate. It provides a suite of high-end software analysis tools enabling users to analyze compiled code across Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms. 

Main capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, supporting a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats. It operates in both user-interactive and automated modes and allows users to develop custom extension components and scripts using Java or Python. 

Intended users include software reverse engineering analysts, security researchers, and developers tackling complex SRE efforts, malicious code analysis, and network and system vulnerability assessments. 

Notable technologies utilized in the framework and its development include Java (JDK 25), Python 3, Gradle, PyGhidra, Eclipse (via the GhidraDev plugin), and Visual Studio Code.

name: hackingtool
description: ALL IN ONE Hacking Tool For Hackers
summary:
HackingTool is an AI-guided, all-in-one security testing platform designed for authorized penetration testing, red teaming, blue-team/SOC operations, DFIR analysis, OSINT research, bug bounties, CTF challenges, and security education. It consolidates 215 curated tools across 21 categories—including reconnaissance, OSINT, web attacks, wireless testing, phishing, forensics, password cracking, and post-exploitation—into a single console on Linux and macOS.

The platform's AI layer translates plain English into precise tool recommendations and exact commands, breaks down objectives into step-by-step execution plans via `/goal`, and discovers new tools across local catalogs and the GitHub API via `/find`. It operates safely with pinned, SHA-256 verified downloads, zero arbitrary `curl | bash` execution, list-form subprocess handling, and optional tmux-backed background panes for long-running scans. 

HackingTool supports interactive terminal usage through `pipx`, `uv`, or Docker, as well as a non-interactive headless orchestration mode for automated engagements. The optional AI integration is fully opt-in and BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) compatible with OpenAI endpoints or local runtimes like Ollama.

name: screenshot-to-code
description: Drop in a screenshot and convert it to clean code (HTML/Tailwind/React/Vue)
summary:
Screenshot to Code is an AI-powered application designed to convert screenshots, mockups, Figma designs, and screen recordings into clean, functional code and prototypes. 

Main capabilities include generating code across multiple supported technology stacks, extracting real assets and logos from screenshots, handling image generation, background removal, and image editing. It also features a screenshot preview option allowing an agent to render and visually check generated pages in a headless browser.

Supported front-end stacks and frameworks include HTML + Tailwind, HTML + CSS, React + Tailwind, Vue + Tailwind, Bootstrap, and Ionic + Tailwind. The application integrates with multiple AI models, including Gemini (3 Flash Preview and 3.1 Pro Preview), GPT variants (GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 Mini), Claude variants (Claude Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.8), and z-image-turbo via Replicate for image generation. 

The software targets developers, designers, and creators looking to self-host or customize a local environment—utilizing a React and Vite frontend, a FastAPI backend, Poetry for package management, Playwright, and Docker—or use an official hosted product. API keys from providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Replicate are utilized to drive code generation and advanced asset processing features.

name: github-readme-stats
description: :zap: Dynamically generated stats for your github readmes
summary: GitHub Readme Stats is an unmaintained project designed to generate dynamic GitHub stats, top languages, repository pin cards, gist cards, and WakaTime stats for display on user profile READMEs. It provides configurable widgets via URL parameters supporting themes, localization, custom layouts (such as compact, donut, and pie charts), and hidden metrics. Intended for GitHub users looking to enhance their profile customization, the project can be self-hosted on platforms like Vercel or deployed via GitHub Actions using personal access tokens to fetch private repository statistics.

name: Ventoy
description: A new bootable USB solution.
summary:
Ventoy is an open-source tool designed to create bootable USB drives, local disks, SSDs, NVMe drives, and SD cards for ISO, WIM, IMG, VHD(x), and EFI files without requiring the disk to be repeatedly formatted. Users can copy multiple image files directly onto the drive to access a dynamic boot menu, or browse and boot image files stored on local disks. 

The tool supports x86 Legacy BIOS, IA32 UEFI, x86_64 UEFI, ARM64 UEFI, and MIPS64EL UEFI alongside MBR and GPT partition styles. It provides compatibility with over 1,300 ISO files across a wide range of operating systems, including Windows, WinPE, Linux, Unix, ChromeOS, VMware, and Xen. Notable capabilities include UEFI Secure Boot, Linux persistence, Windows and Linux auto-installations, file injection, vDisk booting, and support for file systems such as FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, UDF, XFS, Btrfs, and Ext2/3/4. Ventoy also features a plugin framework with a GUI configurator called VentoyPlugson, customizable themes, password protection, and nondestructive version upgrades.

name: code-server
description: VS Code in the browser
summary:
code-server enables users to run VS Code on any remote machine and access it directly through a web browser. Its primary purpose is to provide a consistent development environment on any device, utilizing cloud servers to offload resource-intensive tasks like tests, compilations, and downloads to preserve local battery life. 

Intended for developers and teams seeking remote development solutions, code-server requires a Linux machine with WebSockets enabled, a minimum of 1 GB of RAM, and 2 vCPUs. Users can get started via an automated install script, manual installation, team deployment via coder/coder, one-click cloud provider deployment guides, or devcontainers features. Notable technologies and integrations include VS Code, WebSockets, Google VM, and devcontainers.

name: awesome-public-datasets
description: A topic-centric list of HQ open datasets.
summary: Awesome Public Datasets is a curated collection of high-quality, topic-centric public data sources gathered from blogs, user responses, and web sources. The repository categorizes data across numerous domains—such as agriculture, biology, economics, government, machine learning, physics, and transportation—to serve researchers, developers, and data enthusiasts looking for open datasets. Maintained via automated tooling through **apd-core**, the project acts as a structured directory linking to free and open public data resources worldwide.

name: advanced-java
description: 😮 Core Interview Questions & Answers For Experienced Java(Backend) Developers | 互联网 Java 工程师进阶知识完全扫盲：涵盖高并发、分布式、高可用、微服务、海量数据处理等领域知识
summary:
This repository is a comprehensive knowledge system designed for internet Java engineers and technical interview preparation. Its primary purpose is to systematically organize and share advanced technical domains including high-concurrency architectures, distributed systems, high-availability designs, microservices, and massive data processing. 

The main capabilities include detailed guides, architectural principles, and solutions for foundational components such as message queues (Kafka, ActiveMQ, RabbitMQ, RocketMQ), search engines (Elasticsearch, Lucene), caching systems (Redis, Memcached), database sharding, read-write separation, distributed service frameworks (Dubbo, RPC), distributed locks (ZooKeeper), distributed transactions, circuit breakers and rate limiters (Hystrix, Sentinel), and Spring Cloud microservices. It also addresses large-scale data challenges like TopK problems and memory-efficient data retrieval.

The intended users are Java developers, software engineers, and technical candidates preparing for interviews. The repository highlights notable technologies and frameworks including Java, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Dubbo, Redis, Elasticsearch, ZooKeeper, Kafka, RabbitMQ, RocketMQ, Hystrix, and Sentinel.

name: Prompt-Engineering-Guide
description: 🐙 Guides, papers, lessons, notebooks and resources for prompt engineering, context engineering, RAG, and AI Agents.
summary:
The Prompt Engineering Guide is a comprehensive resource designed to help researchers and developers understand, develop, and optimize prompts for large language models (LLMs). The project aims to improve LLM capabilities on complex tasks such as question answering and arithmetic reasoning through structured guides, latest research papers, lectures, notebooks, and tools. 

Main capabilities include extensive documentation on prompting techniques (such as Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought, Tree of Thoughts, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and ReAct), practical applications, model-specific guidance, prompt hubs, risk assessments, and tools. The repository targets developers and researchers working with LLMs. Notable technologies referenced include specific language models and frameworks such as ChatGPT, GPT-4, LLaMA, Code Llama, Gemini, Mistral 7B, Mixtral, OLMo, and Phi-2, as well as development tools like Next.js, React, and pnpm.

name: elasticsearch
description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine
summary:
Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine, scalable data store, and vector database optimized for speed and relevance on production-scale workloads. It serves as the foundation of Elastic's open Stack platform. 

Main capabilities include near real-time full-text search, vector search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) integration with generative AI applications, log and metric analysis, application performance monitoring (APM), and security log management. 

Intended users include developers, data engineers, and system administrators looking to store and query massive datasets, structured or unstructured text, numerical data, and geospatial data. 

Notable technologies integrated or used include Docker, Kibana, REST APIs, and Gradle as the build system.

name: learn-claude-code
description: Bash is all you need -  A nano claude code–like 「agent harness」, built from 0 to 1
summary:
Learn Claude Code (learn-claude-code) is an open-source educational repository and 17-lesson course focused on harness engineering for software agents. The project is built on the core premise that agency—the capacity to perceive, reason, and act—comes from model training, while an external code infrastructure (the "harness") provides the operational environment. 

The curriculum progresses through foundational capabilities, complex workflow management, session persistence, long-running background tasks, multi-agent coordination, and goal-directed runtime orchestration. Notable harness mechanisms implemented across the chapters include an agent loop, dispatch maps for tool execution, permission and hook governance, structured planning via TodoWrite, context compaction, persistent memory systems, a file-backed task graph, asynchronous background threads, cron scheduling, persistent agent teammates with task-bound worktrees, Model Context Protocol (MCP) plugin routing, and goal-closure verification. 

The repository provides standalone runnable Python implementations for each chapter, along with a web platform, multilingual documentation, and links to production-focused ecosystem projects such as Kode Agent CLI, Kode Agent SDK, and the OpenClaw-based sister tutorial repository claw0. It is licensed under the MIT license.

name: models
description: Models and examples built with TensorFlow
summary:
The TensorFlow Model Garden is a repository containing state-of-the-art (SOTA) model implementations and modeling solutions designed to demonstrate best practices for TensorFlow users in research and product development. Intended users include machine learning practitioners, researchers, and developers leveraging TensorFlow. 

The repository is organized into several key directories:
- **official**: Officially maintained, optimized, and readable example implementations of SOTA models using TensorFlow 2 high-level APIs.
- **research**: Research model implementations in TensorFlow 1 or 2 maintained by researchers.
- **community**: A curated list of GitHub repositories with TensorFlow 2-powered machine learning models.
- **orbit**: A flexible, lightweight library for writing customized training loops in TensorFlow 2.x, integrating seamlessly with `tf.distribute` and supporting CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs.

Notable technologies utilized include TensorFlow (versions 1 and 2), TensorBoard, Python, and associated tools like `tf-models-official` and `tensorflow-text-nightly`.

name: cpython
description: The Python programming language
summary:
CPython is the reference implementation of the Python programming language, written in C and Python. Its purpose is to provide the core interpreter, standard library, and runtime environment to execute Python code. The repository contains the source code for building, testing, and developing Python (version 3.16.0 alpha 0), supporting platforms such as Unix, Linux, BSD, macOS, Cygwin, and Windows. 

Main capabilities include building the interpreter from source, running comprehensive test suites via `make test`, and optimizing builds using Profile Guided Optimization (PGO) and Link Time Optimization (LTO). Intended users include software developers, contributors, system administrators, and anyone building or embedding the Python runtime. Notable technologies and tools referenced include GCC, Clang, GNU Make, Azure Pipelines, and GitHub Actions.

name: gpt4all
description: GPT4All: Run Local LLMs on Any Device. Open-source and available for commercial use.
summary:
GPT4All is an open-source software project that enables users to run large language models (LLMs)—including DeepSeek R1 Distillations and Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct—privately and locally on everyday desktops and laptops without requiring GPUs or external API calls. 

Intended for developers and general users seeking local AI capabilities, the project offers a chat application UI, a Docker-based OpenAI-compatible API server, a Python client providing access to LLMs via `llama.cpp` implementations, and a LocalDocs feature for privately chatting with local data. It also supports Nomic Vulkan for GPU inference on NVIDIA and AMD hardware. Notable technology integrations include Langchain, Weaviate Vector Database, and OpenLIT for OTel-native monitoring. Installers are provided for Windows (including Windows ARM), macOS (optimized for Apple Silicon), and Ubuntu Linux.

name: unsloth
description: Local UI to run and train LLMs and diffusion models. Supports GGUF, MLX, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4, MiniMax-H3, Gemma 4, FLUX and more.
summary:
Unsloth is a desktop application and toolkit designed to run, train, fine-tune, and deploy large language models (LLMs), machine learning, diffusion, embedding, audio, and multimodal models locally or remotely. It aims to accelerate training workflows—supporting LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tuning, pretraining, RL, GRPO, DPO, and FP8—while lowering VRAM requirements. 

Main capabilities include model execution and building via a native desktop app or the Unsloth Studio web UI, agent integrations (such as Claude Code, Codex, and MCP), local search and RAG, image/video diffusion model support, dataset recipes built from files like PDFs and CSVs, remote LAN/Cloudflare HTTPS access, and OpenAI-compatible APIs. It targets developers and AI practitioners looking to run and adapt models efficiently on consumer or server hardware.

Notable technologies and frameworks utilized include Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face (transformers, TRL), llama.cpp, MLX, GGUF, Triton, FlashAttention, and support for multi-GPU configurations alongside NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs, CPUs, and the Vulkan backend. It is dual-licensed under Apache 2.0 and AGPL-3.0.

name: AppFlowy
description: Bring projects, wikis, and teams together with AI. AppFlowy is the AI collaborative workspace where you achieve more without losing control of your data. The leading open source Notion alternative.
summary:
AppFlowy is an open-source AI workspace and alternative to Notion designed to help users manage tasks, projects, documentation, and data while maintaining full control over their information. 

Main capabilities include Kanban boards, databases, documentation sites, templates, integrated AI features, and cross-device synchronization. The project targets individual users seeking data privacy and native performance, as well as enterprises and developers looking for customizable collaboration infrastructure and building blocks. 

AppFlowy is built using **Flutter** for the cross-platform user interface and **Rust** for the backend engine. It supports desktop operating systems (macOS, Windows, Linux) via downloadable binaries, FlatHub, Snapcraft, and Sourceforge, and is also available natively on mobile devices for iOS (iPhone) and Android. Users can choose to self-host the application or build it from source.

name: grafana
description: The open and composable observability and data visualization platform. Visualize metrics, logs, and traces from multiple sources like Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, InfluxDB, Postgres and many more.
summary: Grafana is an open-source platform for monitoring and observability designed to help users query, visualize, alert on, and understand metrics and logs regardless of their storage location. Its main capabilities include fast and flexible client-side visualizations, dynamic and reusable dashboards utilizing template variables, ad-hoc metric exploration with split views and dynamic drilldowns, log exploration with preserved label filters and live streaming, visual alert rule definition with notifications sent to systems such as Slack, PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie, and the ability to mix different data sources on a per-query basis within the same graph. The platform targets teams and developers seeking to create, explore, and share dashboards to foster a data-driven culture. Notable technologies and integrations associated with the project include panel plugins, custom data sources, and testing support via BrowserStack.

name: Font-Awesome
description: The iconic SVG, font, and CSS toolkit
summary: Font Awesome is an internet icon library and toolkit intended for designers, developers, and content creators. It provides scalable vector icons and toolkits distributed across multiple formats including SVG, JavaScript, web fonts, and desktop font files. Main capabilities include integrating and displaying icons in web and desktop environments, with specific licensing structures covering icons under the CC BY 4.0 license, fonts under the SIL OFL 1.1 license, and code under the MIT license.

name: obs-studio
description: OBS Studio - Free and open source software for live streaming and screen recording
summary: OBS Studio is software designed for efficiently capturing, compositing, encoding, recording, and streaming video content. Distributed under the GNU General Public License v2 (or any later version), the project incorporates PVS-Studio as a static analyzer for C, C++, C#, and Java code. Intended users include content creators, streamers, and developers, supported by comprehensive developer and API documentation, a bug tracker, community forums, and translation management via Crowdin.

name: tesseract
description: Tesseract Open Source OCR Engine (main repository)
summary:
Tesseract OCR is an optical character recognition engine comprising the `libtesseract` library and a command-line program (`tesseract`). Designed for developers, software users, and researchers, it provides robust text recognition capabilities across more than 100 languages with full Unicode (UTF-8) support. 

The engine features a neural network (LSTM) based OCR model optimized for line recognition alongside a legacy pattern-recognition OCR engine. It accepts various input image formats—including PNG, JPEG, and TIFF—using the Leptonica library for image handling, and supports multiple output formats such as plain text, hOCR (HTML), PDF, TSV, ALTO, and PAGE. 

Developers can integrate Tesseract using its C and C++ APIs or utilize available community wrappers for other programming languages. The project also supports custom language training. Licensed under the Apache-2.0 License, Tesseract relies on notable technologies including Leptonica, zlib, libpng, and libtiff.

name: nest
description: A progressive Node.js framework for building efficient, scalable, and enterprise-grade server-side applications with TypeScript/JavaScript 🚀
summary:
Nest (NestJS) is a progressive Node.js framework designed for building efficient, scalable, and maintainable server-side applications. Built with TypeScript while maintaining pure JavaScript compatibility, it combines elements of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), Functional Programming (FP), and Functional Reactive Programming (FRP). 

Nest provides a structured application architecture inspired by Angular to address server-side architectural challenges. Under the hood, it primarily utilizes Express while offering compatibility with other libraries like Fastify to support third-party plugins. Its ecosystem includes NestJS Observe, an official observability platform SDK for streaming requests, background jobs, errors, logs, and distributed traces. 

The framework is intended for developers and enterprises building robust, testable, and loosely coupled backend systems using modern JavaScript and TypeScript.

name: archify
description: Agent skill for beautiful, verifiable architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle diagrams—self-contained HTML with motion and crisp export.
summary:
Archify is an open-source tool that transforms ideas, repository structures, travel plans, or system descriptions into interactive, self-contained HTML visual diagrams using AI agents like Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode. 

Designed for developers, system architects, and technical writers, Archify provides five primary diagram types: Architecture, Workflow, Sequence, Data Flow, and Lifecycle. Key capabilities include generating typed JSON IR (Intermediate Representation) from prompts, multi-theme support (light/dark), node focusing, route tracing, upstream/downstream reach analysis, role comparisons, and exporting diagrams as PNGs, share cards, or static web artifacts. It also supports source evidence mapping through Git-verified file and line references.

Built with Node.js, Archify can be installed globally via `npx skills add tt-a1i/archify -g` and features a CLI with built-in validation rules, local loopback preview servers, and automated delivery checks.

name: LeetCodeAnimation
description: Demonstrate all the questions on LeetCode in the form of animation.（用动画的形式呈现解LeetCode题目的思路,完整单步/回看/变速/语音讲解在 algomooc.com）
summary:
LeetCodeAnimation is an open-source project and public repository that provides animated explanations for LeetCode algorithm problems. It visually breaks down core programming and data structure concepts such as pointer movements, state transitions, recursion unfolding, and boundary conditions. 

The project targets learners and developers looking to intuitively understand algorithms—covering topics such as arrays, linked lists, dynamic programming, and graph theory. Each integrated problem solution features reference implementations in Python, C++, and Java (with Python as the default), alongside structured JSON data manifests and topic indexes (`docs/data/manifest.json`, `docs/leetcode-animation-index.md`, and `docs/index-by-topic.md`). 

While the GitHub repository acts as a historical archive, public index, and sync target, the complete interactive platform is hosted externally at algomooc.com, offering single-step controls, speed adjustments, voice-narrated explanations (using an authorized synthesized voice), and an AI algorithm tutor named "Xiao Ou" for real-time problem-solving assistance.

name: redis
description: For developers, who are building real-time data-driven applications, Redis is the preferred, fastest, and most feature-rich cache, data structure server, and document and vector query engine.
summary:
Redis Open Source is an in-memory data structure server, high-performance cache, document database, vector search engine, and message broker. It provides sub-millisecond latency for real-time applications and supports a wide array of native data types and capabilities, including strings, JSON documents, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, geospatial indexes, bitmaps, bitfields, probabilistic data structures (such as Bloom filters, Cuckoo filters, t-digest, Top-k, and Count-min sketches), time series, streams, pub/sub messaging, transactions, and server-side programmability via Lua scripts. Additionally, Redis features built-in search and query capabilities, vector stores for generative AI use cases like semantic caching and RAG, and an extensible modules API. 

Intended for developers building real-time, data-driven applications, Redis can be deployed via fully managed services like Redis Cloud, official Docker images, binary distributions, or built from source using tools like GCC/Clang, CMake, LLVM, Rust, and OpenSSL. It supports client libraries in languages such as Python, C#/.NET, Go, JavaScript, Java, PHP, and C, alongside management tools like `redis-cli` and Redis Insight.

name: imgui
description: Dear ImGui: Bloat-free Graphical User interface for C++ with minimal dependencies
summary:
Dear ImGui is a bloat-free, self-contained, and renderer-agnostic immediate-mode graphical user interface library written in C++. Designed primarily for programmers, it outputs optimized vertex buffers and command lists that can be rendered within any 3D-pipeline-enabled application. 

The library's main purpose is to empower developers to rapidly create content-creation tools, game engine toolsets, visualization utilities, profilers, debuggers, and ad-hoc or long-lived diagnostic interfaces, rather than end-user application UIs. It minimizes state synchronization and user-side state storage, facilitating code-driven and data-driven workflows.

Dear ImGui is intended for software engineers, game developers, and technical artists working on real-time 3D applications, game engines, fullscreen applications, embedded systems, and console platforms. It includes numerous officially maintained platform and renderer backends supporting technologies such as DirectX, OpenGL, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU, SDL, GLFW, Win32, and Emscripten. Numerous third-party bindings extend its use to other programming languages and major frameworks like Unity and Unreal Engine.

name: awesome-claude-skills
description: A curated list of awesome Claude Skills, resources, and tools for customizing Claude AI workflows
summary:
Awesome Claude Skills is a curated repository of over 1,000 production-ready Claude Skills and plugins designed to enhance productivity and enable real-world agent actions across Claude.ai, Claude Code, the Claude API, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and Windsurf. The project provides reusable instruction packages (`SKILL.md`) covering document processing, software development, data analysis, business and marketing, communication, creative media, productivity, project management, and security systems. 

It notably integrates with the Composio MCP Gateway and connect-apps plugins to grant AI agents secure, authenticated tool access across more than 1,000 external applications and SaaS platforms—such as GitHub, Slack, Notion, Jira, Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Stripe—enabling agents to send emails, manage issues, and automate workflows. Intended for developers, indie founders, and knowledge workers, the project utilizes technologies including Python, TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, Playwright, D3.js, PostgreSQL, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The repository is distributed under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: ai-agents-for-beginners
description: 18 Lessons to Get Started Building AI Agents
summary:
This repository contains an educational course designed for beginners to learn how to build AI agents. The project covers foundational concepts, agentic design patterns, tool use, agentic RAG, planning, multi-agent systems, metacognition, agentic memory, agentic protocols, and production deployment. 

Intended users are developers and learners starting to build with generative AI and AI agents. The course materials feature written lessons, videos, and Python code samples. 

Notable technologies and frameworks used include Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF), Microsoft Foundry Agent Service V2, Microsoft Foundry, and OpenAI-compatible providers like MiniMax.

name: openai-cookbook
description: Examples and guides for using the OpenAI API
summary: The OpenAI Cookbook provides example code, guides, and notebooks for accomplishing common tasks using the OpenAI API. Its main capabilities include demonstrating practical implementations of AI concepts through hands-on examples. The project is intended for developers and users of the OpenAI API who want to integrate AI capabilities into their applications. Most code examples are written in Python, though the underlying concepts apply to any programming language. Running the examples requires an OpenAI account, an associated API key configured via the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable or an `.env` file, and an IDE such as Visual Studio Code. The project is licensed under the MIT License.

name: caddy
description: Fast and extensible multi-platform HTTP/1-2-3 web server with automatic HTTPS
summary:
Caddy is an extensible, production-ready server platform and web server written in Go. Its primary purpose is to serve websites and applications with automatic HTTPS enabled by default via Let's Encrypt, ZeroSSL, and a fully-managed local CA. 

Main capabilities include HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 support, automated TLS certificate management and renewal via CertMagic, a modular architecture supporting various plugins, and dynamic configuration through a native JSON config, a JSON API, config adapters, and the user-friendly Caddyfile format. It also functions as a general platform for running long-running Go programs and apps.

Caddy is intended for web developers, system administrators, and organizations of all sizes needing a reliable, secure, and extensible web server or application platform. Notable technologies utilized include Go, CertMagic, ZeroSSL, and standard web protocols like TLS and HTTP/3.

name: Best-websites-a-programmer-should-visit
description: :link: Some useful websites for programmers.
summary:
This repository is a curated, non-exhaustive list of useful websites, resources, and tools for programmers, computer science students, and software developers. Its primary purpose is to help learners and professionals stay informed, learn new technologies, practice coding, and navigate their careers. 

The collection covers a wide array of categories, including coding practice platforms, tech news aggregators, developer blogs, tutorials, interview preparation guides, AI and machine learning resources, system administration tools, cryptocurrency basics, podcasts, MOOCs, and open-source contribution platforms. Notable technologies referenced include Python, JavaScript, Java, C++, Rust, Go, SQL, Git, and various machine learning frameworks. 

Intended for developers at all levels—from absolute beginners seeking basic programming tasks to experienced engineers looking for system design advice, job boards, or interview preparation—the repository provides categorized links to communities like Stack Overflow, competitive programming platforms, documentation sites, and developer tools.

name: cs-self-learning
description: 计算机自学指南
summary:
The project "CS 自学指南" (Computer Science Self-Learning Guide) is a comprehensive online guidebook and curriculum aggregator designed to help beginners and self-taught learners navigate open-source computer science resources. Its stated purpose is to guide novices through a structured 2-to-3-year learning path, helping them build a solid foundation in mathematics and coding, complete extensive project work, and master mainstream programming languages such as C, C++, Java, JS, Python, Go, and Rust. 

The guide covers a wide range of computer science domains, including algorithms, circuits, computer architecture, networking, operating systems, compilers, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, cryptography, information theory, game theory, numerical analysis, statistics, distributed systems, databases, computer graphics, Web development, cloud services, and supercomputing.
