Intended for individuals pursuing self-directed education in computer science for either research or employment, the project is hosted online via csdiy.wiki with both Chinese and English editions. It utilizes MkDocs for documentation and is distributed under the MIT License for contributor-written content.

name: json-server
description: Get a full fake REST API with zero coding in less than 30 seconds (seriously)
summary:
JSON-Server is a Node.js-based tool that allows developers to quickly spin up a full, zero-config REST API using a simple JSON or JSON5 file (`db.json`) as the data source. 

Designed for developers, prototypers, and front-end engineers who need a mock backend quickly, JSON-Server provides full CRUD operations for both array and singular object resources. It supports advanced querying capabilities out of the box, including filtering with conditional operators (such as `gt`, `lt`, `in`, `contains`), sorting, pagination (`_page` and `_per_page`), relation embedding (`_embed`), and complex filtering using `_where`. Additionally, it features automatic static file serving from local directories. 

Technologies utilized include Node.js, npm, JavaScript, and JSON/JSON5.

name: MiroFish
description: A Simple and Universal Swarm Intelligence Engine, Predicting Anything. 简洁通用的群体智能引擎，预测万物
summary:
MiroFish is a next-generation AI prediction and swarm intelligence engine powered by multi-agent technology. It extracts seed information—such as breaking news, policy drafts, financial reports, or literary works—to automatically construct high-fidelity parallel digital worlds. Within these sandboxes, thousands of intelligent agents with independent personalities, long-term memory, and behavioral logic interact and undergo social evolution, allowing users to deduce future trajectories, rehearse scenarios, and test policies.

The main capabilities include GraphRAG-based graph building, entity relationship extraction, persona generation, dual-platform parallel simulation, dynamic temporal memory updates, report generation, and deep interactive chatting with any agent in the simulation. 

Designed for both macro-level decision-makers (such as for policy and public relations testing) and micro-level individual users (such as exploring creative scenarios or alternative novel endings), MiroFish integrates technologies including Node.js, Python, Docker, OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs (recommended via Alibaba Bailian), GraphRAG, and Zep Cloud for memory management, with its simulation engine powered by OASIS (Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations).

name: LlamaFactory
description: Unified Efficient Fine-Tuning of 100+ LLMs & VLMs (ACL 2024)
summary:
LlamaFactory is an open-source framework designed for the unified and efficient fine-tuning of over 100 large language models (LLMs) and multimodal models, including LLaMA, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, Mistral, and Phi. 

**Main Capabilities**
- Supports pre-training, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reward modeling, and reinforcement learning approaches such as PPO, DPO, KTO, ORPO, and SimPO.
- Provides scalable training resources including full-tuning, freeze-tuning, LoRA, and quantized training methods (QLoRA, QOFT) via AQLM, AWQ, GPTQ, HQQ, EETQ, and bitsandbytes.
- Integrates advanced algorithms (such as GaLore, BAdam, APOLLO, Adam-mini, Muon, OFT, DoRA, LongLoRA, LLaMA Pro, PiSSA) and practical performance optimizations like FlashAttention-2, Unsloth, Liger Kernel, and KTransformers.
- Features faster inference, evaluation benchmarks, and deployment capabilities via OpenAI-style APIs, Gradio Web UI (LLaMA Board), CLI, vLLM, and SGLang.
- Offers experiment tracking through LlamaBoard, TensorBoard, Wandb, MLflow, and SwanLab.

**Intended Users**
Researchers, developers, and machine learning engineers seeking to customize, train, evaluate, and deploy large language and multimodal models with zero-code CLI and graphical user interfaces.

**Notable Technologies**
PyTorch, Transformers, Datasets, PEFT, TRL, Gradio, vLLM, SGLang, and Docker.

name: impeccable
description: The design language that makes your AI harness better at design.
summary:
Impeccable is a design guidance tool and skill for AI coding agents that helps eliminate generic, AI-generated frontend design aesthetics (such as default fonts like Inter, purple-to-blue gradients, and nested cards). Created by Paul Bakaus, the project includes 24 interactive commands (such as `polish`, `audit`, `critique`, `distill`, and `animate`), a live browser iteration mode, and 61 deterministic detector rules to audit technical and visual quality.

The project is designed for developers using AI coding assistants and supports a wide range of platforms, including Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, Hermes Agent, OpenCode, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, and Veto. It integrates via a setup flow (`/impeccable init`) that establishes durable product truth in `PRODUCT.md` and maintains design systems via `DESIGN.md`. It also provides a standalone CLI tool (`npx impeccable detect`) for scanning directories, HTML files, or URLs without requiring an AI harness, alongside automated hooks for validating file edits.

name: 30-Days-Of-Python
description: The 30 Days of Python programming challenge is a step-by-step guide to learn the Python programming language in 30 days. This challenge may take more than 100 days. Follow your own pace. These videos may help too: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC7PNRuno1rzYPb1xLa4yktw
summary:
The "30 Days Of Python" repository provides a comprehensive, structured programming challenge designed for absolute beginners and professionals to learn Python 3 step-by-step. The project purpose is to teach foundational and advanced Python concepts through daily lessons, explanations, real-world examples, hands-on exercises, and projects. 

Main capabilities and topics covered include basic syntax, variables, operators, data types (numbers, strings, booleans, lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries), conditionals, loops, functions, modules, list comprehensions, higher-order functions, error handling, date and time, regular expressions, file handling, package management, object-oriented programming, web scraping, virtual environments, statistics, Pandas, web development, MongoDB integration, and building APIs. 

Intended users are individuals looking to master Python for general-purpose programming, web development, data science, or machine learning. Notable technologies and tools referenced throughout the curriculum include Python, Visual Studio Code, Pandas, and MongoDB.

name: superset
description: Apache Superset is a Data Visualization and Data Exploration Platform
summary: Apache Superset is a modern, enterprise-ready business intelligence web application designed for data exploration and data visualization. Its main capabilities include a no-code chart builder, a web-based SQL Editor for advanced querying, a lightweight semantic layer for defining custom metrics and dimensions, dynamic dashboards, a wide array of visualizations ranging from simple bar charts to geospatial plots, a configurable caching layer, extensible security roles and authentication options, and a REST API for programmatic customization. Superset is built with a cloud-native architecture for scale and supports querying data from nearly any SQL-speaking database or data engine utilizing a Python DB-API driver and a SQLAlchemy dialect, including Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Snowflake, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Trino, Presto, and Apache Druid. It is intended for analysts, business users, database administrators, and developers.

name: flask
description: The Python micro framework for building web applications.
summary: Flask is a lightweight WSGI web application framework designed for Python developers to get started quickly and easily while retaining the ability to scale up to complex applications. Built as a wrapper around Werkzeug and Jinja, Flask does not enforce any specific dependencies, project layouts, or tools, leaving those choices to the developer. It accommodates community-provided extensions to add new functionality easily.

name: tabby
description: A terminal for a more modern age
summary:
Tabby (formerly Terminus) is a highly configurable terminal emulator, SSH, and serial client designed for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It serves as an alternative to standard built-in terminals and traditional clients like PuTTY, providing users with a feature-rich terminal environment.

Main capabilities include an integrated SSH2 and Telnet client with a connection manager, X11 and port forwarding, automatic jump host management, agent forwarding, and direct file transfer via Zmodem. It features an integrated serial terminal with readline input, hex byte-by-byte support, and automatic reconnection. Additional terminal features comprise nested split panes, customizable tabs, a dockable "Quake console" window, progress detection, completion notifications, font ligatures, custom shell profiles, and an encrypted container for SSH secrets. It natively supports PowerShell, PS Core, WSL, Git-Bash, Cygwin, MSYS2, Cmder, and CMD, alongside a wide array of installable plugins and themes.

Intended users are developers, system administrators, and power users managing remote environments and local shells who require advanced terminal customization, multi-session management, and extensibility.

name: awesome-react
description: A collection of awesome things regarding React ecosystem
summary: Awesome React is a curated collection of resources, libraries, tools, frameworks, and real-world applications for the React and React Native ecosystems. Intended for developers and engineers building web and mobile applications, it provides categorized references spanning tutorials, component libraries, state management, routing, styling, testing, data fetching, forms, internationalization, and graphics. The repository highlights notable technologies such as Next.js, Gatsby, Remix, Vite, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, GraphQL, Three.js, and D3, serving as a comprehensive directory for modern JavaScript and TypeScript development tools.

name: awesome-machine-learning
description: A curated list of awesome Machine Learning frameworks, libraries and software.
summary:
Awesome Machine Learning is a curated, language-organized list of machine learning frameworks, libraries, software, tools, and educational resources. Its primary purpose is to provide practitioners, developers, and researchers with a comprehensive directory of software for general-purpose machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, speech recognition, data analysis, and visualization.

The repository catalogs projects implemented in dozens of languages, including Python, C, C++, Java, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Julia, R, Ruby, Scala, Clojure, and Swift. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced throughout the list include TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, scikit-learn, OpenCV, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, Apache Spark, ONNX, and CUDA. Intended users span data scientists, software engineers, and machine learning practitioners seeking libraries, tools, and MLOps platforms for model training, inference, experiment tracking, feature stores, and deployment.

name: awesome-scalability
description: The Patterns of Scalable, Reliable, and Performant Large-Scale Systems
summary:
This repository is an updated and organized reading list illustrating the patterns, architecture, and principles of scalable, reliable, and performant large-scale systems. The project purpose is to provide credible references, case studies from battle-tested production systems, and engineering talks that explain how tech giants serve millions to billions of users. 

Its main capabilities include categorizing curated resources across core engineering domains such as system scalability, availability, stability, performance optimization, intelligence (big data and distributed machine learning), architecture, and organizational management. The content highlights real-world architectures, failure handling, caching strategies, distributed storage, and performance tuning. 

The intended users are software engineers, system architects, technical leaders, and candidates preparing for system design interviews. Notable technologies referenced throughout the case studies and materials include AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, Kafka, Redis, Elasticsearch, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Cassandra, HBase, Presto, Spark, and TensorFlow.

name: headroom
description: Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60-95% fewer tokens for JSON, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server.
summary:
Headroom is an open-source context compression layer for AI agents and large language models (LLMs). It reduces token usage by compressing agent inputs (such as tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, source code, files, and conversation history) and outputs before they reach the model. Compression runs locally on the user's machine to keep data private.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Local Compression Engines:** Content types are handled via specialized compressors including SmartCrusher (for JSON data), CodeCompressor (AST-aware for multiple programming languages), and Kompress-v2-base (for prose and text).
- **Multiple Integration Modes:** Operates as a Python or TypeScript library, an ASGI middleware, a drop-in proxy (`headroom proxy`), a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, or an agent wrapper (`headroom wrap`).
- **Reversible Compression (CCR):** Original uncompressed text is cached locally, allowing models to retrieve full text on demand via MCP tools.
- **Cross-Agent Memory & Learning:** Provides a shared memory store across various agents and includes `headroom learn` to mine failed sessions and write corrections to memory markdown files.
- **Output Token Reduction:** Trims model-generated verbosity and adjusts reasoning effort to lower output token costs.

**Intended Users:** Developers and engineering teams running AI agents, coding assistants, or long LLM workflows who want to optimize token consumption and maintain context windows.

**Notable Technologies:** Python, TypeScript, HuggingFace (`chopratejas/kompress-v2-base`), ONNX Runtime, and Apache 2.0 licensing.

name: Front-End-Checklist
description: 🗂 The essential checklist for modern web development, for humans and AI agents
summary:
Front-End Checklist is an open-source front-end quality system and comprehensive checklist designed for both human developers and AI agents. It translates modern web development best practices into practical review workflows spanning 386 rules across 11 categories: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Performance, Accessibility, SEO, Security, Images, Testing, Privacy, and Internationalization. 

The project aims to facilitate code reviews, audits, and remediation workflows. Users can browse the checklist via the main web application, interact with it directly through the repository README, or integrate it into automated agent workflows using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes dedicated MCP tools. 

Intended users include frontend developers, code reviewers, and AI engineering agents performing automated code analysis or audits. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced across the project and its rule corpus include React, Next.js, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, Tailwind, Node.js, and Turborepo within a pnpm-managed monorepo structure utilizing tools like Biome, Playwright, Cypress, and Stylelint.

name: the-algorithm
description: Source code for the X Recommendation Algorithm
summary:
X's Recommendation Algorithm is a set of services and jobs responsible for serving feeds of posts and content across X product surfaces, including the For You Timeline, Search, Explore, and Notifications. The architecture relies on shared data systems, models, and software frameworks. Key data and model components include tweetypie, unified-user-actions, user-signal-service, SimClusters, TwHIN, trust-and-safety-models, real-graph, tweepcred, recos-injector, graph-feature-service, topic-social-proof, and representation-scorer. Core frameworks consist of navi, product-mixer, timelines-aggregation-framework, representation-manager, and the legacy TensorFlow v1-based twml.

For the For You Timeline and Recommended Notifications, the project utilizes candidate sources, ranking models, and mixing/filtering services. Candidate sources and graph engines feature search-index, tweet-mixer, user-tweet-entity-graph (UTEG) built on GraphJet, and follow-recommendation-service (FRS). Ranking and filtering utilize light-ranker, heavy-ranker, home-mixer, visibility-filters, timelineranker, pushservice, pushservice-light-ranker, and pushservice-heavy-ranker. Components utilize Bazel build configurations.

name: SecLists
description: SecLists is the security tester's companion. It's a collection of multiple types of lists used during security assessments, collected in one place. List types include usernames, passwords, URLs, sensitive data patterns, fuzzing payloads, web shells, and many more.
summary:
SecLists is a comprehensive collection of lists used by security testers during security assessments. Maintained by Daniel Miessler, Jason Haddix, Ignacio Portal, and g0tmi1k, the project provides a centralized repository so testers can quickly access necessary lists on a new testing environment. 

The main capabilities of the project include supplying multiple types of data collections, such as usernames, passwords, URLs, sensitive data patterns, fuzzing payloads, and web shells, alongside a `.bin` directory containing wordlist generators and mutators. The intended users are security testers, penetration testers, and security professionals.

name: OpenBB
description: Open Data Platform for analysts, quants and AI agents.
summary:
The Open Data Platform by OpenBB (ODP) is an open-source toolset designed for data engineers to integrate proprietary, licensed, and public financial data sources into downstream applications such as AI copilots and research dashboards. Functioning as a "connect once, consume everywhere" infrastructure layer, ODP consolidates and exposes data to Python environments for quants, the OpenBB Workspace and Excel for analysts, MCP servers for AI agents, and REST APIs for other applications. 

Intended users include data engineers, quantitative analysts, and financial researchers. The project features a Python package (`openbb`) and a command-line interface (`openbb-cli`) allowing users to easily query financial data like historical equity prices. Notable technologies and components mentioned include FastAPI, Uvicorn, Python (3.10–3.14), the OpenBB Workspace, and REST APIs. The software is distributed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.

name: ruflo
description: 🌊 The original agent harness. Deploy intelligent multi-player swarms, coordinate autonomous workflows, and build conversational AI systems. Features adaptive memory, self-learning intelligence, federation, vector RAG integration, and native Claude Code / Codex / Hermes and many more Integrated
summary:
Ruflo (formerly Claude Flow) is an agent meta-harness designed for Claude Code and Codex that adds an execution and coordination layer to AI models. It equips agents with specialized tools, persistent memory, execution loops, sandboxes, and enterprise security guardrails to facilitate multi-agent collaboration.

Main capabilities include over 100 specialized agents, swarm coordination topologies (hierarchical, mesh, and adaptive with consensus), zero-trust agent federation across machines, self-learning architectures (SONA neural patterns and ReasoningBank), HNSW-indexed vector memory (AgentDB), background task workers, automated test generation, documentation maintenance, and security auditing. It also features a MetaHarness module for grading agent setups and scanning tool configurations, alongside a plugin marketplace containing 35+ plugins. 

Intended users are developers, engineering teams, and enterprises seeking to run, coordinate, and secure collaborative AI agent swarms and local or multi-provider LLM workflows. 

Notable technologies integrated within the ecosystem include Rust, TypeScript, Node.js, MCP (Model Context Protocol), Playwright, Ollama, RuVector (GPU-accelerated search and Graph RAG), and multi-provider LLM support (Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Cohere).

name: union
description: The trust-minimized, zero-knowledge bridging protocol, designed for censorship resistance, extremely high security, and usage in decentralized finance.
summary:
Union is a zero-knowledge infrastructure layer designed for general message passing, asset transfers, NFTs, and DeFi. Built on Consensus Verification without trusted third parties, oracles, multi-signatures, or MPC, it implements IBC for Cosmos chain compatibility and connects to EVM chains including Ethereum, Berachain, Arbitrum, Base, BSC, and others. 

The project consists of several core components: `uniond` (the Union node implementation using CometBLS in Go), `galoisd` (a zero-knowledge prover using Go and Gnark), `voyager` (a modular cross-ecosystem relayer in Rust), a Cosmwasm smart contract stack, light clients, `unionvisor`, a faucet (`drip`), an EVM smart contract stack, web applications, and a TypeScript SDK. 

Intended for developers and users operating across heterogeneous blockchain ecosystems, Union uses Nix for reproducible builds and development environments across supported mainnet and testnet networks.

name: awesome-cpp
description: A curated list of awesome C++ (or C) frameworks, libraries, resources, and shiny things. Inspired by awesome-... stuff.
summary:
Awesome C++ is a curated, comprehensive list of C and C++ frameworks, libraries, software, and educational resources. The project serves developers, engineers, and researchers seeking curated tools across a broad spectrum of domains, including artificial intelligence, concurrency, databases, game engines, GUI development, machine learning, networking, and scientific computing. 

It covers standard libraries, cryptographic toolkits, image processing utilities, memory allocators, web frameworks, and testing tools, alongside build systems, static code analysis utilities, and compilers. Additionally, the repository aggregates learning materials such as books, articles, podcasts, talks, and coding standards like the C++ Core Guidelines and CERT C++.

name: awesome-vue
description: 🎉 A curated list of awesome things related to Vue.js
summary:
This repository hosts Awesome Vue, a curated directory of resources, projects, components, libraries, and tools related to the Vue.js JavaScript framework. It aims to help developers find official documentation, learning tutorials, articles, podcasts, community channels, job portals, open-source applications, and commercial products built with Vue.js. 

The collection organizes UI components, frameworks, state management libraries (such as Pinia and Vuex), routing utilities, testing tools, and developer aids—supporting both Vue 2 and Vue 3 ecosystems. It targets frontend developers, full-stack engineers, and learners seeking ecosystem extensions like Nuxt.js, Vite, and TypeScript integrations.

name: stable-diffusion
description: A latent text-to-image diffusion model
summary:
Stable Diffusion is a latent text-to-image diffusion model designed for high-resolution image synthesis, text-guided image-to-image translation, and upscaling. Intended for researchers and developers, the project enables users to generate and modify images from textual prompts and input sketches using a lightweight architecture. 

Main capabilities include text-to-image sampling (txt2img) and image modification (img2img), supported by reference scripts, a safety checker module, invisible watermarking, and integration with the Hugging Face `diffusers` library. 

Notable technologies and components used include an 860M UNet, a 123M frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 text encoder, an 8-factor autoencoder, PLMS and DDIM samplers, PyTorch, and models pretrained on subsets of the LAION-5B database (such as laion2B-en and laion-aesthetics). The software requires a GPU with at least 10GB VRAM and a Conda environment. Model weights are released under the CreativeML OpenRAIL M license, which includes specific use-based restrictions.

name: career-ops
description: Open-source AI job search agent and job finder: scan job boards, score each job 1-5 against your CV before you apply, tailor an ATS-friendly resume and cover letter, get interview prep and a job application tracker. It helps you fill in each application; you press Submit. Runs locally in your AI coding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more).
summary:
career-ops is an open-source AI job search agent that runs locally inside AI coding CLIs like Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, and Grok Build CLI. It helps job seekers filter and evaluate job postings, score alignment against their personal CV, and automate tailored document generation without automatically submitting applications.

Main capabilities include:
- **A-H Evaluation:** Assesses role summaries, CV matches, level strategies, compensation research, legitimacy checks, and interview prep.
- **Human-in-the-Loop Workflow:** Drafts cover letters, emails, answers, and ATS-optimized markdown or Space Grotesk + DM Sans PDF resumes, ensuring the user always reviews and manually submits.
- **Beyond the CV:** Conducts company research, contact discovery for hiring managers/recruiters, and pattern analysis for rejections and funnels.
- **Portal Scanner:** Integrates with pre-configured ATS boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, etc.) and search queries to discover live openings.
- **Dashboard TUI:** A Bubble Tea and Lipgloss-powered terminal user interface to browse and filter applications.

Intended users are job seekers pursuing technology roles who prefer a local-first, privacy-focused approach. Notable technologies used include Node.js, Playwright, Go, and the Agent Skill Standard.

name: anime
description: JavaScript animation engine
summary: Anime.js is a fast, multipurpose, and lightweight JavaScript animation library featuring a simple yet powerful API. It is designed to work with CSS properties, SVG, DOM attributes, and JavaScript Objects, allowing developers and designers to build complex animations using ES modules.

name: strapi
description: 🚀 Strapi is the leading open-source headless CMS. It’s 100% JavaScript/TypeScript, fully customizable, and developer-first.
summary:
Strapi is an open-source, self-hosted or cloud-managed headless Content Management System (CMS) built in JavaScript and TypeScript. It enables developers to rapidly build content APIs and provides content creators with a customizable editing interface and admin dashboard. 

Main capabilities include a visual Content-Type Builder, auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs for every content type, built-in Roles & Permissions, a Media Library, Internationalization (i18n), Draft & Publish workflows, and an AI layer for automated translations, media alt text, and content modeling. The backend architecture follows a request flow utilizing Routes, Middlewares, Controllers, and Services. Strapi supports flexible database options including SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB, and features an extensible plugin system.

Intended users are developers building frontends, mobile applications, or IoT devices, as well as content creators managing digital content. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript, TypeScript, REST, GraphQL, Node.js, and Docker.

name: AFFiNE
description: There can be more than Notion and Miro. AFFiNE(pronounced [ə‘fain]) is a next-gen knowledge base that brings planning, sorting and creating all together. Privacy first, open-source, customizable and ready to use.
summary:
AFFiNE is a privacy-focused, local-first, open-source all-in-one workspace and knowledge management platform designed as an alternative to Notion and Miro. It merges documents, visual whiteboards, presentations, and multi-view databases onto a single edgeless canvas where any building block—such as rich text, sticky notes, embedded web pages, and shapes—can be placed. 

Intended for wildly creative minds, developers, and teams, the platform includes AFFiNE AI to assist with writing, generating slides, converting outlines into mind maps, and drafting prototypes. Key capabilities include real-time collaboration across web and cross-platform clients, data ownership via local-first storage, and support for self-hosting. 

The project utilizes notable technologies such as TypeScript, React, Vite, Electron, Rust-backed components like OctoBase and y-octo, BlockSuite for the collaborative editor, and Yjs for CRDT-based state management and data synchronization.

name: codegraph
description: Pre-indexed code knowledge graph, auto syncs on code changes, for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, AntiGravity, Kiro, CoPilot, and Hermes Agent — fewer tokens, fewer tool calls, 100% local
summary:
CodeGraph is a 100% local, native Rust-powered semantic code intelligence tool designed to supercharge AI coding agents—including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Gemini, Antigravity, Kiro, and GitHub Copilot. 

### Project Purpose
The tool provides AI agents with surgical code context via a pre-built knowledge graph of symbols, call paths, imports, and dependencies. Instead of slow file-by-file exploration using grep and glob, agents use CodeGraph to access precise source snippets, call flows, and impact radii in a single tool call, significantly reducing tool calls, token usage, and latency.

### Main Capabilities
- **Surgical Context & Exploration:** Combines symbol definitions, call hierarchies, and blast-radius analysis into a single unified search (`codegraph_explore`).
- **Always Fresh Auto-Sync:** Uses native OS file events (FSEvents, inotify, ReadDirectoryChangesW) with debounced auto-sync to update the index incrementally as code changes.
- **Framework-Aware Routing:** Links URL patterns to their respective handler functions across 17 web frameworks (e.g., Django, FastAPI, Express, NestJS, Rails, Spring) and maps screen transitions for major routers (Expo Router, Next.js, React Router, TanStack Router, Vue Router, SvelteKit, Angular).
- **Cross-Language Bridging:** Connects static boundaries for mixed iOS and React Native/Expo codebases, including Swift-to-ObjC bridging, React Native legacy bridge and TurboModules, native event emitters, Expo Modules, and Fabric/Paper view components.
- **Full-Text Search & Analysis:** Powered by SQLite with FTS5, providing instant symbol searches, caller/callee tracing, impact analysis, and affected test detection (`codegraph affected`).

### Intended Users
Software engineers and AI-assisted development workflows looking to optimize multi-turn coding agent sessions across small to massive codebases.

### Notable Technologies
- **Kernel/Backend:** Rust (compiled parsing engine utilizing tree-sitter grammars).
- **Storage:** SQLite with FTS5 full-text search and WAL mode.
- **Supported Languages:** 20+ languages including TypeScript, JavaScript, ArkTS, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#, PHP, Ruby, C, C++, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Dart, Svelte, Vue, Astro,

name: OmniRoute
description: Never stop coding. Free MIT AI gateway: one endpoint, 359 providers (150+ free), 1200+ models Kimi, Claude, GPT, Gemini, GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Cline & Copilot. Quota-aware auto-fallback, RTK+Caveman compression saves 15-95% tokens, MCP/A2A, Desktop/PWA. Built by hundreds of contributors
summary:
OmniRoute is a free, self-hosted AI gateway that unifies access to 357 AI providers—including over 150 free tiers and 54 recurring keyless providers—through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/v1`). It features a 19-strategy routing engine with automated failover, built-in rate-limiting resilience, a circuit breaker, TLS stealth capabilities, and a 12-engine token compression pipeline (combining RTK and Caveman modes) that saves 15% to 95% of tokens. 

Designed for developers, teams, and AI coding agents, OmniRoute supports zero-config local execution across 36 developer tools and CLI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Aider, and OpenCode. It includes an embedded dashboard, 110 Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) server, int8-quantized persistent memory, prompt-injection guardrails, and cost telemetry. 

Built with TypeScript and Next.js, it operates locally-first using SQLite with WAL journaling and supports deployment via global npm installations, Docker images across AMD64 and ARM64 architectures, Bun runtimes, desktop applications via Electron, and Android environments using Termux.

name: Apollo-11
description: Original Apollo 11 Guidance Computer (AGC) source code for the command and lunar modules.
summary:
This repository provides the original, digitized Apollo 11 guidance computer (AGC) source code for the Command Module (Comanche055 / Colossus 2A) and the Lunar Module (Luminary099 / Luminary 1A). Transcribed from hardcopy scans provided by the MIT Museum and digitized by Virtual AGC contributors, the project serves as a centralized archive for the historical source code. 

The software was originally prepared by the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory under NASA sponsorship for the Apollo Guidance and Navigation program, with contributions from key figures such as Margaret Hamilton. The codebase relies on the `yaYUL` assembler and can be compiled using the Virtual AGC toolset. The repository welcomes contributions and corrections to match the original source scans.

name: reveal.js
description: The HTML Presentation Framework
summary: reveal.js is an open-source HTML presentation framework that enables users to create web-based presentations using a standard web browser. Designed for developers, speakers, and educators, it offers a powerful feature set including nested slides, Markdown support, Auto-Animate, PDF export, speaker notes, LaTeX typesetting, syntax-highlighted code, and an extensive JavaScript API. The framework is distributed under the MIT license.

name: act
description: Run your GitHub Actions locally 🚀
summary:
Act (`nektos/act`) is a command-line tool that enables developers to run GitHub Actions locally, providing fast feedback for workflow modifications and serving as a local task runner to replace traditional Makefiles. The project is intended for developers working with GitHub Actions who want to test `.github/workflows/` configurations without committing and pushing changes to remote repositories. 

The tool reads GitHub Actions defined in the project structure, determines dependencies and execution paths, and uses the Docker API to pull or build required images and execute containers that replicate GitHub-hosted runner environments, including filesystems and environment variables. Additionally, it integrates with Visual Studio Code via the GitHub Local Actions extension. Implemented in Go (requiring Go 1.20+), `act` utilizes standard Go tooling and a Makefile for building, testing, and installation.

name: moby
description: The Moby Project - a collaborative project for the container ecosystem to assemble container-based systems
summary:
The Moby Project is an open-source initiative created by Docker to enable and accelerate software containerization. It provides a modular toolkit framework and components—such as container build tools, a registry, orchestration tools, and a runtime—to assemble custom container-based systems like Docker Engine. 

Designed for developers, engineers, system integrators, and container enthusiasts, Moby serves as an upstream codebase and experimental sandbox rather than a commercially supported end-user product. The project is guided by principles of modularity, swappable components, usable security, and developer-focused APIs. 

Built using Go, the repository exposes public Go modules including `github.com/moby/moby/client` (a Go client for the Docker Engine API), `github.com/moby/moby/api` (shared API types), and the root module `github.com/moby/moby/v2` used for building container engines.

name: protobuf
description: Protocol Buffers - Google's data interchange format
summary:
Protocol Buffers (protobuf) is Google's language-neutral, platform-neutral, and extensible mechanism for serializing structured data. The project provides a protocol compiler (`protoc`) written in C++ along with language-specific runtimes. It is intended for developers needing efficient data interchange and serialization across systems. 

Main capabilities include compiling `.proto` interface definition files and running serialization libraries across multiple supported languages. Intended users include software developers building multi-language or distributed systems. Notable technologies and languages supported include C++, Java, Python, Objective-C, C#, Ruby, Go, PHP, Dart, JavaScript, Bazel (with Bzlmod and WORKSPACE support), and Maven.

name: daytona
description: Daytona is a Secure and Elastic Infrastructure for Running AI-Generated Code
summary:
Daytona is a secure and elastic infrastructure runtime platform designed for executing AI-generated code and agent workflows. It provides isolated sandboxes—composable virtual environments featuring dedicated kernels, filesystems, network stacks, and allocated resources—that spin up rapidly and support Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript execution. 

Targeting developers and AI agents, the platform offers programmatic tools via SDKs, an API, and a CLI for lifecycle management, filesystem operations, code execution, and environment configuration using Docker/OCI compatibility, snapshots, and volumes. Daytona's architecture consists of an interface plane, control plane, and compute plane. It supplies client libraries and package ecosystems for Python, TypeScript, Ruby, Go, and Java. Notable system capabilities include organization governance, audit logs, OpenTelemetry integration, webhooks, and network controls. 

*Note: Core development moved to a private codebase in June 2026, and this public repository is no longer maintained.*

name: awesome-courses
description: :books: List of awesome university courses for learning Computer Science!
summary:
Awesome CS Courses is a curated list of computer science courses from various universities that offer free online materials such as lectures, notes, assignments, and exams. The project aims to make high-quality educational content accessible to self-learners, students, and educators. 

The repository covers a broad spectrum of computer science topics, including algorithms, artificial intelligence, computer graphics, computer science theory, introductory programming, machine learning, security, systems, programming languages, and compilers. Notable technologies and languages frequently utilized across the listed courses include Python, C, C++, Java, OCaml, Haskell, Racket, Go, Rust, TensorFlow, Torch, and CUDA.

name: gpt_academic
description: 为GPT/GLM等LLM大语言模型提供实用化交互接口，特别优化论文阅读/润色/写作体验，模块化设计，支持自定义快捷按钮&函数插件，支持Python和C++等项目剖析&自译解功能，PDF/LaTex论文翻译&总结功能，支持并行问询多种LLM模型，支持chatglm3等本地模型。接入通义千问, deepseekcoder, 讯飞星火, 文心一言, llama2, rwkv, claude2, moss等。
summary:
GPT Academic (GPT 学术优化) is an open-source web interface and modular extension project designed to assist researchers, developers, and students in interacting with Large Language Models (LLMs) for academic writing, translation, programming, and documentation analysis. 

Its main capabilities include multi-model support (such as OpenAI GPT-3.5/GPT-4, Azure, Baidu Wenxin Yiyan, Tongyi Qianwen Qwen, Zhipu GLM, DeepSeekCoder, and local models like ChatGLM and MOSS), specialized LaTeX and Arxiv paper translation and proofreading, project source code analysis and comment generation, Mermaid diagram rendering, real-time voice dialogue input, and custom hotkeys/plugins. The project supports modular function plugins via `functional.py` and offers deployment options through Docker, pip, and conda.

name: OpenSpec
description: Spec-driven development (SDD) for AI coding assistants.
summary:
OpenSpec is an open-source specification framework designed to add a lightweight planning and requirements layer for AI coding assistants. It helps solo developers and teams align on project goals, requirements, technical design, and implementation tasks in plain Markdown before writing code. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Artifact-guided workflows supporting interactive exploration (`/opsx:explore`), feature proposals (`/opsx:propose`), and implementation tasks using slash commands.
- Support for cross-repo features and shared specifications via separate planning repositories called **Stores** (beta).
- Compatibility with over 30 AI assistants, including Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q, and Codex.
- Built-in commands for initialization, configuration updates, and task management.

**Intended Users:**
Developers and teams utilizing AI coding assistants who want to maintain predictability, context hygiene, and structured planning without rigid waterfall phase gates or complex setup procedures.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Node.js (v20.19.0 or higher)
- npm and Homebrew packaging
- Markdown for specs, proposals, designs, and tasks

name: ansible
description: Ansible is a radically simple IT automation platform that makes your applications and systems easier to deploy and maintain. Automate everything from code deployment to network configuration to cloud management, in a language that approaches plain English, using SSH, with no agents to install on remote systems. https://docs.ansible.com.
summary:
Ansible is an IT automation system designed for configuration management, application deployment, cloud provisioning, ad-hoc task execution, network automation, and multi-node orchestration. It enables complex operations such as zero-downtime rolling updates with load balancers. 

Its design principles emphasize an extremely simple setup process with a minimal learning curve, parallel machine management, and an agentless architecture that leverages the existing SSH daemon without requiring custom agents or additional open ports. It uses a machine- and human-friendly language to describe infrastructure, focuses on security and easy auditability, supports immediate management of new remote machines without bootstrapping software, allows module development in any dynamic language alongside Python, and can be used as a non-root user. 

Intended for system administrators, developers, and IT operations teams, Ansible is installed via pip or package managers and managed through communities and documentation. Notable technologies and components associated with the project include Python, SSH, and `ansible-core`. Created by Michael DeHaan and sponsored by Red Hat, Inc., the project is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

name: MetaGPT
description: 🌟 The Multi-Agent Framework: First AI Software Company, Towards Natural Language Programming
summary:
MetaGPT is a multi-agent framework that assigns different roles to Large Language Models (LLMs)—such as product managers, architects, project managers, and engineers—to form a collaborative software company entity. Guided by the core philosophy `Code = SOP(Team)`, the project materializes Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs) to handle complex tasks. Taking a one-line requirement as input, MetaGPT automates the entire software development process, producing user stories, competitive analysis, requirements, data structures, APIs, documentation, and complete code repositories. 

The framework is intended for developers, researchers, and users seeking to leverage AI agent teams for software engineering, data analysis via components like the Data Interpreter, and automated workflows. Notable technologies and integrations utilized include Python, Node.js, pnpm, and support for various LLM backends such as OpenAI, Azure, Ollama, and Groq.

name: swift
description: The Swift Programming Language
summary: Swift is a high-performance system programming language featuring a clean, modern syntax, memory safety by default, and seamless access to existing C and Objective-C code and frameworks. As an independent language, Swift packages core features like flow control, data structures, and functions alongside high-level constructs including objects, protocols, closures, and generics, while embracing modules to eliminate headers and code duplication. Intended for developers and contributors building software, compilers, and toolchains, the repository includes utilities like the `build-toolchain` script supporting options such as `--dry-run`, `--test`, `--distcc`, and `--sccache` for local builds and Xcode integration.

name: cline
description: Autonomous coding agent as an SDK, IDE extension, or CLI assistant.
summary:
Cline is an open-source coding agent and AI assistant available across IDEs, the terminal, and as a desktop app. Designed for developers and engineers, it reads project structures, edits codebases, executes bash commands, monitors compilation and test errors, and operates through human-in-the-loop approvals or autonomous execution modes. 

The project provides multiple interfaces and integration surfaces, including a CLI (supporting interactive or headless CI/CD operations), native macOS and Windows desktop apps, a VS Code extension, a JetBrains plugin, and a Node.js SDK for building custom agents and integrations. It supports project-specific rules via `.clinerules`, multi-agent teams, scheduled cron-based tasks, messaging platform connectors (such as Slack, Telegram, and Discord), and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. 

Cline is model-agnostic, working with major AI providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, Azure, GCP Vertex, local models via Ollama or LM Studio, and other OpenAI-compatible APIs. Technologies used in the repository structure include Tauri, Bun, and Next.js.

name: oh-my-openagent
description: OmO: Just type "mass ulw" keyword with your prompt. Now you are the master of graph engineering.
summary:
OmO is an AI agent tool designed to perform complex work such as codebase development, multi-source research, and full-stack engineering tasks. It runs on a fork of `pi` (`senpi`) and allows users to accomplish large projects through natural language prompts. 

Key capabilities include:
- **Ultrawork (`ulw` / `mass ulw`)**: Executes automated workflows where multiple agents operate in parallel on graph-engineered tasks, performing deep research, planning, step-by-step verification, and execution.
- **Kibitzer Memory System**: Retains context across sessions using a git repository of markdown files alongside a background assistant model to prevent repeated mistakes.
- **Multi-Model Support**: Integrates frontier and budget models with provider subscriptions (including Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi, and GLM) and automatically routes tasks to appropriate models.
- **Built-in Skills**: Extends model capabilities with specialized tools, including browser use and computer use features.

Intended users include developers, quantitative researchers, and professionals seeking end-to-end automated agent execution. Notable technologies mentioned include Bun, Node.js, and Markdown-based memory tracking.

name: express
description: Fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for node.
summary:
Express is a fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework designed for Node.js. Its primary purpose is to provide small, robust tooling for building HTTP servers, single-page applications, websites, hybrid apps, and public HTTP APIs. 

Main capabilities include robust routing, high performance, HTTP helper utilities (such as redirection and caching), content negotiation, a view system supporting over 14 template engines via packages like `@ladjs/consolidate`, and an executable generator (`express-generator`) for quickly bootstrapping applications. 

The framework is intended for developers building backend services and web applications with Node.js. Notable technologies used include Node.js (requires version 18 or higher) and npm for package management.

name: AI-For-Beginners
description: 12 Weeks, 24 Lessons, AI for All!
summary:
This repository provides a 12-week, 24-lesson beginner-friendly curriculum exploring Artificial Intelligence. The project purpose is to guide students through foundational and modern AI concepts using practical lessons, quizzes, labs, and executable Jupyter Notebooks. 

Main capabilities include covering symbolic AI (Knowledge Representation and Expert Systems), neural networks and deep learning, computer vision (OpenCV, Convolutional Neural Networks, Transfer Learning, GANs, object detection, and semantic segmentation), natural language processing (embeddings, RNNs, transformers, BERT, and Large Language Models), genetic algorithms, deep reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems, and AI ethics. 

The intended users are beginners, educators, and students seeking a structured educational resource to learn AI development. Notable technologies and frameworks utilized throughout the curriculum include TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, and OpenCV.

name: Mole
description: 🐹 Clean, uninstall, analyze, optimize, and monitor your Mac. Free open-source CLI, plus a native Mac app.
summary:
Mole is a free, open-source command-line tool (with a companion native macOS app available separately) designed to clean, uninstall, analyze, optimize, and monitor macOS systems. It functions as an all-in-one terminal binary that combines workflows similar to CleanMyMac, AppCleaner, DaisyDisk, and iStat Menus.

Main capabilities include:
- **Deep Cleaning**: Reclaims disk space by removing safe caches, logs, temporary files, developer artifacts, and leftovers from uninstalled apps.
- **Smart Uninstallation**: Removes applications alongside associated hidden remnants, preferences, and launch agents.
- **Disk Analysis**: Offers an interactive terminal disk explorer with support for vim/arrow navigation, filtering, multi-selection, file size inspection, and Finder previews.
- **System Optimization**: Performs bounded maintenance tasks on Finder, Spotlight, DNS caches, databases, and network services.
- **Project Purging**: Locates and removes rebuildable project build artifacts (such as `node_modules`, `target`, `.build`, and `dist`) while protecting Git repositories and recent work.
- **Installer Management**: Finds and removes installer files (including DMG, PKG, MPKG, ISO, XIP, and ZIP archives) from common download and cache locations.
- **Live Monitoring**: Provides real-time status dashboards for hardware health, CPU, memory, disk activity, network traffic, thermals, and processes.

Intended for macOS users (supporting both Intel and Apple Silicon running macOS 12 or newer), the CLI can be installed via Homebrew (`brew install mole`) or a shell script. Notable technologies and tools referenced include Homebrew, `fd`, `find`, JSON, NDJSON, Raycast, and Alfred.

name: system_prompts_leaks
description: Documented system prompts from Anthropic - Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Claude Design, Claude Code. OpenAI - ChatGPT GPT-6-Astra, Codex. Google - Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.1 Pro, Antigravity. xAI - Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor, Kimi and more! Updated regularly.
summary: System Prompts Leaks is a curated collection of verbatim system prompts from popular AI chatbots, language models, and developer coding tools worldwide. The repository provides researchers, developers, and AI enthusiasts with access to the underlying instructions, guidelines, and configurations used by platforms such as OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, xAI Grok, Meta Muse, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Qwen, Microsoft Copilot, and various other assistants and CLI agents.

name: ripgrep
description: ripgrep recursively searches directories for a regex pattern while respecting your gitignore
summary:
ripgrep (`rg`) is a line-oriented command-line search tool written in Rust that recursively searches directories for regular expression patterns. Designed for developers and system users on Windows, macOS, and Linux, it serves as a fast alternative to tools like grep, The Silver Searcher, and ack. 

Key capabilities include automatic recursive searching, ignoring files based on `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` rules, and skipping hidden and binary files by default. It supports full Unicode searches, file type filtering, context display, compressed file searching (such as gzip, xz, and zst), non-UTF-8 text encodings, input preprocessing filters, and rudimentary search-and-replace functionality. It also features optional PCRE2 integration for advanced regex capabilities like look-around and backreferences. 

ripgrep achieves high performance through Rust’s regex engine, which utilizes finite automata, SIMD optimizations, and aggressive literal searching. It additionally employs a lock-free parallel recursive directory iterator and matches path ignore patterns via `RegexSet`.

name: openinterpreter
description: A coding agent for open models like Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3
summary:
Open Interpreter is a coding agent built in Rust and optimized for low-cost models, operating as a fork of OpenAI's Codex. It allows users to execute native commands across macOS, Linux, and Windows, switch between various model providers and Rust-native model harnesses (such as native, claude-code, zcode, kimi-code, and deepseek-tui), and test web and native applications through a built-in QA skill that utilizes agent-browser and trycua. 

The project is intended for developers and users seeking a portable, tool-neutral coding assistant. It supports the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) for compatible editors, implements the Codex exec protocol, integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP), and uses shared configurations like AGENTS.md and .agents/skills directories. Notable capabilities include running OpenAI-compatible providers through Chat Completions, native sandboxing, hooks, permissions, and command-line interactions via a terminal UI (TUI). Distributed under the Apache-2.0 license, it provides binary overrides for existing Codex SDK workflows and local streaming web chat options.

name: vaultwarden
description: Unofficial Bitwarden compatible server written in Rust, formerly known as bitwarden_rs
summary:
Vaultwarden is an alternative server implementation of the Bitwarden Client API written in Rust. It is designed for self-hosted deployments where running the official resource-heavy service may be impractical, serving individuals, families, and small organizations. 

The project provides a nearly complete implementation of the Bitwarden API, including support for personal vaults, Send features, file attachments, website icons, personal API keys, organizations with collections, password sharing, member roles, groups, event logs, admin password resets, directory connectors, policies, multi-factor authentication methods (Authenticator, Email, FIDO2 WebAuthn, YubiKey, and Duo), emergency access, a dedicated admin backend, and a bundled, modified web vault client. 

Vaultwarden is built upon the Rocket web framework and is distributed primarily via container images on GitHub Container Registry, Docker Hub, and Quay.io, alongside community-driven packages and manual binary builds.

name: node
description: Everything required to run your own Base node
summary:
Base Node provides a Docker build for running a Base node—a secure, low-cost Ethereum L2 built on Optimism's OP Stack. The project's main purpose is to enable developers and node operators to run and configure Base nodes for both mainnet and testnet environments using Docker Compose. 

Main capabilities include supporting mainnet and Sepolia testnet configurations, utilizing snapshots for faster syncing, supporting Flashblocks mode via WebSocket, and offering optional pruning and follow modes. The repository supports `base-reth-node` as the execution client and `base-consensus` as the consensus client. 

Intended users are developers and infrastructure operators looking to run, configure, and maintain Base network nodes. Notable technologies and tools utilized include Docker, Docker Compose, `base-reth-node`, `base-consensus`, Ethereum L1 RPC and beacon endpoints, and Optimism's OP Stack. 

*Note: This repository is archived; development and releases have moved to `base/base`.*

name: docling
description: Get your documents ready for gen AI
summary:
Docling is a document processing project designed to parse diverse file formats and provide advanced PDF understanding—including layout analysis, reading order, table structure, formulas, and OCR for scanned documents. It also supports audio, video, images, office suites, emails, and specialized schemas like XBRL and USPTO patents. 

Main capabilities include a unified representation format (`DoclingDocument`), exports to Markdown, HTML, JSON, and DocTags, local air-gapped execution, a CLI, an API server (`docling-serve`), an MCP server, and chart understanding. It features native plug-and-play integrations with generative AI and agent frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, and Haystack, alongside support for Visual Language Models (e.g., GraniteDocling) and Automatic Speech Recognition models. 

Intended for developers and researchers building AI applications, data pipelines, and intelligent document processing workflows, Docling utilizes technologies like Python, Pydantic, and various machine learning models.

name: uBlock
description: uBlock Origin - An efficient blocker for Chromium and Firefox. Fast and lean.
summary:
uBlock Origin (uBO) is a CPU- and memory-efficient wide-spectrum content blocker designed for browsers such as Firefox and Chromium-based applications. Its primary purpose is to help users neutralize privacy-invading methods by blocking ads, trackers, coin miners, popups, malware sites, and anti-blockers. 

The project's main capabilities include an install-and-forget basic mode with an optimal default configuration, alongside an advanced mode featuring a point-and-click dynamic filtering firewall configurable on a per-site basis. It natively utilizes default filter lists like EasyList, EasyPrivacy, Peter Lowe's Blocklist, Online Malicious URL Blocklist, and uBO filter lists, while supporting custom rules, extended filter syntax, and hosts files. 

Intended for general web users seeking enhanced privacy and performance without technical hurdles, uBO is distributed as a free, open-source browser extension governed by the GPLv3 license. It is available across platforms including Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Opera, and Thunderbird.

name: Chart.js
description: Simple HTML5 Charts using the <canvas> tag
summary: Chart.js is a simple yet flexible JavaScript charting library designed for developers and designers. It provides tools to create various chart types, configure general options, customize axes, and utilize popular extensions. The project is distributed under the MIT license.

name: annotated_deep_learning_paper_implementations
description: 🧑‍🏫 60+ Implementations/tutorials of deep learning papers with side-by-side notes 📝; including transformers (original, xl, switch, feedback, vit, ...), optimizers (adam, adabelief, sophia, ...), gans(cyclegan, stylegan2, ...), 🎮 reinforcement learning (ppo, dqn), capsnet, distillation, ... 🧠
summary:
The labml.ai Deep Learning Paper Implementations repository provides a collection of simple, documented PyTorch implementations of neural networks and related algorithms. Its purpose is to help users understand complex machine learning concepts through clear code and side-by-side formatted notes hosted on its companion website. 

The main capabilities span a wide range of deep learning domains, including Transformers (such as GPT architectures, Vision Transformer, Flash Attention, and JAX implementations), Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), Eleuther GPT-NeoX utilities, Diffusion models (including Stable Diffusion and DDPM), Generative Adversarial Networks (StyleGAN2, CycleGAN), Reinforcement Learning (PPO, DQN), Graph Neural Networks, and Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR). It also covers core neural network components like optimizers, normalization layers, LSTMs, ResNets, U-Net, and language model sampling techniques. 

Intended users are researchers, students, and practitioners seeking clear, educational code implementations of modern deep learning papers. Notable technologies utilized include PyTorch, JAX, and Triton.

name: scikit-learn
description: scikit-learn: machine learning in Python
summary:
**scikit-learn** is a Python module for machine learning built on top of SciPy and distributed under the 3-Clause BSD license. Originally started in 2007 by David Cournapeau as a Google Summer of Code project, it is maintained by a community of volunteers and organizations. 

The project provides machine learning capabilities supported by core dependencies including Python, NumPy, SciPy, Narwhals, joblib, and threadpoolctl. Optional capabilities such as plotting and specific examples utilize Matplotlib, scikit-image, pandas, seaborn, and Plotly. Testing relies on pytest. 

Intended for developers, researchers, and data scientists looking to implement machine learning in Python, scikit-learn includes comprehensive documentation, installation methods via ``pip`` or ``conda``, and a structured contribution and testing workflow.

name: echarts
description: Apache ECharts is a powerful, interactive charting and data visualization library for browser
summary: Apache ECharts is a free, powerful charting and visualization library designed for adding intuitive, interactive, and highly customizable charts to commercial products. Written in pure JavaScript, the project is based on zrender, a lightweight canvas library. It is intended for developers and organizations seeking a declarative framework for the rapid construction of web-based visualizations. Notable capabilities include support for 3D plots, globe visualizations, WebGL acceleration via extensions, and statistical tools. Technologies used include JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, and HTML5 Canvas.

name: design-resources-for-developers

summary: This repository is a curated directory of web design and development resources, tools, and assets. It provides a comprehensive categorized collection covering UI graphics, fonts, color tools, icons, logos, favicons, stock photos, videos, music, vectors, mockups, HTML/CSS templates, CSS frameworks, animations, charting libraries, and UI component kits for frameworks like React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, and React Native. name: claude-code-best-practice

name: gpt4free

GPT4Free (g4f) is a community-driven project created by @xtekky and maintained by @hlohaus that aggregates multiple accessible providers and interfaces to streamline working with modern LLMs and media-generation models. It supports text completions, tool-calling patterns, local inference backends, and media generation (image, audio, and video) via various provider adapters such as PerplexityLabs, Gemini, MetaAI, and Pollinations. 

Intended for developers, researchers, and users seeking flexible, multi-provider AI tooling, GPT4Free can be installed via PyPI, source, Windows executables, or containerized deployments using full and slim Docker images. Notable technologies and frameworks utilized include Python, FastAPI, Docker, and JavaScript.

name: anything-llm
description: Stop renting your intelligence. Own it with AnythingLLM. Everything you need for a powerful local-first agent experience
summary:
AnythingLLM is an all-in-one, private AI application designed for chatting with documents, automating complex workflows with AI Agents, and building custom ChatGPT experiences. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Document ingestion and chatting with source citations (supporting PDF, TXT, DOCX, etc.).
- No-code AI agent building, MCP-compatibility, scheduled tasks, and intelligent skill/tool selection.
- Multi-user instance support with role-based permissions and workspace access control.
- Dynamic model routing, automatic/user-managed memories, and embeddable web chat widgets.
- Extensive integrations supporting dozens of closed and open-source LLMs, embedder models, audio transcription, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and vector databases.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, teams, and organizations seeking a customizable, private, multi-user AI workspace that connects to local or cloud LLMs with minimal setup.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Frontend: ViteJS, React.
- Server & Collector: NodeJS, Express.
- Vector Databases: LanceDB, PGVector, Astra DB, Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, Zilliz.
- Deployment: Docker, AWS, GCP, DigitalOcean, Render, Railway, and various cloud platforms.

name: 33-js-concepts
description: 📜 33 JavaScript concepts every developer should know.
summary:
This project helps JavaScript developers master core language and web platform concepts, ranging from fundamental types and asynchronous programming to advanced performance optimization and browser storage APIs. 

**Project Purpose:** To provide a comprehensive, structured guide—hosted via a dedicated website—with clear explanations, practical code examples, and curated resources for learning JavaScript deeply.

**Main Capabilities:** The guide covers an extensive list of topics categorized into Fundamentals, Functions and Execution, the Web Platform, Object-Oriented JavaScript, Asynchronous JavaScript, Functional Programming, Advanced Topics, Language Mechanics, Memory and Performance, Browser Storage, Observer APIs, and Data Handling. 

**Intended Users:** JavaScript developers at various experience levels looking to solidify their technical foundations, prepare for technical interviews, or deepen their understanding of JavaScript mechanics and internals.

**Notable Technologies:** JavaScript (ES6+), V8 engine, HTML DOM, Fetch API, Web Workers, IndexedDB, and various browser Observer and Storage APIs.

name: mem0
description: The Memory Layer for AI Agents - Drop-in memory infrastructure for AI agents and apps. Context that persists. Built for production.
summary:
Mem0 is an intelligent memory layer designed for AI assistants and autonomous agents to provide personalized interactions and long-term context retention. It features a memory algorithm utilizing single-pass extraction, entity linking, multi-signal retrieval, and temporal reasoning to remember user preferences and adapt over time.

Intended users include developers building AI applications, customer support chatbots, healthcare systems, productivity tools, and gaming environments. Notable capabilities include multi-level memory tracking for users, sessions, and agents, alongside hybrid search combining semantic, BM25 keyword, and entity matching. 

Mem0 provides cross-platform SDKs in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript (`mem0ai`), a command-line interface (`@mem0/cli`), a self-hosted Docker server option, and a fully managed cloud platform. It integrates with frameworks such as LangGraph and CrewAI, supports vector databases like Qdrant, and utilizes large language models and embedding models such as OpenAI's `gpt-5-mini` and `text-embedding-3-small`.

name: ladybird
description: Truly independent web browser
summary:
Ladybird is an independent web browser utilizing a novel engine built on web standards, currently in a pre-alpha state suitable for developers. It targets Linux, macOS, Windows via WSL2, and various \*Nix systems. 

The project features a multi-process architecture comprising a main UI process, sandboxed WebContent renderer processes for each tab, an ImageDecoder process, and a RequestServer process to isolate network connections and image decoding from malicious content. Ladybird relies on core library components inherited from SerenityOS, including the LibWeb rendering engine, LibJS JavaScript engine, LibWasm WebAssembly implementation, LibCrypto and LibTLS for cryptography and TLS, LibHTTP, LibGfx 2D graphics and image decoding, LibUnicode, LibMedia for audio and video playback, LibCore event loop and OS abstraction, and LibIPC for inter-process communication.

name: docusaurus
description: Easy to maintain open source documentation websites.
summary: Docusaurus is a project designed for building, deploying, and maintaining open-source project websites easily. Its main capabilities include handling the website build process, supporting localizable documentation via CrowdIn, and providing customizable pages and sections such as home pages, documentation sections, blogs, and additional support pages. The project is intended for developers and organizations managing open-source projects or documentation sites. Notable technologies and tools referenced include npm, CrowdIn, and an initialization CLI (`npm init docusaurus@latest`).

name: prometheus
description: The Prometheus monitoring system and time series database.
summary:
Prometheus is a systems and service monitoring system that collects metrics from configured targets at given intervals, evaluates rule expressions, displays results, and triggers alerts when specified conditions occur. 

Main capabilities include a multi-dimensional data model defined by metric names and key/value dimensions, the PromQL query language, autonomous single server nodes without distributed storage dependencies, an HTTP pull model for time series collection, support for pushing time series via an intermediary gateway for batch jobs, service discovery or static configuration for targets, graphing and dashboard support, and hierarchical and horizontal federation. 

The project is intended for developers, system administrators, and organizations requiring cloud-native infrastructure monitoring. Notable technologies utilized include Go, NodeJS, npm, Docker, and React.

name: Java
description: All Algorithms implemented in Java
summary: The Algorithms - Java is an open-source repository providing implementations of various algorithms and data structures written in Java. The project serves educational and learning purposes, offering implementations that may be less efficient than the Java standard library. It is designed for students, developers, and programming enthusiasts looking to study or contribute to algorithmic concepts in Java.

name: strix
description: Open-source AI penetration testing tool to find and fix your app’s vulnerabilities.
summary:
Strix is an open-source autonomous AI penetration testing tool designed to find and validate security vulnerabilities in applications through dynamic testing and working proofs-of-concept. Built for developers and security teams, it features multi-agent orchestration (Graph of Agents) to automate reconnaissance, exploitation, and post-exploitation workflows, helping users secure codebases, web applications, APIs, and CI/CD pipelines. 

Key capabilities include an offensive security toolkit (such as an HTTP interception proxy via Caido, browser exploitation with Playwright, custom exploit sandboxes, and OSINT tools), automated vulnerability detection across the OWASP Top 10, real-time local web dashboards (`strix view`), and one-click remediation guidance. 

Intended users include developers, security engineers, and devsecops teams integrating security checks into GitHub Actions and other CI/CD pipelines. The software runs locally via Docker CLI, integrates with various LLM providers (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and DeepSeek via LiteLLM), supports custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and offers managed cloud and enterprise deployments.

name: MediaCrawler
description: 小红书笔记 | 评论爬虫、抖音视频 | 评论爬虫、快手视频 | 评论爬虫、B 站视频 ｜ 评论爬虫、微博帖子 ｜ 评论爬虫、百度贴吧帖子 ｜ 百度贴吧评论回复爬虫  | 知乎问答文章｜评论爬虫
summary:
MediaCrawler is an open-source multi-platform social media data collection tool designed for developers and researchers. It supports scraping public information, posts, and comments from mainstream platforms including Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Bilibili, Weibo, Baidu Tieba, and Zhihu. 

The project leverages Playwright for browser automation and session persistence, bypassing complex JavaScript reverse engineering by utilizing existing browser context login states to extract parameters. It supports keyword searches, specific post IDs, secondary comments, creator profiles, IP proxy pools, and media downloads, alongside providing multiple data storage formats like CSV, JSON, Excel, and MySQL. Users can interact with the project via a command-line interface or an integrated WebUI.

name: webpack
description: A bundler for javascript and friends. Packs many modules into a few bundled assets. Code Splitting allows for loading parts of the application on demand. Through "loaders", modules can be CommonJs, AMD, ES6 modules, CSS, Images, JSON, Coffeescript, LESS, ... and your custom stuff.
summary: Webpack is a static module bundler primarily designed to bundle JavaScript files for browser usage, while also capable of transforming, bundling, or packaging any resource or asset. Its main capabilities include supporting ES Modules, CommonJS, and AMD module formats, creating single or asynchronously loaded chunks via code splitting to reduce initial loading times, resolving dependencies at compile time, and utilizing loaders and a modular plugin system to preprocess various file types like TypeScript, styles, and templates. Webpack is intended for developers building web applications and tooling. Notable technologies and formats mentioned include Node.js, TypeScript, Babel, ES2015+, CommonJS, AMD, ES Modules, and the Tapable hook system.

name: alacritty
description: A cross-platform, OpenGL terminal emulator.
summary:
Alacritty is a modern, fast, cross-platform, GPU-accelerated terminal emulator designed for BSD, Linux, macOS, and Windows. Currently at a beta level of readiness, it provides high performance through integration with other applications rather than reimplementing their functionality, omitting features like tabs or splits in favor of window managers or terminal multiplexers like tmux. 

The project comes with sensible defaults while offering extensive configuration capabilities via TOML files. Notable technologies used include OpenGL (requiring at least OpenGL ES 2.0) and ConPTY support on Windows. Alacritty is released under the Apache License, Version 2.0, and utilizes vtebench for throughput benchmarking.

name: daily_stock_analysis
description: LLM 驱动的多市场股票智能分析系统：多源行情、实时新闻、决策看板与自动推送，支持零成本定时运行。  LLM-powered multi-market stock analysis system with multi-source market data, real-time news, decision dashboard, automated notifications, and cost-free scheduled runs.
summary:
The **股票智能分析系统 (daily_stock_analysis)** is an AI-powered smart stock analysis system designed to evaluate equities across multiple markets including A-shares, Hong Kong, US, Japanese, Korean, and Taiwanese stocks, alongside ETFs.

- **AI Decision Reports & Dashboards**: Generates structured core conclusions, ratings, trends, buy/sell points, risk alerts, and catalyst factors, pushing daily decision dashboards to platforms like WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, Discord, Slack, and email.
- **Multi-Market Data Aggregation**: Combines quotes, K-line charts, technical indicators, news, announcements, and fundamentals.

name: nocode
description: The best way to write secure and reliable applications. Write nothing; deploy nowhere.
summary: No Code is a satirical example application project based on the premise that the best way to write secure and reliable applications is to write nothing and deploy nowhere. The project humorously demonstrates building, deploying, and scaling an application without writing any code or performing any actions.

name: warp
description: Warp is an agentic development environment, born out of the terminal.
summary:
Warp is an agentic development environment originating from the terminal, featuring a built-in coding agent and supporting third-party CLI agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI. Its agentic management workflows are powered by GPT models, with OpenAI as the founding sponsor. The platform introduces Warp Factories, an infrastructure for teams to build cloud software factories with built-in evaluations, benchmarks, and self-improvement capabilities. The project provides dashboards to track issues, specs, implementations, and pull requests managed by agents. 

Targeting developers and software engineering teams, Warp provides a UI framework (`warpui_core` and `warpui` crates) licensed under the MIT license, while the rest of the client codebase is open-sourced under the AGPL v3 license. Notable technologies and dependencies utilized include Tokio, NuShell, Fig Completion Specs, Alacritty, Hyper, FontKit, Core-foundation, and Smol.

name: javascript-questions
description: A long list of (advanced) JavaScript questions, and their explanations :sparkles:
summary:
This repository contains a comprehensive collection of JavaScript interview questions, quizzes, and code challenges ranging from basic to advanced difficulty. The project is designed for developers looking to test, refresh, or expand their knowledge of JavaScript mechanics, syntax, behavior, and design patterns. 

The repository covers core language concepts such as variable scoping, hoisting, closures, event propagation, asynchronous programming (promises, async/await, event loops), prototypes, classes, type coercion, and built-in objects. Each question includes a code snippet, multiple-choice options, and a detailed explanation hidden inside a collapsed section. The project also provides community-contributed translations in over 20 languages.

Intended users include software engineers, frontend developers, and job seekers preparing for coding interviews. Technologies involved include standard vanilla JavaScript.

name: interviews
description: Everything you need to know to get the job.
summary:
This repository maintained by Kevin Naughton Jr. serves as a comprehensive coding interview preparation resource for software engineers. It provides an extensive collection of data structures, algorithms, runtime analyses, and practice problems implemented primarily in Java. 

The project covers foundational data structures—such as linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, tries, heaps, hash maps, and graphs—alongside major algorithmic techniques including sorting, graph traversal (DFS, BFS), Dijkstra's, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, Prim's, Kruskal's, greedy algorithms, and bit manipulation. It also outlines asymptotic complexity analysis using Big O, Little O, Big Omega, Little Omega, and Theta notations. 

Intended for software engineers and developers preparing for technical interviews, the repository organizes its resources alongside references to external online judges, mock interview platforms, video lectures from institutions like MIT and UC Berkeley, and recommended interview books.

name: nocodb
description: 🔥 🔥 🔥 A Free & Self-hostable Airtable Alternative
summary:
NocoDB is an open-source platform designed to build databases online quickly and easily, providing a powerful spreadsheet interface for underlying databases. 

Main capabilities include performing standard CRUD operations on tables, columns, and rows; filtering, sorting, grouping, and hiding columns; and utilizing multiple view types such as Grid, Gallery, Form, Kanban, and Calendar. It also features collaborative and locked views, public or password-protected sharing, diverse cell types (including Links, Lookup, Rollup, Attachments, and Formulas), and fine-grained role-based access control.
