Additionally, NocoDB includes an App Store for workflow integrations (such as Slack, Discord, AWS SES, and AWS S3) and offers programmatic access via REST APIs and a dedicated SDK.

Intended for developers, businesses, and spreadsheet users seeking to leverage database power without vendor lock-in, the project integrates with notable technologies like Docker, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, and Traefik.

name: localstack
description: 💻 A fully functional local AWS cloud stack. Develop and test your cloud & Serverless apps offline
summary:
LocalStack is a cloud software development framework and service emulator that enables developers to build, test, and run AWS applications and Lambdas locally on their machine or within CI environments. It emulates a wide range of AWS services—such as AWS Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, SQS, and SNS—allowing users to test complex CDK applications and Terraform configurations without a remote cloud connection. 

The project is intended for cloud developers and engineers seeking to streamline and accelerate local testing workflows. It is operated via the LocalStack CLI, Docker, Docker Compose, or Helm, and integrates with specialized tools like the `awslocal` CLI, LocalStack Desktop, and the LocalStack Docker Extension. Notable technologies used include Python, Docker, and various AWS APIs. 

*Note: This repository is now archived and read-only as development has been consolidated into a single, unified LocalStack image.*

name: traefik
description: The Cloud Native Application Proxy
summary:
Traefik is a modern HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer designed to simplify microservices deployment by automatically and dynamically configuring routes. It listens to service registries and orchestrator APIs to eliminate the need for manual route updates. 

Main capabilities include continuous live configuration updates, multiple load balancing algorithms, automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt with wildcard certificate support, circuit breakers, retries, a clean web UI, and support for WebSocket, HTTP/2, and gRPC. It also provides metrics (REST, Prometheus, Datadog, Statsd, InfluxDB 2.X), access logs in JSON or CLF, and exposes a REST API. Traefik supports backend integrations for Docker, Docker Swarm mode, Kubernetes, Amazon ECS, and file-based providers.

Intended users include developers, DevOps engineers, and system administrators deploying and managing containerized microservices and orchestrators. 

The project is implemented in Go, packaged as a single binary file, and also distributed as an official Docker image.

name: nerd-fonts
description: Iconic font aggregator, collection, & patcher. 3,600+ icons, 50+ patched fonts: Hack, Source Code Pro, more. Glyph collections: Font Awesome, Material Design Icons, Octicons, & more
summary:
Nerd Fonts is an iconic font aggregator, collection, and patcher designed for developers and technical users. The project purpose is to take popular programming and development-targeted fonts and inject a high number of extra glyphs and icons from iconic font sets such as Font Awesome, Devicons, Octicons, Material Design Icons, Weather Icons, and Powerline. 

Main capabilities include providing over 67 pre-patched font families containing more than 10,000 combined glyphs, along with an included Python-based font patcher script that allows users to patch their own custom fonts. The project supports generating monospaced, double-width, or proportional glyph variations. Intended users include software developers, terminal users, and system administrators looking for icon-rich programming typefaces. Notable technologies used to build and distribute the project include Python 3, FontForge, Docker, Homebrew, Chocolatey, Scoop, and PowerShell. Installation methods vary across multi-platform package managers, release archives, and installation scripts.

name: FFmpeg
description: Mirror of https://git.ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.git
summary:
FFmpeg is a collection of libraries and tools designed to process multimedia content, including audio, video, subtitles, and related metadata. 

The project includes several core libraries: `libavcodec` for codec implementations, `libavformat` for streaming protocols and container formats, `libavutil` for utility functions, hashers, and decompressors, `libavfilter` for altering decoded audio and video via filter graphs, `libavdevice` for capturing and playback device abstraction, `libswresample` for audio mixing and resampling, and `libswscale` for color conversion and scaling routines. 

It also provides command-line tools such as `ffmpeg` to manipulate, convert, and stream multimedia content, `ffplay` as a minimalistic multimedia player, `ffprobe` to inspect multimedia content, along with auxiliary tools like `aviocat`, `ismindex`, and `qt-faststart`. 

The codebase is primarily licensed under the LGPL with optional GPL components.

name: scrapy
description: Scrapy, a fast high-level web crawling & scraping framework for Python.
summary: Scrapy is a cross-platform web scraping framework designed to extract structured data from websites. Maintained by Zyte and numerous contributors, it requires Python 3.11+. The project provides tools for web crawling and data extraction, and can be installed via pip or conda.

name: get-shit-done
description: A light-weight and powerful meta-prompting, context engineering and spec-driven development system for Claude Code by TÂCHES.
summary: GSD is an archived repository that has moved and now continues as GSD Core in the Open GSD repository (https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core). The new repository serves as the active home for current source code, issues, releases, and contribution work.

name: keras
description: Deep Learning for humans
summary:
Keras 3 is a multi-backend deep learning framework designed for developers, researchers, and enterprises building accelerated machine learning models for computer vision, natural language processing, audio processing, timeseries forecasting, and recommender systems. 

It provides a high-level user experience that supports model training and inference across multiple backends, including JAX, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and OpenVINO (inference-only). Keras 3 enables developers to scale from laptops to GPU and TPU clusters while avoiding framework lock-in. It serves as a drop-in replacement for `tf.keras` when using the TensorFlow backend and is compatible with dataset pipelines such as `tf.data.Dataset` and PyTorch `DataLoaders`. 

Notable technologies include Python, JAX, TensorFlow, PyTorch, OpenVINO, CUDA, and modern GPU/TPU hardware.

name: rustlings
description: :crab: Small exercises to get you used to reading and writing Rust code!
summary: Rustlings is an educational project consisting of small exercises designed to help users get accustomed to reading and writing Rust code. It is officially recommended to be used in parallel with reading the official Rust book. The project's main capability is providing hands-on coding exercises for learners, intended for individuals learning the Rust programming language. It utilizes the Rust technology and provides setup information and a demo via its official website at rustlings.rust-lang.org.

name: ai-hedge-fund
description: An AI Hedge Fund Team
summary:
AI Hedge Fund is an educational proof-of-concept project that explores using artificial intelligence to make simulated trading decisions. It is designed for learners, researchers, and developers interested in AI-driven financial strategies. 

The project features an interactive terminal application (`aihf`) supporting two primary modes: paper trading with a hash-chained ledger and simulated fake money, and historical backtesting against a benchmark. Users configure funds with specific strategies, capital, cadences, and tickers, while maintaining control via an approval step before any simulated trade executes. The system utilizes the Financial Datasets API for market prices, fundamentals, and earnings, and integrates with major model providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, xAI, Kimi, and TypeSafe (Jev) to power its investor agents. 

Installation is supported via `pipx`, `uv`, or `pip`, with development managed using Poetry and tested with pytest. The software is provided strictly for learning and research purposes without any guarantees or real-trading capabilities.

name: tldr
description: Collaborative cheatsheets for console commands 📚.
summary:
The **tldr-pages** project is a community-maintained collection of simplified, practical help pages for command-line tools, serving as a more approachable complement to traditional man pages. It targets developers, system administrators, command-line beginners, and anyone looking for quick reminders of common command arguments through practical examples. 

The repository contains Markdown-based help pages covering tools across UNIX, Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, SunOS, Android, Windows, Cisco IOS, and DOS operating systems. Users can access these pages via various official clients written in Python, Rust, and Node.js, or through web clients, PDF exports, and community-provided integrations. Contributions are welcomed through the addition of new commands, translation efforts, and content improvements via GitHub pull requests.

name: openpilot
description: openpilot is an operating system for robotics. Currently, it upgrades the driver assistance system on 300+ supported cars.
summary:
openpilot is an operating system for robotics designed primarily to upgrade the driver assistance system in over 300 supported car models. Built by comma and open-source contributors, it functions as alpha-quality research software that integrates with hardware devices such as the comma four, comma 3X, and chestnut using a compatible car harness. 

The software interfaces with vehicle systems by logging road-facing cameras, CAN bus data, GPS, IMU, magnetometers, thermal sensors, and operating system logs, while driver-facing cameras and microphones require explicit opt-in. It adheres to ISO 26262 safety guidelines, with safety models implemented in C within the panda hardware. Testing methodologies include software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop test suites, Jenkins pipelines, and continuous route-replay testing. 

Intended for developers, automotive enthusiasts, and researchers, openpilot supports customizable installation channels ranging from stable release branches (such as `release-mici` and `release-tizi`) to experimental nightly and development branches.

name: winutil
description: Chris Titus Tech's Windows Utility - Install Programs, Tweaks, Fixes, and Updates
summary:
Chris Titus Tech's Windows Utility (WinUtil) is a PowerShell-based system administration tool designed to streamline software installations, system debloating via tweaks, troubleshooting configurations, and Windows update management on fresh or existing Windows installations. 

Intended for Windows users and power users, the utility supports automation and preset configurations—such as `Standard`, `Minimal`, and `Advanced`—to apply predefined system settings. It must be run with Administrator privileges via PowerShell or Terminal to execute system-wide changes.

name: git
description: Git Source Code Mirror - This is a publish-only repository but pull requests can be turned into patches to the mailing list via GitGitGadget (https://gitgitgadget.github.io/). Please follow Documentation/SubmittingPatches procedure for any of your improvements.
summary: Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system featuring an unusually rich command set that provides both high-level operations and full access to its internals. Originally written by Linus Torvalds with contributions from a global community of developers, Git is an open-source project covered by the GNU General Public License version 2. It is intended for software developers and engineers managing source code and project history. The project includes extensive documentation, tutorials, and migration guides for users transitioning from systems like CVS, as well as support for message string localization using Portable Object (PO) files.

name: nanoGPT
description: The simplest, fastest repository for training/finetuning medium-sized GPTs.
summary:
nanoGPT is a simple and fast repository for training and finetuning medium-sized GPT models, serving as a readable rewrite of minGPT. The project is designed for developers, researchers, and deep learning practitioners who want to train models from scratch or adapt pretrained checkpoints with minimal boilerplate. 

The core implementation consists of plain, accessible code: a training loop (`train.py`) and a GPT model definition (`model.py`), which can optionally load OpenAI's pretrained GPT-2 weights (supporting configurations from 124M up to 1.558B parameters). It supports single-GPU, multi-GPU via PyTorch Distributed Data Parallel (DDP), CPU, and Apple Silicon (MPS) execution. 

Key technologies used include Python, PyTorch (leveraging `torch.compile` for performance), NumPy, Hugging Face `transformers` and `datasets`, `tiktoken` for OpenAI's byte-pair encoding, `wandb` for logging, and `tqdm` for progress tracking. Notable capabilities include character-level training on custom datasets like Shakespeare, reproduction of GPT-2 on the OpenWebText dataset, domain adaptation finetuning, and text generation via inference sampling.

name: memos
description: A personal timeline for quick notes. Write short memos, find them later by search, tag, or date. Open source and self-hosted.
summary:
Memos is a self-hosted, open-source timeline application for capturing and sharing notes and thoughts. It is designed for individuals seeking data ownership and zero telemetry. 

Main capabilities include writing notes in Markdown without titles or folders, organizing via tags and timeline views, searching, pinning important entries, full data exports, and flexible sharing controls that allow memos to be kept private, shared with invited users, or made public. It also features a Web Clipper for Chrome and Firefox to save web pages, selections, and images directly into Memos as source-linked Markdown. 

Intended users are individuals wanting a private or selectively shared micro-blogging and note-taking system. Notable technologies used include Docker for deployment and Markdown for content authoring. The project is licensed under the MIT License.

name: v2rayNG
description: A V2Ray client for Android, support Xray core and v2fly core
summary: v2rayNG is an Android client supporting Xray core and v2fly core. Designed for mobile users, the application manages geoip.dat and geosite.dat files for routing and network configuration, and can run on Android emulators and Windows Subsystem for Android (WSA). The project is built using Kotlin and Gradle, integrates Go-based core components via AndroidLibV2rayLite and AndroidLibXrayLite, and can be compiled directly in Android Studio.

name: last30days-skill
description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary
summary:
/last30days is an AI agent-led search engine designed to aggregate and synthesize real-time data from community-driven platforms rather than traditional editorial sources. 

**Project Purpose:**
It bridges disparate platforms into a single research workflow, allowing users to uncover current community sentiments, trending discussions, and authentic engagement metrics from the past 30 days.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Searches multiple platforms in parallel, including Reddit, X (Twitter), YouTube, TikTok, Instagram Reels, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, arXiv, Techmeme, LinkedIn, Meta Ads, StockTwits, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky, and Perplexity.
- Extracts deep data such as full YouTube transcripts, top-voted Reddit comments, Polymarket prediction odds, and GitHub pull requests.
- Scores findings based on human engagement (upvotes, likes, financial backing, and view counts) rather than SEO or editor ranking.
- Generates synthesized briefs, structured JSON outputs, discovery briefs for trending topics, subscribable Atom feeds, static HTML pages, and local SQLite-backed trend watchlists.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, researchers, executives, creators, and professionals needing up-to-date, community-vetted insights for sales calls, meeting preparation, trend analysis, and tooling comparisons.

**Notable Technologies:**
Built using Python 3.12+, Node.js (vendored Bird client), `yt-dlp`, and the ScrapeCreators API. It integrates natively with AI harnesses and hosts including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Grok Build CLI, Claude Desktop, and OpenClaw via the Agent Skills specification.

name: drawio-desktop
description: Official electron build of draw.io
summary: drawio-desktop is a diagramming desktop application built on Electron that wraps the core draw.io editor. Designed for offline use and strong security isolation, the app operates entirely locally without sending diagram data or usage analytics externally, featuring a strict Content Security Policy that forbids remotely loaded JavaScript. It is available free of charge under the GPL v3 license for Windows (including native ARM64 and portable builds), macOS, and Linux platforms. The repository is primarily intended for running and packaging the application rather than accepting external code contributions.

name: socket.io
description: Bidirectional and low-latency communication for every platform
summary: Socket.IO is a JavaScript library designed for real-time, bidirectional, and event-based communication between web clients and servers. It enables low-latency communication across various platforms and devices.

name: minimind
description: 🧠 Train a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch in just 2h!
summary:
MiniMind is an open-source educational project designed to train a lightweight language model from scratch using minimal hardware and cost. Aimed at developers and AI learners seeking a bottom-up understanding of large language models, MiniMind implements a complete training and inference pipeline using native PyTorch without relying on high-level abstractions from third-party frameworks. 

The project purpose is to demystify LLM internals by providing code covering every stage: tokenizer creation, data cleaning, pretraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), LoRA, reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF including PPO, GRPO, and CISPO), DPO, tool use, agentic reinforcement learning, adaptive thinking, and model distillation. It features both dense Transformer architectures (aligned with Qwen3 ecosystem) and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants like minimind-3 and minimind-3-moe, with distinctive parameters ranging from 26M to nearly 200M. It also extends to visual modalities, diffusion language models, and linear attention models. Technologies utilized include PyTorch, Transformers, Llama-Factory, vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, llama.cpp, and SwanLab/WandB, alongside compatibility with OpenAI-compatible API servers and Streamlit WebUIs.

name: ai-engineering-from-scratch
description: Learn it. Build it. Ship it for others.
summary:
The AI Engineering from Scratch repository is a comprehensive, free, open-source reference manual and curriculum designed to teach artificial intelligence and AI engineering from first principles. It comprises 523 lessons across 20 phases spanning approximately 342 hours of study. 

The project's main capabilities include building core machine learning algorithms, deep learning networks, large language models (LLMs), multimodal systems, autonomous agents, and multi-agent swarms by hand before utilizing production libraries. Every lesson produces a reusable artifact such as a prompt, skill, agent, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. 

Intended users range from beginners seeking a complete technical foundation to software engineers and ML practitioners aiming to master production LLM applications, agent engineering, and infrastructure.

Notable technologies and frameworks used throughout the repository include Python, TypeScript, Rust, Julia, PyTorch, JAX, Docker, Model Context Protocol (MCP), OpenTelemetry, and agent SDKs such as LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen.

name: Magisk
description: The Magic Mask for Android
summary:
Magisk is an open-source suite of software for customizing Android devices running Android 6.0 and higher. Its purpose is to provide advanced system-level control and modification capabilities for Android users and developers. 

The project's main capabilities include:
- **MagiskSU**: Delivers root access for applications.
- **Magisk Modules**: Modifies read-only partitions through installable modules.
- **MagiskBoot**: Unpacks and repacks Android boot images.
- **Zygisk**: Executes custom code within every Android application process.

Magisk is distributed under the GNU General Public License version 3 as free software.

name: astro
description: The web framework for content-driven websites. ⭐️ Star to support our work!
summary: Astro is a website build tool designed for the modern web, combining a powerful developer experience with lightweight output. It is intended for web developers looking to build performant sites. The project provides packages and integrations for various technologies and frameworks, including React, Preact, Solid.js, Svelte, Vue, Alpine.js, MDX, Node.js, Vercel, Cloudflare, Netlify, Partytown, and sitemaps, alongside language tools for TypeScript and VS Code.

name: awesome-chatgpt-prompts-zh
description: ChatGPT 中文调教指南。各种场景使用指南。学习怎么让它听你的话。
summary:
This repository provides a comprehensive collection of Chinese prompts and system instructions designed to tune, guide, and extend the capabilities of large language models like ChatGPT. It serves as a Chinese adaptation and expansion of the popular `awesome-chatgpt-prompts` project.

The project's purpose is to help users interact with AI models more effectively across a wide variety of domains and creative personas. It features numerous categorized prompt templates for academic writing, creative storytelling, technical documentation, programming assistance, translation, data analysis, marketing, role-playing, and interactive gaming. 

Intended users include general users, students, researchers, developers, content creators, and professionals seeking to leverage AI for productivity, education, software development, and specialized tasks. The repository also includes specialized utility prompts, such as regex generators, SQL query optimizers, terminal emulators, and Midjourney image generation helpers, as well as pointers to a Chinese text corpus designed for training and fine-tuning large language models using technologies like Python and R.

name: resume.github.com
description: Resumes generated using the GitHub informations
summary: GitHub Résumé is an opt-in web service that generates professional résumés based on a user's GitHub repositories and activity. Designed for tech-savvy hiring managers and employers, it provides a quick, pre-interview overview of a candidate's development work. Users make their résumé visible by starring the project repository and can view it via a personalized URL on the service's website. The application is built using Ruby and requires the rack gem, running locally in development mode via `rackup config.ru`.

name: OpenMontage
description: World's first open-source, agentic video production system. 12 production pipelines, 100+ tools, 700+ agent skill and production-knowledge files. Turn your AI coding assistant into a full video production studio.
summary:
OpenMontage is an open-source, agentic video production system designed to turn an AI coding assistant (such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or Codex) into a full-scale video production studio. 

**Project Purpose:**
The platform automates end-to-end video creation from plain-language user descriptions or reference videos. It manages live web research, scriptwriting, voice direction, asset generation, music selection, editing, and final composition while maintaining human-in-the-loop approval gates via a local dashboard called Backlot.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **10+ Production Pipelines:** Supports animated explainers, motion graphics, cinematic trailers, clip factories, documentary montages, hybrid videos, localization/dubbing, podcast repurposing, screen demos, and talking heads.
- **Dual Creation Paths:** Operates via cloud/local AI generation or free retrieval-first workflows using actual motion footage from open archives (Archive.org, NASA, Wikimedia Commons) and stock providers (Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay).
- **Quality Governance:** Features pre-compose validation, slideshow risk scoring, post-render self-review (ffprobe, frame sampling, audio analysis), and a scored provider selection engine that evaluates options across 7 dimensions.
- **Budget Control:** Offers pre-execution cost estimation, spend caps, and per-action confirmation thresholds.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, creators, and production teams seeking automated, pipeline-driven video generation without vendor lock-in.

**Notable Technologies:**
- **Runtimes & Rendering:** Remotion (React-based) and HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP) for dynamic visual composition, alongside FFmpeg for core media post-processing.
- **Languages & Frameworks:** Python (core orchestration and tools) and Node.js.
- **Providers & Integrations:** Integrates with Kling, Seedance (Volcengine Ark), Runway, Google Veo, Grok, MiniMax, FLUX, Google Imagen, ElevenLabs, Suno AI, Piper TTS, and local GPU models (WAN 2.1/2.2, Hunyuan, CogVideo, LTX-Video).

name: TrendRadar
description: ⭐AI-driven public opinion & trend monitor with multi-platform aggregation, RSS, and smart alerts.🎯 告别信息过载，你的 AI 舆情监控助手与热点筛选工具！聚合多平台热点 +  RSS 订阅，支持关键词精准筛选。AI 智能筛选新闻 + AI 翻译 +  AI 分析简报直推手机，也支持接入 MCP 架构，赋能 AI 自然语言对话分析、情感洞察与趋势预测等。支持 Docker ，数据本地/云端自持。集成微信/飞书/钉钉/Telegram/邮件/ntfy/bark/slack 等渠道智能推送。
summary:
TrendRadar is an open-source trend-monitoring assistant designed to aggregate, filter, and summarize news and updates across major online platforms and RSS feeds. The project aims for lightweight and easy deployment.

### Project Purpose
TrendRadar helps users bypass information overload by autonomously collecting data from popular information sources, filtering content based on personal interest, tracking trend evolution over time, and delivering structured summaries to various communication channels.

### Main Capabilities
- **Multi-Platform Hotspot Aggregation:** Monitors mainstream websites and platforms (such as Zhihu, Douyin, Bilibili, Baidu, Toutiao, and Weibo).
- **RSS & Atom Feed Support:** Captures and groups subscriptions alongside mainstream trends.
- **Precision and AI Filtering:** Filters news via custom keyword groups, regular expressions, global exclusion lists, or AI-driven natural language interest descriptions.
- **Trend and Sentiment Analysis:** Tracks first-appearance times, ranking changes, lifespan, and cross-platform performance, with optional AI sentiment identification and trend insights.
- **AI-Powered Multi-Language Translation:** Translates collected content into arbitrary target languages using unified AI model configurations.
- **Flexible Scheduling and Notifications:** Supports multiple execution timelines and pushes formatted markdown summaries directly to platforms like WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, Telegram, Email, ntfy, Bark, Slack, and generic webhooks.
- **Interactive Reports and MCP Integration:** Generates web-ready HTML reports with dark mode, wide layouts, search filters, and exposes Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for conversational data querying via AI assistants.

### Intended Users
The project is built for investors, content creators, media professionals, public relations specialists, and anyone seeking customized, filtered news streams without algorithm-driven clutter.

### Notable Technologies
- Python (with uv for dependency management)
- SQLite and S3-compatible remote cloud storage (e.g., Cloudflare R2)
- Docker and Docker Compose
- LiteLLM (for multi-provider AI integration supporting DeepSeek, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, and local Ollama)
- Model Context Protocol (MCP)

name: context7
description: Context7 Platform -- Up-to-date code documentation for LLMs and AI code editors
summary:
Context7 is a developer platform and toolset designed to feed up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples directly into Large Language Models (LLMs) and coding agents. It prevents outdated code generation and hallucinated APIs by retrieving live documentation from the source during prompts. 

The project operates through two primary modes: a CLI and skills approach using `ctx7` commands, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server integration (`@upstash/context7-mcp`). It provides specific utilities to resolve library identifiers (`resolve-library-id`, `ctx7 library`) and fetch precise version documentation (`query-docs`, `ctx7 docs`). 

Intended for software developers and AI coding assistants (such as Cursor, Claude Code, and various MCP-compatible clients), Context7 supports targeted library querying via slash notation (e.g., `/supabase/supabase`) and version specifiers. Additional packages include the TypeScript SDK (`@upstash/context7-sdk`), Vercel AI SDK integration tools (`@upstash/context7-tools-ai-sdk`), and a `pi.dev` extension. The project requires Node.js 18 or newer and is licensed under the MIT License.

name: leetcode-master
description: 《代码随想录》LeetCode 刷题攻略：200道经典题目刷题顺序，共60w字的详细图解，视频难点剖析，50余张思维导图，支持C++，Java，Python，Go，JavaScript等多语言版本，从此算法学习不再迷茫！🔥🔥 来看看，你会发现相见恨晚！🚀
summary:
The project `代码随想录 · LeetCode-Master` is a step-by-step problem-solving guide and learning path designed to help users systematically master data structures and algorithms, ranging from beginner to advanced levels. 

**Project Purpose:**
The repository aims to eliminate the need to sift through coding problems by providing an ordered, logical roadmap of high-frequency interview questions and typical test points. Each problem includes theoretical foundations, practical problem-solving tracks, diagrams, text explanations, and video tutorials.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Structured problem lists covering multiple chapters: arrays, linked lists, hash tables, strings, two-pointer techniques, stacks and queues, binary trees, backtracking, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, monotonic stacks, and graph theory.
- Summary reviews for each module to establish knowledge loops.
- Algorithmic templates and performance analysis guides (time and space complexity).

**Intended Users:**
Developers, job seekers, and students looking to systematically practice coding problems for technical interviews.

**Notable Technologies:**
The repository primarily uses **C++** for its main explanations, with community contributions offering multi-language implementations including **Java**, **Python**, **Go**, and **JavaScript**.

name: coolify
description: An open-source, self-hostable PaaS alternative to Vercel, Heroku & Netlify that lets you easily deploy static sites, databases, full-stack applications and 280+ one-click services on your own servers.
summary:
Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable platform designed to manage and deploy applications, databases, and services on user-owned hardware using an SSH connection. It functions as an alternative to Heroku, Netlify, and Vercel, providing cloud platform convenience while allowing users to retain complete infrastructure control. 

Main capabilities include building and deploying applications from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Gitea using Nixpacks, Railpack, Dockerfile, Docker Compose, or prebuilt Docker images. It supports managed databases and over 300 one-click services with persistent storage and generated credentials. Additionally, Coolify automates deployments on Git pushes, creates pull-request previews, configures custom domains with automatic HTTPS certificates, manages reverse proxies, handles health checks, and monitors multi-server resource status, logs, and container terminals. Workloads are protected through database backups, scheduled tasks, environment variables, secrets, and notifications, with access available via a dashboard, API, CLI, and MCP.

Intended users include developers, system administrators, and teams seeking self-hosted infrastructure management. Notable technologies and formats integrated within the platform include Docker, Nixpacks, Railpack, Git, and SSH.

name: GPT-SoVITS
description: 1 min voice data can also be used to train a good TTS model! (few shot voice cloning)
summary:
GPT-SoVITS-WebUI is a few-shot voice conversion and text-to-speech (TTS) WebUI. It provides zero-shot TTS using a 5-second vocal sample and few-shot TTS requiring about 1 minute of training data. The software supports cross-lingual inference in English, Japanese, Korean, Cantonese, and Chinese.

Main capabilities include WebUI-integrated tools for voice accompaniment separation, automatic training set segmentation, multilingual ASR via Fun-ASR-Nano, SenseVoice, and FunASR, alongside text labeling to assist users in creating training datasets and models. 

Intended users include developers, content creators, and beginners looking to perform voice cloning, speech synthesis, and dataset preparation. Notable technologies and frameworks utilized include Python, PyTorch, CUDA, Docker, Gradio, FFmpeg, FunASR, Faster Whisper, and various pretrained architectures such as VITS, SoundStorm, BigVGAN, and ContentVec.

name: pathway
description: Python ETL framework for stream processing, real-time analytics, LLM pipelines, and RAG.
summary:
Pathway Live Data Framework is a Python ETL framework designed for stream processing, real-time analytics, LLM pipelines, and RAG applications. It provides a unified engine for handling both batch and streaming data using a Python API, backed by a scalable Rust engine built on Differential Dataflow that performs incremental computation, multithreading, multiprocessing, and distributed execution.

The framework's main capabilities include data connectors (such as Kafka, PostgreSQL, GDrive, and Airbyte), stateless and stateful transformations (including windowing, joins, and sorting), state persistence for crash recovery, consistency management, and dedicated LLM tooling with vector indexing and integrations for LangChain and LlamaIndex. 

Intended users include data engineers, developers, and data scientists building real-time event-processing pipelines, alerting systems, and context-aware AI applications. Notable technologies and integrations mentioned include Rust, Docker, Kubernetes, LangChain, LlamaIndex, MinIO, Redpanda, and PaddleOCR.

name: ultralytics
description: Ultralytics YOLO27, YOLO26, YOLO11, YOLOv8 — object detection, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, image classification, pose estimation, object tracking
summary: Ultralytics provides state-of-the-art YOLO models and a computer vision framework built for performance, flexibility, and ease of use. The project supports tasks including object detection, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, depth estimation, image classification, pose estimation, oriented object detection (OBB), and object tracking across video frames. Intended users include developers, researchers, students, and enterprises looking to build AI workflows, train and validate models, or deploy solutions via formats like ONNX and TensorRT. Notable technologies utilized include Python, PyTorch, ONNX, TensorRT, and integrations with platforms such as Weights & Biases, Comet ML, Roboflow, and OpenVINO.

name: marktext
description: 📝A simple and elegant markdown editor, available for Linux, macOS and Windows.
summary:
MarkText is an open-source, simple, and elegant Markdown editor designed for speed, usability, and a distraction-free writing experience across Linux, macOS, and Windows. 

The project's main capabilities include real-time preview (WYSIWYG), support for CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown specifications alongside selective Pandoc markdown support, and markdown extensions such as math expressions via KaTeX, front matter, and emojis. It features paragraph and inline style shortcuts, direct image pasting from the clipboard, document export to HTML and PDF, multiple built-in themes (such as Cadmium Light and Material Dark), and distinct editing modes including Source Code mode, Typewriter mode, and Focus mode. 

MarkText is intended for users seeking a modern, efficient environment for writing and editing markdown documents.

name: termux-app
description: Termux - a terminal emulator application for Android OS extendible by variety of packages.
summary: Termux is an Android terminal application and Linux environment that provides a user interface and terminal emulation for mobile devices. It is intended for Android users seeking a command-line interface and package management capabilities on Android 7 and newer. The application features optional plugin apps such as Termux:API, Termux:Boot, Termux:Float, Termux:Styling, Termux:Tasker, and Termux:Widget. It includes a `termux-shared` library for managing shared constants and utilities to remove hardcoded paths.

name: Pake
description: 🤱🏻 Turn any webpage into a desktop app with one command.
summary:
Pake is a command-line and online tool designed to turn any webpage or local web build into a lightweight desktop application supporting macOS, Windows, and Linux. Intended for users, developers, and AI agents wanting native-like desktop wrappers without heavy resource usage, Pake boasts significantly smaller installation sizes and lower memory footprints compared to traditional Electron packages. 

Core capabilities include one-command CLI packaging, online building via GitHub Actions, automatic website icon fetching, JSON output modes for automation, and configuration schema support. The generated desktop apps feature customizable windows, styling options, ad removal, shortcuts, and drag-and-drop support. 

The project is built using Rust and Tauri, leveraging Node.js for its CLI tooling ecosystem.

name: ghostty
description: 👻 Ghostty is a fast, feature-rich, and cross-platform terminal emulator that uses platform-native UI and GPU acceleration.
summary: Ghostty is a fast, feature-rich, standards-compliant terminal emulator and native GUI application designed to deliver native platform experiences across operating systems. It features rich windowing capabilities including multi-windowing, tabbing, and panes. The core shared logic is written in Zig, with platform-native integrations utilizing SwiftUI and Metal for macOS, and GTK and systemd for Linux. Additionally, the project provides `libghostty`, a cross-platform, zero-dependency C and Zig library (supporting macOS, Linux, Windows, and WebAssembly) enabling developers to embed terminal functionality or build custom terminal emulators. Ghostty targets developers and general users seeking high performance, modern terminal features like the Kitty graphics protocol, and native user interfaces without sacrificing execution speed.

name: remotion
description: 🎥      Make videos programmatically with React
summary: Remotion is a toolset for creating and automating videos using React code as the source of truth. It enables users to build videos agentically with coding agents, interactively via drag-and-drop editing, and programmatically to manage data and complexity. Intended for developers, creators, and organizations, the project supports video automation use cases including design system asset libraries, batch rendering millions of videos on custom infrastructure, and building video applications or editors. Key technical capabilities and integrations include Node.js APIs, server-side rendering, AWS Lambda, Vercel sandboxes, client-side rendering, and a React Player component. Users can get started via Node.js using `npx create-video@latest`. Remotion features a special license that requires a company license in certain cases.

name: chinese-independent-developer
description: 👩🏿‍💻👨🏾‍💻👩🏼‍💻👨🏽‍💻👩🏻‍💻中国独立开发者项目列表 -- 分享大家都在做什么
summary:
This repository is a curated, crowd-sourced directory aggregating software projects, web apps, tools, and platforms built by independent developers from China. 

**Project Purpose:**
The collection satisfies curiosity regarding what independent developers build in their spare time, encourages the community to share their side projects, and helps users discover ready-to-use, practical web applications and mobile apps rather than developer tooling or forum sites.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Comprehensive cataloging of ready-to-use websites, mobile apps, and developer-created utilities.
- Categorization into dedicated sections such as a programmer edition, game edition, and historical archives.
- Tracking of project lifecycles using status indicators (in development, online, or closed/unmaintained).

**Intended Users:**
Independent developers, makers, indie hackers, entrepreneurs, and users looking for practical online tools, applications, and community-built utilities.

**Notable Technologies:**
Includes projects built with modern web and application frameworks, AI integration tools (utilizing APIs from providers like DeepSeek, OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini), Python, Rust, Tauri, and cross-platform stacks. Distinctive project names and toolkits such as Tauri, Rust, and WebAssembly are frequently referenced across submissions.

name: redux
description: A JS library for predictable global state management
summary:
Redux is a JavaScript library for predictable and maintainable global state management. It provides a single source of truth for application state using a centralized store, actions, and pure reducer functions, enabling consistent behavior across client, server, and native environments. 

The library's main capabilities include predictable state containers, developer tools such as live code editing and time-travel debugging, and an extensive ecosystem of addons. It is designed to be used with React, React Native, Next.js, Vite, or any other view library. 

The official and recommended approach for writing Redux logic is **Redux Toolkit**, which wraps the tiny core library (2kB) to incorporate best practices, simplify common tasks, prevent mistakes, and streamline setup using tools like `configureStore` and `createSlice` (leveraging Immer for immutable state updates). 

Intended users are frontend and full-stack developers building applications with moderate to large amounts of data changing over time who require a centralized state architecture. Notable technologies mentioned include JavaScript, TypeScript, React, React Native, Vite, Next.js, and Expo.

name: sway
description: 🌴 Empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient smart contracts.
summary: Sway is a programming language developed for the Fuel blockchain, heavily inspired by Rust, designed to bring modern language development and performance to the blockchain ecosystem. The project includes the Sway compiler, standard library, and the `forc` toolchain. Intended for blockchain developers building smart contracts and applications on the Fuel network, the repository provides tools for compiling, building, and developing within the Sway ecosystem. Built using Rust, it utilizes Cargo for dependency management and building, and `just` for task automation and running scripts such as benchmarks, tests, and CI checks.

name: awesome-flutter
description: An awesome list that curates the best Flutter libraries, tools, tutorials, articles and more.
summary: This repository hosts an awesome list curated for the Flutter ecosystem, serving as a comprehensive directory of resources for Google's UI toolkit. It aggregates articles, tutorials, video courses, UI components, plugins, state management frameworks, templates, open-source applications, testing tools, and desktop/web extensions. The project is designed for Flutter developers, mobile and cross-platform engineers, and software architects looking to discover community-driven packages, widgets, utilities, and learning materials for building natively compiled applications from a single codebase using Dart and Flutter.

name: minio
description: MinIO is a high-performance, S3 compatible object store, open sourced under GNU AGPLv3 license.
summary:
MinIO is a high-performance, S3-API-compatible object storage solution designed for speed and scalability to power data-intensive workloads, AI/ML pipelines, and analytics. It features an embedded web-based MinIO Console for object browsing and management. 

Intended for application developers, infrastructure engineers, and the open-source community, MinIO provides tools such as the MinIO Client (`mc`) for command-line operations, SDKs for various programming languages, and support for Kubernetes deployments via the MinIO Operator and community Helm charts. 

The community edition is distributed as source code only under the GNU AGPL v3.0 license and requires Go (version 1.24 or newer) to build from source or create Docker container images. Notable technologies utilized include Go, Docker, and Kubernetes.

name: pocketbase
description: Open Source realtime backend in 1 file
summary: PocketBase is an open-source Go backend that functions as a standalone executable or a Go framework/toolkit. Its core capabilities include an embedded SQLite database with realtime subscriptions, built-in file and user management, a convenient Admin dashboard UI, and a simple REST-ish API. It also features a JavaScript VM plugin enabling extension via JavaScript. Intended users include developers building custom application business logic and web APIs. Official SDK clients are available for JavaScript (supporting Browser, Node.js, and React Native) and Dart (supporting Web, Mobile, Desktop, and CLI).

name: lodash
description: A modern JavaScript utility library delivering modularity, performance, & extras.
summary: Lodash is a JavaScript utility library designed to simplify working with arrays, numbers, objects, and strings. Its main capabilities include iterating over collections, manipulating and testing values, and creating composite functions. Intended for JavaScript developers, Lodash provides modular methods available in various builds and module formats, including UMD, core builds, full builds, FP builds (featuring immutable, auto-curried, iteratee-first, data-last methods), per-method packages, and ES modules. It supports modern environments and integrates with tools like Node.js, npm, Browserify, Rollup, Webpack, Babel, and AMD.

name: autogen
description: A programming framework for agentic AI
summary: AutoGen is a framework designed for creating multi-agent AI applications that can operate autonomously or work alongside humans. It features a layered and extensible architecture, comprising the Core API for message passing and event-driven agents, the AgentChat API for rapid prototyping and multi-agent patterns, and the Extensions API for LLM clients and execution capabilities. The project also supplies developer tools including AutoGen Studio (a no-code GUI for building multi-agent workflows), AutoGen Bench, and Magentic-One. AutoGen supports cross-language interoperability in Python (version 3.10 or later) and .NET, integrating with model providers like OpenAI and AzureOpenAI. The repository is currently in maintenance mode, with Microsoft Agent Framework recommended for new projects.

name: pi-hole
description: A black hole for Internet advertisements
summary:
Pi-hole is a network-wide DNS sinkhole designed to protect devices from unwanted content, such as advertisements and trackers, without requiring client-side software installation. It runs on Linux hardware and blocks content across non-browser locations like mobile apps and smart TVs, while caching DNS queries to speed up browsing. 

Main capabilities include a responsive Web Interface dashboard for viewing statistics and managing settings, a command-line interface (`pihole`), an optional built-in DHCP server, support for IPv4 and IPv6, and the ability to handle hundreds of millions of queries. The project features FTLDNS (Faster-than-light Engine), a lightweight daemon providing statistics and an API for integration.

Intended users include individuals seeking privacy control and network-wide ad blocking on their own hardware. Notable technologies and components mentioned include Docker, Bash, IPv4, IPv6, and FTLDNS. Installation is supported via automated scripts, manual cloning, or Docker deployment.

name: nuxt
description: The full-stack Vue framework.
summary:
Nuxt is a free and open-source framework designed to create type-safe, performant, and production-grade full-stack web applications and websites with Vue.js. 

Intended for developers building fast, SEO-friendly, and scalable web applications, Nuxt's main capabilities include:
- Server-side rendering, static site generation, hybrid rendering, and edge-side rendering
- Automatic routing with code-splitting and pre-fetching
- Data fetching and state management
- Search engine optimization and meta tag definition
- Auto-imports for components, composables, and utils
- Zero-configuration TypeScript support
- Full-stack capabilities via a dedicated server directory
- Extensibility through 300+ modules and support for deployment to various hosting platforms

Notable technologies utilized in the project include Vue.js and TypeScript.

name: architect-awesome
description: 后端架构师技术图谱
summary: The repository provides a comprehensive technical roadmap and learning resource collection for backend engineers, ranging from junior developers to senior architects. It covers core computer science topics including data structures, algorithms, concurrency, operating systems, networking, databases, distributed systems design, and security. It also details standard middleware, search engines, big data technologies, web servers, caching solutions, and messaging queues such as MySQL, Redis, Kafka, Elasticsearch, Nginx, and Tomcat. Additionally, the project outlines software engineering practices, project management methodologies like Scrum and Kanban, performance tuning, and DevOps tools including Docker and Jenkins, while offering curated reading lists, blogs, and industry resources.

name: Front-end-Developer-Interview-Questions
description: A list of helpful front-end related questions you can use to interview potential candidates, test yourself or completely ignore.
summary:
The Front-end Developer Interview Questions repository provides a curated collection of open-ended questions designed to help hiring managers and interviewers vet potential front-end developer candidates. 

The project's main capabilities include structured question sets covering general concepts, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, accessibility, testing, performance, networking, coding challenges, and general trivia. These resources are intended to help interviewers evaluate required technical skills and spark meaningful discussions regarding a candidate's overall capabilities. 

The intended users are engineering managers, technical recruiters, and interviewers vetting front-end development candidates. Notable technologies and technical areas referenced include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, web accessibility, and software testing.

name: atom
description: :atom: The hackable text editor
summary: Atom is a hackable, deeply customizable text editor for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Built on Electron, it is designed to be approachable using default configurations while supporting package development and advanced customization. Intended users include developers, programmers, and general text-editing users. The project utilizes Electron, Git, and web-based technologies, and includes comprehensive documentation via the Atom Flight Manual and an API reference.

name: bat
description: A cat(1) clone with wings.
summary:
`bat` is a command-line utility written in Rust that serves as a clone of the standard `cat` tool, featuring advanced syntax highlighting and Git integration. Its main capabilities include syntax highlighting for numerous programming and markup languages, communication with `git` to display file modifications relative to the index, highlighting non-printable characters, automatic paging via tools like `less`, and file concatenation. 

Intended for developers and terminal users, `bat` acts as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and integrates smoothly with other command-line tools such as `fzf`, `fd`, `ripgrep`, `tail`, `git`, and `man`. Notable technologies used in the project include Rust, Cargo, and the `syntect` library for parsing Sublime Text syntax definitions and themes.

name: penpot
description: Penpot: The open-source design platform for Product teams that need scalable collaboration.
summary:
Penpot is an open-source, web-based design and prototyping platform built for teams creating digital products at scale. It offers full design infrastructure ownership through self-hosting options while working natively with open standards like SVG, CSS, HTML, and JSON. 

Intended for designers, developers, and product teams, Penpot bridges the gap between design and code. It features real-time collaboration, CSS Grid and Flex Layout for responsive interface design, and native Design Tokens, Components, and Variants to maintain a single source of truth for design systems. Developers benefit from an Inspect mode that provides instant access to code, an MCP server enabling multi-directional workflows, and a robust open API and plugin system for automation and integrations. Deployable via Docker, Kubernetes, or Elestio, Penpot supports enterprise governance requirements through centralized administration and SSO capabilities.

name: plane
description: 🔥🔥🔥 Open-source Jira, Linear, Monday, and ClickUp alternative. Plane is a modern project management platform to manage tasks, sprints, docs, and triage.
summary:
Plane is an open-source project management tool designed for teams to track issues, run cycles, and manage product roadmaps. 

### Main Capabilities
- **Work Items:** Create and manage tasks using a rich text editor with file uploads, sub-properties, and issue linking.
- **Cycles:** Maintain team momentum and track progress with burn-down charts.
- **Modules:** Divide complex projects into smaller, manageable parts.
- **Views:** Customize workflows and filter relevant issues.
- **Pages:** Capture and organize ideas with AI capabilities, rich text editing, and the ability to convert notes into actionable items.
- **Analytics:** Access real-time insights and visualize trends to remove blockers.

### Intended Users
Teams and organizations looking for a modern project management solution that can be used via Plane Cloud or self-hosted on their own infrastructure using Docker or Kubernetes.

### Notable Technologies
- **Frontend:** React Router
- **Backend:** Django
- **Runtime:** Node.js

name: spring-framework
description: Spring Framework
summary: Spring Framework serves as the foundation for the Spring family of projects, providing comprehensive capabilities beyond the Java programming language for creating enterprise applications across a wide range of scenarios and architectures. It is intended for developers building Java-based enterprise software. Technologies associated with the framework include Java and GitHub Actions workflows for continuous integration builds. The project is released under the Apache License 2.0.

name: markdown-here
description: Google Chrome, Firefox, and Thunderbird extension that lets you write email in Markdown and render it before sending.
summary:
Markdown Here is a browser and email client extension for Google Chrome, Firefox, Opera, and Thunderbird that allows users to compose emails, Google Groups posts, Blogger posts, Evernote notes, and WordPress posts using Markdown and render them into rich HTML before sending. 

The project's main capabilities include bidirectional conversion (Markdown to HTML and back), syntax highlighting for code blocks using highlight.js, TeX mathematical formulae processing, and piecemeal conversion of selected text. It is designed for individuals who want to write emails and web content containing code or formatting using Markdown rather than tedious rich-text editors. 

Notable technologies and libraries utilized include JavaScript, GitHub Flavored Markdown (via marked), highlight.js for syntax highlighting, and jsHtmlToText for HTML-to-text conversion. The extension integrates with webmail clients such as Gmail, Hotmail, and Yahoo, as well as desktop clients like Thunderbird.

name: Real-Time-Voice-Cloning
description: Clone a voice in 5 seconds to generate arbitrary speech in real-time
summary:
This repository implements the deep learning framework **SV2TTS** (Transfer Learning from Speaker Verification to Multispeaker Text-To-Speech Synthesis), combined with a real-time vocoder. The project enables users to create a digital representation of a voice from a few seconds of audio and use it as a reference to generate arbitrary speech. 

The three-stage framework utilizes specific models and techniques, including:
- **GE2E (encoder)**: Generalized End-To-End Loss for Speaker Verification
- **Tacotron (synthesizer)**: Tacotron: Towards End-to-End Speech Synthesis
- **WaveRNN (vocoder)**: Efficient Neural Audio Synthesis

The repository provides both a graphical toolbox interface (`demo_toolbox.py`) and a command-line interface (`demo_cli.py`) supporting Windows and Linux environments, with optional NVIDIA CUDA acceleration and integration with Hugging Face for pretrained models. It is intended for researchers and developers interested in speech synthesis and voice cloning.

name: starship
description: ☄🌌️  The minimal, blazing-fast, and infinitely customizable prompt for any shell!
summary: Starship is a minimal, fast, and infinitely customizable command-line prompt designed to work with any shell across various operating systems. Its primary purpose is to display relevant contextual information at a glance while supporting a wide array of development tools. Main capabilities include cross-shell compatibility, extensive configuration options, and quick installation. The project is intended for developers and terminal users looking to enhance their command-line interface. Notable technologies and shells supported include Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, Cmd with Clink, Elvish, Ion, Nushell, Tcsh, Xonsh, and the Rust package ecosystem via crates.io.

name: rclone
description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files
summary:
Rclone is a command-line program designed to sync files and directories to and from a vast array of cloud storage providers, local filesystems, and network protocols. Often described as "rsync for cloud storage," it supports integrations with major cloud services like Amazon S3, Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, and dozens of other object storage, webhosting, and file-sharing backends. 

Key capabilities include file integrity checks using MD5 and SHA-1 hashes, timestamp preservation, one-way sync, bidirectional synchronization (Bisync), copy modes, and hash equality checking. Rclone also provides virtual storage backends supporting transparent encryption (Crypt), compression, chunking for large files, directory combination, and hashing. Additional features include FUSE mounting, multi-threaded downloads, and the ability to serve local or remote files over HTTP, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, and DLNA. The project is licensed under the MIT license.

name: litellm
description: The fastest, litest AI Gateway. Rust core with Python SDK. Call 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format with cost tracking, guardrails, load balancing, and logging [Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI, VertexAI, vLLM, Nvidia NIM]
summary:
LiteLLM is an open-source AI Gateway and Python SDK designed to provide a single, unified interface to call over 100 large language models (LLMs)—including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, and Azure—using standard OpenAI formatting. 

The project's main capabilities include routing, load balancing, retry and fallback logic, spend management, virtual keys for secure access control, observability callbacks, and support for Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocols, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and agent harnesses like Claude Code and Codex. 

LiteLLM is intended for developers building LLM applications and Gen AI Enablement or ML Platform Teams seeking self-hosted, enterprise-ready infrastructure. It supports production deployments via Terraform modules for AWS and GCP, Helm charts, and Docker. Notable technologies used include Python, Docker, Terraform, AWS (ECS, Aurora, ElastiCache), GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Memorystore), PostgreSQL, and Redis.

name: jquery
description: jQuery JavaScript Library
summary: jQuery is a fast, small, and feature-rich JavaScript library designed to simplify HTML DOM tree traversal and manipulation, event handling, CSS animation, and Ajax requests. It aims to make things much simpler to use across a multitude of browsers, while also supporting Node.js, browser extensions, and other non-browser environments. Intended users include web developers building interactive browser-based applications and extensions. Notable technologies and tools associated with the repository include Node.js, npm, Git, ECMAScript modules (ESM), and QUnit for unit testing.

name: mkcert
description: A simple zero-config tool to make locally trusted development certificates with any names you'd like.
summary: mkcert is a simple tool designed for developers to create and manage locally-trusted development certificates without requiring configuration. Its main capabilities include automatically creating and installing a local Certificate Authority (CA) in system and browser trust stores, and generating locally-trusted certificates for specific domain names, IP addresses, email addresses for S/MIME, and client authentication. It supports multiple root stores including macOS, Windows, Linux variants, Firefox, Chrome, Chromium, and Java. Notable technologies and tools referenced include Go, Homebrew, MacPorts, Chocolatey, Scoop, and Node.js.

name: awesome-rust
description: A curated list of Rust code and resources.
summary:
Awesome Rust is a curated, comprehensive repository and directory of Rust code, libraries, development tools, applications, and educational resources. Its primary purpose is to provide a structured index for developers to discover Rust projects ranging from embedded systems and operating systems to web frameworks, databases, artificial intelligence tooling, cryptography libraries, and command-line utilities. 

The repository covers a vast array of technical domains including blockchain development, machine learning frameworks, data processing, GUI toolkits, networking protocols, security tools, and performance profiling. It caters to intended users ranging from beginners learning the language to experienced systems programmers, software engineers, and researchers. Notable technologies highlighted throughout the list include the Cargo package manager, Tokio asynchronous runtime, WebAssembly (Wasm), LLVM, eBPF, and standard database and serialization formats like PostgreSQL, SQLite, and Serde.

name: llama
description: Inference code for Llama models
summary:
This repository provides minimal example code to load and run local inference for Llama 2, a collection of pre-trained and fine-tuned large language models ranging from 7B to 70B parameters. The project aims to unlock the power of large language models for individuals, creators, researchers, and businesses of all sizes, enabling them to experiment, innovate, and scale ideas responsibly. 

Main capabilities include text completion using pre-trained models and dialogue generation using fine-tuned chat models. Intended users span researchers, developers, and commercial entities. Notable technologies utilized include PyTorch, CUDA, and model-parallel (MP) execution via PyTorch's `torchrun`. 

*Note: This repository has been deprecated in favor of consolidated repositories under the Llama Stack ecosystem, including `llama-models`, `PurpleLlama`, `llama-toolchain`, `llama-agentic-system`, and `llama-cookbook`.*

name: shadowsocks-windows
description: A C# port of shadowsocks
summary: Shadowsocks for Windows is a secure SOCKS5/HTTP proxy client designed for Windows users to bypass internet censorship and secure network traffic. Its main capabilities include system proxy configuration, PAC (Proxy Auto-Config) and global modes, GeoSite and user-defined rules, UDP relay, plugin support, and server auto-switching strategies such as load balancing and high availability. It is intended for end-users seeking flexible proxy management and developers looking to customize routing strategies. Built using .NET Framework 4.8 and C#, the project relies on technologies including Visual Studio 2019, WPF, Newtonsoft.Json, ReactiveUI, and utilizes upstream components like v2fly domain-list-community and Privoxy.

name: meilisearch
description: A lightning-fast search engine API bringing AI-powered hybrid search to your sites and applications.
summary:
Meilisearch is a lightning-fast search engine designed to fit into apps, websites, and workflows, offering a search-as-you-type experience with results delivered in under 50 milliseconds. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Hybrid, semantic, and full-text search combining vector search with keyword matching.
- Typo tolerance, custom filtering, and faceted search.
- Sorting, synonym support, and geosearch based on geographic data.
- Conversational search using natural language and AI-generated answers grounded in search results.
- Personalization, search rules, document relations, and multi-tenancy support via tenant tokens.
- Horizontal scalability through replication and sharding.
- AI readiness with out-of-the-box support for LangChain and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
- A RESTful API supported by multiple SDKs and integration tools.

**Intended Users:**
Developers and organizations seeking a customizable, easy-to-install, and maintainable search engine for web applications, e-commerce sites, SaaS platforms, and multi-tenant systems.

**Notable Technologies:**
- RESTful API
- LangChain
- Model Context Protocol (MCP)

name: github-cheat-sheet
description: A list of cool features of Git and GitHub.
summary:
The GitHub Cheat Sheet is a comprehensive collection of hidden and lesser-known features, shortcuts, and tips for Git and GitHub. It serves as a practical reference guide for developers, project maintainers, and students seeking to optimize their workflows using Git and GitHub. 

The project outlines capabilities across two main sections. The GitHub section details web interface features, markdown styling options, repository navigation shortcuts, issue and pull request management tricks, diff viewing enhancements, and collaboration tools such as task lists, templates, and CI status integration. The Git section covers command-line techniques, including branch management, log and status styling, searching with git grep and queries, automated workspace cleanup, and configuration options like aliases and auto-correct.

Notable technologies and tools mentioned throughout the guide include Git, GitHub, Jekyll, Travis CI, Hub, and Linguist.

name: mempalace
description: The best-benchmarked open-source AI memory system. And it's free.
summary:
MemPalace is a local-first AI memory system designed to store conversation history and project files as verbatim text and retrieve them via semantic search. The project avoids summarization, extraction, and paraphrasing, structuring indexes into *wings* (people and projects), *rooms* (topics), and *drawers* (original content) to enable scoped searches. 

Main capabilities include a pluggable backend interface (supporting ChromaDB, SQLite, Rust native vectors, Milvus, Qdrant, and pgvector), a temporal entity-relationship knowledge graph with validity windows, an MCP server with 45 tools for palace operations and agent coordination, and auto-save hooks for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Cursor IDE. It achieves 96.6% R@5 raw retrieval recall on LongMemEval without requiring API calls.

Intended users include developers, AI coding agents, and technical teams looking for private, local-first conversation history and context management. Notable technologies include Python 3.9+, ChromaDB, Rust (PyO3 bindings for native vector searches), Docker, SQLite, and optional OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoints.

name: crewAI
description: Framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents. By fostering collaborative intelligence, CrewAI empowers agents to work together seamlessly, tackling complex tasks.
summary:
CrewAI is an open-source Python framework designed for building production-ready multi-agent systems and event-driven automation workflows. Its core architecture combines **Crews**—role-based, autonomous AI agents that collaborate and execute specialized tasks—with **Flows**, which provide event-driven orchestration, state management, and conditional routing. 

The framework is intended for developers and enterprises seeking to build, scale, and control multi-agent applications, ranging from simple automations to complex production-grade systems. Notable technical capabilities and components include support for structured outputs (Pydantic and JSON), custom tools, memory, checkpointing, agentic reasoning, asynchronous execution, and integrations with large language models via providers like OpenAI and local runtimes like Ollama. Additionally, the project features CLI tooling built with UV, a dedicated CrewAI AMP enterprise control plane for observability and governance, and integration support for Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) workflows.

name: llm-app
description: Ready-to-run cloud templates for RAG, AI pipelines, and enterprise search with live data. 🐳Docker-friendly.⚡Always in sync with Sharepoint, Google Drive, S3, Kafka, PostgreSQL, real-time data APIs, and more.
summary:
The Pathway Live Data Framework AI Pipelines repository provides ready-to-deploy LLM (Large Language Model) application templates for high-accuracy RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and AI enterprise search at scale. The project is intended for developers and organizations seeking to build and productionize real-time AI applications that synchronize with live data sources—such as file systems, Google Drive, SharePoint, S3, Kafka, PostgreSQL, and real-time APIs—without complex infrastructure dependencies.

Main capabilities include built-in in-memory data indexing supporting vector search, hybrid search, and full-text search with caching. The repository includes specialized templates for basic Question-Answering RAG, Live Document Indexing, Multimodal RAG using GPT-4o, Unstructured-to-SQL data pipelines, Adaptive RAG, private local deployments using Mistral and Ollama, Slides AI Search, and Video RAG powered by TwelveLabs. 

Built using the Pathway Live Data Framework (a Python library with a Rust engine), the applications expose HTTP APIs, can be containerized via Docker, and integrate with technologies such as usearch, Tantivy, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Streamlit, and GPT models.

name: rails
description: Ruby on Rails
summary:
Rails is a web application framework designed to create database-backed web applications using the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern. It divides applications into three primary layers: the Model layer (utilizing Active Record and Active Model for domain logic and data mapping), the View layer (utilizing Action View and ERB templates), and the Controller layer (utilizing Action Pack, Action Dispatch, and Action Controller to manage incoming HTTP requests and responses). 

Intended for web developers building structured applications, Rails includes integrated libraries and frameworks such as Action Mailer and Action Mailbox for email handling, Active Job for background queuing, Action Cable for WebSocket integration, Active Storage for cloud and local file attachments, Action Text for rich text content, and Active Support as a collection of utility classes and extensions. Core components like Active Record, Active Model, Action Pack, Action View, and Active Support can also be used independently outside of Rails.

name: zustand
description: 🐻 Bear necessities for state management in React
summary:
Zustand is a small, fast, and scalable state-management solution for JavaScript and TypeScript applications, utilizing simplified flux principles and a hook-based API. It addresses common state management pitfalls such as the zombie child problem, React concurrency, and context loss between mixed renderers without requiring boilerplate code, opinionated patterns, or context providers. 

Intended for React and vanilla JavaScript developers, Zustand allows stores to be created as hooks that hold primitives, objects, or functions. The library supports atomic state selections, shallow equality checks via `useShallow`, asynchronous actions, transient updates for high-frequency changes, and vanilla store usage without React. Notable built-in and community-supported middleware includes `persist`, `immer`, `subscribeWithSelector`, `redux`, and `devtools` integration for Redux DevTools.

name: angular.js
description: AngularJS - HTML enhanced for web apps!
summary:
AngularJS is a client-side JavaScript framework designed for building web applications using an MV* (Model-View-Whatever) architecture. It allows developers to extend HTML syntax using custom directives and templates—supporting formats like HTML, HAML, and Jade/Pug—to express application components clearly. 

The project's main capabilities include automatic two-way data binding between the UI view and JavaScript object models, built-in dependency injection and inversion of control for testability and modularity, server-side communication handling via promises and deferred objects, and client-side navigation supporting hashbang URLs and HTML5 pushState. Intended users are web developers seeking to structure client-side applications with declarative templates and reduced boilerplate code. Notable technologies and concepts include JavaScript, HTML, dependency injection, two-way data binding, and asynchronous promises. Support for AngularJS officially ended in January 2022.

name: OpenManus
description: No fortress, purely open ground.  OpenManus is Coming.
summary:
OpenManus is an open-source framework developed by contributors from MetaGPT for building general AI agents capable of executing user-provided ideas and tasks. 

**Main Capabilities**
- Autonomous task execution driven by LLMs via a terminal interface or multi-agent workflows.
- Native browser automation powered by Browser Use CLI as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, supporting local Chrome/Chromium instances or remote cloud browsers via CDP.
- Specialized agents such as the DataAnalysis Agent for data analysis and visualization tasks.
- Extensible tool integration including browser execution, screenshots, and custom MCP tools.

**Intended Users**
Designed for developers, researchers, and users seeking an open-source, customizable AI agent framework without invite restrictions.

**Notable Technologies**
- Python 3.12
- Browser Use / Browser Use CLI 3.0 (MCP server)
- Playwright and BrowserGym
- Conda and uv for dependency management
- OpenAI GPT models (configurable via TOML)

name: nanochat
description: The best ChatGPT that $100 can buy.
summary:
nanochat is a minimal, hackable experimental harness for training and interacting with Large Language Models (LLMs) on a single GPU node. Designed to cover the entire LLM lifecycle—including tokenization, pretraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning (RL), evaluation, and inference—the project allows users to train a GPT-2 capability model for a fraction of historical costs. 

The repository is built around a single complexity dial (`--depth`) which automatically calculates compute-optimal hyperparameters such as transformer width, attention heads, learning rates, and weight decays. Precision is managed explicitly via a global `COMPUTE_DTYPE` (supporting `bfloat16`, `float16`, and `float32`), utilizing vanilla PyTorch alongside custom `Linear` layers and optimizers like AdamW and Muon. 

Intended for researchers and developers seeking an accessible, readable, and maximally forkable codebase without heavy framework boilerplate, nanochat includes built-in benchmarking utilities, speedrun configurations, and tool execution capabilities. Dependency management and environment setup are handled via `uv`, with native support for CUDA accelerators as well as CPU and Apple Silicon (MPS) fallbacks.

name: gitea
description: Git with a cup of tea! Painless self-hosted all-in-one software development service, including Git hosting, code review, team collaboration, package registry and CI/CD
summary: Gitea is a self-hosted, all-in-one software development service designed to provide an easy and fast solution for Git hosting, code management, code review, issue tracking, project kanban, wikis, team collaboration, package registries, and CI/CD supporting reusable GitHub Actions. Written in Go, Gitea operates across all platforms and architectures supported by Go, including Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, and Windows on x86, amd64, ARM, RISC-V 64, and PowerPC architectures. The project targets developers, teams, and administrators seeking a dedicated, self-hosted code hosting and collaboration platform deployable via containers or built from source. Notable technologies include Go, Docker, Podman, and GitHub Actions-compatible CI/CD runners.

name: yolov5
description: Ultralytics YOLOv5 in PyTorch for object detection, instance segmentation, classification, training, and export.
summary:
Ultralytics YOLOv5 is a fast, accurate, and user-friendly computer vision model developed by Ultralytics and built on the PyTorch framework. Its primary purpose is to provide reliable tools for vision AI tasks, specifically object detection, instance image segmentation, and image classification. 

The project is intended for developers, researchers, and enterprises seeking efficient vision AI integration, offering support for custom model training, validation, test-time augmentation, hyperparameter evolution, and export to formats such as ONNX, TensorRT, and CoreML. Notable technologies and frameworks utilized include PyTorch, Python, Docker, ONNX, and TensorRT, alongside integrations with platforms like Weights & Biases, Comet ML, Roboflow, and ClearML.

name: Win11Debloat
description: A simple, lightweight PowerShell script that allows you to remove pre-installed apps, disable telemetry, as well as perform various other changes to declutter and customize your Windows experience. Win11Debloat works for both Windows 10 and Windows 11.
summary:
Win11Debloat is a lightweight, easy-to-use PowerShell script designed to declutter and customize Windows. Its primary purpose is to remove pre-installed bloatware apps, disable telemetry and intrusive interface elements, manage privacy settings, remove AI features like Microsoft Copilot and Windows Recall, and configure system preferences such as the taskbar, Start Menu, File Explorer, and Windows Update behavior.
