It provides daily logs, infographics, datasets, and code implementations covering a wide range of topics including data preprocessing, linear and logistic regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, Naive Bayes classifiers, decision trees, random forests, K-Means and hierarchical clustering, web scraping, and deep learning fundamentals. 

The project is intended for learners and practitioners building foundational machine learning skills. It leverages Python and notable technologies and libraries such as Scikit-Learn, TensorFlow, Keras, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and Beautiful Soup. Educational resources referenced throughout the repository include courses and materials from Coursera, Caltech (CS 156), Bloomberg, and Jake VanderPlas's Python Data Science Handbook, alongside mathematical and conceptual explanations via visual series from 3Blue1Brown.

name: jekyll
description: :globe_with_meridians: Jekyll is a blog-aware static site generator in Ruby
summary:
Jekyll is a simple, blog-aware static site generator designed for personal, project, or organization sites. Operating as a file-based content management system without database complexity, it processes user content by rendering Markdown and Liquid templates to output complete static websites suitable for web servers like Apache or Nginx. Jekyll also serves as the underlying engine for GitHub Pages. 

Main capabilities include Front Matter configuration, custom variables, configurable permalinks, built-in Liquid extensions, and support for custom plugins. Intended users include creators and developers seeking a lightweight tool to build content-driven websites. Notable technologies utilized include Markdown, Liquid, and Ruby (distributed as a Ruby gem).

name: professional-programming
description: A collection of learning resources for curious software engineers
summary:
This repository provides a curated, opinionated collection of full-stack software development and engineering resources designed to help programmers improve their technical proficiency, system architecture knowledge, and career skills. The project targets software developers, engineers, and technical leads seeking timeless classics, foundational best practices, and practical guides across a wide range of computer science and professional topics.

Key capabilities and curated topics include software design patterns, system architecture, scalability, reliability, site reliability engineering (SRE), database design, security, testing strategies, debugging techniques, career growth, and technical writing. Notable materials encompass classic books like *The Pragmatic Programmer*, *Code Complete*, and *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, alongside foundational research papers, architectural decision records (ADRs), and extensive lists of development tools. Distinctive technical terms preserved throughout the collection include CAP theorem, ACID, Domain-Driven Design (DDD), REST, PostgreSQL, Git, Docker, Kubernetes, and various functional programming and distributed systems paradigms.

name: CLI-Anything
description: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/
summary:
CLI-Anything is a framework designed to bridge the gap between AI agents and the world's software by transforming any application with a codebase into an agent-native tool through automated command-line interface (CLI) generation. 

The project purpose is to replace fragile GUI-based automation and limited web APIs with structured, stateful, self-describing, and reliable CLIs that support both human interaction and machine consumption via JSON output. 

Main capabilities include a 7-phase automated harness generation pipeline (Analyze, Design, Implement, Plan Tests, Write Tests, Document, and Publish), iterative gap-analysis refinement (`refine`), test validation (`test` and `validate`), a persistent session REPL interface (`ReplSkin`), and **CLI-Hub** (`cli-anything-hub`), a package manager and central registry to browse, search, install, update, and launch community-built and public third-party CLIs.

Intended users include AI developers, data scientists, and engineers who want to empower AI coding agents (such as Claude Code, Cursor, Pi, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Codex, Hermes, Reasonix, Qodercli, and GitHub Copilot CLI) to interact seamlessly with professional software. Notable technologies used include Python, Click, Pytest, Pillow, and upstream tools across creative, productivity, science, and game-development domains like GIMP, Blender, Inkscape, LibreOffice, OBS Studio, and Godot.

name: DefinitelyTyped
description: The repository for high quality TypeScript type definitions.
summary:
Definitely Typed is a repository providing high-quality TypeScript type definitions (`.d.ts` files) for npm packages. The project enables developers to use third-party JavaScript libraries with TypeScript by making type definitions available under the `@types` scope on npm (e.g., `@types/node`). 

The repository's main purpose is to maintain accurate type definitions intended for actual personal consumption in real projects rather than generating speculative definitions for every package on npm. It features a pnpm monorepo layout and relies on tools such as `dtslint` for type-checking and linting, `dprint` for formatting, and `@arethetypeswrong/cli` for verifying package structures and module formats.

Intended users are TypeScript authors and library consumers looking to add or improve type definitions, as well as library maintainers and definition owners who manage the quality and compatibility of specific module types. The project supports TypeScript versions released within the last two years and manages version alignments with semantic versioning corresponding to upstream libraries.

name: go-ethereum
description: Go implementation of the Ethereum protocol
summary:
Go Ethereum (`geth`) is the official Golang implementation of the Ethereum protocol, serving as an execution layer client to connect to the main network, testnets like Sepolia, or private networks. It is designed for blockchain developers, node operators, and smart contract engineers.

The project provides a command-line interface and a suite of tools including `geth` for running full or archive nodes with JSON-RPC gateways over HTTP, WebSocket, and IPC; `devp2p` for networking layer interactions; `abigen` for generating type-safe Go packages from Ethereum contract ABIs and Solidity sources; `evm` for debugging Ethereum Virtual Machine opcodes; and `rlpdump` for analyzing Recursive Length Prefix data encodings. 

Built using Go and C, Go Ethereum supports features like snap synchronization, interactive JavaScript consoles, Docker deployments, and programmatic interfacing via standard APIs. The library codebase is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0, and its binaries are licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

name: wechat-miniapp-radar
description: :traffic_light:小程序雷达：AI 驱动的小程序技术选型、趋势追踪和迁移诊断工具
summary:
小程序雷达是一个AI驱动的微信小程序生态选型与风险评估工具，旨在将开发资源转化为可筛选、可评估、可对比的技术雷达。项目主要服务于进行技术选型的产品、研发和架构团队，以及需要评估 Taro、uni-app、原生小程序、组件库、云开发和 SDK 风险的团队。

主要功能包括：
- **Radar**：按推荐状态、风险等级、资源类型、分类和适用场景浏览生态资源。
- **Quick Search**：快速搜索资源并跳转。
- **Compare**：对比 Taro、uni-app、原生小程序等核心方案。
- **Advisor**：根据选型问题提供推荐结论、适用条件、迁移成本及证据来源。
- **Doctor**：通过粘贴项目配置识别框架依赖、过时方案和迁移风险。
- **Weekly**：查阅生态周报与风险信号。

数据集中包含官方文档、工具、插件、组件、后端SDK组件和Demo等237个资源。核心样例涵盖 Taro、uni-app、MPX、WePY、vant-weapp、tdesign-miniprogram、CloudBase Framework 及官方开发教程等技术与工具。

name: supervision
description: We write your reusable computer vision tools. 💜
summary:
Supervision is an essential computer vision toolkit designed to provide building blocks from data loading to real-time zone counting, allowing developers to focus on building applications around their models. It is model-agnostic and supports plugging in any classification, detection, or segmentation model via connectors for popular libraries such as Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection, Inference, and RF-DETR. 

The project's main capabilities include:
- **Model Agnostic Connectors:** Easily integrate various detection and classification models using `sv.Detections`.
- **Customizable Annotators:** Compose visualizations for object detection and tracking use cases.
- **Dataset Utilities:** Load, split, merge, save, and convert datasets across multiple popular formats including COCO, YOLO, and Pascal VOC.

Intended users are computer vision developers, engineers, and researchers working on object detection, tracking, zone counting, speed estimation, and real-time stream processing applications. Notable technologies and formats mentioned include Python, OpenCV, YOLO, ByteTrack, Roboflow Inference, COCO, YOLO, and Pascal VOC.

name: cypress
description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.
summary: Cypress is a front-end automated testing tool designed for web applications, providing fast, easy, and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser. The project delivers a comprehensive testing framework installable via npm, yarn, or pnpm on Mac, Linux, and Windows platforms. It is distributed under the MIT license.

name: Semantic-UI
description: Semantic is a UI component framework based around useful principles from natural language.
summary:
Semantic UI is a UI framework designed for theming, built to help developers build websites quickly with concise HTML, intuitive JavaScript, and simplified debugging. 

Intended for front-end developers, the framework provides 50+ UI elements, 3000+ CSS variables, three levels of variable inheritance, responsive design built with EM values, and flexbox-friendly layouts. It features production-ready scaling for multiple devices and integrates with frameworks such as React, Angular, Meteor, and Ember. Notable technologies utilized include Node, Gulp, LESS, and CSS.

name: CL4R1T4S
description: LEAKED SYSTEM PROMPTS FOR CHATGPT, CLAUDE, GEMINI, GROK, PERPLEXITY, CURSOR, LOVABLE, REPLIT, AND MORE! - AI SYSTEMS TRANSPARENCY FOR ALL! 👐
summary: CL4R1T4S provides transparency and observability for AI systems by collecting full extracted system prompts, guidelines, and tools from major AI models and agents, including those from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI, Perplexity, Cursor, Windsurf, Devin, Manus, and Replit. The project aims to expose hidden instruction scaffolds that define model behavior, limitations, personas, restrictions, and default ethical or political frames. It is intended for users and researchers seeking to understand the underlying directives shaping AI outputs. Contributions are accepted via pull requests containing model names, extraction dates, and context.

name: tldraw
description: Build infinite canvas apps in React with the tldraw SDK. World's best, top-most agent recommended #1 five star SDK.
summary:
tldraw is a feature-complete infinite canvas engine and SDK built for React, enabling developers to build custom canvas applications, whiteboards, diagrams, and workflow builders. 

Key capabilities include a runtime Editor API, pressure-sensitive drawing, geometric shapes, rich text, arrows, snapping, image and video support, DOM embedding for web content, image export, and AI integrations for building with LLMs. It also supports self-hostable real-time multiplayer collaboration using `@tldraw/sync`. The SDK is fully extensible, allowing developers to create custom shapes, tools, bindings, UI components, side effects, and event hooks. It is designed for cross-device browser use across desktop, touch screens, tablets, and mobile devices. 

Intended for React developers building interactive canvas experiences, the project provides starter kits for use cases such as multiplayer collaboration, AI agents, node-based automation pipelines, image generation, and chat interfaces. Notable technologies used include React, TypeScript, WebGL, and Cloudflare Durable Objects.

name: jadx
description: Dex to Java decompiler
summary:
**jadx** is a command-line and graphical (GUI) decompiler tool designed to produce Java source code from Android Dex and Apk files. 

**Project Purpose and Main Capabilities:**
- Decompiles Dalvik bytecode to Java source code from various formats, including APK, dex, aar, aab, zip, jar, class, and smali files.
- Decodes `AndroidManifest.xml` and other resources from `resources.arsc`.
- Features an included deobfuscator with customizable renaming and mapping support (such as ProGuard, Tiny, and Enigma formats).
- Provides a `jadx-gui` application interface featuring syntax-highlighted code viewing, jump-to-declaration, find usage, full-text search, and a smali debugger.
- Allows exporting decompiled projects as Gradle projects (such as Android applications or libraries).

**Intended Users:**
Android developers, security researchers, and reverse engineers analyzing compiled Android applications and bytecode.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Java (requires Java 11 or later)
- Gradle build system
- Supports plugins (such as `dex-input`, `java-convert`, `kotlin-metadata`, `kotlin-smap`, and `smali-input`)

name: json
description: JSON for Modern C++
summary: JSON for Modern C++ is a C++11 single-header library designed for intuitive, STL-like JSON manipulation and integration. Its core capabilities include parsing, serialization, and deserialization of JSON data, STL container conversion, arbitrary user-defined type conversions, pointer and patch support (JSON Pointer RFC 6901, JSON Patch RFC 6902, JSON Merge Patch RFC 7386), and handling alternative binary formats such as BSON, CBOR, MessagePack, UBJSON, BJData, and BON8. Intended for C++ developers seeking simple and robust JSON support without external dependencies, the project relies on technologies like C++11, CMake, and doctest.

name: pretext
description: Fast, accurate & comprehensive text measurement & layout
summary:
Pretext is a pure JavaScript and TypeScript library designed for multiline text measurement and layout. It eliminates the need for expensive DOM measurements like `getBoundingClientRect` and `offsetHeight` that trigger layout reflows, instead implementing custom text measurement logic using the browser's font engine as a ground truth via Canvas. 

Main capabilities include paragraph height and line count calculation without touching the DOM, manual line layouting, measuring line statistics and ranges, variable-width line layout, text wrapping for complex or Southeast Asian scripts via `Intl.Segmenter`, and rich-inline text flows handling mixed fonts, chips, icons, and images. It supports options such as `white-space: pre-wrap`, `word-break: keep-all`, and `letter-spacing`. 

Intended users are frontend developers building performance-sensitive web applications, chat interfaces, virtualized lists, masonry layouts, or custom text rendering engines in DOM, Canvas, and SVG environments. Notable technologies utilized include Canvas 2D, Unicode property escapes, and `Intl.Segmenter`.

name: open-source-mac-os-apps
description: 🚀 Awesome list of open source applications for macOS. https://t.me/s/opensourcemacosapps
summary: This repository is a curated list of free and open-source applications for macOS, featuring hundreds of native and cross-platform tools organized across 49 categories such as audio, development, productivity, graphics, security, and window management. Its primary goal is to help users discover open-source software for the Mac platform and encourage community contributions. The collection highlights tools built using prominent technologies including Swift, Objective-C, JavaScript, C++, Rust, Python, and TypeScript.

name: container
description: A tool for creating and running Linux containers using lightweight virtual machines on a Mac. It is written in Swift, and optimized for Apple silicon.
summary:
`container` is a Swift-written tool optimized for Apple silicon Macs, designed to create and run Linux containers as lightweight virtual machines. It consumes and produces OCI-compatible container images, allowing users to pull, run, build, and push images with standard container registries. 

The project leverages the Apple `Containerization` Swift package for low-level container, image, and process management, utilizing macOS virtualization and networking features. It is intended for developers working on macOS requiring local Linux container environments.

name: query
description: 🤖 Powerful asynchronous state management, server-state utilities and data fetching for the web. TS/JS, React Query, Solid Query, Svelte Query and Vue Query.
summary: TanStack Query is an asynchronous state management library designed to simplify fetching, caching, synchronizing, and updating server state. It features protocol-agnostic fetching supporting REST, GraphQL, and promises. Main capabilities include caching, refetching, pagination, infinite scroll, mutations, dependent queries, background updates, prefetching, cancellation, and React Suspense support.

name: mastodon
description: Your self-hosted, globally interconnected microblogging community
summary:
Mastodon is a free, open-source social network server based on the W3C ActivityPub standard, enabling users to publish text, links, pictures, and videos while communicating seamlessly across a federated network (the Fediverse). 

Main capabilities include a real-time chronological timeline, media attachments for images and videos, robust safety and moderation tools (such as private posts, phrase filtering, muting, blocking, and reporting systems), and an OAuth2 provider with REST and Streaming APIs supporting third-party applications. The platform targets individuals seeking decentralized social networking and server administrators wanting to host interoperable nodes.

Notable technologies used in the project include Ruby on Rails powering the REST API, PostgreSQL as the main database, Redis and Sidekiq for caching and queueing, Node.js driving the streaming API, and React.js alongside Redux for the dynamic interface. Additional requirements and tools include FFmpeg, Docker, and docker-compose configurations. The software is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License (AGPLv3).

name: academic-research-skills
description: Academic Research Skills for Claude Code: research → write → review → revise → finalize
summary:
Academic Research Skills for Claude Code is a comprehensive suite of AI skills designed to support academic research and publication from the initial research phase through peer review. Built with a human-in-the-loop philosophy, the platform automates tedious tasks such as bibliographic referencing, citation formatting, data verification, and logical consistency checks while leaving core decisions—such as defining research questions, choosing methodologies, and interpreting data—to the human researcher. 

The suite is organized into five main skills and an orchestrator:
- **Deep Research:** Offers 8 modes (including systematic reviews, PRISMA support, Socratic guidance, fact-checking, and literature reviews) powered by a multi-agent team and Semantic Scholar API verification.
- **Academic Paper:** Provides 11 modes for planning, drafting, revision coaching, abstract generation, and LaTeX/APA formatting.
- **Academic Paper Reviewer:** Delivers multi-perspective peer review using a journal-fit reviewer, dynamic reviewers, and a devil's advocate.
- **Academic Pipeline:** Orchestrates a 10-stage research workflow featuring automated integrity gates and collaboration evaluation.
- **SR-Screener:** Facilitates protocol-driven study screening with blinded reviewer subagents and PRISMA 2020 reporting.

The project notably integrates guardrails against common AI failure modes, including a Concession Threshold Protocol to prevent sycophancy, an intent-detection layer for Socratic mentoring, and strict artifact reproducibility and data-access level controls. It supports Markdown, DOCX, and LaTeX outputs and operates natively within Claude Code CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains environments.

name: kubernetes-the-hard-way
description: Bootstrap Kubernetes the hard way. No scripts.
summary:
Kubernetes The Hard Way is an educational tutorial designed for learners who want to understand the fundamentals of Kubernetes and how its core components fit together without using fully automated cluster deployment tools. 

The project provides a step-by-step guide to bootstrapping a basic Kubernetes cluster consisting of a single-node control plane and two worker nodes using four ARM64 or AMD64 virtual or physical machines. The curriculum covers prerequisites, jumpbox setup, provisioning compute resources and a Certificate Authority for TLS certificates, generating authentication configuration files and data encryption keys, bootstrapping an etcd cluster, setting up control plane and worker nodes, configuring `kubectl` for remote access, provisioning pod network routes, and running smoke tests.

Intended users are individuals seeking a deep, hands-on understanding of cluster bootstrapping tasks. Notable technologies utilized in the tutorial include Kubernetes v1.32.x, containerd v2.1.x, CNI v1.6.x, and etcd v3.6.x. The resulting clusters are not optimized or intended for production readiness.

name: alist
description: 🗂️A file list/WebDAV program that supports multiple storages, powered by Gin and Solidjs. / 一个支持多存储的文件列表/WebDAV程序，使用 Gin 和 Solidjs。
summary:
AList is a file list program and multi-storage management platform that supports a wide range of local, network, and cloud storage providers, including Aliyundrive, OneDrive, GoogleDrive, S3, Dropbox, BaiduNetdisk, FTP/SFTP, WebDAV, and SMB. 

Designed to be easy to deploy and out-of-the-box, the project provides comprehensive file management and preview capabilities. Main capabilities include web-based file operations (upload, download, delete, move, copy, and folder packaging), multi-threaded download acceleration, offline downloads, direct link copying, WebDAV support, and password-protected routes. It also features built-in previewers for documents, images (gallery mode), videos, audio (with subtitle and lyrics support), and Markdown files.

The project is built using the Gin web framework and SolidJS, and supports containerized deployment via Docker and Cloudflare Workers. It is intended for users seeking a centralized interface to organize, access, stream, and share files across multiple disparate cloud and local storage services.

name: ClickHouse
description: ClickHouse® is a real-time analytics database management system
summary: ClickHouse is an open-source, column-oriented database management system designed to generate analytical data reports in real time. Supported platforms include Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD, with installation available via shell script or through ClickHouse Cloud.

name: upscayl
description: 🆙 Upscayl - #1 Free and Open Source AI Image Upscaler for Linux, MacOS and Windows.
summary:
Upscayl is a free, open-source AI image upscaler designed to enlarge and enhance low-resolution and pixelated images without quality loss. Aimed at general users and developers requiring image enhancement, the application leverages advanced AI algorithms to upscale visuals. 

Main capabilities include batch upscaling, custom model support, and cross-platform installation. The software relies on notable technologies such as Real-ESRGAN, Vulkan architecture via the open-source backend upscayl-ncnn, and Node.js for development. Upscayl requires a Vulkan-compatible GPU to function.

name: PythonDataScienceHandbook
description: Python Data Science Handbook: full text in Jupyter Notebooks
summary:
The Python Data Science Handbook repository contains the complete text of the published book in the form of Jupyter notebooks. Its primary purpose is to provide an educational resource and executable code examples for data science practitioners, researchers, and scientists. The content introduces core Python libraries essential for data work, specifically IPython, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and Scikit-Learn. 

Intended users are individuals familiar with the Python language who want to learn data science tools and techniques. The repository enables users to read the material online, run code locally using provided requirements, or launch executable notebooks directly via Google Colab and Binder.

name: bulma
description: Modern CSS framework based on Flexbox
summary: Bulma is a modern CSS framework based on Flexbox. Its primary purpose is to provide a ready-to-use style layer for web projects, functioning as an environment-agnostic framework with no included JavaScript. Users can utilize the compiled CSS file out of the box or download the Sass source files to customize variables. Notable technologies utilized include CSS Flexbox, Sass, Autoprefixer, and PostCSS. It is compatible with recent versions of major web browsers including Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera, and Safari, with partial support for Internet Explorer 10+.

name: huginn
description: Create agents that monitor and act on your behalf.  Your agents are standing by!
summary:
Huginn is an open-source system designed to build agents that perform automated tasks online, functioning as a self-hosted, hackable alternative to IFTTT or Zapier. It enables users to read the web, monitor events, scrape websites, track locations, run custom JavaScript functions, and execute automated workflows by propagating events along a directed graph. 

The platform connects to numerous services and protocols, including HipChat, FTP, IMAP, Jabber, JIRA, MQTT, Nextbus, Pushbullet, Pushover, RSS, Bash, Slack, StubHub, translation APIs, Twilio, Twitter, Weibo, and WebHooks, alongside Amazon Mechanical Turk workflows via external agent gems. Intended for users who want complete control over their data on their own servers, Huginn is built using Ruby on Rails, supports MySQL and PostgreSQL databases, and provides deployment options via Docker, Heroku, OpenShift, and manual server installations.

name: airi
description: 💖🧸 Self hosted, you-owned Grok Companion, a container of souls of waifu, cyber livings to bring them into our worlds, wishing to achieve Neuro-sama's altitude. Capable of realtime voice chat, Minecraft, Factorio playing. Web / macOS / Windows supported.
summary:
Project AIRI is an open-source "soul container" designed to bring AI waifus, virtual characters, and digital companions into the real world. Heavily inspired by Neuro-sama, AIRI allows users to own and interact with a cyber living entity capable of chatting, streaming, and playing video games such as Minecraft, Factorio, and Kerbal Space Program across various platforms like Discord and Telegram.

The project features a comprehensive modular architecture consisting of a brain for reasoning and memory management (utilizing DuckDB WASM and local inference), ears for speech recognition and audio input, a mouth supporting multiple text-to-speech providers (such as ElevenLabs, Azure, OpenAI-compatible APIs, and Kokoro TTS), and a body supporting VRM and Live2D models with automatic blink, look-at, and idle animations. 

AIRI is intended for developers, AI enthusiasts, artists, and fans of virtual characters. Built with web technologies including WebGPU, WebAudio, Web Workers, and WebAssembly, it runs on modern web browsers and mobile devices via PWA, while also offering native desktop applications powered by Rust-based libraries like HuggingFace's `candle` to leverage NVIDIA CUDA and Apple Metal.

name: pandas
description: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more
summary:
Pandas is a fast, flexible, and expressive Python package designed for practical, real-world data analysis and manipulation of relational or labeled data. It serves as a high-level building block providing core data structures like `DataFrame` and `Series`. 

Main capabilities include handling missing data, size mutability for inserting and deleting columns, automatic and explicit data alignment, powerful group-by split-apply-combine operations, intelligent label-based slicing, fancy indexing, subsetting, merging, joining, reshaping, pivoting, and hierarchical axis labeling. Additionally, it offers robust input/output tools for CSV, Excel files, databases, and HDF5 formats, alongside specialized time series functionality such as date range generation, frequency conversion, and moving window statistics. 

The package is intended for developers and data analysts working with data structures. Notable technologies utilized include Python, NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython, and HDF5.

name: ruff
description: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.
summary:
Ruff is an extremely fast Python linter and code formatter written in Rust. It serves as an all-in-one replacement for tools like Flake8, Black, isort, pydocstyle, pyupgrade, and autoflake, executing up to 100x faster while integrating via a single common interface. 

Intended for Python developers and teams working on codebases of any scale, Ruff offers over 900 built-in lint rules with native re-implementations of popular plugins (such as flake8-bugbear), automatic error fixing, built-in caching, hierarchical configuration support (`pyproject.toml`, `ruff.toml`), and drop-in compatibility with Python 3.15. It can be installed via `pip`, `uv`, `pipx`, standalone installers, Homebrew, or Conda, and includes first-party editor integrations like VS Code, pre-commit hooks, and GitHub Actions. Ruff is backed by Astral and utilized in major open-source projects such as Apache Airflow, FastAPI, Pandas, and SciPy.

name: brew
description: 🍺 The Package Manager for Everywhere
summary: Homebrew is the missing package manager for macOS (and Linux), designed to help users install the open-source tools and software they need. It provides an infrastructure to manage software packages through command-line utilities such as formulae and casks, supporting package installation, updates, dependencies management, and environment maintenance via tools like `brew bundle`, `brew update`, `brew doctor`, and `brew audit`. The project is intended for developers, system administrators, and general users seeking streamlined software management on Unix-like operating systems. Homebrew is a non-profit, volunteer-run project licensed under the BSD 2-Clause "Simplified" License.

name: hacker-scripts
description: Based on a true story
summary:
Hacker Scripts is a collection of automation scripts based on a true story about a terminal-loving build engineer who automated everyday tasks. The project's purpose is to provide implementations of these humorous and practical scripts designed to automate communication, database management, and office hardware interaction. 

Main capabilities include:
- `smack-my-bitch-up.sh`: Automatically texts a spouse with random late-work excuses via Twilio based on active evening SSH sessions.
- `kumar-asshole.sh`: Scans a Gmail inbox for client DBA emails containing distress keywords, automatically rolls back a staging database via SSH, and replies with reassuring messages.
- `hangover.sh`: Automatically sends work-from-home notifications on scheduled dates if no interactive morning SSH sessions are detected.
- `fucking-coffee.sh`: Connects to a networked, Linux-based office coffee machine via a TCP telnet socket to time and brew a latte precisely as the user walks to the machine.

Intended users are developers, system administrators, and enthusiasts interested in terminal-based automation, cron jobs, and humorous shell scripting. Notable technologies used include Ruby, Shell, Cron, Twilio, and Gmail integration.

name: terraform
description: Terraform enables you to safely and predictably create, change, and improve infrastructure. It is a source-available tool that codifies APIs into declarative configuration files that can be shared amongst team members, treated as code, edited, reviewed, and versioned.
summary:
Terraform is a tool for building, changing, and versioning infrastructure safely and efficiently. It manages both popular service providers and custom in-house solutions. 

Key capabilities include Infrastructure as Code using high-level configuration syntax to create versionable, shareable blueprints; Execution Plans that generate preview steps prior to applying changes; a Resource Graph that maps all resources and parallelizes the creation and modification of non-dependent resources; and Change Automation to apply complex changesets with minimal human interaction and reduced error risk. 

The project is intended for operators and developers managing datacenter infrastructure. This repository contains Terraform core, comprising the command line interface and the main graph engine. Providers are implemented as plugins and downloaded automatically from the Terraform Registry. Terraform is licensed under the Business Source License 1.1.

name: x64dbg
description: An open-source user mode debugger for Windows. Optimized for reverse engineering and malware analysis.
summary: x64dbg is an open-source binary debugger for Windows designed for malware analysis and reverse engineering executables without available source code. Intended for security analysts and reverse engineers, the tool supports both 32-bit and 64-bit executables and features a comprehensive plugin system. Notable underlying technologies and components include TitanEngine Community Edition for the debugger core, Zydis for disassembly, XEDParse and asmjit for assembly, Scylla for import reconstruction, Jansson for JSON processing, and lz4 for database compression.

name: Made-With-ML
description: Learn how to develop, deploy and iterate on production-grade ML applications.
summary:
Made With ML is an educational course and repository designed to teach developers, college graduates, and technical leaders how to design, develop, deploy, iterate on, and scale production-grade machine learning applications. The project bridges experimentation and production by emphasizing first principles, software engineering best practices, MLOps, and CI/CD automation without requiring new programming languages.

Key capabilities include end-to-end ML workflows encompassing data ingestion, model training, hyperparameter tuning, experiment tracking, evaluation, inference, and scalable model serving. Notable technologies utilized include Python, Ray, Ray Serve, Anyscale, MLflow, pytest, GitHub Actions, and Jupyter notebooks.

name: tmux
description: tmux source code
summary:
tmux is a terminal multiplexer designed to enable multiple terminals to be created, accessed, and controlled from a single screen. It supports detaching sessions to run in the background and reattaching them later. The project is intended for users operating on OpenBSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, Linux, macOS, and Solaris. 

Notable dependencies include libevent 2.x and ncurses. Building the project requires a C compiler (such as gcc or clang), make, pkg-config, and a suitable yacc implementation (yacc or bison), with optional support for the utempter library.

name: spotube
description: 🎧 Open source music streaming app! Available for both desktop & mobile!
summary:
Spotube is a cross-platform, open-source music streaming application that allows users to bring their own metadata, playlists, and audio sources via community or custom plugins. Built as an extensible alternative for the decentralized music streaming era, it operates locally without telemetry, diagnostics, or data collection. 

Main capabilities include plugin-powered platform support, freely downloadable tracks with tagged metadata, time-synced lyrics, local playback control, and native performance with low data usage. The application targets users seeking an open-source, lightweight streaming client across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS. 

Spotube is developed using Flutter and Dart, incorporating technologies such as MPV, MusicBrainz, Listenbrainz, Piped, Invidious, yt-dlp, LRCLib, and Riverpod.

name: htmx
description: </> htmx - high power tools for HTML
summary: htmx is a small, dependency-free, and extendable JavaScript library that allows developers to access AJAX, CSS Transitions, WebSockets, and Server Sent Events directly in HTML using attributes. Designed as the successor to intercooler.js, the project's purpose is to complete HTML as a hypertext by removing arbitrary constraints on HTTP requests, trigger events, HTTP methods, and screen replacement scopes, enabling the creation of modern user interfaces with the simplicity and power of REST and HATEOAS. Intended for web developers building user interfaces, htmx integrates directly via script tags or through the `htmx.org` npm package.

name: metabase
description: The easy-to-use open source Business Intelligence and Embedded Analytics tool that lets everyone work with data :bar_chart:
summary: Metabase is an open-source data analysis and business intelligence tool designed for everyone in a company to ask questions and learn from data without needing SQL, while still offering a native SQL editor for complex queries. Its main capabilities include building interactive dashboards, utilizing AI via Metabot or custom AI agents, creating long-form documents for analysis, transforming raw data into analytics-ready tables using Data Studio, setting up data alerts, and scheduling dashboard subscriptions via email, Slack, or webhooks. Additionally, it supports Git versioning, content curation in a Library, granular permissions, and embedding components or entire applications. Intended users include team members seeking accessible data insights, data analysts, developers embedding analytics, and administrators managing enterprise data stacks. Metabase supports numerous databases through official and community drivers, and is available in both an AGPL-licensed Open Source edition and commercial editions.

name: LocalAI
description: LocalAI is the open-source AI engine. Run any model - LLMs, vision, voice, image, video - on any hardware. No GPU required.
summary:
LocalAI is an open-source AI engine that allows users to run large language models (LLMs), vision, voice, image, and video models locally on any hardware without requiring a GPU. Designed with a composable, modular architecture, it features a small core that pulls separate best-in-class backends on demand. 

Main capabilities include drop-in API compatibility with OpenAI, Anthropic, and ElevenLabs across text generation, speech-to-text, text-to-audio, image generation, embeddings, vision, object detection, and reranker APIs. It also includes built-in autonomous AI agents with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, multi-user authentication with quotas, and a distributed mode for horizontal scaling.

Intended users include developers, privacy-focused organizations, and system administrators seeking a self-hosted alternative to cloud-based AI services. Notable technologies and upstream engines integrated or wrapped by the project include `llama.cpp`, `vLLM`, `whisper.cpp`, `stable-diffusion`, `MLX`, `MLX-VLM`, `SGLang`, `transformers`, and several native C/C++/GGML engines developed by the team (such as `vllm.cpp`, `parakeet.cpp`, and `voice-detect.cpp`), with hardware acceleration support for NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Apple Silicon Metal, Vulkan, and NVIDIA Jetson.

name: aider
description: aider is AI pair programming in your terminal
summary:
Aider is a command-line AI pair programming tool that allows developers to write new projects or modify existing codebases using large language models (LLMs) such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek R1 & Chat V3, and OpenAI o1, o3-mini, and GPT-4o, alongside support for local models. 

Intended for software developers and engineers, Aider provides a range of capabilities including codebase mapping for large projects, native Git integration with automated commits and diff management, IDE integration via code comments, and support for over 100 programming languages like Python, JavaScript, Rust, Ruby, Go, C++, and PHP. Additional features include visual context integration via images and web pages, voice-to-code inputs, automatic linting and testing with error-fixing capabilities, and workflows for web chat interfaces.

name: new-api
description: A unified AI model hub for aggregation & distribution. It supports cross-converting various LLMs into OpenAI-compatible, Claude-compatible, or Gemini-compatible formats. A centralized gateway for personal and enterprise model management.
summary:
New API is a self-hosted AI gateway designed for applications, agents, and teams to manage model access, routing, usage quotas, access control, and costs in one centralized platform. It connects upstream model services—such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, DeepSeek, and Qwen—and exposes a consistent API to clients. 

Main capabilities include protocol and endpoint support for OpenAI Chat, Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini, embeddings, rerank, audio/image generation, and WebSockets via RelayKit. It provides features for channel priority and weight-based routing, expression-based pricing, usage logs, audit logging, and asynchronous task execution using JavaScript plugins. Access control includes user/group management, fine-grained API key restrictions, OAuth/OIDC, passkeys, and two-factor authentication. A multilingual web console is also included.

Intended users include teams, organizations, and administrators operating private multi-model services, managing API access, or deploying AI gateways. Notable technologies used include Go and Gin for the backend, React 19, TypeScript, Rsbuild, TanStack, and Tailwind CSS 4 for the web console, with support for SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, and ClickHouse databases.

name: awesome-design-patterns
description: A curated list of software and architecture related design patterns.
summary:
This repository is a curated list of software and architectural design patterns. It serves as a reference for developers, architects, and engineers looking for reusable solutions to common problems across various domains. 

The collection covers programming language-specific design patterns for technologies such as C#, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Node.js, PHP, Python, React, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Swift, TypeScript, and Vue.js. It also categorizes general, cloud, and serverless architectures, alongside microservices, distributed systems, Internet of Things (IoT), big data, and machine learning patterns. Additionally, the repository includes resources on database storage (SQL and NoSQL), DevOps and containerization tools like Kubernetes, mobile development (iOS and Android), front-end development, security architecture, and recommended books.

name: awesome-remote-job
description: A curated list of awesome remote jobs and resources. Inspired by https://github.com/vinta/awesome-python
summary:
This repository is a curated, multilingual list of remote working resources, guides, and tools designed for telecommuters, digital nomads, and distributed teams. The project aims to provide comprehensive information to help individuals find remote employment, transition to location-independent lifestyles, and manage distributed organizations effectively.

Main capabilities include directories of remote job boards and aggregators, lists of companies with "remote DNA," relocation incentives, housing and co-working spaces, interview preparation platforms, newsletters, podcasts, and digital collaboration software. The content covers communication tools, project management applications, HR platforms, legal and financial guides for independent contractors, and community spaces. 

Intended users include remote job seekers, software developers, freelancers, digital nomads, and managers of distributed teams. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced across member companies and tools include Ruby on Rails, Python, Go, React, Vue.js, JavaScript, Drupal, WordPress, Kubernetes, and AWS, alongside collaboration applications like Slack, Zoom, and Notion.

name: julia
description: The Julia Programming Language
summary:
Julia is a high-level, high-performance dynamic programming language designed for technical computing, numerical analysis, and computational science. The repository contains the official Julia source code, standard library modules, command-line interface, test suites, and documentation. 

Intended for developers, researchers, scientists, and data practitioners, Julia provides an interactive REPL environment and supports integration with various editors and IDEs, including VS Code, Emacs, Vim, and Jupyter or Pluto notebooks. Key technologies and tools associated with the ecosystem include the `juliaup` binary installer, Git, and GNU make for compiling from source.

name: awesome-java
description: A curated list of awesome frameworks, libraries and software for the Java programming language.
summary: Awesome Java is a curated, categorized list of noteworthy Java frameworks, libraries, tools, and learning resources designed for software developers and engineers working within the Java and JVM ecosystem. The repository covers dozens of technical categories ranging from artificial intelligence, database access, networking, and security to testing, build tools, high-performance computing, and web development. Prominent technologies and tools referenced include Spring, Hibernate, Apache Maven, Gradle, Micronaut, Quarkus, JUnit, and the Java Development Kit (JDK) implementations, helping developers discover production-ready libraries and utilities.

name: obsidian-skills
description: Agent skills for Obsidian. Teach your agent to use Obsidian CLI and open formats including Markdown, Bases, JSON Canvas.
summary:
This project provides a collection of Agent Skills designed for use with Obsidian, following the Agent Skills specification for compatibility with agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Open Code. 

The repository's purpose is to equip AI agents with domain-specific capabilities for working within Obsidian environments. Its main capabilities include:
- **obsidian-markdown**: Creating and editing Obsidian Flavored Markdown with wikilinks, embeds, callouts, and properties.
- **obsidian-bases**: Managing Obsidian Bases with views, filters, formulas, and summaries.
- **json-canvas**: Working with JSON Canvas files (`.canvas`) featuring nodes, edges, groups, and connections.
- **obsidian-cli**: Interacting with Obsidian vaults, plugins, and themes via the Obsidian CLI.
- **defuddle**: Extracting clean markdown from web pages to eliminate clutter and save tokens.
- **knap**: Rendering Markdown templates from JSON or CSV data for batch file generation.

Intended users include developers and vault managers utilizing AI coding assistants and skills-compatible agents to automate tasks within Obsidian. Notable technologies and formats referenced include Obsidian Flavored Markdown, JSON Canvas, Defuddle, Knap, and the Obsidian CLI.

name: qlib
description: Qlib is an AI-oriented Quant investment platform that aims to use AI tech to empower Quant Research, from exploring ideas to implementing productions. Qlib supports diverse ML modeling paradigms, including supervised learning, market dynamics modeling, and RL, and is now equipped with https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent to automate R&D process.
summary:
Qlib is an open-source, AI-oriented quantitative investment platform designed to support the entire quantitative investment chain, from initial exploration and alpha seeking to risk modeling, portfolio optimization, and order execution. It is intended for quantitative researchers, developers, and investors seeking to apply artificial intelligence to financial markets.

The platform provides a comprehensive machine learning pipeline that handles data processing, model training, and back-testing. Main capabilities include supervised learning for non-linear pattern mining from financial data, market dynamics modeling using adaptive concept drift, and reinforcement learning for continuous investment decisions and trading strategy optimization. It also features automated factor mining and model optimization via integration with RD-Agent. 

Qlib supports various machine learning and deep learning models—such as LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, LSTM, GRU, GATs, Transformer, and TabNet—as well as specialized dataset configurations like Alpha158 and Alpha360. Built with modular components, it supports both offline and high-performance online data deployment modes. The platform is implemented in Python and utilizes technologies such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Cython, and Pandas.

name: slidev
description: Presentation Slides for Developers
summary:
Slidev is a presentation slides tool built specifically for developers. Its primary purpose is to enable users to create, customize, and deliver presentations using Markdown while leveraging the power of HTML and Vue components. 

Main capabilities include built-in code highlighting, live coding, themable designs distributed via npm packages, on-demand styling via UnoCSS, interactive Vue components, presenter mode, slide drawing and annotations, LaTeX math equations, Mermaid-based diagrams, direct access to icon sets, integrated and VSCode extension editors, built-in recording with camera views, and export options to PDF, PNGs, or PPTX. It features instant reloading powered by Vite.

Intended users are developers looking for a fast, hackable, and content-focused presentation tool. 

Notable technologies used in the project include Vite, Vue 3, Markdown, UnoCSS, Shiki, Monaco Editor, RecordRTC, VueUse, Iconify, Drauu, KaTeX, and Mermaid.

name: design-patterns-for-humans
description: An ultra-simplified explanation to design patterns
summary:
This project provides an ultra-simplified guide to software design patterns, explaining complex concepts in an accessible way. Its primary purpose is to help developers understand and apply design patterns through clear conceptual explanations and programmatic examples. 

The repository covers three major categories of design patterns:
- **Creational Design Patterns:** Simple Factory, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype, and Singleton.
- **Structural Design Patterns:** Adapter, Bridge, Composite, Decorator, Facade, Flyweight, and Proxy.
- **Behavioral Design Patterns:** Chain of Responsibility, Command, Iterator, Mediator, Memento, Observer, Visitor, Strategy, State, and Template Method.

The intended users are software developers and engineers seeking a straightforward reference for design patterns. The project's code examples are implemented in PHP 7, and the concepts are demonstrated using object-oriented programming principles.

name: algorithm-visualizer
description: :fireworks:Interactive Online Platform that Visualizes Algorithms from Code
summary: Algorithm Visualizer is an interactive online platform and web application designed to bring algorithms to life through visualization, helping students, teachers, and professionals understand algorithmic behavior. The platform visualizes algorithms directly from code written in multiple programming languages by interpreting commands via specialized visualization libraries known as tracers. Users can explore a collection of tutorials, articles, and videos alongside visual demonstrations. The ecosystem comprises multiple repositories including the main React and Redux web application, a Node.js backend server handling APIs and code compilation, an algorithms repository containing menu visualizations, and language-specific tracer libraries. Technologies used include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Redux, and Node.js.

name: cal.diy
description: Scheduling infrastructure for absolutely everyone.
summary:
Cal.diy is a community-driven, open-source scheduling platform and a fork of Cal.com with all enterprise and commercial code removed. Designed for individuals and self-hosters, it provides full control over scheduling infrastructure without requiring commercial dependencies, licenses, or accounts. 

Main capabilities include scheduling management, setup wizards, optional rate limiting via Unkey, and integrations with services such as Google Calendar, Microsoft Graph, Zoom, Daily.co, Basecamp 3, HubSpot, Webex, ZohoCRM, Zoho Calendar, Zoho Bigin, and Pipedrive. 

The project is intended for personal, non-production use by self-hosters and developers comfortable with server administration, database management, and data security. 

Notable technologies used include Next.js, React.js, TypeScript, tRPC, Tailwind CSS, Prisma.io, PostgreSQL, Docker, and Daily.co.

name: nanobot
description: Ultra-lightweight, open-source, self-hosted personal AI agent framework in Python with WebUI, tools, memory, MCP, multi-agent workflows, automation, and chat apps
summary:
nanobot is an ultra-lightweight, self-hosted personal AI agent framework written in Python. It provides a readable core architecture that can run via a browser-based WebUI, a native terminal UI (TUI), command-line interfaces, or various chat applications including Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, and email. 

Main capabilities include model routing, multi-agent delegation, integrated tool use (files, shell, web search/fetch, MCP integrations, image generation, cron jobs, and subagents), long-term memory handling via Dream, long-horizon goal execution, and scheduled automations. It also exposes a Python SDK and an OpenAI-compatible API for custom integrations and gateway deployments. 

The framework is intended for developers, individuals, and teams seeking a self-hosted, customizable AI assistant and automation runtime without heavy monolithic platforms. Notable technologies utilized include Python 3.11+, WebSockets, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Bun for frontend asset management.

name: dayjs
description: ⏰ Day.js 2kB immutable date-time library alternative to Moment.js with the same modern API
summary: Day.js is a minimalist JavaScript library designed to parse, validate, manipulate, and display dates and times in modern browsers. Featuring a lightweight footprint of approximately 2kB, it provides an immutable, chainable, and internationalization-supported API that is largely compatible with Moment.js. Intended for JavaScript developers seeking a fast alternative to Moment.js, Day.js supports all browsers and allows functionality to be extended using independent modules through a plugin system.

name: bevy
description: A refreshingly simple data-driven game engine built in Rust
summary:
Bevy is a free, open-source, data-driven game engine built in the Rust programming language. It is designed to offer a complete 2D and 3D feature set while remaining simple, modular, and fast. The project utilizes a data-oriented architecture based on the Entity Component System (ECS) paradigm, enabling parallelized execution of application logic and customizable cargo features. 

Intended for game developers and programmers working in Rust—ranging from beginners to power users—Bevy emphasizes fast compilation and flexibility, allowing users to use only the modules they need and replace those they do not. Notable technologies used include the Rust compiler and cargo toolchain, alongside a modular plugin system centered around an `App` structure. The repository is dual-licensed under the MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses.

name: shannon
description: Shannon is an AI pentester for web applications and APIs. It analyzes your source code, identifies attack vectors, and executes real exploits to prove vulnerabilities before they reach production.
summary:
Shannon, developed by Keygraph, is an autonomous AI pentester designed for web applications and APIs. Its purpose is to bridge the security gap in fast-paced software development by combining automated security code analysis with live exploitation, testing applications for vulnerabilities before they reach production. 

Shannon is intended for developers, security teams, and red teamers who need continuous, on-demand penetration testing in local environments or CI/CD pipelines. It is distributed as an open-source command-line tool and is also the underlying engine for the commercial Keygraph Enterprise Platform.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Proof-of-Concept Verification:** Executes real exploits and reports only vulnerabilities confirmed with a reproducible proof of concept (no exploit, no report), minimizing speculative noise.
- **Autonomous Execution:** Performs recon, architecture and data-flow analysis, active exploitation, and reporting from a single command.
- **Advanced Security Analysis:** Maps trust boundaries, interfaces, and assets to generate targeted attack paths for OWASP-focused threats such as injection, XSS, SSRF, and broken authentication/authorization.
- **Authenticated Testing:** Supports credentialed scans, login flows, TOTP, email authentication, and rules of engagement.
- **Multi-Format Reporting:** Produces evidence-rich PDF and Markdown reports, alongside structured JSON and SARIF 2.1.0 formats.
- **CI/CD Integration:** Integrates natively with GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD to gate releases based on severity thresholds.
- **Private and Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK):** Operates locally via Docker with ephemeral workspaces, keeping source code and model traffic within user-controlled infrastructure.

**Notable Technologies:**
- **Supported AI Providers:** Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, AWS Bedrock, and any compatible Pi harness catalog provider, with support for custom base URLs, proxies, LLM gateways, and local models (via Ollama, vLLM, or LM Studio).
- **Runtimes & Tools:** Node.js (via `npx`), Docker, Docker Compose, Playwright CLI, and Mantis.

name: awesome-react-components
description: Curated List of React Components & Libraries.
summary:
This repository is a curated, non-comprehensive list of "awesome" React components, libraries, frameworks, utilities, and developer tools. It focuses on unique, problem-solving, beautiful, and actively maintained packages that are not overly ubiquitous, often highlighting fresh code commits and maintainer commentary. 

The collection spans numerous categories including UI components (such as data grids, tables, infinite scroll, modals, notifications, charts, and rich text editors), layout engines, animation tools, full UI frameworks (like Material UI, Chakra UI, and Mantine), device input handlers, and architectural state stores (such as Redux and Zustand). It also features utilities for form logic, internationalization (i18n), server-side rendering, performance optimization, and testing. 

Intended for React developers seeking specialized, high-quality third-party libraries and tools to build web applications, dashboards, and user interfaces, the repository leverages standard web technologies centered around JavaScript, TypeScript, React, CSS, and D3.

name: type-challenges
description: Collection of TypeScript type challenges with online judge
summary:
This project is a collection of TypeScript type challenges designed to help developers understand how the TypeScript type system works, write custom utility types, and improve project maintainability. It provides a wide range of coding exercises categorized by difficulty—from warm-up and easy to medium, hard, and extreme—covering advanced type-level programming concepts such as conditional types, template literal types, recursion, and variadic tuples. 

Intended for developers looking to master TypeScript's Turing-complete type system, the repository supports interactive learning through a TypeScript Playground plugin, a VS Code extension, and local development setups via Node.js and pnpm.

name: react-bits
description: An open source collection of animated, interactive & fully customizable React components for building memorable websites.
summary:
React Bits is a creative library of over 200 animated React components, text animations, backgrounds, and micro interactions designed to help developers build interfaces faster. The project offers copy-paste ready components with minimal dependencies and provides four variants for each item: JS-CSS, JS-TW, TS-CSS, and TS-TW. 

Intended for React developers seeking customizable UI animations, the repository also includes supplementary creative tools such as Background Studio for animated backgrounds, Shape Magic for inner rounded corner generation, and Texture Lab for applying effects like noise, dithering, and ASCII to images and videos. Installation is supported via CLI tools like shadcn and jsrepo, or through manual code copying. Technologies utilized include React, TypeScript, JavaScript, CSS, and Tailwind CSS.

name: pixijs
description: The HTML5 Creation Engine: Create beautiful digital content with the fastest, most flexible 2D WebGL renderer.
summary: PixiJS is a fast, lightweight 2D HTML5 creation engine and graphics library designed for the web and cross-platform applications. It enables developers to build rich, interactive graphics across all devices utilizing WebGL and WebGPU renderers. Main capabilities include an asset loader, full mouse and multi-touch support, flexible text rendering, primitive and SVG drawing, dynamic textures, masking, powerful filters, and advanced blend modes. The project features an easy-to-use yet powerful API and natively supports TypeScript, utilizing `@webgpu/types` or `@types/web` depending on the TypeScript version. Intended users are web developers and creators building high-performance 2D visual applications and interactive experiences.

name: RxJava
description: RxJava – Reactive Extensions for the JVM – a library for composing asynchronous and event-based programs using observable sequences for the Java VM.
summary:
RxJava is a Java VM implementation of Reactive Extensions, serving as a library for composing asynchronous and event-based programs by using observable sequences. It extends the observer pattern to support data and event sequences through declarative operators while abstracting away low-level threading, synchronization, thread-safety, and concurrent data structures. 

The project's main capabilities include supporting asynchronous sequences, backpressure handling, parallel processing, thread scheduling, and type conversions. Core base classes comprise `Flowable`, `Observable`, `Single`, `Completable`, `Maybe`, and `Streamable`. Intended users are JVM developers building concurrent, event-driven, and reactive applications.

Notable technologies and standards used include Java (targeting native Java 26 implementation in version 4.x), `java.util.concurrent.Flow`, Virtual Threads, JPMS, OSGi, the Reactive Streams specification and Test Compatibility Kit, and Gradle/Maven for dependency management.

name: JeecgBoot
description: 【低代码v2.0，一句话即可生成整个系统】企业级AI低代码平台，一键生成前后端代码甚至整个系统。 AI Skills 一句话画流程、设计表单、生成报表、大屏。内置 AI应用平台涵盖：AI聊天、知识库、流程编排、MCP插件等，兼容主流大模型。引领AI低代码「Skills 生成 → 在线配置 → 代码生成 → 手工合并->AI修改」开发模式，解决 Java 项目 90% 重复工作，提高效率又不失灵活。
summary:
JeecgBoot 是一款企业级 AI 低代码开发平台，集成了低代码开发、AI 应用平台和 AI 知识库核心能力。其主要功能涵盖自然语言编程（AI Skills）、一句话生成系统、在线表单与零代码开发、强大的前后端代码生成器、AI 聊天助手、AI 流程编排、MCP 与插件管理、RAG 知识库问答、BPM 工作流、JimuReport 报表及 JimuBI 数据大屏。平台旨在帮助开发者解决重复编码工作，支持“AI生成 → 在线配置 → 代码生成 → 手工合并”的开发模式，大幅提升开发效率并保持源码级扩展性。

平台面向企业开发者与业务人员，适用于 OA、ERP、CRM、MIS、SaaS 及多租户行业数字化系统的开发。后端基于 Spring Boot 4、Spring Cloud Alibaba、MyBatis-Plus、langchain4j 和 Apache Shiro，前端采用 Vue3、TypeScript、Vite、Ant Design Vue 和 Pinia，并提供基于 Uniapp 的多端适配移动端框架（支持 APP、小程序、H5 及鸿蒙）。项目支持单体和微服务架构的无缝切换，兼容 MySQL、Oracle、PostgreSQL、达梦及人大金仓等主流与国产数据库。

name: GitHubDaily
description: 坚持分享 GitHub 上高质量、有趣实用的开源技术教程、开发者工具、编程网站、技术资讯。A list cool, interesting projects of GitHub.
summary:
GitHubDaily is a developer-focused curation platform and repository established in October 2015 to help developers discover trending open-source projects, track cutting-edge technological developments, and improve programming skills through source code reading. The project aggregates, categorizes, and shares over 10,000 open-source repositories, technical tutorials, developer tools, programming websites, and mature applications across multiple social media platforms, including WeChat, Weibo, Zhihu, and X (formerly Twitter). 

Intended for software developers, engineers, and technology enthusiasts at all levels, GitHubDaily maintains annual review indexes (dating from 2018 through 2025) that classify curated tools into domains such as AI utilities, learning tutorials, developer tools, web scrapers, automation frameworks, data science libraries, and productivity software. The repository relies on community contributions via GitHub issues and pull requests to continuously update its comprehensive resource lists.

name: Projects
description: :page_with_curl: A list of practical projects that anyone can solve in any programming language.
summary:
This repository, compiled by Karan Goel, provides a curated list of practical programming projects categorized across multiple domains to help developers build applications in any language. The project categories include Numbers, Classic Algorithms, Graph, Data Structures, Text, Networking, Classes, Threading, Web, Files, Databases, Graphics and Multimedia, and Security. 

The repository is intended for programmers seeking hands-on project ideas to practice their coding skills, implement algorithms, and build functional software ranging from simple utilities to complex systems. Notable problem areas span mathematical computations, graph traversals (such as Dijkstra’s Algorithm and Eulerian Paths), data structures like inverted indexes, networking tools (port scanners and FTP programs), database utilities, and cryptographic ciphers. Contributors can submit implementations to a companion solutions repository or propose new projects following the repository's guidelines.

name: discourse
description: A platform for community discussion. Free, open, simple.
summary:
Discourse is a 100% open-source community platform designed for hosting discussion forums and real-time chat. Intended for organizations and individuals seeking complete control over their site infrastructure, the platform enables users to create discussion topics, connect in real time, customize the experience with themes, and extend functionality via plugins such as Discourse AI and the Data Explorer. 

The project's backend is a RESTful API built with Ruby on Rails, while the frontend utilizes Ember.js. PostgreSQL serves as the main data store, and Redis is used for caching and transient data. Supported development environments include Docker, macOS, Ubuntu, Debian, and Windows, with minimum requirements including Ruby 3.4+, PostgreSQL 15, and Redis 7.

name: moment
description: Parse, validate, manipulate, and display dates in javascript.
summary: Moment.js is a JavaScript date library designed for parsing, validating, manipulating, and formatting dates. It is an OpenJS Foundation project distributed under the MIT license. Currently operating as a legacy project in maintenance mode, it does not accept new features. The library can be installed using package managers such as npm, yarn, or bun.

name: gogs
description: The painless way to host your own Git service
summary:
Gogs is a painless, self-hosted Git service built with Go, distributed as an independent binary supporting Linux, macOS, Windows, and ARM-based systems. It is designed for individuals and teams seeking a simple, stable, and extensible version control platform. 

Main capabilities include repository and organization management, SSH, HTTP, and HTTPS access protocols, webhooks (Slack, Discord, Dingtalk), Git hooks, deploy keys, Git LFS, issue tracking, pull requests, wikis, protected branches, and repository migration or mirroring. It also features a web file and wiki editor, Jupyter Notebook and PDF rendering, and localization across 31 languages. Authentication options include SMTP, LDAP, reverse proxy, GitHub.com, and GitHub Enterprise with 2FA. 

Database backends supported include PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite3, and compatible protocol variants. The software has minimal hardware requirements, running efficiently on low-resource environments such as Raspberry Pi devices or small cloud instances.

name: nvm
description: The Node.js version manager for Windows.
summary:
NVM for Windows is a Node.js version manager designed for Windows developers. It allows users to manage and switch between multiple Node.js versions, featuring support for per-directory version pinning, automatic installation of missing versions and default global modules, parallel simultaneous installations, user-defined aliases, and offline air-gapped downloads. 

The project operates without requiring mandatory administrator privileges and offers two operational modes: a shim mode written in Zig that avoids symlinks, and a link mode utilizing junctions with symlink fallback. It provides native integrations with Windows Apps, the Windows Event Viewer, the Windows Registry, and the Desktop Notification Center. Intended users include individual developers as well as IT administrators managing controlled environments through MSI/MST installers, Microsoft Intune, Active Directory, and Entra integration.

name: Summer2027-Internships
description: Summer 2027 software engineering, data science, AI, quant, product management, and hardware internship postings. Updated daily by Simplify and Pitt CSC.

name: acme.sh
description: A pure Unix shell script ACME client for SSL / TLS certificate automation
summary:
acme.sh is an ACME protocol client written purely in shell script (compatible with Bash, dash, and sh) with no Python dependencies. It enables system administrators and developers to automatically issue, renew, and install SSL/TLS certificates—including ECDSA, SAN, and wildcard certificates—from CAs such as ZeroSSL, Let's Encrypt, SSL.com, and Google Public CA. 

The project supports multiple validation and integration modes, including Webroot, Standalone (HTTP and TLS-ALPN), Apache, Nginx, automated DNS APIs, manual DNS, and persistent DNS modes. It incorporates RFC 9773 ACME Renewal Information (ARI) for intelligent renewal scheduling and automatically manages cron jobs for unattended updates without requiring root/sudoer access for installation. Tested across a vast array of Unix-like operating systems and platforms (including Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, macOS, Windows via Cygwin, and Docker), acme.sh serves as a lightweight, robust tool for automating certificate lifecycles.

name: exo
description: Run frontier AI locally.
summary:
exo connects multiple user devices into a distributed AI cluster, enabling the execution of frontier AI models that exceed the capacity of a single device. It features automatic device discovery, topology-aware auto-parallelization, tensor parallelism (model sharding), and day-0 support for RDMA over Thunderbolt. 

Designed primarily for developers and power users seeking local AI execution, exo uses MLX as its inference backend and MLX distributed for communication on macOS, with CPU support currently available on Linux. It provides multiple API-compatible interfaces, including OpenAI Chat/Responses APIs, Claude Messages API, and Ollama API, allowing seamless integration with existing tools and clients like OpenWebUI. Additionally, users can load custom models directly from the HuggingFace hub and manage clusters via a built-in dashboard. Notable technologies used include Python, Rust, Node.js, MLX, and libp2p.

name: big-list-of-naughty-strings
description: The Big List of Naughty Strings is a list of strings which have a high probability of causing issues when used as user-input data.
summary:
The Big List of Naughty Strings is an evolving collection of strings with a high probability of causing issues when used as user-input data. The project aims to assist both automated and manual QA testing by revealing string-validation issues and edge cases such as unexpected Unicode characters. 

The repository provides `blns.txt`, which consists of newline-delimited strings divided into sections via comment headers for manual reading and copy-pasting, along with a `blns.json` file containing a clean array of strings for programmatic access. A Python script is included in the `scripts` folder to generate the JSON file from the text file. The intended users are software quality assurance engineers and developers testing software they own and manage. Third-party packages implementing the list are available for Node, .NET, PHP, and C++.

name: textgen
description: Open-source desktop app for local LLMs. Text, vision, tool-calling, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API. 100% private.
summary:
TextGen is a 100% offline, open-source desktop and web application designed for running local Large Language Models (LLMs) with zero telemetry. Intended for users seeking private AI capabilities, it supports text generation, vision/multimodal interactions, file attachments, and tool-calling with custom functions and MCP servers. 

The application offers multiple chat and instruction modes formatted via Jinja2 templates, a free-form notebook tab, LoRA fine-tuning for multi-turn chat or raw text datasets, and a dedicated image generation tab for diffusers models like Z-Image-Turbo. It provides an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API for drop-in replacements, along with community extensions such as text-to-speech, voice input, and translation. 

TextGen integrates several notable model backends, including llama.cpp, ik_llama.cpp, Transformers, ExLlamaV3, and TensorRT-LLM, with compatibility for GGUF models. It features portable builds across Linux, Windows, and macOS with CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, and CPU options.

name: GitNexus
description: GitNexus: The Zero-Server Code Intelligence Engine
summary:
GitNexus is a context engine and knowledge graph tool for enterprise codebases. It indexes repositories into a knowledge graph tracking dependencies, call chains, clusters, and execution flows, exposing this structure through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, custom prompts, and resources so AI coding agents can reliably navigate and analyze code. 

Intended users include developers and AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity, and Windsurf seeking deep architectural clarity to prevent broken call chains and missed dependencies.

Main capabilities include repository analysis, multi-file coordinated refactoring, blast-radius impact analysis, path tracing, semantic and hybrid search (BM25, vector search, RRF), multi-repository management through repository groups, automated architecture documentation (wiki) generation, pre-commit change detection, and an interactive Web UI with local backend support. 

Notable technologies used comprise Tree-sitter for AST parsing across 16 supported languages (including TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Go, Rust, C#, and PHP), LadybugDB as an embedded graph database with vector support, HuggingFace transformers.js for local embeddings, Graphology for graph data structures, Sigma.js for WebGL graph rendering, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

name: orm
description: Next-generation ORM for Node.js & TypeScript | PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite, MongoDB and CockroachDB
summary:
Prisma 8 is a TypeScript rewrite of Prisma ORM, engineered to be extensible, composable, and AI-agent friendly by default. It features a minimal core architecture with a public SPI allowing extension authors to integrate custom tools, databases, and libraries, such as `@prisma/orm-extension-pgvector`, `@prisma/orm-extension-postgis`, `@prisma/orm-extension-paradedb`, `@prisma/orm-extension-supabase`, `@prisma/orm-extension-arktype-json`, and `@cipherstash/prisma-next`. 

The project targets developers building applications with Node.js and supports frameworks like Next.js, Hono, Nuxt, Astro, NestJS, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, and Elysia. It offers first-class support for PostgreSQL and MongoDB, with SQLite and MySQL planned. 

Prisma 8 includes built-in agent skills integration for development environments such as Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot Agent, and Devin, allowing AI agents to handle tasks like schema modeling and query writing end-to-end. Prerequisites include Node.js 24+ and a package manager (`npm`, `pnpm`, or `yarn`). Projects can be initialized via interactive scaffolding (`npm create prisma`) or added to existing repositories using `npx prisma orm init` and `npx prisma skills sync`. The project is licensed under Apache-2.0.

name: frontend-dev-bookmarks
description: Manually curated collection of resources for frontend web developers.
summary:
This project is a manually curated collection of resources designed for frontend web developers. Its purpose is to provide a comprehensive, browseable directory of tools, libraries, guides, and materials categorized across appearance, architecture, compatibility, ecosystem, languages, protocols, browser APIs, user interface components, and workflow. 

Intended users include frontend developers, web engineers, and designers seeking structured references and best practices. The repository covers core technologies and concepts such as HTML, Cascading Style Sheets (CSS), JavaScript (ECMAScript), Document Object Model (DOM), HTTP, JSON, Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG), WebAssembly, Responsive Web Design (RWD), Functional Reactive Programming (FRP), Service Workers, and the Web Animations API. It organizes technical topics ranging from UI components, automated testing, and build tools to cross-browser compatibility and version control.

name: Umi-OCR
description: OCR software, free and offline. 开源、免费的离线OCR软件。支持截屏/批量导入图片，PDF文档识别，排除水印/页眉页脚，扫描/生成二维码。内置多国语言库。
summary:
Umi-OCR is a free, open-source, and offline OCR (Optical Character Recognition) software designed for Windows 7 x64 and Linux x64 users. It provides out-of-the-box text recognition capabilities without requiring an internet connection. 

Main capabilities include:
- **Screenshot OCR:** Instantly captures and recognizes text from screen regions with customizable text post-processing and layout parsing options (such as multi-column natural paragraph ordering and code indentation preservation).
- **Batch OCR:** Processes large volumes of local images (supporting multiple formats like JPG, PNG, WEBP, BMP, and TIFF) into output formats such as TXT, JSONL, Markdown, and CSV, featuring an "Ignore Area" tool to exclude watermarks or logos.
- **Document Recognition:** Extracts text or converts PDF, XPS, EPUB, MOBI, FB2, and CBZ document scans into searchable double-layer PDFs.
- **QR Code and Barcode Processing:** Reads and generates barcodes and QR codes across 19 protocols.
- **External Integration:** Supports command-line execution and HTTP APIs for external automation.

Intended users include general desktop users, developers, and researchers seeking a fast, privacy-focused offline text extraction tool. The project integrates offline OCR engines like PaddleOCR-json and RapidOCR-json, built using Python and Qt.

name: scientific-agent-skills
description: Turn any AI agent into an AI Scientist. The #1 Agent Skills library for science, used by 250,000+ scientists worldwide. 177 ready-to-use validated skills plus 100+ scientific databases covering biology, chemistry, medicine, and drug discovery. Compatible with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Antigravity, and the open Agent Skills standard.
summary:
Scientific Agent Skills is a curated collection of 177 procedural knowledge skills for AI coding agents and research assistants, developed by K-Dense.
