The repository provides standardized, version-aware guidance, workflows, and code patterns for specialized scientific libraries, APIs, and over 100 databases. 

Intended for researchers, data scientists, engineers, and clinical investigators, the project covers a broad range of domains including bioinformatics, cheminformatics, proteomics, clinical evidence workflows, healthcare AI, neuroscience, materials science, physics, astronomy, engineering simulations, geospatial analysis, laboratory automation, and scientific communication. 

Notable technologies and tools featured across the collection include Python packages such as RDKit, Scanpy, PyTorch Lightning, scikit-learn, Biopython, PyDESeq2, OpenMM, MDAnalysis, Qiskit, and GeoPandas, as well as platforms like Benchling, Opentrons, LatchBio, and DNAnexus. The project adheres to the open Agent Skills standard and Agent Plugins packaging format, ensuring compatibility with AI hosts like Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and Google Antigravity.

name: 3x-ui
description: Supporting multi-protocol multi-user(Vmess, Vless, Trojan, ShadowSocks, Wireguard, Hysteria, Tunnel, Mixed, HTTP, Tun, MTProto، AmneziaWG)
summary:
**3X-UI** is an advanced, open-source web control panel designed for managing [Xray-core](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core) servers. It provides a multi-language interface with dark and light themes to deploy, configure, and monitor proxy and VPN protocols across single or multi-node server deployments.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Supports numerous multi-protocol inbounds (VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, WireGuard, AmneziaWG, TUIC v5, Hysteria2, MTProto, HTTP, SOCKS, Dokodemo-door, and TUN) and modern transports/security layers like REALITY and XTLS.
- Includes built-in AmneziaWG and TUIC v5 sidecar support.
- Offers comprehensive per-client management (traffic quotas, expiration dates, IP limits, HWID device limits, and live online status), traffic statistics, fallbacks, routing rules, load balancers, and a built-in subscription server.
- Features Telegram/Discord bots for remote monitoring, a RESTful API, fail2ban integration for IP limits, and PWA support.
- Supports database backends in SQLite and PostgreSQL.

**Intended Users:**
The software is intended for personal use in managing proxy and VPN infrastructure.

**Notable Technologies:**
Go, SQLite, PostgreSQL, Docker, Fail2ban, and Xray-core.

name: quill
description: Quill is a modern WYSIWYG editor built for compatibility and extensibility
summary:
Quill is a modern rich text editor built for compatibility and extensibility. Created by Jason Chen and Byron Milligan, and maintained by Slab, the project enables developers to easily integrate a customizable rich text editing interface into web applications. 

The editor provides core functionalities that can be instantiated via CSS selectors and configured using themes and modular stylesheets (such as Snow and Bubble). It is distributed as an npm package (`quill`) and via CDN, allowing integration through standard HTML and JavaScript scripts. The project utilizes a BSD 3-clause license.

name: bruno
description: Opensource IDE For Exploring and Testing API's (lightweight alternative to Postman/Insomnia)
summary:
Bruno is an open-source API client and IDE designed for exploring and testing APIs across macOS, Windows, and Linux. It stores API collections directly on the local filesystem using a plain text markup language called Bru, enabling seamless collaboration through Git or any version control system. Built strictly as an offline-only application to protect user data privacy, Bruno features no cloud-sync capabilities. 

The project includes the Bruno CLI and official Docker images, making it suitable for automated testing and integration into CI/CD pipelines. Intended users include developers and QA engineers seeking an alternative to traditional tools like Postman. Notable technologies and distribution channels utilized include Node.js, npm, Docker, Homebrew, Chocolatey, Scoop, Winget, Snap, Flatpak, and Apt.

name: agentic-awesome-skills
description: AAS Core is the local, agent-first control plane for complete catalog discovery, agent-owned selection, stack validation, and planning, backed by 2,400+ agentic skills. Includes CLI, local MCP, catalog, plugins, and Workbench.
summary:
Agentic Awesome Skills (AAS Core) is a library of over 2,638 installable `SKILL.md` playbooks designed to provide reusable instructions for AI coding assistants. 

**Purpose & Capabilities:** 
AAS Core enables agents such as Codex, Claude, Cursor, and Gemini to search complete local catalogs, record selected skills, validate stacks, and preview plans before changes are applied. It supports local catalog inspection, agent-owned selection, stack validation via the `aas` CLI and MCP, and immutable plan previews. Specialized plugins cover domains like web app building, security engineering, data analytics, product design, and DevOps.

**Intended Users:** 
Developers, AI maintainers, and teams utilizing autonomous coding agents, AI IDEs, or CLIs who want to inspect, review, and reuse structured skill sets across projects.

**Notable Technologies:** 
Built with TypeScript/JavaScript and distributed via npm (`agentic-awesome-skills`), AAS Core integrates with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Antigravity IDE, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, OpenCode, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

name: CowAgent
description: Open-source personal AI assistant & Agent Harness. Plans tasks, runs tools and skills, self-evolves with memory and knowledge. Multi-agent, multi-model, multi-channel. Lightweight, extensible, one-line install.
summary:
CowAgent is an open-source super AI assistant and reference implementation of Agent Harness engineering. It proactively plans tasks, controls computers and external services, creates and executes skills, builds a personal knowledge base with long-term memory, forms multi-agent teams, and supports self-evolution. 

Designed for developers and everyday users, the lightweight assistant can run 24/7 on local machines or servers and deploy across the web and major IM platforms, including Telegram, Slack, Discord, WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, and QQ. 

Core capabilities include a three-tier long-term memory architecture with Deep Dream distillation, auto-curated Markdown wikis and knowledge graphs, a custom skill ecosystem compatible with Skill Hub and GitHub, built-in system tools with Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, and multimodal handling for text, images, voice, and files. CowAgent integrates with major LLM and AI service providers such as Claude, OpenAI GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Doubao, ERNIE, and LinkAI, allowing users to swap providers via a unified web console, desktop client, or CLI.

name: legado
description: Legado 3.0 Book Reader with powerful controls & full functions❤️阅读3.0, 阅读是一款可以自定义来源阅读网络内容的工具，为广大网络文学爱好者提供一种方便、快捷舒适的试读体验。
summary: This repository has been cleared of its original contents following copyright infringement actions and legal liabilities involving China Literature intellectual property. A formal public notice is displayed urging all individuals to immediately cease any copyright-infringement activities, avoid legal violations, and strictly adhere to relevant laws and regulations. The README includes a link to the official China Literature Intellectual Property Protection Notice.

name: react
description: Cheatsheets for experienced React developers getting started with TypeScript
summary:
The React TypeScript Cheatsheet is a reference guide designed to help developers use React with TypeScript effectively. It provides opinionated best practices, copy-and-pasteable code examples, setup advice, and advanced usage instructions for writing reusable type utilities and libraries. The guide covers foundational and advanced concepts including function and class components, hooks, component props, forms, events, context, refs, portals, error boundaries, and concurrent React features such as Suspense and transitions.

Intended for React developers at any skill level who possess a basic understanding of React and TypeScript, the repository also addresses contributing guidelines for DefinitelyTyped. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced throughout the documentation include React, TypeScript, Vite, Next.js, Remix, Gatsby, Expo, and Redux.

name: okhttp
description: A meticulous HTTP client for the JVM, Android, and GraalVM.
summary:
OkHttp is an efficient, modern HTTP and HTTP/2 client designed for Java 8+ and Android 5.0+ applications. Its primary purpose is to handle efficient networking and data exchange by offering features such as connection pooling, transparent GZIP compression, response caching, and silent recovery from common connection problems including IP address failovers. The library adheres strictly to modern HTTP specifications (RFC 9110, RFC 9111, RFC 9112, RFC 9113), WebSockets, and Server-Sent Events (SSE). 

Intended users include Java and Android developers building networked applications who require a reliable, fluent request/response API supporting both synchronous blocking calls and asynchronous callbacks. Notable technologies and integrations utilized by OkHttp include Okio for high-performance I/O, the Kotlin standard library, Conscrypt for TLS integration, GraalVM native image compatibility, and support for Java 9 modules. Additionally, the project includes MockWebServer for testing HTTP, HTTPS, and HTTP/2 clients.

name: airflow
description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows
summary:
Apache Airflow is a platform designed to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows. By defining workflows as code, users can create maintainable, versionable, testable, and collaborative pipelines. Airflow is commonly used for data pipelines, machine learning orchestration (such as training, retraining, evaluation, and deployment), and coordinating LLM-based and agentic workloads.

The platform enables users to author Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) using Python, with a scheduler that executes tasks across workers based on specified dependencies. Key capabilities include a rich command-line utility for managing DAGs and a web user interface featuring DAG views, asset dependencies, grid representations, graphs, backfilling tools, and source code viewers. 

Airflow emphasizes dynamic pipeline generation, extensibility via built-in operators and providers, and flexibility through the Jinja templating engine. It is designed around idempotent tasks and uses metadata passing via XCom rather than transferring large volumes of data between tasks.

Notable technologies and components associated with Apache Airflow include Python, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Celery, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, Flask, Werkzeug, and Docker. It is an Apache Software Foundation project.

name: gods-eye-view
description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.
summary:
God's Eye View is a browser-based 3D geospatial intelligence platform and spy-satellite simulator that aggregates public global signals into a photorealistic, interactive globe. 

**Purpose & Capabilities:**
The project renders live and modeled data layers including flights (OpenSky/adsb.lol), marine vessels (AISStream), satellites (CelesTrak via SGP4), earthquakes, traffic (TomTom/OSM), weather (NOAA/ECMWF), active fires (NASA FIRMS), space missions, public CCTV cameras, radio broadcasts, transit feeds, and infrastructure (datacenters, dams, submarine cables). It features an immersive cockpit mode, an analog radio tuner, vector annotation whiteboards, OSRM street routing, GLSL visual post-processing filters (CRT, NVG, FLIR, Noir, Snow), and a hands-free voice control agent powered by the OpenAI Realtime API.

**Intended Users:**
Geospatial analysts, OSINT researchers, developers, and users interested in spatial-intelligence visualization and exploration tools.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Vanilla JavaScript, CesiumJS, and Vite
- Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and Cesium ion terrain
- OpenAI Realtime API (for voice commands)
- Node.js (for local execution and server-side proxying)
- Pinokio (for zero-terminal installation)

name: v2ray-core
description: A platform for building proxies to bypass network restrictions.
summary:
Project V is a set of network tools designed to help users build a custom computer network, secure network connections, and protect user privacy. The repository notes that the project has moved to `https://github.com/v2fly/v2ray-core`. 

The project relies on notable technologies including Go, `gorilla/websocket`, and `gRPC` in production, along with `miekg/dns` and `h12w/socks` for testing purposes. It is distributed under the MIT License.

name: serverless
description: ⚡ Serverless Framework – Effortlessly build apps that auto-scale, incur zero costs when idle, and require minimal maintenance using AWS Lambda and other managed cloud services.
summary:
The Serverless Framework is a multi-language command-line tool designed to build, deploy, monitor, and manage auto-scaling serverless applications on AWS. It allows developers to configure both code and cloud infrastructure using an approachable YAML syntax (`serverless.yml`), supporting use cases such as APIs, data pipelines, web sockets, scheduled tasks, and AI workloads.

Main capabilities include automated multi-service deployments via Serverless Compose, local-to-cloud event proxying using `serverless dev`, native TypeScript support powered by ESBuild, deployment diffs, browser-based AWS SSO login, sandboxes for ephemeral compute, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore support, and built-in custom domain management. It supports major language runtimes including Node.js, Python, Java, Go, and C#.

The framework is intended for developers and teams ranging from indie hackers to enterprises looking to build maintainable cloud applications with minimal infrastructure management overhead. Notable technologies utilized include AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, AWS API Gateway, AWS CloudFormation, AWS S3, Amazon Bedrock, Terraform, and Doppler.

name: copyparty
description: Portable file server with accelerated resumable uploads, dedup, WebDAV, SFTP, FTP, TFTP, zeroconf, media indexer, thumbnails++ all in one file
summary:
Copyparty is a lightweight, self-contained file server application that turns almost any device into a resumable upload and download server accessible via any web browser. Written in Python (supporting Python 2 and 3), it runs with minimal dependencies and requires no complex setup. 

**Main Capabilities:**
* **Protocols:** Supports HTTP/HTTPS, WebDAV, SFTP, FTP/FTPS, TFTP, and SMB/CIFS.
* **Browser Interface:** Features a single-page web app with a file manager (cut, paste, rename, delete), a directory tree sidebar (navpane), rich media viewing, search by name, date, size, and ID3 tags, batch renaming, RSS/OPDS feeds, and a Markdown viewer.
* **Uploads & Downloads:** Supports resumable chunked uploads (`up2k`) with no filesize limit, deduplication via symlinks or hardlinks, upload undo/self-destruction, zip/tar folder downloads, and on-the-fly audio/video transcoding and image thumbnail generation.
* **Access Control:** Provides per-folder and per-account permissions, temporary file/folder shares, IP range authentication, password hashing, and Identity Provider (IdP) integration.

**Intended Users:** 
Designed for users needing a quick, drop-in file transfer and management solution across diverse operating systems and legacy or resource-constrained hardware.

**Notable Technologies:** 
Built using Python, Jinja2, SQLite, and optional integrations with FFmpeg, Pillow, pyvips, Paramiko, and Pyftpdlib.

name: 30-Days-Of-JavaScript
description: 30 days of JavaScript programming challenge is a step-by-step guide to learn JavaScript programming language in 30 days. This challenge may take more than 100 days,  please just follow your own pace. These videos may help too: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC7PNRuno1rzYPb1xLa4yktw
summary:
This repository contains the "30 Days of JavaScript" programming challenge and learning guide created by Asabeneh Yetayeh. Designed for both beginners and advanced developers, the project provides a step-by-step curriculum to learn JavaScript fundamentals, advanced concepts, and web development techniques. 

The main capabilities include structured daily lessons and mini-projects covering topics such as syntax, data types, operators, conditionals, loops, functions, objects, higher-order functions, DOM manipulation, event listeners, regular expressions, error handling, classes, web storage, and asynchronous JavaScript (promises). It also features practical mini-projects including a solar system explorer, data visualizations for world countries, portfolios, leaderboards, and character animations.

Intended users are individuals ranging from absolute beginners with no prior programming experience to advanced developers looking to master or refresh their JavaScript skills. Notable technologies and tools utilized throughout the course include JavaScript (ES6+), Node.js, Google Chrome (V8 engine/Developer Tools), and Visual Studio Code.

name: monaco-editor
description: A browser based code editor
summary: The Monaco Editor is the fully featured browser-based code editor that powers VS Code, generated directly from VS Code's sources with web-compatible shims. Designed for web developers and applications requiring an advanced code editing interface, it provides rich features like syntax highlighting, code completion, and hover information through underlying concepts such as models, URIs, user-facing editors, smart feature providers, and disposables. Built with technologies including ESM and web workers, the library supports localization and can be installed via npm.

name: siyuan
description: An open-source, privacy-first, self-hosted knowledge workspace where humans and AI agents work together 开源、隐私优先、自托管的知识工作空间，让人与智能体在此协作
summary:
SiYuan is a privacy-first personal knowledge management system featuring fine-grained block-level references, two-way links, and Markdown WYSIWYG editing. The project provides comprehensive knowledge management capabilities including large document editing, mathematical formulas, charts, database table views, flashcard spaced repetition, Tesseract OCR, PDF annotation links, Web clipping, AI writing and Q/A chat via the OpenAI API, and a built-in command-line interface. 

Designed for individuals seeking advanced note-taking and knowledge structuring, the platform supports desktop, mobile (Android, iOS, HarmonyOS), Docker, Kubernetes, and self-hosted deployments. It includes an extensible ecosystem featuring a plugin API, a community marketplace, and native apps. Notable technologies and components used across the ecosystem include the Lute editor engine, SQLite, JavaScript/CSS snippets, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication. SiYuan is open source under the AGPLv3 license, with most features available for free use.

name: iina
description: The modern video player for macOS.
summary:
IINA is a modern video and music player designed specifically for macOS (11.0+). Based on the mpv media player, it provides robust decoding capabilities alongside features such as local and online subtitle matching, video thumbnails, infinite playback history, Picture-in-Picture, Force Touch, and advanced Touch Bar support. 

Intended for macOS users seeking an extensible media player, IINA offers a customizable user interface with multiple color schemes, a standalone Music Mode, comprehensive input and gesture controls, and support for mpv configuration files and scripts. It also provides command-line tools, browser extensions, and an extensive plugin ecosystem supporting features like streaming integrations, scrobbling, and AI-assisted translations.

The application is built using Swift and Xcode, leveraging underlying C/C++ libraries including mpv, with dependency management supported via shell scripts and pre-compiled or manually built binaries.

name: awesome-cheatsheets
description: 👩‍💻👨‍💻 Awesome cheatsheets for popular programming languages, frameworks and development tools. They include everything you should know in one single file.
summary:
Awesome-Cheatsheets is a collection of concise, single-file reference cheatsheets for popular programming languages, frameworks, databases, and development tools. Derived from official documentation and technical literature, the project provides developers with a quick way to assess knowledge, learn new concepts, and save time across various technologies. 

The repository covers multiple domains, including:
- **Languages:** Bash, C, C#, Go, Java, PHP, Python, XML, JavaScript, and TypeScript.
- **Backend:** Laravel, Django, Adonis.js, Express.js, Feathers.js, Moleculer, Node.js, and Sails.js.
- **Frontend:** HTML5, CSS3, React.js, Vue.js, Tailwind.css, Ember.js, Angular, and AngularJS.
- **Databases:** MySQL, MongoDB, and Redis.
- **Tools & Infrastructure:** cURL, Drush, Elasticsearch, Emmet, Git, Puppeteer, Sublime Text, Vim, Visual Studio Code, Xcode, AWS CLI, Docker, GCP CLI, Heroku CLI, Kubernetes, macOS, Nanobox, Nginx, PM2, Ubuntu, and Firebase CLI.

Intended for software developers and engineers looking for fast, centralized technical references, the project also accepts community contributions via pull requests.

name: cli
description: GitHub’s official command line tool
summary: GitHub CLI (`gh`) is a standalone command-line tool that brings GitHub functionality—such as pull requests and issues—directly to the terminal alongside `git`. Intended for developers and users working on GitHub.com, GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and supported GitHub Enterprise Server versions, it supports macOS, Windows, and Linux environments. The tool features an agent skill for driving `gh` from coding agents, supports build provenance attestation utilizing Sigstore, and integrates with GitHub Actions and GitHub Codespaces.

name: pandoc
description: Universal markup converter
summary:
Pandoc is a universal markup converter provided as a Haskell library and command-line tool designed to convert documents from one markup format to another. Its core purpose is to bridge disparate document formats, supporting numerous input and output formats including Markdown variants (such as CommonMark and GitHub-Flavored Markdown), HTML, LaTeX, DocBook, EPUB, Word docx, PowerPoint pptx, Jupyter notebooks (`ipynb`), and various bibliographies and markup languages. 

Pandoc is intended for developers, writers, researchers, and documentation maintainers who need to translate documents programmatically or via command-line interfaces. Notable technologies and concepts utilized include Haskell, an abstract syntax tree (AST) for intermediate document representation, Lua filters for modifying document structures, WebAssembly, and support for generating PDF output via tools like LaTeX, Groff ms, or HTML. The modular design separates parsing (readers) from generation (writers), enabling extensible document transformation workflows.

name: awesome-compose
description: Awesome Docker Compose samples
summary:
Awesome Compose is a curated collection of Docker Compose samples designed as a starting point for integrating multiple services and managing their deployment using a `compose.yaml` file. The repository targets developers and users seeking reference implementations for local development environments, tinkering with software stacks, or personal use. 

The project provides multi-service application samples, single-service samples, and basic setups for different platforms. Notable technologies and frameworks featured across the samples include Docker, Docker Compose, Docker+Wasm, ASP.NET, MS SQL Server, Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana, Go, Nginx, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Java Spark, Python, Flask, MongoDB, Node.js, Redis, React, Rust, Spring, WasmEdge, Kafka, Angular, Vue.js, PHP, Traefik, Django, FastAPI, Gitea, Nextcloud, Pi-hole, Prometheus, Grafana, and WordPress.

name: helix
description: A post-modern modal text editor.
summary: Helix is a modern, terminal-based text editor written in Rust, heavily inspired by Kakoune and Neovim. Designed for developers seeking an efficient modal editing experience, Helix features Vim-like modal editing paired with powerful multiple selections. Its core capabilities include built-in Language Server Protocol (LSP) support for robust IDE-like features and smart, incremental syntax highlighting and code editing powered by tree-sitter. While primarily operating as a terminal application, the project also explores custom rendering utilizing wgpu.

name: system-design
description: Learn how to design systems at scale and prepare for system design interviews
summary:
This repository contains a comprehensive system design course and ebook by Karan Pratap Singh, designed to help developers and engineers learn architecture, infrastructure, data storage, distributed systems, and real-world system design interview preparation. 

The project covers fundamental concepts across five main chapters and an appendix, including networking (IP, OSI model, TCP/UDP, DNS, Load Balancing, Clustering, Caching, CDN, Proxies, Availability, Scalability, Storage), database architectures (SQL, NoSQL, Replication, Indexing, Normalization, ACID/BASE models, CAP and PACELC theorems, Transactions, Distributed Transactions, Sharding, Consistent Hashing, Federation), and architectural patterns (N-tier architecture, Message Brokers, Message Queues, Publish-Subscribe, ESB, Monoliths vs. Microservices, EDA, Event Sourcing, CQRS, API Gateways, REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and Real-time communication protocols like WebSockets and SSE). It also includes advanced topics like Geohashing, Quadtrees, Circuit Breakers, Rate Limiting, Service Discovery, Virtual Machines, Containers, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SSO, and TLS, alongside practical system design walkthroughs for URL shorteners, WhatsApp, Twitter, Netflix, and Uber.

The content is intended for software engineers, developers, and candidates preparing for technical system design interviews.

name: RSSHub
description: 🧡 Everything is RSSible
summary:
RSSHub is an open-source RSS aggregator designed to generate RSS feeds from an extensive variety of online content sources. Functioning as a large RSS network supported by a community, it provides new routes, features, and bug fixes to make diverse web content accessible via RSS feeds. 

Related ecosystem projects include Folo (an AI RSS reader), RSSHub Radar (a browser extension for discovering RSS and RSSHub links), RSSBud (an iOS mobile client), RSSAid (a Flutter-based Android client), and DocSearch (a Raycast integration). RSSHub can be deployed easily across various hosting platforms, including single-click VPS deployment options.

name: TrafficMonitor
description: 这是一个用于显示当前网速、CPU及内存利用率的桌面悬浮窗软件，并支持任务栏显示，支持更换皮肤。
summary:
TrafficMonitor is a Windows-based network speed monitoring application featuring a floating desktop window and a taskbar integration mode. It displays real-time network transmission rates, CPU usage, memory utilization, and hardware metrics including GPU utilization, disk usage, CPU frequency, and component temperatures. 

Intended for Windows users seeking system resource visibility, the software supports historical traffic statistics, multi-network card selection, a plugin system, and extensive customizability through skins supporting custom fonts, colors, XML layouts, and PNG backgrounds. Hardware monitoring features utilize the open-source LibreHardwareMonitor library. The project is distributed in standard and Lite versions, requiring the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable.

name: milvus
description: Milvus is a high-performance, cloud-native vector database built for scalable vector ANN search
summary:
Milvus is a high-performance, distributed vector database built to scale unstructured data management for AI applications such as semantic search, recommendation systems, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). 

Main capabilities include dense and sparse vector search, full-text search with BM25, hybrid search, metadata filtering, range search, real-time streaming updates, multi-tenancy, and hot/cold storage tiers. It supports multiple vector index types including HNSW, IVF, FLAT, SCANN, and DiskANN, along with hardware acceleration for CPU and GPU (such as NVIDIA CAGRA). 

Intended users are AI developers and enterprise engineers building scalable machine learning applications. Milvus is written in Go and C++, features a K8s-native distributed architecture, and provides a Python SDK (`pymilvus`) alongside Milvus Lite for lightweight local deployments.

name: paperless-ngx
description: A community-supported supercharged document management system: scan, index and archive all your documents
summary:
Paperless-ngx is a document management system that transforms physical documents into a searchable online archive. As the official successor to the Paperless and Paperless-ng projects, it is designed to help users maintain a paperless workflow. 

Main capabilities include organizing, archiving, and searching documents. It supports deployment via Docker Compose, with an available automated installation script and migration paths from Paperless-ng. Translations are managed through Crowdin. 

Technologies mentioned include Docker and Docker Compose, with code hosted on GitHub and documentation provided on GitHub Pages.

name: Rocket.Chat
description: The Secure CommsOS™ for mission-critical operations
summary:
Rocket.Chat is an open-source, secure, and fully customizable team communications platform developed in TypeScript, designed for organizations requiring high standards of data protection and privacy. 

The platform enables real-time and asynchronous team collaboration, voice calls, federation, identity management, end-to-end encryption, and role- and attribute-based access control. It supports flexible deployment options including self-hosted environments via Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes, air-gapped workspaces for isolated networks, and custom cloud-hosted solutions. 

Intended for organizations with strict security needs—such as governments, defense agencies, and enterprises—Rocket.Chat serves colleagues, external partners, customers, and citizens. Developers can extend the platform using the open-source Apps-Engine framework, integrate external systems via public marketplace apps, and build upon associated repositories including Rocket.Chat.Electron and Rocket.Chat.ReactNative. The project provides desktop, mobile, and web applications, comprehensive APIs, and dedicated developer documentation.

name: TTS
description: 🐸💬 - a deep learning toolkit for Text-to-Speech, battle-tested in research and production
summary:
🐸TTS is a Python deep learning library designed for advanced Text-to-Speech (TTS) generation, voice cloning, and voice conversion. It provides pretrained models supporting over 1100 languages, alongside comprehensive tools for training new models, fine-tuning existing architectures, curating datasets, and performing dataset analysis. 

The library features a flexible Trainer API, Tensorboard logging, and modular implementations of various spectrogram models (such as Tacotron, Tacotron2, Glow-TTS, FastSpeech2, and VITS), end-to-end architectures (including ⓍTTS, YourTTS, Tortoise, and Bark), speaker encoders (GE2E, Angular Loss), and vocoders (such as MelGAN, HiFiGAN, WaveGrad, and UnivNet). It also supports external integrations like Facebook Research's Fairseq MMS models. 

Intended for developers, researchers, and practitioners in speech synthesis, 🐸TTS can be used programmatically via its Python API or via a command-line interface (`tts`) to synthesize speech, perform zero-shot voice cloning with speaker reference audio, and execute voice conversion.

name: learn-regex
description: Learn regex the easy way
summary: Learn Regex is an educational guide and reference designed to help learners and developers understand regular expressions (regex). The project serves as a comprehensive tutorial explaining foundational concepts and syntax through clear examples. Its main capabilities cover basic matchers, meta characters, character sets, repetitions, capturing and non-capturing groups, alternation, escaping special characters, anchors, shorthand character sets, lookarounds (positive and negative lookaheads and lookbehinds), flags (case-insensitive, global search, and multiline), and greedy versus lazy matching. The repository is intended for programmers, developers, and anyone seeking to learn pattern matching in text processing. The content is available in numerous translations to support a global audience.

name: data-engineering-zoomcamp
description: Data Engineering Zoomcamp is a free 9-week course on building production-ready data pipelines. Join the course here 👇🏼
summary:
The Data Engineering Zoomcamp is a free, 9-week open-source course by DataTalks.Club designed to teach data engineering fundamentals through building an end-to-end data pipeline from scratch. Intended for developers, analysts, and data scientists looking to master the modern data engineering stack without prior domain experience, the curriculum covers containerization, infrastructure as code, workflow orchestration, data warehousing, analytics engineering, batch processing, and streaming. 

The syllabus utilizes industry-standard technologies and tools including Docker, Terraform, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), PostgreSQL, Kestra, dbt, DuckDB, BigQuery, Apache Spark, Kafka, KSQL, Avro, Bruin, and dlt. Students learn via structured modules, hands-on workshops, and a final peer-reviewed project, with options to participate in a structured live cohort featuring deadlines and certificates or to study self-paced.

name: streamlit
description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.
summary: Streamlit is an open-source Python framework designed to help developers build and share interactive data apps, dashboards, reports, and chat applications quickly and easily. Providing a simple and Pythonic API with live script editing, Streamlit enables fast prototyping through input widgets, interactive dataframes, charts, layouts, multi-page structures, and custom Streamlit Components. The platform is targeted at developers, data scientists, and creators building applications for LLMs, chatbots, science, finance, NLP, and other domains. Built apps can be freely deployed, managed, and shared using the Community Cloud platform. Streamlit is available via pip installation and licensed under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: full-stack-fastapi-template
description: Full-stack web application template with FastAPI, React, SQLModel, PostgreSQL, Vite, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, FastAPI Cloud, and Docker Compose.
summary:
The Full Stack FastAPI Template is a project template designed to bootstrap web applications with a Python backend and a React frontend. Its main purpose is to provide a complete, production-ready full-stack architecture featuring JWT authentication, secure password hashing, email-based password recovery, and automated CI/CD workflows using GitHub Actions. 

Main capabilities include an interactive API documentation interface, automated end-to-end testing, local email testing, and dark mode support. Intended users are developers building modern web applications who require a pre-configured stack for rapid prototyping and deployment. 

The technology stack includes FastAPI, SQLModel, Pydantic, and PostgreSQL for the backend. The frontend is built using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui components, with an automatically generated frontend client. Testing is handled by Pytest for the backend and Playwright for frontend end-to-end testing. Deployment options include FastAPI Cloud and self-hosted environments utilizing Docker Compose alongside Traefik as a reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS. Development tools include React Email for templates and Mailpit for local email testing.

name: architecture-samples
description: A collection of samples to discuss and showcase different architectural tools and patterns for Android apps.
summary:
Android Architecture Samples is a project that showcases different architectural approaches for developing Android applications through variations of a TODO app. The project demonstrates a testable and maintainable structure intended for beginners, intermediate developers, and advanced developers seeking a quick reference. 

This specific branch implements a single-activity architecture utilizing Jetpack Compose for the user interface, Navigation Compose for navigation, and a presentation layer featuring a ViewModel per screen or feature. Asynchronous operations and reactive UIs are handled using Kotlin coroutines and Flow. The data layer consists of a repository pattern with local persistence via Room and a fake remote data source, supported by two product flavors (`mock` and `prod`). Dependency injection is managed using Hilt, and the codebase includes a comprehensive suite of unit, integration, end-to-end, and shared tests.

name: Files
description: A modern file manager that helps users organize their files and folders.
summary: Files is a modern open-source file manager designed for Windows to help users organize files and folders with an intuitive design. Built and maintained by the community, its main capabilities include robust multitasking experiences, file tags, and deep integrations. The project is intended for Windows users seeking a feature-rich alternative file management solution, as well as open-source contributors. Files can be installed via the Microsoft Store or a classic installer, with preview versions available for early access to new features.

name: zx
description: A tool for writing better scripts
summary:
The `zx` package is a tool for writing complex command-line scripts using JavaScript or TypeScript instead of traditional shell languages. It provides convenient cross-platform wrappers around `child_process` with argument escaping and sensible defaults, bridging Node.js and shell scripting. 

The project's main capabilities include executing shell commands via tagged template literals, supporting asynchronous operations with `Promise.all`, and handling file paths and variables seamlessly within scripts. It is intended for developers and system administrators who prefer JavaScript for scripting tasks. 

Notable technologies and runtime environments supported include Node.js (version 12.17.0 or higher), Bun (version 1.0.0 or higher), Deno (1.x and 2.x), GraalVM Node.js, Bash, and PowerShell, across Linux, macOS, and Windows operating systems. Both CommonJS (CJS) and ECMAScript Modules (ESM) are supported in JavaScript or TypeScript.

name: nature-skills
description: 符合nature论文学术表达和科研绘图的Skill
summary:
Nature Skills (`nature-skills`) is an open-source library of reusable, academic research skills designed for global scholars and AI agents. It emphasizes practical problem-solving, verifiable workflows, and direct generation of publication-ready scientific assets. 

The project contains 19 core skills that assist researchers across various stages of the scientific process:
- **Writing & Polishing:** `nature-polishing`, `nature-writing`, `nature-proposal-writer`
- **Reading & Analysis:** `nature-reader`, `nature-paper-card`, `nature-academic-search`, `nature-downloader`, `nature-literature-pipeline`
- **Peer Review & Rebuttal:** `nature-reviewer`, `nature-response`, `nature-ref-verifier`
- **Data & Visualization:** `nature-figure`, `nature-statistics`, `nature-data`
- **Presentation & Translation:** `nature-paper2ppt`, `nature-image2ppt`, `nature-paper-to-patent`, `nature-citation`, `nature-experiment-log`

Intended for researchers, students, and academic developers, the repository supports seamless installation across multiple AI coding agents and frameworks including Claude Code, Codex, Chatbox, OpenClaw, OpenCode, and Hermes. Notable technologies involved include Node.js, Python, R, Playwright, and MCP (Model Context Protocol).

name: codebase-memory-mcp
description: High-performance code intelligence MCP server. Indexes codebases into a persistent knowledge graph — average repo in milliseconds. 158 languages, sub-ms queries, 99% fewer tokens. Single static binary, zero dependencies.
summary:
**codebase-memory-mcp** is a high-speed, local-first code intelligence engine designed for AI coding agents. It indexes repositories into a persistent SQLite-backed knowledge graph containing functions, classes, call chains, HTTP routes, and infrastructure configurations. 

### Project Purpose & Capabilities
The project provides a structural analysis backend that answers structural queries in under 1ms and indexes codebases (such as the Linux kernel at 28M LOC) in minutes. It supports 17 Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools—including structural and semantic search, path tracing, change impact analysis, dead code detection, ADR management, and Cypher-like graph queries (`query_graph`). It features a built-in 3D graph visualization UI served locally on `localhost:9749`, a RAM-first indexing pipeline with LZ4 compression, a background watcher for auto-syncing, and a team-shared graph artifact format (`.codebase-memory/graph.db.zst`) for avoiding redundant reindexing.

### Intended Users
The engine is intended for developers and AI coding assistants requiring deep code exploration without file-by-file grep cycles. It configures and integrates automatically across 45 client surfaces (such as Claude Code, Codex, Zed, Cursor, and VS Code) using specialized tiered agent profiles.

### Notable Technologies
- **Tree-sitter**: Vendored AST grammars supporting 162 languages.
- **Hybrid LSP**: A lightweight C implementation providing semantic type resolution for Python, TypeScript/JavaScript/JSX/TSX, PHP, C#, Go, C/C++, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and Perl.
- **SQLite & FTS5**: In-memory and persistent graph storage with full-text search.
- **Nomic Embeddings**: Built-in `nomic-embed-code` model (768d int8) for offline vector search.
- **Distribution**: Ships as a self-contained native executable for macOS, Linux, and Windows with zero external language runtimes, hosted services, or API keys required.

name: Leaflet
description: 🍃 JavaScript library for mobile-friendly interactive maps 🇺🇦
summary: Leaflet is a lightweight, open-source JavaScript library designed for building interactive maps across all major desktop and mobile platforms. Created with a focus on simplicity, performance, and usability, the library weighs about 40 kB of gzipped JavaScript and 3.2 kB of gzipped CSS. It provides essential mapping features for developers, works efficiently out of the box by leveraging modern browser capabilities while remaining compatible with older browsers, and supports extensibility through a wide range of plugins. The project offers a well-documented API and a readable source code tailored for web developers and contributors looking to create online mapping solutions.

name: vnpy
description: 基于Python的开源量化交易平台开发框架
summary:
VeighNa is an open-source quantitative trading system development framework and multi-function platform built with Python. Designed for financial institutions, private equity funds, securities and futures companies, and individual quantitative traders, the platform provides comprehensive capabilities for building trading applications, backtesting strategies, and executing live orders.

Main capabilities include extensive gateway integrations for domestic and international markets (such as CTP, Interactive Brokers, XTP, and TORA), datafeed adapters (including RQData, TuShare, and Wind), database support (SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, QuestDB, MongoDB, and others), and various trading applications like CTA strategy engines, spread trading, option master, portfolio strategy, and algorithm trading. Version 4.0 introduces the `vnpy.alpha` module for AI-driven quantitative strategies, delivering multi-factor machine learning dataset feature engineering, model training templates utilizing algorithms like Lasso, LightGBM, and MLP, strategy research, and workflow management tools.

The platform uses notable technologies including Python, C++, and asynchronous IO clients. Intended users are quantitative traders, developers, and financial firms seeking scalable automated trading solutions.

name: AdminLTE
description: AdminLTE - Free admin dashboard template based on Bootstrap 5
summary:
AdminLTE is an open-source, fully responsive admin dashboard template built on Bootstrap 5.3 and vanilla JavaScript, eliminating the need for jQuery. Designed for web developers and designers, it provides a comprehensive suite of UI elements, layout blueprints, plugins, and pre-built demo pages such as calendars, kanban boards, chat interfaces, file managers, mailboxes, and data tables. 

The core HTML and CSS repository supports modern browsers, dark mode, RTL layouts, and customization via opt-in color stylesheets. AdminLTE also offers official framework-native editions and ecosystem integrations for React, Next.js, Vue 3, Nuxt, Angular, Laravel, Symfony, Django, ASP.NET Core, and Drupal. Notable technologies utilized include TypeScript, ESLint, Stylelint, Astro, FullCalendar, SortableJS, and Tabulator. It is distributed under the MIT license and is suitable for deployment as compiled production assets across diverse backend and frontend stacks.

name: jest
description: Delightful JavaScript Testing.
summary: Jest is a comprehensive JavaScript testing solution designed to work out of the box for most JavaScript projects. Its main capabilities include instant feedback via an interactive watch mode that runs only test files related to changed files, and snapshot testing to capture large object structures and track changes over time. Jest is intended for developers building JavaScript applications and supports integration with notable technologies such as Babel, webpack, Vite, Parcel, and TypeScript.

name: grpc
description: C++ based gRPC (C++, Python, Ruby, Objective-C, PHP, C#)
summary:
gRPC is a modern, open-source, high-performance remote procedure call (RPC) framework designed to run anywhere, enabling client and server applications to communicate transparently and simplifying the construction of connected systems. It is intended for developers building distributed client-server applications across a wide variety of programming languages. 

The project provides a shared C++ core library (`src/core`) alongside language-specific libraries and bindings. gRPC supports numerous technologies and platforms, including C++, C#/.NET (`grpc-dotnet`), Dart (`grpc-dart`), Go (`grpc-go`), Java (`grpc-java`), Kotlin (`grpc-kotlin`), Node.js (`grpc-node`), Objective-C, PHP, Python (`grpcio`), Ruby, WebJS (`grpc-web`), and Swift (`grpc-swift`). Packages are made available through standard language package managers such as NuGet, pub, Maven Central, npm, PECL, pip, and RubyGems.

name: CppCoreGuidelines
description: The C++ Core Guidelines are a set of tried-and-true guidelines, rules, and best practices about coding in C++
summary:
The C++ Core Guidelines is a collaborative project led by Bjarne Stroustrup that provides a comprehensive set of rules for using modern C++ (C++11 and newer) effectively, simply, and safely. The project's purpose is to help developers write code that is statically type-safe, free of resource leaks, fast, and resilient against programming logic errors. 

The guidelines focus on higher-level architectural issues, including interfaces, resource management, memory management, and concurrency, rather than low-level styling conventions. They are intended for C++ developers at various experience levels and are designed for gradual codebase introduction and support by static analysis tools. Many rules rely on the header-only Guidelines Support Library (GSL). The documentation is maintained in GitHub-flavored Markdown.

name: hyperswitch
description: Open source, composable payments platform | PCI compliant | SaaS and Self-host options | Enables connectivity to multiple payment, payout, fraud, vault and tokenization providers | Uplifts authorization with intelligent routing and revenue recovery | Reduce payment processing costs with cost observability | Reduces payment ops with reconciliation
summary:
Hyperswitch is a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for businesses and developers seeking flexibility and control over their payment stacks without vendor lock-in. It provides a comprehensive suite of payment modules including cost observability, revenue recovery, PCI-compliant vaulting, intelligent multi-PSP routing across over 120 processors (such as Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, and Worldpay), reconciliation, and alternate payment method widgets like Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, and Klarna. 

The project is built primarily in Rust for high performance and reliability, utilizing ReScript, TypeScript, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, and Terraform across its broader ecosystem. It offers backend core services, merchant dashboards via the Control Center, and checkout SDKs for web, Android, iOS, React Native, and Flutter. Intended users include merchants, enterprises, and engineering teams scaling multi-PSP routing or rearchitecting payment processing. Deployments are supported locally via Docker, via Helm charts on AWS, GCP, and Azure, or through a fully hosted sandbox environment.

name: bubbletea
description: A powerful little TUI framework 🏗
summary:
Bubble Tea is a fun, functional, and stateful Go framework designed for building terminal applications, supporting simple or complex UIs either inline, full-window, or combined. Based on The Elm Architecture, it provides a robust model-view-update pattern (`Init`, `Update`, `View`) tailored for Go developers. 

Key capabilities include a high-performance cell-based renderer, built-in color downsampling, declarative views, high-fidelity keyboard and mouse handling, and native clipboard support. Notable companion technologies often used with it include [Bubbles](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles) for UI components, [Lip Gloss](https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss) for styling and layout, [Harmonica](https://github.com/charmbracelet/harmonica) for spring animations, [BubbleZone](https://github.com/lrstanley/bubblezone) for mouse event tracking, and [ntcharts](https://github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts) for terminal charting. 

Bubble Tea is intended for developers creating interactive command-line interfaces, tools, and text-based user interfaces (TUIs) in Go. It is used extensively in production environments for tools ranging from developer utilities and file managers to cloud platforms and database clients.

name: mitmproxy
description: An interactive TLS-capable intercepting HTTP proxy for penetration testers and software developers.
summary:
mitmproxy is an interactive, SSL/TLS-capable intercepting proxy designed for HTTP/1, HTTP/2, and WebSockets. It enables developers, testers, and security researchers to inspect, capture, modify, and replay web traffic. 

The project provides three main tools:
- **mitmproxy**: An interactive console-based interface.
- **mitmdump**: A command-line version described as tcpdump for HTTP.
- **mitmweb**: A web-based user interface.

Technologies used include Python and web-based frontend interfaces, supporting multi-platform installation via precompiled binaries or source code.

name: LibreChat
description: Enhanced ChatGPT Clone: Features Agents, MCP, Skills, DeepSeek, Anthropic, AWS, OpenAI, Responses API, Azure, Groq, o1, GPT-5, Mistral, OpenRouter, Vertex AI, Gemini, Artifacts, AI model switching, message search, Code Interpreter, langchain, DALL-E-3, OpenAPI Actions, Functions, Secure Multi-User Auth, Presets, open-source for self-hosting. Active
summary:
LibreChat is a self-hosted, open-source AI chat platform designed to unify major AI providers into a single, privacy-focused interface. Intended for users and enterprises seeking complete control over their AI infrastructure, it supports models from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, and various local or remote providers like Ollama, OpenRouter, and Groq via custom endpoints.

Main capabilities include custom AI agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, sandboxed multi-language code execution, web search integration, generative UI code artifacts, image generation and editing tools, speech-to-text and text-to-speech, conversation branching, and context compaction. It also offers enterprise-ready features such as a browser-based admin panel, multi-user authentication (OAuth2, LDAP, email), role-based permissions, resumable streams, OpenTelemetry observability, and Langfuse integration. Notable technologies mentioned include Redis, Docker, ClickHouse, and OpenID.

name: sentry
description: Developer-first error tracking and performance monitoring
summary: Sentry is a debugging platform designed for developers to detect, trace, and fix issues in software applications. Its main capabilities include error tracking, tracing, log analysis, uptime monitoring, and code insights. The platform provides official SDKs for a wide array of technologies and languages, including JavaScript, Electron, React-Native, Python, Ruby, PHP, Laravel, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, Objective-C, Swift, C#, F#, C, C++, Dart, Flutter, Perl, Clojure, Elixir, Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot Engine, and PowerShell. Intended users are developers looking to diagnose and resolve code breaks efficiently.

name: pyenv
description: Simple Python version management
summary:
pyenv is a simple, Unix-tradition tool designed for easy Python version management. It allows users to switch between multiple versions of Python on a per-user or per-project basis. The project's main capabilities include changing global and local Python versions, supporting multiple Python distributions (such as CPython, PyPy, Stackless Python, and Jython), overriding versions via environment variables, and searching for commands across multiple Python versions concurrently for testing tools like tox. 

Intended for developers and system users needing isolated or multiple Python environments, pyenv operates without depending directly on Python itself, utilizing pure shell scripts and a shim-based approach added to the system `PATH`. It does not manage virtual environments directly, though users can pair it with tools like virtualenv or pyenv-virtualenv. Built using shell scripts and tested with Bats, pyenv is compatible with Linux, macOS, and Windows via WSL (with native Windows support available via forks like pyenv-win).

name: logseq
description: A privacy-first, open-source platform for knowledge management and collaboration. Download link:  http://github.com/logseq/logseq/releases. roadmap: https://logseq.io/p/NX4mc_ggEV
summary:
Logseq is a privacy-first, open-source platform designed for knowledge management and collaboration. It offers powerful tools for organizing notes, structuring ideas, managing tasks, and annotating PDFs, with primary support for Markdown and Org-mode file formats. Intended for students, professionals, and anyone seeking to streamline workflows and boost productivity, Logseq features a growing ecosystem of customizable themes, plugins, and mobile apps. 

The platform supports a database version (DB version) utilizing DB graphs, SQLite database backups, and Real Time Collaboration (RTC) features for multi-device syncing and collaborative workflows. Logseq is built using technologies such as Clojure, ClojureScript, DataScript, OCaml, Angstrom, isomorphic-git, and SCI (Small Clojure Interpreter), alongside a parser named mldoc.

name: payload
description: Payload is the open-source, fullstack Next.js framework, giving you instant backend superpowers. Get a full TypeScript backend and admin panel instantly. Use Payload as a headless CMS or for building powerful applications.
summary:
Payload is a Next.js-native headless CMS and application framework designed to integrate directly into existing `/app` folders. It functions as both a backend and frontend integration tool, allowing developers to query databases directly using React Server Components without relying solely on REST or GraphQL APIs. 

The project's main capabilities include automatic TypeScript type generation, built-in authentication, version control and drafts, localization, a block-based layout builder, a customizable React-based admin panel, a Lexical rich text editor, granular access control, and document- and field-level hooks. It supports flexible deployments across serverless environments like Vercel and Cloudflare, with built-in integrations for tools such as Neon, Vercel Blob, Cloudflare Workers, R2, and D1. 

Payload is intended for developers and teams building modern web applications, websites, blogs, and ecommerce stores who require an open-source, extensible, and vendor-lock-in-free alternative to traditional content management systems. Notable technologies used include React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and various cloud database and storage providers.

name: hindsight
description: Hindsight: Agent Memory That Learns
summary:
Hindsight is an agent memory system designed to enable AI agents to learn and evolve over time rather than merely recall past conversation history. It provides state-of-the-art performance on long-term memory tasks, serving as an alternative to traditional RAG and knowledge graph techniques. 

The project organizes agent memory using biomimetic data structures, categorizing information into world facts, experiences, observations, and mental models. Its core operations include `retain` (storing and extracting normalized facts and temporal relationships), `recall` (retrieving memories using parallel semantic, keyword, graph, and temporal search strategies with reciprocal rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking), and `reflect` (performing deep analysis to form new connections). It features isolated memory banks with configurable disposition traits, multilingual support, and a Memory Defense policy for PII and secret redaction.

Hindsight is intended for conversational AI agents, autonomous task-performing agents, AI employees, and coding assistants. Notable technologies include PostgreSQL with pgvector, Oracle AI Database 23ai, Python, Node.js/TypeScript, Go, Docker, Kubernetes, and native integrations with Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

name: edex-ui
description: A cross-platform, customizable science fiction terminal emulator with advanced monitoring & touchscreen support.
summary:
eDEX-UI is a fullscreen, cross-platform terminal emulator and system monitor designed to replicate a sci-fi computer interface, heavily inspired by the visual effects of the movie *TRON: Legacy*. 

Intended for users seeking a futuristic user experience or a Hollywood-style hacker aesthetic, it offers real-time hardware and network monitoring, a fully featured terminal emulator supporting tabs and mouse events, touch display support with an on-screen keyboard, a directory viewer that tracks the current working directory, and optional sound effects. The interface supports advanced customization through themes, layout configurations, and CSS injections. 

The project is built using JavaScript technologies and notable dependencies include xterm.js, systeminformation, SmoothieCharts, and ENCOM Globe.

name: react-hook-form
description: 📋 React Hooks for form state management and validation (Web + React Native)
summary: React Hook Form is a high-performance, small-sized library designed for form validation and management in React applications, built with a focus on user and developer experience. It features zero dependencies and embraces native HTML form validation while offering out-of-the-box integration with various UI libraries. The project natively supports schema validation through tools such as Yup, Zod, AJV, Superstruct, and Joi. Intended for React developers seeking efficient form state management, the library provides hooks like `useForm` to simplify input registration, error handling, and submission logic.

name: ai-job-search
description: The job search that runs on your machine. AI job application framework built on Claude Code: evaluate postings, tailor CVs, write cover letters, prep interviews. Fork it and own it.
summary:
The **AI Job Search** framework is an open-source, machine-local toolchain built on **Claude Code** designed to automate and manage the entire job search and application lifecycle. 

### Project Purpose
The project serves as a structured workflow to help job seekers find relevant positions, evaluate role fit, tailor application materials, and prepare for interviews using AI assistance. Originally created by a geophysicist to navigate a career transition, the framework aims to reduce the time spent on manual writing and tracking while maintaining candidate authenticity.

### Main Capabilities
- **Onboarding & Profiling (`/setup`):** Ingests documents (master CVs, LinkedIn exports, diplomas, past applications) or conducts interviews to build a comprehensive candidate profile.
- **Job Scraping & Ranking (`/scrape`, `/rank`):** Integrates with job portals to search, deduplicate, batch-score, and shortlist positions against a custom fit framework.
- **Application Pipeline (`/apply`):** Evaluates role fit, drafts tailored CVs and cover letters in LaTeX, deploys a secondary reviewer agent to critique drafts, compiles and visually inspects PDFs, and performs an ATS (Applicant Tracking System) text-layer parseability check.
- **Interview Preparation (`/interview`):** Builds stage-specific prep packs, maps questions to STAR examples, and conducts mock interviews following roleplay protocols.
- **Tracking & Syncing (`/outcome`, `notion-sync`, `gmail-sync`, `html-report`):** Records application outcomes, auto-detects status signals from Gmail, publishes read-only pipeline views to Notion databases, and generates offline-compatible HTML dashboard reports.
- **Competency Expansion & Upskilling (`/expand`, `/upskill`):** Scans public portfolios and online presence to uncover unlisted skills, analyzes skill gaps, and generates targeted learning plans.
- **Extensibility (`/add-template`, `add-portal`):** Registers custom CV/cover letter toolchains (LaTeX, Typst) and scaffolds new market-specific job-portal search skills.

### Intended Users
Job seekers, career changers, and professionals looking for a privacy-focused, automated workflow to manage job hunts directly on their local machines. 

### Notable Technologies
- **Claude Code** (Anthropic CLI)
- **Python** (version 3.10+)
- **Bun** (for TypeScript-based job search CLI tools)

name: reactjs-interview-questions
description: List of top 500 ReactJS Interview Questions & Answers....Coding exercise questions are coming soon!!
summary:
React is an open-source, component-based JavaScript library maintained by Meta for building user interfaces across web and mobile platforms. The repository serves as a comprehensive, multi-section collection of React interview questions, answers, code examples, and deep dives. It covers core React concepts—such as components, props, state, JSX, synthetic events, the Virtual DOM, and React Fiber—alongside modern paradigms like React Hooks (useState, useEffect, useReducer, useContext, useMemo, etc.), React 18/19 concurrent rendering features, Server Actions, and the React Compiler. 

Additionally, the content spans related ecosystem tools including React Router, Redux and Redux Toolkit, Redux-Saga/Thunk, Formik, React Intl for internationalization, testing frameworks like Jest, and React Native. The intended audience includes frontend developers, engineers preparing for technical interviews, and practitioners seeking reference material on React patterns, state management, and performance optimization techniques. No specific build tools or runtime environments are mandated beyond standard JavaScript tooling and modern web browsers.

name: meteor
description: Meteor, the JavaScript App Platform
summary: Meteor is an ultra-simple environment for building modern web applications using modern JavaScript. It allows developers to rapidly prototype, develop, and build applications for any device—including web, iOS, Android, and desktop—using the same codebase. The platform enables out-of-the-box integration with popular frameworks and tools, supporting technologies such as React, Blaze, Vue, Svelte, and Solid. Intended for developers building cross-platform applications, Meteor requires Node.js (version 22 or greater) and provides command-line tools for project creation and execution via `npx meteor` and `meteor create`. Developer resources include Atmosphere packages, Galaxy deployment, and integration with AI coding assistants through Meteor Agent Skills.

name: jan
description: Jan is an open source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100% offline on your computer.
summary:
Jan is an open-source, privacy-first desktop application designed as a ChatGPT replacement to download and run Large Language Models (LLMs) locally with full user control. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Run local AI models (such as Llama, Gemma, Qwen, and GPT-oss) downloaded from HuggingFace.
- Integrate with cloud-based services like OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, and MiniMax.
- Create and manage custom AI assistants for specialized tasks.
- Provide a local OpenAI-compatible API server running at `localhost:1337` for external applications.
- Support Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations for agentic workflows.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, researchers, and privacy-conscious users seeking a local, customizable, and offline-capable alternative to proprietary chat interfaces.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Built using Tauri and Node.js.
- Utilizes Llama.cpp as its local inference engine.
- Supports cross-platform execution on Windows, macOS (including Apple Silicon with Metal support), and Linux, with hardware acceleration options for CPU, Vulkan, Metal, CUDA, and ROCm/HIP.

name: hyper
description: A terminal built on web technologies
summary:
Hyper is a command-line interface terminal application built on open web standards by Vercel. Its project goals focus on delivering a beautiful, extensible, speedy, and stable experience while providing a robust extension API for developers. The project targets command-line interface users and extension authors seeking a customizable and powerful productivity interface. 

Technologies utilized in the project include Node.js, Electron, Webpack, and pnpm. Development supports platforms including Linux, macOS, and Windows.

name: desktop
description: Welcome to a calmer internet
summary: Zen Browser is a Firefox-based web browser designed to enhance user productivity. Built using Firefox versions (including Release and Twilight editions), the open-source project aims to provide a focused browsing experience. It invites community contributions, bug reports via GitHub Issues, and feature requests through GitHub Discussions.

name: cobra
description: A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions
summary:
Cobra is a Go library and accompanying `cobra-cli` generator designed for creating powerful, modern command-line interface (CLI) applications with a structure consisting of commands, arguments, and flags. 

Its main capabilities include supporting easy subcommand-based CLIs with nested subcommands, fully POSIX-compliant flags, global, local, and cascading flags, intelligent command suggestions, automatic help generation, subcommand grouping, automated shell autocomplete for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell, automatically generated man pages, and command aliases. It also features optional seamless integration with the `viper` library for 12-factor applications and utilizes the `pflag` library for flag management.

Cobra is intended for developers building Go-based command-line tools. It is widely used in prominent projects such as Kubernetes, Hugo, and GitHub CLI.

name: cobalt
description: best way to save what you love
summary:
Cobalt is a friendly, efficient media downloader designed to save public content without ads, trackers, paywalls, or caching. Acting as a proxy, it allows users to quickly download free and publicly accessible content by pasting a link. 

Structured as a monorepo, cobalt includes source code for the API, frontend web interface, related packages, and documentation for running and protecting instances. It is intended for end users seeking a straightforward downloading tool, while placing full responsibility for content use and distribution on the user.

name: fd
description: A simple, fast and user-friendly alternative to 'find'
summary:
`fd` is a simple, fast, and user-friendly command-line program designed to find entries in a filesystem as an alternative to `find`. 

**Project Purpose:** Provide sensible, opinionated defaults for recursive filesystem searches with an intuitive syntax, rapid parallelized directory traversal, and colorized output based on file types.

**Main Capabilities:**
* Supports regular expression and glob-based search patterns with smart case handling.
* Automatically ignores hidden files, hidden directories, and patterns listed in `.gitignore` or `.fdignore` files.
* Allows searching by specific file extensions, file sizes, modification times, permissions, owning users/groups, and full paths.
* Features built-in parallel command execution via `-x` (`--exec`) and `-X` (`--exec-batch`) to process search results.

**Intended Users:** Developers, system administrators, and command-line users looking for a faster, more convenient file search utility.

**Notable Technologies:** Built with Rust, leveraging the `regex` and `ignore` crates.

name: EasySpider
description: A visual no-code/code-free web crawler/spider易采集：一个可视化浏览器自动化测试/数据采集/网页爬虫软件，可以无代码图形化的设计和执行爬虫任务。别名：ServiceWrapper面向Web应用的智能化服务封装系统。
summary:
EasySpider (易采集) is a completely free, visual, code-free web crawler and browser automation testing software designed for designing and executing data collection tasks through a graphical user interface. Users can point and click on web elements to select content, extract data fields, loop through lists, follow links to detail pages, and handle complex workflows like pagination and conditional logic. 

The software supports standalone command-line execution for seamless embedding into external systems, writing data to databases such as MySQL, and integrating with proxy networks (e.g., Bright Data, Webshare, Thordata) and AI-driven CAPTCHA-solving services (e.g., CapSolver). 

Intended for developers, researchers, and enterprises needing large-scale public web data extraction, EasySpider is released under the AGPL-3.0 license and is suitable for commercial use and secondary development. It has been featured in academic publications such as The Web Conference (WWW) 2023.

name: jsoncrack.com
description: ✨ Innovative and open-source visualization application that transforms various data formats, such as JSON, YAML, XML and CSV into interactive graphs.
summary:
JSON Crack is an open-source JSON editor and visualization tool designed to transform JSON, YAML, CSV, and XML data into interactive graphs and trees. Intended for developers and data analysts, the tool allows users to explore, format, and validate structured data locally with complete privacy. 

Main capabilities include seamless format conversion (such as JSON to CSV or XML to JSON), JSON Schema generation and validation, jq and JSON path query execution, and code generation for TypeScript interfaces, Golang structs, Kotlin data classes, and Rust serde types. Visualizations can be formatted in dark or light mode and exported as PNG, JPEG, or SVG images. 

The project provides a web application alongside integrations including a VS Code extension, a Chrome extension, and the `jsoncrack-react` npm package. Development prerequisites include Node.js (>=24.x) and pnpm (>=10), with Docker support also available.

name: data-engineer-handbook
description: This is a repo with links to everything you'd ever want to learn about data engineering
summary: The Data Engineering Handbook is a comprehensive curated collection of resources designed for individuals aspiring to become data engineers. It provides structured roadmaps, boot camps, hands-on projects, interview preparation materials, and design patterns. The repository targets beginners and intermediate practitioners looking to build practical skills in data engineering. It covers an extensive array of technologies and tools across orchestration (such as Apache Airflow, Dagster, and Prefect), data lakes and cloud platforms (such as Databricks, Delta Lake, and Apache Iceberg), data warehousing, data quality, analytics, modern OLAP databases (such as ClickHouse and DuckDB), and LLM application libraries. Additionally, the handbook lists prominent books, communities, newsletters, whitepapers, company tech blogs, social media creators, podcasts, courses, and certifications relevant to data engineering and machine learning engineering.

name: headscale
description: An open source, self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale control server
summary:
Headscale is an open-source, self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale control server, designed to provide a free, open-source alternative for self-hosters, hobbyists, and small organizations. Built to work with Tailscale—a modern VPN built on top of Wireguard—Headscale manages a single Tailscale network (tailnet), functioning as an exchange point for Wireguard public keys, assigning client IP addresses, establishing user boundaries, enabling machine sharing, and exposing node routes. 

The project targets self-hosters and enthusiasts looking for a dedicated private overlay network control server. Notable technologies used in its development include Go, Buf, Protobuf, and Nix, with code quality maintained via tools such as golangci-lint, golines, gofumpt, and clang-format. Headscale is not officially associated with Tailscale Inc.

name: lossless-cut
description: The swiss army knife of lossless video/audio editing
summary:
LosslessCut is a cross-platform FFmpeg GUI designed for extremely fast, lossless operations on video, audio, and subtitle files. Its primary purpose is to allow users to trim, cut, merge, and rearrange media files without re-encoding, preserving original quality while discarding unnecessary data. 

Main capabilities include lossless cutting, smart cuts, multi-track stream editing, merging arbitrary files with identical codec parameters, remuxing into different containers, capturing snapshots, extracting frames, editing metadata and chapter marks, and automatic black scene or silent audio detection. It also provides tools for timeline zooming, timecode offset adjustments, rotation correction, and basic CLI and HTTP API access. 

The software is intended for creators, editors, and anyone needing to quickly clean up, edit, or extract segments from large media files captured on cameras, drones, or downloaded from the web. Notable technologies utilized include FFmpeg for underlying media processing and the Chromium browser's HTML5 video player for UI playback. Supported formats and codecs span MP4, MOV, WebM, Matroska, OGG, WAV, H264, H265, AV1, VP8, VP9, AAC, MP3, and FLAC, among others.

name: ccxt
description: A unified trading API with more than 100 crypto exchanges and prediction markets in JavaScript / TypeScript / Python / C# / PHP / Go / Java / Rust
summary:
CCXT is a cryptocurrency trading library providing access to over 100 centralized exchanges (CEX), decentralized exchanges (DEX), and prediction markets. It features a unified API supporting public and private REST and WebSocket endpoints for cross-exchange analytics, algorithmic trading, market data storage, and backtesting. 

The library is intended for coders, developers, data scientists, financial analysts, and technically skilled traders. Its main capabilities include order execution, account management, live price streaming, order book fetching, and historical OHLCV data retrieval. 

CCXT is implemented across multiple languages, supporting JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, C#, PHP, Go, Java, and Rust. It features built-in leaky bucket and rolling window rate limiters, along with a CLI tool and an official MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for AI agent integration. Notable technologies used optionally for performance optimization include orjson and coincurve.

name: kong
description: 🦍 The API and AI Gateway
summary:
Kong (Kong Gateway) is a cloud-native, platform-agnostic, scalable API, LLM, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway designed for orchestrating microservices and agentic traffic with high performance and extensibility via plugins. 

Main capabilities include advanced routing, load balancing, health checking, SSL/TLS termination, L4/L7 traffic proxying, authentication (JWT, basic auth, OAuth, ACLs), and a universal LLM API routing across providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, GCP Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Databricks, Mistral, and Huggingface. It also features MCP traffic governance, security, observability, and autogeneration from RESTful APIs, along with over 60 AI-specific features like semantic routing, semantic caching, security, and observability. Kong supports multiple deployment models including declarative databaseless deployment, hybrid control/data plane separation, native Kubernetes Ingress Controller integration, and a Plugin Development Kit (PDK) allowing developers to write custom plugins in Lua, Go, or JavaScript.

Intended users are software engineers, platform architects, and DevOps teams seeking a centralized gateway layer to manage, secure, and monitor traditional API traffic alongside modern AI and MCP workloads. Notable technologies utilized include Docker, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, and various LLM and cloud AI providers.

name: Fabric
description: Fabric is an open-source framework for augmenting humans using AI. It provides a modular system for solving specific problems using a crowdsourced set of AI prompts that can be used anywhere.
summary:
`fabric` is an open-source framework designed to augment humans using AI by solving integration challenges through organized prompts called "Patterns." Written in Go, it allows users to break complex problems into component parts, execute them via a command-line interface, built-in REST API server, or web interface, and manage AI-driven workflows like content summarization, coding feature creation, and transcript extraction.

Main capabilities include supporting numerous native and OpenAI-compatible AI providers (such as OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Ollama, Azure, Amazon Bedrock, and local models), custom pattern management, prompt strategies (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thought), helper utilities (`to_pdf`, `code2context`, `generate_changelog`), and YouTube transcription. Intended users include developers, command-line power users, and enterprise practitioners looking to integrate AI into daily tasks. Notable technologies utilized include Go, Markdown for prompts, Docker, and various LLM SDKs and gateways.

name: spark
description: Apache Spark - A unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing
summary:
