Apache Spark is a unified analytics engine designed for large-scale data processing. It provides an optimized engine supporting general computation graphs for data analysis along with high-level APIs in Scala, Java, Python, and a deprecated R interface. 

The platform includes a rich set of higher-level tools and libraries:
- **Spark SQL**: For SQL queries and DataFrames.
- **pandas API on Spark**: For pandas workloads.
- **MLlib**: For machine learning tasks.
- **GraphX**: For graph processing.
- **Structured Streaming**: For stream processing.

Spark integrates with storage systems like HDFS using Hadoop core libraries and supports cluster managers such as YARN and Kubernetes. It is built using Apache Maven.

name: zod
description: TypeScript-first schema validation with static type inference
summary:
Zod is a TypeScript-first schema validation library with static type inference. It allows developers to define schemas and parse untrusted data to produce strongly typed, validated results. 

Main capabilities include data parsing and validation (supporting synchronous and asynchronous methods, `safeParse` for error handling without exceptions, and ahead-of-time compilation via `z.compile` for faster performance), static type extraction using `z.infer`, type divergence handling with `z.input` and `z.output`, built-in JSON Schema conversion, and an immutable API. 

The library is intended for TypeScript and JavaScript developers building applications in Node.js or modern browser environments. Notable technologies and features include zero external dependencies, a tiny core bundle footprint, and support for refinements and transforms.

name: babel
description: 🐠 Babel is a compiler for writing next generation JavaScript.
summary: Babel is a JavaScript compiler that enables developers to write next-generation JavaScript and compile newer language features, such as ES2020 syntax, down to versions supported by target environments. Intended for web developers and JavaScript programmers, Babel transforms unsupported code features into backwards-compatible equivalents. The repository is structured as a monorepo containing multiple npm packages and is maintained primarily by a community of volunteers.

name: parcel
description: The zero configuration build tool for the web. 📦🚀
summary:
Parcel is a zero-configuration build tool and web bundler designed to take projects from initial setup to massive production applications. Its primary purpose is to provide an out-of-the-box development experience combined with a scalable architecture for web development. 

Main capabilities include a built-in dev server with hot reloading, error diagnostics, native performance via a Rust-written JavaScript compiler, parallel builds using worker threads, persistent caching, and automatic production optimizations such as tree-shaking, minification, image resizing, content hashing, and automatic code splitting. Additionally, it transforms code for various target environments, supporting modern and legacy browsers alongside zero-configuration JSX and TypeScript compilation. 

Intended users include web developers building web applications or libraries of any size. Notable technologies utilized include Rust, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, JSX, and TypeScript.

name: front-end-interview-handbook
description: Front End interview preparation materials for busy engineers (updated for 2026)
summary:
The Front End Interview Handbook by GreatFrontEnd is a comprehensive preparation guide designed for software engineers navigating front end job interviews. The project addresses domain-specific interview requirements covering HTML, CSS, JavaScript, the DOM, and algorithms. 

Main capabilities and resources provided include:
- Overviews of various front end interview formats, including company-specific processes.
- Front end system design interview guides.
- Answers to front-end developer trivia questions, including the h5bp interview questions.
- JavaScript utility function and coding questions.
- Curated company interview questions.

The handbook is intended for job seekers and front end engineers preparing for technical interviews. It highlights technologies and core concepts such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and DOM manipulation, and offers integrations with the GreatFrontEnd practice platform, study plans, and translations in multiple languages including Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, and Tagalog.

name: react-use
description: React Hooks — 👍
summary:
react-use is a collection of essential React hooks, serving as a port of libreact. It is designed for React developers seeking ready-to-use hooks to handle sensors, UI interactions, animations, side-effects, component lifecycles, and advanced state management. 

The library provides comprehensive capabilities categorized into several areas:
- **Sensors:** Tracks browser and device states such as battery, geolocation, hover, network connection, media queries, orientation, mouse position, scroll position, and window size.
- **UI:** Exposes controls for audio and video playback, handles fullscreen display, speech synthesis, physical vibration, and click-away detection.
- **Animations:** Manages component re-rendering via requestAnimationFrame (`useRaf`), intervals, timeouts, spring dynamics, and tweening.
- **Side-effects:** Manages asynchronous functions, cookies, local and session storage, debouncing, throttling, copy-to-clipboard, browser favicons, and page titles.
- **Lifecycles:** Enhances React lifecycle management with hooks for tracking mounting status, running effects once, handling updates, and logging render cycles.
- **State:** Offers advanced state utilities including persistent state, reducers with middleware, shared state contexts, previous values tracking, validation, and object/array tracking.

Notable technologies utilized include React Hooks and standard browser APIs like the Vibration API and requestAnimationFrame.

name: ray
description: Ray is an AI compute engine. Ray consists of a core distributed runtime and a set of AI Libraries for accelerating ML workloads.
summary:
Ray is a unified, general-purpose distributed framework designed for scaling AI and Python applications from a single laptop to large clusters, cloud providers, and Kubernetes. 

The project consists of a core distributed runtime and a suite of specialized AI libraries. Ray Core relies on key abstractions including Tasks (stateless functions), Actors (stateful worker processes), and Objects (immutable cluster-wide values). Its ML compute libraries comprise Data (scalable datasets), Train (distributed training), Tune (scalable hyperparameter tuning), RLlib (scalable reinforcement learning), and Serve (scalable and programmable model serving). The framework also provides monitoring and debugging tools such as the Ray Dashboard and the Ray Distributed Debugger. 

Ray is intended for developers, data scientists, and machine learning engineers seeking to scale compute-intensive Python and machine learning workloads without managing complex infrastructure.

name: retrofit
description: A type-safe HTTP client for Android and the JVM
summary:
Retrofit is a type-safe HTTP client designed for Android and Java. Developed by Square, Inc., the project simplifies network operations by turning HTTP APIs into Java interfaces. 

Main capabilities include making type-safe HTTP requests and handling data serialization. The library requires a minimum of Java 8+ or Android API 21+ and depends on OkHttp. R8 shrinking and obfuscation rules are included automatically, while ProGuard users must manually configure options from the provided `retrofit2.pro` file along with rules for OkHttp.

name: omarchy
description: Beautiful, Modern & Opinionated Linux
summary: Omarchy is a Linux distribution created by DHH, designed to be beautiful, fun, and agentic. It features an extensive manual covering getting started guides, navigation, themes, hotkeys, a unified clipboard with history, reminders, text extraction, dictation, screenshots, and recording. The OS includes an Omarchy CLI, a terminal environment centered around Neovim, AI capabilities, development and shell tools, TUIs, GUIs, browsers, web apps, gaming support, PDF tools, and a Windows VM. Intended users include individuals transitioning from Mac or Windows as well as developers seeking customized desktop environments. Configuration options support updates, dotfiles, shell plugins, monitors, networking, hardware authentication, custom themes, system snapshots, security, and dual-boot or unattended installations. Omarchy is released under the MIT License.

name: build-web-application-with-golang
description: A golang ebook intro how to build a web with golang
summary: This open-source guide, titled "Build Web Application with Golang," teaches developers how to build web applications using the Go programming language. The project covers web development concepts and practical implementation details, complete with setup configurations for development tools like Vim and Emacs. Available in numerous language versions—including English, Chinese, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish, Bengali, Japanese, Persian, and Thai—the repository serves developers worldwide learning Go web programming. The book content is licensed under the CC BY-SA 3.0 License, while the accompanying code is available under the BSD 3-Clause License.

name: HEU_KMS_Activator
summary: HEU_KMS_Activator is a utility designed for activating Windows and Office products. Its main capabilities include KMS-based activation of Microsoft Windows (Vista, 7, 8, 8.1, 10, 11) and Microsoft Office (various versions including 2010 through 2021/365), along with digital license activation, KMS server management, and OEM information injection. The intended users are system administrators, IT professionals, and individual users seeking a local KMS activation solution for Microsoft products. Notable technologies utilized include the Key Management Service (KMS) protocol, digital licensing mechanisms, and batch/scripting environments suited for Windows systems.

name: TensorFlow-Examples
description: TensorFlow Tutorial and Examples for Beginners (support TF v1 & v2)
summary:
TensorFlow Examples is a tutorial-based repository designed for beginners seeking clear, concise implementations using TensorFlow (supporting both TensorFlow v1 and v2). It provides both Jupyter notebooks and source code with explanations covering basic operations, machine learning introductions, and the MNIST dataset. 

Main capabilities include implementing basic models like Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Word2Vec (Word Embedding), Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT), K-Means, and Random Forest. It also covers supervised and unsupervised neural networks—such as Multi-layer Perceptrons, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (LSTM), Bi-directional and Dynamic RNNs, Auto-Encoders, Variational Auto-Encoders (VAE), Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), and Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN). Additionally, the project features utilities for saving and restoring models, building custom layers, and using Tensorboard for visualization, alongside data management tools for parsing data, TFRecords, image augmentation, and multi-GPU hardware training.

Intended users are developers and beginners diving into deep learning and machine learning concepts. Notable technologies employed include TensorFlow, TFLearn, NumPy, and Tensorboard.

name: reactive-resume
description: A one-of-a-kind resume builder that keeps your privacy in mind. Completely secure, customizable, portable, open-source and free forever. Try it out today!
summary:
Reactive Resume is a free, open-source resume builder designed to help individuals create, update, and share resumes with live previews, 15 customizable templates, and multiple export formats including PDF, JSON, and DOCX. 

Key capabilities include drag-and-drop section ordering, a rich text editor, AI integration (supporting OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Anthropic Claude), multi-language support, sharing via unique links, and JSON Resume importing. It features robust privacy controls, requiring no tracking by default, and supports self-hosting via Docker or Vercel with features like passkeys, two-factor authentication, and client-side PDF rendering. 

Intended for job seekers looking for fine-tuned control over their resume design and data ownership, the platform is built using TypeScript, React 19, Vite, TanStack Router, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM, Better Auth, and Zustand.

name: gradio
description: Build and share delightful machine learning apps, all in Python. 🌟 Star to support our work!
summary:
Gradio is an open-source Python package designed to help developers quickly build and share web applications, demos, machine learning models, APIs, or arbitrary Python functions without requiring JavaScript, CSS, or web hosting experience. 

Main capabilities include creating standard model wrappers via the `gr.Interface` class, custom layouts and complex data flows using `gr.Blocks`, specialized chatbot user interfaces through `gr.ChatInterface`, built-in public URL sharing (`share=True`), hot-reloading development modes, and programmatic querying via Python (`gradio_client`) and JavaScript (`@gradio/client`) clients. It also supports integrating AI coding assistants with project-specific skills.

Intended users include machine learning engineers, data scientists, and Python developers looking to rapidly prototype, test, and distribute interactive web applications. 

Notable technologies utilized in the stack include Python (3.10+), FastAPI, Svelte, Vite, pnpm, Tailwind CSS, Storybook, and Hugging Face Spaces.

name: puter
description: 🌐 The Internet Computer! Free, Open-Source, and Self-Hostable.
summary:
Puter is an advanced, open-source, and self-hostable internet computer designed to function as an all-in-one personal cloud platform. 

For users, Puter delivers a comprehensive suite of applications and features for working, creating, and playing under one roof, including utilities like a Notepad, Voice Recorder, Spreadsheet, and Camera. For developers, it provides an end-to-end environment to build, publish, and monetize web applications and games. Developers can leverage integrated features such as AI, Cloud Storage, a Key-Value Database, and Serverless Workers, and subsequently publish their apps directly to the Puter App Store.

The project supports local development via Node.js and Docker, and offers straightforward self-hosting installation scripts for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Puter is licensed under the AGPL-3.0 license.

name: GPT_API_free
description: 免费大模型API，支持免费调用GPT、DeepSeek等主流模型，免费额度10000点，每日刷新！另付费价格最低官方1-2折！
summary:
GPT-API-free / DeepSeek-API-free is an all-in-one API forwarding and proxy service that provides unified access to major large language models including GPT, DeepSeek, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Qwen, Kimi, Minimax, and GLM. Designed for individual developers, non-commercial users, educators, and researchers, the project enables direct, proxy-free connections from mainland China via dynamic network acceleration and domestic transit hosts. 

The service maintains API standards fully compatible with OpenAI protocols, allowing seamless integration with various software and plugins. It features a free tier with daily and weekly quotas, alongside a paid tier offering high-speed, unthrottled access at a fraction of official pricing. Technologies and models supported span multi-modal, embedding, reasoning, image generation, and speech models such as GPT-5, o3, Claude Code, DeepSeek-R1, and Gemini.

name: open-code-review
description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
summary:
OpenCodeReview is an AI-powered code review CLI tool developed by Alibaba Group. Designed for developers and engineering teams, it reads Git diffs or scans entire codebases to generate structured, line-level code review comments. 

The tool combines deterministic engineering principles—such as precise file selection, smart file bundling, and fine-grained rule matching—with an LLM-driven agent that features specialized prompts and tools. This hybrid architecture prevents position drift and incomplete coverage while optimizing token consumption. Users can configure custom model endpoints, run workspace or branch-range reviews, perform full-file directory audits, or utilize a delegation mode with AI coding agents. 

OpenCodeReview supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, requires Git, and provides plugins and integrations for coding assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code, and OpenCode, alongside CI/CD workflows.

name: CPlusPlusThings
description: C++那些事
summary:
C++ 那些事 (Stories About C Plus Plus) is a comprehensive learning and reference repository designed for C++ beginners, interview candidates, and developers looking to master modern C++. The project covers fundamental C++ concepts, advanced programming techniques, Modern C++ features (C++11/14/17/20), STL source code analysis, design patterns, and concurrent programming.

Main capabilities include structured explanations and code examples for language features (such as `const`, `virtual`, and smart pointers), practice exercises and 10-day training modules, STL container implementations, multi-threading and multi-process concurrency, and C++ idioms like RAII and copy-and-swap. It also provides utility tools for debugging and container output, as well as guides for developer environments using VS Code, Bazel, Docker, and G++. 

Intended users are C++ learners, interviewees preparing for tech positions, and software developers seeking to deepen their understanding of C++ internals. Notable technologies and tools referenced throughout the repository include Modern C++, STL, Bazel, Docker, Jupyter Notebook, and debugging tools such as dbg-macro and rr.

name: agent-browser
description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
summary:
agent-browser is a fast, native Rust CLI and browser automation tool purpose-built for AI agents. It provides deterministic element selection using accessibility snapshots with unique refs (e.g., `@e1`), semantic locators, batch execution, and multimodal capabilities like annotated screenshots and streaming previews via WebSockets. 

Designed for AI systems and developers, agent-browser supports headless and headed modes, profile and session persistence, automated state management, and an integrated MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. It features native React introspection, universal Web Vitals metrics, and embedded axe-core accessibility auditing. Security features include a credential auth vault, domain allowlists, content boundaries, and action policies.

The tool primarily controls Google Chrome via Chrome for Testing (leveraging direct CDP connections or auto-discovery), with support for custom executables, local files, and remote cloud infrastructure providers including Browserless, Browserbase, Browser Use, Kernel, AWS Bedrock AgentCore, and iOS Simulator environments.

name: what-happens-when
description: An attempt to answer the age old interview question "What happens when you type google.com into your browser and press enter?"
summary:
This repository provides an exhaustive, step-by-step technical explanation answering the classic interview question: "What happens when you type google.com into your browser's address box and press enter?" 

The project details every underlying process involved in web navigation, intended for developers, students, and curious engineers. It covers physical keyboard interrupts, operating system message handling (Windows, OS X, Linux), URL parsing, HSTS checks, DNS lookups, and ARP requests. Furthermore, it outlines socket opening, TCP connections, the TLS handshake, TCP congestion control, HTTP requests and server-side request handling (via Apache, nginx, or IIS), and browser-side HTML parsing, CSS interpretation, and GPU-accelerated page rendering. No specific programming language or software framework is implemented, as the project serves as a comprehensive collaborative reference guide documenting standard low-level networking and browser architectures.

name: zig
description: Moved to Codeberg
summary: This repository has been moved to Codeberg and is no longer mirrored on GitHub. No further project information, capabilities, intended users, or technologies are available in the provided content.

name: pm2
description: Node.js/Typescript/Bun Production Process Manager with a built-in Load Balancer.
summary:
PM2 is a production process manager for Node.js and Bun applications with a built-in load balancer. It allows users to daemonize applications, keep them running forever, perform zero-downtime reloads, and facilitate system administration tasks. 

Key capabilities include:
- **Process Management:** Start, stop, restart, delete, and inspect applications (including Node.js, Bun, Python, Ruby, and binaries) with daemonization and monitoring.
- **Cluster Mode:** Load-balance HTTP, TCP, or UDP queries across multiple CPU cores to increase throughput and reliability, alongside hot reloads for zero downtime.
- **Monitoring & Logs:** Terminal-based real-time monitoring (`pm2 monit`), comprehensive log management, log rotation (`pm2-logrotate`), and cross-server monitoring via PM2+.
- **Container and Startup Integration:** Seamless execution in hardened production environments via `pm2-runtime` for Docker, alongside startup script generation for various init systems (`systemd`, `upstart`, `systemv`, `openrc`, `launchd`, `rcd`, `smf`).

PM2 is intended for developers and system administrators managing production applications on Linux, macOS, and Windows. It supports Node.js 18+ and Bun 1+. Notable technologies include Node.js, Bun, and AGPL-3.0 licensing.

name: sub2api
description: Sub2API 一站式开源中转服务，让 Claude、Openai 、Gemini、Grok订阅统一接入，支持拼车共享，更高效分摊成本，原生工具无缝使用。
summary:
Sub2API is an AI API gateway platform designed to manage and distribute API quotas from upstream AI product subscriptions (such as Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI Grok, and Gemini). It provides platform-generated API keys while handling authentication, billing, load balancing, request forwarding, rate limiting, and concurrency control. 

The platform supports multi-account management using OAuth and API keys, token-level usage tracking, intelligent scheduling with sticky sessions, and composite routing groups. It includes a built-in payment system (supporting Stripe, Alipay, WeChat Pay, and EasyPay) and an administrative web interface. Specialized support is also provided for Antigravity, TypeSafe/Jev System One protocols, and asynchronous image/video generation tasks.

Intended users include developers, teams, and enterprises seeking centralized management and cost-effective access to multiple large language models and coding tools (such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI).

Built with a Go (Gin, Ent) backend, a Vue 3 and TailwindCSS frontend, a PostgreSQL 15+ database, and a Redis 7+ cache/queue, Sub2API can be deployed via standalone binaries, Docker Compose, install scripts, or Apple container configurations.

name: diagram-design
description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, and Pi. 42 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
summary:
The **diagram-design** repository provides an editorial diagramming skill designed for AI coding assistants and agent hosts such as Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, Pi, Kiro, and OpenCode. Its primary purpose is to generate self-contained, publication-quality HTML and SVG diagrams tailored to an organization's specific brand identity rather than relying on generic rounded boxes or default templates.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Generates over forty layout grammars and visual types, including architecture, flowcharts, sequence diagrams, state machines, entity-relationship models, timelines, swimlanes, quadrants, Sankey diagrams, fishbone diagrams, Wardley maps, Kanban boards, UML classes, and database schemas.
- Brand onboarding that extracts a website's color palette and font stack to automatically apply custom paper, ink, muted, accent, and typography tokens.
- Import tools that parse and redraw existing `.drawio`, `.mmd` (Mermaid), and `.excalidraw` sources into editorial HTML/SVG outputs using a structured degrade ladder (sizes, detail levels, and audience settings).
- Export capabilities that render standalone SVG files or rasterize PNGs via Playwright, alongside structured JSON block-metadata registries.
- Optional interactive animation modes (`reveal`, `step`, `loop`) with static fallbacks and accessibility compliance.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, technical writers, executives, and content creators looking to embed clean, editorial-quality diagrams into documentation, slides, or websites without manual graphic design tools.

name: DeepSpeed
description: DeepSpeed is a deep learning optimization library that makes distributed training and inference easy, efficient, and effective.
summary: DeepSpeed is a deep learning optimization library designed to achieve extreme speed and scale for distributed training and inference of massive models like large language models. Its primary capabilities include ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer), ZeRO-Infinity, 3D-Parallelism, Ulysses Sequence Parallelism, DeepSpeed-MoE, DeepCompile, and stall-free offloading engines like ZenFlow and SuperOffload. The library is intended for machine learning researchers, developers, and enterprise engineering teams training large-scale transformer-based models and multi-million token sequences. DeepSpeed integrates with popular open-source frameworks such as PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers and Accelerate, PyTorch Lightning, MosaicML, Determined, and MMEngine, and supports hardware accelerators including NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel Gaudi and Xeon processors, Intel XPU, and Huawei Ascend NPUs.

name: python-patterns
description: A collection of design patterns/idioms in Python
summary:
**python-patterns** is a collection of design patterns and idioms implemented in Python, aimed at developers seeking to understand object-oriented design principles and architectural patterns. The repository covers **Creational Patterns** (such as `abstract_factory`, `borg`, `builder`, `factory`, `lazy_evaluation`, `pool`, and `prototype`), **Structural Patterns** (including `3-tier`, `adapter`, `bridge`, `composite`, `decorator`, `facade`, `flyweight`, `front_controller`, `mvc`, and `proxy`), and **Behavioral Patterns** (like `chain_of_responsibility`, `catalog`, `chaining_method`, `command`, `interpreter`, `iterator`, `mediator`, `memento`, `observer`, `publish_subscribe`, `registry`, `servant`, `specification`, `state`, `strategy`, `template`, and `visitor`). 

Additionally, the project provides **Design for Testability Patterns** (`dependency_injection`), **Fundamental Patterns** (`delegation_pattern`), other architectures like `blackboard`, `graph_search`, and `hsm` (hierarchical state machine), and highlights common **Anti-Patterns** to avoid in Python, such as `Singleton`, `God Object`, and `Inheritance overuse`. Technologies and tools referenced include Python, Pipenv, Travis CI, and Mermaid for diagrams.

name: curl
description: A command line tool and library for transferring data with URL syntax, supporting DICT, FILE, FTP, FTPS, GOPHER, GOPHERS, HTTP, HTTPS, IMAP, IMAPS, LDAP, LDAPS, MQTT, MQTTS, POP3, POP3S, RTSP, SCP, SFTP, SMB, SMBS, SMTP, SMTPS, TELNET, TFTP, WS and WSS. libcurl offers a myriad of powerful features
summary: curl is an open-source command-line tool and associated library, libcurl, designed for transferring data to or from servers using URLs. It supports a wide array of protocols, including DICT, FILE, FTP, FTPS, GOPHER, GOPHERS, HTTP, HTTPS, IMAP, IMAPS, LDAP, LDAPS, MQTT, MQTTS, POP3, POP3S, RTSP, SCP, SFTP, SMTP, SMTPS, TELNET, TFTP, WS, and WSS. The project enables developers to integrate robust data transfer capabilities into their own software using libcurl. Distributed under an MIT-like license, curl is intended for users and software developers requiring reliable network protocol interactions.

name: fuels-rs
description: Fuel Network Rust SDK
summary:
`fuels-rs` is the official Rust SDK for the Fuel blockchain ecosystem, inspired by ethers.js. It is designed for developers building, deploying, and testing smart contracts written in Sway. 

The project's main capabilities include compiling, deploying, and interacting with Sway contracts, launching local Fuel networks and nodes, crafting and signing transactions using hand-crafted scripts or contract calls, generating type-safe Rust bindings for contract methods, running Sway scripts, utilizing local test wallets, and providing a command-line interface for common operations. 

Notable technologies associated with the SDK include Rust, Sway, `forc`, `fuel-core`, and WebAssembly (WASM).

name: skills
description: Skills for Designers and Engineers.
summary:
Skills For Designers and Engineers is a collection of domain-expertise skills designed to help designers, engineers, and AI agents build better user interfaces and animations. Based on experience from companies like Vercel and Linear, the project provides guidelines, rules, and shortcuts to help users make correct design and animation choices, avoid common AI mistakes, and improve interface quality. 

The repository includes specific reference skills such as `emil-design-eng`, `animate`, `animate-expo` for React Native and Expo, `review-animations`, `improve-animations`, `find-animation-opportunities`, `animation-vocabulary`, `apple-design`, `write-swift` for modern Swift, `pick-ui-library`, `prototype`, `mobile-native`, `break-ui`, and `ask-sonner` for the Sonner toast library. Technologies mentioned include React Native, Expo, Swift, and Sonner. The package can be installed using `npx skills@latest add emilkowalski/skills`.

name: fuels-ts
description: Fuel Network Typescript SDK
summary:
fuels-ts is the TypeScript SDK for Fuel, designed to help developers build decentralized applications (dApps) on the Fuel network. The project purpose is to provide tooling for connecting to Fuel networks, building Sway programs, and interacting with smart contracts using TypeScript. 

Main capabilities include connecting to Mainnet, Testnet, or local Fuel nodes using providers, scaffolding fullstack dApps, and utilizing a comprehensive CLI (`fuels`). The CLI supports initializing configuration files (`fuels.config.ts`), building Sway workspaces, generating TypeScript types from Sway ABI JSON files (`typegen`), deploying contracts, and running a local Fuel node with hot-reload capabilities (`dev` and `node` commands).

The intended users are TypeScript and blockchain developers building applications on the Fuel VM. Notable technologies and components integrated within the ecosystem include TypeScript, GraphQL, the Fuel Core, Fuel Wallet SDK, Sway programming language, and the `forc` toolchain.

name: aria2
description: aria2 is a lightweight multi-protocol & multi-source, cross platform download utility operated in command-line. It supports HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, SFTP, BitTorrent and Metalink.
summary:
aria2 is an ultra-fast command-line download utility that supports HTTP(S), FTP, SFTP, BitTorrent, and Metalink protocols. It enables segmented downloading from multiple sources simultaneously to maximize bandwidth utilization, and can concurrently download via HTTP/FTP/SFTP while uploading data to a BitTorrent swarm. 

Key capabilities include Metalink chunk validation, BitTorrent extensions (such as DHT, PEX, Fast extension, and Web-Seeding), JSON-RPC and XML-RPC interfaces, daemon mode, IPv6 support with Happy Eyeballs, cookie management, speed throttling, and disk caching. It can also be integrated as a C++ library via `libaria2`. 

Intended for users seeking an efficient, highly configurable multi-protocol download manager, aria2 relies on notable technologies including C++11, OpenSSL, GnuTLS, libssh2, c-ares, zlib, libxml2, Expat, and sqlite3.

name: langgraph
description: Build resilient agents.
summary:
LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework designed for building, managing, and deploying long-running, stateful agents and workflows. Its main capabilities include durable execution that persists through failures and resumes automatically, human-in-the-loop oversight for inspecting and modifying state, comprehensive short-term and long-term memory, execution debugging and tracing via LangSmith, and scalable production-ready deployment. 

Intended for developers building stateful AI agents and LLM applications, LangGraph integrates seamlessly with LangChain products and works alongside tools like LangSmith, LangSmith Deployment, and Deep Agents. Inspired by Pregel, Apache Beam, and NetworkX, the project is available for Python via PyPI, with an equivalent JavaScript/TypeScript library known as LangGraph.js.

name: diagrams
description: :art: Diagram as Code for prototyping cloud system architectures
summary:
Diagrams is a "Diagram as Code" tool that lets developers and system architects draw cloud system architecture using Python code. It is designed for prototyping new system architecture designs and visualizing existing ones without relying on traditional graphical design tools. 

Main capabilities include tracking architecture diagram changes in version control systems and supporting major cloud providers and technologies such as AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, Alibaba Cloud, Oracle Cloud, OpenStack, Firebase, DigitalOcean, Elastic, On-Premises nodes, SaaS, and various programming frameworks and languages. The tool utilizes Graphviz for rendering diagrams and does not control actual cloud resources or generate cloud formation or terraform code. 

Intended users include developers, cloud architects, and data engineers looking to programmatically generate and maintain architecture diagrams. Notable technologies mentioned include Python (>= 3.9), Graphviz, and Pyodide for browser-based execution in the online playground.

name: yazi
description: 💥 Blazing fast terminal file manager written in Rust, based on async I/O.
summary:
Yazi is a blazing fast terminal file manager written in Rust, built on non-blocking asynchronous I/O and multi-threaded task scheduling. It provides an efficient, customizable file management experience featuring multi-tab support, cross-directory selection, bulk renaming, archive extraction, Git integration, a trash bin, and a virtual filesystem for remote file management. 

Yazi includes built-in support for multiple image protocols (such as Kitty unicode placeholders, iTerm2 inline images, and Sixel), code highlighting, image decoding, and asynchronous pre-loading. It offers a concurrent plugin and theme system written in Lua, a data distribution service for cross-instance communication via a publish-subscribe model, and an integrated package manager. The project also integrates with tools like ripgrep, fd, fzf, zoxide, and Rclone, and features Vim-like keybindings and components.

Intended for users seeking a high-performance, feature-rich command-line file manager, Yazi supports macOS, Linux, and Windows terminals.

name: git-flight-rules
description: Flight rules for git
summary:
"Flight rules for Git" is a comprehensive guide and scenario-specific standard operating procedure manual for programmers using Git, modeled after NASA's operational flight rules. Its primary purpose is to provide step-by-step instructions on what to do when things go wrong in Git, covering common and complex scenarios such as repository creation, commit editing, staging, discarding changes, branch management, rebasing, merging, stashing, searching history, and handling submodules. 

The intended users are developers and programmers ranging from beginners to advanced users seeking practical troubleshooting steps and reliable command patterns. The repository documents standard command-line operations compatible with Git version 2.13.0 and above, while referencing supporting tools and third-party utilities like bfg-repo-cleaner, fzf, and various Git GUI clients.

name: ailearning
description: AiLearning：数据分析+机器学习实战+线性代数+PyTorch+NLTK+TF2
summary:
AiLearning is a comprehensive, community-driven educational repository focused on machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing (NLP), graph computing, and knowledge graphs. Its primary purpose is to provide beginner-friendly tutorials, practical code implementations, notes, and video resources for students, software developers, and AI learners looking to transition from theoretical concepts to practical coding. 

The project covers foundational machine learning algorithms (such as KNN, decision trees, Naive Bayes, logistic regression, SVM, random forests, AdaBoost, regression, K-Means, Apriori, FP-growth, PCA, SVD, and MapReduce), deep learning architectures (CNN, RNN, LSTM, backpropagation), and a wide spectrum of NLP tasks (including Chinese word segmentation, text classification, language modeling, image captioning, machine translation, question answering, speech recognition, document summarization, named entity recognition, and sentiment analysis). 

Notable technologies and frameworks used throughout the repository include Python, TensorFlow 2.x, Keras, PyTorch, and Spark GraphX. The repository emphasizes accessible learning materials by pairing code explanations with video courses across platforms like Bilibili, AcFun, Youku, and NetEase Cloud Classroom, alongside curated datasets and reference materials.

name: agno
description: Build, run, and manage agent platforms.
summary:
Agno is a framework and runtime designed to build, run, and manage agent platforms. It enables developers to own their agent stack while maintaining control over data, memory, and security posture. 

Main capabilities include a production-ready API with over 50 endpoints (supporting Server-Sent Events and WebSockets), persistent storage for sessions, memory, knowledge, and traces, over 100 pre-built toolkits (integrating with services like GitHub, Slack, and Postgres), live context providers, human approval workflows, and OpenTelemetry-based observability. It also features JWT-based role-based access control (RBAC) for multi-tenant isolation, multi-platform interfaces (Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, AG-UI, A2A), cron-based scheduling, and container deployment capabilities. 

The ecosystem consists of the Agno SDK for building agents, the AgentOS runtime to run them as a service, and the AgentOS UI for platform management. Deployment is supported via Docker and templates for Railway, AWS, GCP, Azure, Fly, Render, Modal, and Helm.

name: daisyui
description: 🌼 🌼 🌼 🌼 🌼  The most popular, free and open-source Tailwind CSS component library
summary: daisyUI is a popular, free, and open-source component library designed for Tailwind CSS. It provides a collection of reusable UI components that help developers build web interfaces more efficiently using Tailwind CSS utilities.

name: free
description: 翻墙、免费翻墙、免费科学上网、免费节点、免费梯子、免费ss/v2ray/trojan节点、蓝灯、谷歌商店、翻墙梯子
summary: This project provides regularly updated, crowdsourced free proxy nodes (including v2ray, vmess, and Shadowsocks protocols) gathered from the internet. It offers tools and instructions for clients like v2rayN on Windows and v2rayNG on Android, allowing users to import and update subscription URLs or individual node configurations for network connectivity.

name: gkd
description: 基于无障碍，高级选择器，订阅规则的自定义屏幕点击安卓应用 | An Android APP with custom screen tapping based on Accessibility, Advanced Selectors, and Subscription Rules
summary:
GKD is a custom screen-clicking Android application that automates interactions based on specified conditions, such as recognizing particular text or nodes on a designated interface. It is designed to simplify repetitive workflows—like automated login confirmations—and bypass annoying startup flows or splash screens in various software applications. 

The project operates using a combination of Advanced Selectors (similar to CSS selectors that target node contexts), Subscription Rules, and Snapshot Review (via `gkd-kit/inspect`). GKD does not provide rules by default, requiring users to add local rules or fetch remote rules via subscription links.

Notable technologies and related tools associated with the project include Kotlin, Kotlin-JSON5, and Jetpack Compose-related derivatives. The software is licensed under the GPL-3.0-only license and is intended for study and communication purposes.

name: Alamofire
description: Elegant HTTP Networking in Swift
summary:
Alamofire is an HTTP networking library written in Swift, built on top of Apple's `URLSession`. It provides an expressive, compact syntax with features including chainable request and response methods, Swift Concurrency and Combine support, URL and JSON parameter encoding, file upload and download handling, authentication via `URLCredential`, HTTP response validation, cURL command output generation, dynamic request adaptation and retry, TLS certificate and public key pinning, and network reachability monitoring. 

Intended for Swift developers building applications across platforms such as iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS, the library streamlines complex networking workflows—such as background parsing into `Decodable` models and statistical metrics gathering. Additional ecosystem components include `AlamofireImage` for image handling and caching, and `AlamofireNetworkActivityIndicator` for managing network activity feedback on iOS. Installation is supported via the Swift Package Manager, CocoaPods, Carthage, and manual integration. Alamofire is released under the MIT license and maintained by the Alamofire Software Foundation.

name: BettaFish
description: 微舆：人人可用的多Agent舆情分析助手，打破信息茧房，还原舆情原貌，预测未来走向，辅助决策！从0实现，不依赖任何框架。
summary:
BettaFish (微舆) is an innovative, multi-agent public opinion and data analysis system designed to help users break through information cocoons, analyze trends, and assist in decision-making through natural conversation. The system monitors 30+ mainstream domestic and international social media platforms and millions of user comments using automated AI crawler clusters, advanced search capabilities, and multimodal content analysis engines. 

Core capabilities include broad news searching, multimodal processing of short-form videos and cards, deep private database mining via Insight Agent, and a collaborative ForumEngine where specialized agents debate and refine research paths via chained thoughts. The system also features an automated ReportEngine that synthesizes findings into customizable, interactive HTML and PDF reports using Markdown templates. 

Intended for researchers, developers, and analysts needing flexible business insights or public sentiment tracking, the project integrates fine-tuned sentiment analysis models (such as BERT, GPT-2 LoRA, and Qwen variants), traditional machine learning methods, and standard OpenAI-compatible LLM backends. It is built using Python with Flask, Streamlit, PostgreSQL/MySQL, Playwright, and SQLAlchemy, and supports deployment via Docker Compose.

name: stats
description: macOS system monitor in your menu bar
summary: Stats is a macOS system monitor that lives in your menu bar. Designed for users running macOS 12 (Monterey) and newer, the application allows users to monitor various hardware metrics and system performance indicators, including CPU utilization, GPU utilization, memory usage, disk utilization, network usage, battery level, fan control, sensor information (temperature, voltage, and power), Bluetooth devices, and multiple time zone clocks. It can be installed manually, via Homebrew, or configured as a remote monitoring agent over SSH to stream metrics to a System Stats account. Built without telemetry, Stats interacts with external APIs solely for update checks and public IP retrieval. The project is open-source under the MIT license.

name: fastlane
description: 🚀 The easiest way to automate building and releasing your iOS and Android apps
summary:
Fastlane is an automation tool designed for iOS and Android developers to streamline and simplify the deployment and release process of mobile applications. Its primary purpose is to automate tedious and repetitive development tasks, such as generating screenshots, managing provisioning profiles, and releasing apps to stores. 

Main capabilities include executing workflows interactively or non-interactively to handle app distribution and configuration management securely on local machines or servers. The tool is intended for iOS and Android developers, supporting execution via Ruby or Swift. Notable technologies and integrations associated with the project include Ruby, Swift, Homebrew, Bundler, and Xcode.

name: WeChatMsg
summary: WeChatMsg is a repository designed to help users preserve and take ownership of their personal WeChat chat histories and conversational data. The project emphasizes the importance of retaining life experiences and personal memories to empower individual AI companions and personal data centers. It includes support for generating annual reports, such as individual and dual-person annual reports, allowing users to review and summarize past conversations. The repository also references related projects by the author, including TrailSnap (an intelligent AI photo album application for recording and organizing travel experiences) and EasyBox (a multifunctional utility toolbox for PDF conversion, web-to-PDF rendering, and image metadata modification). WeChatMsg is licensed under the MIT License.

name: herdr
description: the runtime your coding agents live on
summary:
Herdr is a runtime built for coding agents and terminal workflows, distributed as a standalone Rust binary without Electron. It functions as a background server that keeps terminals running when clients close or SSH connections drop, restoring saved layouts after machine restarts. 

Main capabilities include:
- **Multi-Machine Management:** Combines local work and remote SSH machines into a single window with independent reconnects.
- **State Monitoring:** Marks every pane as working, blocked, or idle to highlight when an agent needs input.
- **Agent-Native Control:** Enables agents to drive Herdr via a CLI and socket API to spawn panes, prompt each other, and wait for blocked states.
- **Terminal Integration:** Owns the terminals for existing tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Opencode, and Grok without wrapping them.
- **Interface Flexibility:** Supports both tmux-style prefix keys and mouse interactions (click, drag, split), alongside a plugin ecosystem and marketplace.

Intended users are developers and AI agent builders looking to manage autonomous coding sessions and complex terminal layouts. Notable technologies mentioned include Rust and a socket API.

name: awesome-system-design-resources
description: Learn System Design concepts and prepare for interviews using free resources.
summary:
This repository is a curated collection of free system design resources and interview preparation materials aimed at software engineers and developers. The project's purpose is to help learners master fundamental distributed system concepts, networking, database design, caching strategies, asynchronous communication, and architectural patterns. 

The repository structures its content into core concepts—such as scalability, availability, CAP theorem, and consistent hashing—alongside networking and API fundamentals, database scaling techniques, and system design tradeoffs. It provides an answering framework for system design interviews and categorizes practical interview problems by difficulty (Easy, Medium, and Hard), featuring real-world system examples like TinyURL, WhatsApp, Netflix, Uber, and Google Docs. 

Additionally, the collection points users to external courses, newsletters, books, YouTube channels, and notable engineering articles and foundational distributed systems papers (such as MapReduce, Dynamo, Kafka, and Spanner). No specific software implementation or programming language is required, as the repository focuses entirely on educational conceptual material and architectural guidance.

name: chatbox
description: Powerful AI Client
summary:
Chatbox is a cross-platform desktop, mobile, and web client designed as an AI copilot for large language models. It provides a unified interface to interact with multiple LLM providers, including OpenAI (ChatGPT), Azure OpenAI, Claude, Google Gemini Pro, Ollama (supporting local models like Llama 2, Mistral, and Vicuna), and ChatGLM-6B, alongside Dall-E-3 image generation. 

Intended for end users and teams seeking a centralized AI assistant, the application emphasizes local-first data storage to maintain user privacy. Key capabilities include streaming replies, enhanced prompting, a prompt library, message quoting, team collaboration features, and full support for Markdown, LaTeX, and code syntax highlighting. The user interface features ergonomic design with a dark theme, keyboard shortcuts, and extensive multilingual localization. 

The project is built using Node.js, pnpm, React, Electron, and Vitest, and is licensed under the GPLv3 license.

name: Xray-core
description: Xray, Penetrates Everything. Also the best v2ray-core. Where the magic happens. An open platform for various uses.
summary:
Project X provides a set of network tools originating from the XTLS protocol, most notably including Xray-core and REALITY. The project's purpose is to deliver networking and proxy capabilities through components like VLESS, XTLS, REALITY, XUDP, and PLUX. 

Intended users include developers, system administrators, and network privacy enthusiasts seeking advanced proxy configurations. The ecosystem supports a vast array of client applications and management panels across multiple platforms, including Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, tvOS, OpenWrt, and Asuswrt-Merlin. Notable GUI clients, wrappers, and tools integrated or compatible with Project X include v2rayN, v2rayNG, Streisand, Shadowrocket, sing-box, mihomo, and various web panels such as Marzban and Remnawave.

Technologies used include Go for the core implementation, alongside Docker, systemd, OpenRC, and Wintun for Windows TUN functionality. Project X is licensed under the Mozilla Public License Version 2.0.

name: swiper
description: Most modern mobile touch slider with hardware accelerated transitions
summary:
Swiper is a modern, free mobile touch slider built with hardware-accelerated transitions and native behavior. It is designed for use in mobile websites, mobile web apps, and hybrid or native mobile applications. 

Main capabilities include 1:1 touch movement, tree-shakeability, a Mutation Observer for automatic DOM and style updates, 100% RTL support, multi-row slides layouts, virtual slides, images lazy loading, and transition effects such as Fade, Flip, 3D Cube, and 3D Coverflow. It also features loop mode, autoplay, keyboard and mousewheel control, nested sliders, history and hash navigation, accessibility (A11y) support, and a comprehensive API for custom pagination, navigation, and parallax effects. 

Swiper is library-agnostic and does not require JavaScript libraries like jQuery, though it integrates seamlessly with frameworks such as React, Vue, and jQuery. It utilizes a modern Flexbox layout for sizing and slide grids. The project is intended for web and mobile developers targeting modern platforms.

name: duckdb
description: DuckDB is an analytical in-process SQL database management system
summary:
DuckDB is a high-performance analytical database system designed to be fast, reliable, portable, and easy to use. It provides a rich SQL dialect supporting arbitrary and nested correlated subqueries, window functions, collations, and complex types including arrays, structs, and maps, alongside capabilities for direct data import from CSV and Parquet files. 

The project is intended for data analysts and developers seeking analytical database capabilities. It is available as a standalone CLI application and offers clients for Python, R, Java, and Wasm, featuring deep integrations with packages such as pandas and dplyr. 

DuckDB is built using C++17 and CMake, requiring a C++17 compliant compiler and Python 3 for development and compilation.

name: black
description: The uncompromising Python code formatter
summary:
Black is an uncompromising, opinionated Python code formatter designed to enforce a consistent PEP 8 compliant code style with speed and determinism. It reformats entire files in place while offering deliberately limited style configuration options, relying on sensible defaults and a `pyproject.toml` configuration file when needed. As a safety measure, Black checks that reformatted code produces a valid, equivalent Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). 

Main capabilities include formatting standard Python source files, directories, and Jupyter Notebooks (via an optional dependency), producing minimal diffs to streamline code reviews, and providing a parallel test suite and continuous integration runner. The project targets Python developers seeking freedom from manual formatting minutiae and `pycodestyle` nagging. Notable technologies utilized include Python (version 3.10+), PyInstaller for standalone executables, and AST parsing. The repository is distributed under the MIT license.

name: tabler
description: Tabler is free and open-source HTML Dashboard UI Kit built on Bootstrap
summary:
Tabler is a free, open-source HTML dashboard UI kit and component library built on Bootstrap 5. It provides ready-made layouts, demo pages, and UI components designed for admin panels, dashboards, and web applications. Intended for web developers building administrative interfaces, Tabler works with any backend or frontend framework, including React, Vue, Angular, Next.js, Laravel, Django, and Rails. 

Main capabilities include support for light and dark color modes, RTL stylesheets, over 120 demo pages, more than 20 bundled third-party plugins (such as ApexCharts, Tom Select, and FullCalendar), and native integration with Tabler Icons and Tabler Flags. The project supports customization through Sass sources and CSS custom properties, and includes TypeScript declarations for typed JavaScript usage.

name: Sunshine
description: Self-hosted game stream host for Moonlight.
summary:
Sunshine is a self-hosted, low-latency game stream host designed for Moonlight clients. It functions as a cloud gaming server, providing hardware-accelerated video encoding and comprehensive gamepad emulation across multiple operating systems, including Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and macOS. 

Key capabilities include cross-platform screen capture (utilizing methods such as DXGI Desktop Duplication, KMS/DRM, ScreenCaptureKit, Wayland, and X11) and hardware encoding support for AMD (AMF, VAAPI), Intel (QuickSync, VAAPI, Video Toolbox), Nvidia (NVENC, VAAPI), and Apple (Video Toolbox) GPUs, alongside software encoding. Sunshine also features a built-in web UI for server configuration and client pairing. Intended users include gamers seeking to self-host high-performance game streaming to various client devices. Notable technologies integrated into the project include AMF, NVENC, QuickSync, VAAPI, Video Toolbox, Vulkan Video, and ViGEmBus or Virtual HID Broker for gamepad support.

name: cheat.sh
description: the only cheat sheet you need
summary:
Cheat.sh is a unified access platform for community-driven cheat sheet repositories and programming knowledge sources like StackOverflow. The project purpose is to provide concise, ultrafast, and universal answers for programming languages, database management systems, and UNIX/Linux commands without requiring complex setup. 

Main capabilities include HTTP/HTTPS and command-line interfaces (`curl` or the `cht.sh` client), interactive shell mode with query history and clipboard integration, shell tab-completion, stealth mode for automatic queries from mouse selections, code editor integration, and on-the-fly generation of language queries when missing. It covers over 50 programming languages, multiple DBMSes, and more than 1,000 UNIX/Linux commands.

Intended users are software developers, system administrators, and technical interviewees seeking immediate code snippets and syntax explanations directly within their workflow. Notable technologies and integrations mentioned include Docker, Redis, Vim, Emacs, Visual Studio Code, Sublime Text, IntelliJ IDEA, Qt Creator, Bash, Zsh, and Scoop for Windows.

name: hexo
description: A fast, simple & powerful blog framework, powered by Node.js.
summary: Hexo is a fast, simple, and powerful blog framework powered by Node.js. Designed for users looking to create blogs and static sites, Hexo features blazing-fast static file generation, support for GitHub Flavored Markdown and most Octopress plugins, and one-command deployment to platforms like GitHub Pages and Heroku. It offers a powerful API for limitless extensibility alongside hundreds of available themes and plugins.

name: claude-howto
description: A visual, example-driven guide to Claude Code — from basic concepts to advanced agents, with copy-paste templates that bring immediate value.
summary:
Claude How To is a structured, visual, example-driven tutorial guide designed to help developers master Claude Code. It provides a progressive learning path to take users from basic interactions to orchestrating advanced workflows. 

The project's main capabilities cover ten core tutorial modules and copy-paste configuration templates for:
- Slash Commands and CLI Basics
- Persistent Memory (`CLAUDE.md`)
- Reusable Skills and Specialized Subagents
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers
- Event-driven automation via Hooks
- Plugins and Checkpoints/Rewind capabilities
- Advanced features like Planning Mode, Extended Thinking, and Background Tasks

Intended users include software developers, DevOps engineers, and technical teams looking to leverage Claude Code for automated code reviews, documentation generation, security audits, and complex refactoring. Notable technologies and protocols utilized throughout the guide include Python (`pytest`, `uv`, `ruff`, `bandit`, `mypy`), Mermaid diagrams, EPUB generation, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The repository is distributed under the MIT License and remains actively maintained and synchronized with Claude Code 2.1+.

name: pure-bash-bible
description: 📖 A collection of pure bash alternatives to external processes.
summary:
The "pure bash bible" repository is a collection of pure `bash` alternatives to external processes, commands, and utilities. Its stated purpose is to document commonly-known and lesser-known methods for performing tasks using only built-in `bash` features, helping scripts run faster and remove unneeded dependencies. 

Main capabilities include pure implementations for string manipulation, array operations, loops, file handling, file paths, variables, escape sequences, parameter and brace expansions, conditional expressions, arithmetic operations, traps, performance tuning, internal variables, terminal information, type conversions, and code golf snippets. Notable techniques leverage built-in parameter expansion, associative arrays, mapfile, `printf` format strings, regex matching, and ANSI escape sequences. 

The intended users are shell script developers and system administrators seeking to optimize scripts, reduce external dependencies, and deepen their understanding of `bash`. The project notably references and grew out of the development of tools like `neofetch` and `pxltrm`.

name: uni-app
description: A cross-platform framework using Vue.js
summary:
uni-app is a cross-platform frontend development framework built with Vue.js that allows developers to write a single codebase and publish applications to iOS, Android, HarmonyOS, Web, and various mini-programs (including WeChat, Alipay, Baidu, Douyin, Lark, QQ, Kuaishou, DingTalk, Taobao, JD.com, and Xiaohongshu), quick apps, and HarmonyOS atomic services. 

The repository features the next-generation `uni-app x` branch, which uses native rendering on App platforms while supporting JS, TS, and the cross-platform `uts` language (compiled to Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS, ArkTS for HarmonyOS NEXT, and JS for Web and mini-programs) for native plugin extensions. It delivers high-performance rendering and long lists, outperforming native platforms in benchmark tests across Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS. The framework targets frontend developers aiming for multi-platform delivery, offering an AI-friendly ecosystem utilizing Vue, JS/TS, and CSS, alongside tools for AI model training and reinforcement learning.

name: dubbo
description: The java implementation of Apache Dubbo. An RPC and microservice framework.
summary:
Apache Dubbo is a powerful Web and RPC framework designed for building enterprise-grade microservices. It provides comprehensive solutions for communication, service discovery, traffic management, observability, security, and tooling. 

Main capabilities include dynamic service registration and discovery, traffic routing, metrics, tracing, native image support, and integration with Kubernetes and service meshes. Dubbo supports multiple RPC protocols such as Triple (gRPC-compatible), Dubbo2 (TCP), and REST, and offers seamless integration with Spring Boot. It provides multi-language implementations including Java, Go, Python, PHP, Erlang, Rust, and Node.js/Web. 

The framework is intended for developers and enterprises building scalable, distributed microservice architectures across various programming languages. Notable technologies and registries utilized include Zookeeper, Nacos, Spring Boot, and gRPC.

name: yarn
description: The 1.x line is frozen - features and bugfixes now happen on https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry
summary:
Yarn 1.x is a fast, reliable, and secure dependency management tool designed for software developers and projects requiring deterministic package installations. Its primary purpose is to manage project dependencies with high performance, utilizing concurrent operations, package caching, and checksum verification to ensure code integrity. 

Key capabilities include an Offline Mode that allows repeating installations without an internet connection, deterministic locking for consistent setups across different machines, network resilience with automatic request retries and queue management, and a Flat Mode that resolves mismatched dependency versions into a single version. 

This repository holds the legacy source code for Yarn 1.x (version 1.22), which is currently maintained primarily for historical purposes and occasional hotfixes, with active development directed to the successor repository, yarnpkg/berry.

name: ColossalAI
description: Making large AI models cheaper, faster and more accessible
summary:
Colossal-AI is a unified deep learning system designed for large-scale parallel training and inference, aiming to make large AI models cheaper, faster, and more accessible. It targets AI researchers, developers, and data scientists working with large-scale neural networks. 

The project provides comprehensive parallelization strategies, including Data Parallelism, Pipeline Parallelism, 1D/2D/2.5D/3D Tensor Parallelism, Sequence Parallelism, ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer), and Auto-Parallelism. It also features heterogeneous memory management via PatrickStar and optimized inference tools like Colossal-Inference and SwiftInfer. Colossal-AI supports various real-world applications and models, including large language models (such as LLaMA, GPT, MoE, and PaLM), video generation models (Open-Sora), ChatGPT-style RLHF pipelines (ColossalChat), AIGC models (Stable Diffusion), and biomedicine tools (FastFold for AlphaFold).

Notable technologies used include Python, PyTorch, CUDA, and Docker.

name: Awesome-Design-Tools
description: The best design tools and plugins for everything 👉
summary:
Awesome Design Tools is a curated, comprehensive directory of digital design resources, software, and utilities for UI/UX designers, developers, and product teams. The repository organizes thousands of entries into structured categories including accessibility, animation, augmented reality, collaboration, color picking, design systems, design-to-code, version control, experience monitoring, typography, gradients, icons, illustrations, information architecture, logo design, mockups, no-code tools, pixel art, prototyping, screenshot software, sketching, social media marketing, sound design, stock photos and videos, UI design, user flows, user research, visual debugging, wireframing, and 3D modeling software. 

The project aims to streamline the creative and technical workflows of digital creators by connecting them with free and paid tools, plugins, UI kits, and inspiration sources. Notable featured technologies and platforms include Sketch, Figma, Adobe XD, InVision, Abstract, and various open-source web and mobile development frameworks. Maintained as a community-driven initiative originally created by the Flawless App team (which later joined Abstract), the repository welcomes contributions via pull requests.

name: AstrBot
description: AI Agent Assistant & development framework that integrates lots of IM platforms, LLMs, plugins and AI feature, and can be your openclaw alternative. ✨
summary:
AstrBot is an open-source, all-in-one Agent chatbot platform designed for individuals, developers, and teams to build production-ready conversational AI applications. It integrates with mainstream instant messaging applications including QQ, Telegram, Slack, Feishu, DingTalk, WeChat Work, and Discord.

The platform provides features such as AI LLM conversations, multimodal support, agent workflows, Model Context Protocol (MCP), skills, knowledge bases, persona settings, and auto-context compression. It also includes an Agent Sandbox for isolated execution of code and shell calls, a WebUI, a Web ChatUI with built-in web search, internationalization (i18n), and an extensible plugin system with over 1,000 plugins.

AstrBot supports integrations with multiple LLM services and AI platforms (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama, Dify, Coze, and Alibaba Cloud Bailian) as well as various text-to-speech and speech-to-text providers. It can be deployed via Docker, Python (`uv`), cloud services like RainYun, desktop apps, or container management panels such as 1Panel and CasaOS.

name: sniffnet
description: Comfortably monitor your network traffic 🕵️‍♂️
summary:
Sniffnet is a cross-platform, open-source application designed to comfortably monitor and inspect network traffic in real time. Intended for users seeking visibility into their internet activity, it provides intuitive tools to analyze bandwidth usage, identify local network connections, discover remote host geographical locations, and resolve domain names and ASNs. 

Main capabilities include selecting network adapters, applying traffic filters, importing and exporting PCAP capture reports, viewing real-time charts and overall statistics, identifying over 6,000 upper-layer services, protocols, trojans, and worms, tracking bandwidth by application, saving favorites, setting custom network event notifications, and importing IP blacklists. 

Sniffnet is built using Rust and leverages the iced cross-platform GUI library for its graphical interface, with IP geolocation and ASN data provided by MaxMind. It supports custom themes and includes a thumbnail mode for minimized monitoring. Pre-compiled binaries and packages are available for Windows, macOS, and Linux distributions.

name: manim
description: A community-maintained Python framework for creating mathematical animations.
summary:
Manim (specifically the community edition, ManimCE) is a programmatic animation engine designed for creating precise, explanatory mathematics videos. Originally forked from Grant Sanderson's 3b1b/manim project, it is maintained collectively to provide continuous development, improved features, and enhanced documentation. 

Intended for educators, mathematicians, developers, and content creators, Manim allows users to write Python scripts defining geometric objects, transformations, and scenes, which are then rendered into video files via command-line tools. Key capabilities include programmatic shape manipulation, smooth animations (such as transformations and fades), command-line rendering controls (including quality flags and preview options), and built-in IPython magic support for seamless integration within JupyterLab and Jupyter notebooks. Docker images and online Jupyter environments are also provided to facilitate usage.

Notable technologies utilized include Python, Docker, IPython/Jupyter, and uv for dependency management. The software is released under the MIT License.

name: zju-icicles
description: 浙江大学课程攻略共享计划
summary:
The Zhejiang University Course Guide Sharing Project (浙江大学课程攻略共享计划) is a collaborative open-source repository designed to centralize and share academic resources and course experiences for Zhejiang University students, primarily covering computer science professional courses. 

The project purpose is to eliminate repetitive independent efforts and transform fragmented, word-of-mouth information into publicly accessible, easily retrievable, and continuously improving shared materials. Its main capabilities include providing course selection guides, electronic textbooks, homework answers, past examination papers, review materials, and open-book exam A4 cheat sheets. Intended users are current and future university students seeking to navigate academic coursework and examinations more efficiently. 

The platform utilizes GitHub as its infrastructure, leveraging directory structures, README files, Issues, and Pull Requests to organize files and facilitate community-driven contributions. Contributed content is shared under the CC-BY-NC-SA (Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike) license, while explicitly excluding pirated materials, paid software installers, and unauthorized course content.

name: nw.js
description: Call all Node.js modules directly from DOM/WebWorker and enable a new way of writing applications with all Web technologies.
summary: NW.js (formerly node-webkit) is an app runtime built on Chromium and Node.js that allows developers to write native desktop applications using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and WebGL. Its main capabilities include calling Node.js modules and third-party npm modules directly from the DOM, running Node and WebKit in the same thread for high performance, and supporting easy app packaging and distribution. NW.js is intended for developers building cross-platform native applications for Linux, Mac OS X, and Windows. Notable technologies utilized include Chromium, Node.js, WebKit, HTML5, and WebGL.

name: styled-components
description: Fast, expressive styling for React. Server components, client components, streaming SSR, React Native—one API.
summary:
styled-components is a CSS-in-JS styling library for React and React Native designed to provide fast, expressive component styling. Its primary purpose is to allow developers to write actual CSS code to style components with automatic scoping, removing the need for class name management or separate style sheets. 

Main capabilities include support for server components, client components, streaming server-side rendering (SSR), dynamic props, style extension, polymorphic `as` props, pseudo-classes, nested selectors, custom plugins for vendor prefixing, keyframe animations, theming via React context, and global styles. It also features a `createTheme` utility for RSC-compatible custom properties, shared style blocks, and an attributes API.

Intended users are frontend developers and React/React Native engineers seeking a robust styling solution with built-in TypeScript support and type inference. The notable technologies used throughout the project include JavaScript, TypeScript, React, React Server Components, and React Native.

name: vim
description: The official Vim repository
summary:
Vim (Vi IMproved) is an advanced, highly configurable text editor designed for editing programs and plain text files efficiently. Serving as an improved version of the classic UNIX Vi editor, it maintains Vi compatibility while introducing numerous features, including multi-level undo, syntax highlighting, command-line history, on-line help, spell checking, filename completion, block operations, a built-in script language (including Vim9 script), and a Graphical User Interface (GUI). When compiled with a minimal feature set (`vim.tiny`), it aims to provide a POSIX-compatible vi implementation often used as a default on Linux distributions.

Intended for programmers, system administrators, and touch-typists who work rapidly using keyboard commands, Vim supports mouse interaction and user-mapped function keys. It runs natively on MS-Windows, macOS, Haiku, VMS, and almost all flavors of UNIX, with historical support for numerous other systems. Distributed as charityware under a GPL-compatible license, Vim encourages donations to support orphans in Uganda.

name: Codewhale
description: Open-source coding agent for your terminal, built in Rust and on a journey of continuous community improvement. Issues and PRs welcome.
summary:
Codewhale is an open-source AI coding agent that reads projects, edits files, runs commands, and validates its work. Designed for developers, it operates locally or via hosted models, supporting workflows from single terminal tasks to coordinated multi-agent jobs. 

Main capabilities include an interactive terminal user interface (TUI), a local web client, scriptable headless execution via `codewhale exec`, and optional Computer Use features for interacting with other applications. Users can switch between planning and working modes, manage permissions (Ask, Auto-Review, Full Access), use `/undo` and `/restore` for workspace recovery, and set durable goals. Codewhale supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, skills, hooks, and custom agent roles.

The project integrates with various model providers, including local runtimes such as Ollama, vLLM, and SGLang. Installation is supported via shell scripts, npm, Cargo, Docker, Nix, and platform-specific installers.

name: vuetify
description: 🐉 Vue Component Framework
summary:
Vuetify is a UI component library built for Vue applications. It provides a massive collection of handcrafted, responsive UI components designed to help users build web applications without requiring dedicated design skills. 

Main capabilities include extensive customization through SASS/SCSS variables, presets, and blueprints; a powerful theme system for consistent color palettes; Vite support with automatic tree-shaking for smaller bundle sizes; internationalization supporting over 42 languages; and responsive default layouts. It targets frontend developers building modern web applications. Notable technologies and tools associated with the project include Vue, Vite, SASS/SCSS, Nuxt, Laravel, and modern JavaScript package managers like npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun.

name: ToolJet
description: Open-source foundation of ToolJet AI - the enterprise app generation platform for internal tools, dashboards, business applications, workflows and AI agents. Build visually, from a prompt, or from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor over MCP 🚀
summary:
ToolJet is an open-source platform designed for building internal tools, admin panels, dashboards, and operational applications that connect to existing databases, APIs, and SaaS systems. 

Main capabilities include a visual app builder with 80+ responsive components, multiplayer editing, a built-in no-code ToolJet Database, support for over 90 data sources, and the ability to write JavaScript and Python code anywhere within apps. It also features a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling coding agents (such as Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, and Cursor) to generate and modify pages, queries, and components directly from prompts against governed platform schemas. Enterprise features include AI-driven app generation, query building, debugging, agent building, automated workflows, multi-environment management, and GitSync CI/CD.

Intended users include developers, operations teams, and organizations seeking low-code or AI-assisted internal tooling solutions. The platform can be deployed via ToolJet Cloud or self-hosted using Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, Azure, and OpenShift, utilizing technologies such as PostgreSQL, JavaScript, Python, and Docker.

name: faiss
description: A library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors.
summary:
Faiss is a library developed by Meta's Fundamental AI Research group for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors. It provides algorithms that handle vector sets of any size, including those exceeding RAM capacity, using L2 (Euclidean) distances, dot products, and cosine similarity. 

Main capabilities include exact and approximate nearest neighbor search, clustering (such as Lloyd's k-means), evaluation tools, and parameter tuning. It features compressed vector representations for billion-scale similarity search on a single server, as well as graph-based and tree-based indexing structures like HNSW and NSG. 

The library is primarily written in C++ with complete wrappers for Python/numpy, and supports single and multi-GPU usage via CUDA, AMD ROCm, and NVIDIA cuVS backends. Intended users include developers and researchers working on high-dimensional vector search, machine learning, and large-scale data retrieval.

name: appsmith
description: Platform to build admin panels, internal tools, and dashboards. Integrates with 25+ databases and any API.
summary:
Appsmith is an open-source low-code platform designed to streamline the development, deployment, and maintenance of custom applications such as dashboards, admin panels, customer 360 views, IT automation, and service management tools. It is intended for organizations and business teams including sales, support, customer success, and human resources to help knowledge workers build tools and configure automations specific to their business. 

The platform includes Appsmith Agents, an agentic AI capability that integrates AI models with private and proprietary data at scale without requiring model fine-tuning or complex retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) implementations. Appsmith can be deployed via Appsmith Cloud, Docker, Kubernetes, or AWS AMI, and is made available under the Apache License 2.0.

name: vue2-elm
description: Large single page application with 45 pages built on vue2 + vuex. 基于 vue2 + vuex 构建一个具有 45 个页面的大型单页面应用
summary:
This project is a high-fidelity, full-featured frontend single-page application modeled after the Ele.me food delivery platform, comprising 45 distinct pages designed to provide a comprehensive, production-like user experience with complex transaction logic and state management. 

**Main Capabilities**
- Location services, including city selection, address searching, and managing delivery addresses.
