- Restaurant discovery and listing, featuring sorting and filtering by distance, sales, ratings, signature dishes, and delivery methods.
- Comprehensive food ordering and shopping cart functionality, handling item selection, order notes, invoices, and order histories.
- User account management, covering registration, login, password recovery, SMS/voice verification, profile details, avatar uploading, balance, points, red packets, and VIP cards.
- Customer service and help center integration.

**Intended Users**
- Developers seeking practical, advanced single-page application reference implementations beyond basic demos and display projects.

**Notable Technologies**
- Vue 2
- Vuex
- Vue Router
- Webpack
- ES6/7
- Fetch API
- Sass
- Flexbox
- SVG

name: ChatGLM-6B
description: ChatGLM-6B: An Open Bilingual Dialogue Language Model | 开源双语对话语言模型
summary:
ChatGLM-6B is an open-source, bilingual (Chinese-English) conversational language model featuring 6.2 billion parameters and based on the General Language Model (GLM) architecture. It is designed to generate human-preferential responses for dialogue, question answering, and downstream text generation tasks. Intended for researchers, developers, and commercial users (via registration), the repository supports local deployment on consumer-grade hardware through model quantization (such as INT4 and INT8) and efficient parameter fine-tuning via P-Tuning v2. 

Key capabilities include bilingual dialogue generation, multi-card and CPU/GPU deployment options, a Gradio-based web UI, a command-line demo, and a FastAPI-based API server. Notable technologies integrated or supported include PyTorch, Transformers, Gradio, FastApi, FlashAttention, Multi-Query Attention, and P-Tuning v2.

name: llvm-project
description: The LLVM Project is a collection of modular and reusable compiler and toolchain technologies.
summary:
The LLVM Compiler Infrastructure is a toolkit for constructing highly optimized compilers, optimizers, and run-time environments. Its core component provides tools, libraries, and header files to process intermediate representations and convert them into object files, featuring an assembler, disassembler, bitcode analyzer, and bitcode optimizer. 

The project includes multiple sub-components:
- **Clang**: A frontend for C, C++, Objective-C, and Objective-C++ languages that compiles code into LLVM bitcode and object files.
- **libc++**: A C++ standard library.
- **LLD**: A linker.

Designed for developers, compiler engineers, and systems programmers, LLVM facilitates the creation and optimization of software across diverse hardware targets.

name: remote-jobs
description: Source for remoteintech.company — a community-maintained directory of remote-friendly tech companies
summary:
Remote In Tech provides the source code for [remoteintech.company](https://remoteintech.company), a community-maintained directory of remote-friendly tech companies. The project is designed for developers, job seekers, and contributors looking to browse or add remote technology companies to the platform. 

Main capabilities include maintaining a structured repository of company profiles via Markdown files with frontmatter, automated PR validation checks, and a production build system. Contributions are integrated by adding company markdown files in `src/companies/` and running a build process. 

Notable technologies used in the project include Node.js (version 22+) and Eleventy Excellent, a static site generator starter by Lene Saile.

name: awesome-cursorrules
description: 📄  Configuration files that enhance Cursor AI editor experience with custom rules and behaviors
summary:
Awesome Cursor Rules is a curated collection of Markdown-based `.mdc` project rules designed to enhance the behavior of the Cursor AI editor. The project provides reusable coding standards, architectural guidance, and domain constraints across various frontend frameworks, backend stacks, mobile development ecosystems, languages, testing methodologies, and deployment targets. 

Intended for developers and teams using Cursor AI, the repository helps maintain style consistency, reduce repetitive editing, and align AI-assisted code generation with project-specific workflows. Supported technologies span React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Node.js, Python, FastAPI, Go, Rust, Solidity, Tailwind CSS, Supabase, Docker, Kubernetes, and many others.

name: outline
description: The fastest knowledge base for growing teams. Beautiful, realtime collaborative, feature packed, and markdown compatible.
summary:
Outline is a fast, collaborative knowledge base for teams designed for running self-hosted instances or contributing to development. Its primary purpose is to provide a team documentation platform. 

The application is built using React, Node.js, TypeScript, and styled-components. It relies on Sequelize for database migrations and Vitest for testing API endpoints, authentication, and other critical code paths. Container images are available via Docker for deployment in production configurations. Intended users include development teams and organizations seeking to host their own documentation wiki, as well as developers looking to contribute to the project codebase.

name: it-tools
description: Collection of handy online tools for developers, with great UX.
summary:
IT-Tools is a collection of handy online utilities and tools tailored for developers and IT professionals. The project provides a web-based suite designed with a focus on user experience to assist with everyday technical tasks. 

Intended for developers, IT workers, and homelab enthusiasts, IT-Tools can be accessed via the web or self-hosted using Docker images from Docker Hub or GitHub Packages, as well as deployment platforms like Cloudron, Tipi, and Unraid. 

The repository is built using technologies such as Vue.js, TypeScript, Vite, pnpm, ESLint, and Vitest. It includes developer workflows for generating new tools, running unit tests, type-checking with vue-tsc, and compiling for production. The project is open-source under the GNU GPLv3 license and is continuously deployed on Vercel.

name: DeepTutor
description: DeepTutor: Lifelong Personalized Tutoring. https://deeptutor.info/.
summary:
DeepTutor is an agent-native, lifelong personalized learning workspace that unifies tutoring, problem-solving, quiz generation, academic research, data visualization, and mastery practice. Designed for students, educators, and developers, the platform combines a multi-engine retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system with continuous, inspectable three-layer memory, persistent AI companions, and markdown-based drafting capabilities.

Key capabilities include a single runtime loop supporting multiple modes such as Chat, Ask Questions, Quiz, Research, Solve, Course Study, Mastery Path, and Immersive Reading/Video Learning. It features a task board for tracking study activities, a "living book" compiler that transforms sources into interactive typed blocks, and a pluggable knowledge center supporting LlamaIndex, PageIndex, GraphRAG, LightRAG, WeKnora, Tencent IMA, and Obsidian vaults. It also provides a CLI interface and integration options for external coding harnesses, MCP services, and IM-connected AI partners.

Technologies utilized include Python (3.11–3.14), Next.js 16, FastAPI, LlamaIndex, FAISS, PyMuPDF4LLM, and Docker. Installation is supported via PyPI, source checkouts, and containerized deployments.

name: trpc
description: 🧙‍♀️  Move Fast and Break Nothing. End-to-end typesafe APIs made easy.
summary:
tRPC is a framework designed to build and consume fully typesafe APIs without requiring schemas or code generation. Its primary purpose is to provide end-to-end type safety, autocompletion, and error inference on the client side for inputs and outputs. 

Main capabilities include zero runtime bloat or build pipelines, a lightweight zero-dependency client footprint, request batching, and subscription support. It provides built-in adapters for React.js, Next.js, Express.js, and Fastify, while supporting various community extensions. 

The project targets web developers building or maintaining full-stack applications who want to share type declarations between servers and clients without sharing server implementation code. Notable technologies referenced include TypeScript, React.js, Next.js, Express.js, Fastify, and Prisma.

name: chakra-ui
description: Chakra UI is a component system for building SaaS products with speed ⚡️
summary: Chakra UI is a component system and accessible React component library designed for building high-quality web applications and design systems with speed. It provides simple, composable APIs and supports Next.js RSC (React Server Components). Notable technologies used include React, Emotion (`@emotion/react`), and packages distributed via npm (`@chakra-ui/react`). The project is intended for developers and teams seeking to build accessible, consistent user interfaces efficiently.

name: 50projects50days
description: 50+ mini web projects using HTML, CSS & JS
summary:
This repository contains the source code for the "50 Projects in 50 Days" course by Traversy Media. It serves as the central collection of small web development projects built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. 

The main purpose of the project is to provide practical, hands-on examples and exercises for developers learning frontend web development. The repository features a wide variety of interactive components and mini-applications—such as expanding cards, progress steps, rotating navigation, blurry loading, a sound board, a movie app, a Pokedex, a quiz app, a todo list, and an insect catch game—designed to strengthen core HTML, CSS, and JavaScript capabilities.

name: tidb
description: TiDB is built for agentic workloads that grow unpredictably, with ACID guarantees and native support for transactions, analytics, and vector search. No data silos. No noisy neighbors. No infrastructure ceiling.
summary:
TiDB is an open-source, cloud-native, distributed SQL database designed for high availability, horizontal and vertical scalability, strong consistency, and high performance. Its primary purpose is to provide enterprise-grade hybrid transactional and analytical processing (HTAP) with MySQL 8.0 compatibility. 

Main capabilities include distributed transactions utilizing a two-phase commit protocol for ACID compliance, automated failover and high availability powered by the Raft consensus protocol, and an HTAP architecture featuring separate storage engines: TiKV for row-based storage and TiFlash for columnar storage. It supports cloud-native deployments across public clouds, on-premises environments, and Kubernetes via TiDB Operator, alongside managed deployments through TiDB Cloud. 

Intended users include developers, database administrators, and organizations seeking scalable, highly available relational databases compatible with existing MySQL protocols, frameworks, and tools without requiring extensive code modifications. 

Notable technologies and components utilized in TiDB include Go, TiKV, TiFlash, Raft, Kubernetes, TiDB Operator, and MySQL.

name: nushell
description: A new type of shell
summary:
Nushell is a cross-platform, modern shell designed around structured data and functional programming principles, drawing inspiration from PowerShell and Unix pipelines. Rather than treating inputs and files as raw text streams, Nushell handles data as structured tables, records, and lists that can be queried, filtered, and transformed through composable pipelines. It natively parses multiple file and URL formats—such as TOML—allowing users to seamlessly inspect, load, and manipulate configuration files or process lists. 

Intended for developers and system administrators seeking a modern command-line experience on Windows, macOS, and Linux, Nushell also maintains compatibility with native platform executables and supports extensible third-party plugins communicating via a JSON-RPC protocol.

name: qBittorrent
description: qBittorrent BitTorrent client
summary: qBittorrent is a cross-platform BitTorrent client programmed in C++ and Qt, utilizing the libtorrent (libtorrent-rasterbar) library by Arvid Norberg. It is designed to be a fast, stable alternative to other BitTorrent clients, offering Unicode support and a wide range of features. Notable capabilities include resolving peer countries using the free IP to Country Lite database by DB-IP. The intended users are individuals seeking a reliable, feature-rich BitTorrent client.

name: openhuman
description: OpenHuman is the fastest, cheapest, most efficient open-source agent harness. Written in Rust
summary:
OpenHuman is an open-source, lightweight, and modular agent harness featuring a Rust core. It provides a desktop application (built with Tauri v2 and Wry), a browser UI, a terminal client (using `ratatui`), and a Rust embedding library (`openhuman-embed`). 

The project is designed to minimize vendor sprawl while supporting diverse LLMs (including Ollama, LM Studio, MLX, Claude, and 26 BYOK providers), embedding engines, memory backends (such as Memory Trees on TinyCortex, local Obsidian vaults, and remote memory solutions), and search options. It features "Jev," a small decision model used for fast tool retrieval and confirmation logic, and integrates with the `tinyflows` engine for typed, agent-proposed automation workflows.

OpenHuman is intended for users seeking a privacy-focused, highly localizable, and performant AI agent ecosystem capable of running thousands of agents concurrently in a single process. Notable technologies used include Rust, Node.js, Tauri, Wry, and Ratatui.

name: croc
description: Easily and securely send things from one computer to another :crocodile: :package:
summary:
Croc is a cross-platform command-line tool designed for secure peer-to-peer file and folder transfers between any two computers, supporting relay fallbacks, browser clients, and Tor or SOCKS5 proxies. Its main capabilities include end-to-end encryption using Password-Authenticated Key Agreement (PAKE), multiple file and folder transfers, resumable interrupted transfers, encrypted temporary file storage, and shared terminal sessions via `croc ssh`. 

Intended for developers, system administrators, and general users seeking quick, secure command-line or browser-based data sharing without requiring local servers, port forwarding, or account setups, the tool runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and web browsers. Notable technologies and protocols utilized include Go, WebAssembly, React/Vite, Tailscale userspace WireGuard (Tailcat), SOCKS5, and PAKE.

name: php-src
description: The PHP Interpreter
summary:
The PHP Interpreter (php-src) is the source code repository for PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language especially suited to web development. It provides the core engine that powers everything from blogs to major websites. 

Intended for developers, contributors, and systems administrators, the project enables users to build the PHP interpreter from source, run extensive parallel test suites, and manage bundled or additional PHP extensions utilizing tools like PIE (PHP Installer for Extensions) and PECL. 

Building from source relies on technologies and tools such as autoconf, bison, re2c, libxml2, and libsqlite3. The codebase is distributed under the Modified BSD License (BSD-3-Clause).

name: wrk
description: Modern HTTP benchmarking tool
summary:
wrk is a modern HTTP benchmarking tool designed to generate significant load from a single multi-core CPU. It utilizes a multithreaded architecture combined with scalable event notification systems such as epoll and kqueue. The tool allows users to specify concurrency, thread count, test duration, custom HTTP headers, and timeouts via command-line options. Additionally, wrk supports optional LuaJIT scripts for customized HTTP request generation, response processing, and custom reporting. 

The project incorporates code from several established open-source components, including the 'ae' event loop from Redis, the `http-parser` from nginx, joyent, and node.js, and Mike Pall's LuaJIT.

name: phaser
description: Phaser is a fun, free and fast 2D game framework for making HTML5 games for desktop and mobile web browsers, supporting Canvas and WebGL rendering.
summary:
Phaser is a free, open-source HTML5 game framework designed for building games using JavaScript or TypeScript for desktop and mobile web browsers, YouTube Playables, Discord Activities, and native platforms via third-party tools. 

Main capabilities include WebGL and Canvas rendering, a node-based render architecture, unified filters, built-in physics (Arcade and Matter.js), animations, input handling, tilemaps, particles, and high-performance rendering components like `SpriteGPULayer` and `TilemapGPULayer` for handling massive quantities of sprites and tiles. It also features a framework-agnostic design supporting React, Vue, Angular, and Svelte, alongside comprehensive TypeScript definitions and specialized AI agent skill sets for AI-assisted development.

name: BitNet
description: Official inference framework for 1-bit LLMs
summary:
bitnet.cpp is the official inference framework designed for 1-bit and ternary large language models (such as BitNet b1.58) and embedding models. The project provides optimized kernels—including I2_S, TL1, and TL2 implementations—supporting fast, lossless, and energy-efficient inference on CPU and GPU architectures, including x86 and ARM platforms. 

The framework is intended for developers, researchers, and users deploying resource-efficient language and embedding models on local devices or edge infrastructure. Notable technologies and components utilized include CMake, Clang, Python, Conda, Hugging Face model integration, GGUF format conversion utilities, and a codebase built upon the llama.cpp framework with Lookup Table methodologies from T-MAC.

name: photoprism
description: AI-Powered Photos App 🌈💎✨
summary:
PhotoPrism is an AI-powered, privacy-first web application designed for browsing, organizing, searching, and sharing photos and videos. Intended for individuals seeking a self-hosted or cloud-based media management solution, it allows users to handle RAW images, live photos, and standard video formats through an intuitive Progressive Web App (PWA). 

Key capabilities include automated content- and location-based image labeling, facial recognition for family and friends, interactive world maps, and advanced search filters supporting labels, locations, resolution, color, chroma, and quality metrics. It also supports metadata extraction and merging from Exif and XMP sources, background mobile device synchronization via compatible apps like PhotoSync, and direct file access and editing through WebDAV clients such as Windows Explorer and Apple Finder. 

The software is packaged as a multi-architecture image utilizing Docker for deployment across Mac, Linux, and Windows environments, supporting 64-bit AMD, Intel, and ARM processors including Raspberry Pi and Apple Silicon.

name: fiber
description: ⚡️ Express inspired web framework written in Go
summary:
Fiber is an Express-inspired web framework built on top of Fasthttp, designed to ease web development in Go with high performance and a low memory footprint. Targeted at Go developers—particularly those transitioning from Node.js—Fiber provides a familiar, minimalist API that follows the Unix way. 

Main capabilities include robust routing, serving static files, template engine integration, WebSocket and Server-Sent Events (SSE) support, rate limiting, and an extensive collection of built-in middlewares like CORS, JWT/key auth, caching, logging, and compression. It also offers net/http compatibility through an adaptor middleware and supports Express-style request/response handlers and zero-memory-allocation principles. 

Notable technologies used include Go (version 1.26 or higher), Fasthttp, and various template engines such as Pug.

name: marker
description: Convert PDF to markdown + JSON quickly with high accuracy
summary:
Datalab's Marker is a document intelligence tool designed to convert documents—including PDF, image, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX, HTML, and EPUB files across all languages—into Markdown, JSON, chunks, and HTML. It accurately processes tables, forms, equations, inline math, links, references, and code blocks while extracting images and removing headers, footers, and artifacts. 

The software targets developers and organizations needing document conversion and RAG ingestion. It features a modular pipeline built around the Surya VLM and various CPU models. Notable technologies used include PyTorch, vLLM, llama.cpp, Surya, and optional integration with LLM services such as Google Gemini, Google Vertex, Ollama, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and OpenRouter. 

Marker operates in multiple modes (balanced, fast, and no-OCR) and runs on GPU, CPU, or MPS. It supports Python API usage, a CLI, a Streamlit interactive app, a FastAPI server, and custom processing via configurable converters, providers, builders, processors, and renderers.

name: agents
description: Multi-harness agentic plugin marketplace for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Google Antigravity, and Pi
summary:
The Agentic Plugin Marketplace is a collection of production-ready agentic workflow building blocks containing 94 plugins, 202 agents, 184 skills, 105 commands, and 16 orchestrators. Built for Claude Code, the repository serves as a single Markdown source-of-truth that is consumed natively by the OpenAI Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, the Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Pi. 

The project provides domain expert agents (spanning architecture, infrastructure, security, data, and machine learning), modular knowledge skills with progressive disclosure, slash commands, and multi-agent coordination workflows. It features an isolated and composable architecture where installing a plugin loads only its specific components into context. It also includes `plugin-eval`, an evaluation framework for static linting and experimental LLM-judged scoring of plugin and skill quality, along with external memory integration via Pensyve.

name: shellcheck
description: ShellCheck, a static analysis tool for shell scripts
summary:
ShellCheck is a static analysis tool designed for bash and sh shell scripts. Its primary purpose is to identify and clarify syntax errors, intermediate semantic problems, subtle caveats, corner cases, and pitfalls in shell scripts. It helps users catch issues related to quoting, conditionals, misused commands, beginner mistakes, style, data types, robustness, and portability across different shells.

ShellCheck is intended for developers, system administrators, and advanced users writing shell scripts. It can be used interactively on the web via ShellCheck.net, executed directly from the terminal, integrated into various code editors such as Vim, Emacs, Sublime, VSCode, and Pulsar Edit, or incorporated into build and test suites and continuous integration pipelines like Travis CI, GitHub Actions, CircleCI, and GitLab. 

The software is written in Haskell and can be compiled using Cabal or Stack. It is distributed across many package managers, container registries like Docker Hub, and binary releases. ShellCheck is licensed under the GNU GPLv3.

name: posthog
description: :hedgehog: PostHog is the leading platform for building self-driving products. Our developer tools – AI observability, analytics, session replay, flags, experiments, error tracking, logs, and more – capture all the context agents need to diagnose problems, uncover opportunities, and ship fixes. Steer it all from Slack, web, desktop, or the MCP.
summary:
PostHog is an open-source platform designed to help developers and product teams build self-driving products by capturing comprehensive user context and product data. Its main capabilities include product and web analytics, session replays, feature flags, experiments, error tracking, logs, surveys, a data warehouse, data pipelines, AI observability for LLM-powered apps, and automated workflows. 

The platform supports setup via JavaScript web snippets, an API, or numerous SDKs across frontend frameworks (like React, Vue, Next.js), mobile platforms (such as iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter), and backend languages (including Python, Node, PHP, Ruby, Go, and .NET). Users can steer PostHog through integrations with Slack, the web, desktop applications, or via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in editors like Cursor and Claude Code. It offers a managed cloud service alongside an advanced option for self-hosting hobby deployments using Docker on Linux.

name: novu
description: The open-source communication infrastructure for agents and products
summary:
Novu is an open-source communication infrastructure for products and AI agents, providing a unified API and conversation model to manage messaging across multiple channels such as Inbox/In-App, Email, SMS, Push, and Chat. 

Designed for developers, products, and agent builders, Novu features an embeddable React `<Inbox />` and preferences component, a notification workflow and digest engine, a no-code email editor, and bidirectional messaging capabilities for agents. It abstracts platform-specific quirks and webhooks for services like Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp, and numerous email, SMS, and push providers. 

The project utilizes an open-core model with core technologies licensed under the MIT license, while enterprise-specific modules are governed by a commercial license.

name: esbuild
description: An extremely fast bundler for the web
summary:
esbuild is an extremely fast JavaScript bundler designed to bring a new era of build tool performance to web development. Its primary purpose is to provide an easy-to-use modern bundler that operates 10 to 100 times faster than existing web build tools without requiring a cache. 

Major features include built-in support for JavaScript, CSS, TypeScript, and JSX, as well as the ability to bundle both ESM and CommonJS modules. It supports CSS modules, tree shaking, minification, source maps, a local development server, watch mode, and a plugin system. esbuild offers a straightforward API accessible via the command-line interface (CLI), JavaScript, and Go. 

The project targets developers seeking high-performance web building and bundling capabilities. Notable technologies and formats explicitly mentioned include JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, CSS, ESM, CommonJS, CSS modules, CLI, and Go.

name: bert
description: TensorFlow code and pre-trained models for BERT
summary:
BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) is a method of pre-training language representations for natural language processing (NLP) tasks. It provides an unsupervised, deeply bidirectional system utilizing the Transformer architecture to generate contextual word representations based on both left and right contexts. 

The project purpose is to enable transfer learning by pre-training general-purpose language understanding models on large text corpora, such as Wikipedia and BookCorpus, which can then be fine-tuned efficiently for downstream tasks like question answering, sentence classification, and named entity recognition. Intended users include NLP researchers and developers with access to CPU, GPU, or Cloud TPU environments. 

Main capabilities include pre-training models from scratch, fine-tuning pre-trained checkpoints on tasks like SQuAD and GLUE, extracting fixed contextual feature vectors, and tokenizing input text using WordPiece and whole word masking techniques. Notable technologies used include TensorFlow, Python, and the Transformer neural network architecture. The repository includes various pre-trained model variants such as BERT-Base, BERT-Large, multilingual models, and compact BERT models designed for resource-restricted environments.

name: insomnia
description: The open-source, cross-platform API client for GraphQL, REST, WebSockets, SSE and gRPC. With Cloud, Local and Git storage.
summary:
Insomnia is an open-source, cross-platform API client designed for developers, testers, and teams to debug, design, test, mock, and build CI/CD pipelines for APIs. It supports GraphQL, REST, WebSockets, Server-Sent Events (SSE), gRPC, and other HTTP-compatible protocols. Key capabilities include a native OpenAPI editor and visual preview, native test suites, a collection runner, mocking servers, and support for third-party plugins. 

Intended users include software engineers and API developers seeking versatile collaboration and workflow tools. Insomnia offers flexible data storage options, including Local Vault for fully local storage, Git Sync for third-party Git repositories, and Cloud Sync for cloud-based collaboration with optional end-to-end encryption (E2EE), alongside a Private Environments feature for localized environment configurations. The project also provides a native Insomnia CLI (`inso`) for linting and testing. 

Built as a Node.js monorepo for macOS, Windows, and Linux, the application utilizes technologies such as Electron, React, ESLint, and Git.

name: ink
description: 🌈 React for interactive command-line apps
summary:
Ink is a React renderer designed for building and testing command-line interface (CLI) applications using components. It provides a component-based UI development experience similar to React in the browser, leveraging the Yoga layout engine to build Flexbox layouts in the terminal using CSS-like properties. 

Main capabilities include full support for React features, built-in layout and styling components (`<Box>`, `<Text>`, `<Newline>`, `<Spacer>`, `<Static>`, `<Transform>`), comprehensive hooks for handling user input (`useInput`, `usePaste`), terminal streams, window size, focus management, animations, and cursor control. It also supports concurrent rendering, alternate screen buffers, the kitty keyboard protocol, React Devtools integration, and basic ARIA-based screen reader accessibility.

Ink is intended for JavaScript and TypeScript developers building interactive CLI tools, terminal dashboards, task runners, and command-line utilities. Notable technologies used include React, Node.js, Yoga, chalk, and cli-boxes.

name: gorm
description: The fantastic ORM library for Golang, aims to be developer friendly
summary:
GORM is a full-featured, developer-friendly Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) library for the Golang programming language. Its main capabilities include handling associations such as Has One, Has Many, Belongs To, Many To Many, polymorphism, and single-table inheritance, alongside support for hooks, eager loading with `Preload` and `Joins`, transactions with nested transaction and savepoint rollbacks, context, prepared statement mode, and dry-run mode. 

Additionally, GORM provides batch insert operations, SQL building, upserts, locking, optimizer and index hints, composite primary keys, auto migrations, and a logger. The framework features an extendable plugin API supporting database resolvers for read/write splitting and Prometheus integration. It is intended for Go developers seeking a robust tool to manage database interactions.

name: LightRAG
description: [EMNLP2025] LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary:
LightRAG is a lightweight, graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to bridge vector-based and graph-based retrieval approaches. It features a dual-layer architecture to manage knowledge graphs and vector embeddings efficiently, providing high scalability, low retrieval costs, and support for incremental updates and selective document deletion.

Main capabilities include multimodal document processing supporting text, images, tables, and equations through integrations like MinerU, Docling, and native parsers; multiple text chunking strategies including fixed-length, recursive character, vector semantic, and paragraph semantic approaches; and five distinct query modes (local, global, hybrid, naive, and mix). It also offers role-specific LLM configurations, reranking support, and multiple backend storage options such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB, OpenSearch, Neo4j, and Milvus.

Intended users include developers, researchers, and enterprises building scalable knowledge-retrieval and question-answering systems for complex, multi-format, or domain-specific data. Notable technologies utilized include Python, Docker, PostgreSQL, Neo4j, Milvus, and various large language and embedding models.

name: openscreen
description: Create stunning demos for free. Open-source, no subscriptions, no watermarks, and free for commercial use. An alternative to Screen Studio.
summary:
OpenScreen is a free, open-source alternative to Screen Studio designed to create polished product demos and walkthroughs for platforms like X, Reddit, and YouTube. The project is currently archived, with a community-driven spin-off available. 

Intended for creators, developers, and users seeking a no-cost screen recording solution, OpenScreen provides core capabilities including window or full-screen capture, microphone and system audio recording, webcam overlays with picture-in-picture, and manual or auto-zooming that follows cursor movement. It features custom cursor settings, motion blur, timeline editing (crop, trim, and per-segment speed control), annotations, and offline, on-device automatic caption generation. Users can customize backgrounds with wallpapers, gradients, or custom images, and export recordings to MP4 or GIF formats. 

OpenScreen supports macOS, Windows, and Linux across multiple distribution channels, utilizing platform-native capture pipelines like ScreenCaptureKit and Windows Graphics Capture where applicable. The software is distributed under the MIT License without any paid tiers or paywalls.

name: halo
description: Halo 是一款强大易用的开源建站工具，从个人博客、知识库，到企业官网、在线商城，Halo 都能助您轻松实现，一站式满足您的多样化建站需求。
summary:
Halo is a powerful and easy-to-use open-source website building tool designed to meet diverse website creation needs, ranging from personal blogs and knowledge bases to corporate websites and online stores. It provides an all-in-one solution with an application ecosystem featuring numerous themes and plugins. 

Intended users include personal developers, tech enthusiasts, open-source projects, enterprises, and online merchants. Notable technologies and deployment options mentioned include Docker and the Linux server operations and management panel 1Panel. Halo is available in multiple editions—including a free open-source community edition licensed under GPLv3, a professional edition with value-added features like AI website building and mobile app management, and a store edition featuring integrated online shopping capabilities tailored for Chinese payment ecosystems like WeChat Pay and Alipay.

name: polars
description: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames, written in Rust
summary:
Polars is an extremely fast analytical query engine for DataFrames designed to be fast, expressive, and easy to use. Its purpose is to provide high-performance data processing and analysis through multi-threaded, vectorized SIMD execution and built-in query optimization. 

Main capabilities include lazy and eager execution, larger-than-RAM data processing via a streaming engine for datasets that exceed memory limits, an expressive expression-based API, and native extensibility through I/O and expression plugins. It also supports optional NVIDIA GPU query acceleration and distributed horizontal scaling on clusters. Polars is interoperable with the Apache Arrow Columnar Format for zero-copy data sharing.

Intended users include data scientists, software engineers, and analysts working with large datasets who require high performance and low memory overhead. 

Notable technologies used include Rust (the language in which Polars is written), Python, Node.js, R, SQL, Apache Arrow, and maturin.

name: video.js
description: Video.js - open source HTML5 video player
summary:
Video.js is a full-featured, open-source web video player and framework designed for all web-based platforms, including desktops, mobile devices, tablets, and web-based Smart TVs. Out of the box, it supports common media formats alongside streaming formats such as HLS and DASH. The framework can be extended and customized through a robust ecosystem of plugins. 

Intended for web developers embedding and managing media playback, Video.js can be integrated via CDNs (such as Fastly, unpkg, or cdnjs), npm, or downloaded directly from GitHub releases. It supports both automatic setup via HTML5 `<video>` elements configured with a `data-setup` attribute and manual initialization through JavaScript using the `videojs` function, options objects, and event listeners. Compatibility testing is performed using BrowserStack.

name: OpenMAIC
description: Open Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom — Get an immersive, multi-agent learning experience in just one click
summary:
OpenMAIC (Open Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom) is an open-source AI platform that transforms topics or uploaded documents into immersive, interactive classroom experiences. Designed for students, educators, and lifelong learners, the platform utilizes multi-agent orchestration to generate structured course outlines, slides, quizzes, interactive simulations, and project-based learning activities. 

Main capabilities include real-time multi-agent discussions, AI teacher narration, shared whiteboard illustrations, text-to-speech, speech recognition, web grounding search, and `.pptx` or `.html` export. Version 1.0.0 introduces a chat-first Pro agent workbench with durable server sessions, session material uploads, and 24 built-in curriculum skills, supported by an OpenMAIC Skill package compatible with OpenClaw, Codex, DeepSeek, and WorkBuddy.

OpenMAIC is built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, LangGraph, Tailwind CSS, and PostgreSQL. It offers neutral provider support for LLM, TTS, ASR, image, video, and search services (including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, MiniMax, Grok, OpenRouter, Ollama, Lemonade, and FunASR), alongside self-hosted deployment options via Docker and Vercel.

name: ChatTTS
description: A generative speech model for daily dialogue.
summary:
ChatTTS is a generative text-to-speech model optimized specifically for dialogue scenarios, such as LLM assistants, supporting both English and Chinese languages. The project provides algorithm infrastructure, pretrained models, and examples for natural and expressive conversational speech synthesis. 

Main capabilities include:
- Conversational TTS supporting multiple speakers and interactive dialogues.
- Fine-grained prosody control, including the prediction and generation of laughter, pauses, and interjections (`[laugh]`, `[uv_break]`, `[lbreak]`).
- Streaming audio generation and zero-shot inferring code utilizing a DVAE encoder.

Intended users include researchers, developers, and academics seeking to implement dialogue-oriented speech generation. 

Notable technologies and libraries utilized include PyTorch, torchaudio, Hugging Face models, vLLM, and Vocos as a pretrained vocoder, with supporting WebUI and command-line interfaces.

name: Kronos
description: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
summary:
Kronos is an open-source decoder-only foundation model family designed for financial candlesticks (K-line sequences), pre-trained on data from over 45 global exchanges to handle the high-noise characteristics of financial markets. The project employs a two-stage framework consisting of a specialized tokenizer that quantizes continuous, multi-dimensional OHLCV data into hierarchical discrete tokens, and a large, autoregressive Transformer pre-trained on these tokens to serve as a unified quantitative forecasting model. 

Targeted at quantitative researchers and developers, Kronos provides capabilities for single-series and batch forecasting via the `KronosPredictor` class, as well as multi-GPU fine-tuning and backtesting pipelines compatible with Qlib and PyTorch. Notable technologies and components include Hugging Face integration, custom tokenizer and model architectures (`Kronos-mini`, `Kronos-small`, `Kronos-base`, and `Kronos-large`), Pandas for data handling, and `torchrun` for distributed training.

name: aseprite
description: Animated sprite editor & pixel art tool (Windows, macOS, Linux)
summary:
Aseprite is a program designed to create animated sprites, specifically tailored for pixel art and retro game development. Its main purpose is to provide a comprehensive set of tools for creating, editing, and managing pixel-based animations and graphics. 

Main capabilities include a timeline with separated layers and frames, color profiles supporting RGBA, Indexed, and Grayscale modes, real-time animation previews, onion skinning, and tiled modes for patterns and textures. It offers pixel-art specific tools such as Pixel Perfect freehand mode, shading ink, custom brushes, outlines, and wide pixels, alongside general drawing features like pressure sensitivity, symmetry, gradients, and stroke and fill selections. Users can transform multiple frames and layers simultaneously, organize work with layer groups and reference layers, and import or export sprite sheets, GIFs, and image sequences. Additionally, Aseprite includes Lua scripting capabilities, a command-line interface (CLI) for task automation, data recovery, and non-linear undo and redo operations.

Aseprite is intended for pixel artists, animators, and game developers. Notable technologies associated with the project include Lua for scripting and libraries such as laf, clip, undo, and observable.

name: ShareX
description: ShareX is a free and open-source application that enables users to capture or record any area of their screen with a single keystroke. It also supports uploading images, text, and various file types to a wide range of destinations.
summary:
ShareX is a free and open-source screen capture, screenshot, file sharing, and productivity tool designed for Windows. It provides users with fast capture capabilities, including full screen, active window, scrolling screenshot, and region-based capture, along with video and GIF screen recording. 

Main capabilities include a built-in image editor for annotations, redactions, and image effects, automated file sharing and upload integrations with destinations such as Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Cloudflare R2, and configurable hotkey-driven workflow automation. Additional integrated productivity utilities comprise an OCR text recognizer, color picker, QR code scanner, ruler, pin-to-screen tool, video converter, and hash checker. 

The project is intended for developers, designers, support teams, content creators, QA testers, and power users who require precise control over screen capture and workflow automation. It is implemented as a lightweight desktop application.

name: zoxide
description: A smarter cd command. Supports all major shells.
summary:
zoxide is a smarter `cd` command inspired by `z` and `autojump`. It tracks frequently used directories and allows users to jump to them in a few keystrokes using a ranking and matching algorithm. 

Main capabilities include fast directory navigation, interactive selection using `fzf`, command completion across major shells, an aging algorithm to manage database size, support for custom hooks, path exclusion via globs, and data import from utilities like `atuin`, `autojump`, `fasd`, `z`, `z.lua`, and `zsh-z`. 

It is intended for command-line users across all major shells—including Bash, Zsh, Fish, Nushell, PowerShell, Elvish, Xonsh, Tcsh, and POSIX shells—on Linux, macOS, Windows, BSD, and Android. It also provides integrations for text editors like Neovim, Vim, and Emacs, file managers like Yazi, Ranger, and Nnn, terminal multiplexers, and launchers. 

Technologies utilized include Rust, Nix, and `fzf`.

name: NewPipe
description: A libre lightweight streaming front-end for Android.
summary:
NewPipe is a libre, lightweight streaming front-end application for Android designed to provide a private, ad-free, and account-free media consumption experience. It supports multiple platforms, including YouTube, YouTube Music, PeerTube, Bandcamp, SoundCloud, and media.ccc.de. 

The project's main capabilities include watching videos up to 4K resolution, background audio playback, a floating picture-in-picture popup player, live stream viewing, subtitle toggling, search functionality across channels, playlists, and albums, local and remote playlist management, subscription tracking without logins, watch history, and downloading media streams. 

The app functions by querying official platform APIs or parsing website data through the NewPipe Extractor. Built as free and open-source software, it intentionally omits proprietary frameworks like Google Play Services, making it fully compatible with devices and custom ROMs lacking Google apps. It is intended for Android users seeking a privacy-focused alternative for media streaming.

name: drawdb
description: Free, simple, and intuitive online database diagram editor and SQL generator.
summary: drawDB is a free, simple, and intuitive database schema editor and SQL generator designed as a robust browser-based entity relationship diagram (ERD) tool. Its main capabilities include building diagrams with a few clicks, exporting and importing SQL scripts, generating migrations, and customizing the editor without requiring an account. Optional features like file sharing can be enabled by setting up a companion backend server. The project utilizes technologies such as Docker, npm, and Vite.

name: mindshub
description: The unified workspace where open-source models get things done for you.
summary:
MindsHub is an open-source agent workspace designed for completing knowledge work, conducting research, analyzing data, and developing software. It serves as a platform superproject combining a desktop/web application, agent backend, and data engine, allowing users to build and run the entire stack from source. 

The platform supports flexible deployment options—including local machines, VPCs, on-premises, and air-gapped infrastructure—and is intended for creators, strategists, operators, and developers. 

Key capabilities include:
- **Model Router:** Switch between frontier models (such as Claude, GPT, and Gemini) and open models (such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi) using a unified provider selection.
- **Open Agents:** Run and swap interchangeable open-source agent harnesses, such as Anton and Hermes.
- **Connected Data:** Securely link external systems like BigQuery, Postgres, Gmail, Drive, HubSpot, Notion, and Linear while keeping credentials scoped per connection.
- **Artifacts & Automation:** Automate multi-step repetitive reading and writing workflows, build internal AI tools, apps, dashboards, and documents, and publish them to a live URL.
- **Memory, Skills & Scheduling:** Utilize cross-session memory, a reusable skill library, and scheduled tasks.

Notable technologies and tools used include Python (3.10–3.13), Electron, and Git submodules, under the MIT License.

name: erpnext
description: Free and Open Source Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)
summary:
ERPNext is a 100% open-source enterprise resource planning (ERP) system designed to help businesses manage daily operations, including accounting, order management, manufacturing, asset management, and project tracking. Intended for business owners, organizations, and administrators seeking a centralized platform to handle finances, inventory, production cycles, and personnel, ERPNext consolidates tasks traditionally requiring separate software solutions. 

Key capabilities include managing cash flow and financial reports, tracking inventory and supply chains, simplifying manufacturing and capacity planning, handling asset lifecycles, and delivering projects within time and budget constraints. 

The project is built on the **Frappe Framework**, a full-stack web application framework written in Python and JavaScript that provides a database abstraction layer, user authentication, and a REST API. It utilizes **Frappe UI**, a Vue-based UI library, to deliver a modern single-page application interface. Deployments support MariaDB databases and can be hosted via Frappe Cloud or self-hosted using Docker and the Frappe Bench CLI.

name: open-notebook
description: An Open Source implementation of Notebook LM with more flexibility and features
summary:
Open Notebook is an open-source, privacy-focused, and self-hosted alternative to Google's Notebook LM. Designed for researchers, learners, and professionals seeking full data sovereignty, the project serves as an intelligent research assistant and multi-modal knowledge manager. 

Main capabilities include organizing diverse content types (PDFs, videos, audio, web pages, and Office documents), performing full-text and vector search, running context-aware AI chat conversations with citations, generating multi-speaker podcasts with custom episode profiles, and executing customizable content transformations. It supports over 18 AI providers—including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, LM Studio, and DeepSeek—via the Esperanto integration library, accommodating both cloud APIs and local models. 

The application features a multi-language user interface, a comprehensive REST API for automation, optional password protection, and support for reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3. Built with Python, FastAPI, Next.js, React, SurrealDB, and LangChain, Open Notebook can be easily deployed via Docker for complete control over research data and AI infrastructure.

name: awesome-copilot
description: Community-contributed instructions, agents, skills, and configurations to help you make the most of GitHub Copilot.
summary: Awesome GitHub Copilot is a community-created collection of custom agents, instructions, skills, hooks, workflows, and plugins designed to enhance the GitHub Copilot experience. The project aims to provide developers with extensible tools, including specialized Copilot agents that integrate with MCP servers, automated coding standards instructions, self-contained skills with bundled assets, and curated workflow plugins. Intended for developers utilizing GitHub Copilot in environments like VS Code or the Copilot CLI, the repository also includes a cookbook with recipes for Copilot APIs and a Learning Hub featuring guides and tutorials. Key technologies and concepts referenced include GitHub Copilot, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, VS Code, and structured machine-readable listings via `llms.txt`.

name: styleguide
description: Style guides for Google-originated open-source projects
summary:
Google Style Guides is a repository containing the coding conventions and style guidelines used for Google code across numerous programming languages and formats. Its purpose is to help developers write consistent code when working on projects that originated at Google. 

The project provides guidelines for languages and technologies including C++, C#, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, TypeScript, Swift, Objective-C, Common Lisp, Haskell, HTML/CSS, JSON, Markdown, R, Shell, Vim script, XML, and Emacs settings (`google-c-style.el`). It is intended for developers modifying or contributing to Google-owned and originated open-source projects. 

External code contributions to the repository are not accepted, as the guides are maintained primarily to reflect Google's internal style guidelines.

name: googletest
description: GoogleTest - Google Testing and Mocking Framework
summary:
GoogleTest is Google's C++ test framework, merging the formerly separate GoogleTest and GoogleMock projects. It is an xUnit-based testing framework designed for C++ developers to write unit tests. 

Main capabilities include automatic test discovery, a rich set of built-in assertions, user-defined assertions, death tests for verifying error-handling behavior, fatal and non-fatal failures, value-parameterized tests, type-parameterized tests, and flexible options for running tests (including individual execution, ordered runs, and parallel execution). 

The project requires at least C++17 and follows Google's Foundational C++ Support Policy for compilers, platforms, and build tools. Intended users include C++ developers seeking a robust unit testing framework, as utilized by notable projects such as Chromium, LLVM, Protocol Buffers, and OpenCV.

name: quivr
description: Opiniated RAG for integrating GenAI in your apps 🧠   Focus on your product rather than the RAG. Easy integration in existing products with customisation!  Any LLM: GPT4, Groq, Llama. Any Vectorstore: PGVector, Faiss. Any Files. Anyway you want.
summary:
Quivr is an opinionated, fast, and efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to serve as a user's second brain and personal assistant. The project allows developers to ingest various file formats—such as PDF, TXT, and Markdown—and build customizable RAG applications with just a few lines of Python code using the `quivr-core` package. 

Quivr supports any Large Language Model (LLM), including models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Gemma, and local models via Ollama. It features customizable workflows, support for internet search, integrated tools, and file ingestion compatibility with Megaparse and reranking suppliers like Cohere. The intended users are developers looking to easily integrate advanced RAG capabilities and customizable retrieval strategies into their applications without managing complex underlying pipelines. The project requires Python 3.10 or newer and is licensed under the Apache 2.0 License.

name: Deep-Learning-Papers-Reading-Roadmap
description: Deep Learning papers reading roadmap for anyone who are eager to learn this amazing tech!
summary:
This repository provides a curated reading roadmap of deep learning papers designed for newcomers and researchers in the field. The project is organized around guidelines progressing from foundational concepts to state-of-the-art developments, moving from general foundations to specific application domains. 

The roadmap spans three main sections:
1. **Deep Learning History and Basics:** Covers foundational texts, surveys, and the evolution of milestone architectures in ImageNet classification (such as AlexNet, VGGNet, GoogLeNet, and ResNet) and speech recognition.
2. **Deep Learning Methods:** Explores models, optimizations, unsupervised learning and deep generative models (like VAEs and GANs), recurrent neural networks, sequence-to-sequence models, neural Turing machines, deep reinforcement learning, transfer learning, and one-shot learning.
3. **Applications:** Categorizes papers across multiple domains including natural language processing, object detection, visual tracking, image captioning, machine translation, robotics, artificial styling and art generation, and object segmentation. 

Notable architectures and frameworks referenced include AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, word2vec, R-CNN, Fast R-CNN, Faster R-CNN, YOLO, SSD, Mask R-CNN, and AlphaGo. The repository is intended as a continually updated guide for learners to navigate historical milestones and frontier research directions in deep learning.

name: oh-my-claudecode
description: Teams-first Multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code
summary:
oh-my-claudecode (published as `oh-my-claude-sisyphus`) is a multi-agent orchestration tool designed for the Claude Code CLI. It provides a natural-language interface and automated workflows to coordinate specialized AI agents for autonomous execution, architectural planning, verification, and team-based coding pipelines. 

The project's main capabilities include team orchestration via staged pipelines (`team-plan`, `team-prd`, `team-exec`, `team-verify`, `team-fix`), terminal-launched tmux CLI workers for external AI models, autopilot task execution, Socratic requirements clarification through deep interviews, custom skill management, and real-time HUD statusline monitoring. It supports multi-model integrations with external AI toolsets such as Codex, Gemini, Antigravity (`agy`), Grok, and Cursor. 

Intended for developers and engineering teams utilizing Claude Code who want to scale single-session capabilities into parallelized, persistent multi-agent workflows. Notable technologies utilized include Node.js, TypeScript, tmux, and the `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`.

name: FastChat
description: An open platform for training, serving, and evaluating large language models. Release repo for Vicuna and Chatbot Arena.
summary:
FastChat is an open platform designed for training, serving, and evaluating large language model (LLM) based chatbots, notably powering Chatbot Arena and its online LLM Elo leaderboard. Its core capabilities include a distributed multi-model serving system equipped with a web UI and OpenAI-compatible RESTful APIs, alongside training and evaluation frameworks for state-of-the-art models such as Vicuna, LongChat, and MT-bench. 

Intended users include researchers, developers, and ML practitioners looking to host, benchmark, or fine-tune open-source conversational models. The project supports a wide range of architectures and integrations, including Llama 2, Alpaca, ChatGLM, Falcon, Vicuna, OpenAI APIs, Anthropic, Gemini, LangChain, vLLM, and Hugging Face transformers, while providing optimization options like 8-bit compression, CPU offloading, and multi-GPU parallelization.

name: ruoyi-vue-pro
description: 🔥 官方推荐 🔥 RuoYi-Vue 全新 Pro 版本，优化重构所有功能。基于 Spring Boot + MyBatis Plus + Vue & Element 实现的后台管理系统 + 微信小程序，支持 RBAC 动态权限、数据权限、SaaS 多租户、Flowable 工作流、三方登录、支付、短信、商城、CRM、ERP、MES、IM、AI 大模型、IoT 物联网等功能。你的 ⭐️ Star ⭐️，是作者生发的动力！
summary:
The Yudao rapid development platform (ruoyi-vue-pro) is a comprehensive, open-source enterprise application backend and management system built with developer productivity in mind. Its primary purpose is to provide a fully open-source foundation for building business systems, featuring multi-module architecture, a code generator for one-click CRUD output, and multi-tenancy support.

Main capabilities include system user and permission management, infrastructure tools, Flowable-powered workflow engines (supporting both BPMN and钉钉/飞书 style simple designers), payment integration (Alipay, WeChat), data and large-screen report designers, a member center, a WeChat official account manager, and built-in vertical domain applications such as Mall, ERP, WMS, CRM, MES, HRM, FMS, PMS, OA, AI large language models, IoT, and IM instant messaging.

Intended users are software developers and enterprises seeking a free, production-ready rapid development framework. 

Notable technologies used include Java, Spring Boot, Spring Security, MySQL, MyBatis Plus, Redis, Redisson, Flowable, Vue3 (Element Plus, Vben, Ant Design Vue, Naive UI), Vue2, uni-app for mobile/mini-program support, WebSocket, SkyWalking, and JUnit/Mockito for unit testing.

name: devdocs
description: API Documentation Browser
summary:
DevDocs is an API documentation browser that combines multiple developer documentations into a clean, organized web UI featuring instant search, offline support, a mobile version, dark theme, and keyboard shortcuts. It aims to make reference reading fast, consistent, and fully functional offline without acting as a full-text search engine or programming guide. 

The application is built using client-side JavaScript, a Sinatra and Sprockets backend, and a Ruby-based scraper module. The scraper uses Nokogiri and HTML::Pipeline to parse, clean, and generate documentation indices and normalized HTML partials from online sources or local files. Command-line tasks are managed via Thor, and the platform can be easily run locally using Docker or installed manually with Ruby and Node.js. 

DevDocs is intended for developers seeking fast, clutter-free, and unified API reference documentation. Created by Thibaut Courouble and operated by freeCodeCamp, the project is licensed under the Mozilla Public License v2.0.

name: reverse-skill
description: Reverse Engineering / Authorized Penetration Testing / Security Research Skill Router Pack AI-powered routing + On-demand toolchain bootstrapping + Self-evolving knowledge base  Supports Claude Code, Kiro, Cursor, Cline, and other AI coding clients 逆向/渗透/安全技能路由包 - AI 自动路由 + 按需自举工具链 + 自动进化经验库 | 支持 Claude Code / Kiro / Cursor / Cline 等代码 AI 客户端
summary:
reverse-skill is a cybersecurity skills router designed to guide AI agents and security professionals through reverse engineering, binary analysis, penetration testing, malware analysis, and CTF challenges. Instead of arbitrary command execution, the project maps specific tasks—such as APK, ELF, iOS, .NET, frontend JavaScript encryption, and PCAP analysis—to structured methodologies, available tools, and repeatable workflows. 

Main capabilities include automated task routing through a centralized JSON configuration, case initialization, scope management, evidence tracking, tool index verification, and a regression test suite with over 170 benchmark cases. Intended users comprise AI coding assistants (such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor) and security practitioners working across Windows, Linux, and macOS environments. 

Notable technologies and tools integrated within the framework include Python, Node.js, PowerShell, Bash, Java, Docker, IDA Pro, Ghidra, radare2, Binary Ninja, jadx, apktool, and Frida.

name: leveldb
description: LevelDB is a fast key-value storage library written at Google that provides an ordered mapping from string keys to string values.
summary:
LevelDB is a fast, lightweight, embeddable key-value storage library written in C++ at Google. It provides an ordered mapping from arbitrary byte array keys to string values, supporting custom comparison functions, atomic batch writes, transient snapshots, and bidirectional iteration. 

Key capabilities include automatic data compression using the Snappy compression library and optional Zstd compression support. Operating system and file system interactions are managed through a virtual interface (`Env`) for custom environment handling. 

LevelDB is designed as an embedded library and does not include a built-in client-server architecture, relational data model, SQL support, or indexes. It is limited to single-process concurrent access. 

The project uses CMake for building across POSIX (Linux and macOS) and Windows platforms, adhering to the Google C++ Style Guide.

name: dioxus
description: Fullstack app framework for web, desktop, and mobile.
summary:
Dioxus is a portable, fullstack web and native application framework written in Rust. It enables developers to build cross-platform apps for the web, desktop, and mobile from a single codebase utilizing signals-based state management, a zero-config setup, and integrated hot-reloading via its CLI (`dx serve`). 

Key capabilities include:
- **Cross-Platform Rendering**: Supports WebAssembly for the web, webview or experimental WGPU/Skia-based native renderers for desktop (macOS, Linux, Windows) and mobile (Android, iOS).
- **Fullstack Integration**: Deeply integrates with `axum` to provide server-side rendering, server functions, WebSockets, SSE, streaming, and middleware support.
- **UI & Styling**: Uses HTML and CSS, including built-in TailwindCSS support and primitive components modeled after `shadcn/ui` and `Radix-Primitives`.
- **Developer Experience**: Features subsecond hot-patching, asset hot-reloading, and an optimized bundler (`dx bundle`) supporting minification and compression.

Intended for Rust developers building high-performance web applications, native desktop software, and mobile applications with a unified architecture.

name: colibri
description: Run frontier MoE models on hardware you already own — pure C, zero deps, experts streamed from disk. Tiny engine, immense model. 🐦
summary:
Colibrì is a high-performance, pure C inference engine and open research platform designed to run massive Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) frontier models—ranging from 35B to 2.8T parameters—on consumer and heterogeneous hardware. By treating storage (NVMe SSD), RAM, and VRAM as a single tiered inference hierarchy with AI memory multitiering, it streams necessary routed experts on demand while keeping dense model components resident. 

The project supports nine major model families today, including GLM-5.2/5.3, Inkling, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4/V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3.6, and OLMoE. It features zero engine dependencies, a model-agnostic CLI launcher (`coli`), an OpenAI-compatible HTTP gateway, and a responsive web dashboard. Key capabilities include JIT-inspired expert caching, batched expert union reads, `O_DIRECT` streaming, router-lookahead prefetching, hardware-aware parallel execution (CPU, OpenMP, CUDA, Metal, and Vulkan backends), persistent warm conversation states, native speculative decoding, and Brio mode for evaluating probability distributions across closed answer sets. 

Intended for researchers, developers, and hardware enthusiasts, Colibrì makes private frontier-model execution practical on modest local systems without requiring hyperscaler-class accelerator clusters.

name: awesome-deepseek-integration
description: Integrate the DeepSeek API into popular software
summary:
This repository is an curated collection of integrations, applications, frameworks, plugins, and tools that incorporate the DeepSeek API and models (such as DeepSeek-R1 and V3) into popular software. 

Its primary purpose is to provide developers, engineers, and general users with a centralized directory of software extensions and libraries supporting DeepSeek across multiple ecosystems. Main capabilities and integration categories include:
- **Applications and Client Interfaces:** Cross-platform chat clients, mobile apps, watchOS apps, knowledge bases, and document readers.
- **Development & IDE Extensions:** Code assistants, editors, and plugins for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Neovim, and Emacs.
- **AI Agent & RAG Frameworks:** Tools for building multi-agent systems, graph-based RAG engines, workflow orchestration, and vector-database search.
- **Browser, Office, and IM Extensions:** Productivity extensions for web browsers, Microsoft Office/WPS suites, and chatbot integrations for platforms like WeChat, Discord, and Telegram.
- **Backend Libraries and Providers:** Client SDKs for languages such as PHP, Swift, Go, and .NET, alongside MLOps, observability, security assessment, and API management tools.

Intended users include developers, AI engineers, researchers, enterprises, and productivity enthusiasts seeking to deploy or integrate DeepSeek models into existing workflows. Notable technologies referenced include Rust, Swift, Go, Python, PHP, .NET, Solana, Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), Docker, and various LLM infrastructure stacks.

name: bark
description: 🔊 Text-Prompted Generative Audio Model
summary:
Bark is a transformer-based, fully generative text-to-audio model created by Suno. Designed for research and commercial use under the MIT License, Bark generates highly realistic multilingual speech alongside music, background noise, and simple sound effects without relying on intermediate phonemes. Its capabilities include nonverbal communications like laughing, sighing, and crying, as well as automatic language identification and speaker presets across over 12 languages.

The repository is intended for researchers, developers, and creators interested in advanced audio generation. Notable technologies and architectures utilized include a GPT-style model architecture similar to AudioLM and Vall-E, EnCodec for quantized audio representation, PyTorch, and integration with the Hugging Face Transformers library.

name: mattermost
description: Mattermost is an open source platform for secure collaboration across the entire software development lifecycle..
summary: Mattermost is an open-core, self-hosted collaboration platform designed for use cases such as DevSecOps, incident resolution, and IT service desks. Its main capabilities include chat, workflow automation, voice calling, screen sharing, and AI integration. Written in Go and React, the platform runs as a single Linux binary backed by PostgreSQL and is available via web interface, cloud deployment, and native mobile and desktop apps for Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux. The repository serves developers contributing to the core platform or building custom integrations through APIs, webhooks, slash commands, Apps, and plugins.

name: UI-TARS-desktop
description: The Open-Source Multimodal AI Agent Stack: Connecting Cutting-Edge AI Models and Agent Infra
summary:
TARS is a multimodal AI Agent stack that ships two primary projects: Agent TARS and UI-TARS-desktop. 

Agent TARS is a general multimodal AI agent stack designed to bring GUI agent and vision capabilities to the terminal, computer, browser, and products. It includes a CLI and Web UI, leveraging cutting-edge multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations to execute human-like workflows. Core features include an out-of-the-box CLI supporting headful Web UI and headless server execution, a hybrid browser agent using visual grounding and DOM strategies, a protocol-driven Event Stream, and MCP Server mounting for real-world tool connections.

UI-TARS-desktop is a native desktop application providing GUI automation based on the UI-TARS and Seed-1.5-VL/1.6 series models. It offers local and remote computer and browser operators for natural language control, screenshot and visual recognition, precise mouse and keyboard manipulation, real-time feedback, and cross-platform support across Windows, macOS, and browsers. 

Intended for developers and users seeking automated GUI interaction and task completion, the repository utilizes technologies such as Node.js, TypeScript, MCP, and advanced Vision-Language Models.

name: OpenViking
description: Self-evolving Context Database for AI Agents. Unify Agent Memory, Knowledge RAG and Skills.
summary:
OpenViking is an open-source context database designed for AI agents that organizes knowledge, memory, and skills into a virtual filesystem under the `viking://` URI scheme. Rather than treating agent memory as a black box vector pool, OpenViking allows agents and users to navigate context using familiar file operations such as `ls`, `tree`, `read`, `write`, `grep`, and `find`. 

Main capabilities include directory-scoped semantic search, three-tier context loading (L0 abstracts, L1 overviews, and L2 details), session archiving, context compilation, and multi-tenant user isolation with resource ACLs. It supports integration with various coding agents and AI frameworks (including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, TRAE, OpenClaw, Hermes, OpenCode, and LangChain) through hooks, plugins, and MCP clients. 

Intended users include developers, researchers, and engineers building stateful AI agents and long-horizon applications who require persistent, inspectable, and token-efficient memory management. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced include Python, Node.js, Go, TypeScript, HTTP APIs, TrieHI, VikingMem, VikingRAG, and Volcengine.

name: umami
description: Umami is a privacy-first analytics platform. Traffic, campaigns, behavior, conversions, and revenue in one place — no cookies, no surveillance, self-hosted or in the cloud.
summary: Umami is a privacy-first analytics platform designed to track traffic, campaigns, user behavior, conversions, and revenue in one place without cookies or surveillance. It can be self-hosted or deployed in the cloud. The platform requires Node.js (version 18.18+) and a PostgreSQL database (version v12.14+), and it provides support for Docker and Docker Compose deployments.

name: metasploit-framework
description: Metasploit Framework
summary: The Metasploit Framework is an open-source tool released under a BSD-style license. It is designed to help users find, test, and validate vulnerabilities, and is interacted with primarily through the `msfconsole` interface. The framework is officially supported on Linux and macOS via dedicated installers, and it comes pre-installed with Kali. It provides comprehensive documentation, nightly installers, an API for writing modules, and a development setup guide for contributors. Community support, bug tracking, and feature requests are managed through GitHub Issues, GitHub Discussions, and Slack.

name: spacedrive
description: Spacedrive is an open source cross-platform file explorer, powered by a virtual distributed filesystem written in Rust.
summary:
Spacedrive is a cross-device data platform and virtual distributed file system (VDFS) designed to index, search, and synchronize files, emails, notes, and cloud storage across macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android devices. It functions as a local-first interface layered above operating system file managers like Finder or Explorer. 

Key capabilities include peer-to-peer (P2P) sync without centralized servers using Iroh and QUIC, content identity tracking via BLAKE3 hashing for deduplication, cloud volume indexing for S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Azure, and GCS, and script-based data source adapters for platforms like Gmail, Obsidian, and Slack. It also integrates with Spacebot for AI agent runtimes, featuring vector search via LanceDB and safety screening tools like Prompt Guard 2.

The project core is written in Rust utilizing Tokio, SQLite, SeaORM, and OpenDAL. Desktop apps are built with Tauri 2, mobile apps use React Native and Expo, and the frontend relies on React 19, Vite, TanStack Query, and Tailwind CSS. Intended users include individuals and developers seeking local-first data sovereignty, cross-device file synchronization, and secure, AI-ready file system automation.

name: Folo
description: 🧡 Folo is the AI RSS Reader
summary:
Folo is an open-source AI-powered RSS reader designed to aggregate blogs, news sites, newsletters, podcasts, video channels, and social feeds into a single timeline. Its main capabilities include AI-driven article and timeline summarization, multi-language translation, interactive conversational queries, scheduled AI briefings, text-to-speech narration, and specialized layouts for various media formats. It also provides integrations with external tools like Obsidian, Readwise, Instapaper, Zotero, Cubox, Outline, Readeck, and Eagle, along with support for RSS, Atom, JSON feeds, and RSSHub routes. 

Intended for users seeking a consolidated, distraction-free reading experience enhanced by artificial intelligence, Folo offers cross-platform synchronization and native applications for the web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux. Notable technologies utilized include MCP (Model Context Protocol) services, OPML import/export, and GitHub artifact attestations.

name: project-nomad
description: Project NOMAD is an offline-first knowledge and education server. Wikipedia, thousands of books, courses, maps, and optional local AI, all running on hardware you own with no internet required.
summary:
Project NOMAD is a self-contained, offline-first knowledge and education server featuring a management UI called the Command Center and an API. It is designed to run on Debian-based operating systems (such as Ubuntu LTS) to provide critical tools, educational resources, and AI capabilities without requiring a continuous internet connection. 

The project orchestrates a variety of containerized services via Docker, including local AI chat and semantic search through Ollama and Qdrant, offline information libraries via Kiwix, Khan Academy course integration via Kolibri, offline regional maps via ProtoMaps, data analysis utilities via CyberChef, and markdown-supported note-taking via FlatNotes. It also includes a Supply Depot app catalog, automatic update features, hardware benchmarking, and a guided setup wizard. 

NOMAD is intended for users seeking offline-accessible knowledge systems, educators, or anyone needing localized digital infrastructure. Notable technologies utilized include Docker, Ollama, Qdrant, Kiwix, Kolibri, ProtoMaps, and CyberChef.

name: langextract
description: A Python library for extracting structured information from unstructured text using LLMs with precise source grounding and interactive visualization.
summary:
LangExtract is a Python library designed to extract structured information from unstructured text documents using Large Language Models (LLMs) based on user-defined instructions and few-shot examples. 

Main capabilities include precise source grounding that maps every extracted data point to its exact character span in the source text, reliable structured outputs via schema-enforced generation, text chunking with parallel processing optimized for long documents, and interactive HTML visualization of extracted entities. It adapts to various extraction tasks—such as clinical notes, medication information, and literary texts—without requiring model fine-tuning. 

The library supports cloud-based models including the Google Gemini family and OpenAI models (such as GPT-4o), as well as local open-source models via Ollama. It also offers a lightweight plugin system for adding custom model providers and supports batch processing APIs. 

Intended users include developers, researchers, and data scientists looking to extract, trace, and structure text data reliably across domains like healthcare and literature.

name: preact
description: ⚛️ Fast 3kB React alternative with the same modern API. Components & Virtual DOM.
summary:
Preact is a fast, lightweight 4kB alternative to React that provides a modern Virtual DOM component model with the same API. Its main purpose is to build user interfaces using familiar React patterns such as ES6 classes, hooks, and functional components, while maintaining extensive React compatibility via the `preact/compat` alias. 

Main capabilities include JSX support, a Virtual DOM (VDOM) with an optimized diff algorithm, DevTools integration, Hot Module Replacement (HMR), Server-Side Rendering (SSR) with seamless hydration, and transparent asynchronous rendering via a pluggable scheduler. Preact supports all modern browsers. 

Intended users are web developers seeking a high-performance, lightweight UI library that mirrors React's syntax and component lifecycle. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript (ES6), JSX, and HTM (JavaScript Tagged Templates).

name: lapce
description: Lightning-fast and Powerful Code Editor written in Rust
summary:
Lapce is a lightning-fast and powerful code editor designed for developers seeking high performance. Its main capabilities include built-in Language Server Protocol (LSP) support for intelligent code features like completion, diagnostics, and code actions; first-class toggleable modal editing (Vim-like); built-in remote development support; a WASI-based plugin system; and a built-in terminal. 

The project is written in pure Rust with a user interface built in Floem. It utilizes Rope Science principles for fast computation and leverages wgpu for rendering. Lapce provides pre-built releases for Windows, Linux, and macOS.

name: RevokeMsgPatcher
description: :trollface: A hex editor for WeChat/QQ/TIM - PC版微信/QQ/TIM防撤回补丁（我已经看到了，撤回也没用了）
summary:
RevokeMsgPatcher is a Windows utility designed to prevent message recall on the PC versions of WeChat, QQ, and TIM.
