The application modifies specific binary files—such as WeChat's `WeChatWin.dll` and QQ/TIM's `IM.dll`—to block message recalls and also provides an optional multi-instance feature for WeChat. 

Intended for Windows users (Windows 7 or later), the tool automatically detects installation paths via the system registry for standard installations or allows manual path selection for portable versions. It includes a companion utility for running multiple WeChat instances. 

The project requires .NET Framework 4.5.2 or higher and is distributed under the GPLv3 license.

name: google-research
description: Google Research
summary:
This repository contains source code and datasets released by Google Research. It serves as a central collection for various research projects, experiments, and associated datasets developed by the organization. 

The repository encompasses a wide range of topics and technical implementations corresponding to individual research initiatives. Because of the large overall size of the repository, users are advised to download specific subdirectories of interest rather than cloning the entire history. 

All source files are released under the Apache 2.0 license, and all datasets are provided under the CC BY 4.0 International license.

name: ant-design-pro
description: 👨🏻‍💻👩🏻‍💻 Use Ant Design like a Pro!
summary:
Ant Design Pro is an out-of-box React boilerplate and UI solution designed for building enterprise applications. It provides a comprehensive stack for developers, featuring common application templates such as dashboards, forms, lists, profiles, results, exceptions, accounts, user authentication, and an AI assistant page. 

The project incorporates TypeScript, block templates, responsive design, built-in internationalization (i18n), mock development utilities, unit and end-to-end testing, and theme customization using Tailwind CSS v4 and antd-style. Notable technologies used include React 19, Ant Design 6, Umi Max 4, utoopack, and Ant Design X for AI chatbot integration. It also ships with built-in Claude Code skills for automated project upgrades and querying component APIs.

name: materialize
description: Materialize, a CSS Framework based on Material Design
summary:
MaterializeCSS is a CSS framework based on Google's Material Design. The project provides web developers and designers with pre-styled components, a responsive grid system, and interactive elements to build modern web applications and sites. 

Main capabilities include a comprehensive set of UI components, cross-browser compatibility supporting Chrome 35+, Firefox 31+, Safari 9+, Opera, Edge, and Internet Explorer 11+, and a documentation site that can be run locally. 

Technologies used in the project and its development workflow include Node.js, Grunt, BrowserSync, and the Jasmine testing framework. Materialize can be integrated into projects via direct download, Git cloning, CDNJS, npm, Bower, and Atmosphere for Meteor.

name: Hyprland
description: Hyprland is an independent, highly customizable, dynamic tiling Wayland compositor that doesn't sacrifice on its looks.
summary:
Hyprland is a 100% independent, dynamic tiling Wayland compositor designed to deliver the latest Wayland features combined with extensive visual customization and eyecandy. Built without relying on wlroots, libweston, kwin, or mutter, the project offers custom bezier and spring curves, gradient borders, shadows, blur effects, and animations that reload instantly upon saving configurations. 

Key capabilities include tiling, pseudotiling, floating, fullscreen, window groups in tabbed mode, special workspaces, and fully dynamic workspaces. It provides socket-based IPC, native IME and input panels, tearing support for enhanced gaming performance, global keybinds, and powerful window, monitor, and layer rules. Hyprland supports extensive layouts—including Dwindle, Scrolling, Master, Monocle, and custom layouts via Lua or plugins—alongside a built-in plugin manager and powerful plugin support. Intended users include Linux desktop users and developers seeking a high-performance, visually rich, and highly customizable Wayland compositor with bleeding-edge features and an active development cycle. Notable technologies utilized include Wayland and Lua.

name: tesseract.js
description: Pure Javascript OCR for more than 100 Languages 📖🎉🖥
summary:
Tesseract.js is a JavaScript library designed to extract text from images in almost any language. It acts as a wrapper for a WebAssembly port of the Tesseract OCR engine, bringing optical character recognition capabilities to web browsers (via webpack, ESM, or script tags/CDNs) and server-side environments using Node.js. 

Main capabilities include image and real-time video text recognition, rotation preprocessing, auto-rotate options, and support for parallel processing through schedulers. The library is intended for developers building applications that require optical character recognition without processing PDF files or modifying core recognition models. Notable technologies used within the project include JavaScript, WebAssembly, Node.js, and webpack.

name: engineering-blogs
description: A curated list of engineering blogs
summary:
This repository is a curated, categorized collection of software engineering blogs and resources. It compiles technical blogs authored by technology companies, individual developers, group contributors, and project teams focused on specific programming languages, frameworks, and tools. 

The project aims to serve developers, software engineers, and technical leaders seeking knowledge, tutorials, and engineering insights from industry practitioners. The listed resources cover a wide variety of development stacks, system architectures, and engineering cultures. Content is organized alphabetically within categories for companies, individuals, and products or technologies, and an OPML file is provided to allow users to easily import the RSS feeds into feed readers.

name: python-cheatsheet
description: Comprehensive Python Cheatsheet
summary:
The comprehensive Python cheatsheet is a reference guide providing syntax examples, code snippets, and usage patterns for the Python programming language. It is intended for developers, data analysts, and students looking for a quick reference on Python collections, data types, syntax rules, system calls, data formats, and built-in or third-party libraries.

The repository covers core Python concepts such as lists, dictionaries, sets, tuples, ranges, iterators, generators, functions, classes, decorators, exceptions, type annotations, and context managers. It also details standard and third-party libraries for handling dates and times, regular expressions, file input and output, path manipulations, SQLite databases, JSON, CSV, pickle, bytes, structs, arrays, threading, and asynchronous programming. 

Additionally, the guide includes examples and capabilities for data analysis and visualization libraries including NumPy, Pandas, Plotly, and Matplotlib, as well as modules for image processing (Pillow), GUI development (FreeSimpleGUI), web scraping (BeautifulSoup, Selenium), web applications (Flask), audio handling, console applications (curses), and game development using Pygame. Distinctive technical terms and libraries referenced include Cython, SQLAlchemy, pytest, and tqdm.

name: Langchain-Chatchat
description: Langchain-Chatchat（原Langchain-ChatGLM）基于 Langchain 与 ChatGLM, Qwen 与 Llama 等语言模型的 RAG 与 Agent 应用 | Langchain-Chatchat (formerly langchain-ChatGLM), local knowledge based LLM (like ChatGLM, Qwen and Llama) RAG and Agent app with langchain
summary:
LangChain-Chatchat (formerly Langchain-ChatGLM) is an open-source RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and Agent application framework designed for offline, private deployment, with optimized support for Chinese language scenarios and open-source models. 

**Project Purpose:**
To establish a complete, locally runnable knowledge-base question-answering and agent solution entirely powered by open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) and application frameworks.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Local knowledge base QA, file RAG (supporting BM25, KNN, and vector retrieval), and document processing.
- Advanced Agent capabilities optimized for function calling and tool use.
- Multi-modal image conversation, database chat (Text-to-SQL), Arxiv literature chat, Wolfram integration, and text-to-image generation.
- FastAPI-based backend services with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints and a Streamlit-based WebUI.
- Support for local knowledge base management and customized system prompts.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, researchers, and enterprises seeking to build secure, private, offline-capable AI assistants and knowledge management systems using open-source models.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Frameworks & Libraries: LangChain, FastAPI, Streamlit.
- Model Inference & Loading Frameworks: Xinference, Ollama, LocalAI, FastChat, One API.
- Supported LLMs & Models: GLM-4-Chat, ChatGLM3, Qwen2-Instruct, Llama3, OpenAI ChatGPT, Anthropic Claude, Baichuan, and various embedding and rerank models.

name: financial-services
summary:
This repository provides reference agents, skills, and data connectors for financial services workflows, including investment banking, equity research, private equity, and wealth management. The project is designed to be installed as a Claude Cowork plugin or deployed through the Claude Managed Agents API. It aims to draft analyst work product—such as financial models, memos, research notes, and reconciliations—for human review and sign-off, without executing transactions or providing financial advice.

Main capabilities include end-to-end workflow agents like the Pitch Agent, Market Researcher, GL Reconciler, and KYC Screener, alongside vertical plugins for investment banking, equity research, private equity, fund administration, and operations. It supports modeling skills (comps, DCF, LBO, 3-statement), document auditing, and spreadsheet automation via slash commands (`/comps`, `/dcf`, `/earnings`, `/ic-memo`). 

The repository features Model Context Protocol (MCP) data connectors for platforms such as Daloopa, Morningstar, S&P Global, FactSet, Moody's, MT Newswires, Aiera, LSEG, PitchBook, Chronograph, Egnyte, and Box, as well as admin tooling for deploying the Claude Microsoft 365 add-in.

name: tiptap
description: The headless rich text editor framework for web artisans.
summary:
Tiptap Editor is a headless, framework-agnostic rich text editor built on top of the ProseMirror library. Designed for developers seeking total design freedom, it lacks a default user interface and integrates seamlessly with frontend frameworks like Vue, React, and plain JavaScript. 

The editor's functionality is entirely extension-based, offering over 100 community and core extensions—ranging from basic text styling to advanced block editing, custom nodes, and AI-related features—to build tailored editing experiences. Pro Extensions add advanced capabilities such as collaborative editing, commenting, versioning, and document conversion. Real-time collaboration is supported natively via integration with the open-source collaboration backend Hocuspocus and the CRDT library Yjs. 

Intended for frontend developers and application creators, Tiptap is part of the broader Tiptap Suite, which includes developer components, Content AI, and Tiptap Cloud services.

name: cli
description: 🥧 HTTPie CLI  — modern, user-friendly command-line HTTP client for the API era. JSON support, colors, sessions, downloads, plugins & more.
summary:
HTTPie is a command-line HTTP client designed to make CLI interaction with web services, APIs, and HTTP servers human-friendly. Intended for developers and system administrators testing, debugging, and interacting with APIs, it provides `http` and `https` commands to create and send arbitrary HTTP requests using a simple and natural syntax.

Main capabilities include expressive and intuitive syntax, formatted and colorized terminal output, built-in JSON support, forms and file uploads, HTTPS, proxies, authentication, arbitrary request data, custom headers, persistent sessions, and `wget`-like downloads. It also features an offline mode to build and print requests without sending them.

name: portainer
description: Making Docker and Kubernetes management easy.
summary: Portainer is a lightweight container management UI designed for Docker, Swarm, Podman, Kubernetes, and ACI environments. The Community Edition (CE) serves homelab operators, hobbyists, students, and individuals experimenting with containers on personal hardware for non-production deployments. Portainer Business Edition builds upon the open-source base to provide production and enterprise features such as RBAC, GitOps, edge management, audit capabilities, and SSO. Technologies utilized include Docker, Swarm, Podman, Kubernetes, and ACI.

name: sqlmap
description: Automatic SQL injection and database takeover tool
summary: sqlmap is an open-source penetration testing tool designed to automate the detection and exploitation of SQL injection flaws and the takeover of database servers. Intended for penetration testers, the software features a powerful detection engine and supports a broad range of switches and capabilities. These include database fingerprinting, fetching data from databases, accessing the underlying file system, and executing operating system commands via out-of-band connections. The project is implemented in Python (supporting versions 2.7 and 3.x) and runs out of the box on any platform.

name: PageIndex
description: 📑 PageIndex: Document Index for Vectorless, Reasoning-based RAG
summary:
PageIndex is a vectorless, reasoning-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine designed to replace traditional vector databases and chunking with a hierarchical tree index and Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning. It mirrors human reading behavior to achieve context-aware, traceable, and explainable document retrieval. The project is primarily intended for analyzing long and complex professional documents, such as financial reports, legal documents, regulatory filings, technical manuals, medical literature, and academic textbooks. 

Main capabilities include local indexing and chat modes via the `pageindex` Python SDK, fast tree index generation via PageIndex Flash, and managed cloud-based document parsing, OCR, image understanding, and metadata/folder management via PageIndex Cloud. It also supports multi-document reasoning through the PageIndex File System layer and agent integration with frameworks like the OpenAI Agents SDK and Claude Agent SDK. Notable technologies mentioned include Python, OpenAI APIs, and custom local/cloud LLM integrations.

name: xyflow
description: React Flow | Svelte Flow - Powerful open source libraries for building node-based UIs with React (https://reactflow.dev) or Svelte (https://svelteflow.dev). Ready out-of-the-box and infinitely customizable.
summary:
xyflow is an open-source monorepo containing powerful libraries for building node-based user interfaces and interactive flowcharts. Built for developers using React and Svelte, the project provides ready-to-use and infinitely customizable components for node and edge management. 

The repository houses four primary packages:
- `@xyflow/react` (React Flow 12)
- `reactflow` (React Flow 11)
- `@xyflow/svelte` (Svelte Flow)
- `@xyflow/system` (a shared helper library)

The libraries offer built-in features such as minimaps, controls, backgrounds, and state management hooks to handle nodes, edges, and connections. It is intended for developers creating node-based applications, visual programming interfaces, or graph editors. The project is licensed under the MIT License and maintained by the xyflow team.

name: Retrieval-based-Voice-Conversion-WebUI
description: Easily train a good VC model with voice data <= 10 mins!
summary:
Retrieval-based-Voice-Conversion-WebUI (RVC) is a user-friendly, retrieval-based voice conversion and voice-changing framework designed for training and real-time inference. It aims to prevent timbre leakage by using top-1 retrieval to replace input source features with training set features.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Fast model training on low-end or modest GPUs using small amounts of data (recommended minimum of 10 minutes of low-noise speech).
- Timbre alteration via model merging (ckpt-merge).
- Built-in vocal and accompaniment separation utilizing `pymss/MSST` models.
- Advanced voice pitch extraction using the `InterSpeech2023-RMVPE` algorithm to prevent clipping or mute issues while maintaining fast processing and low resource usage.
- Web-based graphical user interfaces for both training/inference and real-time voice changing, achieving end-to-end latency down to 170ms (or 90ms using ASIO hardware drivers).

**Intended Users:**
Developers, researchers, and content creators looking to train customized AI voice and singing models or execute real-time voice conversion.

**Notable Technologies:**
Python 3.12, PyTorch, Gradio, FFmpeg, ContentVec, VITS, HIFIGAN, RMVPE, and DirectML (for Windows AMD/Intel support).

name: sing-box
description: The universal proxy platform
summary: sing-box is a universal proxy platform developed by nekohasekai. It serves as a tool for proxying network traffic, utilizing the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later.

name: everyone-can-use-english
description: 人人都能用英语
summary: Enjoy is an AI-powered assistant designed for foreign language learning. It acts as an AI teaching assistant, helping users learn languages through tools such as web applications, desktop applications, and browser extensions that integrate with platforms like YouTube and Netflix. Its main capabilities include supporting video learning, electronic books (e-books), flashcards, and structured courses. The project provides comprehensive reading materials and documentation related to self-training, pronunciation shaping, and language acquisition resources including "1000h" and "Everyone Can Use English".

name: dspy
description: DSPy: The framework for programming—not prompting—language models
summary:
DSPy (Declarative Self-improving Python) is a framework for programming foundation and language models through compositional Python code rather than brittle prompts. Its primary purpose is to enable fast iteration when building modular AI systems—such as simple classifiers, sophisticated RAG pipelines, and agent loops—by compiling declarative language model calls into self-improving pipelines. 

The framework's main capabilities include offering optimization algorithms for prompts and weights, enforcing computational constraints via DSPy Assertions, and composing retrieval and language models for knowledge-intensive natural language processing (NLP). It is intended for developers and researchers building advanced AI systems and multi-stage language model programs. DSPy is implemented in Python and integrates with large language models.

name: harness
description: Harness Open Source is an end-to-end developer platform with Source Control Management, CI/CD Pipelines, Hosted Developer Environments, and Artifact Registries.
summary:
Harness Open Source is an end-to-end development platform functioning as the next generation of Drone. It provides teams with code hosting, automated DevOps pipelines, hosted development environments (Gitspaces), and artifact registries. Designed for software development and CI/CD operations, the platform integrates a full user interface, a REST API with Swagger documentation, and a command-line interface (CLI). 

Intended for developers and engineering teams seeking an open-source DevOps ecosystem, the platform can be run locally via Docker or built directly from source. Notable technologies utilized include Go (version 1.20 or higher), Node, Yarn, Protobuf, and Docker for running containerized pipelines.

name: aspnetcore
description: ASP.NET Core is a cross-platform .NET framework for building modern cloud-based web applications on Windows, Mac, or Linux.
summary:
ASP.NET Core is an open-source, cross-platform framework designed for building modern cloud-based, internet-connected applications, including web apps, IoT apps, and mobile backends. It runs on the .NET application runtime and consists of modular components with minimal overhead, providing flexibility for cloud-deployed or on-premises solutions across Windows, Mac, and Linux operating systems. 

Intended for developers building connected applications, the framework integrates with related technologies such as Entity Framework Core for data access, Razor for syntax compiling and tooling, and the .NET SDK and runtime environments.

name: istio
description: Connect, secure, control, and observe services.
summary:
Istio is an open-source service mesh that integrates transparently with existing distributed applications and cluster management platforms like Kubernetes. Its primary purpose is to provide a uniform, efficient way to secure, connect, and monitor microservices without requiring service code changes. Key capabilities include load balancing, service-to-service authentication, traffic management, policy enforcement, and telemetry aggregation. 

The architecture consists of three main components: **Envoy**, which acts as sidecar proxies handling ingress and egress traffic; **Ztunnel**, a lightweight data plane proxy written in Rust used in Ambient mesh mode; and **Istiod**, the control plane providing service discovery, configuration, and certificate management. Intended users include developers and operators building and managing cloud-native microservice architectures. The project utilizes technologies such as Go, Rust, Envoy proxy, and Kubernetes.

name: prompt-eng-interactive-tutorial
description: Anthropic's Interactive Prompt Engineering Tutorial
summary:
Anthropic's Prompt Engineering Interactive Tutorial is a comprehensive, step-by-step educational course designed to help users engineer optimal prompts within Claude. The project purpose is to teach foundational and advanced prompt engineering techniques, recognize common failure modes, understand model strengths and weaknesses, and build strong prompts for common use cases. 

The intended users are individuals looking to master prompt design with Claude. The curriculum spans nine sequential chapters—divided into beginner, intermediate, and advanced levels—alongside an appendix covering advanced methods such as prompt chaining, tool use, and search and retrieval. Each lesson includes practical exercises and an "Example Playground." 

The tutorial utilizes the Claude 3 model family (specifically Claude 3 Haiku, alongside references to Claude 3 Sonnet and Claude 3 Opus) and is available both natively and via Google Sheets using the Claude for Sheets extension. Notable technical concepts and methods covered include basic prompt structure, role assignment, data and instruction separation, output formatting, precognition (thinking step by step), few-shot examples, hallucination avoidance, and complex industry use cases spanning chatbots, legal services, financial services, and coding.

name: VoxCPM
description: VoxCPM2: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Multilingual Speech Generation, Creative Voice Design, and True-to-Life Cloning
summary:
VoxCPM2 is a tokenizer-free, end-to-end Text-to-Speech (TTS) system designed for multilingual speech generation, creative voice design, and realistic voice cloning. Built on a 2B parameter model trained on over two million hours of multilingual speech data and leveraging a MiniCPM-4 backbone and AudioVAE V2 latent space, it generates 48kHz studio-quality audio.

Main capabilities include:
- **Multilingual Synthesis:** Direct text-to-speech support for 30 languages (plus several Chinese dialects) without requiring language tags.
- **Voice Design:** Creation of brand-new voices using natural-language text descriptions alone, without reference audio.
- **Controllable Voice Cloning:** Cloning voices from short reference clips while applying style guidance to steer emotion, pace, and expression.
- **Ultimate Cloning:** Seamless vocal continuation reproducing timbre, rhythm, and emotion using reference audio and its exact transcript.
- **Real-Time Streaming & Serving:** Support for low-latency streaming inference, integration with Nano-vLLM and vLLM-Omni for high-throughput production serving with OpenAI-compatible APIs, and on-device execution through llama.cpp-omni.
- **Fine-Tuning:** Compatibility with both full SFT and parameter-efficient LoRA fine-tuning.

Intended users include developers, researchers, and creators requiring high-fidelity, controllable, and multilingual speech synthesis models under an Apache-2.0 open-source license.

name: compose
description: Define and run multi-container applications with Docker
summary:
Docker Compose is a tool for running multi-container applications on Docker, defined using the Compose file format. Its main capabilities allow users to configure multiple containers making up an application and create and start the entire application in an isolated environment with a single command (`docker compose up`). 

The project workflow involves defining an application's environment with a `Dockerfile`, defining services in a `compose.yaml` file, and running the application. It is intended for developers and system administrators working with Docker containers. Notable technologies associated with the project include Docker, Go, Redis, and a legacy Python version available under the `v1` branch.

name: 500-AI-Agents-Projects
description: The 500 AI Agents Projects is a curated collection of AI agent use cases across various industries. It showcases practical applications and provides links to open-source projects for implementation, illustrating how AI agents are transforming sectors such as healthcare, finance, education, retail, and more.
summary:
This repository is a curated collection of over 500 AI agent projects, use cases, tutorials, and working implementations across various industries and frameworks. 

The project aims to provide developers, researchers, students, and engineering teams with real-world agent examples, ranging from quick single-agent tools to complex, stateful multi-agent systems. It categorizes implementations by industry sectors—such as Healthcare, Finance, Education, Cybersecurity, E-commerce, Legal, Transportation, and Software Development—and maps them to major agent frameworks including LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Agno, and LlamaIndex. 

Intended users include developers building AI agents, researchers exploring agent architectures, and teams evaluating frameworks for production environments. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced throughout the documentation comprise LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Agno, LlamaIndex, Qdrant, DALLE, GPT-4V, Llava, and Whisper.

name: interview
description: 📚 C/C++ 技术面试基础知识总结，包括语言、程序库、数据结构、算法、系统、网络、链接装载库等知识及面试经验、招聘、内推等信息。This repository is a summary of the basic knowledge of recruiting job seekers and beginners in the direction of C/C++ technology, including language, program library, data structure, algorithm, system, network, link loading library, interview experience, recruitment, recommendation, etc.
summary: This repository is a comprehensive knowledge summary and interview preparation guide tailored for college graduates and beginners focusing on C/C++ technical roles. It covers fundamental topics including C/C++ language features, the Standard Template Library (STL), data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer networks, network programming, databases, design patterns, and system link-loading libraries. Additional resources include coding problem references, system design topics, development direction summaries, and recruitment information. Notable technologies highlighted across the curriculum include standard C++ features, TCP/IP networking protocols, STL containers, B/B+ trees, hash tables, and standard memory management mechanisms.

name: maigret
description: 🕵️‍♂️ Collect a dossier on a person by username from 6K websites
summary:
Maigret is an OSINT and reconnaissance tool designed to collect dossiers on individuals using only a username, checking for account registrations across thousands of sites and extracting available profile data without requiring API keys. 

Main capabilities include scanning thousands of platforms with category and country filtering, performing recursive searches using discovered IDs, extracting user details and links from profile pages and APIs, bypassing blocks and CAPTCHAs, and supporting Tor, I2P, proxies, and experimental Cloudflare bypasses via FlareSolverr. It also offers an optional AI analysis mode using OpenAI-compatible APIs to generate investigation summaries, a built-in web interface with D3 graphs, and multiple report export formats including HTML, PDF, XMind, CSV, JSON, and Neo4j Cypher scripts. Maigret can be executed via command-line interface, container images, or embedded directly into Python projects as a library. 

Intended users include professional investigators, analysts, security researchers, and OSINT practitioners. The project requires Python 3.10+ and is distributed under the MIT License.

name: trivy
description: Find vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, secrets, SBOM in containers, Kubernetes, code repositories, clouds and more
summary:
Trivy is a comprehensive and versatile open-source security scanner developed by Aqua Security. It is designed to find security issues across various targets, including container images, filesystems, remote Git repositories, virtual machine images, and Kubernetes clusters. 

Trivy's main capabilities include detecting known vulnerabilities (CVEs), OS packages and software dependencies for SBOM generation, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) issues and misconfigurations, sensitive information and secrets, and software licenses. It supports most popular programming languages, operating systems, and platforms. 

Intended for developers, security engineers, and operators, Trivy can be used via command-line interface, downloaded as a binary, run via Docker, or integrated into platforms and tools such as GitHub Actions, Kubernetes operators, and VS Code plugins.

name: ai-engineering-hub
description: In-depth tutorials on LLMs, RAGs and real-world AI agent applications.
summary:
The AI Engineering Hub is a comprehensive learning and building resource featuring over 93 production-ready projects and tutorials across beginner, intermediate, and advanced difficulty levels. The repository is designed for beginners, practitioners, and researchers looking to gain hands-on experience in AI engineering. 

The main capabilities span multiple technical domains, including OCR and vision tasks, chat interfaces and UI implementations, basic and advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, multimodal media processing, voice and audio agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, model evaluation and observability, fine-tuning, and production-grade multi-agent systems and workflows. 

Notable technologies and frameworks referenced throughout the projects include Llama, DeepSeek, Gemma, Qwen, LlamaIndex, Ollama, CrewAI, AssemblyAI, Milvus, Groq, Qdrant, FireCrawl, Microsoft AutoGen, Unsloth, and NVIDIA NIM.

name: Trilium
description: Build your personal knowledge base with Trilium Notes
summary:
Trilium Notes is a free, open-source, cross-platform hierarchical note-taking application and personal knowledge base builder. It enables users to organize notes in an arbitrarily deep tree with support for note cloning, rich WYSIWYG editing, source code editing with syntax highlighting, versioning, and per-note encryption. 

Intended for individuals building large personal knowledge bases, the application offers fast navigation, full-text search, note hoisting, attributes for scripting and organization, a REST API for automation, and self-hosted synchronization. It includes specialized note types such as canvas sketching, relation maps, mind maps, and geo maps. 

Notable technologies used include CKEditor 5, CodeMirror, Excalidraw, Mind Elixir, Leaflet, Tabulator, FancyTree, jsPlumb, Electron, and Docker. The application provides a desktop client, touch-optimized mobile frontend, web clipper, and multi-language UI support.

name: MPAndroidChart
description: A powerful 🚀 Android chart view / graph view library, supporting line- bar- pie- radar- bubble- and candlestick charts as well as scaling, panning and animations.
summary:
MPAndroidChart is an Android charting library rewritten in Kotlin, supporting nine chart types, a Jetpack Compose module, and a property-based API. It provides interactive features including zooming, dragging, highlighting, markers, animations, and detailed styling control over every pixel, supporting high-performance rendering for thousands of data points. 

Intended for Android developers building mobile applications that require data visualization, the library supports both traditional Android Views and Jetpack Compose. Notable technologies used include Kotlin 2.0, Java 17, and Jetpack Compose.

name: impress.js
description: It's a presentation framework based on the power of CSS3 transforms and transitions in modern browsers and inspired by the idea behind prezi.com.
summary:
impress.js is a presentation framework for modern web browsers, inspired by prezi.com and built on CSS3 transforms and transitions. Designed for creating dynamic presentations or animations directly in HTML, the framework utilizes native browser features such as the DataSet API, ClassList API, CSS 3D Transforms, and CSS Transitions without depending on external JavaScript libraries like jQuery. 

Intended for presenters and web developers, the project includes core source files, an extensible plugin architecture, official demos, classic slide templates, and a test suite utilizing QUnit and Syn. Notable technologies involved include JavaScript, CSS3, Node.js, and npm.

name: servo
description: Servo aims to empower developers with a lightweight, high-performance alternative for embedding web technologies in applications.
summary: Servo is a prototype parallel web browser engine written in the Rust language. Its project purpose is to provide a modern, high-performance browser engine developed for 64-bit macOS, 64-bit Linux, 64-bit Windows, 64-bit OpenHarmony, and Android. It includes components such as servoshell and relies on technologies like Rust, uv, rustup, cargo, and the mach build tool.

name: directus
description: The flexible backend for all your projects 🐰 Turn your DB into a headless CMS, admin panels, or apps with a custom UI, instant APIs, auth & more.
summary:
Directus is a collaborative backend and data platform that connects to any SQL database—including Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, MS SQL, SQLite, OracleDB, and CockroachDB—to instantly generate REST and GraphQL APIs. It features a visual management Studio for non-technical users and a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects AI tools like Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT directly to live data. 

Intended for builders, engineers, non-technical teammates, and AI agents, Directus provides policy-based access control with granular field-level permissions, an embedded AI assistant for content creation and workflow triggering, and extensibility via custom endpoints, hooks, interfaces, and modules. The platform can be self-hosted locally, deployed via Railway with PostgreSQL, Redis, and S3-compatible storage, or managed through Directus Cloud. It is licensed under the Monospace Sustainable Core License (MSCL) 1.0, with free usage available under an Open Innovation Grant for organizations with under $5M in annual revenue and 50 employees, as well as a free core tier.

name: v
description: Simple, fast, safe, compiled language for developing maintainable software. Compiles itself in <1s with zero library dependencies. Supports automatic C => V translation. https://vlang.io
summary:
The V Programming Language is a statically typed, compiled systems programming language designed for simplicity, fast compilation, safety, and high performance. Its primary capabilities include rapid code compilation (often generating human-readable C code), safety features like immutability by default and no null pointers, hot code reloading, C-to-V translation, flexible memory management options, and cross-compilation. It also features a built-in web framework (`veb`), an ORM, a REPL, a cross-platform UI library, and built-in graphics libraries (`sokol`, `gg`). 

Intended for software developers ranging from beginners to systems engineers, V is well-suited for building low-level software (such as kernels and operating systems like Vinix), GUI applications, web applications, and mobile apps via the `vab` tool. Notable technologies and tools integrated or utilized include the Tiny C Compiler (TCC), Clang, GCC, Microsoft Visual C++, JavaScript, and OpenSSL or MbedTLS for networking.

name: searxng
description: SearXNG is a free internet metasearch engine which aggregates results from various search services and databases. Users are neither tracked nor profiled.
summary: SearXNG is a free, open-source metasearch engine designed to aggregate results from various search services while ensuring that users are neither tracked nor profiled. The project is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL-3.0-or-later).

name: Coursera-ML-AndrewNg-Notes
description: 吴恩达老师的机器学习课程个人笔记
summary:
This repository provides comprehensive Chinese notes and learning materials for Andrew Ng's 2014 Machine Learning course on Coursera. Its purpose is to help learners master fundamental machine learning theory, algorithms, and practical applications through structured documentation and resources. 

Main capabilities and topics include supervised learning (linear regression, logistic regression, support vector machines, neural networks), unsupervised learning (clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, recommender systems), best practices for machine learning systems, and application examples such as Photo OCR. The repository contains course transcripts, original PPT slides, Python code implementations, and notes formatted in Markdown, Word (docx), HTML, and PDF formats. 

Intended users are students, developers, and practitioners seeking a thorough, foundational introduction to artificial intelligence and machine learning in Chinese. Notable technologies and tools referenced throughout the curriculum include Python, Octave, and web-based mathematical formula rendering.

name: rufus
description: The Reliable USB Formatting Utility
summary: Rufus is a reliable utility designed to format and create bootable USB flash drives, memory cards, and virtual drives. Its main capabilities include formatting drives to FAT, FAT32, NTFS, UDF, exFAT, ReFS, ext2, and ext3, as well as creating BIOS or UEFI bootable drives from bootable ISOs, disk images, FreeDOS, and MS-DOS. It allows users to create Windows 11 installation drives bypassing TPM or Secure Boot requirements, Windows To Go drives, persistent Linux partitions, and VHD, VHDX, or FFU images. Additionally, Rufus can download official Microsoft Windows and UEFI Shell ISOs, compute image checksums, check for bad blocks to detect fake flash drives, perform runtime validation of UEFI bootable media, and automatically set up OOBE parameters for Windows installations. Intended for users needing portable media creation tools, the software features a small footprint, requires no installation, is Secure Boot compatible, and supports 38 native languages under the GPL v3 license. It can be compiled using Visual Studio 2026 or MinGW.

name: freecodecamp.cn
description: FCC China open source codebase and curriculum. Learn to code and help nonprofits.
summary:
FreeCodeCampChina is the open-source codebase and curriculum for FreeCodeCamp China (freecodecamp.cn), designed to help learners build job-worthy portfolios of real applications while assisting nonprofit organizations. 

The project provides a self-paced, browser-based full-stack JavaScript curriculum structured around four certification paths:
1. **Front End Certification**: Teaches web fundamentals using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, and Bootstrap through 10 front-end projects and JavaScript algorithms.
2. **Data Visualization Certification**: Covers advanced styling and frameworks using Sass, React, and D3.js via 5 React apps and 5 data visualization apps.
3. **Back End Certification**: Focuses on server-side development and source control using Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and Git to build 5 APIs and 5 full-stack apps.
4. **Full Stack Certification**: Provides real-world experience through agile collaboration on apps built from scratch and maintained for nonprofits.

Intended users include students ("campers") learning to code and developers contributing to the open-source community. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript, HTML, CSS, jQuery, Bootstrap, Sass, React, D3.js, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and Git.

name: playwright-mcp
description: Playwright MCP server
summary:
The **Playwright MCP** project is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides browser automation capabilities using [Playwright](https://playwright.dev). It enables large language models (LLMs) to interact with web pages through structured accessibility snapshots, avoiding the need for pixel-based screenshots or vision models.

### Main Capabilities
- **Core Browser Automation:** Navigate URLs, click elements, fill forms, type text, hover, drag and drop, handle dialogs, and manage tabs.
- **Accessibility Snapshots:** Capture structured tree snapshots and search within them using text or regular expressions instead of relying on vision models.
- **Opt-in Capabilities:** Extended modules for storage (cookies and local/session storage), network management (mocking routes, network state), PDF generation, coordinate-based vision interactions, testing assertions, and DevTools features (such as video and trace recording, element highlighting, and script execution).
- **Flexible Configuration:** Supports persistent profiles, isolated testing sessions, connection to existing browsers via Chrome extensions, DevTools Protocol (CDP) endpoints, and Docker deployment.

### Intended Users
Developers and AI engineers configuring coding agents, AI clients (such as VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and Claude Desktop), or autonomous workflows that require browser introspection and interaction.

### Notable Technologies
- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev)
- Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Node.js

name: OpenVoice
description: Instant voice cloning by MIT and MyShell. Audio foundation model.
summary:
OpenVoice is a versatile instant voice cloning project developed by researchers from MIT, Tsinghua University, and MyShell. It is designed to accurately clone reference tone colors and generate speech in multiple languages and accents. The project provides flexible voice style control over emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses, and intonation, alongside zero-shot cross-lingual voice cloning capabilities where neither the generated nor the reference language needs to be present in the training dataset. 

OpenVoice V2 introduces native multi-lingual support for English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean, alongside improved audio quality. The repository is intended for developers, researchers, and creators looking for instant voice cloning capabilities. Both OpenVoice V1 and V2 are released under the MIT License for free commercial and research use. The codebase builds upon projects such as TTS, VITS, and VITS2.

name: CopilotKit
description: The Frontend Stack for Agents & Generative UI. React, Angular, Mobile, Slack, and more.  Makers of the AG-UI Protocol
summary:
CopilotKit is an SDK for building full-stack agent-native applications, generative UI, and chat interfaces. It acts as a horizontal integration layer between AI agents and user interfaces, allowing developers to connect agent frameworks to web, mobile, and messaging platforms without rewriting core logic.

Main capabilities include a customizable chat UI, backend tool rendering, dynamic generative UI, real-time shared state synchronization, human-in-the-loop workflows, rich persistent threads, and automatic learning. The platform also provides "CopilotKit Intelligence" for user memories, analytics, and self-hosted deployments, alongside the Channels SDK for deploying agents into Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, WhatsApp, and Telegram. CopilotKit is the creator of the AG-UI Protocol.

The project targets developers building agentic workflows across frameworks like React, Next.js, Angular, Vue, and React Native. Notable technologies and protocols mentioned include the AG-UI Protocol, LangChain, CrewAI, Mastra, PydanticAI, and the `useAgent` hook.

name: awesome-shell
description: A curated list of awesome command-line frameworks, toolkits, guides and gizmos. Inspired by awesome-php.
summary:
Awesome Shell is a curated list of command-line frameworks, toolkits, guides, shells, and system utilities. The repository aims to provide developers, system administrators, and power users with resources to improve terminal productivity, navigation, customization, and script development. 

The collection covers base shells (such as Bash, Zsh, Fish, and Rust-based shells like Ion and Nushell), command-line productivity tools (fuzzy finders, terminal multiplexers, file managers), directory navigation utilities, and shell prompt customization themes. It also features developer tools, version control enhancements, system monitoring utilities, downloading and serving applications, multimedia processors, games, shell package managers, testing frameworks, and educational guides. Notable technologies referenced include Rust, Go, Python, and various POSIX-compliant shell environments.

name: taro
description: 开放式跨端跨框架解决方案，支持使用 React/Vue 等框架来开发微信/京东/百度/支付宝/字节跳动/ QQ 小程序/H5/React Native 等应用。
summary:
Taro is an open-source, multi-framework, and cross-platform solution designed to build applications that run on mini-programs (such as WeChat, Jingdong, Baidu, Alipay, ByteDance, and QQ), Web, and React Native using a single codebase. Its primary purpose is to help developers reduce the high cost of maintaining separate multi-platform codebases by writing one set of code that adapts across multiple targets. 

The project supports popular front-end frameworks including React, Vue, and Nerv. Intended users are developers building scalable, cross-platform applications across diverse modern device formats and mini-program ecosystems. Notable technologies utilized and integrated within the Taro ecosystem include React, Vue, Nerv, React Native, H5, and various UI component libraries like taro-ui, NutUI, taroify, VantWeapp, and Tard.

name: GFPGAN
description: GFPGAN aims at developing Practical Algorithms for Real-world Face Restoration.
summary:
GFPGAN is a practical algorithm designed for real-world blind face restoration. It leverages rich and diverse generative facial priors encapsulated in a pretrained face GAN, such as StyleGAN2, to restore degraded, low-quality, or high-quality face images while preserving natural details and identity. The project also supports optional background enhancement using Real-ESRGAN.

Main capabilities include performing inference via Python scripts or web-based interfaces, handling multiple model versions (V1, V1.2, V1.3, and V1.4) with distinct restoration characteristics, and training custom face restoration models using datasets like FFHQ. Intended users include researchers, developers, and practitioners working in computer vision, image processing, and digital media restoration. 

Notable technologies and libraries utilized include Python, PyTorch, BasicSR, facexlib, Real-ESRGAN, StyleGAN2, and ArcFace, with support for running on CPU or NVIDIA GPU via CUDA.

name: wtfjs
description: 🤪 A list of funny and tricky JavaScript examples
summary:
**wtfjs** is a collection of funny, tricky, and counterintuitive JavaScript examples accompanied by explanations based on the ECMAScript specification. Its purpose is to help beginners dive deeper into the language and provide professional developers with a reference for JavaScript quirks, edge cases, and unexpected behaviors. 

Intended for developers of all skill levels, the project can be read as a web resource or installed via npm as a command-line handbook. It covers a wide array of peculiar behaviors related to type coercion, arithmetic anomalies, comparison operators, prototypes, and syntax eccentricities. Distinctive technical terms and features referenced include abstract equality comparison (`==`), strict equality (`===`), type coercion (`ToNumber`, `ToPrimitive`, `ToString`), `NaN`, `document.all`, automatic semicolon insertion (ASI), tagged template literals, arrow functions, and generators.

name: deeplearningbook-chinese
description: Deep Learning Book Chinese Translation
summary:
This repository contains the collaborative Chinese translation and Markdown/HTML conversion of the authoritative textbook *Deep Learning* (deeplearningbook.org). The project aims to make deep learning literature accessible to Chinese-speaking researchers and learners through community-driven translation, proofreading, and open-source documentation. 

**Project Purpose and Capabilities**
- Translates the complete text of the original *Deep Learning* book across 20 chapters and sections, covering mathematical foundations (linear algebra, probability, numerical computation), machine learning basics, deep networks (feedforward, convolutional, recurrent, and generative models), regularization, optimization, and advanced topics.
- Provides accessible Markdown sources and rendered web documentation for reading and indexing.
- Establishes a community-based workflow via GitHub issues and pull requests for continuous translation refinement and proofreading.

**Intended Users**
- Chinese-speaking students, researchers, engineers, and machine learning practitioners studying deep learning.

**Notable Technologies**
- Markdown, HTML, LaTeX conversion scripts, and `pdf2htmlEX`.

name: REKCARC-TSC-UHT
description: 清华大学计算机系课程攻略 Guidance for courses in Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University
summary: 清华大学计算机系课程攻略（REKCARC-TSC-UHT）是一个旨在提供课程攻略、学习资料、选课与考试经验的项目。该项目主要面向清华大学学生及相关学习者，收录了丰富的课程内容与参考书目。项目支持通过 GitHub、ReadTheDocs 网站以及清华大学校内 Git 镜像进行访问，并欢迎通过 Issue、PR 或匿名邮件等方式进行内容贡献。贡献内容遵循 Creative Commons BY-SA 4.0（知识共享署名 - 相同方式共享 4.0）国际许可协议。

name: dokploy
description: Open Source Alternative to Vercel, Netlify and Heroku.
summary:
Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS) designed to simplify the deployment and management of applications and databases on virtual private servers. It serves developers and system administrators as an open-source alternative to platforms like Vercel, Heroku, and Netlify. 

Main capabilities include deploying various application types (Node.js, PHP, Python, Go, Ruby), managing databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MariaDB, libsql, and Redis), automating database backups to external storage, and running complex applications using native Docker Compose support. It also enables multi-node scaling via Docker Swarm, single-click open-source template deployments, and multi-server remote management. Routing and load balancing are handled through Traefik integration. Additional features comprise real-time resource monitoring (CPU, memory, storage, network), Docker container management, CLI and API access, and deployment notifications through Slack, Discord, Telegram, and email.

name: Hello-Python
description: Curso para aprender el lenguaje de programación Python desde cero y para principiantes. 100 clases, 44 horas en vídeo, código, proyectos y grupo de chat. Fundamentos, frontend, backend, testing, IA...
summary:
Hello Python is a comprehensive educational repository and video course designed to teach the Python programming language from scratch to beginners and intermediate developers. The project covers foundational concepts, intermediate topics, backend development, frontend web development, and AI integrations. 

Main capabilities and curriculum sections include:
- **Basic and Intermediate Courses:** Coverage of variables, operators, data structures (lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries), conditionals, loops, functions, object-oriented classes, exception handling, modules, dates, list comprehensions, lambda functions, file handling, regular expressions, and error types.
- **Backend Development:** Building REST APIs with FastAPI, incorporating type hints, handling HTTP requests, routing, static resources, OAuth2 authentication with JWT, and integrating MongoDB databases.
- **Frontend and Specialized Topics:** Web development tutorials, integrating ChatGPT and AI into projects, voice translation applications, and introductory software testing workshops.

Intended users are complete beginners and developers looking to learn or strengthen their Python skills and build real-world applications. Notable technologies utilized include Python, FastAPI, MongoDB, ChatGPT (GPT-4), Reflex, and Vercel.

name: arthas
description: Alibaba Java Diagnostic Tool Arthas/Alibaba Java诊断利器Arthas
summary:
Arthas is an open-source Java diagnostic tool created by Alibaba, designed to help developers troubleshoot production issues in Java applications on-the-fly without requiring code modifications or server restarts. It operates as a non-intrusive observer that avoids suspending existing threads or business services.

Main capabilities include checking and tracking loaded classes, decompiling classes via `jad`, viewing classloader statistics and hierarchy, monitoring method execution details (parameters, return values, and exceptions), tracing method invocations to identify performance bottlenecks, and tracking system metrics such as thread states, CPU usage, and garbage collection statistics. It also features a memory compiler (`mc`), class hotswapping (`retransform`), heap object querying (`vmtool`), a time tunnel (`tt`) for recording and replaying method invocations, and profiler/Flame Graph integration.

Intended users are Java developers and system administrators needing remote or local production diagnostics. Arthas supports JDK 8 through JDK 25 on Linux, macOS, and Windows. It provides an interactive command-line interface with auto-complete, telnet, and WebSocket support, and includes web console and Spring Boot starter integration. Notable underlying technologies include bytekit, async-profiler, and termd.

name: khoj
description: Your AI second brain. Self-hostable. Get answers from the web or your docs. Build custom agents, schedule automations, do deep research. Turn any online or local LLM into your personal, autonomous AI (gpt, claude, gemini, llama, qwen, mistral). Get started - free.
summary:
Khoj is an open-source personal and enterprise AI application designed to extend user capabilities through local or online large language models such as Llama 3, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, GPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek. 

The project's main capabilities include chatting with AI, retrieving answers from the internet and documents (including images, PDFs, Markdown, org-mode, Word, and Notion files), advanced semantic search, image generation, voice interaction, and automated research via newsletters and notifications. Users can also create custom agents with specific knowledge, personas, models, and tools. 

Intended for individuals and enterprises seeking private or cloud-hosted AI assistance, Khoj can be accessed via a web browser, desktop, phone, WhatsApp, or integrated into platforms like Obsidian and Emacs. It can be self-hosted locally on a user's computer or deployed via cloud and hybrid solutions.

name: llmfit
description: Hundreds of models & providers. One command to find what runs on your hardware.
summary:
`llmfit` is a terminal tool and library that right-sizes open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) to a user's system hardware. It is intended for developers, system administrators, and AI enthusiasts looking to deploy or evaluate LLMs locally. 

The project inspects hardware configurations—including CPU cores, system RAM, discrete and integrated GPUs, VRAM, and unified memory architectures (supporting NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon, AMD ROCm, and Intel OneAPI)—and analyzes model parameter counts, context lengths, and quantization formats (GGUF, AWQ, GPTQ, EXL2). It scores models across memory fit, estimated speed, quality, and context dimensions.

Key capabilities include hardware auto-detection, a compatibility engine for speed and memory projection, community benchmarking support via `llmfit bench --share`, a storage capacity estimator, and local runtime provider integration (Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, Docker Model Runner, LM Studio). Interfaces include an interactive TUI, a classic CLI mode, a web dashboard, and a standard HTTP JSON REST API (`/api/v1/system`, `/api/v1/models`).

Written primarily in Rust, `llmfit` supports macOS, Linux, and Windows, and is available via Cargo, Homebrew, MacPorts, Scoop, Docker, and direct binary downloads.

name: claude-code-router
description: One local control plane for every AI agent: route across models, fuse new capabilities, orchestrate tools, and stay fully in control.
summary:
Claude Code Router (CCR) is a local model gateway and control plane designed to manage AI coding agents and LLM providers from a single application. It provides a stable local endpoint for agents such as Claude Code, Claude Design, Codex, Grok CLI, Kimi CLI, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Pi, ZCode, and WorkBuddy. 

Main capabilities include unified provider management, switching models without changing agent configurations, request retries, credential pooling, key rotation, ordered fallbacks, request logging, cost estimation, access quotas, and tool extensions via Fusion vision, web search, MCP tools, and ToolHub. It also features AgentClaw for relaying agents through messaging platforms like Slack, Discord, Telegram, and Feishu. CCR supports providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, SiliconFlow, Moonshot, Kimi Code, and Mistral. 

The software is intended for developers and engineers using AI coding agents who need centralized routing, observation, and failover controls. It is built with technologies including Node.js, Electron, Docker, and SQLite, and is available as a desktop application, npm CLI tool, and Docker container under the MIT License.

name: chatwoot
description: Open-source live-chat, email support, omni-channel desk. An alternative to Intercom, Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud etc. 🔥💬
summary:
Chatwoot is a modern, open-source, and self-hosted customer support platform designed as an alternative to proprietary solutions like Intercom, Zendesk, and Salesforce Service Cloud. It provides businesses with tools to manage customer conversations, streamline support workflows, and retain control over their customer data. 

Main capabilities include omnichannel support that centralizes live chat, email, and messaging platforms (such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, WhatsApp, Telegram, Line, and SMS) into a single inbox. It features Captain, an integrated AI agent for automating responses; a built-in Help Center portal for publishing FAQs and guides; collaboration and productivity tools like private notes, mentions, keyboard shortcuts, canned responses, and auto-assignment; customer data management, segmentation, and proactive campaigns; extensive reporting and CSAT metrics; and integrations with Slack, Dialogflow, Shopify, Google Translate, and Linear. 

The platform is intended for businesses and support teams seeking scalable and flexible customer service infrastructure. Deployable via Heroku and DigitalOcean Kubernetes apps, Chatwoot utilizes a git-flow branching model with `develop` as its base branch and is released under the MIT License.

name: LLM101n
description: LLM101n: Let's build a Storyteller
summary:
LLM101n is an unreleased educational course developed by Eureka Labs designed to guide students through building a Storyteller AI Large Language Model from scratch. The project purpose is to enable learners to create, refine, and illustrate short stories using a functioning web application similar to ChatGPT, providing a deep understanding of AI, LLMs, and deep learning. 

The intended users are learners with minimal computer science prerequisites seeking an end-to-end curriculum. The syllabus spans seventeen chapters—from Bigram Language Models, Micrograd, Attention, and Transformers (GPT-2) to tokenization, optimization (AdamW), GPU hardware execution, mixed precision training, distributed optimization, datasets, KV-caching, quantization, supervised finetuning (SFT), reinforcement learning (RLHF, PPO, DPO), deployment, and multimodal architectures (VQVAE, diffusion transformers). 

Notable technologies and technical concepts utilized across the curriculum include Python, C, CUDA, Assembly, PyTorch, JAX, backpropagation, byte pair encoding (minBPE), ZeRO, LoRA, RoPE, RMSNorm, Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), and Mixture of Experts (MoE).

name: Data-Science-For-Beginners
description: 10 Weeks, 20 Lessons, Data Science for All!
summary:
Data Science for Beginners is a 10-week, 20-lesson project-based curriculum designed for students and complete beginners. The project purpose is to teach foundational data science principles—including data ethics, statistics and probability, data preparation, relational and NoSQL databases, data visualization, the data science lifecycle, and cloud-based data science. 

The main capabilities of the curriculum include structured lessons featuring pre- and post-lesson quizzes, written instructions, step-by-step project guides, knowledge checks, challenges, and code solutions. Intended users include absolute beginners, students, self-directed learners, study groups, and teachers utilizing classroom resources. 

Notable technologies and tools utilized throughout the curriculum include Python, Pandas, Matplotlib, SQL, NoSQL document databases, Azure Machine Learning Studio, GitHub Codespaces, and VS Code Remote Containers.

name: awesome-english-ebooks
description: 经济学人(含音频)、纽约客、卫报、连线、大西洋月刊等英语杂志免费下载,支持epub、mobi、pdf格式, 每周更新
summary: This repository provides downloadable resources and weekly or monthly updates for prominent English-language foreign magazines and periodicals, specifically including The Economist, The New Yorker, The Atlantic, and Wired, intended for English learners, readers, and test preparation. Additionally, it recommends tools and applications such as the 英阅阅读器 (eReader) application—which features click-to-look-up vocabulary, sentence translation, mdict dictionaries, reading notes, and AI-powered grammar and vocabulary analysis—along with Duolingo, Duokan, and Kindle for reading EPUB and MOBI formats.

name: textual
description: The lean application framework for Python.  Build sophisticated user interfaces with a simple Python API. Run your apps in the terminal and a web browser.
summary:
Textual is a Rapid Application Development framework for Python that enables developers to build cross-platform user interfaces that run in the terminal or a web browser. 

**Project Purpose:** To provide a lean, modern Python API combined with web-world development paradigms for creating and maintaining terminal and browser-based applications.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Supports running applications in the terminal or a web browser via `textual serve`.
- Provides a comprehensive library of built-in widgets including buttons, tree controls, data tables, inputs, text areas, list views, and digits.
- Features a flexible layout system, predefined themes, and a fuzzy-search command palette (`ctrl+p`).
- Includes an asynchronous framework architecture that integrates with async libraries while remaining optional for synchronous use.
- Supplies an advanced testing framework and a separate dev console via `textual-dev` for debugging system messages, events, and log outputs.

**Intended Users:** Python developers seeking to build sophisticated terminal user interfaces (TUIs) and web-accessible text-mode applications.

**Notable Technologies:** Python, `textual-dev`, `textual-web`, and asynchronous programming paradigms.

name: Open-Assistant
description: OpenAssistant is a chat-based assistant that understands tasks, can interact with third-party systems, and retrieve information dynamically to do so.
summary:
Open-Assistant is a completed open-source project by LAION-AI designed to provide everyone access to a chat-based large language model (LLM). Its primary purpose is to build a personalized, extensible, small, and efficient assistant capable of performing meaningful work, using APIs, and dynamically researching information on consumer hardware. 

The project's main capabilities include data collection for model prompts and responses, crowdsourced ranking and labelling, a reward model training phase, and RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) training following the InstructGPT methodology. The final published dataset is available on HuggingFace as `OpenAssistant/oasst2`. 

Intended users include developers, researchers, and community contributors interested in open language models and crowdsourced dataset creation. Notable technologies used in the repository and development stack include Docker, Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, a web frontend, and Python-based inference systems.

name: claude-plugins-official
description: Official, Anthropic-managed directory of high quality Claude Code Plugins.
summary:
The Claude Code Plugins Directory is a curated repository that hosts high-quality plugins for Claude Code. It features two primary sections: `/plugins` for internal extensions developed and maintained by Anthropic, and `/external_plugins` for third-party submissions from partners and the community. 

The intended users include developers and partners extending Claude Code functionality through custom integrations. The project documents a standardized plugin structure utilizing metadata via `plugin.json`, MCP server configurations (`.mcp.json`), slash commands, agents, and skill definitions. It also supports skill-bundle plugins that declare explicit skill arrays (`SKILL.md`) without requiring a standard manifest. Installation is supported directly through Claude Code's plugin system and marketplace discovery features using commands such as `/plugin install`.

name: tutorials
description: Getting Started with Spring Boot 3:
summary: This repository contains a collection of small, focused tutorials covering various aspects of development in the Java ecosystem, with a strong emphasis on the Spring Framework, including Spring, Spring Boot, and Spring Security. Each tutorial targets a single, well-defined area of development. The project uses Apache Maven build profiles to segregate its numerous modules across different JDK versions (such as JDK 8, JDK 17, JDK 21, and newer) and test types, supporting both unit tests and integration tests. It is designed for developers seeking practical examples and guidance across the Java and Spring ecosystems. Notable technologies utilized include Java, Spring, Spring Boot, Spring Security, and Maven.

name: glance
description: A self-hosted dashboard that puts all your feeds in one place
summary:
Glance is a lightweight, highly customizable dashboard designed to display user feeds and information in a streamlined, mobile-optimized interface. Its primary purpose is to aggregate various data sources—such as RSS feeds, Reddit posts, Hacker News, weather forecasts, YouTube channel uploads, Twitch channels, market prices, Docker container statuses, and server stats—into a single customizable view with support for multiple pages and tabs. 

Intended for users seeking a fast self-hosted dashboard, Glance features low memory usage, few dependencies, minimal vanilla JS, and page load times typically under one second via cached requests. Configuration is managed through YAML files, and users can extend functionality using custom widgets like `iframe`, `html`, `extension`, and `custom-api`. 

Technologies used include Go, Docker, and standard web formats (YAML, HTML, CSS). Glance is distributed as a single precompiled binary for multiple operating systems and architectures, as well as a compact Docker container.

name: PDFMathTranslate
description: [EMNLP 2025 Demo] PDF scientific paper translation with preserved formats - 基于 AI 完整保留排版的 PDF 文档全文双语翻译，支持 Google/DeepL/Ollama/OpenAI 等服务，提供 CLI/GUI/MCP/Docker/Zotero
summary:
PDFMathTranslate is an open-source software tool designed for translating scientific PDF documents while preserving their original layouts, including formulas, charts, tables of contents, and annotations. 

Intended users include researchers, students, and professionals seeking to overcome language barriers in academic literature without losing formatting integrity. 

Main capabilities include multilingual and multi-service translation support, automated optical character recognition (OCR), partial document translation, batch processing, and both command-line interfaces (CLI) and graphical user interfaces (GUI) via web servers or Docker containers. It also supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) modes and Zotero integration.

Notable technologies and libraries utilized include Python, Docker, Gradio, PyMuPDF, Pdfminer.six, DocLayout-YOLO, Tesseract OCR, ONNX, and large language models alongside various commercial translation services like Google, DeepL, and OpenAI.

name: CasaOS
description: CasaOS - A simple, easy-to-use, elegant open-source Personal Cloud system.
summary:
CasaOS is an open-source personal cloud system designed to establish user data autonomy, reduce SaaS costs, and serve as a home data center. 

Its main capabilities include a human-centric, user-friendly web UI built for home scenarios, one-click installation of curated applications from an app store (such as Nextcloud, HomeAssistant, AdGuard, and Jellyfin), support for easily deploying over 100,000 apps from the Docker ecosystem, intuitive drive and file management, and system and application resource widgets. 

CasaOS is intended for individuals, creators, and small organizations seeking an affordable, self-hosted edge computing and storage solution. It officially supports hardware architectures like amd64/x86-64, arm64, and armv7 across base operating systems including Debian, Ubuntu Server, and Raspberry Pi OS, with community support for Armbian and other distributions.

name: interview_internal_reference
description: 2025年最新总结，阿里，腾讯，百度，美团，头条等技术面试题目，以及答案，专家出题人分析汇总。
summary: This repository provides a comprehensive collection of technical interview questions, answers, and expert analyses targeting major technology companies such as Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, Meituan, and ByteDance. The project covers a wide range of subjects including company-specific interview contents, MySQL, Redis, MongoDB, Zookeeper, Nginx, algorithms, memory, CPU, disk, network communication, system security, and concurrency. It is designed to assist software engineers, developers, and job seekers—particularly those focusing on C, C++, and Go directions—in preparing for technical assessments, campus recruitment, and experienced-hire interviews.

name: gym
description: A toolkit for developing and comparing reinforcement learning algorithms.
summary:
Gym is an open-source Python library designed for developing and comparing reinforcement learning algorithms. It provides a standard API for communication between learning algorithms and environments, alongside a standard set of compliant environments. The project is intended for researchers and developers working in reinforcement learning, serving as a field standard API. 

Key capabilities include environment creation, step execution, action sampling, environment versioning for reproducibility, and modular dependency installation for specific environment families such as Atari and MuJoCo. The library models environments as simple Python `env` classes and supports technologies including Python 3.7 through 3.10 on Linux and macOS, with dependencies like `mujoco`. 

Note that development has moved to Gymnasium, a drop-in replacement, and Gym will receive no future updates. Notable related libraries built on or associated with the ecosystem include CleanRL, Tianshou, RLlib, and PettingZoo.

name: fastify
description: Fast and low overhead web framework, for Node.js
summary:
Fastify is a high-performance, low-overhead web framework designed for developers building efficient backend applications and APIs. Inspired by Express and Hapi, Fastify focuses on maximizing request throughput and minimizing infrastructure costs while maintaining robust security validation and an expressive developer experience. 

Main capabilities include an extensible architecture built on hooks, plugins, and decorators, schema-based route validation and output serialization using JSON Schema, and optimized logging via Pino. It supports asynchronous route definitions, HTTP/2, TypeScript, and serverless environments. Intended users are software developers and engineers seeking a fast, scalable web framework for Node.js environments. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON Schema, Pino, and the OpenJS Foundation ecosystem.

name: marked
description: A markdown parser and compiler. Built for speed.
summary:
Marked is a low-level JavaScript compiler built for speed, designed to parse Markdown without caching or blocking for extended periods. It is lightweight while implementing all Markdown features from supported flavors and specifications, and it can be easily adapted using custom extensions. 

The project operates in web browsers, on servers via Node.js, and from a command-line interface (CLI). It supports current and LTS Node.js versions as well as browsers meeting Baseline Widely Available compatibility. Note that Marked does not sanitize output HTML, so developers are advised to use a separate sanitization library such as DOMPurify, sanitize-html, or insane.

name: mpv
description: 🎥 Command line media player
summary:
mpv is a free media player designed for the command line, supporting a wide variety of media file formats, audio and video codecs, and subtitle types. Based on the MPlayer and mplayer2 projects, it features video rendering and scaling powered by shaders rather than GPU fixed function hardware. 

The software targets users running Linux, Windows 10 (1607 or later), or macOS (10.15 or later) with reasonably capable CPUs and GPUs. Notable technologies and dependencies used in its compilation and operation include Meson, FFmpeg libraries (such as libavutil, libavcodec, libavformat, libswscale, and libavfilter), libplacebo, libass, Lua, and zlib, alongside optional hardware decoding libraries like nvdec and vaapi.

name: AdGuardHome
description: Network-wide ads & trackers blocking DNS server
summary:
AdGuard Home is a free, open-source, network-wide software designed to block advertisements and tracking across all home devices without requiring client-side software installation. It operates as a DNS server that redirects tracking domains to a "black hole" to prevent devices from connecting to them. 

Main capabilities include custom blocklist management, network activity monitoring, a built-in DHCP server, HTTPS support for the admin interface, encrypted DNS upstream servers (such as DNS-over-HTTPS, DNS-over-TLS, and DNSCrypt), phishing and malware domain blocking, parental controls, and forced safe search on search engines. 

Intended for users seeking centralized privacy protection and ad-blocking for their home network—including IoT devices and smart TVs that cannot run traditional ad blockers—the software offers per-client configuration and a REST API for integrations. 

Notable technologies used in its development include Go, Node.js, React.js, Docker, and Playwright for end-to-end frontend testing.

name: pytorch-image-models
description: The largest collection of PyTorch image encoders / backbones. Including train, eval, inference, export scripts, and pretrained weights -- ResNet, ResNeXT, EfficientNet, NFNet, Vision Transformer (ViT), MobileNetV4, MobileNet-V3 & V2, RegNet, DPN, CSPNet, Swin Transformer, MaxViT, CoAtNet, ConvNeXt, and more
summary:
PyTorch Image Models (`timm`) is an open-source library that provides a comprehensive collection of state-of-the-art computer vision models, layers, utilities, optimizers, learning rate schedulers, and data augmentations. Built for PyTorch, the repository includes reference scripts for training, validation, and inference, aiming to facilitate the reproduction of ImageNet training results.

The project encompasses a wide array of model architecture families, with a strong focus on Vision Transformers (ViTs), convolutional networks, MLPs, and hybrid architectures, including recent additions like DINOv3, SigLIP 2, NaFlexViT, and various optimized backbones. It features extensive support for multi-scale feature map extraction, custom classifiers, and flexible preprocessing.

Intended for machine learning researchers, practitioners, and developers, `timm` provides a unified API across diverse model architectures. It includes a rich set of optimization algorithms (such as Muon, AdaBelief, Adafactor, and Lion) and advanced augmentation and regularization techniques (including Mixup, CutMix, RandAugment, DropPath, and Stochastic Depth). Distributed under the Apache 2.0 license, the repository integrates pretrained weights for numerous models while noting external licensing constraints associated with specific datasets like ImageNet.

name: HowToLiveBetter
description: 高性价比人生指南: 长寿防病、急救、省钱理财、法律红线、失业与工伤、医保社保、恋爱婚育、怀孕育儿、创业与做平台合规、出国与技能。每条写明成本、收益、证据等级和原始出处，只引期刊论文与官方文件。
summary:
The repository **HowToLiveBetter** (高性价比人生指南) provides a comprehensive, evidence-based practical guide for everyday life decisions under current laws and regulations in mainland China. It contains 654 actionable recommendations designed to optimize lifespan, health, time, energy, financial assets, and personal freedom while minimizing waste and legal or financial pitfalls. 

**Main Capabilities & Features:**
- **Cost-Benefit Ranking:** Recommendations are organized by cost-effectiveness across 34 thematic chapters spanning health, career, legal compliance, personal finance, relationships, family emergencies, and technical/programming risks.
- **Strict Evidence Grading:** Every entry outlines exact inputs (cost, time, effort required), plain-language expected outcomes, and an evidence grade (A, B, or C). Sources are restricted to peer-reviewed journal articles with DOI/PubMed links and official regulatory documents.
- **Interactive Tools & AI Integration:** Includes a static online search interface supporting multi-dimensional filtering (by keywords, chapters, evidence levels, and resource costs), downloadable EPUB/PDF/HTML versions, and an AI assistant skill compatible with Claude Code and Codex to query repository entries directly.

**Intended Users:** Individuals seeking practical, risk-averse life strategies, legal self-protection guides, and reliable cost-benefit analyses for personal, family, and professional decisions.

**Notable Technologies:** Python (local HTTP server), Node.js, Pandoc, Typst, and static web deployments (GitHub Pages).

name: mediapipe
description: Cross-platform, customizable ML solutions for live and streaming media.
summary:
