MediaPipe is an open-source framework and suite of solutions for building efficient, on-device machine learning and artificial intelligence pipelines. Designed for developers, researchers, and engineers, MediaPipe enables the deployment of innovative ML features across mobile (Android, iOS), web, desktop, edge devices, and IoT environments. 

The project's core capabilities are divided into pre-built **MediaPipe Solutions**—supporting vision, text, and audio tasks—and the low-level **MediaPipe Framework**, which utilizes packets, graphs, and calculators to construct custom perception pipelines. Notable tools include **MediaPipe Tasks** for cross-platform deployment APIs, **MediaPipe Models** offering pre-trained ready-to-run models, **MediaPipe Model Maker** for customizing models with proprietary data, and **MediaPipe Studio** for browser-based visualization, evaluation, and benchmarking. 

MediaPipe Tasks prioritize user privacy by processing input data such as images, video, and text entirely on-device without transmitting raw inputs to Google servers. The project supports development in C++, Python, JavaScript/web apps, and mobile environments, providing comprehensive guides and pre-trained architectures for tasks like object detection, text classification, audio classification, and real-time tracking.

name: firecracker
description: Secure and fast microVMs for serverless computing.
summary:
Firecracker is an open-source virtual machine monitor (VMM) purpose-built for secure, multi-tenant, minimal-overhead execution of container and function workloads in serverless operational models. Developed at Amazon Web Services, Firecracker uses the Linux Kernel Virtual Machine (KVM) to run lightweight virtual machines called microVMs. By excluding unnecessary devices and guest-facing functionality, it reduces memory footprints and attack surfaces while ensuring fast startup times and high hardware utilization. 

Main capabilities include an OpenAPI-specified REST API for configuring vCPUs, memory, network interfaces, file-backed block devices, rate limiters, logging, metrics, vsock sockets, entropy devices, pmem devices, memory hotplugging, and virtio device hot-plug/hot-unplug. It also features demand fault paging, CPU oversubscription, thread-specific seccomp filters, and a Jailer process for cgroup and namespace isolation. 

Firecracker is intended for cloud providers, infrastructure engineers, and developers building container runtimes (such as Kata Containers and Flintlock) or serverless services (such as AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate). It supports x86_64 and aarch64 architectures across various Intel, AMD, and AWS Graviton processors.

name: tailscale
description: The easiest, most secure way to use WireGuard and 2FA.
summary:
Tailscale is an open-source project that makes private WireGuard-based networks easy to set up and manage. The repository contains the majority of Tailscale's open-source code, notably the `tailscaled` daemon and the `tailscale` command-line interface (CLI) tool. The `tailscaled` daemon operates on Linux, Windows, macOS, and to varying degrees on FreeBSD and OpenBSD. Additionally, code from this repository is utilized by Tailscale iOS and Android applications, alongside various platform packages and clients. 

Intended for users seeking secure, private mesh networking, the project is built using the Go programming language (requiring the latest Go release, such as Go 1.27) and incorporates build scripts like `build_dist.sh` to embed version and commit metadata into binaries.

name: keycloak
description: Open Source Identity and Access Management For Modern Applications and Services
summary: Keycloak is an open-source identity and access management solution designed to add authentication to applications and secure services with minimal effort, eliminating the need to handle user storage or authentication directly. Its main capabilities include user federation, strong authentication, user management, and fine-grained authorization. The project is intended for developers and administrators seeking to secure applications and manage users. Notable technologies associated with the project include Java, Docker, and Node.js.

name: wtfpython
description: What the f*ck Python? 😱
summary:
wtfpython is an educational project designed to help developers explore and understand Python's internals through surprising, counter-intuitive, and lesser-known code snippets. The repository explains what happens under the hood during unexpected program executions, covering topics such as syntax oddities, scoping rules, mutability quirks, caching behaviors, and CPython implementation details. 

Intended for Python programmers of all experience levels—from beginners learning language semantics to experienced developers looking for a challenge—the project provides clear, code-backed explanations for each behavior. Notable technical concepts and terms explored include string interning, constant folding, the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), name mangling, method descriptors, banker's rounding, and circular references.

name: 1Panel
description: 🔥 1Panel is a modern, open-source Linux server management panel and a lightweight AI management platform.
summary:
1Panel is a modern, open-source Linux server management panel and lightweight AI management platform. Designed for self-hosters and system administrators, it provides a web-based GUI for efficient visual operations, including host monitoring, file management, database administration, and container management. 

Its main capabilities include:
- **AI Management**: A unified platform ranging from bare metal to agents (Metal-to-Agent), integrating an AI gateway, Skills Hub, and centralized management for agents and models.
- **Rapid Website Deployment**: Deep integration with tools like WordPress and Halo, supporting one-click domain binding and SSL certificate configuration.
- **Curated App Store**: A built-in marketplace offering over 165 open-source applications with one-click installation and upgrades.
- **Enterprise-Grade Security**: Container-based application deployment, WAF, log auditing, and vulnerability minimization.
- **One-Click Data Backup**: Built-in backup and restoration supporting various cloud storage solutions.

Technologies utilized include Docker, Linux, WordPress, Halo, and OpenClaw (for AI agents). The project is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

name: 500-AI-Machine-learning-Deep-learning-Computer-vision-NLP-Projects-with-code
description: 500 AI Machine learning Deep learning Computer vision NLP Projects with code
summary:
This repository provides a curated, continuously updated master list of over 500 artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and natural language processing (NLP) projects complete with source code. Designed as a comprehensive directory for developers, researchers, and learners, it aggregates tutorials, implementation guides, and open-source repositories spanning various technical domains. 

The collection features categorized resources covering time series forecasting, neural networks, sentiment analysis, recommendation systems, web scraping, chatbot development, object detection, and generative adversarial networks (GANs). It highlights industry-specific solutions such as healthcare and COVID-19 analytics, alongside production-ready machine learning frameworks and geospatial data analysis using Google Earth Engine. Notable technologies and toolsets referenced throughout the curated links include Python, TensorFlow, OpenCV, Django, and diverse transformer-based language models.

name: one-api
description: LLM API 管理 & 分发系统，支持 OpenAI、Azure、Anthropic Claude、Google Gemini、DeepSeek、字节豆包、ChatGLM、文心一言、讯飞星火、通义千问、360 智脑、腾讯混元等主流模型，统一 API 适配，可用于 key 管理与二次分发。单可执行文件，提供 Docker 镜像，一键部署，开箱即用。LLM API management & key redistribution system, unifying multiple providers under a single API. Single binary, Docker-ready, with an English UI.
summary:
One API is an open-source management system and API gateway designed to provide unified access to various large language models through standard OpenAI API formatting. 

**Project Purpose and Capabilities**
The project aggregates multiple generative AI services into a single platform, enabling out-of-the-box routing and management. Key capabilities include:
- Support for extensive large language models and providers, including OpenAI ChatGPT, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google PaLM2/Gemini, Mistral, Baidu Wenxin Yiyan, Alibaba Tongyi Qianwen, 360 Zhinao, Tencent Hunyuan, Moonshot AI, Baichuan, MiniMax, Groq, Ollama, DeepSeek, and Cloudflare Workers AI.
- Load balancing across multiple channels, streaming responses for typewriter effects, automatic request retries, and drawing/image generation interfaces.
- Comprehensive administrative features such as multi-machine deployment support, token management with configurable expiration and usage quotas, redemption code generation and batch creation, user and channel group management with customizable multipliers, quota tracking, and invitation rewards.
- Customizable branding and login mechanisms, including email whitelist registration, Feishu/GitHub authorization, and WeChat integration.

**Intended Users**
Developers, platform administrators, and organizations seeking to consolidate, manage, and distribute access to multiple AI models through a standardized interface.

**Notable Technologies**
- Go (Backend)
- React/JavaScript (Frontend web UI)
- Docker and Docker Compose
- MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite (Database support)
- Redis (Caching and clustering support)

name: linux-command
description: Linux命令大全搜索工具，内容包含Linux命令手册、详解、学习、搜集。https://git.io/linux
summary: The `linux-command` repository is a comprehensive, non-profit collection of over 600 Linux commands serving as a searchable quick-reference manual. Its primary purpose is to provide detailed command explanations, usage examples, and learning resources via a web interface, Docker images, and an npm package containing Markdown files and JSON indexes. Intended users include Linux learners, system administrators, and developers looking for a searchable command reference or offline documentation. The project integrates technologies such as Docker, Node.js/npm, HTML, Markdown, and Vercel/Netlify for deployments.

name: JavaFamily
description: 【Java面试+Java学习指南】 一份涵盖大部分Java程序员所需要掌握的核心知识。
summary:
This repository provides a comprehensive Java and backend engineering learning and interview preparation guide. Its purpose is to help developers, students, and job seekers master essential technical knowledge, system design, and algorithms for career advancement. 

Main capabilities include structured knowledge nodes covering Java fundamentals, JVM internals, concurrent multi-threading, data structures, and algorithms. It also features common backend frameworks and distributed system technologies such as Spring, SpringCloud, Dubbo, Netty, Zookeeper, Redis, Kafka, RocketMQ, MySQL, ElasticSearch, and Docker/Kubernetes. 

The intended users are software developers, computer science students, and backend engineers preparing for technical interviews at major internet companies. Notable technologies and tools referenced include Java, Git, Linux, IDEA, JMC, btrace, Hive, Spark, Hadoop, Flink, and Elasticsearch. Additionally, the repository includes real interview experiences, company overviews, resume templates, and developer productivity tools.

name: Vane
description: Vane is an AI-powered answering engine.
summary: Vane is a privacy-focused AI answering and search engine designed to run on local hardware while delivering cited answers. It supports major AI providers including local LLMs via Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and Groq. The platform offers smart search modes (Speed, Balanced, and Quality), domain-specific searching, web, discussion, and academic paper sources, as well as image and video search capabilities. Additionally, Vane features file uploads for documents like PDFs and text files, interactive UI widgets for calculations and weather, smart query suggestions, local search history, and a discover section for trending content. Web search functionality is powered by SearxNG. Intended for users seeking a private alternative to traditional search engines, developers can also integrate its search capabilities using the provided API. The application is built using Next.js and can be deployed via Docker or from source.

name: server
description: ☁️ Nextcloud server, a safe home for all your data
summary:
Nextcloud Server is a self-hosted data storage and collaboration platform designed to provide a safe home for files, contacts, calendars, and communication data. It enables users to store data on a server of their choosing, synchronize it across devices, and share content for collaboration. The platform is expandable with hundreds of apps available in the App Store—such as Calendar, Contacts, Mail, and Video Chat (Spreed)—and includes security features like encryption mechanisms, two-factor authentication, and a HackerOne bounty program. 

Intended users include individuals, organizations, enterprises, public sector bodies, and educational users seeking to access, share, and protect their data. 

Technologies and frameworks utilized within the development and testing ecosystem include PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHPUnit for PHP unit tests, Behat for PHP integration tests, Vitest for JavaScript and TypeScript unit tests, and Playwright for end-to-end tests, alongside tools like BrowserStack, WAVE, and Lighthouse for cross-browser, accessibility, and performance testing.

name: Real-ESRGAN
description: Real-ESRGAN aims at developing Practical Algorithms for General Image/Video Restoration.
summary:
Real-ESRGAN is a practical algorithms repository for general image and video restoration, extending the ESRGAN architecture to real-world blind super-resolution using pure synthetic training data. 

Main capabilities include general image and video super-resolution, specialized models for anime illustrations and anime videos (such as *RealESRGAN_x4plus_anime_6B* and *AnimeVideo-v3*), denoising via the `-dn` option, face enhancement integration using GFPGAN, arbitrary output scaling, and support for tiling, alpha channels, gray images, and 16-bit images. It provides Python inference scripts, training and finetuning code, and portable NCNN executables (*Real-ESRGAN-ncnn-vulkan*) for Windows, Linux, and MacOS supporting Intel, AMD, and Nvidia GPUs without requiring a PyTorch or CUDA environment.

Intended users include developers, researchers, and multimedia enthusiasts seeking to upscale and restore low-quality photographs, illustrations, and anime content. 

Notable technologies and frameworks used include Python, PyTorch, BasicSR, GFPGAN, facexlib, NCNN, and Vulkan.

name: Clone-Wars
description: 100+ open-source clones of popular sites like Airbnb, Amazon, Instagram, Netflix, Tiktok, Spotify, Whatsapp, Youtube etc. See source code, demo links, tech stack, github stars.
summary:
Clone Wars is a curated list of over 100 open-source clones and fully functional alternatives to popular websites and applications such as Airbnb, Amazon, Instagram, Netflix, Spotify, TikTok, WhatsApp, and YouTube. Created by Gourav Goyal, the repository serves as a learning resource by organizing projects that feature source code, tutorials, demo links, tech stacks, and GitHub star counts. 

The collection is divided into two main categories: full-stack clones paired with tutorials or courses, and general clones or alternatives categorized by functional implementation and UI similarity. The listed projects span a wide variety of notable technologies and frameworks, including React, Next.js, Vue.js, Angular, Node.js, Python/Django, PHP, Ruby on Rails, Flutter, Docker, Firebase, PostgreSQL, and GraphQL. The intended users are developers, students, and hobbyists looking to learn software development by studying real-world application architecture and implementations.

name: awesome-docker
description: :whale: A curated list of Docker resources and projects
summary:
Awesome Docker is a curated, volunteer-maintained list of open-source projects, tools, and resources dedicated exclusively to Docker and container technologies. The repository indexes projects whose core value proposition relies directly on Docker, spanning categories such as container engines and runtimes, image building, registries, image scanning, supply chain security, composition, orchestration, deployment platforms, networking, storage, observability, security, user interfaces (desktop, terminal, web, and IDE integrations), developer workflows, CI/CD, testing, and learning materials. 

Intended for developers, system administrators, and DevOps engineers, the project provides a comprehensive directory to discover utilities for building, shipping, running, securing, and monitoring containerized applications. Notable technologies and tools referenced throughout the catalog include Docker Compose, BuildKit, Podman, Kubernetes, containerd, gVisor, Trivy, Cosign, Portainer, and Prometheus.

name: MockingBird
description: 🚀Clone a voice in 5 seconds to generate arbitrary speech in real-time
summary:
MockingBird is a real-time Chinese voice cloning and text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis tool forked from Real-Time-Voice-Cloning, designed to support Mandarin datasets such as aidatatang_200zh, magicdata, aishell3, and data_aishell. The project enables users to clone voices and generate speech by reusing pretrained encoders and vocoders alongside newly trained synthesizers. 

Main capabilities include preprocessing audio and mel-spectrograms, training encoders, synthesizers, and vocoders, running a web server for remote calls, utilizing a graphical demo toolbox, and executing command-line voice generation. Intended users include developers, researchers, and hobbyists interested in speech synthesis and voice cloning. Notable technologies and models utilized include PyTorch, FFmpeg, PyQt5, Tacotron, GE2E (encoder), WaveRNN, HiFi-GAN, and Fre-GAN (vocoders), supporting Windows, Linux, and macOS (including Apple Silicon M1 chips).

name: shadowsocks-android
description: A shadowsocks client for Android
summary:
Shadowsocks for Android is a lightweight tunnel proxy client designed for Android, Chrome OS, and Android TV (API 23+). The project enables users to bypass censorship and secure their internet traffic using the Shadowsocks protocol. 

Built primarily using Kotlin and Rust, the application integrates notable technologies such as shadowsocks-rust, tun2socks, redsocks, libevent, libsodium, and OpenSSL. It requires JDK 11+, the Android SDK with NDK, and Rust with configured Android targets for building via Android Studio or Gradle scripts.

name: sglang
description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.
summary:
SGLang is an open-source inference framework designed for large language models, vision-language models, and diffusion models, optimized specifically for agentic workloads, reinforcement learning rollouts, and large-scale serving. 

Its main capabilities include high-speed text and image generation (via its built-in SGLang Diffusion engine), audio model serving through SGLang Omni, speculative decoding support, and hierarchical KV caching (utilizing projects like HiCache and Mooncake) for distributed inference. 

The framework targets AI researchers, developers, and enterprises deploying models in production. It offers broad hardware support across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD Instinct, Google TPUs, Intel GPUs and CPUs, Apple Silicon, Huawei Ascend NPUs, and Moore Threads GPUs, alongside integration frameworks like Ray Serve and NVIDIA Dynamo.

name: pnpm
description: Fast, disk space efficient package manager
summary:
pnpm is a fast, disk-space-efficient package manager for Node.js. Its primary purpose is to optimize package installation speeds and reduce disk usage through a content-addressable filesystem and hard-linking or reflinks (copy-on-write). 

Main capabilities include:
- Fast package installation and execution, running up to 2x faster than alternatives.
- Disk-space efficiency by storing files in a single content-addressable storage.
- Monorepo support via workspaces.
- Strict dependency resolution where packages can only access dependencies explicitly specified in their `package.json`.
- Deterministic installations using a lockfile named `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- Functionality as a Node.js version manager.
- Cross-platform support across Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- An experimental Rust port of the CLI called pacquet.

Intended users include JavaScript and Node.js developers and development teams of all sizes managing projects ranging from single applications to large monorepos. Notable technologies mentioned include Node.js, npm, Yarn, Rush, and Rust.

name: postiz-app
description: 📨 The ultimate agentic social media scheduling tool 🤖
summary:
Postiz is an open-source social media management platform designed for scheduling, automating, and analyzing content across major networks including Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, Facebook, Reddit, and Discord. It is suitable for individuals, marketing teams, and developers looking for content planning tools or API-driven automations. 

Key capabilities include cross-posting, calendar views, analytics, team collaboration, RSS auto-posting, and AI-powered copilot workflows for generating text, images, and videos. It integrates with various AI agents and tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and MCP servers, and supports workflow automation via a Public API, NodeJS SDK, N8N custom nodes, and Make.com integrations. 

The project is built as a monorepo using pnpm workspaces, Next.js for the frontend, NestJS for the backend, Prisma with PostgreSQL for data management, Temporal for workflow orchestration, and Resend for email notifications. It is available as a self-hosted edition under the AGPL-3.0 license or as a fully managed cloud service.

name: typeorm
description: TypeScript & JavaScript ORM for Node.js — supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, and more.
summary:
TypeORM is an Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) framework designed for TypeScript and JavaScript (ES2023) applications. It runs across Node.js, Browser, Cordova, Ionic, React Native, NativeScript, Expo, and Electron platforms. The project aims to support modern JavaScript features and accommodate applications ranging from small tables to large-scale enterprise systems using multiple databases.

Main capabilities include support for both Active Record and Data Mapper design patterns, migrations, transactions, connection pooling, replication, a flexible QueryBuilder, query caching, logging, and listeners/hooks. It also supports schema declarations in models or separate configuration files, along with a Command Line Interface (CLI).

Intended users are developers building scalable, maintainable applications in JavaScript or TypeScript that require robust database integration. 

Notable technologies and databases supported include MySQL, MariaDB, Postgres, CockroachDB, SQLite, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, SAP Hana, sql.js, and Google Spanner, alongside the MongoDB NoSQL database.

name: leetcode
description: 🔥LeetCode solutions in any programming language | 多种编程语言实现 LeetCode、《剑指 Offer（第 2 版）》、《程序员面试金典（第 6 版）》题解
summary: This project is a comprehensive collection of programming problem solutions, including problems from LeetCode, "Coding Interviews" (剑指 Offer), and "Cracking the Coding Interview" (程序员面试金典). Its primary purpose is to help developers practice algorithmic problem-solving and improve thinking skills. The repository features multi-language implementations covering Java, Python, C++, Go, TypeScript, Rust, and C#. It is intended for developers, software engineers, and programming enthusiasts preparing for technical interviews or enhancing their expertise in data structures, basic algorithms, search, dynamic programming, advanced data structures, and graph theory.

name: date-fns
description: ⏳ Modern JavaScript date utility library ⌛️
summary:
date-fns is a comprehensive, modular JavaScript library designed to provide a simple and consistent toolset for manipulating dates in browsers and Node.js. 

Main capabilities include over 200 functions for various date-related operations, first-class time zone support, internationalization with dozens of locales, and support for tree-shaking when bundled with tools like webpack, Browserify, or Rollup. The library operates on native JavaScript date types without extending core objects, ensuring safety through immutable and pure functions that always return new date instances. 

Intended for JavaScript and TypeScript developers, date-fns is 100% TypeScript with handcrafted types and is distributed as an npm package under the MIT license.

name: medusa
description: The world's most flexible commerce platform for agents and developers
summary: Medusa is a commerce platform and open-source framework designed for building custom digital commerce applications, B2B or DTC commerce stores, marketplaces, distributor platforms, PoS systems, and service businesses without reinventing core commerce logic. Its core features include foundational commerce primitives, modular architecture, and freely available npm modules, alongside Enterprise Edition features. Intended for developers and organizations building custom commerce solutions, Medusa utilizes an open-core licensing model with the core licensed under the MIT License and Enterprise Edition materials requiring a commercial agreement.

name: HanLP
description: Natural Language Processing for the next decade. Tokenization, Part-of-Speech Tagging, Named Entity Recognition, Syntactic & Semantic Dependency Parsing, Document Classification
summary:
HanLP is a multilingual natural language processing (NLP) library designed for researchers and enterprises to advance state-of-the-art deep learning techniques in academia and industry. Built on PyTorch and TensorFlow 2.x, the library offers 10 joint tasks across 130 languages, including tokenization, lemmatization, part-of-speech tagging, token feature extraction, dependency parsing, constituency parsing, semantic role labeling, semantic dependency parsing, and abstract meaning representation (AMR) parsing. 

HanLP provides lightweight RESTful APIs for agile and mobile development alongside native Python APIs supporting GPU or TPU acceleration. It accommodates mono-lingual models for English, Chinese, and Japanese alongside multi-task learning models, and includes capabilities for users to train and evaluate custom deep learning models with reproducible scores. Intended users include developers, researchers, and enterprises requiring scalable and high-accuracy text analysis tools.

name: docs
description: Ink Documentation
summary:
The InkChain Documentation App is an advanced, streamlined documentation platform designed for InkChain. It serves developers, technical users, and project contributors by providing a structured and responsive interface to access project guides and reference materials. 

The application is built using Next.js (utilizing the Pages Router) and Nextra, styled with Tailwind CSS, and powered by Node.js (v20.11.0 or higher). Code quality and documentation accuracy are maintained using ESLint, Prettier, Remark for Markdown processing, and CSpell for real-time spell checking. The repository supports local development via pnpm and containerization using Docker.

The CI/CD pipeline relies on GitHub Actions to execute automated linting, formatting, and spell-checking checks on every pull request. Feature branches and the `main` production branch are continuously deployed using AWS Amplify to enable live previews and automated production releases.

name: og-aws
description: 📙 Amazon Web Services — a practical guide
summary:
The Open Guide to Amazon Web Services (AWS) is an open-source, practical reference manual written by and for engineers. Its purpose is to consolidate real-world experience, tips, gotchas, best practices, and structured documentation across a wide range of AWS infrastructure, platform, and serverless technologies. 

The guide covers general cloud architecture topics alongside specific AWS services, including EC2, S3, IAM, VPCs, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront, Route 53, CloudWatch, EFS, EBS, CloudFormation, Kinesis, Redshift, EMR, ECS, EKS, Fargate, and IoT. It details core capabilities such as compute virtualization, object and block storage, managed relational and NoSQL databases, serverless execution, container orchestration, content delivery, messaging, and security access control.

Intended for both beginners and experienced cloud architects, operators, and developers, the repository provides architectural guidance, cost management strategies, high-availability setups, and service comparisons. It notably preserves distinctive nomenclature like Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), Elastic Block Store (EBS), Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), and Identity and Access Management (IAM), while remaining independent of official AWS sponsorship.

name: node
description: How to run an Ink Node
summary:
Ink Node is a Docker Compose-based setup for running an Ink blockchain node using an `op-geth`-based stack, along with supporting health check and monitoring services. It provides a complete local orchestration configuration for operating nodes on either `ink-sepolia` or `ink-mainnet` networks.

The project's primary capabilities include automated one-time initialization via a `bedrock-init` container, execution and rollup clients (`op-geth` and `op-node`), health check sidecars, and monitoring integration with Prometheus, Grafana, and InfluxDB. It supports both `full` node bootstrapping and `archive` node snapshot synchronization via Gelato ChainSnap indexes. 

Intended users are node operators and developers deploying and managing Ink network validators or RPC endpoints. Notable technologies utilized include Docker, Docker Compose, `op-geth`, `op-node`, InfluxDB, Prometheus, and Grafana.

name: wails
description: Create beautiful applications using Go
summary:
Wails is a project that enables developers to build desktop applications using Go and web technologies. Instead of running a built-in web server and opening an external browser, Wails wraps both Go code and a web frontend into a single binary, utilizing native rendering engines rather than an embedded browser. 

Main capabilities include using standard Go for the backend, building user interfaces with familiar frontend technologies, utilizing pre-built templates, directly calling Go methods from JavaScript, and generating automatic TypeScript definitions for Go structs and methods. It also features a unified eventing system between Go and JavaScript, native dialogs and menus, native dark and light mode support, modern translucency and frosted window effects, and a powerful CLI tool to generate and build multiplatform projects.

The intended users are Go programmers who want to bundle HTML, JavaScript, and CSS frontends into lightweight desktop applications. Notable technologies involved include Go, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and native platform rendering engines.

name: 955.WLB
description: 955 不加班的公司名单 - 工作 955，work–life balance (工作与生活的平衡)
summary:
955.WLB is a curated whitelist of companies that promote a work-life balance, operating on schedules closer to 955 (9 AM to 5 PM, 5 days a week), 965, or related variations rather than the demanding 996 work schedule. Acting as a counterpart to 996.ICU, the project aims to help individuals find companies with healthier working hours. 

The repository provides a categorized list of companies with locations spanning cities such as Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, and others, including major technology firms, financial institutions, and multinational corporations like Amazon, Apple, Cisco, Google, Intel, Microsoft, and NVIDIA. It includes disclaimers that work hours can vary by specific departments, branches, and regions. Intended for job seekers and professionals seeking alternatives to overtime-heavy work cultures, the project also offers a WeChat mini-program (955WLB) for mobile access and channels for internal referrals.

name: restic
description: Fast, secure, efficient backup program
summary:
Restic is a fast, efficient, secure, and easy-to-use backup program designed to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of data through cryptography. It supports data de-duplication, verifiable restores, and FUSE-based mounting to browse previous snapshots. 

Intended for general users and administrators seeking reliable data protection, restic operates across major operating systems including Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD. It provides native support for multiple storage backends, such as local directories, SFTP servers, HTTP REST servers, Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage, OpenStack Swift, Backblaze B2, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, and additional services via rclone.

name: jax
description: Composable transformations of Python+NumPy programs: differentiate, vectorize, JIT to GPU/TPU, and more
summary: JAX is a Python library designed for accelerator-oriented array computation, program transformation, and high-performance numerical computing and large-scale machine learning. Its primary capabilities include automatic differentiation to any order (supporting both reverse-mode via `jax.grad` and forward-mode), just-in-time compilation via `jax.jit` using XLA, and auto-vectorization via `jax.vmap` to map functions along array axes. Additionally, JAX provides features for scaling computations across thousands of devices through compiler-based automatic parallelization, explicit sharding with automatic partitioning, and manual per-device programming. The library targets researchers and developers working on numerical computing and machine learning tasks on hardware accelerators such as TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs. Notable technologies and frameworks integrated into JAX include Python, NumPy, and OpenXLA.

name: sheetjs
description: 📗 SheetJS Spreadsheet Data Toolkit -- New home https://git.sheetjs.com/SheetJS/sheetjs
summary: SheetJS Community Edition is an open-source project licensed under the Apache 2.0 License, designed for extracting useful data from complex spreadsheets and generating new spreadsheets compatible with both legacy and modern software. Its main capabilities include data processing, while SheetJS Pro offers advanced features such as editing complex templates, custom styling, adding images, graphs, and PivotTables, evaluating formula expressions for web apps, and automating spreadsheet tasks. The project provides NodeJS modules and scripts, with its source repository hosted on git.sheetjs.com.

name: frigate
description: NVR with realtime local object detection for IP cameras
summary:
Frigate NVR is a local network video recorder (NVR) designed for Home Assistant featuring real-time AI object detection. It uses OpenCV and TensorFlow to process IP camera feeds locally, leveraging GPUs or AI accelerators for optimal performance while minimizing resource usage. 

The project's main capabilities include low-overhead motion detection to trigger object detection only when necessary, multiprocessing architecture for high frame rates, MQTT communication for system integration, and flexible video recording options such as 24/7 recording and object-based retention settings. It also provides RTSP re-streaming, WebRTC and MSE support for low-latency live views, a built-in mask and zone editor, and a custom component for tight Home Assistant integration. 

Intended users are smart home enthusiasts and security system managers seeking a self-hosted, low-latency NVR solution with advanced local AI capabilities. Notable technologies utilized include OpenCV, TensorFlow, MQTT, WebRTC, MSE, and RTSP.

name: ink-kit
description: React component library for onchain applications - See README for modern alternatives
summary: Ink Kit is an archived React component library and onchain-focused development toolkit created by `@inkonchain/ink-kit`. It provides UI components, app layout templates, animated components, vibrant themes (including light, dark, contrast, neo, and morpheus), and a wallet connection component built on wagmi. The library uses the `ink:` CSS prefix and supports customization through CSS variables. Designed for developers building polished, engaging web3 interfaces, Ink Kit is available under the MIT license.

name: bitchat
description: bluetooth mesh chat, IRC vibes
summary:
bitchat is a decentralized, peer-to-peer messaging application designed for offline and global communication without accounts, phone numbers, or central servers. Its dual transport architecture combines a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh network for local, multi-hop offline messaging with the Nostr protocol for internet-based global reach and location-based geohash channels. 

The app features intelligent message routing that defaults to Bluetooth and falls back to Nostr, end-to-end encryption using the Noise Protocol for mesh sessions and XChaCha20-Poly1305 via BitChat private envelopes for Nostr, an IRC-style command interface, emergency data wipe, LZ4 compression, and adaptive battery modes. It is implemented as a universal app natively supporting iOS and macOS.

Intended users include individuals seeking privacy-first, serverless communication for disasters, remote areas, local events, or regional discussions. Notable technologies and protocols utilized include Bluetooth LE, the Nostr protocol, Noise Protocol, and XChaCha20-Poly1305.

name: vault
description: A tool for secrets management, encryption as a service, and privileged access management
summary:
Vault is a tool designed for securely accessing, managing, and storing secrets such as API keys, passwords, and certificates. Its main capabilities include secure secret storage with encrypted data persistence (supporting disk, Consul, and more), on-demand generation of dynamic secrets with automatic lease revocation, data encryption and decryption without storage, and comprehensive lease renewal and revocation features for intrusion response and key rolling. 

Intended for developers, security teams, and system administrators, Vault provides tight access control and detailed audit logs to track secret usage across modern distributed systems. The project is implemented in Go, utilizes Go Modules, and offers libraries via `github.com/hashicorp/vault/api` and `github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk`.

name: AgentGPT
description: 🤖 Assemble, configure, and deploy autonomous AI Agents in your browser.
summary:
AgentGPT is a web-based platform that allows users to configure and deploy autonomous AI agents directly within their browser. Users can name custom AI agents and assign them arbitrary goals. The agents attempt to reach these goals by autonomously thinking of tasks, executing them, and learning from the outcomes. 

The project is intended for developers and users looking to build, deploy, and experiment with autonomous AI workflows. 

Notable technologies used in the stack include:
- **Frameworks & Languages:** Next.js 13, TypeScript, FastAPI
- **Authentication:** Next-Auth.js
- **ORM & Database:** Prisma, SQLModel, PlanetScale, MySQL
- **Validation & Styling:** Zod, Pydantic, TailwindCSS, HeadlessUI
- **LLM Tooling:** Langchain

name: prompt-optimizer
description: An AI prompt optimizer for writing better prompts and getting better AI results.
summary:
Prompt Optimizer is an AI prompt optimization and management tool designed to help users write better prompts and improve AI response quality across text and image generation tasks. 

**Main Capabilities**
- Intelligent optimization with multi-round iterative improvements for both system and user prompts.
- Dual-mode optimization, analysis, single-result evaluation, and multi-result compare evaluations.
- Support for Text-to-Image (T2I), Image-to-Image (I2I), and multi-image generation workflows.
- Advanced testing features including context variable management, multi-turn conversation testing, and Function Calling support.
- Resource-aware smart favorites with version history, source binding, and complete backup exports.
- Multi-platform access as a web application, desktop application, Chrome extension, Docker deployment, and an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for applications like Claude Desktop.

**Intended Users**
Developers, prompt engineers, and AI users looking to structure, test, optimize, and manage prompt assets across various large language models.

**Notable Technologies**
- Multi-model integration with OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, Zhipu AI, SiliconFlow, MiniMax, Seedream, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Docker, Vercel, and Cloudflare deployment options.
- MCP (Model Context Protocol).

name: graphrag
description: A modular graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system
summary:
GraphRAG is a research-backed data pipeline and transformation suite designed to extract structured data from unstructured text and form targeted contexts for question answering using Large Language Models (LLMs). The project utilizes knowledge graph memory structures to enhance LLM discovery, reasoning, and outputs regarding narrative and private data. 

Main capabilities include a command-line interface for system execution, indexing workflows, prompt tuning tools for optimizing results on specific datasets, and automated configuration initialization. The system is intended for developers, researchers, and data practitioners working to improve LLM comprehension of private or unstructured data sources. Notable technologies and concepts include Large Language Models (LLMs) and knowledge graphs.

name: just
description: 🤖 Just a command runner
summary:
`just` is a command runner designed to save and execute project-specific commands, acting as a modern, simpler alternative to `make`. Commands, known as recipes, are defined in a file called a `justfile` using a syntax inspired by `make`. 

The project purpose is to streamline development workflows, such as testing, building, linting, and deploying, across projects regardless of their primary language or build system. Main capabilities include recipe parameters (including flags and options), a rich expression language with built-in functions, `.env` file loading, parallel execution, cross-platform support without additional runtime dependencies, shebang and script recipes supporting arbitrary languages (like Python or Node.js), modules and imports for organizing large justfiles, and conditional recipe execution.

Intended users are developers and teams seeking a robust command runner to organize and automate project tasks across Linux, macOS, Windows, and BSD environments. `just` is written in Rust and can be installed via Cargo, Homebrew, Nix, various package managers, pre-built binaries, or Docker.

name: hello-algorithm
description: 🌍 针对小白的算法训练 | 包括四部分：①.大厂面经 ②.力扣图解  ③.千本开源电子书 ④.百张技术思维导图（项目花了上百小时，希望可以点 star 支持，🌹感谢~）推荐免费ChatGPT使用网站
summary: 小浩算法是一个针对初学者的完整算法训练与学习项目，旨在提供系统化的算法练习流程。该项目主要涵盖四个部分：算法基础知识与数据结构总结（包括链表、栈、队列、哈希表、树、图等）、力扣（LeetCode）算法题目的详细图解与题解分类（涵盖数组、动态规划、字符串、二叉树、滑动窗口、博弈论、位运算、二分法等系列）、大厂面试经验分享与精选面经分类，以及计算机科学（CS）知识汇总。项目主要面向算法初学者以及准备大厂技术面试的求职者，提供结构化的思维导图、题解指南及可供下载的PDF版本文档。

name: carbon
description: :black_heart: Create and share beautiful images of your source code
summary:
Carbon is a web application designed to create and share beautiful, customizable images and snippets of source code. Its primary purpose is to transform plain code into aesthetically pleasing visuals suitable for sharing on platforms like Twitter, Slack, or personal websites and blogs. 

Main capabilities include importing source code via file drops, typing directly into the editor, or linking GitHub gists, along with extensive customization options for syntax themes, window themes, background colors, padding, shadows, and fonts. Users can save snippets by creating an account, embed snippets using iFrames or encoded URLs, tweet directly with accessible alt text, and download images as PNG or SVG files. It also supports offline usage as a Progressive Web App (PWA).

Intended users include developers, technical writers, and content creators looking to share code visually. The project ecosystem features community-built editor plugins for IntelliJ IDEA, Atom, VS Code, Sublime Text, Vim, Emacs, and Xcode, alongside CLI tools, chatbot integrations, and extensions for platforms like Slack and R.

name: zsh-autosuggestions
description: Fish-like autosuggestions for zsh
summary:
zsh-autosuggestions is a Zsh plugin that provides Fish-like fast and unobtrusive autosuggestions as you type, based on command history and completions. It is intended for Zsh users (v4.3.11 or later) looking to enhance their terminal workflow with inline command suggestions displayed after the cursor.

Main capabilities include configurable suggestion strategies (`history`, `completion`, and `match_prev_cmd`), custom highlight styles, asynchronous suggestion fetching for modern Zsh versions, widget mapping, key bindings to accept or clear suggestions, pattern-based filtering for history and completions, and support for disabling suggestions on large buffers. The testing suite uses Ruby, RSpec, tmux, and Docker.

name: continue
description: open-source coding agent
summary: Continue is an open-source coding agent and AI developer tool designed to assist developers directly within their development environments. It is provided as a Command Line Interface (CLI), a VS Code extension, and a JetBrains plugin. The project features a final 2.0.0 release that includes bug fixes, the removal of anonymous telemetry, and the extraction of authentication mechanisms. Technologies and platforms utilized include VS Code, npm, JetBrains/IntelliJ, and the Apache 2.0 license. The repository is currently no longer actively maintained and serves in a read-only state.

name: next-ai-draw-io
description: A next.js web application that integrates AI capabilities with draw.io diagrams. This app allows you to create, modify, and enhance diagrams through natural language commands and AI-assisted visualization.
summary:
Next AI Draw.io is an AI-powered web application that integrates Large Language Models with draw.io diagrams, allowing users to create, modify, enhance, and replicate diagrams through natural language commands, image uploads, PDFs, and text files. 

Main capabilities include an interactive chat interface, real-time diagram editing, version control and history tracking, specialized cloud architecture diagram support (AWS, GCP, Azure), animated connectors, and an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for integration with AI agents like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code. It features multi-provider AI support (including AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, DeepSeek, and custom endpoints), an administrative management panel, and server-side multi-model configuration.

The project is intended for developers, architects, and general users seeking automated diagram generation. It is built as a Next.js application leveraging React, the Vercel AI SDK, and react-drawio, with deployment options available for Docker, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, and EdgeOne Pages.

name: solid
description: A declarative, efficient, and flexible JavaScript library for building user interfaces.
summary:
Solid is a declarative JavaScript library for building user interfaces without a Virtual DOM. Instead, it compiles templates directly to real DOM nodes and uses reactive primitives for fine-grained updates, ensuring that only code dependent on changed state will rerun. 

Main capabilities include fine-grained real DOM updates, automatic dependency tracking, a render-once component mental model, built-in state management (Context and Stores), Suspense, concurrent rendering, streaming server-side rendering (SSR), and progressive hydration. Solid supports web components, custom renderers, and isomorphic execution across client and server environments. 

Intended for web developers and engineers building high-performance single-page applications (SPAs) or server-rendered web applications, Solid leverages notable technologies such as JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, Vite, Babel, and Node, while remaining compatible with modern browser runtimes, Deno, and Cloudflare Workers.

name: lerna
description: Lerna is a fast, modern build system for managing and publishing multiple JavaScript/TypeScript packages from the same repository.
summary: Lerna is a fast, modern build system designed for managing and publishing multiple JavaScript and TypeScript packages from a single repository. Stewardship of the project has transitioned to Nx. It targets developers working with monorepos, providing capabilities for distributed caching and streamlined workflows. Notable technologies and tools associated with the repository include JavaScript, TypeScript, Nx, and semantic-release.

name: slate
description: Beautiful static documentation for your API
summary: Slate is an API documentation generator created by @lord in 2013 and formerly used by projects at NASA, Sony, Best Buy, Clearbit, Dwolla, Parrot Drones, WooCommerce, and Axidraw. The original creator and administrator removed the project from GitHub in January 2026 in protest of Microsoft's contracts with ICE and the IDF, noting that a read-only archive of the codebase remains hosted on their personal website alongside further explanation on their blog.

name: CyberChef
description: The Cyber Swiss Army Knife - a web app for encryption, encoding, compression and data analysis
summary:
CyberChef is a web-based application designed to perform various "cyber" operations such as simple encoding, complex encryption (including AES, DES, and Blowfish), data compression, hash and checksum calculation, IPv6 and X.509 parsing, and character set conversions. It functions entirely client-side within the web browser and is intended for both technical and non-technical analysts to manipulate data without needing to handle complex tools or algorithms directly. 

The application features a drag-and-drop interface composed of an input area, output area, operations list, and a recipe builder where multiple operations can be chained together. Key capabilities include automatic execution ("Auto Bake"), automated encoding detection ("Magic"), breakpoints for step-by-step debugging, deep linking via URL hashes, and local recipe saving. It supports deployment via Docker or local execution using Node.js.

name: drizzle-orm
description: ORM
summary:
Drizzle is a headless, lightweight, zero-dependency ORM for Node.js, TypeScript, and JavaScript, designed to be serverless-ready by design. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite databases, including serverless variants such as Turso, Neon, Xata, PlanetScale, Cloudflare D1, FlyIO LiteFS, Vercel Postgres, Supabase, and AWS Data API. The project runs across major JavaScript runtimes including Node.js, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Edge runtimes, and browsers. 

Drizzle enables developers to declare SQL schemas and construct both relational and SQL-like queries while maintaining type safety. The ecosystem includes **Drizzle Kit**, a CLI companion for generating migrations and applying schema changes, and **Drizzle Studio**, a tool for browsing and manipulating database data.

name: bulletproof-react
description: 🛡️ ⚛️ A simple, scalable, and powerful architecture for building production ready React applications.
summary:
Bulletproof React is an opinionated guide and collection of resources and best practices designed to help developers build simple, scalable, secure, and high-performance production-ready React applications. It provides a solid architectural foundation and a sample app codebase to address common real-world challenges, maintain clean boundaries within codebases, and ensure consistency across development teams. 

The repository covers a comprehensive set of topics including application overview, project standards, project structure, components and styling, API layers, state management, testing, error handling, security, performance, and deployment. While it is structured as a guide rather than a rigid template, framework, or boilerplate, it incorporates various modern React ecosystem tools and technologies—including Next.js and Vite, as referenced in its CI workflows—while encouraging developers to adapt its core principles and concepts to fit their specific project requirements.

name: filebrowser
description: File Browser provides a file managing interface within a specified directory and it can be used to upload, delete, preview and edit your files.
summary: File Browser is an archived create-your-own-cloud software designed to provide a web-based file managing interface for a specified directory on a server. Its main capabilities include uploading, deleting, previewing, and editing files. It is intended for users who want to host and access their files through a browser interface. Notable technical aspects and features mentioned include a command execution runner and self-contained JWT-based session handling. The project is distributed under the Apache License 2.0.

name: browser
description: Lightpanda: the headless browser designed for AI and automation
summary:
Lightpanda Browser is a headless browser built from scratch in Zig specifically for AI agents, web automation, and scraping. Unlike traditional solutions, it is not a Chromium or WebKit fork, omitting a graphical rendering engine to achieve significantly higher performance (reportedly 16x lighter and 9x faster than Chromium).

The project is designed for developers, automation engineers, and AI agent builders. Its core capabilities include JavaScript execution (powered by V8), a DOM tree, HTML parsing via `html5ever`, HTTP loading via `libcurl`, Ajax/XHR/Fetch support, cookie management, custom HTTP headers, proxy support, network interception, robots.txt compliance, and an adblocker. It supports integration via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) and Webdriver Bidi, allowing compatibility with automation tools like Puppeteer and Playwright. 

Additionally, Lightpanda features an integrated AI agent mode supporting major LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Vertex AI, Mistral, Ollama, Vercel AI Gateway, and OpenRouter) to control the browser using natural language, outputting token-free PandaScript. It also provides a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with HTTP and stdio transport options for session-isolated multi-agent workflows.

name: How-To-Ask-Questions-The-Smart-Way
description: 本文原文由知名 Hacker Eric S. Raymond 所撰寫，教你如何正確的提出技術問題並獲得你滿意的答案。
summary:
How-To-Ask-Questions-The-Smart-Way (提問的智慧) is a comprehensive Traditional Chinese translation and guide based on the classic text by Eric S. Raymond and Rick Moen. Its core purpose is to teach programmers, developers, and technology users how to ask technical questions effectively in hacker and open-source communities to maximize their chances of getting useful answers. 

The repository details main capabilities and best practices, such as conducting prior research (using search engines, reading manuals and FAQs), selecting appropriate forums like Stack Overflow or project mailing lists, writing descriptive titles, and providing precise problem descriptions accompanied by minimal reproducible test cases. It targets software developers, system administrators, and open-source users navigating technical support channels. The guide emphasizes technical communication norms using standard plain text formats and explicitly discourages vague queries, demanding instant fixes, or claiming unverified bugs.

name: vim-plug
description: :hibiscus: Minimalist Vim Plugin Manager
summary: vim-plug is a minimalist plugin manager for Vim and Neovim designed for fast, parallel installation and updates. Built with a single-file architecture and no external dependencies, it provides an intuitive syntax to manage plugins, tags, branches, commits, and custom directories. Its primary capabilities include shallow cloning to minimize disk space, on-demand loading via commands or file types, post-update execution hooks, and tools to review and rollback updates. It is intended for Vim and Neovim users seeking an efficient and stable configuration workflow. Notable technologies utilized include Git, Vim script, and Lua.

name: refine
description: A React Framework for building  internal tools, admin panels, dashboards & B2B apps with unmatched flexibility.
summary:
Refine CORE is an open-source React meta-framework designed for building enterprise, CRUD-heavy web applications such as admin panels, dashboards, internal tools, B2B apps, and customer-facing storefronts. Its headless architecture decouples business logic from UI and routing, providing industry-standard hooks and components for authentication, access control, routing, networking, state management, and i18n. 

Intended for React developers building data-intensive applications, Refine CORE integrates seamlessly with any custom design or UI framework, offering built-in support for TailwindCSS, Ant Design, Material UI, Mantine, and Chakra UI, alongside platform support for Next.js, Remix, React Native, and Electron. Notable technologies and capabilities include React Query for state management and mutations, Server-Side Rendering (SSR) support, real-time application support, audit logs, document versioning, and connectors for over 15 backend services such as REST API, GraphQL, Supabase, Firebase, Strapi, Hasura, Appwrite, and Airtable.

name: DragGAN
description: Official Code for DragGAN (SIGGRAPH 2023)
summary:
Drag Your GAN (DragGAN) is a project for interactive point-based image manipulation on the generative image manifold, presented at SIGGRAPH 2023. It enables users to precisely "drag" image points to desired locations, controlling pose, shape, expression, and layout of GAN-generated images across categories such as objects, animals, humans, and landscapes. 

The repository provides a Python implementation utilizing PyTorch and builds upon StyleGAN3 and StyleGAN-Human architectures. Main capabilities include a Gradio-based web demo, a graphical user interface (GUI), scripts to download pre-trained model weights (including StyleGAN2, StyleGAN-Human, and Landscapes HQ datasets), and Docker support for deployment. Intended users include researchers, developers, and creators working with generative image models and computer vision. Real image editing is supported through prior GAN inversion techniques.

name: jq
description: Command-line JSON processor
summary: `jq` is a lightweight, flexible, and portable command-line JSON processor written in C with zero runtime dependencies. Akin to tools like `sed`, `awk`, and `grep`, it is designed for developers and system administrators to easily slice, filter, map, and transform structured JSON data. The project relies on technologies such as portable C, Docker, libtool, make, automake, autoconf, and Oniguruma.

name: DeepSeek-Reasonix
description: A reliable coding agent for complex software engineering tasks.
summary:
Reasonix is a reliable, config-driven coding agent designed for complex software engineering tasks, maintained by Huahui Yu. Built as a single Go binary, it provides a local engine accessible through multiple interfaces including a terminal (CLI/TUI), a desktop application called Reasonix Studio, a browser interface, and editor integrations over ACP (Agent Client Protocol). 

Main capabilities include plan modes, runtime permissions, a workspace sandbox, cache-aware context maintenance, and per-turn checkpoints with rewind functionality. It supports multi-model and composable configurations (such as DeepSeek and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and allows running separate executor and planner models. Extensibility is supported via MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and the Extension Protocol v1, enabling custom tools, prompts, resources, runtime event interception, and UI extensions.

Intended users include developers and software engineers seeking autonomous yet controllable assistance for coding tasks. Notable technologies utilized include Go (1.25+), Node.js (24+), pnpm (10), and the MIT license.

name: lottie-android
description: Render After Effects animations natively on Android and iOS, Web, and React Native
summary: Lottie for Android is a mobile library that parses Adobe After Effects animations exported as JSON using Bodymovin and renders them natively on mobile devices. Designed for developers and mobile application designers, the library enables teams to ship complex vector animations directly into applications without manual recreation. Main capabilities include native mobile rendering of exported vector graphics and support for Lottie-Compose. Notable technologies utilized include Gradle, AndroidX, and Android Studio.

name: UTM
description: Virtual machines for iOS and macOS
summary:
UTM is a full-featured system emulator and virtual machine host for iOS and macOS, enabling users to run operating systems like Windows and Linux on Mac, iPhone, and iPad. Built using QEMU, it supports over 30 processors—including x86_64, ARM64, and RISC-V—and provides VGA graphics via SPICE and QXL, text terminal mode, USB device support, and JIT-based acceleration using QEMU TCG. 

On macOS, UTM additionally features hardware-accelerated virtualization utilizing Hypervisor.framework and QEMU, alongside the ability to boot macOS guests using Virtualization.framework on macOS 12+. The project also includes UTM SE, a slowed-down edition utilizing a threaded interpreter that executes without requiring jailbreaking or JIT workarounds, supporting ARM, PPC, RISC-V, and x86 architectures. Intended for developers and general users seeking virtualization and emulation on Apple devices, UTM features native frontends designed for macOS and iOS using modern APIs.

name: awesome-react-native
description: Awesome React Native components, news, tools, and learning material!
summary:
Awesome React Native is a curated, maintenance-checked list of libraries, tools, frameworks, and learning resources designed for building modern applications with React Native and Expo. 

The repository provides a structured directory categorized into AI-assisted development tools (such as MCP servers, agents, and on-device AI inference with ExecuTorch and llama.rn), UI components, navigation solutions, state management libraries, storage and database options, networking tools, services, payments, testing frameworks, and debugging utilities. Notable technologies featured include React Native, Expo, Reanimated, Skia, MMKV, and SQLite. 

Intended for mobile and web developers building cross-platform applications, the project helps users discover reliable, actively maintained packages and open-source production apps—such as Bluesky and Joplin—while offering comprehensive learning materials and community updates.

name: koa
description: Expressive middleware for node.js using ES2017 async functions
summary:
Koa is an expressive HTTP middleware framework for Node.js designed to make web applications and APIs more enjoyable to write. Its middleware stack flows in a stack-like manner, allowing developers to execute actions downstream and filter or manipulate responses upstream. 

Core capabilities include content negotiation, normalization of Node inconsistencies, redirection, and default error handling. Koa integrates only common HTTP server methods into its small codebase and is not bundled with any middleware. It provides encapsulated `Context`, `Request`, and `Response` objects that delegate to Node's native `IncomingMessage` and `ServerResponse` to maintain a clean interface and robust stream handling.

Intended for Node.js developers building web applications and APIs, Koa requires Node v18.0.0 or higher to support ES2015 features and async functions.

name: zellij
description: A terminal workspace with batteries included
summary: Zellij is a terminal workspace and multiplexer designed for developers, ops-oriented users, and terminal enthusiasts. It balances simplicity out of the box with advanced capabilities such as deep customizability, personal automation via layouts, true multiplayer collaboration, unique user experience features like floating and stacked panes, and a plugin system supporting any language that compiles to WebAssembly. Additionally, Zellij features a built-in web-client that makes a terminal optional. It is targeted at both beginner and power users. The project is implemented in Rust (using Cargo for installation and development builds) and is released under the MIT license.

name: manifesto
description: The OpenTF Manifesto expresses concern over HashiCorp's switch of the Terraform license from open-source to the Business Source License (BSL) and calls for the tool's return to a truly open-source license.
summary: The OpenTF Manifesto aims to ensure Terraform remains truly open source by urging HashiCorp to return the project to a fully open license and prevent community fragmentation. It introduces the OpenTF fork, hosted in the opentffoundation/opentf repository, to maintain an open-source alternative. The initiative targets the Terraform user and developer community, providing a roadmap toward a stable release for the fork.

name: ai-website-cloner-template
description: Clone any website with one command using AI coding agents
summary:
The AI Website Cloner Template is a project designed to recreate any website as a clean, modern Next.js application using an AI coding agent with a single command. Intended for developers, creators, and learners, it supports platform migration, recovering lost source code, and studying production layouts and behaviors. 

The project operates through a multi-phase pipeline executed by AI agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor. This pipeline includes reconnaissance (screenshots, design token extraction, and interaction sweeps), foundation setup, component specification writing, parallel building via git worktrees, and assembly with visual quality assurance.

The core technology stack consists of Next.js 16 utilizing the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS v4 with oklch design tokens, shadcn/ui built on Radix primitives, and Lucide React icons. The repository structure includes dedicated directories for application routes, UI and custom components, public assets, research documentation, design references, and agent skill definitions.

name: HowToLiveLonger
description: 程序员延寿指南 | A programmer's guide to live longer
summary: The "Programmer Life Extension Guide" is a repository aimed at helping developers live longer and spend less time working through evidence-based health data. It systematically analyzes and aggregates scientific literature regarding all-cause mortality (ACM) and life expectancy. The project outlines actionable inputs—such as consuming white meat, vegetables, chili peppers, nuts, coffee, tea, and specific supplements like spermidine and glucosamine, while avoiding ultra-processed foods, sugar-sweetened beverages, smoking, and excessive alcohol—alongside outputs including racket sports, regular tooth brushing, baths, and targeted sleep durations. Additionally, it examines contextual factors like body weight, socioeconomic status, and emotional health. Intended for software developers and individuals seeking longevity insights, the repository references numerous academic studies, clinical trials, and public health databases (such as JAMA, BMJ, Lancet, and Science) to quantify the impact of dietary, lifestyle, and environmental variables on human lifespan.

name: awesome-cto
description: A curated and opinionated list of resources for Chief Technology Officers, with the emphasis on startups
summary:
Awesome CTO is a curated and opinionated list of resources designed for Chief Technology Officers and VP R&D, with a specific emphasis on startups and hyper-growth companies. 

The repository's purpose is to provide guidance across various operational, managerial, and technical domains. Its main capabilities include collecting articles, guides, handbooks, and tools covering topics such as the CTO position, hiring and interviewing, people management, career growth, project management, development processes, architecture, technologies, data engineering, startups, technical due diligence, money and finance, product management, and marketing. 

Intended users are technical leaders, engineering managers, founders, and executives in software and technology organizations. Notable technologies, frameworks, and methodologies referenced throughout the resources include JavaScript, TensorFlow, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Scrum, Agile, CI/CD, DevOps, RESTful APIs, and microservices.

name: buzz
description: A hive mind communication platform
summary:
Buzz is a self-hostable team workspace built around a Nostr relay where humans and AI agents share rooms, communicate, and collaborate. Built primarily as a Rust workspace of focused crates, it treats every message, workflow step, review approval, and Git event as a signed event in a single audit trail. Agents act as full team members with their own cryptographic keys, channel memberships, and specific tools to open repositories, submit patches, execute code reviews, and run workflows.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Unified Event Log:** Combines conversation threads, Git events, media, and search into a single protocol.
- **Agent Integration:** Allows AI agents (such as Goose, Codex, and Claude Code via an Agent Client Protocol/ACP harness) to answer questions using historical context, triage bugs, review code, and execute release pipelines.
- **Project Workflows & Rooms:** Turns feature branches into dedicated channels where patches (via NIP-34), CI results, and review decisions reside together.
- **Media & Canvases:** Supports frame-anchored video comments and shared canvases.

**Intended Users:**
Developers and teams seeking a unified workspace to build alongside AI agents without relying on disjointed chat, forge, CI, and search tools.

**Notable Technologies:**
Rust, TypeScript, React, Tauri, Docker, PostgreSQL (with Full-Text Search), Redis, MinIO/S3, and Nostr protocol specifications.

name: QwenPaw
description: Your Personal AI Assistant; easy to install, deploy on your own machine or on the cloud; supports multiple chat apps with easily extensible capabilities.
summary:
QwenPaw (Qwen Personal Agent Workstation) is a personal AI assistant and Agent OS designed to be deployed locally or in the cloud. It features a three-layer memory architecture—including live working context, full verbatim history, and a self-evolving personal knowledge base powered by ReMe—to continuously convert conversations and resources into readable, editable, and searchable Markdown memory. 

Intended for general users and developers seeking a customizable, privacy-conscious digital assistant, QwenPaw supports local execution via the QwenPaw-Flash model series (2B, 4B, 9B), Ollama, and LM Studio, alongside over 14 cloud providers. Its main capabilities include multi-agent and parallel task execution, unified file workspace management, automated scheduling via cron and heartbeat, and integration across chat channels such as DingTalk, Lark, WeChat, Discord, and Telegram. Security is handled via a kernel-level sandbox, Tool Guard, File Guard, Skill Scanner, and Access Policies. The project also provides extensible capabilities through skills, plugins, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, a Terminal UI (TUI), and a web-based Console.

name: Python
description: My Python Examples
summary:
This repository provides a collection of Python scripts designed to reduce human workload, automate tasks, and serve as educational examples for beginners. The project offers practical utilities ranging from system administration and file management to web scraping, media downloading, and simple games. 

Notable capabilities and scripts include:
- **System and Network Operations:** Batch file renaming, directory management, environment checking, disk space and OS information reporting, log zipping, DNS lookups via `nslookup_check.py`, subnet pinging, server health checks, MAC address modification (`changemac.py`), and serial port scanning.
- **Web and Media Scraping:** Fast parallel YouTube downloading using `aria2c`, Google image retrieval, XKCD comic downloading, Google News headlines and live cricket scores via BeautifulSoup, and WhatsApp online status monitoring using Selenium and chat analysis using `matplotlib`.
- **Utilities and Entertainment:** A calculator, custom stopwatch, character counter, text-to-speech voice control for Windows programs (`JARVIS.py`), a terminal Twitter client (`tweeter.py`), a test case generator, and classic games like Blackjack and Space Invaders.

The repository is intended for beginners and users seeking Python automation tools. Technologies and libraries referenced include Python 3.10+, BeautifulSoup, Selenium, and Matplotlib.

name: fullPage.js
description: fullPage plugin by Alvaro Trigo. Create full screen pages fast and simple
summary:
fullPage.js is a simple and easy-to-use library for creating fullscreen scrolling websites (single-page or one-page sites) featuring landscape sliders nested inside sections. It supports touch navigation for mobile phones, tablets, and touch-screen computers, and is fully functional on modern browsers and IE 11. 

The project's main capabilities include auto-scrolling, vertical and horizontal scrolling transitions, lazy loading of media elements, auto-playing and pausing of embedded media (such as HTML5 video/audio and YouTube iframes), state classes, callbacks, methods, and a variety of configurable options like anchors, navigation dots, and responsive modes. Official wrapper components are available for Vue, React, and Angular. Intended users include web developers building interactive storytelling experiences, portfolio sites, or single-page applications. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript (Vanilla JS), jQuery, CSS3 transforms, flexbox, and optional module loaders like Webpack, Browserify, and Require.js.

name: langfuse
description: 🪢 Open source agent evals & observability: Trace, evaluate, and improve LLM applications with one open platform.
summary:
Langfuse is an open-source LLM engineering platform designed to help teams collaboratively develop, monitor, evaluate, and debug AI applications. 

Its main capabilities include LLM application observability for tracking calls, retrievals, embeddings, and agent actions; centralized prompt management with version control and server/client-side caching; evaluations supporting LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, and custom pipelines; datasets for structured testing and benchmarking; an interactive LLM playground; and a comprehensive API with typed SDKs for Python and JS/TS. 

The platform is intended for developers and teams building AI-powered applications, agents, and multi-agent systems. It integrates with popular frameworks and model providers such as OpenAI, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, LiteLLM, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, DSPy, and Ollama. Langfuse can be used via Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted locally using Docker Compose, on a single Virtual Machine, or via Kubernetes (Helm) and Terraform templates. It is built using the ClickHouse open source database.

name: husky
description: Git hooks made easy 🐶 woof!
summary:
Husky is a lightweight tool for managing native Git hooks, designed to improve commits and development workflows. Its main capabilities include supporting all 13 client-side Git hooks, branch-specific hooks, and POSIX shell scripting for advanced use cases. It leverages the Git feature `core.hooksPath` and aligns with npm best practices using the `prepare` script. 

Intended for developers and teams using Git across macOS, Linux, and Windows, Husky supports Git GUIs, Node version managers, custom hook directories, nested projects, and monorepos. Notable technical characteristics include a size of approximately 2 kB gzipped with zero dependencies, fast execution running in roughly 1ms, opt-in/opt-out options, and user-friendly error messages.

name: airllm
description: AirLLM 70B inference with single 4GB GPU
summary:
AirLLM is a Python library that dramatically reduces inference and training memory usage for large language models, allowing massive models (such as 70B to 671B parameters) to run on low-end commodity hardware and small VRAM GPUs (like a single 4GB or 12GB card) without quantization, distillation, or pruning. 

The project achieves this by streaming frozen model weights disk-to-GPU one decoder layer at a time. It supports popular open-source model families including Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, Gemma, ChatGLM, Baichuan, InternLM, Yi, and Kimi. Key capabilities include 4-bit and 8-bit block-wise weight quantization for faster inference speeds, dynamic layer prefetching, CPU inference support, macOS compatibility on Apple Silicon via MLX, and low-VRAM LoRA training where adapters remain resident while base layers stream. 

Intended for developers, researchers, and hobbyists with limited GPU resources, AirLLM provides a unified `AutoModel` interface compatible with Hugging Face models. Notable technologies and dependencies referenced include PyTorch, bitsandbytes, flash-attn, compressed-tensors, and MLX.

name: awesome-sysadmin
description: A curated list of amazingly awesome open-source sysadmin resources.
summary:
Awesome Sysadmin is a curated, open-source resource directory designed for system administrators, DevOps engineers, and IT professionals. The repository provides a comprehensive list of free and open-source software (FLOSS) and tools categorized across various domains of systems administration and infrastructure management. 

Its main capabilities span numerous operational categories, including automation, backups, configuration management, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD), control panels, distributed filesystems, DNS management, identity management (LDAP, SSO, and OAuth), log management, monitoring, networking, platform-as-a-service (PaaS), queuing, software containers, version control, virtualization, and VPN solutions. Notable technologies referenced throughout the curated list include Docker, Kubernetes, Ansible, Terraform, Proxmox, and WireGuard.

name: hackathon-starter
description: A boilerplate for Node.js web applications
summary:
Hackathon Starter is a boilerplate for Node.js web applications designed for rapid prototyping and ease of use in hackathons and general projects. It provides a structured MVC architecture, local and OAuth 2.0 authentication (supporting Google, Microsoft, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Twitch, GitHub, and Discord), user profile management, two-factor authentication (2FA), passkey/biometric authentication via WebAuthn, contact forms, file uploads, and device camera access. 

The project includes extensive API examples and boilerplates for backoffice tools (Lob, PayPal, QuickBooks, Stripe, Twilio), data and media integrations (Alpha Vantage, GitHub, Foursquare, Last.fm, New York Times, PubChem, Twitch, Tumblr, Steam, GIPHY), maps and location (Google Maps, HERE Maps), productivity (Google Drive, Google Sheets), and AI capabilities featuring a LangGraph ReAct AI agent, RAG pipelines, and support for foundational models via LangChain, Groq, and Hugging Face.
