Intended for developers seeking a jumpstart on web applications, the codebase is built with Node.js, Express, Mongoose, Pug, Bootstrap 5.3, and Sass, utilizing MongoDB for data persistence and session storage. It also includes testing frameworks like Mocha, Chai, and Playwright.

name: nativefier
description: Make any web page a desktop application
summary:
Nativefier is a command-line tool designed to easily create native-looking desktop applications for any website with minimal configuration. Targeted at developers and users who want standalone desktop wrappers for web services like WhatsApp Web or Messenger, the tool packages websites into OS-compatible executables (`.app`, `.exe`, etc.) for Windows, macOS, and Linux. 

Main capabilities include the automatic retrieval of app names and icons, and the injection of custom JavaScript and CSS via a robust API and command-line flags. Optional integration supports tools like ImageMagick or GraphicsMagick for icon conversion and Wine for cross-platform Windows app building. Nativefier is built using Node.js and npm, and wraps web applications using Electron with Chromium under the hood. It can also be run via Docker, Snap, or AUR packages. Note that the repository is currently unmaintained.

name: seaweedfs
description: SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for object storage (S3), file systems, and Iceberg tables, designed to handle billions of files with O(1) disk access and effortless horizontal scaling.
summary:
SeaweedFS is a simple and highly scalable distributed file system designed to store billions of files and serve them quickly. Its core purpose is to provide an S3 object store, a POSIX file system, and a lakehouse with S3 Tables under a single binary (`weed`) over identical data. 

Key capabilities include O(1) disk read and write complexity, active-active cross-cluster replication, transparent cloud tiering and caching, erasure coding for warm data, and full implementations of the S3 API, IAM, STS, and Iceberg/Lance REST catalogs. It supports various interfaces including FUSE, WebDAV, SFTP, and HDFS. Metadata can be stored in external systems like LevelDB, RocksDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Cassandra.

Intended users include data engineers, developers, and system administrators requiring a fast, scalable alternative to systems like HDFS, Ceph, or GlusterFS, particularly optimized for handling massive quantities of small files alongside large files. The project is primarily written in Go, utilizes a Raft consensus group for master nodes, and provides tools for deployment via Docker, Docker Compose, and Kubernetes with Helm.

name: jieba
description: 结巴中文分词
summary:
Jieba is a Python Chinese text segmentation module designed for NLP tasks, text analysis, and search engine indexing. Its primary purpose is to provide efficient and accurate Chinese word breaking, keyword extraction, and part-of-speech tagging. 

Main capabilities include four segmentation modes (Accurate, Full, Search Engine, and Paddle deep learning-based mode), support for Traditional Chinese, custom dictionary loading and dynamic word frequency adjustment, keyword extraction using TF-IDF and TextRank algorithms, token positioning, parallel processing via Python's multiprocessing module, and a command-line interface. It utilizes a prefix dictionary structure combined with a directed acyclic graph (DAG), dynamic programming, and a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) utilizing the Viterbi algorithm for unknown word recognition. 

Intended users include developers, data scientists, and search engine engineers working with Chinese text processing in Python. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced include Python, PaddlePaddle, Whoosh, and multiprocessing.

name: awesome-agent-skills
description: A curated collection of 1000+ agent skills from official dev teams and the community, compatible with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and more.
summary:
Awesome Agent Skills is a curated collection of real-world Agent Skills created by leading development teams and the community, designed to extend the capabilities of AI coding assistants and agent frameworks. The project purpose is to provide hand-picked, production-grade agent skills rather than bulk-generated AI content, helping engineering teams build, test, secure, deploy, and monitor applications efficiently.

Main capabilities include integration across major AI development tools—such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, and Windsurf—and organized collections spanning cloud architecture, test automation, web scraping, search, security auditing, CI/CD, marketing, design, and database management. Intended users are software engineers, site reliability engineers, product managers, security professionals, and AI application developers looking to enhance their coding agents with reliable domain expertise.

Notable technologies and platforms featured across the repository include Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, Cloudflare, Supabase, Firebase, Vercel, Netlify, Terraform, ClickHouse, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kubernetes, Docker, React, Next.js, and TypeScript, alongside dedicated MCP servers and specialized CLI tools.

name: kitty
description: If you live in the terminal, kitty is made for you! Cross-platform, fast, feature-rich, GPU based.
summary: kitty is a fast, feature-rich, cross-platform, GPU-based terminal emulator designed for users who spend a significant amount of time in the terminal. Developed by Kovid Goyal, the project provides a high-performance command-line environment leveraging GPU acceleration.

name: netty
description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework
summary:
Netty is an asynchronous event-driven network application framework designed for the rapid development of maintainable, high-performance protocol servers and clients. It provides robust capabilities for network programming, including support for native transports like `io_uring`. 

The framework is intended for developers and engineers building high-performance network applications. System requirements include Java 8 or newer (with Java 9 or newer required for the optional `io_uring` native transport), along with Apache Maven and OpenJDK for building. Netty also provides support for the Java Platform Module System (JPMS).

name: awesome-javascript
description: 🐢 A collection of awesome browser-side  JavaScript libraries, resources and shiny things.
summary:
Awesome JavaScript is a curated collection of browser-side JavaScript libraries, resources, and tools aimed at developers. The project provides an extensive directory categorized into package managers, loaders, transpilers, bundlers, testing frameworks, QA tools, MVC frameworks, templating engines, data visualization, utilities, UI widgets, animations, machine learning, and WebSockets. 

Notable technologies and tools referenced include npm, Yarn, Bun, webpack, Vite, TypeScript, React, Vue, Svelte, D3.js, Three.js, TensorFlow.js, Prisma, and Socket.io. It serves developers seeking libraries for storage, routing, security, internationalization, form validation, and full-text search, alongside reading materials and other awesome lists for continuous learning.

name: glide
description: An image loading and caching library for Android focused on smooth scrolling
summary:
Glide is a fast and efficient open-source media management and image loading framework for Android. Its primary purpose is to wrap media decoding, memory and disk caching, and resource pooling into a simple, easy-to-use interface focused on making list scrolling smooth and fast. 

Main capabilities include fetching, decoding, and displaying video stills, images, and animated GIFs, as well as resizing remote images. Glide provides a flexible API supporting custom network stacks, including a default `HttpUrlConnection`-based stack alongside optional integration libraries for Google's Volley and Square's OkHttp. 

Intended users are Android developers seeking a reliable tool to manage image loading and caching within their applications. Notable technologies mentioned include Android SDK, Gradle, Maven, R8, Proguard, Volley, and OkHttp.

name: the-way-to-go_ZH_CN
description: 《The Way to Go》中文译本，中文正式名《Go 入门指南》
summary:
《Go入门指南》是一本由国内编程爱好者发起并开源的中文翻译版 Go 语言学习教程。该书翻译自 Ivo Balbaert 所著的英文经典著作《The Way to Go》，旨在帮助国内编程爱好者和 Go 语言初学者克服语言障碍，更好地学习和掌握 Go 语言。

该项目内容已获得原作者授权，并根据当前 Go 语言版本对部分过时内容进行了适当修改。项目面向广大 Go 语言学习者与开发者，旨在壮大国内的 Go 语言学习群体。内容采用 CC BY-SA 3.0 License 许可协议授权，代码遵循 BSD 3-Clause License。

name: web-check
description: 🕵️‍♂️ All-in-one OSINT tool for analysing any website
summary:
Web-Check is a comprehensive, on-demand open-source intelligence (OSINT) and auditing tool designed to provide deep insights into the inner workings of any website. Intended for developers, security professionals, and website owners, it uncovers potential attack vectors, analyzes server architecture, examines security configurations, and identifies technologies used by a target site. 

Main capabilities include running diagnostics such as DNS lookups, SSL analysis, traceroutes, port scans, threat checks, performance metrics, and social presence evaluations. Users can deploy the application via Docker, Netlify, Vercel, Hostinger, Render, or run it directly from source. The project is built using Node.js, Yarn, and Chromium, featuring both a web-based graphical user interface (GUI) and a backend API. Optional integrations with external APIs like Shodan, Google PageSpeed, Cloudmersive, Tranco, and CertSpotter can be configured to expand its scanning capabilities and raise rate limits.

name: raylib
description: A simple and easy-to-use library to enjoy videogames programming
summary:
raylib is a simple, easy-to-use programming library designed for video game development, prototyping, tooling, graphical applications, embedded systems, and education. Inspired by the Borland BGI graphics library and the XNA framework, it targets developers seeking a straightforward, pure-coding approach to game programming. 

The library is written in plain C (C99) with no external dependencies and provides hardware acceleration through OpenGL (versions 1.1 through 4.3, and ES 2.0/3.0) alongside a standalone OpenGL abstraction layer (`rlgl`), a software renderer backend (`rlsw`), and a math module (`raymath`). Main capabilities include full 3D support with shapes, models, heightmaps, PBR materials, and skeletal animations (IQM, M3D, glTF), as well as shaders, post-processing, multiple font and texture formats, audio streaming (WAV, QOA, OGG, MP3, FLAC, XM, MOD), and VR stereo rendering. 

raylib supports multiple platforms including Windows, Linux, macOS, Raspberry Pi, Android, and HTML5 (WebAssembly), with bindings available for over 70 programming languages.

name: framework
description: Laravel is a web application framework with expressive, elegant syntax.
summary: Laravel is a web application framework featuring an expressive and elegant syntax designed to make development an enjoyable and creative experience. This repository contains the core code of the framework. Laravel aims to simplify common tasks used in web projects by providing main capabilities such as a simple and fast routing engine, a powerful dependency injection container, multiple back-ends for session and cache storage, database-agnostic schema migrations, robust background job processing, and real-time event broadcasting. It is intended for developers building web applications ranging from small projects to large, robust enterprise systems.

name: OCRmyPDF
description: OCRmyPDF adds an OCR text layer to scanned PDF files, allowing them to be searched
summary:
OCRmyPDF is a scriptable command-line tool that adds a searchable text layer to scanned PDF files and images. It generates validated PDF/A documents while preserving the exact resolution of original embedded images, optimizing file sizes, and accurately positioning OCR text below images to enable seamless copy and paste. 

Key capabilities include multilingual text recognition across more than 100 languages, automatic page deskewing and cleaning, metadata modification, input and output validation, and multi-core CPU parallel processing. It features a plugin interface supporting alternative engines such as Apple Vision Framework, EasyOCR, and PaddleOCR. 

Intended users include individuals and organizations seeking to process scanned documents, convert images to searchable PDFs, and automate document archiving workflows. Notable technologies utilized include Python, the Tesseract OCR engine, Ghostscript, and PDF/A standards.

name: qdrant
description: Qdrant - High-performance, massive-scale Vector Database and Vector Search Engine for the next generation of AI. Also available in the cloud https://cloud.qdrant.io/
summary:
Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine and vector database written in Rust, designed for AI applications, neural networks, and semantic-based matching. It provides a production-ready client-server architecture and Qdrant Edge for resource-constrained environments to store, search, and manage vectors with additional JSON payloads.

Main capabilities include dense, sparse, and multi-vector search, rich payload filtering, hybrid search using fusion strategies like Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), vector quantization, on-disk storage, distributed deployment with sharding and replication, faceting, recommendations, discovery, multitenancy, query planning, payload indexing, SIMD hardware acceleration, GPU support, asynchronous I/O via `io_uring`, and write-ahead logging. It also includes a Web UI and supports REST (OpenAPI 3.0) and gRPC interfaces.

Qdrant targets developers and organizations building AI applications, semantic search engines, recommendation systems, visual search, and extreme classification platforms. Official client libraries are available for Python, Rust, Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, .NET/C#, and Java, alongside community clients for Kotlin and PHP and pre-built agent skills for AI coding assistants.

name: btop
description: A monitor of resources
summary:
btop++ is a cross-platform command-line system resource monitor written in C++23. It serves as a continuation of bashtop and bpytop, displaying real-time usage and statistics for processors, memory, disks, network interfaces, processes, and GPUs. 

Main capabilities include a responsive, game-inspired UI with full mouse support, process filtering, tree views, signal sending, auto-scaling network graphs, disk I/O activity tracking, battery meters, and customizable color themes and layout presets. It supports hardware monitoring features such as CPU temperature, frequency, package power consumption in watts, and GPU utilization, power usage, and clock speeds for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel hardware.

The tool is intended for system administrators, developers, and general users seeking a feature-rich terminal monitor. It runs on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, and OpenBSD, utilizing technologies such as C++23, CMake, GNU make, and libraries like ROCm SMI for AMD GPUs and nvidia-ml for NVIDIA GPUs.

name: AnotherRedisDesktopManager
description: 🚀🚀🚀A faster, better and more stable Redis desktop manager [GUI client], compatible with Linux, Windows, Mac.
summary:
Another Redis Desktop Manager is a faster, better, and more stable desktop manager for Redis that is compatible with Linux, Windows, and macOS, designed specifically to avoid crashing when loading massive keys. 

Main capabilities include support for Redis Clusters, Sentinel, SSL/TLS, SSH tunnels (including private keys and clusters), ACLs, execution logs, memory analysis, key import/export, command line (CLI) arguments, and custom viewers. It handles multiple data formats and viewers such as RedisJSON, Protobuf, Msgpack, Java/Pickle, Brotli, Gzip, Deflate, TimeSeries, Vector, and Array. 

The project is intended for developers, database administrators, and engineers managing Redis instances. Built using Electron and Node.js, it provides both precompiled desktop packages and source-level development workflows for cross-platform deployment.

name: stb
description: stb single-file public domain libraries for C/C++
summary:
stb is a collection of single-file public-domain or MIT-licensed libraries for C and C++ designed for easy distribution and integration without external dependencies. Intended for developers building games, graphics applications, and general software, the project provides 21 lightweight libraries spanning graphics, audio, 3D rendering, utilities, user interfaces, parsing, game development, math, and miscellaneous tasks. 

Notable components include image loaders and writers (`stb_image.h`, `stb_image_write.h`), an image resizer (`stb_image_resize2.h`), a TrueType font text rasterizer (`stb_truetype.h`), and typesafe dynamic arrays and hash tables (`stb_ds.h`). Other modules include audio decoding and synthesis (`stb_vorbis.c`, `stb_hexwave.h`), rectangle packing (`stb_rect_pack.h`), Perlin noise (`stb_perlin.h`), fast sprintf formatting (`stb_sprintf.h`), text editor guts (`stb_textedit.h`), voxel and 3D rendering helpers (`stb_voxel_render.h`, `stb_dxt.h`, `stb_easy_font.h`), tilemap generators (`stb_tilemap_editor.h`, `stb_herringbone_wang_tile.h`), a C-like language lexer (`stb_c_lexer.h`), euclidean division (`stb_divide.h`), grid reachability (`stb_connected_components.h`), memory leak checking (`stb_leakcheck.h`), and recursive GLSL include support (`stb_include.h`).

name: detectron2
description: Detectron2 is a platform for object detection, segmentation and other visual recognition tasks.
summary:
Detectron2 is a PyTorch-based next-generation computer vision library by Facebook AI Research (Meta) that provides state-of-the-art detection and segmentation algorithms. As the successor to Detectron and maskrcnn-benchmark, it is designed for computer vision researchers and production applications. 

Main capabilities include panoptic segmentation, Densepose, Cascade R-CNN, rotated bounding boxes, PointRend, DeepLab, ViTDet, and MViTv2. The library supports faster training times, facilitates building modular research projects on top of its framework, and allows models to be exported to TorchScript or Caffe2 formats for deployment. It also provides a Model Zoo containing a large set of baseline results and pre-trained models.

name: changedetection.io
description: Best and simplest tool for website change detection, web page monitoring, and website change alerts. Perfect for tracking content changes, price drops, restock alerts, and website defacement monitoring—all for free or enjoy our SaaS plan!
summary:
changedetection.io is a self-hosted web page and JSON API change monitoring tool designed to detect content updates, price drops, and restocks in real time. It is intended for individuals, developers, and professionals in data science, journalism, and network security seeking to automate website surveillance. 

Main capabilities include visual element selection, interactive browser steps for logging in and handling forms, conditional triggers, scheduled watches, price and stock trend tracking, and AI-powered filtering and summaries. It supports change detection on PDF files and provides multi-service notifications via Apprise (including Discord, Email, Slack, Telegram, and Webhooks), alongside a full REST API and browser extensions.

Notable technologies used include Python, Docker, Playwright, WebDriver, Chrome, LXML, Jinja2, and Apprise. It supports LLM integrations through LiteLLM with providers like OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Ollama, and vLLM, and query tools such as XPath, CSS selectors, JSONPath, and jq.

name: C-Plus-Plus
description: Collection of various algorithms in mathematics, machine learning, computer science and physics implemented in C++ for educational purposes.
summary: The Algorithms - C++ is an open-source repository containing a wide variety of algorithms implemented in C++ covering computer science, mathematics, statistics, data science, machine learning, and engineering. Intended as a learning resource for educators, students, and developers, the project features well-documented, atomic source code relying solely on the Standard Template Library (STL) without external library dependencies. It adheres strictly to the C++17 standard to ensure portability across major operating systems—Windows, MacOS, and Linux—as well as embedded systems like ESP32 and ARM Cortex. The modular implementation and MIT License allow the functions to be easily studied, tested via built-in self-checks, and utilized in external applications.

name: k9s
description: 🐶 Kubernetes CLI To Manage Your Clusters In Style!
summary:
K9s is a terminal UI application written in Go designed to let users interact with, navigate, observe, and manage Kubernetes clusters. It continually watches clusters for changes and provides commands to interact with observed resources. 

Main capabilities include resource navigation, real-time logging, port-forwarding (including automated fast-forwards and WebSocket support), shell access into nodes via a nodeShell feature gate, HTTP endpoint benchmarking via integration with Hey, resource sanitizing via Popeye, custom view rendering through JSON parse expressions, resource jumps, command aliases, hotkeys, customizable plugins with inputs, and skinnable interfaces. 

Intended users are Kubernetes administrators, developers, and operators seeking a productive, keyboard-driven terminal interface to manage applications and resources in the wild.

Notable technologies used include Go (v1.23+), Docker, Kubernetes (preferring v1.28+), and various open-source libraries such as Hey for benchmarking and Popeye for cluster sanitization.

name: v2ray-core
description: A platform for building proxies to bypass network restrictions.
summary: Project V (V2Ray) is a set of network tools designed to help users build their own computer networks, secure network connections, and protect privacy. It provides capabilities for network security and privacy enhancement. The project relies on notable technologies including Go libraries such as gorilla/websocket, quic-go/quic-go, pires/go-proxyproto, seiflotfy/cuckoofilter, google/starlark-go, jhump/protoreflect, and inetaf/netaddr.

name: diffusers
description: 🤗 Diffusers: State-of-the-art diffusion models for image, video, and audio generation in PyTorch.
summary:
🤗 Diffusers is a modular Python library designed for state-of-the-art pretrained diffusion models to generate images, audio, and molecular 3D structures. Intended for researchers and developers, the project supports simple inference solutions as well as training custom diffusion models. 

The library centers around three core components:
- **Diffusion Pipelines:** Ready-to-run inference pipelines supporting tasks like unconditional image generation, text-to-image, text-guided image-to-image, inpainting, image variation, and super-resolution using models such as Stable Diffusion, ControlNet, unCLIP, DeepFloyd IF, Kandinsky, and DDPM.
- **Schedulers:** Interchangeable noise schedulers that allow users to tune diffusion speeds and output quality.
- **Models:** Pretrained building blocks that can be combined with schedulers to construct end-to-end diffusion systems.

Built primarily on **PyTorch**, 🤗 Diffusers emphasizes usability, customizability, and modular architecture over rigid abstractions.

name: mihomo
description: A simple Python Pydantic model for Honkai: Star Rail parsed data from the Mihomo API.
summary:
mihomo is a Python library providing Pydantic models with type hinting and autocompletion support for parsed Honkai: Star Rail data obtained from the Mihomo API. It is intended for developers building applications that consume player and character data from the game. 

The project's main capabilities include fetching user information for both API version 1 (`StarrailInfoParsedV1`) and version 2 (`StarrailInfoParsed`), generating asset URLs for icons, previews, and portraits, and utilizing built-in tools to remove duplicate characters or merge character data across API refreshes. It also supports data persistence workflows using formats like JSON and pickle. Notable technologies used include Python and Pydantic.

name: ntfy
description: Send push notifications to your phone or desktop using PUT/POST
summary:
**ntfy** is a simple HTTP-based publish-subscribe notification service that enables users to send push notifications to phones or desktops via PUT or POST requests from any computer. Designed for developers and general users who want to trigger alerts from scripts without mandatory sign-ups or fees, the open-source project supports self-hosting alongside its public service at ntfy.sh. 

Notable capabilities include sending and receiving alerts via a command-line interface, a web application, and dedicated open-source mobile clients. The ecosystem includes companion applications such as the open-source Android app and iOS app. 

The project is built using **Go** for the server backend and leverages technologies such as SQLite (`mattn/go-sqlite3`), Firebase Admin SDK, and `go-smtp`. The web application is built with **React** and **Material UI components**, utilizing Dexie.js for IndexedDB persistence, while the CLI is powered by `urfave/cli`. The software is dual-licensed under the Apache License 2.0 and the GPLv2 License.

name: mise
description: dev tools, env vars, task runner
summary:
mise (mise-en-place) is a command-line interface tool designed to manage development tools, environment variables, and project tasks within a single unified setup. Project configurations are declared via a `mise.toml` file, allowing developers to maintain consistent environments across shells, text editors, and continuous integration systems. 

Main capabilities include:
- **Dev Tools:** Installing and managing multiple versions of runtimes and packages such as Node.js, Python, Go, and hundreds of others on a per-project or global basis.
- **Environments:** Setting project-specific environment variables and loading `.env` files.
- **Tasks:** Executing build, test, and command workflows bundled with the appropriate tools and environment variables.
- **Bootstrap:** Declaring machine setups, including system packages, dotfiles, and services.

Intended for developers and engineering teams, mise offers features like optional shell activation for automatic environment switching upon directory entry, execution wrappers without shell activation, exact version pinning, and lockfiles. Notable technologies mentioned include TOML, Node.js, Python, Go, and shell environments like Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell.

name: backstage
description: Backstage is an open framework for building developer portals
summary:
Backstage is an open-source framework designed for building developer portals by unifying infrastructure tooling, services, and documentation into a streamlined, end-to-end development environment. Created by Spotify and hosted by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), Backstage targets product teams and developers seeking to manage microservices, libraries, data pipelines, websites, and machine learning models while maintaining autonomy and shipping high-quality code quickly. 

Main capabilities include the Backstage Software Catalog for centralized asset management, Backstage Software Templates for rapidly spinning up new projects and standardizing tooling with organizational best practices, Backstage TechDocs for a "docs like code" approach to technical documentation, and an ecosystem of open-source plugins that expand customizability and functionality.

name: caffe
description: Caffe: a fast open framework for deep learning.
summary: Caffe is a deep learning framework developed by Berkeley AI Research (BAIR) / The Berkeley Vision and Learning Center (BVLC) and community contributors, designed with an emphasis on expression, speed, and modularity. It serves researchers and developers working on deep learning tasks, particularly in vision, by providing tools for fast feature embedding, tutorial documentation, reference models, and a model zoo. Notable technologies and custom distributions mentioned include Intel Caffe (optimized for CPUs and multi-node environments, particularly Intel Xeon processors), OpenCL Caffe (supporting AMD and Intel devices), and Windows Caffe. The project is released under the BSD 2-Clause license.

name: awesome-ai-research-writing
description: Elevate your AI research writing, no more tedious polishing ✨
summary:
This project is an open-source collection of prompt templates, agent skills, and best practices designed to improve AI-assisted academic writing for researchers. It aggregates writing techniques from top-tier research institutions and universities to lower the barrier of prompt engineering and agent skill utilization in paper writing.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Prompt Library:** Provides structured, production-ready prompts for LaTeX and Word environments covering translation, abbreviation, expansion, expression polishing, logic checking, anti-AI tone rewriting, architecture diagram generation, experiment plot recommendations, figure/table caption generation, experiment analysis, and reviewer-perspective self-review.
- **Agent Skills:** Integrates extension packages for AI coding agents (such as Cursor and Claude Code) via OpenSkills to streamline tasks like end-to-end machine learning paper drafting, format migration across conferences, paper checklist verification, BibTeX reference management, LaTeX table generation, document co-authoring, and vector design illustration.

**Intended Users:** Academic researchers, graduate students, and scientists looking to optimize their prompt workflows and leverage AI agents for scientific writing and paper publication.

**Notable Technologies:** Utilizes LaTeX, Microsoft Word (`.docx`), OpenSkills, Cursor, Claude Code, and various large language models (such as Claude series, Gemini, and Qwen).

name: selenium
description: A browser automation framework and ecosystem.
summary:
Selenium is an umbrella project and web browser automation infrastructure providing a platform and language-neutral coding interface compatible with all major web browsers, adhering to the W3C WebDriver specification. Intended for developers contributing to the project or building browser automation bindings and tools, the repository supports multiple programming languages including Java, Python, Ruby, Rust, C#, and JavaScript. 

The project utilizes Bazel as its primary build and test tool, frequently wrapped with custom Rake tasks executed via a `./go` command. Development environments can be configured natively across platforms (such as macOS, Windows, and Linux) utilizing Bazelisk and Java JDK 17 or greater, or via alternative setups like GitPod, Dev Containers, and Docker images. Testing capabilities include language-specific suites, size and tag filters, and headless or virtual X-server execution. Notable technologies associated with the project infrastructure and tooling include Bazel, W3C WebDriver, Selenium Manager, Rake, Ruff, and Google Java Format.

name: Vibe-Trading
description: "Vibe-Trading: Your Personal Trading Agent"
summary:
Vibe-Trading is an open-source personal trading agent and quantitative research workspace designed to bridge natural-language prompts with market data, backtesting engines, automated strategy generation, institutional analysis tools, and portfolio monitoring. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- **AI Agent Core & Swarm Teams:** Supports natural-language market queries, document/chart reading, persistent cross-session memory, self-evolving skills, and 30 multi-agent collaboration teams (e.g., investment, quant, crypto, and risk committees).
- **Cross-Market Backtesting & Data Sourcing:** Provides 10 dedicated backtesting engines supporting A-shares, Hong Kong, US, Canada, UK, India, Korea, Vietnam equities, crypto, futures, forex, options portfolios, and cross-market composites. It integrates with 28 automated market-data sources with smart fallback routing (including Tushare, AKShare, Yahoo, OKX, CCXT, Moongate/Mootdx, and local files).
- **Alpha Zoo & Quantitative Research:** Houses 462 pre-built quant alphas (across Qlib158, Kakushadze 101, GTJA 191, academic, and PIT fundamental factor libraries) with IC/IR metrics, purity gating, and a Strategy Development Manager for strategy lifecycles.
- **Institutional Valuation & Metrics:** Delivers automated DCF, comparable company analysis (comps), three-statement projections, Brinson-Fachler attribution, risk x-rays, and over 300 tested financial functions via a dedicated `quantlib` library.
- **Broker & Portfolio Integration:** Connects to 18 broker profiles (such as IBKR, Robinhood, Alpaca, OKX, Binance, Futu, eToro, and MT5) to provide unified read-only multi-broker portfolio aggregation, asset-valuation snapshots, and bounded mandate-gated trade execution.
- **Delivery & Integrations:** Exports strategies to TradingView Pine Script, TDX, and MetaTrader 5 (MQL5), provides a 75-tool Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and bridges chats into 16 instant messaging channels (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Feishu, etc.).

**Intended Users:** Quantitative researchers, algorithmic traders, developers building automated financial agents, and individual investors looking for natural-language driven portfolio simulations and backtesting.

**Notable Technologies:** Python

name: SmartTube
description: Browse media content with your own rules on Android TV
summary:
SmartTube is a free and open-source media client designed for Android TVs and TV boxes. It provides a TV-optimized interface to browse and play content from public sources, featuring SponsorBlock integration, adjustable playback speed, support for resolutions up to 8K at 60fps, HDR compatibility, live chat viewing, and customizable buttons. The application does not require Google Services and operates independently of official app stores.

Intended users are owners of Android-based televisions, TV boxes, and streaming sticks such as Amazon FireTV (models prior to October 2025), NVIDIA Shield, and Chromecast with Google TV. It is not optimized for or supported on smartphones, tablets, or non-Android platforms like Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, or Apple TV. 

Notable technologies and integrations utilized include AV01, VP9, and AVC video codecs, SponsorBlock for skipping sponsored segments, and optional bridge applications for system voice search integration.

name: openpose
description: OpenPose: Real-time multi-person keypoint detection library for body, face, hands, and foot estimation
summary:
OpenPose is a real-time multi-person system designed to jointly detect human body, hand, facial, and foot keypoints (totaling 135 keypoints) from single images. Authored and maintained by researchers at the CMU Perceptual Computing Lab, the project provides whole-body 2D pose estimation, single-person 3D pose reconstruction via multi-view triangulation, a camera calibration toolbox, and single-person tracking. 

The software supports multiple input sources including images, videos, webcams, Flir/Point Grey cameras, and IP cameras, while outputting visualized displays, files in formats such as JSON, XML, or YML, and custom data arrays. Intended for researchers and developers, OpenPose offers a command-line demo alongside C++ and Python APIs for custom pipeline integration. 

Notable technologies used include CUDA for Nvidia GPUs, OpenCL for AMD GPUs, CPU-only fallback options, and a Unity Plugin for cross-platform integration. Operating systems supported include Ubuntu, Windows, Mac OSX, and Nvidia TX2.

name: etcher
description: Flash OS images to SD cards & USB drives, safely and easily.
summary: Etcher is an OS image flasher built with web technologies designed to write OS images to SD cards and USB drives safely and easily. Its main capabilities include protecting users from accidentally writing to hard drives, ensuring data is written correctly with byte verification, and directly flashing Raspberry Pi devices that support USB device boot mode. The project is intended for users seeking a reliable flashing utility across Linux, Windows, and macOS operating systems. Etcher is developed by the balena.io team and provides installers and package repository support for Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat, Fedora, Arch, and Manjaro Linux, alongside Windows package support via WinGet and Chocolatey.

name: ChatDev
description: ChatDev 2.0: Dev All through LLM-powered Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary:
ChatDev 2.0 (DevAll) is a zero-code multi-agent orchestration platform designed for developing diverse applications through simple configuration. Building upon its legacy iteration—ChatDev 1.0, a virtual software company model utilizing intelligent agents like CEOs and programmers for automated software development lifecycles—ChatDev 2.0 empowers users to define customized agents, workflows, and tasks without writing code. 

The platform facilitates complex orchestration scenarios, including data visualization, 3D generation (via Blender and blender-mcp), game development, deep research, and video generation. It supports multi-agent collaboration frameworks such as MacNet (using directed acyclic graphs) and evolving orchestration topologies. 

Intended users include software developers, innovative entrepreneurs, and researchers exploring large language model (LLM) powered multi-agent systems. The technology stack comprises a FastAPI backend (`server/`), a Vue 3 and Vite frontend (`frontend/`), runtime agent abstractions (`runtime/`), and workflow orchestration configurations (`yaml_instance/`), with support for deployment via `uv`, Docker, and a Python SDK (`chatdev`).

name: CLIP
description: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining),  Predict the most relevant text snippet given an image
summary:
CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training) is a neural network trained on a variety of image and text pairs, capable of predicting relevant text snippets for a given image using natural language instructions. Designed for zero-shot prediction and representation learning in computer vision, it matches the performance of traditional supervised models like ResNet50 on datasets such as ImageNet without requiring task-specific labeled training examples. 

The project provides a Python package built with PyTorch and TorchVision. Its main capabilities include loading pre-trained models via `clip.load()`, tokenizing text with `clip.tokenize()`, encoding images and text into feature embeddings using `model.encode_image()` and `model.encode_text()`, and computing cosine similarity logit scores. It supports zero-shot classification and linear-probe evaluation workflows combined with libraries such as scikit-learn and torchvision datasets like CIFAR-100. Intended users include machine learning researchers and developers working on multimodal computer vision and natural language processing tasks.

name: MonitorControl
description: 🖥 Control your display's brightness & volume on your Mac as if it was a native Apple Display. Use Apple Keyboard keys or custom shortcuts. Shows the native macOS OSDs.
summary:
MonitorControl is a macOS application designed to control external and built-in display brightness, volume, and contrast directly from the menubar or via keyboard shortcuts, including native Apple media keys. It displays native on-screen display (OSD) elements and provides smooth brightness transitions. 

The project supports multiple protocols, including DDC/CI for hardware-level control on external LCD displays, native Apple protocols for built-in and Apple displays, Gamma table control for software dimming, and shade control for AirPlay, Sidecar, DisplayLink, and virtual screens. It allows for combined hardware and software dimming, full black dimming, ambient light sensor synchronization, and synchronized controls across multiple displays.

Intended for macOS users managing external monitors or televisions, the application offers an unobtrusive user interface and extensive customization options. Built using Xcode, it incorporates tools like SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, and BartyCrouch, alongside third-party dependencies including MediaKeyTap, Settings, SimplyCoreAudio, KeyboardShortcuts, and Sparkle.

name: zapret-discord-youtube
summary:
This repository provides a tool for bypassing DPI (Deep Packet Inspection) blocks to restore access to restricted services such as Discord and YouTube on Windows systems. Built as an alternative distribution of the original `zapret` project by bol-van, the repository utilizes WinDivert for network traffic interception and filtering. Its purpose is to help users test, configure, and automate various circumvention strategies (including ALT and FAKE profiles) via batch scripts (`general.bat` and `service.bat`). 

Main capabilities include managing automatic service installation, filtering traffic by games or IP sets, running diagnostics and strategy tests, updating domain and IP lists (`ipset-all.txt`), and automatically modifying the hosts file to support web versions and voice chats. Intended users are Windows desktop users seeking to overcome regional network restrictions. Notable technologies and components mentioned include WinDivert, Secure DNS (DNS over HTTPS), and batch script automation.

name: gold-miner
description: 🥇掘金翻译计划，可能是世界最大最好的英译中技术社区，最懂读者和译者的翻译平台：
summary:
掘金翻译计划是一个由社区驱动的项目，专注于将国外优质的互联网技术文章翻译为中文。其核心目的是为热爱新技术的新锐开发者提供一个学习、研究和交流高质量技术内容的平台。

该项目覆盖的技术与应用领域广泛，包括区块链、人工智能（AI/Deep Learning/Machine Learning）、Android、iOS、前端、后端、设计、产品、算法等，并收录了如 TensorFlow、GraphQL、React、Flutter、Next.js、WasmEdge 以及系统设计等多个官方文档与技术指南。项目主要面向广大软件开发者、设计人员和技术爱好者。贡献者通过协作完成文章的翻译与校对工作，共同推动开源技术知识的传播。

name: rustfs
description: RustFS is an open-source, S3-compatible high-performance object storage system supporting migration and coexistence with other S3-compatible platforms such as MinIO and Ceph.
summary:
RustFS is a high-performance, distributed object storage system built in Rust. Designed to provide memory safety and raw performance alongside S3 API compatibility and OpenStack Swift API support, it is optimized for big data, AI, and data lake workloads. 

Main capabilities include S3-compatible core operations, distributed and single-node deployment modes, versioning, WORM object lock, server-side encryption, IAM and OIDC/SSO authentication, lifecycle management, site replication, audit logging, and a web console. It also supports optional integrations such as SFTP, FTPS, WebDAV, OpenStack Keystone, and RustFS KMS (with Vault and AWS KMS backends).

Intended users include developers, enterprises, and cloud-native operators seeking a business-friendly, Apache 2.0-licensed object storage solution for edge, IoT, and large-scale cluster environments. Notable technologies utilized include Rust, Docker, Kubernetes Helm charts, Nix, and Prometheus/Grafana/Jaeger for observability.

name: github-chinese
description: GitHub 汉化插件，GitHub 中文化界面。 (GitHub Translation To Chinese)
summary:
GitHub 中文化插件 (GitHub Chinese Plugin) is a browser extension and user script designed to fully translate the GitHub user interface into Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. 

Its primary purpose is to localize GitHub elements—such as menus, titles, buttons, and time components—while offering intelligent regular expression matching and repository description translations. The project targets Chinese-speaking developers and users navigating the GitHub platform. 

Notable technologies used include Tampermonkey, Violentmonkey, and Macaque script managers, along with VS Code extension support, mutation observers, and CSS variables for dark theme compatibility.

name: formik
description: Build forms in React, without the tears 😭
summary: Formik is an open-source library designed to help developers build forms in React. Created by Jared Palmer and Ian White, Formik aims to simplify form state management, validation, and submission handling within React applications. The project is organized as a monorepo utilizing technologies such as Yarn for package management, TypeScript, Playwright for end-to-end testing, Changesets for release management, and TSDX for its zero-config TypeScript CLI and Rollup configuration. It is intended for React developers seeking a streamlined, efficient way to construct and manage complex web forms.

name: nginx-proxy-manager
description: Docker container for managing Nginx proxy hosts with a simple, powerful interface
summary:
Nginx Proxy Manager is a pre-built Docker application designed to provide users with an easy way to accomplish reverse proxying hosts with SSL termination. It aims to offer a low barrier to entry for self-hosters and administrators without requiring deep knowledge of Nginx or Let's Encrypt. 

Main capabilities include creating forwarding domains, redirections, streams, and 404 hosts via a secure admin interface, generating free SSL certificates using Let's Encrypt, or supplying custom SSL certificates. It also supports access lists, basic HTTP authentication, advanced Nginx configurations for super users, user management, permissions, and audit logs. 

Intended users range from beginners seeking a straightforward gateway to manage web services on a home network or server to advanced administrators requiring custom configurations. 

Technologies used include Docker, Nginx, Let's Encrypt, Node.js, and Tabler for the administrative interface.

name: poetry
description: Python packaging and dependency management made easy
summary:
Poetry is a Python packaging and dependency management tool designed to help developers declare, manage, and install project dependencies while ensuring consistent environments across systems. It replaces traditional files such as `setup.py`, `requirements.txt`, `setup.cfg`, `MANIFEST.in`, and `Pipfile` with a unified `pyproject.toml`-based format. 

Main capabilities include deterministic dependency resolution, support for dependency groups and optional dependencies, script declarations, and project building via PEP 517 build-systems utilizing `poetry-core`. The tool targets Python developers and maintainers seeking streamlined package management. Notable technologies and formats referenced include Python, `pyproject.toml`, Git dependencies, and SemVer constraint matching. Related projects include `poetry-core`, `poetry-plugin-export`, and `poetry-plugin-bundle`.

name: JavaScript
description: Algorithms and Data Structures implemented in JavaScript for beginners, following best practices.
summary: The Algorithms - JavaScript is an open-source repository that implements various algorithms and data structures in JavaScript for demonstrative purposes. It serves as a community-driven educational resource where developers can contribute implementations, look up algorithm explanations via its wiki, and explore a categorized directory of available code. The project adheres to the standard.js code style and utilizes GitHub Actions and Codecov for continuous integration checks.

name: node-v0.x-archive
description: Moved to https://github.com/nodejs/node
summary: This repository serves as a historical archive for Node.js prior to its migration to the main `nodejs/node` repository. It preserves historical issues and pull requests relevant to Node versions v0.10 and v0.12 that were created before the move. New issues and pull requests for all branches are explicitly directed to the primary `nodejs/node` repository and will be automatically rejected if opened in this archive. The project utilizes technologies associated with early Node.js versions (v0.10 and v0.12) and is intended for developers referencing legacy issues, pull requests, and the pre-convergence version of the README.

name: fish-shell
description: The user-friendly command line shell.
summary:
Fish is a smart and user-friendly command-line shell designed for macOS, Linux, and other Unix-like systems, including Windows via WSL, Cygwin, or MSYS2. Its primary purpose is to provide an interactive and accessible shell experience with zero configuration required. 

Main capabilities include syntax highlighting, autosuggest-as-you-type, and tab completions that work out of the box. It also features a web-based configuration tool (`fish_config`), automated completion generation from manual pages, and system clipboard integration. 

Intended users are developers, system administrators, and general command-line users seeking an intuitive alternative to traditional shells like bash or zsh. 

Notable technologies used in its development and building include Rust (version 1.85 or later with Cargo), CMake, PCRE2, gettext, and Sphinx.

name: nps
description: 一款轻量级、高性能、功能强大的内网穿透代理服务器。支持tcp、udp、socks5、http等几乎所有流量转发，可用来访问内网网站、本地支付接口调试、ssh访问、远程桌面，内网dns解析、内网socks5代理等等……，并带有功能强大的web管理端。a lightweight, high-performance, powerful intranet penetration proxy server, with a powerful web management terminal.
summary:
NPS is a lightweight, high-performance intranet penetration proxy server featuring a powerful web management terminal. Its primary purpose is to expose internal networks and services through secure proxy connections. 

Main capabilities include comprehensive protocol support (TCP, UDP, HTTP/HTTPS, SOCKS5, P2P, and HTTP proxy), HTTPS integration with multi-certificate support, server and client-side control, domain name resolution features (custom headers, URL routing, site protection, and pan-resolution), and extension functions such as caching, compression, encryption, traffic limiting, bandwidth limiting, and port reuse. It also provides real-time traffic, bandwidth, and system information display alongside multi-user and user registration support.

The software offers full platform compatibility across Linux, Windows, macOS, and Synology, with straightforward system service installation. Most requirements can be configured simply through its web UI. Intended users include administrators and developers seeking robust intranet access and proxy management solutions.

name: swc
description: Rust-based platform for the Web
summary: SWC (Speedy Web Compiler) is a super-fast TypeScript and JavaScript compiler written in Rust. Designed to make web development faster, it functions as both a Rust library and a JavaScript library, providing tools such as an ECMAScript parser (`swc_ecma_parser`). It is intended for Rust and JavaScript developers seeking high-performance compilation and transformation capabilities as an alternative to tools like Babel. The project utilizes Rust (with a Minimum Supported Rust Version of 1.73) and Node.js (supporting Node v10+ for usage and v20+ for development), offering native npm packages with self-loading compressed addons across targeted architectures like x64 and arm64 on macOS, Windows MSVC, and Linux GNU/musl. SWC is distributed under the Apache License (Version 2.0).

name: oh-my-pi
description: ⌥ Coding agent with the IDE wired in. Built by Stencil Labs.
summary:
oh-my-pi (omp) is a coding agent and terminal-first IDE harness built by Stencil Labs as a fork of Pi. It provides an interactive TUI, SDK, RPC, and ACP interface where the IDE is wired directly into the agent. 

Main capabilities include over 60 model providers, 31 built-in tools (such as file operations, AST editing via ast-grep, grep, structural memory management, and browser/desktop interaction), integrated LSP operations, DAP-based debugging, parallel subagent task orchestration, persistent Python and JavaScript code execution cells, and live session collaboration. 

The intended users are developers seeking an all-in-one AI coding agent that runs natively across macOS, Linux, and Windows without relying on external core utils or slow fork-exec loops. 

Notable technologies used include TypeScript, Bun, and Rust (comprising crates like `pi-natives`, `pi-shell`, `pi-ast`, `pi-iso`, `pi-voice`, and `pi-walker`), utilizing N-API bindings, tree-sitter, and a vendored fork of brush-shell to execute shell utilities and grep routines in-process.

name: happy-llm
description: 📚 从零开始构建大模型
summary:
Happy-LLM is a systematic, open-source learning tutorial and practical project designed to help learners deeply understand the core principles, architecture, and training workflows of large language models (LLMs). 

The project purpose is to guide users from basic natural language processing (NLP) concepts and Transformer architectures (including attention mechanisms) to building, pre-training, fine-tuning, and evaluating an LLM from scratch. 

Main capabilities include implementing a complete LLaMA2 model, training tokenizers, executing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA/QLoRA), and exploring advanced practical applications such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI Agents, and agentic reinforcement learning (e.g., GRPO, OPD, Search-R1, ReTool). 

Intended users include university students, researchers, and LLM enthusiasts who possess Python programming experience and basic knowledge of deep learning and NLP. 

Notable technologies and frameworks used throughout the repository include Python, PyTorch, Transformers, ModelScope, and SwanLab.

name: ControlNet
description: Let us control diffusion models!
summary:
ControlNet is a neural network structure designed to add extra conditions to text-to-image diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion. The project works by duplicating neural network blocks into a locked copy—which preserves the original production-ready model—and a trainable copy that learns specific conditions using small datasets of image pairs without causing distortion. It introduces "zero convolution," a 1×1 convolution with weights and biases initialized to zero, ensuring training begins without altering output or requiring layers to be trained from scratch. 

Main capabilities include controlling diffusion models using diverse spatial and structural conditions such as Canny edges, M-LSD lines, HED boundaries, user scribbles, human poses, semantic segmentation, depth maps, and normal maps. It features a "Guess Mode" (non-prompt mode) that allows the encoder to interpret control maps without text prompts, supports combining multiple ControlNets for multi-condition control, and enables integration with community models. 

Intended users include AI researchers, developers, and digital artists seeking controllable image generation. Notable technologies utilized include Python, PyTorch, Gradio, and Hugging Face models.

name: k3s
description: Lightweight Kubernetes
summary:
K3s is a fully conformant, production-ready lightweight Kubernetes distribution packaged as a single binary under 100 MB, designed to run with half the memory footprint of upstream Kubernetes. It is well-suited for edge, IoT, CI, development, ARM architectures, and embedded environments. 

The project aims to stay as close as possible to upstream Kubernetes without diverging as a fork. It removes in-tree storage drivers and cloud providers to minimize binary size while bundling several core technologies into a single launcher: Containerd and runc for container runtime, Flannel for CNI, CoreDNS, Metrics Server, Traefik for ingress, Klipper-lb for service load balancing, Kube-router for network policy, Helm-controller for CRD-driven Helm deployments, Kine as a datastore shim, and local-path-provisioner for volume provisioning. K3s defaults to sqlite3 while also supporting etcd3, MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, and features automatic TLS certificate management, real-time local manifest auto-deployment, and secure node communications via websocket tunnels.

name: zxing
description: ZXing ("Zebra Crossing") barcode scanning library for Java, Android
summary:
ZXing ("zebra crossing") is an open-source, multi-format 1D/2D barcode image processing library implemented primarily in Java, with ports and wrappers available for numerous other languages. The project supports various barcode formats, including UPC-A, UPC-E, EAN-8, EAN-13, Code 39, Code 93, Code 128, Codabar, ITF, QR Code, Data Matrix, Aztec, PDF 417, MaxiCode, RSS-14, and RSS-Expanded. 

The repository contains several active modules such as `core` for image decoding and test code, `javase` for JavaSE client code, `android` for the Barcode Scanner client, `android-integration` for `Intent`-based support, `android-core` for shared Android code, alongside source files for `zxing.org` and the web-based barcode generator at `zxing.appspot.com`. The project is currently in maintenance mode, driven exclusively by contributed patches for bug fixes and minor enhancements, with no active roadmap.

name: learnGitBranching
description: An interactive git visualization and tutorial. Aspiring students of git can use this app to educate and challenge themselves towards mastery of git!
summary:
LearnGitBranching is an interactive Git repository visualizer, sandbox, and educational tutorial platform. Its primary purpose is to help beginner and intermediate developers understand and master version control concepts through dynamic commit tree visualization and gamified challenges. 

Key capabilities include a sandbox mode for free-form command experimentation, structured lesson levels featuring a "git golf" efficiency challenge, a built-in level builder, and support for shareable permalinks with custom command sequences. Users enter standard Git commands, and the nearby commit tree dynamically updates to reflect their effects. 

The project is intended for developers seeking to polish their Git skills. Technically, LearnGitBranching is a 100% client-side JavaScript application requiring no backend database or AJAX requests. It utilizes Vite for building and bundling, Jasmine for testing, and ESLint for correctness checks.

name: clipboard.js
description: :scissors: Modern copy to clipboard. No Flash. Just 3kb gzipped :clipboard:
summary:
clipboard.js is a modern, lightweight (3kb gzipped) JavaScript library designed to copy and cut text to the system clipboard without relying on Flash or bloated frameworks. 

The project provides a declarative API utilizing HTML5 data attributes (`data-clipboard-target`, `data-clipboard-action`, and `data-clipboard-text`) alongside an imperative API for dynamic configuration. It employs DOM event delegation for memory efficiency and fires custom `success` and `error` events to handle user feedback and application logic. Advanced options support dynamic target and text functions, custom containers for focused elements, and lifecycle cleanup via `.destroy()`. 

Intended for web developers seeking a simple, performant clipboard solution, the library relies on the browser Selection and `execCommand` APIs with graceful degradation for older browsers.

name: spring-boot-demo
description: 🚀一个用来深入学习并实战 Spring Boot 的项目。
summary:
The Spring Boot Demo project is a comprehensive collection of integration examples designed for deep learning and practical application of Spring Boot. It aims to provide developers with working implementations of popular enterprise technologies and libraries integrated into Spring Boot environments. 

Main capabilities include monitoring and logging with Actuator, Spring Boot Admin, Logback, and GrayLog; database access and ORM via JdbcTemplate, JPA, MyBatis, MyBatis-Plus, BeetlSQL, MongoDB, Neo4j, and multi-datasource configurations; caching using Redis and Ehcache; and messaging through RabbitMQ and Kafka. It also covers security and authentication with Spring Security (RBAC, JWT), Spring Session, and JustAuth for third-party logins; scheduling with Quartz and XXL-JOB; search engines via Elasticsearch; and API documentation with Swagger. Additional integrations feature Dubbo, Docker, WebSocket, Zookeeper for distributed locks, rate limiting (Guava and Redis + Lua), Flyway, and code generation.

Intended users are developers looking to learn, reference, or implement specific Spring Boot integrations. Notable technologies used include Java (JDK 1.8+), Spring Boot 2.1.0.RELEASE, Maven, MySQL, and various template engines (Freemarker, Thymeleaf, Beetl, Enjoy).

name: timesfm
description: TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model) is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for time-series forecasting.
summary:
TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model) is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for univariate and multivariate time-series forecasting. It features zero-shot generalist capabilities and native support for past-only and past-and-future dynamic covariates without requiring per-task tuning. 

The project's latest version, TimesFM 3.0, achieves top performance across major time-series benchmarks including fev-bench, TIME Benchmark, and GIFT-Eval. It supports continuous quantile forecasting, variable context lengths, and deployment integration via BigQuery ML, Google Sheets, and Vertex Model Garden. 

TimesFM is intended for data scientists, researchers, and enterprise users performing time-series analysis and forecasting. The repository provides code implementations supporting both a PyTorch backend and an MLX-native backend optimized for Apple Silicon. Key technologies utilized include Python, PyTorch, MLX, Hugging Face Transformers, and PEFT (LoRA) for fine-tuning. The source code is licensed under Apache-2.0, while TimesFM 3.0 pretrained weights are distributed under a non-commercial, non-production license (`timesfm-non-commercial-license-v1.0`), with commercial and production use permitted via authorized Google Cloud services.

description: 12306智能刷票，订票
summary:
This project is a 12306 train ticket-purchasing assistant implemented in Python (versions 3.6–3.7.4). Its primary purpose is to automate the ticket booking process for the China Railway 12306 platform. 

Main capabilities include automated CAPTCHA recognition (using local models or cloud-based captcha servers), automatic login, scheduled advance reservations, ticket scavenging ("捡漏"), smart waitlisting, and notification alerts via email and Server酱 (Server酱通知). 

The intended users are individuals seeking to streamline or automate the acquisition of train tickets for travel. Notable technologies and dependencies utilized within the project include Python, TensorFlow, Docker, and Docker Compose.

name: libpku
description: 贵校课程资料民间整理
summary:
libpku 是一个由学生民间整理的北京大学课程资料与攻略共享项目。其主要目的是汇集并公开各类课程相关资源，帮助学生避免重复劳动和弯路，将隐晦的口口相传资料转变为易于获取的共享内容。

该项目的主要能力与内容包括：
- 提供电子书、历年试卷、A4 纸复习资料及选课与考试攻略。
- 允许用户通过项目网站（lib-pku.github.io）直接访问和下载资料链接。
- 支持社区贡献，用户可以通过 GitHub Web 端上传文件、提交 Pull Request、开启 Issue 或发送电子邮件来补充或纠错资料，同时可在课程文件夹的 `README.md` 中撰写课程评价。

项目主要面向北京大学的学生及需要相关课程参考资料的学习者。

name: SillyTavern
description: LLM Frontend for Power Users.
summary:
SillyTavern is a locally installed user interface designed for AI hobbyists to interact with text generation LLMs, image generation engines, and text-to-speech voice models. It provides a single unified interface supporting multiple LLM APIs—including KoboldAI/CPP, Horde, NovelAI, Ooba, Tabby, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Claude, and Mistral—alongside integrations for Automatic1111 and ComfyUI. 

Key capabilities include a mobile-friendly layout, Visual Novel Mode, WorldInfo (lorebooks), customizable UI, auto-translate, extensive prompt options, and third-party extensions. The project is free, open-source under the GNU Affero General Public License, and contains no hosted online services or user tracking. Hardware requirements are minimal, needing only NodeJS 20 or higher to run locally on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android via Termux, or Docker.

name: ExplorerPatcher
description: This project aims to enhance the working environment on Windows
summary:
ExplorerPatcher is a Windows utility designed to enhance the operating system's working environment by restoring classic user interface elements. Its main capabilities include replacing the default taskbar with the Windows 10 taskbar style, switching to the Windows 10 Start menu, and enabling the Windows 10 Alt+Tab window switcher, alongside various other customizable configuration options managed through a dedicated properties interface. 

The project supports Intel, AMD, and Snapdragon (ARM64) processors via dedicated setup executables (`ep_setup.exe` and `ep_setup_arm64.exe`). It is intended for Windows users seeking to customize and optimize their desktop interface experience. Notable features include built-in update management and straightforward uninstallation methods through the Control Panel, Settings app, or command-line switches.

name: TaskMatrix
summary:
TaskMatrix connects ChatGPT with a series of Visual Foundation Models to enable sending and receiving images during chat sessions. It acts as an AI system capable of handling various tasks by combining the general language capabilities of LLMs with the domain-specific knowledge of visual experts. 

Key capabilities include talking, drawing, and editing images through integrated tools such as GroundingDINO, segment-anything, Stable Diffusion, and ControlNet. The project introduces templates—pre-defined execution flows created by humans—that allow ChatGPT to seamlessly assemble complex, multi-model tasks like infinity outpainting, object detection, and image segmentation without requiring additional training.

Intended for researchers and developers exploring task automation and multimodal AI, the project provides modular support for numerous visual foundation models spanning image captioning, question answering, depth estimation, edge detection, and pose estimation. Notable technologies utilized include Python, PyTorch, OpenAI APIs, and multiple state-of-the-art vision and diffusion models.

name: BetterDisplay
description: Unlock your displays on your Mac. Flexible HiDPI scaling, XDR/HDR extra brightness, virtual screens, DDC control, image adjustments, PIP/streaming, EDID override. More info -  betterdisplay.pro/guide
summary: BetterDisplay is a macOS application designed to give users comprehensive control over displays directly from the menu bar. Its main capabilities include flexible HiDPI scaling, XDR and HDR brightness upscaling, virtual screen creation, custom 3D LUTs, advanced image adjustments, DDC and HDMI-CEC hardware control, picture-in-picture window streaming, and display arrangement management. The tool is intended for Mac users managing single-monitor or complex multi-display setups, including headless Macs and remote access workflows. Notable technologies and protocols utilized include EDID, DPCD, DSC, HDMI-CEC, DDC, and a built-in CLI for automation and scripting integrations.

name: spaCy
description: 💫 Industrial-strength Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Python
summary:
spaCy is an industrial-strength library designed for advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Python and Cython, built for real-world production use. It targets developers and data scientists seeking high-speed, robust text processing capabilities. 

The library provides pretrained pipelines and supports tokenization and training for over 70 languages. Its core features include neural network models for part-of-speech tagging, dependency parsing, named entity recognition (NER), text classification, lemmatization, morphological analysis, entity linking, sentence segmentation, and custom component integration. It also supports multi-task learning with pretrained transformers like BERT, pretrained word vectors and embeddings, and integration with large language models (LLMs). Furthermore, spaCy includes a production-ready training system, built-in visualizers for syntax and NER, and tools for model packaging, workflow management, and GPU processing via CUDA. Custom models can be integrated using frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow.

name: WSL
description: Windows Subsystem for Linux
summary: Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) enables users to run Linux command-line tools, utilities, and applications unmodified and directly on Windows without the overhead of a traditional virtual machine or dual-boot setup. The project's main capability is allowing seamless integration of Linux environments within Windows via commands like `wsl --install`. It is intended for Windows users who need to execute Linux workflows. The repository ecosystem includes related projects such as WSL2-Linux-Kernel, WSLg for Linux GUI app support, and WSL documentation.

name: react-beautiful-dnd
description: Beautiful and accessible drag and drop for lists with React
summary: react-beautiful-dnd is a high-level list-based drag-and-drop abstraction library designed for React applications, providing a beautiful, natural, and accessible user experience. The project supports vertical and horizontal lists, movement between lists, multi-drag operations, item combining, virtual lists, tables, and nested structures, with inputs handling mouse, keyboard, touch, and custom sensors. Notable capabilities include robust screen reader support, auto-scrolling, unopinionated styling, server-side rendering (SSR) compatibility, and flexible item sizing. It is intended for React developers seeking to implement accessible list reordering and interaction patterns.

name: FreeCAD
description: Official source code of FreeCAD, a free and opensource multiplatform 3D parametric modeler.
summary:
FreeCAD is an open-source parametric 3D modeler designed for creating real-life objects of any size, making it suitable for product design, mechanical engineering, and architecture. Its capabilities include modifying designs through model history parameters, sketching geometry-constrained 2D shapes as a base for 3D objects, adjusting dimensions, and generating production drawings from 3D models. The project is intended for hobbyists, programmers, experienced CAD users, students, and teachers. 

FreeCAD is cross-platform, running on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Key underlying technologies include the OpenCASCADE geometry kernel, the Coin3D library for Open Inventor-compliant 3D scene representation, a broad Python API for scripting, and a graphical user interface built with Qt.

name: kafka
description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform
summary: Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform used for high-performance data pipelines, streaming analytics, data integration, and mission-critical applications. Built using Java (versions 17 and 25) and Scala (version 2.13), the project relies on Gradle as its build system and supports tools such as Checkstyle, SpotBugs, Spotless, and JMH for code quality checks and microbenchmarking. It targets developers and organizations building real-time data streaming infrastructure and applications.

name: carbon-lang
description: Carbon Language's main repository: documents, design, implementation, and related tools. (NOTE: Carbon Language is experimental; see README)
summary:
Carbon is an experimental successor programming language designed for C++ developers, focusing on performance-critical software, bidirectional C++ interoperability, and scalable migration. Built to address technical debt and modern requirements, Carbon delivers C++ matching performance via LLVM while introducing a modern generics system, checked definitions, and an incremental path toward memory safety. 

The project's main capabilities include seamless function and template-based interop with existing C++ codebases, robust governance, and a batteries-included open-source toolchain featuring a compiler, linker, libraries, and package manager. Intended users are C++ developers and organizations seeking a modern evolution path for large-scale, performance-critical codebases without rewriting entire software stacks. Notable technologies utilized include LLVM, Bazel, Clang, and LLD.

name: paper-reading
description: 深度学习经典、新论文逐段精读
summary:
This repository provides comprehensive, paragraph-by-paragraph video readings, notes, and discussions on influential deep learning papers from the past decade. The project covers a wide range of core topics including computer vision (CNN, Transformer, object detection, contrastive learning, video understanding), generative models, natural language processing (Transformer, Llama, GPT), systems (distributed training, ZeRO, Megatron-LM), graph neural networks, optimization algorithms, and advanced applications such as AlphaFold 2, Codex, and OpenAI Sora. 

Designed for researchers, students, and practitioners interested in artificial intelligence and deep learning, the repository serves as a curated reading list and educational resource for mastering seminal and cutting-edge machine learning literature.

name: tabby
description: Self-hosted AI coding assistant
summary:
Tabby is a self-hosted, open-source AI coding assistant designed as an on-premises alternative to GitHub Copilot. It operates as a self-contained server with no requirement for external database management systems or cloud services, featuring an OpenAPI interface for easy integration with existing infrastructures like Cloud IDEs and supporting consumer-grade GPUs. 

Designed for developers and engineering teams, Tabby offers code completion, an Answer Engine for internal knowledge retrieval, and integrations with repositories and merge requests from platforms like GitHub and GitLab. It provides extensions for popular IDEs including VSCode, Vim, and IntelliJ. Notable technologies and models integrated into the project include Docker, Rust, SQLite, Protobuf, Llamafile, StarCoder, Qwen, CodeGemma, CodeQwen, CodeLlama, and Codestral, alongside support for Apple Metal inference and CUDA devices.

name: awesome-gpt-image-2
description: Prompt as Code | GPT Image 2 / 2.5 提示词与案例库，530+ 个案例、20+ 套工业级模板与可复用 Skills，新增 2.5 同提示词对比专区，附完整提示词与生成记录，持续更新。
summary:
The project is an industrial prompt engine and template library called **GPT-Image2**, designed to transform community AI image generation prompts into structured "Prompt-as-Code" assets for automation workflows, agents, and batch production. 

**Project Purpose:**
The repository provides structured protocols and composable schemas (such as atomic breakdowns for subjects, lighting, materials, and layout) to achieve stable, controllable, and reusable AI image generation, moving beyond isolated prose-style prompts.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Over 500 reverse-engineered cases and 20+ industrial prompt templates categorized into UI/interfaces, charts/infographics, posters, products, brands, architecture, photography, illustration, characters, scenes, classical themes, and documents.
- Integration with GPT Image 2.5 spotlights (including Sunburst and Flare models) with side-by-side comparisons and prompt documentation.
- A visual web application for browsing galleries, filtering styles, and testing generations.
- An included agent skill (`gpt-image-2-style-library`) compatible with Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor via npm or GitHub Packages.
- Database schemas and migration scripts for Supabase user management, Stripe and Alipay billing, membership plans, and APIMart generation task integration.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, engineering teams, AI agents, and creators seeking structured, reusable prompt templates and automated workflows for AI image and video generation.

**Notable Technologies:**
- GPT-Image2 / GPT Image 2.5 (Sunburst, Flare)
- Supabase / PostgreSQL
- Stripe / Alipay billing APIs
- Node.js / npm
- Vercel deployment infrastructure

name: czkawka
description: Multi functional app to find duplicates, empty folders, similar images etc.
summary:
Krokiet is a free, open-source, multiplatform GUI application designed to remove unnecessary files from computers, succeeding the older GTK4-based Czkawka frontend. Built using the memory-safe Rust programming language, it leverages multithreading and efficient algorithms to provide fast performance and cache-supported secondary scans. 

The project encompasses multiple interfaces, including a CLI frontend, the core library (`czkawka_core`) for functional reuse, the Slint-based Krokiet and Android-focused Cedinia GUIs, and Python bindings. Intended for users seeking comprehensive system cleaning and optimization, Krokiet includes tools to find duplicates, empty folders and files, big files, temporary files, similar images and videos, music duplicates, invalid symbolic links, broken files, bad extensions, and bad names, alongside an Exif metadata remover and a video optimizer.

name: serenity
description: The Serenity Operating System 🐞
summary:
SerenityOS is a graphical, Unix-like operating system designed for 64-bit x86, Arm, and RISC-V architectures. It combines the aesthetic of late-1990s productivity software with the power-user accessibility of late-2000s Unix systems. 

The project features a modern 64-bit kernel with pre-emptive multi-threading, a comprehensive network stack supporting protocols like IPv4, TCP, UDP, DNS, HTTP, and TLS, POSIX-like virtual file systems including ext2, and good POSIX compatibility via a custom LibC and shell. It includes a built-in web browser with JavaScript and WebAssembly support, system services such as WindowServer and AudioServer, various development tools like the HackStudio IDE, and a rich collection of native GUI applications, games, and libraries built entirely from scratch. Intended for developers and power users seeking an independent, retro-styled yet modern computing environment, the system supports cross-compilation from Linux, macOS, and Windows with WSL2, running primarily inside QEMU.

name: codex-plugin-cc
description: Use Codex from Claude Code to review code or delegate tasks.
summary:
The Codex plugin for Claude Code integrates OpenAI's Codex into Claude Code workflows, allowing users to perform code reviews, delegate tasks, manage background jobs, and transfer sessions. Intended for users of Claude Code who want to leverage Codex capabilities, the plugin wraps the local Codex CLI and Codex app server, utilizing existing authentication and configurations from user or project-level `config.toml` files.

Main capabilities include:
- `/codex:review`: Conducts read-only code reviews of uncommitted changes or branches against a base.
- `/codex:adversarial-review`: Executes steerable reviews to pressure-test design choices, failure modes, assumptions, and alternative approaches.
- `/codex:rescue`: Delegates tasks such as bug investigation and patch implementation via the `codex:codex-rescue` subagent.
- `/codex:transfer`: Converts current Claude Code sessions into persistent Codex threads for seamless context handoff.
- `/codex:status`, `/codex:result`, and `/codex:cancel`: Manages and monitors background Codex jobs.
- `/codex:setup`: Verifies installations, authentications, and optional review gates.

Requirements include a ChatGPT subscription or OpenAI API key and Node.js 18.18 or later. Notable technologies referenced include Claude Code, Codex CLI, and the Codex app server.

name: motion
description: A modern animation library for React and JavaScript
summary:
Motion is an open-source, production-ready animation library designed for JavaScript, React, and Vue (formerly known as Framer Motion). Its project purpose is to deliver 120fps, GPU-accelerated animations by combining JavaScript control with native browser APIs. 

Main capabilities include a simple API with batteries-included features such as gestures, springs, layout transitions, scroll-linked effects, and timelines. It also offers Motion Studio—a visual animation editor—alongside AI integration features like Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, documentation indexes, and coding agent skills.
