Intended users are frontend developers and web designers looking to build smooth, high-performance web animations across multiple JavaScript frameworks. Notable technologies used include JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and Vue.

name: LeetCode-Go
description: ✅ Solutions to LeetCode by Go, 100% test coverage, runtime beats 100% | LeetCode 题解
summary:
This repository provides algorithm question solutions written in **Go (Golang)**, adhering strictly to the Google Golang Style Guide. The project serves as a practical resource for developers looking to sharpen their algorithmic skills, prepare for technical interviews at companies like Google, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Apple, and expand their knowledge of fundamental data structures and algorithms. 

The repository covers a wide spectrum of topics categorized into data structures—such as arrays, strings, linked lists, stacks, trees, heaps, hash tables, and tries—and algorithms, including dynamic programming, backtracking, binary search, sorting, bit manipulation, union find, sliding windows, segment trees, and graph theory. 

Additionally, the project compiles these solutions and explanations into an accompanying e-book titled *LeetCode Cookbook*, which is made available for online reading, progressive web application (PWA) installation, and offline PDF downloads. The code implementations are licensed under the MIT License, while the book content utilizes a Creative Commons license.

name: glances
description: Glances an Eye on your system. A top/htop alternative for GNU/Linux, BSD, macOS and Windows operating systems.
summary:
Glances is a cross-platform system monitoring tool written in Python. It provides real-time monitoring of system metrics including CPU, memory, disk, network usage, running processes, logged-in users, temperatures, voltages, fan speeds, and containers (such as Docker, LXC, and Podman). 

Designed for system administrators, developers, and AI assistants, Glances operates in standalone, client/server, and web modes with interfaces that include a terminal user interface (TUI), web UI, RESTful/XML-RPC APIs, and a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for direct AI querying. Stats can be exported to files, STDOUT, message brokers, and time-series databases like InfluxDB, Prometheus, Elasticsearch, and PostgreSQL. Glances can also be utilized as a Python library via the `glances.api` module.

Notable technologies used include Python, psutil, FastAPI, Uvicorn, and Docker. Installation is supported via PyPI, Pipx, uv, Docker, Homebrew, MacPorts, and native package managers.

name: awesome-awesomeness
description: A curated list of awesome awesomeness
summary:
"Awesome Awesomeness" is a curated list and directory of resources spanning a wide range of programming languages, general technologies, development practices, and specialized topics. The repository serves developers, engineers, and technology enthusiasts seeking structured collections of tools, libraries, frameworks, guides, and open-source projects. 

Covered programming languages and technologies include Ada, C/C++, Go, Java, JavaScript (along with frameworks like React, Angular, VueJS, and Node.js), Python, Rust, Swift, TypeScript, and numerous others. General topics encompass algorithms, artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, cloud platforms like Amazon Web Services (AWS), cybersecurity, databases, design patterns, DevOps, front-end and mobile development, machine learning, robotics, and system administration. The project organizes external GitHub repositories and documentation links into a comprehensive index without introducing proprietary tooling or executable code.

name: gpt-pilot
description: The first real AI developer
summary:
GPT Pilot is an AI-powered developer companion and code generation tool designed to research and demonstrate how Large Language Models (LLMs) can build fully working, production-ready applications with human oversight. Rather than generating an entire codebase at once, GPT Pilot operates iteratively through a team of specialized agents—including a Specification Writer, Architect, Tech Lead, Developer, Code Monkey, Reviewer, and Debugger—to write features step-by-step, review progress, and troubleshoot issues.

The project targets software developers and technical users looking for an AI pair programmer capable of scaling beyond simple scripts to build complete applications. It supports context-filtering mechanisms to manage large codebases efficiently across multiple development tasks.

GPT Pilot is implemented in Python and supports multiple LLM providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Groq, with configurable backend data storage using SQLite or PostgreSQL. It can be run as a standalone CLI tool or integrated into development environments via the Pythagora VS Code extension.

name: openclaude
description: runs anywhere. uses anything
summary:
OpenClaude is an open-source coding-agent command-line interface designed to work with both cloud-based and local large language model providers. It provides a terminal-first workflow supporting prompts, tools, agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP), slash commands, and streaming outputs. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Supports numerous backends and cloud APIs, including OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Google Gemini, GitHub Models, Codex OAuth, Ollama, Atomic Chat, and specialized partner gateways (such as AI/ML API, Concentrate, LLMTR, Command Code, ApiSmart, API Route, Hicap, Fireworks AI, LongCat, ClinePass, Gitlawb Opengateway, OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go, Xiaomi MiMo, NEAR AI, and Cloudflare Workers AI).
- Executes tool-driven coding workflows including bash execution, file read/write/edit, grep, glob, agents, tasks, and web tools (with DuckDuckGo, Ollama, and Firecrawl integrations).
- Features session management with conversation continuation, branching (forking), and non-interactive background sessions.
- Offers codebase intelligence via an auto-injected structural repository map ranked by PageRank importance.
- Includes a headless gRPC server for bidirectional streaming integration, a bundled VS Code extension for launch integration, and truecolor pixel-art terminal companions.

**Intended Users:**
Developers and technical users seeking a single, provider-agnostic terminal environment for AI-assisted coding and agentic workflows.

**Notable Technologies:**
TypeScript, Node.js, Bun, ripgrep, and gRPC.

name: AndroidUtilCode
description: :fire: Android developers should collect the following utils(updating).
summary:
AndroidUtilCode is a powerful, easy-to-use library for Android designed to improve development efficiency by encapsulating commonly used functions, complete with demos and unit tests. The project targets Android developers and supports API level 14 and above under the Apache-2.0 license. 

The library consists of two main modules:
- **utilcode**: Contains utilities commonly used in daily Android development.
- **subutil**: Contains less frequently used utilities that help simplify the main module.

name: easyexcel
description: 快速、简洁、解决大文件内存溢出的java处理Excel工具
summary:
EasyExcel is a Java-based Excel parsing and generation framework developed by Alibaba, designed to solve the high memory consumption issues common in traditional libraries like Apache POI and JXL. 

Project Purpose: 
EasyExcel provides an efficient, low-memory solution for reading, writing, and handling large Excel files without encountering OutOfMemoryError issues. It optimizes memory utilization by rewriting the parsing mechanism for the 07 version of Excel and wrapping the SAX-based model of the 03 version with simplified upper-layer model conversions.

Main Capabilities:
- Low memory consumption: Capable of parsing large datasets (e.g., reading 75MB files with 460,000 rows and 25 columns using minimal memory).
- Simplified reading and writing of Excel files via callback listeners and entity mapping.
- Support for web-based file upload and download operations through HTTP responses and multipart files.

Intended Users:
Java developers and enterprise applications requiring high-performance data processing and tabular data import/export capabilities.

Notable Technologies:
Java, Apache POI (underlying dependency), SAX parsing model, Maven.

name: anoma
description: Reference implementation of Anoma
summary:
This repository contains the implementation of the Anoma protocol. The project provides software to run an Anoma node, with support for deployment via pre-built binaries, source compilation, and Docker images. 

Main capabilities include running an Anoma instance via interactive or non-interactive shells, managing dependencies for node operation, and participating in the protocol's bi-weekly release development workflow. The intended users are developers, contributors, and operators working with the Anoma network and its specifications.

Notable technologies used in the implementation and build pipeline include Elixir, Rust, Protobuf (`protoc-gen-elixir`), Docker, CMake, OpenSSL, and ncurses.

name: vue-vben-admin
description: A modern vue admin panel built with Vue3, Shadcn UI, Vite, TypeScript, and Monorepo. It's fast!
summary:
Vue Vben Admin is a free, open-source middle and back-end front-end template and solution. Designed for developers and learners starting new projects, it provides an out-of-the-box architecture utilizing modern web technologies. 

Main capabilities include dynamic route-based permission generation, comprehensive built-in internationalization support, and customizable multiple theme colors. 

The project is built with notable technologies including Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. It targets modern web browsers and excludes Internet Explorer support.

name: shadowsocks
summary: The provided repository content was removed according to regulations, so no project details, capabilities, users, or technologies are available to summarize.

name: nuwa-skill
description: 你想蒸馏的下一个员工，何必是同事。蒸馏任何人的思维方式——心智模型、决策启发式、表达DNA。Distill how anyone thinks.
summary:
女娲.skill (Nuwa) is an open agent skill compatible with 50+ AI runtimes including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Gemini CLI. Based on the Agent Skills protocol, Nuwa automatically researches, distills, and verifies the cognitive frameworks of historical figures, industry leaders, and public icons (such as Steve Jobs, Elon Musk, Charlie Munger, Richard Feynman, and Naval Ravikant) into runnable perspective skills.

Rather than simple role-playing, Nuwa extracts a five-layer cognitive operating system: speech DNA, mental models, decision heuristics, anti-patterns/values, and honesty boundaries. The extraction pipeline uses parallel source collection across writings, podcasts, interviews, and timelines, followed by multi-criteria verification. 

The repository includes over a dozen pre-distilled person and topic skills (such as Paul Graham, Andrej Karpathy, Ilya Sutskever, and MrBeast) featuringfidelity scorecards. Nuwa is intended for developers, knowledge workers, and creators seeking to apply world-class cognitive models directly within their AI agent workflows. It is distributed under the MIT License.

name: vscodium
description: binary releases of VS Code without MS branding/telemetry/licensing
summary:
VSCodium provides scripts to automatically build Microsoft's `vscode` repository into freely-licensed, telemetry-free binaries under the MIT license with a community-driven default configuration. The project serves developers and users seeking a Free/Libre Open Source Software (FLOSS) alternative to Visual Studio Code for Windows, macOS, and GNU/Linux across architectures including x64, arm64, riscv64, loong64, and ppc64le. 

Rather than using the proprietary Microsoft extension marketplace, VSCodium integrates with `open-vsx.org` as an open-source extension registry. Notable underlying technologies include Electron, Node.js tooling, and CI workflows utilizing GitHub Actions to automatically generate daily builds when new Microsoft releases appear. Installation is supported through package managers such as Homebrew, WinGet, Chocolatey, Scoop, Snap, Flatpak, and the Arch User Repository (AUR).

name: x-algorithm
description: Algorithm powering the For You feed on X
summary:
This repository contains the core codebase for the X **For You** feed algorithm, which assembles and ranks posts per request by blending in-network content from followed accounts with out-of-network content discovered through machine learning and other mechanisms. 

The system operates via two primary pipelines: a Post Pipeline that handles candidate sourcing, pre-scoring filtering, scoring using multi-action probability prediction, final ranking, and post-selection filtering; and a Blending Pipeline that interleaves organic posts with ads, recommendations, and prompts. Out-of-network retrieval and ranking leverage systems such as Phoenix, SimClusters, and Thunder, supported by content understanding modules—including Grox, media-model-proxy, CLIP, Agatha, BDSM, and user-cred-v2—alongside visibility filtering rules governed by Scarecrow, botmaker, and abuse enforcement services. 

Intended for the public, developers, and researchers seeking transparency into post distribution, the repository highlights notable technical components such as transformer-based models implemented in JAX with Rust serving layers, determinantal point process reranking via `vm-ranker`, and an "Under the Hood" label transparency tool for auditing account visibility. The project uses Apache License 2.0.

name: oh-my-codex
description: OmX - Oh My codeX: Your codex is not alone. Add hooks, agent teams, HUDs, and so much more.
summary:
oh-my-codex (OMX) is a workflow and runtime layer for the OpenAI Codex CLI. It enhances Codex sessions by providing robust prompt wrappers, structured workflows, and state management under `.omx/`. OMX is primarily designed for macOS and Linux environments using Codex CLI, with secondary support for Windows via `psmux` or WSL2.

Main capabilities include:
- A canonical staged workflow consisting of `$deep-interview` for ambiguity clearance, `$ralplan` for architecture and consensus planning, and `$ultragoal` for durable multi-goal execution.
- `$team` for coordinated parallel execution across dedicated worktrees using tmux.
- Mission queue running (`omx mission`) for executing sequential prompt batches.
- Built-in utilities such as `omx doctor`, HUD monitoring (`omx hud`), sparkshell inspection (`omx sparkshell`), and a markdown-first project wiki (`omx wiki`).
- Scoped setup and agent guidance management via `AGENTS.md`.

Intended users are developers using the OpenAI Codex CLI who want structured task routing, dependable multi-step planning, and managed parallel execution. Notable technologies utilized include Node.js, TypeScript, Git worktrees, and `tmux`.

name: nacos
description: an easy-to-use dynamic service discovery, configuration and service management platform for building AI cloud native applications.
summary:
Nacos (Dynamic Naming and Configuration Service) is an easy-to-use platform designed for dynamic service discovery, configuration, and service management to help build cloud-native applications and microservices platforms. It supports services such as Dubbo, gRPC, Spring Cloud RESTful, and Kubernetes services.

Main capabilities include:
- **Service Discovery and Service Health Check:** Enables service registration and discovery via DNS or HTTP interfaces, alongside real-time health checks to prevent routing to unhealthy instances.
- **Dynamic Configuration Management:** Centralized and dynamic configuration management across all environments without requiring application redeployment.
- **Dynamic DNS Service:** Supports weighted routing for mid-tier load balancing, flexible routing policies, flow control, and DNS-based service discovery.
- **Service and MetaData Management:** Provides a service dashboard for managing metadata, configurations, Kubernetes DNS, and health metrics.

Intended users include developers and architects building cloud-native systems, microservices architectures, and distributed applications. Notable technologies integrated with Nacos include Dubbo, gRPC, Spring Cloud, and Kubernetes.

name: CheatSheetSeries
description: The OWASP Cheat Sheet Series was created to provide a concise collection of high value information on specific application security topics.
summary:
The OWASP Cheat Sheet Series is an Open Worldwide Application Security Project® (OWASP) initiative designed to provide good security practices for builders to secure their applications. The project offers a comprehensive collection of security cheat sheets authored as Markdown files, which serve as working sources for the official website. Intended users include application builders, developers, and security professionals seeking guidance on application security. 

The repository provides tools for local development and offline use, including an automated build available as a ZIP archive, local site generation using Make, and containerization support utilizing Docker and Podman with Python 3.x. Additionally, the project includes automated quality assurance workflows utilizing npm scripts for markdown and terminology linting.

name: remix
description: The fully-stacked web framework
summary:
Remix 3 is a web development framework focused on model-first development, deep alignment with standard Web APIs (such as Web Streams, Fetch API, and Web Crypto), runtime simplicity without heavy static analysis or build-step dependencies, and high composability. Its design emphasizes portability across runtimes like Node.js, Bun, Deno, and Cloudflare Workers. 

The repository consists of a single `remix` umbrella package alongside numerous independent, standalone JavaScript and TypeScript packages. Notable modules include utilities and components for authentication (`auth`), routing (`fetch-router`), schema validation (`data-schema`), typed relational queries (`data-table` supporting MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite), file storage (`file-storage` with S3 support), session management (`session`), HTTP and security middleware (CORS, CSRF, compression, logging), a component runtime with server rendering and browser hydration (`component`), and a built-in test framework (`test`). 

Intended for web developers building modern full-stack applications and tooling, Remix 3 offers a CLI (`cli`) for scaffolding apps and supports agent-driven workflows via built-in agent skills.

name: go-zero
description: A cloud-native Go microservices framework with cli tool for productivity.
summary:
go-zero is a web and RPC framework written in Go, designed to ensure the high availability and stability of high-concurrency microservices. It integrates extensive engineering practices and resilience mechanisms, such as chained timeout control, concurrency control, rate limiting, adaptive circuit breakers, and adaptive load shedding. 

The framework features `goctl`, a code generation and management tool that parses `.api` and `.proto` descriptions to automatically generate server-side Go code as well as client code for iOS, Android, Kotlin, Dart, TypeScript, and JavaScript. It also supports automatic request parameter validation, service discovery, load balancing, call tracing, and cache management. 

Intended for backend developers and engineers building scalable, resilient microservice architectures, go-zero facilitates AI-native development workflows through companion tooling projects like `ai-context`, `zero-skills`, and `mcp-zero` for assistants such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor.

name: github-mcp-server
description: GitHub's official MCP Server
summary:
The GitHub MCP Server connects AI tools, agents, assistants, and chatbots directly to the GitHub platform using natural language interactions. Its primary purpose is to enable repository management, issue and pull request automation, CI/CD and workflow intelligence, code analysis, security checks, and team collaboration. 

Main capabilities include browsing and querying repositories, managing files and commits, automating issues and PRs, monitoring GitHub Actions, handling Dependabot and code scanning alerts, configuring repository rulesets and custom properties, and interacting with GitHub Discussions, Gists, Projects, and Copilot features. Intended users are developers connecting AI tools to GitHub context.

Notable technologies and terms include Go, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Docker, GitHub Actions, Dependabot, GitHub Copilot, GitHub Enterprise Server, and GitHub Enterprise Cloud.

name: chatbot-ui
description: AI chat for any model.
summary:
Chatbot UI is an open-source AI chat application designed for general users to interact with artificial intelligence models. The project provides capabilities for managing chat data, supporting multi-modal use cases, and integrating with both cloud-based and local AI models. 

Notable technologies and tools utilized in the project include Next.js, Supabase (PostgreSQL), Docker, and Ollama for running local models. It also integrates with external AI providers such as OpenAI and Azure OpenAI. The application can be deployed locally using Docker and the Supabase CLI, or hosted in the cloud using platforms like Vercel combined with a remote Supabase backend.

name: tokio
description: A runtime for writing reliable asynchronous applications with Rust. Provides I/O, networking, scheduling, timers, ...
summary:
Tokio is an event-driven, non-blocking I/O runtime designed for writing reliable, fast, and scalable asynchronous applications using the Rust programming language. It leverages Rust's ownership, type system, and concurrency model to guarantee thread safety and minimize bugs while delivering bare-metal performance. 

Intended for Rust developers building high-performance network services, Tokio provides core runtime capabilities including a multithreaded work-stealing task scheduler, an OS event queue-backed reactor supporting epoll, kqueue, and IOCP, and asynchronous TCP and UDP sockets. The project ecosystem features related libraries such as `axum`, `hyper`, `tonic`, `warp`, `tower`, `tracing`, `mio`, `bytes`, and `loom`.

name: cursor
summary: Cursor is a software project available for download at cursor.com. It provides a platform for users to create new posts regarding bugs or feature requests on the official Cursor community forum, and includes designated guidelines for reporting security vulnerabilities privately via email.

name: certbot
description: Certbot is EFF's tool to obtain certs from Let's Encrypt and (optionally) auto-enable HTTPS on your server.  It can also act as a client for any other CA that uses the ACME protocol.
summary:
Certbot is an easy-to-use client developed as part of the Electronic Frontier Foundation's (EFF) effort to encrypt the internet by automating the acquisition and deployment of digital certificates. Its primary purpose is to fetch free certificates from Let’s Encrypt—or other ACME-compliant services—and deploy them directly to web servers. 

Main capabilities include supporting multiple web servers such as Apache 2.4+ and nginx/0.8.48+, as well as webroot and standalone modes. Certbot generates private keys locally, acquires domain-validated (DV) certificates, revokes certificates, supports ECDSA and RSA private keys, installs HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects, logs configuration changes for easy reversion, and provides full automation. 

Intended users are web administrators and server operators who have root or administrator access to command-line web servers. Notable technologies and specifications utilized include the ACME protocol (RFC 8555), Let's Encrypt, Apache, nginx, ECDSA, and RSA.

name: agents-course
description: This repository contains the Hugging Face Agents Course.
summary:
The Hugging Face Agents Course is an educational project designed to take learners from the basics of AI agents to a final assignment involving benchmarks. The course covers the definition of agents, Large Language Models (LLMs), fine-tuning LLMs for function-calling, frameworks for AI agents, agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), observability, evaluation, and agents in games. 

The main capabilities include learning how to build effective AI agents, trace and evaluate them, and participate in an automated evaluation leaderboard. The intended users are individuals with basic knowledge of Python and LLMs. Notable technologies and frameworks used throughout the course include Hugging Face, `smolagents`, `LangGraph`, and `LlamaIndex`.

name: WxJava
description: 微信开发 Java SDK ，支持包括微信支付，开放平台，小程序，企业微信，视频号，公众号等的后端开发
summary:
WxJava is a Java development SDK for WeChat back-end development. It provides comprehensive support for multiple functional modules, including WeChat Official Accounts (MP), WeChat Mini Programs (MiniApp), WeChat Pay, Enterprise WeChat (CP), WeChat Open Platforms (Open), and WeChat Channels (Channel). 

Designed for Java developers and backend service maintainers, WxJava simplifies the integration of WeChat ecosystem services into applications. The library is structured into modular components—such as `weixin-java-mp`, `weixin-java-pay`, and `weixin-java-miniapp`—which can be imported individually using Maven or managed collectively via a BOM dependency. It requires Java 8 or higher and leverages Lombok to simplify code compilation. Additionally, the repository includes a `skills` directory containing AI programming agent skills to assist users with module selection, integration, troubleshooting, and upgrade migrations.

name: heretic
description: Fully automatic censorship removal for language models
summary:
Heretic is a command-line tool designed for fully automatic censorship removal (safety alignment) in transformer-based language models without requiring expensive post-training or an understanding of transformer internals. 

The project's main capabilities include automated parameter optimization via Optuna using a TPE-based optimizer, which co-minimizes refusals and KL divergence from the original model to preserve intelligence. It supports dense models, several Mixture of Experts (MoE) architectures, multimodal models, and hybrid architectures like Qwen3.5. Features include hardware batch-size benchmarking, bitsandbytes model quantization, built-in model evaluation, and Hugging Face integration.

Heretic implements directional ablation (abliteration) by orthogonalizing transformer component matrices—specifically attention out-projections and MLP down-projections—with respect to residual directions. Residual directions are computed using difference-of-means between first-token residuals for harmful and harmless prompts. Key technical innovations include flexible ablation weight kernels, linear interpolation of float-valued residual direction indices across layers, and component-specific ablation parameters.

Intended users include AI researchers, developers, and practitioners looking to decensor language models via the command line. Notable technologies used include Python, PyTorch, Optuna, and uv.

name: surrealdb
description: A scalable, distributed, collaborative, document-graph database, for the realtime web
summary:
SurrealDB is a multi-model database built in Rust designed to unify document, graph, relational, time-series, geospatial, and key-value data models into a single engine. It features full-text, vector, and hybrid search, ACID transactions, real-time live queries, and an integrated API and authentication backend service with granular row-level permissions. 

Intended for application developers, data engineers, and AI agents, SurrealDB can be deployed as an embedded in-app library, run in browsers via WebAssembly, executed on the edge, or scaled out in distributed cloud clusters. It supports custom logic via embedded JavaScript functions and integrates with large language models through an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. SurrealDB provides official SDKs for Rust, JavaScript, Python, Golang, .NET, PHP, Java, and other platforms, utilizing its custom SQL-like query language, SurrealQL.

name: shadPS4
description: PlayStation 4 emulator for Windows, Linux, macOS and FreeBSD written in C++
summary:
shadPS4 is an early PlayStation 4 emulator written in C++ for Windows, Linux, and macOS. The repository provides the emulator core, while a separate QtLauncher is available for end-users seeking a graphical user interface. The project aims to execute PlayStation 4 titles and ELF files, with current support running games such as Bloodborne, Dark Souls Remastered, and Red Dead Redemption. 

Intended for users and developers interested in console emulation and reverse engineering, the software loads select official PlayStation 4 firmware modules and supports standard peripherals including keyboards, mice, and Xbox or DualShock controllers. The project is implemented in C++ and builds via Docker, Windows, Linux, and macOS environments. Notable technologies and design influences mentioned include a shader compiler patterned after yuzu's Hades compiler to handle modern AMD GPU emulation, alongside collaborative insights from projects like Panda3DS and fpPS4. The software is licensed under the GPL-2.0-or-later license.

name: hiddify-app
description: Multi-platform auto-proxy client, supporting Sing-box, X-ray, TUIC, Hysteria, Reality, Trojan, SSH etc. It’s an open-source, secure and ad-free.
summary:
Hiddify app is an open-source, ad-free, multi-platform proxy client based on the Sing-box tool-chain, designed to provide a secure and private way to access the internet. It targets everyday users seeking uncensored internet access across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux, with specific configuration suitability for regions like Iran, China, and Russia. 

Main capabilities include delay-based automatic node selection, TUN mode, remote profile management, automatic subscription updates, profile traffic and remaining-day displays, and a dark/light mode interface. It supports a wide range of protocols—including Vless, Vmess, Reality, TUIC, Hysteria, Wireguard, and SSH—as well as subscription link and configuration formats such as Sing-box, V2ray, Clash, and Clash Meta. The project is community-driven and compatible with all proxy management panels. Notable technologies utilized include Sing-box, Flutter, Go, Swift, and Kotlin.

name: modern-unix
description: A collection of modern/faster/saner alternatives to common unix commands.
summary:
Modern Unix is a curated collection of modern, fast, and user-friendly command-line tools designed as replacements or enhancements for traditional Unix utilities. Aimed at developers and system administrators, the repository highlights tools built in languages like Rust that improve standard workflows. 

Main capabilities include enhanced file viewing and listing (`bat`, `eza`, `lsd`), advanced searching and finding (`fd`, `ripgrep`, `fzf`), and improved system and process monitoring (`bottom`, `glances`, `gtop`, `procs`, `dust`, `duf`). It also features powerful Git and diff integrations (`delta`, `lazygit`), command-line HTTP clients and networking utilities (`httpie`, `curlie`, `xh`, `gping`, `doggo`), benchmarking (`hyperfine`), shell history navigation (`mcfly`), directory navigation (`broot`, `zoxide`), text manipulation and querying (`choose`, `jq`, `sd`), and quick documentation lookup (`cheat`, `tldr`).

name: brackets
description: An open source code editor for the web, written in JavaScript, HTML and CSS.
summary:
Brackets is a modern open-source code editor specifically designed for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript web development. Intended for web developers and programmers, the project is itself built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and runs as a desktop application within a thin native shell (brackets-shell) to access local files. 

Main capabilities include Quick Edit, an inline interface that surfaces context-specific code and tools to prevent clutter, and Live Preview, which synchronizes directly with web browsers to push code edits instantly and navigate between source code and browser views. The editor's text component is based on CodeMirror, and functionality can be further expanded using the Brackets Extension Registry.

name: podman
description: Podman: A tool for managing OCI containers and pods.
summary:
Podman is a daemonless container and pod management tool designed for OCI-compliant containers, pods, and volumes on Linux, macOS, and Windows. It provides full container lifecycle management—including creation, execution, checkpointing via CRIU, and removal—alongside image pulling, pushing, and building via a Docker-compatible CLI and REST API. Intended for developers and operators, Podman supports rootless execution utilizing user namespaces for enhanced security and resource isolation without requiring elevated privileges. 

The project incorporates technologies such as the libpod library for lifecycle APIs, Netavark and Aardvark-dns for networking, pasta for rootless networking, Buildah for container image builds, and runc or crun as OCI runtimes. It integrates with companion projects like Podman Desktop for GUI-based local environments and Skopeo for image storage operations.

name: mmdetection
description: OpenMMLab Detection Toolbox and Benchmark
summary:
MMDetection is an open-source object detection toolbox and benchmark based on PyTorch, and part of the OpenMMLab project. It features a modular design that allows users to easily construct customized frameworks by combining different components such as backbones, necks, and loss functions. 

The project supports multiple computer vision tasks out of the box, including object detection, instance segmentation, panoptic segmentation, and semi-supervised object detection. Notable methods and models included are RTMDet, MM-Grounding-DINO, Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN, DETR, and YOLOv3, among many others. MMDetection provides high execution efficiency with GPU-accelerated bounding box and mask operations. It is intended for researchers and engineers in computer vision seeking to implement standard models, train on custom datasets, or develop novel detection algorithms. The toolbox relies on foundational libraries like MMEngine and MMCV.

name: Proton
description: Compatibility tool for Steam Play based on Wine and additional components
summary:
Proton is a compatibility tool for the Steam client that enables Windows-exclusive games to run on Linux using Wine. It is primarily intended to be used directly through Steam, though the source code is available to advanced users who wish to alter Proton or use custom Wine versions. 

Main capabilities include building custom Proton distributions via Makefiles, Docker, or Podman (with rootless Podman recommended), installing local builds into Steam's compatibility tools directory, debugging via unstripped builds and symbol integration, and tuning runtime configurations for specific games using environment variables or configuration files. The tool supports rendering and synchronization options utilizing technologies such as DXVK, vkd3d-proton, wined3d, and Vulkan.

name: homepage
description: A highly customizable homepage (or startpage / application dashboard) with Docker and service API integrations.
summary:
Homepage is a modern, fast, secure, and fully proxied application dashboard designed to serve as a customizable start page and monitoring hub. It targets self-hosters and home server users seeking to organize bookmarks, view container statistics, and interact with various services. 

Main capabilities include quick search, web and service bookmarks, automatic Docker container status and service discovery via labels, and over 100 integrations with third-party applications (such as Plex, Jellyfin, Radarr, Sonarr, qBittorrent, and various self-hosted tools). It also provides utility and information widgets for weather, time, date, and system metrics. Homepage supports full internationalization with over 40 languages and offers extensive layout, theme, CSS, and JS customization. 

Built as a Next.js application, Homepage generates pages statically for performance while proxying backend API requests to protect sensitive keys. It provides official multi-architecture Docker images (AMD64, ARM64) and can be configured through YAML files or Docker labels. Optional authentication guards include built-in OIDC and password login flows.

name: numpy
description: The fundamental package for scientific computing with Python.
summary: NumPy is the fundamental package for scientific computing with Python. It provides a powerful N-dimensional array object, sophisticated broadcasting functions, tools for integrating C, C++, and Fortran code, and capabilities for linear algebra, Fourier transforms, and random numbers. The project is intended for developers and researchers engaged in scientific computing and data analysis using Python. Testing relies on pytest, with optional dependencies including Meson, Cython, and Hypothesis.

name: ML-From-Scratch
description: Machine Learning From Scratch. Bare bones NumPy implementations of machine learning models and algorithms with a focus on accessibility. Aims to cover everything from linear regression to deep learning.
summary:
Machine Learning From Scratch is a Python repository providing transparent, accessible implementations of fundamental machine learning models and algorithms. Rather than prioritizing maximal optimization or computational efficiency, the project emphasizes clarity regarding their inner workings. 

The codebase covers supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, and deep learning. Included implementations feature supervised techniques like Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, Gradient Boosting, and Multilayer Perceptrons; unsupervised methods such as K-Means, DBSCAN, Principal Component Analysis, Apriori, and Generative Adversarial Networks; reinforcement learning via Deep Q-Networks; and a deep learning module featuring customizable layers such as convolutional, pooling, recurrent, activation, and batch normalization layers. 

Intended for learners, developers, and practitioners seeking to understand foundational algorithms from the ground up, the project relies purely on Python and standard data science libraries to build these models without relying on high-level black-box machine learning frameworks.

name: fish-speech
description: SOTA Open Source TTS
summary:
Fish Speech (Fish Audio S2 Pro) is a state-of-the-art multilingual text-to-speech (TTS) and voice generation system. Designed for developers, researchers, and LLM agents, the project enables high-quality expressive speech synthesis, rapid voice cloning from short audio samples, native multi-speaker conversation generation, and multi-turn dialogue capabilities across over 80 languages.

The core of Fish Speech is its innovative Dual-Autoregressive (Dual-AR) architecture—comprising a 4B parameter slow AR transformer and a 400M parameter fast AR module utilizing RVQ audio codecs—which provides high audio fidelity and fast inference speeds. It incorporates Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for reinforcement learning alignment and supports fine-grained inline control of prosody and emotions through free-form natural language tags (e.g., `[whisper]`, `[excited]`). The project integrates natively with optimization frameworks like SGLang and vLLM-Omni for extreme streaming performance, achieving low latency and high throughput. Inference is available via command-line tools, a WebUI, Docker, and server APIs.

name: ShadowsocksX-NG
description: Next Generation of ShadowsocksX
summary:
ShadowsocksX-NG is a next-generation macOS graphical user interface client for Shadowsocks, developed in Swift. It aims to provide a lightweight and maintainable alternative to the original ShadowsocksX by separating the GUI from the core logic, running `ss-local` from shadowsocks-libev as a background Launch Agent service via `launchd`. 

The project is intended for macOS (10.12+) users seeking a proxy client with advanced routing and sharing capabilities. Main capabilities include support for SIP003 plugins (`kcptun`, `simple-obfs`, and `v2ray-plugin`), AEAD ciphers, HTTP proxying via `privoxy`, PAC file updates using GFW List from GitHub, custom PAC rules, a manual mode bypassing system proxy settings, and server profile sharing or importing via URLs, pasteboards, and screen QR codes. 

Building the project requires Xcode 12.5.1+ and CocoaPods 1.10.1+. It is released under the GPLv3 license.

name: yew
description: Rust / Wasm framework for creating reliable and efficient web applications
summary:
Yew is a modern Rust framework designed for creating multi-threaded, front-end web applications using WebAssembly. Intended for web developers building interactive client-side apps, Yew features a macro for declaring interactive HTML with Rust expressions, offering a developer experience similar to JSX in React. 

Main capabilities include high performance achieved by minimizing DOM API calls per page render, built-in support for offloading processing to background web workers, and JavaScript interoperability that enables developers to leverage NPM packages and integrate with existing JavaScript applications. The framework utilizes Rust and WebAssembly technologies.

name: Handy
description: A free, open source, and extensible speech-to-text application that works completely offline.
summary:
Handy is a free, open-source, and extensible cross-platform desktop application designed for privacy-focused speech-to-text transcription. It allows users to press a configurable keyboard shortcut to speak and instantly insert transcribed text into any active text field. Operating entirely offline on the user's computer, Handy requires no cloud connection and uses local speech processing.

Main capabilities include configurable recording shortcuts (hold-only, toggle-only, and tap modes), silence filtering via Silero Voice Activity Detection (VAD), and support for multiple transcription models such as Whisper models (Small, Medium, Turbo, and Large) with GPU acceleration and the CPU-optimized Parakeet V3 model. It works on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and includes integrations such as a Raycast extension, debug tools, and single-instance CLI parameters.

Intended for general users seeking privacy-first accessibility tooling and developers looking to extend an open-source transcription foundation, the project is built using technologies including Tauri, Rust, Whisper, ggml, and Silero.

name: floating-ui
description: A JavaScript library to position floating elements and create interactions for them.
summary:
Floating UI (formerly Popper) is a small library designed to help developers create floating elements such as tooltips, popovers, and dropdowns. Its main capabilities include anchor positioning across all platforms—which keeps floating elements anchored to target elements while avoiding viewport collisions—and user interaction hooks and components for building accessible floating UI components in React. 

The project is intended for web and mobile developers utilizing vanilla JavaScript, React DOM, React Native, Vue, or custom platforms like Canvas and WebGL. Built as a monorepo in TypeScript using pnpm workspaces, the codebase incorporates technologies such as Next.js SSG and Tailwind CSS for its website, Vite for bundling, and Playwright for visual testing.

name: echo
description: High performance, minimalist Go web framework
summary:
Echo is a high-performance, extensible, minimalist web framework built for Go and interoperable with Go's standard `net/http` library. It provides developers with a fast radix-tree router, an extensible middleware framework, request data binding for JSON, XML, and form payloads, centralized HTTP error handling, and template rendering capabilities. 

Designed for building robust and scalable RESTful APIs, Echo features route-level, group-level, and root-level middleware definition, optimized route prioritization, automatic TLS via Let's Encrypt, and HTTP/2 support. Notable ecosystem integrations include official and third-party middlewares for JWT, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Swagger, and various logging libraries such as Zap, Zerolog, and slog. 

The framework is intended for Go developers building web applications, microservices, and cloud backends. It is distributed under the MIT license.

name: sharp
description: High performance Node.js image processing, the fastest module to resize JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and TIFF images. Uses the libvips library.
summary:
Sharp is a high-speed Node-API module designed to convert large images in common formats into smaller, web-friendly JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, and AVIF images of varying dimensions. It supports all JavaScript runtimes providing Node-API v9, including Node.js (>= 20.9.0), Deno, and Bun. 

Built on top of libvips, resizing images with sharp is typically 4x to 5x faster than ImageMagick and GraphicsMagick while utilizing Lanczos resampling to maintain high quality. It correctly handles colour spaces, embedded ICC profiles, and alpha transparency channels. Beyond resizing, available operations include rotation, extraction, compositing, and gamma correction. Most modern macOS, Windows, and Linux systems require no additional installation or runtime dependencies.

name: awesome-php
description: A curated list of amazingly awesome PHP libraries, resources and shiny things.
summary: Awesome PHP is a curated, comprehensive list of PHP libraries, frameworks, components, tools, software, and learning resources intended for PHP developers. The repository serves as a directory covering dependency management, web frameworks like Laravel and Symfony, content management systems (CMS), database tools, testing frameworks, static analysis, security utilities, and deployment systems. Notable technologies and tools referenced include Composer, Doctrine, PHPUnit, PHPStan, ReactPHP, Swoole, and various deployment and cloud platforms like AWS and Serverless. It is designed to help developers discover production-ready packages and educational resources for building and maintaining PHP applications.

name: react-three-fiber
description: 🇨🇭 A React renderer for Three.js
summary:
@react-three/fiber is a React renderer for Three.js that enables developers to build 3D scenes declaratively using re-usable, self-contained components expressed in JSX. The project targets React and Three.js developers looking to build interactive 3D graphics, applications, and games. 

Key capabilities include zero runtime overhead, direct access to native Three.js elements and APIs, state management integration, and support for a render-loop via hooks like `useFrame`. It maintains full compatibility with standard Three.js features and updates without relying on wrapper updates. It supports both React DOM and React Native environments using technologies such as React, Three.js, JSX, and TypeScript.

name: cockroach
description: CockroachDB — the cloud native, distributed SQL database designed for high availability, effortless scale, and control over data placement.
summary:
CockroachDB is a cloud-native, distributed SQL database built on a transactional and strongly-consistent key-value store. Designed to build, scale, and manage modern, data-intensive applications, it provides horizontal scalability, fault tolerance that survives infrastructure failures with minimal latency, and support for strongly-consistent ACID transactions via a familiar SQL API. 

The database supports the PostgreSQL wire protocol, enabling users to connect via standard PostgreSQL client drivers and object-relational mapping (ORM) tools. Intended users include developers and administrators building resilient cloud or on-premise applications. CockroachDB can be deployed via managed cloud services (CockroachCloud), manually across multiple machines, or through popular open-source orchestration systems.

name: pytorch-tutorial
description: PyTorch Tutorial for Deep Learning Researchers
summary:
This repository provides tutorial code and examples designed for deep learning researchers to learn PyTorch. Most models are implemented concisely in fewer than 30 lines of code. 

The project covers four main categories:
1. **Basics**: PyTorch basics, linear regression, logistic regression, and feedforward neural networks.
2. **Intermediate**: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Deep Residual Networks (ResNet), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks, and RNN-based Language Models (RNN-LM).
3. **Advanced**: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Variational Auto-Encoders (VAE), Neural Style Transfer, and Image Captioning (CNN-RNN).
4. **Utilities**: TensorBoard integration with PyTorch.

Intended users are researchers and developers seeking practical, implementation-focused tutorials on deep learning architectures. The repository relies on Python (2.7 or 3.5+) and PyTorch (0.4.0+), alongside TensorBoard for utilities.

name: swr
description: React Hooks for Data Fetching
summary:
SWR is a React Hooks library for data fetching created by Vercel. Named after the stale-while-revalidate cache invalidation strategy, SWR first returns cached data before sending a request to revalidate and fetch up-to-date data. It aims to simplify data fetching logic for React and React Native applications while providing continuous and automatic data updates to UI components.

Main capabilities include fast, lightweight, and reusable data fetching, transport and protocol agnosticism, built-in caching, request deduplication, real-time experiences, polling, pagination, scroll position recovery, support for server-side rendering (SSR) and static site generation (SSG), local mutation (Optimistic UI), smart error retries, and React Suspense integration. 

The library is built with TypeScript and exposes a primary `useSWR` hook that accepts a unique identifier key and an asynchronous fetcher function, returning data, error, and loading states. It is intended for developers building reactive web and mobile interfaces who need robust state management and data synchronization capabilities.

name: hono
description: Web framework built on Web Standards
summary:
Hono is a small, simple, and ultrafast web framework built on Web Standards with zero dependencies. Its main purpose is to provide a unified API for developing web applications and APIs that can run unchanged across multiple JavaScript runtimes, including Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Deno, Bun, Vercel, AWS Lambda, Lambda@Edge, and Node.js. 

Main capabilities include a high-performance routing system utilizing `RegExpRouter`, `SmartRouter`, `LinearRouter`, and `PatternRouter`, a lightweight footprint (with the `hono/tiny` preset weighing under 12kB), and comprehensive middleware support encompassing built-in, custom, and third-party options. The framework is intended for developers seeking a high-performance, cross-platform routing solution with first-class TypeScript support and a clean API.

name: self-llm
description: 《开源大模型食用指南》针对中国宝宝量身打造的基于Linux环境快速微调（全参数/Lora）、部署国内外开源大模型（LLM）/多模态大模型（MLLM）教程
summary:
This project provides a comprehensive, beginner-focused Linux tutorial for deploying, using, and fine-tuning open-source large language models (LLMs). It aims to simplify the adoption of open-source models for students, researchers, and developers, covering over 50 mainstream models including LLaMA, ChatGLM, Qwen, InternLM, and DeepSeek.

Main capabilities include environment configuration guides, deployment and usage tutorials (spanning command-line calls, online demos, and LangChain integration), and fine-tuning methods such as full-parameter distributed training, LoRA, and P-Tuning. Dedicated sections offer specialized deployment and ROCm/Ascend NPU environment instructions for alternative hardware platforms like AMD GPUs, Ascend NPUs, and Apple Silicon. Intended users comprise students, NLP learners, and practitioners seeking to build domain-specific or private LLMs. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced include vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, MindIE, SGLang, and XTuner.

name: WindTerm
description: A professional cross-platform SSH/Sftp/Shell/Telnet/Tmux/Serial terminal.
summary:
WindTerm is a high-performance, cross-platform client designed for DevOps professionals, system administrators, and developers. It supports SSH v2, Telnet, Raw Tcp, Serial, and local shell protocols (including Windows Cmd and PowerShell, as well as Linux and macOS bash and zsh), alongside integrated SFTP/SCP clients, local file managers, and tmux integration. 

Intended for technical users managing remote and local environments, WindTerm offers a feature-rich graphical user interface with multilingual support, auto-completion, command palettes, sync input, split views, vim keybindings, and customizable color schemes. It implements advanced SSH capabilities such as agent forwarding, X11 forwarding, various authentication methods (including public-key, password, and GSSAPI), port forwarding, and HTTP/SOCKS5/Jump Server proxy support. Built with the WindEdit text component, the project emphasizes low latency, minimal memory usage through dynamic memory compression, and high-speed file transfers. It is available as a partial open-source project under the Apache-2.0 license, free for both commercial and non-commercial use.

name: Recordly
description: Create polished demo videos without editing skills. Mac/Windows/Linux
summary:
Recordly is an open-source desktop screen recorder and editor designed to create polished walkthroughs, demos, and product videos. Targeted at creators, developers, and product teams, it provides motion-driven presentation tools that eliminate the need to send raw footage to a motion designer. 

Main capabilities include automatic and manual zoom suggestions, smooth cursor polish and motion effects, dynamic webcam bubble overlays, and a drag-and-drop timeline editor supporting trims, speed adjustments, annotations, and crop-aware edits. Users can style final compositions with wallpapers, solid colors, gradients, blur, padding, drop shadows, and custom aspect ratios, and export projects to MP4 or GIF formats. It also features a community-driven extension system via the Recordly Marketplace.

Recordly runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Platform-specific integrations include native ScreenCaptureKit helpers on macOS, native Windows Graphics Capture (WGC) and WASAPI audio on Windows, and Electron-based capture on Linux. Scene composition during preview and export is handled by PixiJS. The application saves project states as `.recordly` files and is licensed under the AGPL 3.0.

name: claude-code-templates
description: CLI tool for configuring and monitoring Claude Code
summary:
Claude Code Templates (aitmpl.com) provides ready-to-use configurations, AI agents, custom slash commands, settings, hooks, model context protocols (MCPs), and reusable skills designed for Anthropic's Claude Code. The project aims to enhance developer workflows by offering over 100 domain-specific components—such as security auditors, performance optimizers, database integrations, and testing generators. 

Intended for developers using Claude Code, the repository includes a command-line interface distributed via npm (`claude-code-templates`) to install complete development stacks or individual components interactively. Additionally, it bundles developer tools such as Claude Code Analytics for real-time session monitoring, a mobile-optimized Conversation Monitor with Cloudflare Tunnel support, an installation Health Check utility, and a Plugin Dashboard.

Notable technologies utilized include Node.js, NPX, Cloudflare Tunnels, and various integrations (including GitHub, PostgreSQL, Stripe, AWS, and Bright Data MCPs). The project incorporates community and official contributions from sources such as Anthropic, K-Dense-AI, and Jesse Obra.

name: onyx
description: Open Source AI Platform - AI Chat with advanced features that works with every LLM
summary:
Onyx is a knowledge and context layer designed for teams and AI agents to index, search, and surface information from over 50 applications. It protects data sovereignty through flexible self-hosted, air-gappable deployments using Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and Terraform. 

Key capabilities include Agentic RAG (hybrid index and custom agent harness), Deep Research reports, Custom Agents, live Web Search (with providers like Serper, Google PSE, Brave, and SearXNG), external actions via MCP, a secure code execution sandbox, downloadable Artifacts, and Voice Mode (speech-to-text and text-to-speech). Onyx supports major proprietary and self-hosted LLM providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, LiteLLM, and vLLM.

Intended for users ranging from individual developers to large enterprises, Onyx provides access interfaces including a web and desktop app, Slack and Discord bots, an MCP server, a Chrome extension, and an embeddable widget. Enterprise features include Single Sign-On (Google OAuth, OIDC, SAML), SCIM user provisioning, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), analytics, query history auditing, and whitelabeling. The project is offered in a resource-efficient Lite mode and a Standard mode utilizing vector and keyword indexing, Redis, and MinIO.

name: signoz
description: SigNoz is an open-source, OpenTelemetry-native observability platform for your team and their AI agents. Get logs, metrics, and traces in one tool with features like APM, distributed tracing, log management, infra monitoring, etc. Combined with SigNoz MCP and a native AI teammate (in SigNoz Cloud) it helps you build more resilient apps.
summary:
SigNoz is an open-source observability platform built on OpenTelemetry, designed as an enterprise-grade alternative to fragmented monitoring stacks. It consolidates logs, metrics, traces, exceptions, alerts, and dashboards into a single tool to help engineering and operations teams debug production issues faster. 

Main capabilities include APM overview, log management, infrastructure and Kubernetes monitoring, distributed tracing, trace funnels, LLM and AI observability, and agent-native workflows utilizing a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Users can query data using a visual query builder, PromQL, or ClickHouse SQL. 

Intended users include developers, DevOps engineers, and SREs looking for full data plane control via self-hosted deployments (Docker, Kubernetes, Linux) or managed cloud options. Notable technologies utilized include OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, ClickHouse, and MCP.

name: MS-DOS
description: The original sources of MS-DOS 1.25, 2.0, and 4.0 for reference purposes
summary: This repository contains the original source code and compiled binaries for MS-DOS v1.25 and v2.0, as well as the source code for MS-DOS v4.00, which was jointly developed by Microsoft and IBM. Published for historical reference, the project aims to make these early PC operating system files easier to find, reference, explore, and experiment with. The repository is intended for individuals interested in early PC operating systems and historical reference. All files are released under the MIT License.

name: conductor
description: Conductor is an event driven agentic workflow engine providing durable and highly resilient execution engine for applications and AI Agents
summary:
Conductor is an open-source durable execution platform and workflow engine designed for microservices, AI agents, and adaptive workflow graphs. Originating at Netflix and maintained by Orkes and the community, it turns runtime choices—such as loops, branching, fan-out, tool calls, human approvals, retries, and cancellation—into durable, inspectable executions that survive system crashes and network failures. 

Main capabilities include explicit declarative orchestration, native LLM tasks, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calling, vector workflows for RAG, execution recovery, and dynamic runtime resolution of workflows and tasks. It supports polyglot workers written in Java, Python, Go, JavaScript, C#, Ruby, and Rust. Intended users are developers and operators building resilient, scalable distributed systems and autonomous AI agents. The platform offers self-hosted deployments with Apache 2.0 licensing, supporting multiple persistence backends (including Redis, Postgres, and MySQL) and message brokers. Notable technologies utilized include Docker, Node.js, Java, and Elasticsearch or OpenSearch. SDKs are available for major programming languages alongside CLI tools and terminal integrations for AI coding assistants.

name: refined-github
description: :octocat: Browser extension that simplifies the GitHub interface and adds useful features
summary:
Refined GitHub is a browser extension designed for developers and power users that simplifies the GitHub interface and adds a wide range of useful features and bug fixes. It supports standard GitHub and GitHub Enterprise across multiple browsers, including Chrome, Firefox, and Safari. 

The extension enhances repository management, file handling, code viewing, writing and reading comments, pull request workflows, commit histories, releases, profiles, and notifications. Key capabilities include making whitespace visible, displaying unreleased commits, linkifying references, auto-resizing textareas, showing reaction avatars, adding custom keyboard shortcuts, enabling one-click actions, and applying various UI and CSS fixes to address GitHub interface shortcomings.

name: QtScrcpy
description: Android real-time display control software
summary:
QtScrcpy is a lightweight, cross-platform desktop application designed to display and control Android devices (version 5.0 and above) via USB or network without requiring root privileges. It focuses on low latency, high performance (30–60 fps), high resolution, and quick startup times. 

Main capabilities include real-time screen mirroring, mouse and keyboard control, custom key mapping for games and apps, multi-device and group control, screen recording, screenshot capture, file transfer, APK installation, clipboard synchronization, and device audio forwarding (on Android 10+ using `sndcpy`). Wireless connections over a local area network are supported alongside USB connections.

Intended users include developers, gamers, and general users looking to manage or interact with Android devices directly from Windows, macOS, or GNU/Linux desktops. 

The project is built in C++ utilizing the Qt framework, OpenGL for video rendering, FFmpeg for video encoding, and ADB (Android Debug Bridge) for device communication. It serves as a Qt-based alternative to the original `scrcpy` project, providing custom GUI customization and asynchronous signal-slot processing.

name: fairseq
description: Facebook AI Research Sequence-to-Sequence Toolkit written in Python.
summary:
Fairseq is a sequence modeling toolkit designed for researchers and developers to train custom models for tasks such as translation, summarization, and language modeling. It provides reference implementations for various architectures including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), LSTMs, Transformers, and non-autoregressive Transformers, alongside self-supervised learning models like wav2vec and RoBERTa. 

Intended for machine learning researchers and developers, Fairseq supports multi-GPU and multi-machine training using data and model parallelism, gradient accumulation, mixed precision training with NVIDIA tensor cores, and full parameter and optimizer state sharding with CPU offloading. Notable technologies used include PyTorch, Python, Hydra for flexible configuration, and integration with xFormers and NVIDIA apex.

name: TrackersListCollection
description: 🎈 Updated daily! A list of popular BitTorrent Trackers! / 每天更新！全网热门 BT Tracker 列表！
summary:
XIU2/TrackersListCollection provides a daily-updated curated list of popular BitTorrent trackers designed to improve BitTorrent download speeds by helping users connect with other peers. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Offers multiple categorized tracker lists, including a best-performing list (`best.txt`), a comprehensive list (`all.txt`), HTTP(S)-only lists (`http.txt`), and non-HTTP lists (`nohttp.txt`).
- Provides lists formatted specifically for Aria2 (`*_aria2.txt`) alongside standard plaintext formats.
- Aggregates public trackers from sources such as ngosang/trackerslist, newtrackon.com, OpenTracker, and DeSireFire/animeTrackerList.

**Intended Users:**
BitTorrent users and download managers seeking to optimize and troubleshoot peer connections and download speeds.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Aria2
- BitComet
- qBittorrent / qBittorrent Enhanced Edition
- Motrix

name: material-design-lite
description: Material Design Components in HTML/CSS/JS
summary:
Material Design Lite (MDL) implements Material Design components using vanilla CSS, JavaScript, and HTML. It allows developers to add a Material Design look and feel to static content websites without relying on any external JavaScript frameworks or libraries. The project is optimized for cross-device use, gracefully degrades in older browsers, and is accessible out of the box. 

Intended for web developers looking to build or style websites, MDL supports modern browsers with full A-grade compatibility and provides CSS-only fallback experiences for B-grade environments like IE9. Notable technologies used include vanilla CSS, JS, and HTML, with distribution available via npm, CDNJS, and GitHub releases. The repository is currently in limited support, with core development having moved to Material Components for the web.

name: FinceptTerminal
description: FinceptTerminal is a modern finance application offering advanced market analytics, investment research, and economic data tools, designed for interactive exploration and data-driven decision-making in a user-friendly environment.
summary:
Fincept Terminal is a native desktop financial intelligence platform and research terminal designed for students, academics, hobbyists, and financial professionals. It provides institutional-grade analytics, automation, and extensive data connectivity within a single binary without relying on Electron or browser runtimes.

The platform includes capabilities such as DCF modeling, portfolio optimization, VaR/Sharpe analysis, derivatives pricing, fixed income, an 18-module QuantLib suite, an AI agent system supporting custom LLM keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, and Ollama), and 100+ data connectors including FRED, IMF, World Bank, DBnomics, AkShare, Polygon, Kraken, and Yahoo Finance. Additional features include crypto and equity feeds, a paper-trading engine, 16 broker integrations, a visual node editor, MCP tools, an AI Quant Lab for ML, factor discovery, and RL, plus maritime tracking and geopolitical analysis.

The repository is maintained under the AGPL-3.0-or-later license for personal use, learning, and academic research. Notable technologies used include C++20, Qt6, embedded Python 3.11, and CMake.

name: dokku
description: A docker-powered PaaS that helps you build and manage the lifecycle of applications
summary: Dokku is a Docker-powered mini-Heroku and a lightweight Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) implementation designed for application deployment. It enables developers and system administrators to manage and host applications on a virtual machine using containerization. The project runs on operating systems including Ubuntu (22.04, 24.04, 26.04) and Debian 11+ across amd64 and arm64 architectures. Dokku utilizes SSH keypairs for authentication and deployment management, and is configured via command-line utilities for domain management and user access.

name: rocksdb
description: A library that provides an embeddable, persistent key-value store for fast storage.
summary:
RocksDB is a persistent key-value store library developed and maintained by the Facebook Database Engineering Team, built on earlier work on LevelDB by Sanjay Ghemawat and Jeff Dean. It functions as a core building block for fast key-value servers optimized for flash drives and RAM storage. 

Utilizing a Log-Structured-Merge-Database (LSM) design, RocksDB provides flexible tradeoffs between Write-Amplification-Factor (WAF), Read-Amplification-Factor (RAF), and Space-Amplification-Factor (SAF). Its main capabilities include multi-threaded compactions, making it particularly suitable for storing multiple terabytes of data within a single database. The library is intended for developers building high-performance storage systems and data-intensive applications. It is dual-licensed under both the GPLv2 and Apache 2.0 licenses.

name: lottie-web
description: Render After Effects animations natively on Web, Android and iOS, and React Native. http://airbnb.io/lottie/
summary:
Lottie is a mobile and web library that parses Adobe After Effects animations exported as JSON via Bodymovin and renders them natively. Designed for web, Android, iOS, React Native, and Windows, Lottie enables designers to create and ship vector animations without engineers needing to recreate them by hand. 

The project purpose is to streamline animation workflows by bridging design tools and native runtime rendering. Main capabilities include loading animations via object data or file paths, controlling playback (play, pause, stop, speed adjustment, framing, and looping), supporting multiple renderers (`svg`, `canvas`, `html`), handling events, and updating text layers dynamically. Intended users are designers and developers looking to integrate high-quality, lightweight animations into applications. Notable technologies utilized include Adobe After Effects, Bodymovin, JavaScript, SVG, and HTML5 Canvas.

name: graphql-engine
description: Blazing fast, instant realtime GraphQL APIs on all your data with fine grained access control, also trigger webhooks on database events.
summary:
The Hasura GraphQL Engine is an open-source project designed to accelerate modern application development by providing instant, secure access to data via a single, composable API endpoint. 

The repository contains both Hasura V2 (the current stable version) and Hasura V3 (powering Hasura DDN), serving developers building applications with data delivery engines. Hasura V3 supports PostgreSQL and its variants, MongoDB, ClickHouse, and MS SQL Server, while enabling custom business logic through Connector SDKs for TypeScript, Python, and Go. It utilizes open-source Data Connectors accessible via the Connector Hub. 

Intended for application developers and data engineers, the project facilitates rapid database access, schema composition, and data federation. Notable technologies and components mentioned include PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ClickHouse, MS SQL Server, TypeScript, Python, Go, and the Apache License 2.0.

name: run
description: 润学全球官方指定GITHUB，整理润学宗旨、纲领、理论和各类润之实例；解决为什么润，润去哪里，怎么润三大问题； 并成为新中国人的核心宗教，核心信念。
summary:
This repository serves as a comprehensive, community-driven digital library and resource center dedicated to "Run philosophy" (润学)—the study and practice of international migration and emigration from China. The project's core purpose is to address why people migrate, where they can go, and how they can successfully relocate, encompassing countries such as the United States, Australia, and Japan. 

The repository's main capabilities include organizing theoretical frameworks, practical methodologies, government and visa information (such as H-1B, EB-1A, NIW, and EB-5), financial guidance, and firsthand migration case studies contributed by users. Intended users include Chinese citizens seeking emigration pathways, overseas relocation strategies, or comparative global data on immigration. The project encourages collaborative contributions through Markdown files and Pull Requests, assembling an extensive knowledge base for prospective emigrants.

name: linera-protocol
description: Main repository for the Linera protocol
summary:
Linera is a decentralized blockchain infrastructure designed for highly scalable, secure, and low-latency Web3 applications. The repository provides a comprehensive Rust-based protocol implementation structured into modular crates, including base cryptography, data structure key-value storage mapping via `linera-views`, persistent application execution and runtime logic (`linera-execution`), block chains and cross-chain messaging (`linera-chain`), storage abstractions, core client and server logic, RPC messages, client and service libraries, and a WebAssembly (Wasm) SDK for application development. 

Intended users include developers building high-performance decentralized applications and smart contracts using Rust. Notable technologies utilized include Rust, Wasm, RocksDB, and Docker. Key capabilities encompass running local test networks, managing microchains and wallets via a CLI, handling cross-chain interactions, querying chain and user balances, and executing token transfers.

name: DevToys
description: A Swiss Army knife for developers.
summary:
DevToys, described as a "Swiss Army knife for developers," is a utility application designed to streamline daily development tasks by bundling numerous small, specific tools. It eliminates the need to use multiple external websites for routine operations. The application features Smart Detection, which intuitively analyzes clipboard data to automatically select the most appropriate tool. 

DevToys 2.0 includes 30 default tools categorized into:
- **Converters**: JSON <> YAML, Date, and Number bases.
- **Encoders/Decoders**: HTML, URLs, Base64, GZip, JWT, and QR Code.
- **Formatters**: JSON, SQL, and XML.
- **Generators**: Hash & Checksum, Lorem Ipsum, and Passwords.
- **Graphics Tools**: Color Blindness Simulator and PNG/JPEG Compressors.
- **Testers**: JSONPath, RegEx, and XML.
- **Text Utilities**: Markdown Preview, Text Comparer, and Analyzer & Utilities.

Additionally, the application supports extensions for adding more tools and allows users to develop custom tools. Intended for software developers and technical professionals, the repository features technologies and formats such as JSON, YAML, SQL, XML, JWT, GZip, RegEx, and QR Code.

name: GPTs
description: leaked prompts of GPTs
summary: This repository is a curated collection of leaked prompts, configurations, and system instructions for various custom GPT models. The project serves as an archive of instructions gathered from public sources, user pull requests, and direct extraction. It covers a wide range of specialized AI assistants—including coding tutors, writing and translation aids, image generators, RPGs, productivity utilities, and domain-specific experts—created by numerous community developers and organizations.

name: MoneyPrinterV2
description: Automate the process of making money online.
summary:
MoneyPrinter V2 (MPV2) is an application designed to automate online monetization workflows through a modular architecture. Built as a complete rewrite of the original project, its main capabilities include automated Twitter bot operations and YouTube Shorts generation managed via CRON job schedulers, Amazon and Twitter-based affiliate marketing, and local business scraping for cold email outreach. 

The project is intended for users seeking to automate social media content creation, marketing, and outreach tasks. Notable technologies and tools utilized in the project include Python 3.12, the Go Programming Language (for email outreach capabilities), KittenTTS, and gpt4free.

name: alpine
description: A rugged, minimal framework for composing JavaScript behavior in your markup.
summary:
Alpine.js is a rugged, minimal framework for composing JavaScript behavior directly in your markup, offering a reactive and declarative approach similar to Vue or React at a much lower cost. Designed for web developers seeking lightweight DOM manipulation, Alpine.js provides reactive state management and behavior binding directly within HTML.

This repository is structured as an npm workspaces monorepo containing the main `alpinejs` core package alongside several official plugins: `collapse` for smooth element animations, `csp` for Content Security Policy-safe builds, `focus` for managing element focus, `history` for binding data to query strings via the history API, `intersect` for viewport intersection triggers, `mask` for text input formatting, `morph` for intelligent HTML morphing, `persist` for state persistence across page loads, and `docs`. 

Built using ESBuild, the project outputs both self-initializing CDN builds and standard JavaScript modules (ESM and CJS). The testing suite utilizes Cypress for integration tests and Vitest for unit tests. Intended users are web developers looking to add reactive behavior to web pages with minimal overhead.

name: Antigravity-Manager
description: Professional Antigravity Account Manager & Switcher. One-click seamless account switching for Antigravity Tools. Built with Tauri v2 + React (Rust).专业的 Antigravity 账号管理与切换工具。为 Antigravity 提供一键无缝账号切换功能。
summary:
Antigravity Tools is an all-in-one desktop application and protocol proxy system designed for developers and AI enthusiasts to manage multiple accounts and act as a local AI relay station. The project purpose is to combine multi-account matrix dispatch, protocol conversion, and request scheduling, transforming web sessions from providers like Google and Anthropic into standardized API interfaces. 

Main capabilities include smart account dashboards with real-time monitoring, OAuth 2.0 authorization, multi-dimensional token imports, protocol conversion supporting OpenAI format, Anthropic format, and Gemini format, smart self-healing rotation for error handling, a model router center with series-based mapping and tiered routing, and multimodal support for Imagen 3 image generation.

Intended users include developers, AI hobbyists, and enterprise users seeking stable, high-speed, and low-cost access to AI model APIs. Notable technologies used in the project stack include Tauri (v2), Rust for the backend, React for the frontend, Axum server architecture, and Docker for containerized deployments.

name: html2canvas
description: Screenshots with JavaScript
summary:
html2canvas is a JavaScript HTML renderer that allows users to take webpage screenshots directly within the browser. By reading the DOM and applied styles, the script builds a canvas image of a webpage or specific elements without requiring server-side rendering. 

Intended for client-side use, the library is not suitable for Node.js environments and respects browser content policy restrictions, requiring proxies for cross-origin content. It utilizes JavaScript `Promise`s and supports browsers including Firefox 3.5+, Google Chrome, Opera 12+, IE9+, and Safari 6+ (with a `Promise` polyfill for older browsers). Notable technologies and tools used in the project include Git and npm.

name: code-review-graph
description: Local-first code intelligence graph for MCP and CLI. Builds a persistent map of your codebase so AI coding tools read only what matters, with benchmarked context reductions on reviews and large-repo workflows.
summary:
`code-review-graph` is a local code knowledge graph tool that provides AI coding tools with precise review context via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It parses codebases into structural graphs of nodes (functions, classes, imports) and edges (calls, inheritance, test coverage) using Tree-sitter, keeping them updated incrementally through git diffs, hooks, or a multi-repo daemon.
