Designed for developers using AI assistants, the tool significantly reduces token consumption by serving compact, targeted impact radiuses and review sets rather than full repository corpora. It supports Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, C/C++, C#, PHP, Ruby, Kotlin, Swift, and numerous other languages, alongside Jupyter/Databricks notebooks and framework-specific analyzers for Laravel, Spring, and Composer PSR-4.

Notable features include blast-radius analysis, semantic search via optional local or cloud vector embeddings (sentence-transformers, Gemini, MiniMax, Voyage AI, or OpenAI-compatible endpoints), risk-scored PR review comments via a GitHub Action, interactive D3.js and GraphML visualisations, and a multi-repo registry. The tool requires Python 3.10+ and stores data locally in a single SQLite file within `.code-review-graph/`.

name: agent-skills
description: Vercel's official collection of agent skills
summary:
Agent Skills is a collection of packaged instructions and scripts designed to extend the capabilities of AI coding agents. The repository provides standardized guidelines, automated auditing tools, and workflow capabilities primarily focused on web development, React, Next.js, and Vercel infrastructure.

Key skills included are:
- **vercel-optimize**: Audits Vercel projects for cost, performance, reliability, caching, and function usage.
- **react-best-practices**: Prioritized Vercel Engineering guidelines covering React and Next.js performance, bundle optimization, and server-side rendering.
- **web-design-guidelines**: UI and accessibility auditing rules covering WCAG compliance, performance, forms, animation, and localization.
- **writing-guidelines**: Vercel writing handbook rules for documentation and prose voice, tone, and formatting.
- **react-native-guidelines**: Performance, architecture, and platform-specific guidelines for building React Native and Expo apps.
- **react-view-transitions**: Integration rules and utilities for implementing native-feeling page and component animations using React's View Transition API and Next.js.
- **composition-patterns**: React component architecture patterns for reducing boolean prop proliferation via compound components and state lifting.
- **vercel-deploy-claimable**: Instant application and website deployment tool for Vercel that auto-detects over 40 frameworks and returns claimable preview URLs.

Intended users are developers utilizing AI coding assistants to build, review, optimize, and deploy web and mobile applications.

name: interactive-coding-challenges
description: 120+ interactive Python coding interview challenges (algorithms and data structures).  Includes Anki flashcards.
summary:
The project provides over 120 continually updated, test-driven, and interactive coding challenges focusing on algorithms and data structures for coding interviews. Intended users include software engineers preparing for technical interviews and system design discussions. 

Main capabilities include interactive challenge and solution notebooks detailing problem statements, constraints, test cases, algorithm discussions, and Big-O time and space complexities. The repository also supplies unit-tested reference implementations for common data structures (such as Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, Binary Search Trees, Graphs, Min Heaps, Tries, Priority Queues, and Hash Maps) and algorithms (including Sorting, Graph Traversals, Shortest Paths, and Dynamic Programming). Additionally, it integrates Anki flashcard decks for coding and design concepts via spaced repetition.

Notable technologies used include Python (tested on Python 2.7 and Python 3.x), IPython/Jupyter Notebooks, nbviewer, Binder, and Anki.

name: vimrc
description: The ultimate Vim configuration (vimrc)
summary:
The Ultimate vimrc is a comprehensive, customizable Vim configuration repository designed for developers seeking an enhanced text-editing experience. It offers two setup variants: a minimal Basic version for lightweight remote servers, and an Awesome version packed with pre-configured plugins, color schemes, and fonts like IBM Plex Mono, Hack, and Source Code Pro. 

Key capabilities include fuzzy file and buffer searching via `ctrlp.vim`, fast grep searches with `ack.vim`, syntax and lint checking through `ale`, Git integration via `vim-fugitive`, AI autocompletion with `copilot.vim`, distraction-free writing using `goyo.vim` and `vim-zenroom2`, and code execution support for languages such as Python, C, C++, Java, Go, and Bash. It also features extensive key mappings, custom window management, and support for multiple color schemes including peaksea, dracula, and solarized. 

The project targets developers, programmers, and system administrators using Vim or NeoVim across Linux, macOS, and Windows operating systems. Notable technologies utilized include Vimscript, Python, and various open-source Vim plugins and color schemes.

name: mantine
description: A fully featured React components library
summary:
Mantine is a fully featured React component library and ecosystem designed for web development. It provides a comprehensive collection of packages and tools to build modern user interfaces. 

Its main capabilities span over 100 core components (`@mantine/core`), a collection of 80+ state and UI management hooks (`@mantine/hooks`), form management (`@mantine/form`), and a charts library powered by Recharts (`@mantine/charts`). Additionally, it includes specialized modules such as a notifications system (`@mantine/notifications`), a `Ctrl + K` command center spotlight (`@mantine/spotlight`), code highlighting built with highlight.js (`@mantine/code-highlight`), a Tiptap-based rich text editor (`@mantine/tiptap`), file dropzone management (`@mantine/dropzone`), carousels (`@mantine/carousel`), navigation progress bars (`@mantine/nprogress`), centralized modal management (`@mantine/modals`), and a schedule component for displaying events (`@mantine/schedule`). 

Mantine is intended for developers building web applications who require a robust, modular, and extensible set of UI primitives and utilities.

name: nginx
description: The official NGINX Open Source repository.
summary:
NGINX is a high-performance web server, load balancer, reverse proxy, API gateway, and content cache. Distributed under a 2-clause BSD-like license, it serves as free and open-source software designed to scale efficiently across operating systems using a multi-process architecture consisting of a master process and worker processes. 

Key capabilities include TLS/SSL encryption support, HTTP load balancing, rate limiting for API gateway use cases, and content caching for CDNs and edge servers. NGINX functions through extensible modules, which can be compiled statically at build-time or loaded dynamically at runtime, including popular options such as NGINX JavaScript (njs). 

Intended users include system administrators, web developers, and DevOps engineers managing web infrastructure. The software provides stable and mainline binary distributions for Linux, FreeBSD, and Windows, alongside instructions and scripts to build the project from source code using compilers like `gcc` and `make`, along with dependency libraries such as `libpcre3-dev`, `zlib1g-dev`, and `libssl-dev`.

name: CodexPlusPlus
description: An enhanced tool for CodexApp, striving to make Codex better to use and more comfortable 一个CodexApp的增强工具，努力让Codex变得更好用更舒服
summary:
Codex++ is an external launcher and management tool for OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT desktop applications. It provides vendor switching, protocol conversion, session management, and interface enhancements via the Chromium DevTools Protocol and a local auxiliary service, without modifying the official application’s `app.asar` or writing patch files to its installation directory.

Key capabilities include supplier configuration (supporting official login, official login mixed with API, pure API, and aggregated routing with failover), model and context management (such as window adjustments and metadata imports), local session management with Markdown export and token tracking, WeChat personal account session mapping, and extensive Codex UI enhancements (such as theme skin management, step-wise suggestions, paste fixes, and localized Chinese menus). It also supports developer workflows like upstream worktree creation and user script execution.

Intended for developers, teams, and AI tool users, Codex++ is built using Rust (1.85+) and Tauri (2.x), running as a silent launcher and a dedicated management application on Windows and macOS.

name: k6
description: A modern load testing tool, using Go and JavaScript
summary:
**k6** is a modern, developer-centric load-testing tool designed for performance testing in the DevOps era. Its primary purpose is to enable developers and testers to write tests as code, simulate heavy application traffic, and integrate performance assertions into continuous integration workflows.

Main capabilities include configurable load generation, support for multiple protocols (such as HTTP, WebSockets, gRPC, and Browser), flexible metrics storage and visualization, and native integration with Grafana Cloud. It features an embedded JavaScript engine combined with Go performance, allowing users to write modular scripts with custom thresholds, stages, and virtual user behaviors. 

Intended users are software developers and testers looking for unit-testing-style performance validation. Notable technologies used and supported include JavaScript, Go, HTTP, WebSockets, gRPC, and Kubernetes.

name: invisible_playwright_mcp
description: Playwright MCP server undetected by anti-bots and captchas: AI agent browses the web on anti-detect stealth Firefox, Python, undetected browser automation, scraping, computer use.
summary:
`invisible_playwright_mcp` is an anti-bot-evading web browsing agent and MCP (Model Context Protocol) server designed to perform real web automation invisibly without triggering captchas. It drives web pages like a human user by moving pointers and pressing keys, supporting complex multi-step tasks that require page judgment and calendar interactions. 

The project can be used in two ways: integrated into AI assistants (such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI) via MCP, or standalone using its built-in web UI powered by an OpenRouter API key. 

Notable technical features and options include configurable proxies (which automatically adjust timezone, locale, and egress via an internal GeoIP database), engine binary paths (`STEALTHFOX_BINARY`), persistent browser profiles via `--profile-dir`, reproducible browser identities via `--seed`, headed mode, and `.env` file support. The ecosystem also includes `invisible_playwright` (a Python library mirroring the Playwright API) and `invisible_core` (handling seeds, fingerprints, proxies, and geolocation). Distributed under the MIT license, it runs entirely locally on the user's machine without external telemetry servers.

name: anki
description: Anki is a smart spaced repetition flashcard program
summary: Anki is a spaced repetition program designed to help users memorize information efficiently through scheduled flashcard reviews. This repository contains the source code for the computer version of the application. The project is intended for anyone looking to use spaced repetition for learning, as well as developers and contributors interested in building, testing, and contributing to the desktop software.

name: lux
description: 👾 Fast and simple video download library and CLI tool written in Go
summary:
Lux is a fast and simple command-line video, image, and audio downloader built with Go. Its primary purpose is to allow users to extract and download media streams from numerous popular websites, including YouTube, Bilibili, Douyin, Youku, Twitter, Instagram, TikTok, and Reddit. 

Main capabilities include downloading single videos or entire playlists, handling multiple inputs, resuming interrupted downloads, supporting HTTP/SOCKS5 proxies, multi-threaded downloading, auto-retrying failed downloads, passing cookies, specifying custom referrers, and downloading or embedding subtitles. It also features debug modes, JSON metadata extraction, and integration with Aria2 RPC. 

Intended users are developers, content creators, and general users looking for an efficient command-line utility to archive media content across various supported platforms. The tool relies on FFmpeg for final file merging. Distinctive technologies and tools mentioned include Go, FFmpeg, and Aria2.

name: jumpserver
description: JumpServer is an Open-source Privileged Access Management (PAM) platform with AI-powered capabilities, providing DevOps and IT teams a unified workspace to securely access SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, databases, websites, RemoteApp, VirtualApp, and more.
summary:
JumpServer is an open-source Privileged Access Management (PAM) platform equipped with AI-powered capabilities. Designed for DevOps and IT teams, it serves as a bastion host providing a unified workspace for secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, databases, websites, RemoteApp, and VirtualApp. 

The platform's architecture comprises several core components: JumpServer for core PAM logic, Lina for the web interface, Luna for the web terminal and native client, KoKo for general-purpose protocol connection and proxying, Chen for web database connections, and Kael for AI integration. It also includes enterprise components (such as Tinker, Panda, Razor, Magnus, and Nec), supporting services like Video Worker and JDMC, and deployment tools including Installer and Docker Web.

name: nuclei
description: Nuclei is a fast, customizable vulnerability scanner powered by the global security community and built on a simple YAML-based DSL, enabling collaboration to tackle trending vulnerabilities on the internet. It helps you find vulnerabilities in your applications, APIs, networks, DNS, and cloud configurations.
summary:
Nuclei is a modern, high-performance vulnerability scanner designed for security professionals, penetration testers, and enterprise security teams. It utilizes simple, human-readable YAML-based templates to design custom vulnerability detection scenarios that mimic real-world conditions with zero false positives. 

Key capabilities include ultra-fast parallel scan processing, request clustering, CI/CD pipeline integration, and support for multiple protocols such as HTTP, DNS, TCP, SSL, WHOIS, JavaScript, WebSocket, and Code. It also features integrations with platforms like Jira, Splunk, GitHub, Elastic, and GitLab, alongside an open-source template library contributed to by a global security community. 

Nuclei is built primarily as a command-line interface (CLI) tool using Go (version 1.24.2 or higher) and offers Pro and Enterprise editions for large-scale, continuous scanning environments.

name: awesome-openclaw-usecases
description: A community collection of OpenClaw use cases for making life easier.
summary:
Awesome OpenClaw Use Cases is a community-driven repository providing a curated collection of real-life applications and workflows for the OpenClaw platform (formerly known as ClawdBot and MoltBot). Its primary purpose is to help users discover practical ways to leverage AI agents to improve their daily lives and productivity. 

The project outlines over forty practical use cases spanning multiple domains:
- **Social Media & Content:** Automated digests (Reddit, YouTube, tech news), X/Twitter automation via the TweetClaw plugin, YouTube content pipelines, multi-agent content factories, podcast production pipelines, and natural language AI video editing.
- **Creative & Building:** Goal-driven autonomous task execution (including overnight mini-app building), autonomous game development pipelines, and idea validation tools.
- **Infrastructure & DevOps:** n8n workflow orchestration via webhooks and self-healing home servers with SSH and cron capabilities.
- **Productivity & Assistance:** Autonomous project management, multi-channel customer service, phone-based personal assistants, personal CRM systems, inbox de-cluttering, Todoist task syncing, family calendar aggregation, desktop cowork applications, and habit tracking.
- **Research & Learning:** AI earnings tracking, personal knowledge bases using RAG, market research, semantic memory search, arXiv paper reading, and conversational LaTeX paper writing.
- **Finance & Trading:** Polymarket autopilot paper trading.

Intended users include developers, AI builders, and everyday users seeking to automate workflows, manage tasks, and build applications using OpenClaw. Technologies and integrations referenced include Discord, Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Instagram, n8n, Next.js, DuckDB, Jira, Linear, Todoist, Hugging Face, arXiv, and LaTeX.

name: Avalonia
description: Develop Desktop, Embedded, Mobile and WebAssembly apps with C# and XAML. The future of .NET UI
summary:
Avalonia is a mature, production-ready, cross-platform UI framework for .NET designed as a modern spiritual successor to WPF. It provides a flexible styling system and allows developers to build applications targeting Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and WebAssembly. 

Intended for XAML developers and .NET software engineers, Avalonia enables the creation of cross-platform applications with a familiar development experience. Notable technologies utilized include .NET, XAML, C#, and NuGet for package distribution. The framework integrates with development environments such as Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code (via the Avalonia for Code extension), and JetBrains Rider. Additionally, the project offers Avalonia XPF, a commercial product enabling existing WPF applications to run on macOS and Linux with minimal code changes.

name: Scrapegraph-ai
description: Python scraper based on AI
summary:
ScrapeGraphAI is an open-source web scraping Python library that leverages large language models (LLMs) and direct graph logic to build flexible data extraction pipelines for websites and local documents (such as XML, HTML, JSON, and Markdown). Instead of relying on traditional rigid selectors, users simply state what information they want to extract, and the library handles the extraction process.

The project provides multiple pipeline variants, including `SmartScraperGraph`, `SearchGraph`, `SpeechGraph`, `ScriptCreatorGraph`, and their multi-page graph counterparts, supporting single-page and multi-page scraping, audio generation, and Python script creation. 

Intended users include developers, data scientists, and researchers looking to integrate web scraping with AI agents and data analytics pipelines. Notable technologies and integrations used within the project include Python, Node.js, Playwright, Langchain, Llama Index, Crew.ai, Agno, CamelAI, Ollama, OpenAI, Groq, Azure, Gemini, and MiniMax, alongside low-code platform plugins and an MCP server.

name: fabric.js
description: Javascript Canvas Library, SVG-to-Canvas (& canvas-to-SVG) Parser
summary: Fabric.js is a simple and powerful JavaScript HTML5 canvas library that provides interactive object manipulation and SVG-to-canvas parsing capabilities. Its main capabilities include out-of-the-box interactions such as scaling, moving, rotating, skewing, and grouping, alongside built-in shapes, controls, animations, image filters, gradients, patterns, brushes, and input/output support for JPG, PNG, JSON, and SVG formats. It is designed for developers building browser-based and Node.js applications that require programmatic manipulation of HTML5 canvas elements. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, Node.js, node-canvas, and jsdom.

name: chatgpt-web
description: 用 Express 和  Vue3 搭建的 ChatGPT 演示网页
summary:
ChatGPT Web is a full-stack open-source web application designed to interface with ChatGPT using dual models and multiple API methods, including OpenAI API keys (`ChatGPTAPI`) and web access tokens via unofficial proxy servers (`ChatGPTUnofficialProxyAPI`). 

The project features a frontend webpage and a Node.js backend service. Main capabilities include multi-session storage, context handling, code and message formatting/beautification, data import and export, saving messages as local images, multilingual interfaces, and theme customization. It supports access control through secret keys, rate limiting, and various proxy configurations (HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5). Intended users include developers and individuals looking for a customizable, self-hosted web interface for ChatGPT. 

The application can be deployed manually, using Docker and Docker Compose, or through platforms like Railway and Sealos. Notable technologies utilized include Node.js, PNPM, Vite, and Docker.

name: webtorrent
description: ⚡️ Streaming torrent client for the web
summary:
WebTorrent is a streaming torrent client written entirely in JavaScript for use in Node.js and web browsers. In the browser, it leverages WebRTC data channels for plugin-free, peer-to-peer communication over the BitTorrent protocol, enabling seamless video and file streaming directly into HTML elements like `<video>` tags. In Node.js, it operates as a standard torrent client using TCP and UDP. 

Main capabilities include downloading multiple torrents simultaneously, exposing files as streams to support on-demand piece fetching and media seeking, magnet URI parsing via `ut_metadata`, and peer discovery through DHT, trackers, local service discovery (LSD), and `ut_pex`. Intended users include web developers and application builders aiming to integrate decentralized file sharing and video streaming into browser applications and Node.js services. Notable technologies used include JavaScript, WebRTC, Node.js, Browserify, and Webpack.

name: graphiti
description: Build Real-Time Knowledge Graphs for AI Agents
summary:
Graphiti is an open-source framework for building, updating, and querying temporal context graphs tailored for AI agents and interactive applications. Unlike static knowledge graphs or standard RAG methods, Graphiti continuously integrates structured and unstructured data into an evolving graph where facts feature temporal validity windows, source data provenance via episodes, and support for both prescribed and learned ontologies. 

The framework is designed for AI developers and enterprise engineers seeking real-time data integration without batch recomputation. It enables hybrid retrieval combining semantic embeddings, keyword search, and graph traversal. Notable technologies and integrations include support for graph backends such as Neo4j, FalkorDB, Amazon Neptune, and Kuzu, alongside LLM inference and embeddings providers including OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, and Groq, as well as OpenAI-compatible local servers like Ollama.

name: cognee
description: Cognee is the open-source AI memory platform for agents. Give your AI agents persistent long-term memory with small models for free
summary:
Cognee is a free, open-source AI memory platform that provides AI agents with persistent, long-term memory across sessions by transforming documents, code, and conversations into self-hosted knowledge graphs. It enables users to build a searchable "Company Brain," maintain project context across runs, and ground agents in custom domain models and ontologies.

The platform is designed to run locally using CPU-based models such as GLiNER for extraction and local embedding models without requiring an API key, while also supporting optional cloud LLMs like OpenAI or local Ollama models. Cognee supports core operations including `remember`, `recall`, `improve`, and `forget`, and integrates with agent ecosystems and interfaces through plugins, an MCP server, and SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Rust. It features clients and integrations for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Cursor, and Cline, alongside deployment pathways via Docker Compose and a managed cloud option.

name: HEAD
description: A simple guide to HTML <head> elements
summary: HEAD is a simple guide to HTML `<head>` elements, providing a comprehensive reference for web developers, designers, and site maintainers. The project outlines the recommended minimum setup, correct element ordering for performance and rendering, and a wide variety of meta tags, link relations, scripts, and icons. It covers configuration for social sharing standards such as Open Graph, Schema.org, Google JSON-LD, Pinterest, OEmbed, QQ/WeChat, Dublin Core, and the Fediverse, alongside platform-specific settings for Apple iOS, Google Android, Google Chrome, and Chinese mobile browsers like 360, QQ, and UC. Additionally, the project details App Links and lists related ecosystem tools such as Atom and Sublime Text snippets, a CLI interface, and a Vue.js meta manipulation package. The documentation is maintained using HTML5 and Jekyll for GitHub Pages deployment.

name: 9router
description: Unlimited FREE AI coding. Connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, Copilot, Antigravity to FREE Claude/GPT/Gemini via 40+ providers. Auto-fallback, RTK -40% tokens, never hit limits.
summary:
9Router is a free AI router and token saver designed to connect CLI coding tools—such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, and Cline—to over 40 AI providers and 100+ models. 

The project purpose is to prevent rate limits, maximize subscription quotas, and reduce AI operational costs through automated fallback tiers (Subscription, Cheap, and Free providers) and built-in token optimization techniques. 

Main capabilities include:
- **RTK Token Saver**: Automatically compresses tool outputs (like `git diff` and `grep`) to cut 20–40% of input tokens per request.
- **Smart 3-Tier Fallback**: Automatically routes requests across subscription, low-cost, and free options with zero downtime.
- **Format Translation**: Seamlessly translates requests between OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Kiro, and Vertex formats.
- **Multi-Account & OAuth Support**: Handles round-robin multi-account load balancing and automatic token refreshes.
- **Additional Enhancements**: Includes real-time quota tracking, usage analytics, request logging, Cloud Sync, and optional prompt-compression systems like Caveman and Ponytail modes.

Intended users are software developers and engineers utilizing AI-assisted coding CLI tools who want to avoid recurring rate limits and minimize token expenditure. Notable technologies used include Node.js, Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, and Server-Sent Events (SSE).

name: qmd
description: mini cli search engine for your docs, knowledge bases, meeting notes, whatever. Tracking current sota approaches while being all local
summary:
QMD (Query Markup Documents) is an on-device local search engine designed for markdown notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and agentic workflows. It combines BM25 full-text search (SQLite FTS5), vector semantic search, and LLM re-ranking running locally via `node-llama-cpp` using GGUF models. 

Key capabilities include hybrid search pipelines with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), automatic and manual query expansion, tree-sitter AST-aware chunking for code files, and structured metadata filtering and discovery via a recursive JSON AST grammar. The engine supports hierarchical context descriptions to improve LLM relevance, interactive benchmarking, and flexible document retrieval (by path, docid, or glob patterns).

QMD is intended for developers, knowledge workers, and AI agents requiring local semantic search. It exposes its functionality via a CLI, a TypeScript SDK, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server supporting both stdio and HTTP transports. Notable technologies used include Node.js, Bun, SQLite, sqlite-vec, and HuggingFace GGUF models (`embeddinggemma-300M`, `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B`, and a fine-tuned `Qwen3-1.7B` query expansion model).

name: facefusion
description: Industry leading face manipulation platform
summary: FaceFusion is an industry-leading face manipulation platform. It provides tools for face manipulation through standard execution, headless mode, batch processing, and a job management system with capabilities to list, create, submit, delete, and execute queued or drafted jobs and steps. The project is implemented in Python, utilizing command-line options and execution commands like `facefusion.py`, and offers dedicated Windows and macOS installers alongside terminal-based installation.

name: frontend-slides
description: Create beautiful slides on the web using a coding agent's frontend skills
summary:
Frontend Slides is a coding-agent skill for creating HTML presentations from scratch or by converting PowerPoint files, packaged primarily as a Claude Code plugin with support for other filesystem-enabled coding agents. 

The project purpose is to help non-designers generate web presentations without requiring knowledge of CSS or JavaScript. Instead of text-based preference descriptions, it uses a visual style discovery approach where users select from generated previews, curated presets, and an optional **Bold Template Pack** containing 34 distinct design systems.

Main capabilities include zero-dependency single-file HTML generation with inline CSS and JS, visual style shortlisting, PowerPoint conversion via Python (`python-pptx`), deployment to live URLs via Vercel, and PDF export utilizing Playwright. Intended users are non-designers, professionals, and developers looking to produce accessible, fixed 16:9 production-quality slide decks. Notable technologies and formats mentioned include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Node.js, and Vercel.

name: jitsi-meet
description: Jitsi Meet - Secure, Simple and Scalable Video Conferences that you use as a standalone app or embed in your web application.
summary:
Jitsi Meet is an open-source set of projects that empowers users to deploy and use video conferencing platforms. Designed for individuals, developers, organizations, and businesses, it provides browser-based access, mobile applications for Android and iOS, and web and native SDKs for integration. 

Main capabilities include HD audio and video, content sharing, raise hand and reactions, private and group chat, polls, virtual backgrounds, and End-to-End Encryption (E2EE). The platform supports all current browsers and offers scalable deployment options via Debian packages, a comprehensive Docker setup, or building from source. For users seeking to avoid operational complexity, 8x8 Jitsi as a Service (JaaS) provides an enterprise-ready managed platform.

name: Rectangle
description: Move and resize windows on macOS with keyboard shortcuts and snap areas
summary: Rectangle is a window management application for macOS based on Spectacle, designed to move and resize windows using keyboard shortcuts, snap areas, and URL commands. Its purpose is to help users organize their desktop workspace by snapping windows to halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, ninths, corners, and custom grid layouts in rows or columns. It also features stacked window cycling and the ability to ignore specific apps. Intended for macOS users seeking efficient window arrangement, Rectangle supports macOS v14+ (with older legacy versions available for earlier macOS releases). The project utilizes technologies such as Swift, Swift Package Manager, MASShortcut, and Sparkle.

name: genesis-world
description: Simulation platform for general-purpose robotics & embodied AI learning.
summary:
Genesis World is a physical AI simulation platform designed for robotics developments, machine learning pipelines, and agentic simulation, scaling from single laptop kernels to datacenter-grade GPUs. It features a unified multi-physics engine supporting Rigid, FEM, MPM, Particle (PBD/SPH), explicit coupling, and SAP solvers sharing a single scene and state. It integrates a photo-realistic renderer called Nyx (alongside Luisa and Pyrender paths) and a cross-platform compiler named Quadrants, which lowers Python kernel code to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64 with built-in autodiff and GPU graphs. 

The platform exposes a Pythonic simulation interface supporting asset parsing (URDF, MJCF, OBJ, GLB, USD), entity accessors, controllers, sensors (depth cameras, IMU, lidar, tactile, contact force), parallel and heterogeneous environments, and a built-in GUI with ImGui and debug drawing. Intended for researchers and developers in robotics and embodied AI, Genesis World relies on PyTorch and is distributed under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: picoclaw
description: Tiny, Fast, and Deployable anywhere — automate the mundane, unleash your creativity
summary:
PicoClaw is an ultra-efficient, independent personal AI assistant developed in Go by Sipeed. Designed to run on inexpensive hardware with a minimal footprint, it requires less than 10MB of RAM and boots in milliseconds across x86_64, ARM64, MIPS, RISC-V, and LoongArch architectures, including low-cost single-board computers, Android phones, and Docker environments.

The project provides capabilities including native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, a multi-modal vision pipeline for images and files, smart rule-based model routing across over 30 LLM providers (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, and local runtimes like Ollama and vLLM), and integrations with 19+ messaging channels including Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, WeChat, Slack, and Matrix. It also includes modular skills from ClawHub, built-in web search engines (DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Brave, etc.), cron-based scheduled task management, and a browser-based WebUI Launcher. 

Intended for developers, hobbyists, and users seeking a lightweight, portable AI agent framework, PicoClaw can be managed via command-line interface instructions or web interfaces for tasks ranging from automated server operations and code generation to smart surveillance and device reminders.

name: Telegram
description: Telegram for Android source
summary: This repository contains the official source code for the Telegram messenger application for Android, focused on speed and security. It is intended for developers looking to use the Telegram API and source code to build applications on the platform. The project utilizes the Telegram API and the MTproto protocol, and supports reproducible builds. Compiling the application requires Android Studio 2025.1.4, Android NDK 27.2.12479018, Android SDK 36, and Firebase messaging integration via `google-services.json`.

name: serena
description: A powerful MCP toolkit for coding, providing semantic retrieval and editing capabilities  - the IDE for your agent
summary:
Serena is an IDE-like toolset designed for coding AI agents to provide symbol-level semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring, and debugging capabilities. Operating through agent-first abstractions, it integrates with any client or large language model via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). 

Main capabilities include symbol navigation, dependency searching, cross-file refactoring (such as renames, moves, and safe deletions), symbolic editing (replacing or inserting around symbol bodies), memory management for long-lived workflows, and interactive debugging. Serena supports two alternative analysis backends: Language Server Protocol (LSP) language servers covering over 40 programming languages, and the paid Serena JetBrains Plugin leveraging JetBrains IDE environments. Basic utilities such as regex search, file finding, and shell command execution are also included.

Intended users are AI coding agents operating across large codebases, multi-language monorepos, and developer workflows using clients like Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, and various IDE extensions. Notable technologies used include Python (managed via `uv`), MCP, LSP, and optional integration with JetBrains IDEs.

name: awesome-quant
description: A curated list of insanely awesome libraries, packages and resources for Quants (Quantitative Finance)
summary:
Awesome Quant is a curated, multilingual directory of open-source libraries, frameworks, datasets, tools, and educational resources dedicated to quantitative finance, algorithmic trading, and financial data analysis. Designed for quants, traders, and developers, the repository aggregates solutions spanning numerical computing, financial instruments and pricing, technical indicators, backtesting and live execution engines, portfolio optimization, risk analysis, factor research, alternative data, time-series analysis, and prediction markets. 

The collection highlights projects built in Python, R, Julia, Rust, C++, Java, TypeScript, and Go. Prominent technical capabilities include high-performance numerical manipulation (NumPy, Pandas, Polars), derivatives pricing and risk management (QuantLib ports, Vollib, FinancePy), technical analysis (TA-Lib, Tulipy), event-driven and vectorised backtesting engines, machine learning pipelines (Qlib, FinRL), and automated trading framework integrations across major brokerages and cryptocurrency exchanges. It also features extensive alternative data connectors, SEC EDGAR and financial statement parsers, model context protocol (MCP) servers, and academic references for reproducing institutional research.

name: mcp-for-blender
description: Community plugin to control Blender 3D with any LLM of your choice. Not affiliated with the official Blender Foundation.
summary:
MCP for Blender (`mcp-for-blender`) is a third-party integration that connects Blender to any LLM using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The project enables prompt-assisted 3D modeling, scene creation, inspection, and manipulation through AI applications like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, OpenCode, and Antigravity. 

Main capabilities include two-way socket communication with Blender, object and material manipulation, arbitrary Python code execution, and asset retrieval from Poly Haven, Sketchfab, and Poly Pizza. It also supports AI-generated 3D models via Hyper3D Rodin, Hunyuan3D, and Tripo.

The system consists of two core components: a Blender addon (`addon.py` / `blender_mcp.py`) acting as a socket server, and an MCP server (`src/blender_mcp/server.py`). The project is intended for 3D artists, developers, and AI users looking to automate or generate 3D workflows through natural language prompts. It features optional safe mode script validation, environment variable controls, and persistent credential storage. Notable technologies utilized include Python, Blender, TCP sockets, and the Model Context Protocol, with installation managed primarily via the `uv` package manager and `uvx`.

name: dsh-desktop
description: 为 DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 插件生态打造的现代化桌面端解决方案。万物皆「插件」，桌面本身也是「插件」。
summary:
DSH Desktop 是一个面向 Windows 和 macOS 的开源桌面客户端，基于 DeepSeek Harness 构建。其主要目的是将上游的本地 Web UI、Host 服务和插件系统集成到独立的原生桌面应用中，提供免命令行的开箱即用体验。

该项目的主要 capabilities 包括：
- 自动启动和管理本地 Harness 服务，并集成原生桌面窗口、系统托盘、终端、更新及工作配置。
- 内置手机远程控制功能（通过 Agents-Anywhere），允许用户在 iOS 和 Android 设备上发起任务和追踪 Agent 进度。
- 内置 DSH Community Market 插件市场，支持插件的发现、详情查看、安装与管理。
- 采用“万物皆插件”的架构，桌面壳本身也作为插件与上游能力组合进同一运行时。

intended users 包括普通终端用户以及希望开发或组合扩展包的插件作者和开发者。 notable technologies 使用了 DeepSeek Harness、Cordis、Electron、Yarn、pnpm workspace 以及 NSIS 和 DMG 打包工具。

name: awesome-osint
description: :scream: A curated list of amazingly awesome OSINT
summary:
Awesome OSINT is a curated list of open-source intelligence tools and resources designed for beginners and advanced practitioners in cyber threat intelligence (CTI), threat hunting, and digital investigations. 

The repository provides categorized links, platforms, frameworks, scripts, and search engines covering a wide range of investigative domains. Main capabilities include general and specialized search engine utilization, Google dorking, data breach analysis, threat actor tracking, social media and messaging platform reconnaissance (such as Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, Telegram, and Discord), domain and IP research, file and document discovery, username checking, people and company investigations, email and phone number research, geospatial mapping, image analysis, and threat intelligence feeds.

Intended users include security researchers, penetration testers, threat hunters, digital forensic analysts, law enforcement investigators, and privacy-conscious individuals. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced across the catalog include Python, Rust, Node.js, Maltego, Shodan, Censys, SpiderFoot, Maigret, Sherlock, and various automated reconnaissance tools.

name: apollo
description: Apollo is a reliable configuration management system suitable for microservice configuration management scenarios.
summary:
Apollo is a reliable configuration management system designed to centrally manage application and cluster configurations, particularly suitable for microservice architectures. 

**Main Capabilities**
* Centralized configuration management across different environments, clusters, and namespaces.
* Real-time configuration changes (hot release) with SDK updates occurring within one second.
* Version management supporting configuration rollbacks and grayscale releases for targeted instance rollouts.
* Global search for configuration items, authorization and permission control separating editing from publishing, operation audit logs, and client instance monitoring.
* Open platform APIs allowing complex format validation and custom validation logic.

**Intended Users**
* Software engineers, system administrators, and SRE roles managing distributed microservice environments and multi-environment application configurations.

**Notable Technologies**
* Server side developed with Spring Boot and Spring Cloud.
* Native SDKs for Java and .Net, alongside HTTP APIs and third-party SDKs for Golang, Python, NodeJS, PHP, C, and Rust.
* Relies primarily on MySQL for deployment with minimal external dependencies.

name: yeti
description: A CSS-first, native, zero-build layout and styling framework for web designers.
summary:
Yeti (the successor to Foundation for Sites) is a CSS-first, native, zero-build layout and styling framework designed for web designers to build coherent sites rapidly using human-readable and agent-writable markup. Provided as a single stylesheet (`yeti.css`), it leverages modern platform capabilities—including container queries, cascade layers, native nesting, `light-dark()`, `dialog`, `popover`, and scroll-snap—without requiring JavaScript, Sass, Node, or bundlers. 

The framework delivers intent-based named layouts, composed recipes, a runtime token scale where type and space derive from a single base and ratio, built-in accessibility with focus handling and ARIA, and a machine-readable manifest to support documentation, type hints, and an MCP server for agents. Yeti targets Baseline 2025 browser support and includes seventeen layout primitives, three recipes, twenty-two components, seven utilities, and two example themes. It is intended for web designers and developers modernizing their styling workflows. Yeti is released under the Functional Source License 1.1 with a future MIT license.

name: 90DaysOfDevOps
description: This repository started out as a learning in public project for myself and has now become a structured learning map for many in the community. We have 3 years under our belt covering all things DevOps, including Principles, Processes, Tooling and Use Cases surrounding this vast topic.
summary:
90DaysOfDevOps is a structured learning project and resource repository designed to help individuals build foundational knowledge of DevOps principles, processes, and tooling. Intended for learners and practitioners seeking to understand the DevOps and DevSecOps spaces, the project provides written content, community sessions, and resources accessible via free, community, and open-source software. 

The repository is organized into distinct learning tracks:
- **DevOps**: Foundational written content developed across a 90-day period and enhanced by the community.
- **DevSecOps**: Content focusing on security and additional topics with perspectives from community subject matter experts.
- **Community Edition**: Video sessions and media shared by the community to expand available learning resources.

The project relies entirely on community contributions, translations, and subject matter expertise rather than vendor sponsorship.

name: sim
description: Sim is the collaborative workspace to build, deploy, and monitor AI agents and workflows. Used by 100,000+ builders.
summary:
Sim is a workspace platform designed to build, deploy, manage, and monitor AI agents and workflows. It provides a unified environment featuring a visual workflow builder, chat interfaces, built-in databases (tables), file management, and knowledge bases to give agents memory and context. The platform supports over 1,000 integrations—including Slack, Notion, HubSpot, and Salesforce—alongside support for major large language models (LLMs), local models via Ollama and vLLM, and code execution environments. 

Sim is intended for developers and teams looking to orchestrate AI workflows and intelligent agents. It offers cloud-hosted, desktop (macOS), and self-hosted deployment options managed via an interactive wizard (`npx sim-setup`). 

The notable technologies used in the project include Next.js (App Router), Bun, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Better Auth, Zod, Tailwind CSS, Shadcn, Streamdown, Zustand, TanStack Query, ReactFlow, Fumadocs, Turborepo, Socket.io, Trigger.dev, E2B, and isolated-vm.

name: netbird
description: Connect your devices, users, and agents into a secure WireGuard®-based overlay network with SSO, MFA and granular access controls.
summary:
NetBird is a configuration-free, peer-to-peer private networking and centralized access control platform designed to build secure virtual private networks for organizations or home users. It combines a WireGuard-based overlay network with granular access policies, SSO and MFA support, identity provider integrations, private DNS, and device posture checks. 

The platform relies on several core components: a NetBird agent running on machines to manage WireGuard, a Management Service to hold network state and distribute updates, ICE via pion/ice for peer-to-peer candidate discovery utilizing STUN servers, a Signal Service for encrypted connection negotiation, and a Relay Service as a fallback when direct NAT traversal is unsuccessful. NetBird also offers quantum-resistance via Rosenpass, browser-based SSH and RDP capabilities, and an experimental NetBird Agent Network for identity-aware access to AI agents and LLM APIs.

Intended for administrators, developers, and organizations seeking secure remote access across diverse environments, the project supports numerous platforms including Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS, FreeBSD, OpenWRT, Docker, and containerized or serverless environments.

name: ProxmoxVE
description: Proxmox VE Helper-Scripts (Community Edition)
summary:
Proxmox VE Helper-Scripts is a community-driven automation project that provides one-command installations for self-hosted services, containers, and virtual machines on Proxmox VE. Designed for Proxmox administrators and system operators, the repository features hundreds of scripts spanning categories such as home automation, media servers, networking tools, databases, monitoring stacks, security, and developer utilities. 

The main capabilities include automated setup via Default or Advanced execution modes, letting users either apply sensible resource allocations quickly or customize container settings, networking, and storage backends. Additionally, installed containers include post-install helpers for managing updates, configuration adjustments, and troubleshooting directly from the Proxmox shell. Requirements include Proxmox VE (Debian-based host OS versions 8.4, 9.0, 9.1, or 9.2) with root shell access and an active internet connection. The project builds upon tteck's original work and is released under the MIT License.

name: awesome-generative-ai-guide
description: A one stop repository for generative AI research updates, interview resources, notebooks and much more!
summary:
The **awesome-generative-ai-guide** is a comprehensive educational hub and resource repository for generative AI. It is designed for individuals looking to use AI in their work, build AI systems, understand underlying research, or prepare for AI-related interviews. 

The repository structures its content—including over 90 free courses, code notebooks, research papers, and video transcripts—into distinct journeys and progressive levels (101 Start, 201 Practitioner, and 301 Advanced). Core topics covered include LLM foundations, prompting, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), fine-tuning, AI agents, evaluation and observability, multimodal applications, production and LLMOps, and safety and security. 

Notable resources include featured LevelUp Labs courses such as *AI Evals for Everyone*, *OpenClaw Mastery for Everyone*, *Agentic AI Crash Course*, *Generative AI Genius*, and *Applied LLMs Mastery*. It also provides a role-based interview preparation hub for AI Engineers, AI Product Managers, Forward-Deployed Engineers, and AI Strategists, alongside living research updates, living research tables, and a glossary of LLM terminology.

name: smolagents
description: 🤗 smolagents: a barebones library for agents that think in code.
summary:
`smolagents` is a lightweight Python library for building and running AI agents that reason and write actions in code. Designed around simplicity with a core implementation under 1,000 lines of code, the library provides first-class support for `CodeAgent` alongside the standard `ToolCallingAgent`. 

Key capabilities include modality-agnostic support for text, vision, video, and audio inputs, as well as being model-agnostic, integrating with Hugging Face Hub, `transformers`, `ollama`, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers via `LiteLLM`. It also features tool-agnostic integration with MCP servers, LangChain, and Hub Spaces. For secure execution of code actions, `smolagents` supports sandboxed environments including Blaxel, E2B, Modal, and Docker, alongside a CLI for running generalist and web-browsing agents.

The project targets developers and AI practitioners seeking a minimal yet extensible framework for agentic workflows, featuring easy agent sharing via the Hugging Face Hub and robust support for open-source and proprietary models.

name: micro
description: A modern and intuitive terminal-based text editor
summary:
Micro is a terminal-based text editor designed to be intuitive, easy to use and install, and serve as a modern successor to the nano editor. It is aimed at developers and users who prefer working in a terminal or regularly edit files over SSH. 

Main capabilities include full mouse support (dragging to select, double-click for words, triple-click for lines), multiple cursors, split screens and tabs, syntax highlighting for over 130 languages, a built-in plugin manager supporting Lua plugins, persistent undo, automatic linting, macros, system clipboard integration, and true color support. It distributes as a single, static binary with no external dependencies.

Micro is written in Go and cross-platform compatible across operating systems supported by the Go runtime and the tcell library.

name: h4cker
description: This repository is maintained by Omar Santos (@santosomar) and includes thousands of resources related to ethical hacking, bug bounties, digital forensics and incident response (DFIR), AI security, vulnerability research, exploit development, reverse engineering, and more. 🔥 Also check: https://hackertraining.org
summary:
HackerRepo.org is a curated cybersecurity repository maintained by Omar Santos that serves as supplemental material for his books, video courses, and live training. The project provides a comprehensive collection of references, scripts, tools, code, labs, and training resources. 

Its main capabilities and structure are organized into several key areas:
- **Cybersecurity Domains**: Covers fundamentals, offensive security, defensive security, application security, cloud and container security, infrastructure and network security, cryptography and PKI, hardware and embedded security, governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), and practice labs.
- **AI**: Features resources on AI security, LLM engineering, AI-assisted incident response and automation, and AI ethics, privacy, and governance.
- **Certifications**: Provides certification roadmaps and exam preparation references for Cisco SCOR, cloud technologies, Kubernetes/CNCF, CompTIA, ISC2, and offensive security certifications.
- **Build Your Own Lab**: Offers resources for constructing cyber ranges and practice labs.
- **Training Reference**: Includes cheat sheets, O'Reilly resources, curated people and projects to follow, and organized tool indexes.

The repository is intended for students, practitioners, and learners seeking structured cybersecurity training, lab setups, and certification preparation materials.

name: nautilus_trader
description: Production-grade Rust-native trading engine with deterministic event-driven architecture
summary:
NautilusTrader is an open-source, production-grade, Rust-native engine designed for multi-asset, multi-venue trading systems. It spans research, deterministic simulation, and live execution within a single event-driven architecture. Python serves as the control plane for strategy logic, configuration, and orchestration, utilizing PyO3 bindings, while trading systems can also be written entirely in Rust. 

Intended for individual and small-team quantitative traders, quantitative researchers, and AI training agents (reinforcement learning/evolutionary strategies), the platform is asset-class-agnostic and supports crypto exchanges (CEX and DEX), traditional markets (FX, equities, futures, options), and betting exchanges. 

Main capabilities include nanosecond-resolution backtesting across multiple venues simultaneously, live execution with identical strategy implementations to research environments, support for advanced order types, conditional triggers, contingency orders, and modular adapters for integrating any REST API or WebSocket feed. Notable technologies utilized include Rust, Python, tokio, mimalloc, PyO3, Redis, Docker, and cargo-nextest.

name: Open-Generative-AI
description: Unrestricted Open-source alternative to AI video platforms — Free AI image & video generation studio with 600+ models (Flux, Midjourney, Kling, Sora, Veo). No content filters. Self-hosted, MIT licensed.
summary:
Open Generative AI is a free, open-source alternative to proprietary AI video and image platforms. It provides a unified studio interface offering access to over 400 models across 14 categories, supporting text-to-image, image-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, audio generation, lip sync, body swap, workflow automation, and agent-driven tasks. The project is designed for users seeking unrestrictive creative workflows with no forced subscriptions, closed ecosystems, or content filters.

Key capabilities include multi-image input supporting up to 14 reference images, specialized cinema camera controls, a visual node-based workflow builder, and local model inference options through `sd.cpp` (bundled C++ engine for image diffusion models like SD 1.5, SDXL, and Z-Image) and `Wan2GP` (a remote Gradio server for video and large image models). 

The platform is targeted at developers, content creators, and entrepreneurs looking to self-host an AI creative suite or launch a white-labeled product using MuAPI. Built as a Next.js monorepo with a shared React component library (`packages/studio`), the project can be run locally via source code or deployed as a desktop application using Electron for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Notable technologies utilized include Next.js 14, React 18, Tailwind CSS, npm workspaces, and the MuAPI API gateway.

name: composer
description: Dependency Manager for PHP
summary:
Composer is a dependency management tool for PHP designed to help developers declare, manage, and install libraries and packages required by PHP projects. Its main capabilities include handling project dependencies, integrating with public and private package registries via Packagist and Private Packagist, and automating package installation and updates. 

The intended users are PHP developers and development teams managing third-party library dependencies. 

Notable technologies and system requirements associated with the project include PHP (supporting versions 7.2.5 and above for the latest release, as well as an LTS version supporting PHP 5.3.2 through 8.1), along with binary dependencies and version control systems such as Git, Mercurial, Fossil, Perforce, Subversion, and archive utilities like unzip and tar. Additionally, the dependency solver incorporates architecture concepts adapted from openSUSE's Libzypp satsolver.

name: vue-cli
description: 🛠️ webpack-based tooling for Vue.js Development
summary: Vue CLI is a standard tooling system for Vue.js development that is now in maintenance mode, with recommendations to use create-vue and Vite for new projects. It is a monorepo maintained with Lerna under the MIT license.

name: harbor
description: An open source trusted cloud native registry project that stores, signs, and scans content.
summary:
Harbor is an open source trusted cloud native registry project that stores, signs, and scans container images and Helm charts. Extending Docker Distribution, Harbor is designed for users in cloud-native environments, container runtimes, and orchestration platforms who require enhanced security, identity management, and operational control. 

Key capabilities include role-based access control (RBAC), policy-based image replication between registries, vulnerability scanning with policy checks, enterprise LDAP/AD integration, OpenID Connect (OIDC) support for single sign-on, image deletion and garbage collection, auditing logs, and a RESTful API with embedded Swagger UI. Harbor can be deployed via Docker Compose, Helm charts, or the Harbor Operator.

name: hallmark
description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
summary:
Hallmark, created by Together AI, is a design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex designed to generate user interfaces that avoid AI-generated aesthetics. The project selects a macrostructure for a given brief, applies one of twenty-one themes (or switches to a made-to-measure Custom design), and passes fifty-seven slop-test gates alongside a pre-emit self-critique to prevent default LLM design patterns. 

The tool operates via four primary verbs: the default action for building new UI, `hallmark audit <target>` to score existing code against anti-patterns without editing, `hallmark redesign <target>` to rebuild structure while preserving copy, information architecture, and brand, and `hallmark study <screenshot | URL>` to extract design DNA—such as macrostructure, type-pairing, and color anchors—while optionally emitting a portable `design.md` file. 

Intended for developers and designers using AI coding assistants, Hallmark outputs self-contained HTML and CSS. It can be installed via an `npx skills` command or by manually placing its configuration files into respective tool directories. Technologies involved include HTML, CSS, and integration rules for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

name: notepad-plus-plus
description: Notepad++ official repository
summary: Notepad++ is a free source code editor and Notepad replacement designed for the MS Windows environment. It supports multiple programming languages and natural languages. The project is governed by the GPL License and runs on all Microsoft-supported Windows systems.

name: phantomjs
description: Scriptable Headless Browser
summary:
PhantomJS is a scriptable headless WebKit engine that allows developers to interact with web pages using JavaScript. Its primary use cases include headless web testing, page automation using standard DOM APIs or libraries like jQuery, programmatic screen capture of CSS, SVG, and Canvas content, and network monitoring for performance analysis with HAR export capabilities. 

Key features include multiplatform support for Windows, Mac OS X, Linux, and other Unices, native and fast implementation of web standards without emulation, and pure headless operation on Linux (without X11) making it suitable for continuous integration environments, Amazon EC2, Heroku, and Iron.io. The intended users are developers, testers, and system administrators. Technologies mentioned include JavaScript, WebKit, DOM, CSS, SVG, Canvas, and jQuery. 

Development of PhantomJS is currently suspended until further notice. It is distributed as free open-source software under the BSD license.

name: chroma
description: Search infrastructure for AI
summary: Chroma is an open-source data infrastructure for AI that functions as an embedding database and vector search engine. It provides tools for AI developers to build applications with large language models by handling tokenization, embedding, and indexing automatically. The core API supports creating collections, adding and querying documents with metadata and text filters, and supporting both in-memory prototyping and a client-server mode. Chroma offers client libraries for Python (`chromadb`) and JavaScript (`npm install chromadb`), alongside a hosted serverless service called Chroma Cloud that powers vector, hybrid, and full-text search. The project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: standard
description: 🌟 JavaScript Style Guide, with linter & automatic code fixer
summary:
JavaScript Standard Style is a zero-configuration JavaScript style guide, linter, and formatter designed for developers and project maintainers. It enforces code quality and consistency by eliminating the need for configuration files like `.eslintrc` and avoiding stylistic debates (bikeshedding). 

Main capabilities include automated code formatting via `standard --fix`, catching syntax and style errors early to streamline code reviews, and providing a Node.js API (`lintFiles` and `lintText`) along with command-line usage. It supports environment configurations such as Mocha, Jest, Web Workers, and Service Workers, and integrates with experimental features and custom parsers like `@babel/eslint-parser`. Related ecosystem tools include `ts-standard` for TypeScript and variants like `semistandard` and `standardx`.

Intended users are JavaScript developers, open-source maintainers, and teams seeking automated code standard enforcement. Notable technologies utilized include Node.js, npm, ESLint, and Git pre-commit hooks, with available integrations for text editors and IDEs such as VS Code, Sublime Text, Atom, Vim, Emacs, and WebStorm.

name: Seal
description: 🦭 Video/Audio Downloader for Android, based on yt-dlp
summary:
Seal is an open-source video and audio downloader for Android. It serves as a graphical user interface (GUI) for **yt-dlp**, utilizing **youtubedl-android**. 

Main capabilities include:
- Downloading videos and audio files from any platform supported by yt-dlp.
- Embedding metadata and video thumbnails into extracted audio files using **mutagen**.
- Downloading entire playlists with a single click.
- Utilizing an embedded **aria2c** instance as an external downloader.
- Embedding subtitles into downloaded videos.
- Executing custom yt-dlp commands with templates, along with in-app download and template management.

The application targets Android users seeking a user-friendly download utility. It features a Material Design 3 user interface with dynamic color themes. The app's architecture and logic are implemented in pure **Kotlin**, utilizing a single activity structure with Jetpack Compose destinations.

name: project-guidelines
description: A set of best practices for JavaScript projects
summary:
This repository provides comprehensive guidelines and best practices for developing and maintaining JavaScript projects. Its primary purpose is to help engineering teams establish consistent standards across codebases, making projects easier to maintain, scale, and collaborate on. 

The guide covers eleven core topics:
- **Git:** Feature-branch workflows, interactive rebasing, branch protection, and commit message standards.
- **Documentation:** README structures, inline commenting, and keeping documentation up to date.
- **Environments:** Environment-specific configuration, environment variables, validation via `joi`, and consistent development environments using `nvm` and Docker.
- **Dependencies:** Lockfiles, package auditing, and monitoring unused packages with tools like `depcheck`.
- **Testing:** Unit testing conventions, test-driven principles, pure functions, and static typing.
- **Structure and Naming:** Feature-based directory organization and clear component naming rules.
- **Code Style:** Modern JavaScript syntax, ESLint configuration (incorporating Airbnb guidelines and Flow rules), Prettier formatting, EditorConfig, and Git hooks.
- **Logging:** Production-ready logging practices using libraries such as `winston` or `node-bunyan`.
- **API Design & Security:** Resource-oriented RESTful design, JSON property naming rules, HTTP status codes, versioning, pagination, rate limiting, and security checklists.
- **Accessibility (a11y):** Auditing with Lighthouse and axe, a11y linters, semantic markup, contrast requirements, and alt text.
- **Licensing:** Proper usage of open-source licenses and media rights.

Intended users are JavaScript developers and project maintainers seeking to enforce robust engineering standards. Notable technologies referenced include JavaScript, Node.js, Git, Docker, ESLint, Prettier, Airbnb style guide, FlowType, Winston, Bunyan, Lighthouse, and axe-core.

name: Hover
description: A collection of CSS3 powered hover effects to be applied to links, buttons, logos, SVG, featured images and so on. Easily apply to your own elements, modify or just use for inspiration. Available in CSS, Sass, and LESS.
summary: Hover.css is a collection of CSS3-powered hover effects designed for links, buttons, logos, SVG elements, and featured images. It is intended for web developers, designers, and front-end engineers who want to apply animations to user interface elements, either by copying and pasting individual effects into custom stylesheets or by referencing the complete stylesheet. The project is available in CSS, Sass, and LESS formats. Notable technologies used within the development workflow include CSS3 transitions, animations, transforms, pseudo-elements, Grunt, Sass, and LESS.

name: nx
description: The Monorepo Platform that amplifies both developers and AI agents. Nx optimizes your builds, scales your CI, and fixes failed PRs automatically. Ship in half the time.
summary:
Nx is a monorepo solution designed for TypeScript and polyglot codebases, built with Rust for performance and extensible via TypeScript. It provides fast builds and incremental execution by caching unchanged outputs and running only affected tasks. 

Key capabilities include an AI-native CLI optimized for autonomous AI agents, an integrated CI solution featuring remote caching, task distribution across machines, automatic test splitting, and a self-healing CI pipeline that detects failures, analyzes root causes, and proposes fixes. It also includes a polyglot plugin system for automatic task discovery and code scaffolding. 

Nx is used by organizations ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies. It supports integration with npm, pnpm, yarn workspaces, Vite, Webpack, Jest, Vitest, ESLint, Gradle, Maven, .NET, Go, and major CI providers like GitHub Actions, GitLab, and Azure.

name: deskflow
description: Share a single keyboard and mouse between multiple computers.
summary:
Deskflow is a free and open-source software application that functions as a software-based KVM switch, enabling users to control multiple nearby computers using a single keyboard, mouse, or trackpad. 

Main capabilities include seamless multi-computer control, clipboard sharing, and default TLS encryption. It features native support for Wayland on Linux via `libei` and `libportal`. The project is intended for users seeking to share peripherals across different machines without hardware switches. 

Deskflow supports major operating systems including Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD. Notable technologies and libraries used in the project include Qt (version 6.7+ for the GUI on Linux), C++, Homebrew, Flatpak, and the OpenSSL exception under the GPL-2.0 license.

name: CloudflareSpeedTest
description: 🌩「自选优选 IP」测试 Cloudflare CDN 延迟和速度，获取最快 IP ！当然也支持其他 CDN / 多个解析 IP 的网站 ~
summary:
XIU2/CloudflareSpeedTest is a command-line utility written in Go designed to test the latency and download speed of Cloudflare CDN IP addresses (IPv4 and IPv6) to identify optimal, low-latency, and high-performance endpoints, particularly for users in mainland China experiencing poor default routing. The software also supports testing other CDNs and websites with multiple resolution IPs.

Main capabilities include TCPing and HTTPing latency measurement modes, packet loss filtering, speed sorting, customizable concurrency threads, and region-specific matching via IATA airport codes or country/city codes. It supports platforms such as Windows, Linux, and macOS, and outputs detailed results to the console or a CSV file. Intended users are developers, network administrators, and general users seeking to optimize CDN connection performance. Notable technologies utilized include Go and support for CDNs such as Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, Fastly, Gcore, CDN77, and Bunny.

name: ente
description: 💚 End-to-end encrypted cloud for everything.
summary:
Ente is a fully open-source, end-to-end encrypted platform designed for secure cloud data storage without requiring trust in the service provider. The monorepo contains both the backend server and client applications across iOS, Android, F-Droid, Web, Linux, macOS, and Windows. 

The repository includes three main applications:
- **Ente Photos:** A privacy-focused alternative to Apple and Google Photos offering 3x data replication, face detection, semantic search, private sharing, collaborative albums, and background uploads.
- **Ente Auth:** An end-to-end encrypted two-factor authentication (2FA) app serving as an alternative to Authy.
- **Ente Locker:** A secure space to protect credentials, important documents, and notes with end-to-end encryption, private sharing, and emergency access configurations.

Intended for users seeking privacy-centric, zero-knowledge cloud storage alternatives, Ente supports self-hosting in addition to managed tiers. The codebase and cryptography have undergone external security audits by Cure53, Symbolic Software, and Fallible.

name: Mindustry
description: The automation tower defense RTS
summary: Mindustry is an automation tower defense real-time strategy (RTS) game written in Java. The project enables players to construct supply chains, feed resources into turrets, build production structures, and defend against waves of enemies. Intended for gamers and developers, Mindustry supports desktop, server, and Android platforms. The technology stack utilizes Java, Gradle, and JDK 17, featuring build-time code generation for entities, network packets (`mindustry.gen`), and asset references.

name: authelia
description: The Single Sign-On Multi-Factor portal for web apps. OpenID Certified™ and Post-Quantum Cryptography Ready.
summary:
Authelia is an open-source authentication and authorization server designed to provide multi-factor authentication and single sign-on (SSO) capabilities for applications via a web portal. It functions as a companion for reverse proxies and ingress controllers—including Nginx, Traefik, Caddy, Skipper, Envoy, and HAProxy—by allowing, denying, or redirecting HTTP requests.

Main capabilities include OpenID Connect 1.0 and OAuth 2.0 support, Post-Quantum Cryptography, passwordless authentication via WebAuthn (Passkeys), email-based password resets, brute-force protection, and fine-grained access control rules based on subdomains, users, user groups, request URIs, methods, and networks. It supports multiple second-factor methods such as FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys (e.g., YubiKey), Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP), and mobile push notifications via Duo. The project also provides high availability through remote databases and Redis.

Intended users include administrators and developers seeking to secure internal infrastructure and web services behind a centralized access control plane. Notable technologies utilized include Go, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Redis, OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, and WebAuthn.

name: create-t3-app
description: The best way to start a full-stack, typesafe Next.js app
summary:
`create-t3-app` is an interactive command-line interface (CLI) designed to streamline the initialization and scaffolding of full-stack, typesafe web applications using the T3 Stack. The project aims to provide developers with a modular setup experience where each component is optional and tailored to specific project needs. 

The main capabilities center around generating customized project templates adhering to core axioms: solving specific problems without bloat, bleeding responsibly by adopting bleeding-edge tech only in low-risk areas, and maintaining strict end-to-end typesafety. 

Intended users are web developers looking for an opinionated, productive starting point for full-stack applications. The notable technologies utilized and integrated within the stack include Next.js, tRPC, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, Prisma, Drizzle, and NextAuth.js.

name: maple-font
description: Maple Mono: Open source monospace font with round corner, ligatures and Nerd-Font icons for IDE and terminal, fine-grained customization options. 带连字和控制台图标的圆角等宽字体，中英文宽度完美2:1，细粒度的自定义选项
summary:
Maple Mono is an open-source monospace font designed to smooth the coding flow and enhance the user's working experience. It provides variable font formats, fine-grained italic glyphs, round corners, and numerous smart ligatures alongside first-class Nerd-Font support for terminal icons. The project also offers Chinese and Japanese language support (CN versions based on Resource Han Rounded) with 2:1 alignment for multilingual display and Markdown tables. 

Intended for developers and users seeking customizable coding typography, Maple Mono includes build scripts and configuration options (`config.json`) to adjust font weights, glyph widths, line heights, presets, and OpenType features. Notable technologies used in its development and building process include Python, Docker, and the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

name: swift-algorithm-club
description: Algorithms and data structures in Swift, with explanations!
summary:
The Swift Algorithm Club provides open-source implementations of popular algorithms and data structures written in Swift, accompanied by detailed explanations. The project is designed for computer science students and self-taught programmers seeking to learn algorithm theory, emphasizing code clarity and readability over reusable production libraries. 

The repository covers searching algorithms (such as Binary Search and Boyer-Moore), sorting algorithms (including Quicksort, Merge Sort, and Radix Sort), string search, compression, mathematics, machine learning techniques, graph operations, puzzles, and data structures like stacks, queues, trees, and hash tables. Technologies used include Swift 4.2 and Xcode 10.

name: keepassxc
description: KeePassXC is a cross-platform community-driven port of the Windows application “KeePass Password Safe”.
summary:
KeePassXC is a modern, secure, and open-source password manager designed for Windows, macOS, and Linux systems to store and manage sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, URLs, attachments, and notes in an offline, encrypted KDBX format database (supporting KDBX4 and KDBX3). 

Intended for users with high demands for secure personal data management, it offers core capabilities including a password generator, advanced search, TOTP storage and generation, YubiKey and OnlyKey challenge-response support, Auto-Type, browser integration (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Chromium, Vivaldi, Brave, and Tor-Browser) with passkey support, and database imports from CSV, 1Password, Bitwarden, Proton Pass, and KeePass1. Advanced features include database reports, CSV/XML/HTML exports, field references, file attachments, entry history, a command line interface (`keepassxc-cli`), SSH Agent integration, FreeDesktop.org Secret Service support, and additional encryption choices such as Twofish and ChaCha20.

name: swagger-ui
description: Swagger UI is a collection of HTML, JavaScript, and CSS assets that dynamically generate beautiful documentation from a Swagger-compliant API.
summary:
Swagger UI allows development teams and end consumers to visualize and interact with API resources without requiring the implementation logic. Automatically generated from the OpenAPI (Swagger) Specification, it provides visual documentation to facilitate backend implementation and client-side consumption. 

The project publishes multiple modules, including traditional npm packages for single-page applications, dependency-free modules for server-side or unresolvable dependency projects (`swagger-ui-dist`), and a React component package (`swagger-ui-react`). It also supports plain HTML, JavaScript, and CSS via direct releases. 

Intended users include developers building applications, teams consuming APIs, and contributors working with React or standard web technologies. Notable technologies utilized include OpenAPI, React, Webpack, Browserify, Scarf for analytics, and Cypress for end-to-end integration testing.

name: immer
description: Create the next immutable state by mutating the current one
summary: Immer is a JavaScript library designed to create the next immutable state tree by simply modifying the current tree. It enables developers to work with immutable state using a convenient mutable API. The project targets JavaScript and React developers seeking efficient state management solutions.

name: postcss
description: Transforming styles with JS plugins
summary:
PostCSS is a software tool designed to transform styles using JavaScript plugins. It parses CSS files into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) and provides an API for plugins to analyze rules, lint code, transpile future CSS syntax, support variables and mixins, inline images, and automate vendor prefixing. 

Intended for web developers, frontend engineers, and enterprises, PostCSS integrates with build tools and task runners such as Webpack, Parcel, Gulp, npm scripts, Browserify, and various IDEs like VS Code, WebStorm, and Vim. Notable technologies and related tools mentioned include Autoprefixer, Stylelint, cssnano, and CSS-in-JS solutions like astroturf.

name: todomvc
description: Helping you select a JavaScript framework - Todo apps for React.js, Angular, Vue and many more
summary:
TodoMVC is an open-source project designed to help developers evaluate and select JavaScript frameworks and UI libraries by providing functionally identical implementations of a standard Todo application. It serves as a side-by-side comparison tool for syntax, structure, and idioms across various modern technologies. 

The project's intended users are software developers, web engineers, and AI coding agents seeking to understand or implement basic UI patterns. Main capabilities include building, serving, and testing standardized applications using an explicit app specification via a Cypress test suite.
