Maintained examples feature prominent modern technologies such as React 19, Vue 3.5, Angular 21, Svelte 5 (with runes), Preact 10, Lit 3.3, and React Redux 9 (with Redux Toolkit 2), alongside numerous legacy framework showcases. Tooling references include bundlers like Vite, webpack, and rollup. Additionally, TodoMVC forms the core of the cross-browser Speedometer benchmark utilized by major browser engines for performance optimization.

name: SpringAll
description: 循序渐进，学习Spring Boot、Spring Boot & Shiro、Spring Batch、Spring Cloud、Spring Cloud Alibaba、Spring Security & Spring Security OAuth2，博客Spring系列源码：https://mrbird.cc
summary:
This repository contains source code and tutorials for a comprehensive Spring series matching the author's personal blog. The project aims to provide practical guides and code examples covering enterprise Java development topics, including Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Spring Security, Spring Security OAuth2, Apache Shiro, Apache Dubbo, and Spring Batch. 

Main capabilities and modules include basic and advanced Spring Boot configurations (such as multi-datasources, caching with Redis and Ehcache, WebFlux, Kafka, MongoDB, and security defenses), microservice architectures via Spring Cloud components (Eureka, Ribbon, Hystrix, Feign, Zuul, Config, Sleuth, and Alibaba Nacos and Sentinel), security implementations using Shiro and Spring Security, distributed RPC services with Dubbo and Zookeeper, and batch data processing using Spring Batch. Additionally, it offers deep-dive guides into foundational Spring framework principles like bean lifecycles, AOP, declarative transactions, and circular dependencies. 

The tutorials are intended for Java developers and Spring practitioners seeking hands-on integration examples and architectural patterns for modern cloud-native and enterprise applications.

name: reflex
description: 🕸️ Web apps in pure Python 🐍
summary: Reflex is a library designed to build performant, customizable full-stack web applications in pure Python without requiring JavaScript. Intended for developers seeking an accessible yet scalable web development framework, Reflex handles both frontend UI definition and backend state management entirely in Python. Main capabilities include fast refreshes for instant previewing during development, event handlers for asynchronous processing, and UI components such as inputs, buttons, headings, and images. Notable technologies utilized include Python, uv, and OpenAI integration.

name: hyperfine
description: A command-line benchmarking tool
summary: Hyperfine is a command-line benchmarking tool designed for developers and system administrators to measure the execution time of arbitrary shell commands. Its primary capabilities include statistical analysis across multiple runs, statistical outlier detection, support for warmup runs, cache-clearing command execution before timing runs, and automated shell-spawning time correction. Additionally, it supports parameterized benchmarks with numerical scans or custom lists and enables result exports to CSV, JSON, Markdown, and AsciiDoc formats. The tool is cross-platform, compatible with Linux, macOS, and Windows.

name: pydantic
description: Data validation using Python type hints
summary: Pydantic is a data validation and parsing library for Python 3.10+ that enforces types using native Python type hints. It allows developers to define data structures via classes inheriting from `BaseModel` to validate, coerce, and serialize external inputs. Designed to be fast and extensible, Pydantic integrates with IDEs and linters, supporting incremental upgrades from V1 to the ground-up rewrite in V2. It is installed via `pip` or `conda`, and is complemented by related tooling like Pydantic Logfire for application monitoring.

name: celery
description: Distributed Task Queue (development branch)
summary:
Celery is an asynchronous task queue and job management system based on distributed message passing. Designed primarily for Python applications, it enables work to be distributed across threads, machines, or datacenters using dedicated worker processes that monitor queues for incoming tasks via a message broker. 

Main capabilities include high availability with automatic reconnection and failover, high throughput supporting millions of tasks per minute, and extensive extensibility for custom serialization, concurrency pools, and storage backends. It integrates seamlessly with web frameworks such as Django, Flask, FastAPI, Pyramid, and Tornado.

Celery supports multiple message transports including RabbitMQ, Redis, Amazon SQS, and Google Pub/Sub; concurrency models such as Prefork, Eventlet, and gevent; and numerous result stores including SQLAlchemy, Django ORM, Redis, Apache Cassandra, and Elasticsearch. Intended for developers building scalable distributed applications, Celery requires Python 3.10 or newer (for version 5.7.x) and is licensed under the New BSD License.

name: machine-learning-for-software-engineers
description: A complete daily plan for studying to become a machine learning engineer.
summary:
This repository provides a top-down, hands-on learning path designed specifically for software engineers transitioning into machine learning engineering. The curriculum prioritizes practical application and abstracts heavy mathematical prerequisites for beginners, following a practice-first methodology. 

Intended for software developers and programmers looking to build machine learning expertise without pursuing traditional advanced computer science degrees, the guide outlines a structured daily study plan. It compiles curated resources including beginner and practical books, Kaggle knowledge competitions, video series, MOOCs, open-source contribution targets, AI coding games, podcasts, communities, conferences, and interview questions. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced throughout the roadmap include Python, R, scikit-learn, and TensorFlow.

name: redash
description: Make Your Company Data Driven. Connect to any data source, easily visualize, dashboard and share your data.
summary:
Redash is a browser-based tool designed to enable users of all technical levels to explore, query, visualize, and share data from various sources. Intended for SQL users and organizations seeking data-driven decision-making, Redash provides a query editor with schema browsers and auto-complete, drag-and-drop visualizations, shareable dashboards, scheduled refreshes, and data change alerts. It also offers a REST API and an extensible data source API. 

Redash features native support for over 35 SQL and NoSQL data sources, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Snowflake, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, InfluxDB, and Prometheus.

name: xgboost
description: Scalable, Portable and Distributed Gradient Boosting (GBDT, GBRT or GBM) Library,  for Python, R, Java, Scala, C and more. Runs on single machine, Hadoop, Spark, Dask, Flink and DataFlow
summary: XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting) is an optimized distributed gradient boosting library designed for high efficiency, flexibility, and portability. It implements machine learning algorithms under the Gradient Boosting framework, providing parallel tree boosting (GBDT, GBM) to solve data science problems quickly and accurately. The library enables the same code to run across major distributed environments—including Kubernetes, Hadoop, SGE, Dask, Spark, and PySpark—capable of handling datasets exceeding billions of examples. Intended for data scientists and developers, XGBoost originates from a research project at the University of Washington and is licensed under the Apache-2 license.

name: void
summary:
Void is a deprecated open-source desktop application and fork of Microsoft VS Code designed to use AI agents on codebases, checkpoint and visualize changes, and bring any AI model or host locally while communicating directly with providers without retaining user data. 

As a VS Code fork reference, Void features a custom build pipeline mounting React and scoped Tailwind CSS, GitHub Actions for packaging, signing, and auto-updating, and an AI provider architecture built from scratch supporting FIM autocomplete, custom grammars for `<thinking>` and tool tags, IPC, and Content Security Policy (CSP) compliance. It includes custom services such as EditCodeService for streaming code diffs token by token and VoidModelService for background file editing and OS file synchronization with text buffers. Technologies used include React, Tailwind, and TypeScript.

name: GoodbyeDPI
description: GoodbyeDPI — Deep Packet Inspection circumvention utility (for Windows)
summary:
GoodbyeDPI is a Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) circumvention utility designed for Windows (7 through 11) to bypass ISP-level censorship that blocks specific websites. It counters both passive DPI systems (which reply faster than destinations using optical splitters or port mirroring) and active DPI systems connected in sequence. 

The software utilizes the WinDivert driver and Windows Filtering Platform to process network traffic in userspace. Its core capabilities include TCP-level fragmentation, HTTP/HTTPS header manipulation (such as modifying Host header case, spacing, and values), and sending fake HTTP or HTTPS packets using custom TTL values, incorrect checksums, or altered sequence numbers to prevent DPI classification. It also supports DNS redirection features and optional blacklist filtering. 

Intended for users seeking to bypass internet censorship, GoodbyeDPI can be run interactively or installed as a Windows service using bundled command scripts. The project is built using GNU Make and MinGW, relying on WinDivert as its primary dependency.

name: Web
description: 千古前端图文教程，超详细的前端入门到进阶知识库。从零开始学前端，做一名精致优雅的前端工程师。
summary:
This repository contains an ultra-detailed Web front-end tutorial and knowledge base designed to take learners from beginner to advanced levels. Titled "千古前端图文教程" (Qiangu's Front-End Illustrated Tutorial), the project aims to provide an accessible learning path for absolute beginners with no prior programming experience, helping them become proficient front-end engineers. 

Main capabilities include serving as a comprehensive learning resource, offering structured learning roadmaps, and functioning as a reference dictionary for front-end developers to review concepts and fill knowledge gaps. The intended users are front-end beginners, individuals transitioning into web development, and developers looking for high-quality study materials to improve learning efficiency. The project is maintained as an open-source text and web-based guide available at web.qianguyihao.com and GitHub.

name: repomix
description: 📦 Repomix is a powerful tool that packs your entire repository into a single, AI-friendly file. Perfect for when you need to feed your codebase to Large Language Models (LLMs) or other AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Gemini, Gemma, Llama, Grok, and more.
summary:
Repomix is an open-source command-line tool, library, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that packs an entire code repository into a single, AI-friendly format (such as XML, Markdown, JSON, or plain text) for use with large language models and developer tools like Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and others. 

Its main capabilities include token counting and token count tree visualization, token budgeting, Git integration (sorting by change frequency, logs, and diffs), customizable file inclusion/exclusion using glob patterns and ignore files, and automatic code compression powered by Tree-sitter to extract essential signatures while stripping implementation details. It also features built-in security scans using Secretlint to detect sensitive credentials, external file preprocessing via custom command-based processors, output file splitting for large codebases, watch mode for auto-repacking, and the generation of structured Claude Agent Skills.

Repomix is intended for developers, AI agents, and CI pipelines seeking to feed codebase context efficiently into generative AI systems. It can be run via CLI (`npx repomix`), Docker, GitHub Actions, browser/VS Code extensions, a web interface at repomix.com, or used programmatically as a Node.js library. Notable technologies used include TypeScript, JavaScript, Tree-sitter, Secretlint, and WebAssembly (WASM).

name: clash-rules
description: 🦄️ 🎃 👻 Clash Premium 规则集(RULE-SET)，兼容 ClashX Pro、Clash for Windows 等基于 Clash Premium 内核的客户端。
summary:
This project generates rule sets (RULE-SET) tailored for the Clash Premium kernel and compatible Clash GUI clients such as ClashX Pro, clash-party, clash-verge-rev, Clash for Windows, clashmi, Clash Meta for Android, and OpenClash. The repository automatically builds and updates its rules daily using GitHub Actions. 

Data sources include @Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat, @v2fly/domain-list-community, @felixonmars/dnsmasq-china-list, and @17mon/china_ip_list. The generated rule files provide categorized network traffic routing lists—such as direct connection domains, proxy domains, ad-rejection lists, Apple and Google domain lists, GFWList domains, and IP address ranges for Telegram, local networks, and mainland China. 

Intended users are individuals utilizing Clash Premium or compatible clients who require organized rule providers for whitelist or blacklist traffic routing configurations. Notable technologies and formats utilized include YAML, GitHub Actions, and standard Clash rule-provider configurations.

name: mlx
description: MLX: An array framework for Apple silicon
summary:
MLX is an array framework designed by machine learning researchers for machine learning research, tailored for Apple silicon as well as CPU and GPU devices. It aims to provide efficient model training and deployment while maintaining a conceptually simple design that allows researchers to easily extend and explore new ideas.

Main capabilities include a unified memory model where arrays live in shared memory and can be processed across supported devices without data transfers, lazy computation, dynamic graph construction, and composable function transformations supporting automatic differentiation, automatic vectorization, and computation graph optimization. 

Intended users are machine learning researchers and developers. The framework provides a Python API mirroring NumPy, fully featured C++, C, and Swift APIs, and higher-level packages (`mlx.nn` and `mlx.optimizers`) with APIs closely following PyTorch.

Notable technologies and models integrated or supported through examples include NumPy, PyTorch, Jax, ArrayFire, LLaMA, LoRA, Stable Diffusion, and OpenAI's Whisper.

name: Awesome-CV
description: :page_facing_up: Awesome CV is LaTeX template for your outstanding job application
summary:
Awesome CV is a LaTeX template designed for creating professional job application documents, including a Curriculum Vitae (CV), résumé, or cover letter. Inspired by Fancy CV, the project features clean, semantic markup that allows users to easily customize and compile their documents into PDF format. 

Intended for job seekers, professionals, and academics—particularly those in math and computer science—the template utilizes a full TeX distribution (such as TeX Live) or Docker for compilation via `xelatex`. Notable technologies and styling resources integrated into the project include LaTeX, the FontAwesome6 LaTeX package, the Roboto font, and Source Sans Pro. Additionally, templates can be edited directly on Overleaf.

name: openwrt
description: This repository is a mirror of https://git.openwrt.org/openwrt/openwrt.git It is for reference only and is not active for check-ins.  We will continue to accept Pull Requests here. They will be merged via staging trees then into openwrt.git.
summary:
OpenWrt is a Linux operating system designed for embedded devices, providing a fully writable filesystem and package management (`opkg`) instead of static vendor firmware. It enables users to fully customize device applications and configurations, while serving as a framework for developers to build applications without constructing a complete firmware. 

Main capabilities include prebuilt firmware images available via the OpenWrt Firmware Selector, a build system for cross-compiling the GNU/Linux kernel and applications, a modular web interface (`LuCI`), and support for community-ported packages, routing protocols, and video display servers (Xorg and Wayland). The project is intended for both end users seeking device customization and developers creating embedded software. Building custom firmware requires a GNU/Linux, BSD, or macOS system with standard development tools (such as `gcc`, `make`, `python3`, and `perl`).

name: semantic-kernel
description: Integrate cutting-edge LLM technology quickly and easily into your apps
summary:
Semantic Kernel (now Microsoft Agent Framework) is a model-agnostic, enterprise-ready software development kit and orchestration framework designed for developers to build, orchestrate, and deploy intelligent AI agents and multi-agent systems. 

Main capabilities include multi-provider language model support (such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, Nvidia NIM, Ollama, LMStudio, and ONNX), modular AI agents equipped with tools and planning capabilities, multi-agent workflow orchestration, and multimodal processing for text, vision, and audio. It features a rich plugin ecosystem supporting native code functions, prompt templates, OpenAPI specs, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), alongside vector database integrations like Azure AI Search, Elasticsearch, and Chroma. 

Targeted at developers building single assistants or complex enterprise-grade multi-agent workflows, the framework supports Python (3.10+), .NET (10.0+), and Java (JDK 17+) across Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms. It provides structured business process modeling, strict observability, and secure APIs.

name: Pixelle-Video
description: 🚀 AI 全自动短视频引擎 | AI Fully Automated Short Video Engine
summary:
Pixelle-Video is an AI-powered automated short video engine designed for users with zero video editing experience. By simply inputting a theme topic, the system automatically writes scripts, generates AI illustrations or dynamic videos, synthesizes voice narration, adds background music, and merges the elements into a final video. 

Main capabilities include automated script generation, image and video creation pipelines, action transfer, digital human talking heads, text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis, multi-language support, custom asset analysis, and BGM integration. The architecture supports both modular workflows via ComfyUI and RunningHub, as well as direct API integrations with media model providers. 

The software targets content creators, marketers, educators, and hobbyists seeking zero-barrier video production. Notable technologies and integrations referenced include Python, Streamlit, uv, ffmpeg, ComfyUI, RunningHub, Edge-TTS, Index-TTS, Ollama, and various large language and media models such as GPT, Qwen (通义千问), DeepSeek, WAN 2.1, DashScope, OpenAI, Seedream, Seedance, and Kling.

name: reverse-interview
description: Questions to ask the company during your interview
summary:
The Reverse Interview repository is a curated, multilingual list of questions designed for technology job applicants to ask interviewers. Its purpose is to help candidates evaluate potential employers, uncover red flags, and gauge company culture, team dynamics, and engineering practices. 

The questions are organized into categories covering the specific role, technical stacks and workflows, team structure, coworkers, company maturity and career progression, social issues, conflict resolution, business models, remote work policies, compensation, and time-off benefits. Notable technical and operational topics include CI/CD, source control, testing, bug tracking, disaster recovery, documentation, static code analysis, and dependency management. The project is intended for software developers and tech professionals seeking to drive more comprehensive and informative technical interviews.

name: the-super-tiny-compiler
description: :snowman: Possibly the smallest compiler ever
summary: The Super Tiny Compiler is an ultra-simplified JavaScript example demonstrating all major pieces of a modern compiler from end to end. The project purpose is to serve as a guided educational tool to help users learn how most compilers work and understand underlying concepts used in various development tools. It is intended for developers and learners curious about compiler architecture. The codebase is written in JavaScript and includes a test suite that can be executed using Node.js via `node test.js`.

name: fingerprintjs
description: The most advanced free and open-source browser fingerprinting library
summary: FingerprintJS is an open-source, client-side browser fingerprinting library that queries browser attributes to compute a hashed visitor identifier. Operating entirely in the browser, the generated fingerprint persists across incognito and private browsing modes, as well as instances when browser data is purged. The project is distributed under the MIT license and supports installation via npm and CDN. Intended for developers seeking client-side device identification, it includes API references and sample usage for platforms like React and StackBlitz.

name: mastra
description: Mastra is the modern TypeScript framework for AI-powered applications and agents.
summary:
Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI-powered applications, autonomous agents, and workflows. Designed for developers scaling AI products from prototypes to production, it integrates with frontend and backend frameworks such as React, Next.js, and Node.js, or deploys as a standalone server. 

Main capabilities include a model router connecting to over 40 providers (including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini), an autonomous agent system with tool-use reasoning, and a graph-based workflow engine supporting control flow operations like `.then()`, `.branch()`, and `.parallel()`. Mastra also features human-in-the-loop capabilities with state persistence for pausing and resuming execution, context management with conversation history and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), Model Context Protocol (MCP) server authoring, and built-in evaluation and observability tools. UIs can be built using integrations with Vercel's AI SDK UI and CopilotKit.

name: live
description: ✯ 可直连访问的电视/广播图标库与相关工具项目 ✯ 🔕 永久免费 直连访问 完整开源 不断完善的台标 支持IPv4/IPv6双栈访问 🔕
summary:
This project is a free, open-source television and radio icon library paired with related utility tools, featuring direct access and support for IPv4 and IPv6 dual-stack connectivity. 

**Main Capabilities & Tools:**
- **Icon Library:** Direct access paths for TV (`/tv/{name}.png`) and radio (`/radio/{name}.png`) logos, with community contributions accepted via Pull Requests.
- **EPG Interface:** Provides an EPG XML endpoint (`/e.xml`) distributed via 112114.xyz.
- **Format Conversion Tools:** Web-based tools for TXT-to-M3U and online M3U-to-TXT conversion.
- **Media Utilities:** Includes a Bing Daily Picture service, an online m3u8 downloader, and a web-based M3U8 Web Player.
- **Subscription Support:** Guides and demo files (`demo.m3u`) for creating and hosting custom m3u subscription lists using GitHub Pages.

**Intended Users:**
Live television and radio enthusiasts, developers, and users managing custom IPTV/m3u playlists who require standardized channel logos, EPG data, and format conversion utilities.

**Notable Technologies:**
- GitHub (hosting, Pages, Actions, Issues)
- CloudFlare (CDN, security protection, Pages hosting)
- Vercel (hosting for conversion tools)
- IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking

name: crush
description: Glamourous agentic coding for all 💘
summary:
Crush is a terminal-based AI coding assistant developed by Charmbracelet that integrates user tools, codebases, and workflows with large language models (LLMs). Built on the Charm ecosystem, it targets developers seeking an interactive command-line interface for AI-assisted programming.

Main capabilities include multi-model support with mid-session switching, session-based project management, LSP enhancement for codebase context, and extensibility via MCPs (Model Context Protocols supporting `http`, `stdio`, and `sse`). It also supports agent skills based on the Agent Skills standard, custom prompt contexts, permission controls, and local model auto-discovery.

Crush works across macOS, Linux, Windows, Android, and BSD terminals. It connects natively to Charm Hyper or supports OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs, local providers like Ollama and llama.cpp, Google Vertex AI, and Amazon Bedrock. Configuration is managed through a Bash-based `crushrc` file or traditional JSON files, and project initialization generates context files such as `AGENTS.md`.

name: spleeter
description: Deezer source separation library including pretrained models.
summary: Spleeter is an open-source audio source separation library developed by Deezer, written in Python and powered by TensorFlow. It provides state-of-the-art pretrained models to split audio tracks into multiple stems, supporting 2-stem (vocals and accompaniment), 4-stem (vocals, drums, bass, and other), and 5-stem (vocals, drums, bass, piano, and other) configurations. Designed for high performance and exceptional speed—capable of processing 4-stem separation significantly faster than real-time on a GPU—Spleeter can be used directly from the command line, integrated into development pipelines as a Python library, or deployed via Docker and Google Colab. It is intended for developers, researchers, and audio professionals, and its models have been integrated into various third-party digital audio workstations and software suites such as iZotope RX, SpectralLayers, VirtualDJ, and djayPRO. The project relies on Poetry for dependency management and testing.

name: table
description: 🤖 Headless UI for building powerful tables & datagrids for TS/JS -  React-Table, Vue-Table, Solid-Table, Svelte-Table
summary:
TanStack Table is a headless table library designed for building powerful datagrids with complete control over markup, styles, and behavior. It provides a framework-agnostic core alongside official bindings and adapters for React, Preact, Vue, Solid, Svelte, Angular, Ember, Lit, Alpine, and Octane. 

Main capabilities include sorting, filtering, grouping, aggregation, row selection, virtualization, and server-side data handling. The library is fully customizable, allowing developers to bring their own UI components and styles while keeping the core lightweight and flexible. It is intended for frontend developers and engineers seeking a headless, high-performance table and datagrid solution across diverse JavaScript frameworks.

name: label-studio
description: Label Studio is a multi-type data labeling and annotation tool with standardized output format
summary:
Label Studio is an open-source data labeling tool designed to prepare raw data or improve existing training data to build more accurate machine learning models. It supports multiple data types—including audio, text, images, video, HTML, and time-series—and features multi-user support, customizable labeling interfaces, cloud storage imports (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage), and model format exports. 

The software enables pre-labeling, active learning, and online learning by connecting machine learning models via the Label Studio Machine Learning SDK. It includes a Data Manager, a REST API, and built-in templates for various labeling tasks. 

Intended users include data scientists, machine learning engineers, and teams managing data pipelines for AI models. Notable technologies used in its stack include Python, Django, PostgreSQL, Nginx, Docker, React, and mobx-state-tree. Deployment options range from local installations via pip, poetry, Anaconda, and Docker to cloud instances on Heroku, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.

name: programmer-job-blacklist
description: :see_no_evil:程序员找工作黑名单，换工作和当技术合伙人需谨慎啊 更新有赞
summary:
This project serves as a curated blacklist and reference repository for software developers and tech professionals seeking employment. Its purpose is to document controversial incidents, workplace disputes, unfair labor practices, and management issues associated with various companies and startups, helping candidates evaluate potential employers and avoid career pitfalls. 

The repository categorizes collected reports—sourced primarily from public discussions and media articles on platforms like Zhihu, Maimai, and V2EX—into sections for general programmers, technical co-founders, and uncertain cases. Notable organizations mentioned include Hangzhou Youzan, Bianlifeng, Huawei, Baidu, and Alibaba (DingTalk), with documented issues ranging from forced overtime and abrupt layoffs to compensation disputes and founder conflicts. 

Intended for programmers, job seekers, and technical professionals, the repository encourages community contributions via GitHub issues. It does not employ specific software technologies or frameworks, functioning purely as an information-sharing Markdown resource for career due diligence.

name: android_guides
description: Extensive Open-Source Guides for Android Developers
summary:
CodePath Android Cliffnotes is a central crowdsourced resource and documentation repository providing up-to-date Android content, tutorials, and guides. The project aims to replace outdated blog posts and forum answers by offering practical, real-world development guides for beginners, intermediate, and advanced engineers. 

The guides cover practical Android development topics—such as using the ActionBar, creating and using fragments, Android testing options, and building flexible user interfaces for multiple devices—reflecting techniques used in professional contract app development. The intended users are mobile software developers, engineers, and students looking to learn or improve their Android development skills. Created originally by Nathan Esquenazi and supported by CodePath alumni, staff, and instructors, the repository relies on community contributions to update existing guides, expand stubs, and create new topics.

name: InvokeAI
description: Invoke is a leading creative engine for Stable Diffusion models, empowering professionals, artists, and enthusiasts to generate and create visual media using the latest AI-driven technologies. The solution offers an industry leading WebUI, and serves as the foundation for multiple commercial products.
summary:
Invoke is a leading creative AI engine built to empower professionals and enthusiasts to generate, refine, and iterate on visual media. The project provides an industry-leading web-based user interface running via a locally hosted web server and React UI, serving as the foundation for multiple commercial products under a commercially friendly license. 

Main capabilities include a Unified Canvas for in/out-painting, brush tools, and image augmentation; node-based workflow management for customizable generation pipelines; board and gallery management with rich metadata recall; upscaling tools; an embedding and model manager; and object segmentation and selection support via SAM and SAM2. The platform features extensive model support, including SD (1.5, 2.0, SDXL, 3.5 Medium, 3.5 Large), CogView 4, Flux variants (Dev, Schnell, Kontext, Krea, Redux, Fill, 2 Dev, 2 Klein 4B/9B), Z-Image, Krea 2, Anima, Qwen Image, Ideogram 4, ERNIE-Image, Nano Banana, GPT Image, and Wan, with compatibility for ckpt, diffusers, and gguf formats. 

Intended users are visual media professionals, artists, and creators looking to build AI-driven workflows and stunning visual media.

name: ResumeSample
description: Resume template for Chinese programmers . 程序员简历模板系列。包括PHP程序员简历模板、iOS程序员简历模板、Android程序员简历模板、Web前端程序员简历模板、Java程序员简历模板、C/C++程序员简历模板、NodeJS程序员简历模板、架构师简历模板以及通用程序员简历模板
summary: This repository provides a collection of programmer resume templates tailored for various technical roles, including PHP, iOS, Android, Web Front-End, Java, C/C++, NodeJS, Architects, and General software engineers. The templates are provided by the AI Career Advisor 🐰 Zhiqiaotu. Additionally, the project references related resources such as the online Markdown resume writing tool Lengxiong Resume, its self-hosted counterpart DeerResume, a tutorial on writing effective technical resumes, and a guide on establishing a one-person business methodology.

name: obscura
description: The headless browser for AI agents and web scraping
summary:
**Obscura** is an open-source headless browser engine written in Rust designed for web scraping and AI agent automation. Built as a lightweight, stealthy, and drop-in replacement for headless Chrome, it executes real JavaScript via the embedded V8 engine and supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), allowing it to integrate seamlessly with Puppeteer and Playwright. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Native rendering engine supporting CSS layout/paint, screenshots, live screencasting, and PDF export without Chromium.
- Built-in anti-detection and tracker blocking via an optional `--stealth` mode.
- Support for CLI-driven single-page fetching (`obscura fetch`), parallel scraping (`obscura scrape`), CDP server hosting (`obscura serve`), and an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for AI assistants like Claude Desktop and Cursor.
- Flexible extraction output options, including HTML, plain text, links, markdown, assets, and original response bodies.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, data engineers, and AI agents requiring high-performance web automation, data scraping, and browser interactions with low memory overhead and fast startup times.

**Notable Technologies:**
Rust, V8, Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), Puppeteer, Playwright, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Docker.

name: Chat2DB
description: Chat2DB is a free, cross-platform, local-first database client and SQL workspace for developers, DBAs, analysts, and data teams. Connect to 40+ databases, manage data, edit and run SQL, and use your own AI model to generate, explain, and optimize queries. Available on desktop, web, Docker, and CLI, with MCP support.
summary:
Chat2DB Community is a free, cross-platform, local-first database client and SQL workspace designed for developers, DBAs, analysts, and data teams. It provides an AI assistant to generate, explain, and optimize SQL using user-connected models, alongside tools for metadata browsing, DDL/DML table and object management, visual data editing, dashboards, charts, and data import and export. 

The application supports over 40 databases—including MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis, and Snowflake—with plugin expansion for new JDBC databases via configuration alone. Notable technical features include an open-source CLI with Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, AES-256-GCM encryption for stored credentials using per-installation keys, and flexible deployment via native desktop installers, Docker, or source builds. The tech stack utilizes Java (Eclipse Temurin 17), Maven, Node.js, and Yarn.

name: awesome-actions
description: A curated list of awesome actions to use on GitHub
summary:
This project is a curated, community-driven list of awesome resources, tools, tutorials, and workflows related to GitHub Actions. It serves developers, DevOps engineers, and repository maintainers looking to automate software development workflows—from idea to production—directly within GitHub. 

The collection categorizes official and community-contributed materials into areas such as workflow examples, official tool and automation actions, language setup utilities (Node.js, Python, Go, Java, .NET, Ruby, PHP, Rust, and others), and custom action development using JavaScript, TypeScript, or Docker containers. It also covers continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) integrations for platforms like AWS, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, Docker, Netlify, and Heroku, alongside utilities for static analysis, testing, linting, security scanning, code coverage, pull request management, notifications, and machine learning operations (MLOps).

name: trufflehog
description: Find, verify, and analyze leaked credentials
summary:
TruffleHog is a powerful secrets discovery, classification, validation, and analysis tool designed to find leaked credentials—such as API keys, database passwords, and private keys—across a wide variety of sources. 

Intended for developers, security engineers, and organizations, TruffleHog scans targets including Git repositories, GitHub, GitLab, Docker images, Amazon S3 and Google Cloud Storage (GCS) buckets, filesystems, CI/CD platforms (CircleCI, Travis CI), chat and wiki platforms, Postman workspaces, Jenkins, Elasticsearch, and Hugging Face.

Main capabilities include:
- **Discovery**: Locating credentials in files, commits, logs, and object stores.
- **Classification**: Identifying over 800 secret types and mapping them to specific identities.
- **Validation**: Programmatically testing classified credentials against respective APIs to confirm if they are active or live, categorized as verified, unverified, or unknown.
- **Analysis**: Inspecting permissions and resources accessible by commonly leaked credentials.

Notable technologies used include Go, Docker, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and custom regular expressions. TruffleHog is released under the AGPL-3.0 license.

name: vibe-kanban
description: Get 10X more out of Claude Code, Codex or any coding agent
summary:
Vibe Kanban is a project management and execution platform designed for software engineers planning, reviewing, and working with coding agents. It provides a kanban board interface for creating, prioritizing, and assigning issues individually or with a team. 

Key capabilities include workspaces that equip coding agents with a dedicated branch, terminal, and development server; diff reviews with inline commenting; a built-in browser featuring devtools, inspect mode, and device emulation; support for switching between more than 10 coding agents including Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Amp, Cursor, OpenCode, Droid, CCR, and Qwen Code; and functionality to create pull requests with AI-generated descriptions.

Intended for software engineers and development teams looking to streamline planning, review workflows, and agent execution, Vibe Kanban is built using Rust, Node.js, and pnpm.

name: mlflow
description: The open source AI engineering platform for agents, LLMs, and ML models. MLflow enables teams of all sizes to debug, evaluate, monitor, and optimize production-quality AI applications while controlling costs and managing access to models and data.
summary:
MLflow is an open-source AI engineering and machine learning platform designed for building, debugging, evaluating, monitoring, and optimizing production-quality AI agents, large language models (LLMs), and traditional machine learning models. 

Its main capabilities include production-grade observability via OpenTelemetry tracing, systematic LLM evaluation and monitoring, versioned prompt management and automated prompt optimization, an AI Gateway for routing requests and managing model access, experiment tracking, a model registry, and flexible deployment tools. The platform provides extensive integrations with popular agent frameworks (such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, and AutoGen), numerous model providers, and vector databases or tooling.

Intended users include data scientists, ML engineers, and AI developers looking to manage the complete lifecycle of generative AI applications and machine learning models from experimentation to production. MLflow supports multiple programming languages—primarily Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Java—and can be hosted locally, on-premises, or across cloud platforms including Databricks, Amazon SageMaker, Azure ML, and Kubernetes.

name: design.md
description: A format specification for describing a visual identity to coding agents. DESIGN.md gives agents a persistent, structured understanding of a design system.
summary:
DESIGN.md is a format specification and command-line interface tool designed to give coding agents a persistent, structured understanding of a visual identity and design system. By combining machine-readable YAML front matter design tokens with human-readable markdown prose rationale, it allows agents to accurately produce UIs matching specific palettes, typography, spacing, and shapes.

Main capabilities include validating `DESIGN.md` files for structural correctness, checking token references and WCAG contrast ratios, comparing version diffs for regressions, exporting tokens into formats such as Tailwind v3 (`json-tailwind`), Tailwind v4 (`css-tailwind`), and W3C Design Tokens Format Module (`dtcg`), and outputting the format specification. 

Intended for developers and automated coding agents working with design systems, the package is distributed as `@google/design.md` on npm and provides both a CLI (using commands like `lint`, `diff`, `export`, and `spec`) and a programmatic TypeScript API. Notable technologies and formats utilized include YAML, Markdown, JSON, CSS, and Tailwind CSS.

name: waifu2x
description: Image Super-Resolution for Anime-Style Art
summary:
Waifu2x is an image super-resolution and noise-reduction tool designed specifically for anime-style art, while also supporting standard photographs. Inspired by SRCNN, the project leverages Deep Convolutional Neural Networks to perform 2x image upscaling, noise reduction, and combined processing. 

Main capabilities include command-line tools for single-image or batch conversion, video frame processing pipelines, a built-in web application interface, and utilities for training custom models with user datasets. 

The software is intended for artists, developers, and users looking to upscale and enhance low-resolution images or remove compression artifacts. Notable technologies utilized include Torch7, NVIDIA CUDA, cuDNN, Lua, and Docker for containerized deployment, with NVIDIA GPU hardware required for acceleration.

name: fastai
description: The fastai deep learning library
summary:
The fastai repository contains a deep learning library built on top of PyTorch, designed to provide practitioners with high-level components for state-of-the-art results in standard domains, and low-level components for researchers to build new approaches. It aims to deliver ease of use, flexibility, and performance without compromise. 

Main capabilities include a GPU-optimized computer vision library, a type dispatch system for Python, a semantic tensor type hierarchy, a modular optimizer, a two-way callback system capable of modifying data, models, or optimizers during training, and a data block API. These features enable users to quickly build image classifiers, image segmentation models, text sentiment models, recommendation systems, and tabular models. 

Intended users include deep learning practitioners, researchers, and coders learning deep learning. The project utilizes Python, PyTorch, fastcore, and nbdev, and supports migration from plain PyTorch, Ignite, Lightning, and Catalyst.

name: bagisto
description: Open Source eCommerce & Multi-Vendor Marketplace Platform Built with Laravel for Enterprise-Scale Commerce, Supporting 10M+ SKUs
summary:
Bagisto is an open-source Laravel eCommerce and multi-vendor marketplace platform designed for building scalable online commerce solutions, single-vendor stores, B2B platforms, and SaaS-based multi-tenant systems. 

Main capabilities include multi-vendor marketplace management, point of sale (POS) operations, headless commerce integration using Next.js, mobile app support via Flutter, AI-powered applications utilizing large language models (such as GPT-5, Gemini 3, LLaMA 4, and Deepseek), and decentralized blockchain commerce supporting Ethereum and Solana.

The platform is intended for merchants, developers, and enterprises looking to launch and customize online stores or digital marketplaces. It is built using technologies including Laravel, Vue.js, Next.js, and Flutter.

name: Probabilistic-Programming-and-Bayesian-Methods-for-Hackers
description: aka "Bayesian Methods for Hackers": An introduction to Bayesian methods + probabilistic programming with a computation/understanding-first, mathematics-second point of view. All in pure Python ;)
summary:
Bayesian Methods for Hackers is an open-source, interactive book and tutorial repository that introduces Bayesian inference and probabilistic programming from a computational and understanding-first perspective. Its primary purpose is to bridge the gap between heavy mathematical analysis and practical application by leveraging computational power instead of complex mathematical prerequisites. 

The project's main capabilities include teaching how to build and analyze Bayesian models, understand Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, apply loss functions, and handle priors through real-world examples such as A/B testing, fraud detection, Bayesian clustering, and financial predictions. The intended users are programmers, data enthusiasts, and practitioners seeking a practical, code-driven approach to Bayesian methods without getting bogged down in formal mathematical proofs.

Notable technologies used throughout the project include Python, PyMC (supporting versions 2 and 3), NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, and Jupyter Notebooks for rendering interactive code and text. Additional data-mining utilities like PRAW and requests are also utilized for specific examples.

name: claude-task-master
description: An AI-powered task-management system you can drop into Cursor, Lovable, Windsurf, Roo, and others.
summary:
Taskmaster (`task-master-ai`) is a task management and development system designed for AI-driven software development. It integrates directly with AI chat interfaces, supporting popular code editors like Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, and Q CLI via the Model Control Protocol (MCP), alongside a standalone Command Line Interface (CLI). 

The project enables developers to parse requirements from a Product Requirements Document (PRD), automatically generate tasks, manage task dependencies and tags, track workflow progress, and perform AI-driven research. Taskmaster supports multiple AI providers and models—including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Perplexity, xAI, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, and local Claude Code or Codex CLI instances—by requiring corresponding API keys or OAuth setups. 

Intended for software developers and engineering teams utilizing AI assistants for coding workflows, Taskmaster includes customizable tool-loading modes (`all`, `standard`, `core`, and custom selections) to optimize context window token usage. The project is distributed as an npm package under the MIT License with Commons Clause.

name: ios_rule_script
description: 分流规则、重写写规则及脚本。
summary:
This repository provides a collection of platform-specific traffic diversion rules, rewrite rules, and automation scripts primarily developed for learning and researching ES6. 

**Main Capabilities:**
* **Diversion and Rewrite Rules:** Collects and organizes open-source network rules sourced from the internet.
* **Automation Scripts:** Includes various task and utility scripts, such as automated check-ins for platforms like Baidu Tieba (with retry logic), Manmanbuy, Dingdong Maicai, Fa Family, and Luka; ad-blocking and task execution for SMZDM; app startup ad removal for cached local advertisements; Synology Download Station offline resource downloading; and Apple Store product stock monitoring.
* **Integrations:** Supports configurations for Quantumult X Gallery and BoxJS subscriptions.

**Notable Technologies:**
* ES6
* MagicJS 2/3 (scripting framework)
* Quantumult X
* BoxJS

name: backbone
description: Give your JS App some Backbone with Models, Views, Collections, and Events
summary: Backbone is a JavaScript library that provides structure to JavaScript-heavy applications. It supplies models with key-value binding and custom events, collections featuring a rich API of enumerable functions, and views with declarative event handling. Backbone connects these components to existing applications over a RESTful JSON interface.

name: so-vits-svc
description: SoftVC VITS Singing Voice Conversion
summary: SoftVC VITS Singing Voice Conversion (so-vits-svc) is an open-source framework designed for Singing Voice Conversion (SVC) rather than Text-to-Speech (TTS), enabling developers to have fictional characters perform singing tasks. The project uses a SoftVC content encoder and alternative extractors such as ContentVec, Whisper-PPG, HuBERT, WavLM, and DPHuBERT to extract speech features directly into VITS while preserving pitch and intonation. It replaces the standard vocoder with NSF HiFiGAN or Snake HiFiGAN to prevent sound interruptions, and supports shallow diffusion mechanisms, K-means clustering, and top-K feature retrieval for timbre leakage control and sound quality enhancement. Intended users include developers and researchers exploring academic voice conversion, with additional support for static and dynamic timbre mixing, ONNX export, and F0 estimators like RMVPE, FCPE, Crepe, Dio, PM, and Harvest.

name: Python
description: 小白 python 教程
summary:
This project is a comprehensive, step-by-step Python tutorial and learning guide designed primarily for beginners and zero-foundation learners. The project's purpose is to help practitioners master foundational to advanced Python programming concepts through structured learning materials. 

Its main capabilities include providing two learning platforms: an interactive web version where users can write code directly in the browser, receive instant automated scoring, and unlock progressive challenges; and a thorough documentation version for system reading and quick reference. The tutorial is built for Python 3.10+ and covers modern features from versions 3.11 to 3.13. 

Notable topics and technologies include basic syntax, data types, object-oriented programming, iterators and generators, magic methods, multi-threading and multi-processing, regular expressions, decorators, async/await concurrency, `pathlib`, `dataclass`, `Pydantic`, `uv`, `ruff`, `pytest`, `logging`, and `typer`.

name: aos
description: Animate on scroll library
summary:
AOS (Animate on Scroll) is a lightweight JavaScript library designed to apply CSS-driven animations to elements as they scroll into view. Its main capabilities include triggering various built-in fade, flip, slide, and zoom animations, customizing animation properties (such as duration, delay, offset, easing, and anchor placements) on a global or per-element basis via `data-aos` attributes, and automatically detecting DOM mutations to refresh element positions. It also exposes JavaScript events and an API with methods like `init`, `refresh`, and `refreshHard`. 

The project is intended for web developers and designers looking to enhance web pages with scroll-triggered visual effects. It supports integration with package managers like npm and yarn, build tools like Parcel, and can be extended with custom CSS animations, easings, or integrated with external CSS libraries such as Animate.css. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript, CSS, SCSS, and HTML.

name: Graphite
description: Community-built comprehensive 2D content creation appplication for graphic design, digital art, and interactive real-time motion graphics powered by a node-based procedural graphics engine
summary:
Graphite is a free, open-source vector and raster graphics engine designed as a procedural toolbox for 2D content creation. It features a fully nondestructive editing workflow that combines layer-based compositing with a node-based generative design core. Built similarly to a game engine, Graphite wraps its tools around a node graph to support user-friendly workflows for vector and raster graphics, with planned expansions for photo editing, motion graphics, digital painting, desktop publishing, and VFX compositing. 

The project is intended for artists, designers, graphics programmers, and Rust developers seeking a comprehensive, accessible content creation tool. Notable technologies and architectural aspects include a node graph core supporting nondestructive boolean operations, procedural patterns, and infinite scalability. The source code is implemented in Rust and dual-licensed under the MIT License and the Apache License 2.0.

name: valkey
description: A flexible distributed key-value database that is optimized for caching and other realtime workloads.
summary: Valkey is a high-performance data structure server optimized for key/value workloads, originally forked from the Redis project. It supports a wide range of native data structures and provides an extensible plugin architecture for adding new structures and access patterns. Intended for developers and system administrators running high-throughput database or caching workloads, Valkey features built-in and modular support for Transport Layer Security (TLS), experimental Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA), systemd integration, and Zstandard streaming compression. The project can be compiled and built using a traditional `Makefile` or an experimental `CMake` build system, supporting memory allocators such as `jemalloc` and `libc` malloc across Unix-like operating systems including Linux, macOS, and various BSD distributions.

name: Daily-Interview-Question
description: 我是依扬（木易杨），公众号「高级前端进阶」作者，每天搞定一道前端大厂面试题，祝大家天天进步，一年后会看到不一样的自己。
summary: The repository contains a collection of daily frontend interview questions and detailed answers designed to help developers prepare for interviews at major technology companies. Intended for frontend developers and learners seeking technical advancement, the project provides regular coding challenges, algorithm problems, and conceptual questions covering JavaScript, CSS, performance optimization, and frameworks such as Vue.

name: axum
description: HTTP routing and request-handling library for Rust that focuses on ergonomics and modularity
summary:
Axum is an HTTP routing and request-handling library for Rust that focuses on ergonomics and modularity. Its main capabilities include routing requests via a macro-free API, declaratively parsing requests using extractors, providing a predictable error handling model, and generating responses with minimal boilerplate. 

Axum leverages the `tower` and `tower-http` ecosystem by utilizing `tower::Service` directly instead of a custom middleware system, allowing applications to integrate features like timeouts, tracing, compression, and authorization while sharing middleware with other libraries such as `hyper` and `tonic`. Built as a thin layer on top of `hyper`, the library ensures high performance with low overhead and is implemented in 100% safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). The minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) is 1.80.

Intended users are Rust developers building web applications and HTTP services who want a modular, extensible routing framework compatible with the Tower ecosystem.

name: libuv
description: Cross-platform asynchronous I/O
summary:
libuv is a multi-platform support library focused primarily on asynchronous I/O. Its core capabilities include a full-featured event loop backed by epoll, kqueue, IOCP, and event ports, as well as asynchronous TCP and UDP sockets, DNS resolution, and file system operations. It also supports file system events, ANSI escape code controlled TTY, IPC with socket sharing via Unix domain sockets or named pipes, child processes, a thread pool, signal handling, high-resolution clocks, and threading and synchronization primitives. 

Originally developed for Node.js, libuv is additionally utilized by projects such as Luvit, Julia, and uvloop. It follows semantic versioning and maintains a stable ABI across major releases under the MIT license. Supported building methods include autotools and CMake across multiple operating systems, with specific integration options via Homebrew, vcpkg, and Conan.

name: codemirror5
description: In-browser code editor (version 5, legacy)
summary: CodeMirror 5 is a versatile JavaScript text editor for the browser, specialized for editing code. It comes with over 100 language modes providing fully-featured syntax highlighting, along with various addons for advanced editing functionality. The library offers a rich programming API and a CSS theming system for customization and extension. It is intended for developers seeking to embed a robust code editor in web applications. Notable technologies include JavaScript, CSS, and Node.js.

name: awesome-low-level-design
description: Learn Low Level Design (LLD) and prepare for interviews using free resources.
summary:
This repository provides comprehensive resources for learning Low-Level Design (LLD), Object-Oriented Design (OOD), and concurrency to help engineers prepare for technical interviews. The content covers OOP fundamentals, class relationships, design principles (such as SOLID, DRY, KISS, and YAGNI), design patterns (creational, structural, and behavioral), and Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagrams. It also explores concurrency and multi-threading concepts, synchronization primitives, concurrency challenges, and concurrency patterns. 

Designed for software engineers and job seekers preparing for LLD and concurrency interviews, the repository offers a curated list of practice problems categorized by difficulty—ranging from easy systems like parking lots and vending machines to medium systems like LRU caches and elevators, and hard systems like ride-sharing services and movie ticket booking platforms. Additionally, it features multi-threaded programming problems such as thread-safe caches, concurrent hash maps, and blocking queues, along with recommended reading materials, books, courses, and external resources.

name: ace
description: Ace (Ajax.org Cloud9 Editor)
summary:
Ace (Ajax.org Cloud9 Editor) is a standalone, browser-based code editor written in JavaScript. It is designed to match and extend the features, usability, and performance of native editors such as TextMate, Vim, and Eclipse, serving as the primary editor for Cloud9 IDE and the successor to the Mozilla Skywriter (Bespin) Project. 

Intended for web developers and applications requiring embedded text or code editing capabilities, Ace can be easily integrated into any web page or JavaScript application as a textarea replacement or advanced code editor. 

Main capabilities include syntax highlighting for over 120 languages, more than 20 themes, automatic indent and outdent, support for huge documents up to 4,000,000 lines, fully customizable key bindings including Vim and Emacs modes, regular expression search and replace, code folding, multiple cursors and selections, live syntax checking, and full language client support via ace-linters. 

Notable technologies utilized in the project include JavaScript, Node.js, requireJS, and the dryice build tool with uglify-js for minification.

name: the_silver_searcher
description: A code-searching tool similar to ack, but faster.
summary:
The Silver Searcher (known as `ag`) is a code-searching tool similar to `ack`, built for high performance and speed. It is designed for developers seeking a fast command-line utility to search through source code repositories. 

The project's main capabilities include searching files in parallel across multiple CPU cores, automatically ignoring file patterns specified in `.gitignore`, `.hgignore`, and custom `.ignore` files, and performing both literal string and regular expression searches. 

To achieve high performance, The Silver Searcher utilizes several notable technologies and optimization techniques:
- POSIX Threads (Pthreads) for multi-core parallel searching
- `mmap()` instead of standard buffer reading
- Boyer-Moore string search algorithm for literal strings
- PCRE's JIT compiler and `pcre_study()` for regular expressions
- Pre-loaded, binary-searched arrays for non-regex ignore patterns rather than repeated `fnmatch()` calls

The tool integrates with text editors and environments such as Vim, Emacs, and TextMate.

name: tree-sitter
description: An incremental parsing system for programming tools
summary: Tree-sitter is a parser generator tool and incremental parsing library designed to build concrete syntax trees for source files and efficiently update them as files are edited. It aims to be general enough to parse any programming language, fast enough to parse on every keystroke within a text editor, robust enough to yield useful results despite syntax errors, and entirely dependency-free. Its pure C runtime library can be embedded into any application. The project provides bindings for Rust and WebAssembly (Wasm), alongside a command-line interface.

name: ai
description: The AI Toolkit for TypeScript. From the creators of Next.js, the AI SDK is a free open-source library for building AI-powered applications and agents
summary:
The AI SDK is a provider-agnostic TypeScript toolkit designed to help developers build AI-powered applications and agents. Created by Vercel and Next.js team members, it provides a unified API and architecture to interact with major model providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, either directly via dedicated SDK packages or out-of-the-box through the Vercel AI Gateway.

Main capabilities include generating text, generating structured data via schemas using Zod, building agents with tool loops, and streaming UI responses. The toolkit offers UI integration modules with framework-agnostic hooks supporting popular UI frameworks and runtimes like Next.js, React, Svelte, Vue, Angular, and Node.js. Intended users are developers building generative user interfaces, chatbots, and AI agents. Notable technologies utilized include TypeScript, Node.js 22+, Zod, and the Vercel AI Gateway.

name: GDevelop
description: 🎮 Open-source, cross-platform 2D/3D/multiplayer game engine designed for everyone.
summary:
GDevelop is a full-featured, no-code, open-source game development software designed to build 2D, 3D, and multiplayer games for mobile, desktop, and the web. Intended for creators, developers, and teams of all skill levels, it allows users to make games using an event-based system, modular behaviors, and AI-assisted tools. 

The technical architecture comprises:
- `newIDE`: The game editor built with JavaScript, React, Electron, PixiJS, and Three.js.
- `GDJS`: The TypeScript game engine utilizing PixiJS and Three.js for 2D and 3D WebGL rendering.
- `Core`: C++ core classes defining game structure and IDE tooling.
- `GDevelop.js`: Bindings of `Core`, `GDJS`, and extensions to JavaScript with WebAssembly for IDE usage.
- `Extensions`: Built-in features, objects, behaviors, and WebAssembly-powered physics engines including Box2D and Jolt Physics.

name: react-virtualized
description: React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data
summary: React Virtualized is a library providing React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data through virtualization. Its main capabilities include performance optimization for extensive datasets via components like `List`, `Table`, `Grid`, `Masonry`, `Collection`, `InfiniteLoader`, and `AutoSizer`. The project is intended for web developers building performant React applications that handle substantial amounts of data or large collections. Notable technologies utilized include React, ReactDOM, ES6, CommonJS, UMD, Webpack, and CSS.

name: dns-blocklists
description: DNS-Blocklists: For a better internet - keep the internet clean!
summary:
HaGeZi DNS Blocklists is an all-in-one network-wide DNS filtering project designed to block advertisements, trackers, telemetry, phishing, malware, scams, cryptojacking, and other unwanted domains. Intended for privacy-conscious users and network administrators, it supports popular DNS servers, ad blockers, and content blockers through multiple tiered lists—including Light, Normal, Pro, Pro++, Ultimate, and Threat Intelligence Feeds (TIF)—alongside specialized lists for native trackers, social networks, gambling, adult content, and dynamic DNS abuse. 

The blocklists are distributed in multiple standard formats such as Adblock, DNSMasq, Wildcard Asterisk, Wildcard Domains, and Response Policy Zones (RPZ). Notable tools provided within the project include a Direct Link Generator and a Blocklist Lookup utility. The repository is licensed under the GPL-3.0.

name: wg-easy
description: The easiest way to run WireGuard VPN + Web-based Admin UI.
summary:
WireGuard Easy provides an all-in-one solution for installing and managing WireGuard VPN on any Linux host, combining the WireGuard service with an integrated Web UI. It is designed for administrators and users seeking a simple way to deploy and manage a WireGuard server. 

Main capabilities include listing, creating, editing, deleting, enabling, and disabling clients, displaying client QR codes, downloading configuration files, viewing connection statistics, and monitoring Tx/Rx charts for connected clients. Additional features comprise Gravatar support, automatic light and dark mode, multilingual support, one-time links, client expiration, Prometheus metrics, IPv6 and CIDR support, two-factor authentication (2FA), per-client firewall filtering via iptables, and OIDC support for authentication providers such as Google, GitHub, Authelia, and Authentik. 

The project is packaged primarily for containerized environments using Docker, Docker Compose, Podman, and Node.js for development.

name: nanoid
description: A tiny (118 bytes), secure, URL-friendly, unique string ID generator for JavaScript
summary:
Nano ID is a tiny, secure, URL-friendly, and unique string ID generator for JavaScript. Built without dependencies and weighing only 127 bytes (minified and brotlied), it offers high performance and uses hardware random generators to ensure unpredictability and uniformity. By leveraging a larger alphabet (`A-Za-z0-9_-`) than UUID, Nano ID reduces standard ID length from 36 to 21 symbols while maintaining a comparable collision probability. 

The library supports custom alphabets, custom random byte generators, non-secure fallback modes, TypeScript type casting, and a command-line interface (CLI). It is intended for JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, Deno, and browser developers seeking fast and compact unique identifiers. Nano ID has also been ported to over 20 programming languages, including Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#, and PHP.

name: rethinkdb
description: The open-source database for the realtime web.
summary:
RethinkDB is an open-source, distributed NoSQL database designed for building realtime web applications. It stores schemaless JSON documents and offers high availability with automatic failover and fault tolerance. Its primary capability enables developers to instruct the database to continuously push updated query results directly to applications via changefeeds, eliminating the need for polling. 

Intended for developers building scalable realtime applications such as liveblogs, collaborative tools, and chat bots, RethinkDB features official drivers for JavaScript, Python, Ruby, and Java, alongside a wide ecosystem of community-supported third-party drivers for languages including C#, C++, Clojure, Elixir, Go, Haskell, PHP, Rust, and Scala. 

The project exposes the ReQL API for database queries and management. Built using technologies such as C++ (GCC or Clang), Protocol Buffers, jemalloc, and OpenSSL, the repository provides build instructions for Linux, FreeBSD, and Windows environments. RethinkDB is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license by the Linux Foundation.

name: react-admin
description: A frontend Framework for single-page applications on top of REST/GraphQL APIs, using TypeScript, React and Material Design
summary:
react-admin is a frontend framework for building single-page applications running in the browser on top of REST or GraphQL APIs. Designed for frontend developers and engineers, it enables the creation of administrative interfaces, e-commerce apps, CRMs, and helpdesk tools. 

The framework is backend agnostic, connecting to any API via data provider adapters, and provides a comprehensive suite of building blocks including authentication, routing, forms and validation, datagrids, search and filters, roles and permissions, internationalization (i18n), and theming. Notable features include optimistic rendering, undo capabilities, saved queries, and complete component customization. 

Built using TypeScript, React, Material Design (Material UI), react-hook-form, react-router, and react-query, react-admin supports optional TypeScript usage, offers modular architecture, and supplies complete documentation alongside multiple example applications.

name: hashcat
description: World's fastest and most advanced password recovery utility
summary:
Hashcat is a free and open-source password recovery platform designed for GPUs, CPUs, and large distributed systems. Aimed at security professionals and researchers, it functions as a password cracker supporting over 590 hash modes and 10 attack modes, including wordlist, combination, brute-force, PCFG, table, hybrid, mask, generic plugin feeds, and association. 

Core capabilities include an in-kernel rule engine, a Brain feature to skip previously tried candidates, an assimilation bridge for adding hash modes in C, Python, or Rust, distributed cracking networks, automatic performance tuning, an integrated thermal watchdog, and encrypted plains support. It reads candidates from wordlists, stdin, or external programs, and utilizes Markov chain keyspace ordering. 

Hashcat operates across Linux, Windows, and macOS, utilizing backends such as CUDA, HIP, Metal, and OpenCL. Distributed under the MIT license, it supports multi-device and mixed-device systems, multi-hash cracking, interactive pause and resume, session restoration, built-in benchmarking, and keyboard layout mapping.

name: awesome-piracy
description: A curated list of awesome warez and piracy links
summary:
Awesome Piracy is an archived curated list of resources, tools, and guides dedicated to digital file sharing, media consumption, privacy, and data archiving. The repository compiles a vast directory covering VPN services, privacy extensions, browser userscripts, password managers, antivirus tools, and decentralized networks. 

Main capabilities and technical categories include:
- **Torrenting and P2P:** Public and private trackers, torrent clients (e.g., qBittorrent, rTorrent, Deluge), seedboxes, and automation scripts.
- **Usenet:** Providers, indexers, and newsreaders like SABnzbd and NZBGet.
- **Direct Downloads (DDL) and Streaming:** Search engines, open directories, premium link generators, and HD streaming platforms for movies, TV shows, and anime.
- **Media Management:** Tools and integrations for Plex, Kodi, Stremio, and Emby, alongside automation suites like Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and Bazarr.
- **Gaming, Ebooks, and Education:** Emulators, ROMs, repacks, academic papers via LibGen and Sci-Hub, textbooks, and online courses.

Intended users include data hoarders, media enthusiasts, and privacy-conscious internet users seeking to structure and streamline accessing digital content. Notable technologies referenced include Python, Node.js, Docker, BitTorrent, Usenet, FUSE, and various CLI utilities.

name: OI-wiki
description: :star2: Wiki of OI / ICPC for everyone. （某大型游戏线上攻略，内含炫酷算术魔法）
summary:
**OI Wiki** is a free, open, and continuously updated knowledge integration platform designed for programming and competitive programming enthusiasts. Its primary purpose is to provide a systematic, accessible learning resource containing fundamental concepts, common problem types, problem-solving strategies, and essential tools to help beginners and participants navigate competitive programming efficiently. 

The project targets students, developers, and anyone interested in competitive programming who seeks structured guidance without navigating scattered online documentation. Developed as a community-driven, non-commercial initiative advocating knowledge freedom, the repository relies on **MkDocs** and **Python 3** (utilizing `uv` for dependency management) to build and deploy its static site documentation. It also supports MathJax rendering (requiring **Node.js**), local server execution, and provides offline access formats. Distinctive resources referenced include CTF Wiki for project inspiration and collaboration with the 24OI community.

name: DeepSpeech
description: DeepSpeech is an open source embedded (offline, on-device) speech-to-text engine which can run in real time on devices ranging from a Raspberry Pi 4 to high power GPU servers.
summary: Project DeepSpeech is a discontinued open-source Speech-To-Text engine that implements a model trained by machine learning techniques based on Baidu's Deep Speech research paper. The project utilizes Google's TensorFlow to facilitate implementation. It provides capabilities for speech recognition, with documentation, installation guides, usage instructions, training models, pre-trained models, and checkpoints available for users.

name: elixir
description: Simple from zero to scale
summary: Elixir is a programming language designed for building scalable and maintainable applications. Intended for developers and contributors building software within the Elixir ecosystem, the project relies on Erlang. The repository contains the source code, build utilities via `make`, and instructions for compiling from source, testing, reporting bugs, and proposing new features through the Elixir Core mailing list. The software is released under the Apache License 2.0.

name: typesense
description: Open Source alternative to Algolia + Pinecone and an Easier-to-Use alternative to ElasticSearch ⚡ 🔍 ✨ Fast, typo tolerant, in-memory fuzzy Search Engine for building delightful search experiences
summary:
Typesense is an open-source, fast, typo-tolerant search engine designed as an alternative to Algolia and an easier-to-use alternative to Elasticsearch. Built in C++, it delivers low-latency search experiences (<50ms) with zero runtime dependencies as a single self-contained binary. 

Key capabilities include typo tolerance, tunable ranking, faceting and filtering, grouping, federated search across multiple collections, geo-search, vector search for nearest-neighbor queries, and hybrid search combining keyword and semantic matching via built-in or external machine learning models (such as S-BERT, E-5, and OpenAI). It also supports conversational search (built-in RAG), natural language intent detection, image search using CLIP, voice search with Whisper, scoped API keys for multi-tenancy, SQL-like JOINs, synonyms, curation, and Raft-based clustering for high availability.

Typesense provides official API clients in JavaScript, PHP, Python, and Ruby, along with numerous community clients and framework integrations for Laravel, Firebase, WordPress, and InstantSearch.js. It is intended for developers and organizations building scalable search and recommendation experiences.

name: jenkins
description: Jenkins automation server
summary: Jenkins is an open-source automation server built with Java that is used to automate development workflows, build projects, run tests, perform static code analysis, and handle deployments. It features over 2,000 plugins and offers official distributions including WAR files, Docker images, and native packages. Jenkins targets developers, software teams, and enterprises seeking to execute repetitive tasks and optimize software delivery pipelines. The project is licensed under the MIT License.

name: miaosha
description: ⭐⭐⭐⭐秒杀系统设计与实现.互联网工程师进阶与分析🙋🐓
summary:
This repository is a comprehensive collection of personal engineering projects, frameworks, learning notes, and architectural diagrams curated by GEEK.Q. It is intended for developers and architects seeking to master advanced backend technologies and system design. 

The repository encompasses several distinct projects and modules:
- **tydeus-monitor**: A logging and monitoring solution designed to track business system metrics, success/failure rates, and handle method-level logging (parameters, return values, exceptions) without intrusive code changes.
- **three-high-import (threadandjuc)**: A multi-threading project focused on high-performance, high-availability, and high-reliability data importing and reporting for millions to hundreds of millions of records, ensuring data consistency and retry mechanisms during failures.
- **memoryoptimization**: A guide and practical resource for JVM memory tuning, parameter configuration, monitoring, and garbage collection (GC) log analysis in production environments.
- **qrzFlowEngine**: A lightweight node-based workflow and process engine designed for complex logic orchestration (such as machine auditing) to achieve balanced architectural design.
- **zookeeperDesign**: A module exploring the design philosophy of ZooKeeper for distributed application coordination, configuration maintenance, and synchronization.
- **Designpattern**: A collection of design patterns applied to internet-scale distributed architectures.

Technologies and tools referenced throughout the repository include Spring, Spring Boot, MQ, Redis, Dubbo, ZooKeeper (ZK), Maven, Lua, and multithreading (JUC).

name: flatbuffers
description: FlatBuffers: Memory Efficient Serialization Library
summary:
FlatBuffers is a cross-platform serialization library designed for maximum memory efficiency, enabling direct access to serialized data without prior parsing or unpacking while maintaining forward and backward compatibility. The project provides the `flatc` compiler to generate language-specific code and accessors from `.fbs` schema files using a `FlatBufferBuilder`. 

Intended users include developers seeking high-performance, memory-efficient data serialization and cross-language data exchange. Notable technologies and tools include CMake, C++ (C++11 and newer), and support for operating systems such as Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android. The library provides code generation and runtime support for a wide range of programming languages, including C, C++, C#, Dart, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Lobster, Lua, Nim, PHP, Python, Rust, Swift, and TypeScript.

name: 12-factor-agents
description: What are the principles we can use to build LLM-powered software that is actually good enough to put in the hands of production customers?
summary:
12-Factor Agents is a methodology and guide for building reliable, production-grade LLM applications and AI agents. It addresses the limitations of monolithic AI frameworks by advocating for modular, software-driven design patterns. 

The project outlines twelve core principles—ranging from natural language tool calls and prompt/context ownership to structured outputs, stateless reducers, and human-in-the-loop tool integrations—designed to help developers construct scalable, maintainable LLM software. Intended for software engineers and technical founders aiming to deploy robust AI features to production customers, the project provides architectural concepts applicable across programming languages like TypeScript and Python.

name: winget-cli
description: WinGet is the Windows Package Manager. This project includes a CLI (Command Line Interface), PowerShell modules, and a COM (Component Object Model) API (Application Programming Interface).
summary:
