The Windows Package Manager (`winget`) is a command-line client designed for Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server to quickly discover, install, upgrade, list, and manage software packages. 

**Main Capabilities:**
* Access packages from default sources including the Microsoft Store (`msstore`), the WinGet community repository (`winget`), or custom private REST-based sources.
* Execute package management operations via the command line or through native cmdlets provided by the `Microsoft.WinGet.Client` PowerShell module.
* Support for group policy configurations and custom administrative installation privileges.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, system administrators, and Windows users looking to automate and streamline software installation and environment setup.

**Notable Technologies:**
* Windows Package Manager (`winget`) / WinGet Client
* MSIX / App Installer
* PowerShell (`Microsoft.WinGet.Client` module)
* REST API (for private sources)

name: open-r1
description: Fully open reproduction of DeepSeek-R1
summary:
Open R1 is a fully open reproduction of DeepSeek-R1 designed to let developers and researchers replicate and build upon the R1 pipeline. The project provides scripts, configurations, and tools to train models, generate synthetic data, and evaluate performance across reasoning, mathematics, and coding tasks.

Main capabilities include Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training using DDP or DeepSpeed (ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3), synthetic data generation pipelines, evaluation workflows, and dataset decontamination tools. It supports reward functions for code execution via integration with sandboxes and routers like E2B, Morph, and Piston. Intended users include AI researchers and engineers working on large language model alignment, reasoning, and distributed training.

Notable technologies and libraries used include PyTorch, vLLM, FlashAttention, 🤗 Accelerate, DeepSpeed, TRL, Distilabel, LightEval, Weights and Biases, and Slurm for cluster management.

name: ultimatevocalremovergui
description: GUI for a Vocal Remover that uses Deep Neural Networks.
summary:
Ultimate Vocal Remover GUI is a desktop application designed to remove vocals and separate audio sources using state-of-the-art AI models, including VR Architecture, MDX-Net, Demucs v3/v4, and MDX23C. Developed by Anjok07 and aufr33, the software targets musicians, audio engineers, and creators seeking high-quality vocal extraction. 

Key capabilities include audio source separation, built-in time-stretching, and pitch-shifting tools. The application relies on FFmpeg for processing non-WAV audio files and the Rubber Band library for time and pitch adjustments. It supports hardware acceleration through PyTorch, CUDA, Apple Silicon (MPS), and DirectML. 

The repository provides automated installers and manual installation instructions for Windows, macOS, and Linux systems. Distributed under the MIT license, the project incorporates architectures and weights contributed by notable developers such as ZFTurbo, tsurumeso, Kuielab, and Adefossez.

name: flink
description: Apache Flink
summary: Apache Flink is an open-source stream processing framework featuring powerful stream- and batch-processing capabilities. Its streaming-first runtime delivers high throughput and low event latency alongside fault-tolerance with exactly-once processing guarantees. Key capabilities include event time and out-of-order processing via the Dataflow Model, flexible windowing, natural back-pressure, custom memory management, and libraries for graph processing, machine learning, and complex event processing. Flink provides fluent APIs in Java and includes integration and compatibility layers for Apache Hadoop ecosystems, YARN, HDFS, HBase, and various externalized connectors such as Kafka, JDBC, Elasticsearch, and AWS. Intended users include developers and data engineers building real-time data streaming and batch applications. The project is built using Maven and Java (versions 11, 17, or 21) and supports development environments like IntelliJ IDEA.

name: nixpkgs
description: Nix Packages collection & NixOS
summary:
Nixpkgs is a comprehensive collection of over 140,000 software packages designed for installation via the Nix package manager, while also implementing NixOS, a purely-functional Linux distribution. The repository provides Nix expressions, build scripts, and NixOS modules to build and configure software and operating system environments. 

Intended for developers, system administrators, and Linux users seeking reproducible and declarative system configuration, Nixpkgs utilizes the Hydra continuous integration system for building, testing, and distributing software artifacts through Nix channels. Related technologies and tools within the ecosystem include Nix, NixOps for remote deployment, and specialized hardware profiles. The project welcomes community contributions via GitHub and is maintained under the MIT License, though individual built packages retain their respective licenses.

name: grapesjs
description: Free and Open source Web Builder Framework. Next generation tool for building templates without coding
summary:
GrapesJS is a free and open-source Web Builder Framework designed to help developers build HTML templates easily and quickly for websites, newsletters, and mobile apps. Primarily created to be embedded inside Content Management Systems (CMS) to speed up dynamic template creation, the framework manages structure (HTML), style (CSS), and variables. 

Key capabilities include a Block Manager, Style Manager, Layer Manager, Code Viewer, Asset Manager, built-in commands, and support for local and remote storage. Intended for developers and application creators, GrapesJS offers official and community plugins, presets such as webpage and newsletter builders, and a React wrapper (`@grapesjs/react`). Notable technologies and integrations associated with the ecosystem include CKEditor, TOAST UI Image Editor, PostCSS, IndexedDB, and Cloud Firestore. The project is distributed under the BSD 3-clause license.

name: docker_practice
description: 最新Docker容器技术，从真实案例中学习最佳实践！| Learn and understand Docker&Container technologies, with real DevOps practice!
summary:
"Docker 从入门到实践" is an open-source technical book and guide designed to help readers systematically master Docker container technology, from core concepts and underlying principles to advanced practical applications. 

Based on Docker Engine v29.x, the book targets application developers, system administrators, DevOps engineers, and IT professionals with basic Linux knowledge. It provides structured learning content ranging from fundamental operations—such as images, containers, and registries—to advanced topics including Dockerfile, data and network management, Buildx, and Compose. Additionally, it explores underlying implementations, container orchestration systems like Kubernetes and Etcd, container security, monitoring and logging systems (Prometheus, ELK), and ecosystem projects such as Fedora CoreOS and Podman.

name: spotify-downloader
description: Download your Spotify playlists and songs along with album art and metadata (from YouTube if a match is found).
summary:
spotDL v4 is a command-line music downloader designed to find songs from Spotify playlists on YouTube and download them along with album art, lyrics, and metadata. 

Main capabilities include downloading tracks, saving Spotify metadata without downloading, retrieving direct URLs, synchronizing local directories with Spotify playlists, updating song file metadata, and providing a limited-feature web interface. The tool sources audio from YouTube to achieve the highest possible bitrate (128 kbps for regular users and up to 256 kbps for YouTube Music premium users).

Intended users are individuals looking to manage, download, and sync music collections based on Spotify links. Notable technologies utilized include Python, FFmpeg, Deno, yt-dlp, Docker, and the PyPI ecosystem, with installation supported via pip, prebuilt executables, Termux, Arch User Repository, and Docker containers. The project is distributed under the MIT License.

name: ILSpy
description: .NET Decompiler with support for PDB generation, ReadyToRun, Metadata (&more) - cross-platform!
summary:
ILSpy is an open-source, cross-platform .NET assembly browser and decompiler. Its primary purpose is to inspect and decompile .NET assemblies back into C#, supporting whole-project decompilation and advanced navigation such as type, method, and property searches, base/derived type browsing, bookmarks, and an assembly metadata explorer. 

The project provides multiple frontends, including a cross-platform desktop UI built on Avalonia (running on Windows, Linux, and macOS), a Visual Studio extension, a Visual Studio Code extension, a .NET command-line tool (`ILSpyCmd`), PowerShell cmdlets, and NuGet packages (`ICSharpCode.Decompiler` and `ILSpyX`) for integration into third-party projects. Additional capabilities include BAML-to-XAML decompilation, Avalonia resource support, and ReadyToRun binary support for .NET Core.

Intended users include .NET developers, reverse engineers, and security analysts requiring assembly inspection and decompilation tools. The software is written using technologies such as .NET (targeting .NET 10.0 and 11.0 SDKs), Avalonia, and PowerShell, and is distributed under the MIT License.

name: typescript-go
description: Staging repo for development of native port of TypeScript
summary:
This repository served as the staging environment for the TypeScript 7.0 native port process (typescript-go), which is now completed. The project provides preview builds of the native TypeScript port via npm (`@typescript/native-preview` using the `tsgo` command) and a preview VS Code extension. 

The purpose of the project is to develop a native port of TypeScript while maintaining feature parity with TypeScript 6.0 across program creation, parsing and scanning, command line and `tsconfig.json` parsing, type resolution and checking, JavaScript inference and JSDoc, JSX, declaration and JavaScript output emit, watch mode, build mode, and incremental builds. The language service (LSP) is in progress, while the API is not yet ready. Intended users include developers and contributors testing the native TypeScript 7 preview releases. Notable technologies and tools involved include TypeScript, npm, and VS Code.

name: dapr
description: Dapr is a portable runtime for building distributed applications across cloud and edge, combining event-driven architecture with workflow orchestration.
summary:
Dapr (Distributed Application Runtime) is an open-source, graduated CNCF project designed as a runtime for durable execution, AI agents, and secure distributed applications. Operating as a sidecar via HTTP and gRPC, it enables developers to build microservices, event-driven systems, and multi-agent AI workflows without framework lock-in or low-level infrastructure boilerplate.

Main capabilities include durable workflow execution that automatically resumes after crashes or restarts, reliable AI agent orchestration with state persistence and LLM integration via a Conversation API, secure service-to-service communication with mutual TLS (mTLS), verifiable execution, secret management, pub/sub messaging, state management, actors, and distributed locks. 

Intended users include software engineers and platform teams building cloud-native, microservice-based, or compliance-sensitive distributed systems. Dapr runs anywhere—including Kubernetes, cloud providers, virtual machines, bare metal, and edge environments. It features native SDKs for .NET, Java, Python, Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, C++, and PHP. Notable technologies integrated across its ecosystem include Go, gRPC, and pluggable vendor-neutral components for state stores and message brokers on major cloud platforms like Azure, AWS, and GCP.

name: Rust
description: All Algorithms implemented in Rust
summary: The Algorithms - Rust is an open-source educational repository that provides implementations of various algorithms written in the Rust programming language. Designed for educational purposes, the project offers a structured directory of algorithmic solutions to help users learn and understand algorithm implementation in Rust.

name: masscan
description: TCP port scanner, spews SYN packets asynchronously, scanning entire Internet in under 5 minutes.
summary:
Masscan is an Internet-scale asynchronous port scanner designed to scan the entire Internet in under 5 minutes from a single machine at rates exceeding 10 million packets per second. Its syntax, parameters, and output formats are similar to `nmap`. 

Main capabilities include simultaneous IPv4 and IPv6 scanning, custom TCP/IP stack implementation, banner checking across multiple protocols (such as HTTP, FTP, SSH, SMTP, POP3, IMAP4, SSL, SMBv1/v2, Telnet, RDP, VNC, and memcached), randomized target generation via encryption, and multiple output formats (XML, JSON, binary, grepable, and list). Intended users are security professionals, network administrators, and researchers conducting wide-range network discovery. 

Notable technologies and components used include an ad hoc user-mode TCP/IP stack, C90 standard C, `libpcap`, and optional support for high-performance network drivers like PF_RING ZC. It compiles using standard C compilers such as `gcc`, `clang`, or Microsoft Visual Studio, with primary support for Linux alongside Windows and macOS.

name: zulip
description: Zulip server and web application. Open-source team chat that helps teams stay productive and focused.
summary:
Zulip is an open-source, organized team chat application designed for both live and asynchronous conversations through unique topic-based threading. Aimed at remote teams, Fortune 500 companies, open-source projects, and organizations of all sizes, it combines the best elements of email and chat. 

The project can be self-hosted on Ubuntu or Debian Linux, via Docker, or deployed using prebuilt images for DigitalOcean and Render, and is also available through Zulip Cloud hosting options. Zulip is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: squoosh
description: Make images smaller using best-in-class codecs, right in the browser.
summary: Squoosh is an image compression web application that reduces image sizes across numerous formats by processing images entirely locally on the user's device without sending them to a server. The app utilizes Google Analytics to collect basic visitor data, before and after image size values, PWA installation types, and PWA installation timestamps.

name: kratos
description: Your ultimate Go microservices framework for the cloud-native era.
summary:
Kratos is a lightweight Go framework designed for building cloud-native microservices. It provides explicit APIs and components for transport, middleware, registry, configuration, logging, encoding, and code generation, enabling developers to focus primarily on business logic. 

Main capabilities include API-first development using Protobuf, a unified transport layer supporting HTTP and gRPC, composable middleware for recovery, logging, validation, tracing, metrics, and authentication, as well as pluggable configuration and registry components. It leverages standard-library `log/slog` for logging and offers a contrib ecosystem for optional observability and integration features. 

The framework is intended for Go developers building and maintaining microservices and cloud-native applications. Notable technologies and tools used include Go (version 1.25 or later), Protobuf, gRPC, and OpenTelemetry.

name: simple-icons
description: SVG icons for popular brands
summary: Simple Icons is a collection of over 3,400 SVG icons representing popular brands, designed for developers and designers. The project provides direct SVG downloads via its website, CDN hosting (supporting customizable colors and dark mode variants), and native packages for Node.js, TypeScript, and PHP. Numerous third-party extensions and wrapper libraries exist for frameworks such as Angular, Astro, Blazor, Django, Flutter, React, Svelte, and Vue.

name: beszel
description: Lightweight server monitoring with historical data, docker stats, and alerts.
summary:
Beszel is a lightweight server monitoring platform designed to track system metrics, Docker statistics, and historical data with simple configuration and a user-friendly web interface. 

Project capabilities include customizable alerts for most metrics supporting various notification services, network monitoring, S.M.A.R.T. disk health tracking, automatic backups to disk or S3-compatible storage, and multi-user support with OAuth/OIDC authentication. It monitors comprehensive metrics such as CPU, memory, disk usage and I/O, network usage, load average, temperature, fan speed, GPU usage, battery charge, container status, and ZFS pools.

The architecture consists of a hub web application built on PocketBase for dashboard management, and an agent that runs on monitored systems to communicate metrics. It is intended for administrators and users needing an out-of-the-box, resource-efficient monitoring solution. Notable technologies include Docker, Podman, and PocketBase.

name: biome
description: A toolchain for web projects, aimed to provide functionalities to maintain them. Biome offers formatter and linter, usable via CLI and LSP.
summary:
Biome is a performant, zero-configuration toolchain designed for web development projects to maintain code health. It unifies formatting and linting into a single cohesive experience, operating independently of Node.js while offering high-fidelity parsing and first-class Language Server Protocol (LSP) support. 

Main capabilities include a fast formatter with 97% Prettier compatibility and a performant linter featuring over 500 rules derived from ESLint, typescript-eslint, and other sources. It provides detailed, contextualized diagnostics and interactive editor integration to format and lint malformed code in real time. 

Biome supports JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, JSON, CSS, and GraphQL. It is intended for web developers and CI environments seeking high-performance code processing, parallel work distribution, caching, and descriptive diagnostics.

name: YouCompleteMe
description: A code-completion engine for Vim
summary:
YouCompleteMe is a fast, as-you-type fuzzy-search code completion, comprehension, and refactoring engine for Vim. It operates on a client-server architecture, utilizing a thin Vim client communicating with a backend `ycmd` HTTP+JSON server. 

The project's main capabilities include asynchronous identifier-based completion, intelligent suggestion ranking via subsequence matching, real-time diagnostic error/warning displays, signature help, semantic highlighting, inlay hints, symbol search, and type/call hierarchies. It supports code navigation (such as jumping to declarations, definitions, implementations, and references), automated refactoring fixes via `FixIt`, semantic renaming, and code formatting.

Intended users are Vim and Neovim developers seeking advanced, IDE-like semantic features and auto-completion across multiple programming languages. 

YouCompleteMe integrates built-in semantic completion engines and Language Server Protocol (LSP) clients. Supported technologies include `clangd` and `libclang` for C-family languages (C, C++, Objective-C, Objective-C++, CUDA), `Jedi` for Python, `OmniSharp-Roslyn` for C#, `Gopls` for Go, `TSServer` for JavaScript and TypeScript, `rust-analyzer` for Rust, `jdt.ls` for Java, and generic Language Server Protocol servers for arbitrary languages.

name: fmt
description: A modern formatting library
summary:
{fmt} is an open-source C++ formatting library designed as a fast, type-safe, and safe alternative to C `stdio` and C++ iostreams. Its primary purpose is to provide efficient string formatting, printing, and localized text handling with high performance and low code bloat. 

Main capabilities include an implementation of C++20 `std::format` and C++23 `std::print`, a format string syntax similar to Python's `str.format`, a fast IEEE 754 floating-point formatter using the Dragonbox algorithm, portable Unicode support, a safe `printf` implementation, support for user-defined types, compile-time format string checks, date and time printing, container formatting, file writing, and text styling with colors.

Intended users are C++ developers seeking high-performance and reliable text formatting in applications ranging from logging and systems programming to databases and machine learning libraries. Notable projects utilizing {fmt} include Apple's FoundationDB, ClickHouse, Envoy, MariaDB, MongoDB, PyTorch, and Windows Terminal. 

Notable technologies and standards mentioned are C++20, C++23, Dragonbox, Python, and standard C/C++ libraries. The project has no external dependencies, offers an optional header-only or modular configuration, and uses the MIT license.

name: modern-cpp-tutorial
description: 📚 Modern C++ Tutorial: C++11 to C++26 On the Fly | https://changkun.de/modern-cpp/
summary:
The "Modern C++ Tutorial: C++11 to C++26 On the Fly" repository provides a comprehensive open-source tutorial and book designed to introduce the features of modern C++ ranging from C++11 through C++26. 

The project's purpose is to offer a quick start guide that covers language features alongside their historical technical backgrounds, encouraging developers to adopt modern C++ in new projects and migrate older codebases. 

The intended users are individuals already familiar with traditional C++ (C++98 or earlier) who want to quickly understand modern C++ features, as well as advanced readers looking to review the material. 

The repository includes chapter-by-chapter source code examples, exercises with answers, and materials to build the documentation locally using Docker. The project's companion website is built using Hexo and Vue.js.

name: ChromeAppHeroes
description: 🌈谷粒-Chrome插件英雄榜, 为优秀的Chrome插件写一本中文说明书, 让Chrome插件英雄们造福人类~  ChromePluginHeroes, Write a Chinese manual for the excellent Chrome plugin, let the Chrome plugin heroes benefit the human~ 公众号「0加1」同步更新
summary:
The project "谷粒-Chrome插件英雄榜" (ChromeAppHeroes) is a curated Chinese manual and collection dedicated to excellent Chrome browser extensions and plugins, aiming to help users discover tools that enhance productivity and browser utility. It provides detailed descriptions, use cases, and feature highlights for over 130 plugins, covering capabilities such as ad-blocking (e.g., uBlock Origin Lite), video and media downloading, translation and language learning (e.g., Immersive Translate), developer tools (e.g., Console Importer, Sourcegraph), reading and note-taking modes, and user interface customizations. 

The project is primarily intended for web developers, designers, students, and general internet users seeking to optimize their browsing experience and workflow. Built using the open-source documentation tool **docsify** and hosted on GitHub Pages, the repository serves as an open knowledge base for browser extensions compatible with Chromium-based ecosystems.

name: fetch
description: A window.fetch JavaScript polyfill.
summary:
This project is a browser-based polyfill implementing a subset of the standard Fetch specification (`window.fetch`), providing a Promise-based mechanism for web requests as a viable replacement for `XMLHttpRequest`. Intended for web developers building browser applications, it supports features such as HTML and JSON parsing, response metadata extraction, form POST requests, and file uploads. Notable capabilities include support for the abortable fetch API via `AbortController` and `AbortSignal`, when combined with additional polyfills. 

Designed exclusively for web browsers and incompatible with Node.js, the project targets older environments including Internet Explorer 10+ and legacy versions of Safari, Chrome, and Firefox. Modern browsers implement `window.fetch` natively, rendering the polyfill inactive on those platforms. Technologies utilized include JavaScript, Promises, and `FormData`.

name: authentik
description: The authentication glue you need.
summary: authentik is an open-source Identity Provider (IdP) designed for modern single sign-on (SSO) and identity management, ranging from small self-hosted labs to large production clusters and enterprise environments. It provides capabilities for secure authentication and authorization using protocols such as SAML, OAuth2/OIDC, LDAP, and RADIUS. The project targets organizations seeking to manage user identities or replace existing identity providers like Okta, Auth0, Entra ID, and Ping Identity. Supported installation technologies and platforms include Docker Compose, Kubernetes via Helm charts, AWS CloudFormation, and the DigitalOcean Marketplace.

name: localForage
description: 💾 Offline storage, improved. Wraps IndexedDB, WebSQL, or localStorage using a simple but powerful API.
summary:
localForage is a fast and simple JavaScript storage library designed to improve web application offline experiences. It provides an asynchronous storage API similar to `localStorage`, using IndexedDB, WebSQL, or localStorage as storage backends depending on browser support. 

Main capabilities include supporting native JavaScript objects, Blobs, ArrayBuffers, and TypedArrays alongside JSON-serializable data, configuring database parameters, managing multiple instances, and defining custom drivers. It offers a dual API supporting both Node-style callbacks and Promises, as well as `async`/`await` syntax. Integration options include RequireJS and TypeScript, with framework drivers available for AngularJS, Angular, Backbone, Ember, Vue, and NuxtJS. 

Intended users are web developers seeking robust offline client-side storage beyond traditional string-only limitations. Notable technologies and tools referenced include IndexedDB, WebSQL, localStorage, RequireJS, TypeScript, PhantomJS, Node, and npm.

name: shap
description: A game theoretic approach to explain the output of any machine learning model.
summary:
SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is a game-theoretic approach designed to explain the output of any machine learning model by connecting optimal credit allocation with local explanations using Shapley values. The project provides unified model-agnostic capabilities as well as specialized high-speed approximation and exact algorithms tailored for different machine learning architectures. 

Main capabilities include `TreeExplainer` for exact and GPU-accelerated tree ensemble methods, `DeepExplainer` and `GradientExplainer` for deep learning models, `LinearExplainer` for linear models, and `KernelExplainer` as a model-agnostic method for arbitrary functions. It also supports natural language processing pipelines through Hugging Face transformers and computes SHAP interaction values. Visualization tools include waterfall plots, force plots, dependence scatter plots, beeswarm plots, and image/text plots.

Intended users include data scientists, machine learning practitioners, and researchers seeking interpretable machine learning. The repository supports notable technologies such as XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, scikit-learn, PySpark, TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch, and Hugging Face transformers, utilizing Python and C++ implementations.

name: Apktool
description: A tool for reverse engineering Android apk files
summary:
Apktool is a tool for reverse engineering third-party, closed, binary Android apps. Its primary purpose is to decode resources to a nearly original form, allow step-by-step debugging of smali code, and rebuild modified apps. It streamlines workflows by providing a project-like file structure and automating repetitive tasks such as building APKs. 

Intended users include developers and researchers looking to localize apps, add new features, or add support for custom platforms. The project utilizes technologies associated with Android application packages and smali code manipulation.

name: Claude-Code-Game-Studios
description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.
summary:
Claude Code Game Studios is a template and orchestration framework designed to transform a single Claude Code session into a structured game development studio. It organizes AI interactions into a hierarchical team comprising 49 specialized agents (spanning directors, department leads, and specialists across design, programming, art, audio, narrative, QA, and production), 74 slash commands (skills), 12 automated hooks, 13 path-scoped coding rules, and 39 document templates. 

The project provides dedicated support for major game engines including Godot 4, Unity, and Unreal Engine 5. It is intended for solo developers and teams looking to add professional studio structure, quality gates, and workflow pipelines to AI-assisted game development. Key technologies and standards referenced include Python 3, Bash, Git, JSON, GDScript, C#, and C++. The software is released under the MIT License.

name: faster-whisper
description: Faster Whisper transcription with CTranslate2
summary:
Faster-Whisper is a Python library that provides a high-performance reimplementation of OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model using CTranslate2, a fast inference engine for Transformer models. It delivers up to four times faster transcription than the original implementation while maintaining identical accuracy and using reduced memory, with further efficiency gains available through 8-bit quantization on both CPU and GPU. 

The project is intended for developers, researchers, and users requiring efficient audio transcription, speech-to-text, and translation. Key capabilities include support for standard and batched transcription, Distil-Whisper model checkpoints, word-level timestamps, and an integrated Silero Voice Activity Detection (VAD) filter to remove non-speech audio. It utilizes PyAV for audio decoding, eliminating external FFmpeg system dependencies, and requires NVIDIA cuBLAS and cuDNN libraries for GPU execution.

name: promptfoo
description: Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs. Red teaming/pentesting/vulnerability scanning for AI. Compare performance of GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more. Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration.  Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.
summary:
Promptfoo is an open-source CLI and library designed for evaluating and red-teaming LLM-based applications. It aims to help developers ship secure, reliable agents by replacing trial-and-error with data-driven metrics. 

Main capabilities include running automated evaluations to test prompts and models, conducting red teaming and vulnerability scanning for security and compliance, comparing models side-by-side, automating checks in CI/CD pipelines, reviewing pull requests via code scanning, and generating security vulnerability reports. The tool runs locally to ensure privacy and supports live reload and caching.

Intended users are software developers and engineering teams building production-grade LLM applications. 

Notable technologies and providers supported include OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, and Ollama, alongside distribution channels via npm, Homebrew (`brew`), and `pip`.

name: ngx-admin
description: Customizable admin dashboard template based on Angular 10+
summary:
ngx-admin is an open-source admin dashboard template built for developers and organizations using Angular. Its primary purpose is to accelerate web application development by providing a feature-rich, responsive layout with over 40 Angular components and 60 usage examples. 

Main capabilities include flexible configurable themes with hot-reload support, an authentication module with multiple providers, high-resolution and RTL support, and a backward-compatible Material theme. The template includes six visual themes (Material Dark, Material Light, Dark, Default, Cosmic, and Corporate). 

Intended users are frontend developers and enterprises seeking to build admin panels or dashboards efficiently. Notable technologies used in the project include Angular, TypeScript, Nebular, Bootstrap 4+, SCSS, and Node.js.

name: NativeScript
description: ⚡ Write Native with TypeScript ✨ Best of all worlds (TypeScript, Swift, Objective C, Kotlin, Java, Dart). Use what you love ❤️ Angular, React, Solid, Svelte, Vue with: iOS (UIKit, SwiftUI), Android (View, Jetpack Compose), Flutter and you name it compatible.
summary:
NativeScript is an open-source framework that empowers developers to directly access native APIs from JavaScript and TypeScript for rich mobile development across iOS, Android, and visionOS. 

Main capabilities include a core primitives package (`@nativescript/core`), comprehensive platform type definitions, UI mobile base classes, and Webpack build utilities (`@nativescript/webpack`). The project supports building applications using popular web frameworks and libraries through dedicated starters, including Angular, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. 

Intended users are mobile application developers seeking to build cross-platform native apps using JavaScript/TypeScript and popular frontend frameworks. Notable technologies and languages involved include JavaScript, TypeScript, C++, Objective-C, Swift, Java, Kotlin, Android SDKs, and iOS SDKs.

name: MiniGPT-4
description: Open-sourced codes for MiniGPT-4 and MiniGPT-v2 (https://minigpt-4.github.io, https://minigpt-v2.github.io/)
summary:
MiniGPT-V (including MiniGPT-4 and MiniGPT-v2) provides open-source vision-language models designed to enhance vision-language understanding and serve as a unified interface for vision-language multi-task learning. The project enables users to perform complex image-to-text tasks—such as visual question answering, captioning, object detection, and multimodal conversation—by connecting advanced large language models with visual encoders. 

Intended users include researchers, developers, and practitioners working in multimodal artificial intelligence, computer vision, and natural language processing. 

Notable technologies and architectures utilized include Llama 2 Chat, Vicuna (7B and 13B), BLIP-2, and the LAVIS library.

name: modern-js-cheatsheet
description: Cheatsheet for the JavaScript knowledge you will frequently encounter in modern projects.
summary:
The Modern JavaScript Cheatsheet project provides a comprehensive reference guide for modern JavaScript concepts, focusing primarily on features introduced in ES2015 (ES6) and contemporary syntax frequently encountered in modern codebases. It is designed to help developers with basic knowledge navigate modern sample code and frameworks like React without learning JavaScript from scratch.

The guide covers a wide range of notions, including variable declarations (`var`, `const`, `let`), arrow functions, default parameters, object and array destructuring, functional array methods (`map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `find`), the spread operator and rest parameters, object property shorthands, promises, template literals, tagged templates, module imports and exports, the `this` operator, classes, inheritance via `extends` and `super`, async/await, truthy/falsy values, anamorphisms, catamorphisms, generators, and static methods, complete with sample code, explanations, and external learning resources.

name: asdf
description: Extendable version manager with support for Ruby, Node.js, Elixir, Erlang & more
summary:
asdf is a single CLI tool designed to manage multiple language runtime versions on a per-project basis, functioning similarly to tools like `gvm`, `nvm`, `rbenv`, and `pyenv`. Targeted at developers, it enables consistent commands for managing various languages through a unified global configuration and a per-project `.tool-versions` configuration file. 

Main capabilities include automatic runtime version switching during directory traversal, support for legacy configuration files such as `.node-version`, `.nvmrc`, and `.ruby-version` to facilitate migration, and shell completion for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and Elvish. The tool is extendable via a simple plugin system that allows users to add support for any programming language of choice using plugins or custom-built solutions.

name: iris
description: The fastest HTTP/2 Go Web Framework. New, modern and easy to learn. Fast development with Code you control. Unbeatable cost-performance ratio :rocket:
summary: Iris is a fast, feature-rich web framework for Go designed to provide an expressive and efficient foundation for building websites and APIs. Its capabilities include HTTP/2 support, built-in middleware (such as Basicauth, CORS, JWT, and Rate limit), API versioning, Model-View-Controller architecture, WebSockets, gRPC, auto-HTTPS, ngrok integration, a dynamic path router, view engines, caching, localization, and rich request/response handling. The upcoming v14 release introduces Go generics, compiler-checked application builders, automated request validation helpers, and a central error map. Designed for Go developers and backend engineers, Iris offers comprehensive dependency injection, an extensive testing suite, and detailed built-in documentation.

name: stagehand
description: The SDK to extract data and interact with any site on the web. Get started with Claude Code, Codex, Eve, Mastra, and more.
summary:
Stagehand is an open-source SDK designed for browser agents and web automation, providing familiar Playwright-style APIs alongside natural language capabilities. Its main capabilities include self-healing browser actions (`act`), element observation (`observe`) to securely retrieve selectors, and schema-validated structured data extraction (`extract`) using technologies like Zod and Pydantic. It also features token-efficient accessibility-tree trimming, WebMCP tool discovery, batch commands, nested iframe/Shadow DOM support, and OpenTelemetry (OTel) traces. 

Stagehand is intended for developers building AI agents and automation suites who require reliable browser interactions. It supports TypeScript, Python, and Go via a unified SDK monorepo. The framework integrates seamlessly with Browserbase for cloud execution, model gateways, server-side caching, and session recordings, and offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for coding assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Additionally, it provides lightweight `search` and `fetch` add-ons to retrieve web page content as markdown or perform token-efficient web searches without launching a full browser.

name: vit-pytorch
description: Implementation of Vision Transformer, a simple way to achieve SOTA in vision classification with only a single transformer encoder, in Pytorch
summary:
This repository provides PyTorch implementations of the Vision Transformer (ViT) and a wide array of its variants, extensions, and self-supervised learning methods for computer vision and video understanding. 

Project Purpose: 
To offer accessible, modular, and easy-to-use PyTorch implementations of foundational and modern vision transformer architectures, facilitating research, experimentation, and efficient training.

Main Capabilities:
- Includes code for standard ViT, SimpleViT, NaViT, DeepViT, CaiT, Token-to-Token ViT, CCT, CrossViT, PiT, LeViT, CvT, Twins SVT, RegionViT, CrossFormer, ScalableViT, SepViT, MaxViT, NesT, MobileViT, XCiT, JetViT, ViT-5, and 3D/video variants (ViViT, 3D ViT).
- Supports self-supervised training frameworks like SimMIM, Masked Autoencoder (MAE), Masked Patch/Position Prediction, Dino, and EsViT.
- Provides utilities for knowledge distillation, attention and embedding extraction (Recorder and Extractor wrappers), adaptive token sampling, and patch merging.

Intended Users: 
Researchers and developers working in computer vision, deep learning, and video/medical imaging who want to experiment with vision transformers.

Notable Technologies: 
PyTorch.

name: homebridge
description: HomeKit support for the impatient.
summary:
Homebridge is a lightweight Node.js server that emulates the HomeKit Accessory Protocol (HAP) and optionally supports the Matter smart home standard. Its primary purpose is to integrate third-party, non-HomeKit smart home devices into Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Samsung SmartThings, and other Matter-compatible controllers, enabling voice control via Siri and other assistants. 

The platform relies on community-contributed plugins available through npm to connect various manufacturer APIs. Notable technologies and libraries used include Node.js, `matter.js` for the Matter protocol implementation, and HAP-NodeJS. Homebridge is intended for smart home enthusiasts and developers seeking to bridge unsupported devices. It supports installation on Raspberry Pi, Linux (Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat, CentOS, Fedora, Arch/Manjaro), macOS, Windows 10/11 (via Hyper-V), Docker, and Synology DSM.

name: request
description: 🏊🏾 Simplified HTTP request client.
summary: Request is a deprecated simplified HTTP client for Node.js designed to make HTTP and HTTPS calls easy. It supports callbacks, streaming, promises, and async/await interfaces. Key capabilities include handling URL-encoded and multipart form uploads, HTTP and digest authentication, custom HTTP headers, OAuth 1.0 signing, proxying with HTTP tunneling and environment variable support, UNIX domain sockets, TLS/SSL protocol configurations, HAR 1.2 support, cookie management via cookie jars, response compression (gzip), and custom timeouts. Distinctive names and technologies include Node.js, HAR 1.2, OAuth, TLS/SSL, and UNIX Domain Sockets.

name: en.javascript.info
description: Modern JavaScript Tutorial
summary: The Modern JavaScript Tutorial repository hosts the English content for the tutorial published at javascript.info, maintained by Ilya Kantor. The project serves as a comprehensive, community-driven resource for learning JavaScript, structured into chapters, articles, and tasks using an enhanced Markdown format. It is intended for learners and developers seeking to understand JavaScript and welcomes contributions, including corrections, new topics, and translations into multiple languages.

name: awesome-claude-code-subagents
description: A collection of 100+ specialized Claude Code subagents covering a wide range of development use cases
summary:
This repository is a curated collection of over 161 specialized Claude Code subagents categorized across 10 domains, including core development, language-specific experts, infrastructure and DevOps, quality and security, data and AI, developer experience, specialized domains, business and product, meta and orchestration, and research and analysis. 

Designed to serve as dedicated AI assistants that enhance Claude Code, these subagents feature independent context windows, granular tool permissions, and task-specific system prompts. They can be installed via Claude Code plugins, interactively through shell scripts, or manually. Notable supporting tools include the `subagent-catalog` command for browsing and fetching subagents within Claude Code. The project targets developers, engineers, and technical teams seeking to scale automation, enforce consistent workflows, and structure interactions across complex software development lifecycles.

name: OmniParser
description: A simple screen parsing tool towards pure vision based GUI agent
summary: OmniParser is a screen parsing tool designed for pure vision-based GUI agents to convert user interface screenshots into structured, easy-to-understand elements. The project aims to enhance the ability of vision and language models, such as GPT-4V, to generate actions accurately grounded in specific interface regions. Its main capabilities include fine-grained icon detection, prediction of interactable screen elements, interactive region detection utilizing YOLOv9-E, and icon functional descriptions. Additionally, it integrates with OmniTool to control Windows 11 virtual machines and build training data pipelines for domain-specific agents. Intended users include developers and researchers building computer-use agents, multi-agent orchestrations, and vision-based GUI automation systems. Notable technologies and components used comprise YOLOv9, Python, Gradio, and Hugging Face model checkpoints.

name: .tmux
description: Oh my tmux! My self-contained, pretty & versatile tmux configuration made with 💛🩷💙🖤❤️🤍
summary:
Oh my tmux! is a self-contained, versatile, and visually polished tmux configuration designed to provide sane defaults, enhanced usability, and advanced status line features for terminal users. It targets developers and system administrators running tmux (>= 2.6) on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, or Windows via WSL. 

Main capabilities include a Powerline-inspired visual theme, secondary `C-a` prefix support, enhanced window and pane navigation with Vim-style key bindings, mouse mode toggles, session management shortcuts, and automatic OS clipboard integration. It also supports pane maximizing into new windows, SSH/Mosh-aware hostname and username tracking, uptime and battery status information, and integrations with PathPicker, Urlscan, Urlview, and TPM (Tmux Plugin Manager). 

Intended users are command-line power users and developers seeking a feature-rich, customizable tmux environment. The project is implemented using shell configuration files and relies on standard command-line tools like awk, sed, grep, and perl, alongside terminal emulators supporting true color and Powerline fonts.

name: howler.js
description: Javascript audio library for the modern web.
summary:
howler.js is a pure JavaScript audio library designed for the modern web. It provides a single, unified API that defaults to the Web Audio API and falls back to HTML5 Audio, ensuring reliable cross-browser and cross-platform audio handling. 

Main capabilities include automatic caching, simultaneous playback of multiple sounds, individual or group/global sound control, sound sprite definitions, streaming support for large files, and full control over fading, rates, seeking, and volume. It also includes an optional spatial plugin for 3D spatial sound and stereo panning. Intended users are web developers looking for a lightweight (7kb gzipped), dependency-free solution for managing web audio. 

The library supports all major codecs (such as WebM, MP3, WAV, AAC, and Dolby Audio) and features automatic mobile audio unlocking and handling of environment-specific bugs.

name: toBeTopJavaer
description: To Be Top Javaer - Java工程师成神之路
summary:
To Be Top Javaer (Java工程师成神之路) is a comprehensive knowledge system and learning guide designed for Java engineers to progress from beginners to experts. Authored by Hollis, an Alibaba technical expert, the project outlines a structured learning path encompassing core Java technologies, knowledge体系 refinements, and new technology integrations across multiple version updates. 

Main capabilities include providing a structured knowledge repository for reading via GitHub Pages and Gitee Pages, offering a companion interview question set consisting of over 500 questions and 600,000 words, and distributing an updated mind map via an official WeChat public account. The intended users are Java developers, software engineers, and programming learners seeking to master computer programming and Java core technologies. The project encourages community participation through issues and pull requests on GitHub under the GPL license.

name: v8
description: The official mirror of the V8 Git repository
summary: V8 is Google's open-source JavaScript and WebAssembly engine written in C++. It implements ECMAScript as specified in ECMA-262. V8 can run standalone or be embedded into any C++ application, and it serves as the JavaScript engine used in Chromium, Google's open-source browser.

name: PhotoSwipe
description: JavaScript image gallery for mobile and desktop, modular, framework independent
summary: PhotoSwipe is a JavaScript image gallery and lightbox library designed for web applications and sites. It provides core functionality and a lightbox entry point for displaying images in a responsive, interactive gallery format. The repository structure includes source and distribution files built using Rollup, alongside documentation and a demo website.

name: pentagi
description: Fully autonomous AI Agents system capable of performing complex penetration testing tasks
summary:
PentAGI (Penetration testing Artificial General Intelligence) is an autonomous, self-hosted security testing platform designed for information security professionals and ethical hackers. It provides a sandboxed Docker environment where AI agents plan and execute penetration tests using over 20 built-in security tools such as nmap, metasploit, and sqlmap.

Key capabilities include a smart memory system backed by PostgreSQL and pgvector, an optional Neo4j/Graphiti knowledge graph for semantic relationship tracking, web intelligence gathering via a built-in browser, and support for 10+ LLM providers and aggregators including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Ollama, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, MiniMax, Mistral, and xAI. It features specialized AI agent roles, multi-layered agent supervision (execution monitoring and intelligent task planning), comprehensive monitoring via Prometheus/Grafana, and vulnerability reporting. Programmatic access is available through full-featured REST and GraphQL APIs with Bearer token authentication.

Intended for authorized ethical hackers, security researchers, and enterprise security teams, PentAGI operates entirely within isolated Docker containers to perform secure penetration testing workflows.

name: TDengine
description: High-performance, scalable time-series database designed for Industrial IoT (IIoT) scenarios
summary:
TDengine is an open-source, high-performance, cloud-native, and AI-powered time-series database (TSDB) engineered specifically for Internet of Things (IoT), connected cars, and industrial IoT workloads. It efficiently ingests, processes, and analyzes high-cardinality, terabyte-to-petabyte-scale data generated by billions of data collection points.

Key capabilities include real-time data ingestion and querying, high compression rates, built-in caching, stream processing, data subscription, and super tables for simplified data organization. Its cloud-native architecture features native distributed sharding and partitioning, separation of compute and storage, RAFT consensus, and Kubernetes support. It is also AI-powered via TDgpt, an integrated AI agent connecting to foundation models, machine learning algorithms, and large language models to enable forecasting, anomaly detection, imputation, and classification. 

Intended users include developers, database administrators, and data analysts working with large-scale time-series data. The project utilizes notable technologies such as CMake, C/C++, Python, Go, and Rust bindings, and supports deployment on Linux, macOS, and container platforms under the GNU Affero General Public License 3.0.

name: llm-action
description: 本项目旨在分享大模型相关技术原理以及实战经验（大模型工程化、大模型应用落地）
summary:
This repository serves as a comprehensive knowledge base and practical tutorial collection for Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI engineering. Its purpose is to help researchers and developers master the end-to-end lifecycle of LLMs, covering training, fine-tuning, inference, compression, evaluation, data engineering, and infrastructure deployment.

The main capabilities span full-stack LLM technologies:
- **Training & Fine-Tuning**: Pre-training, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods (PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA, GaLore) using distributed parallel techniques (data, pipeline, tensor, and sequence parallelism).
- **Inference & Optimization**: High-performance inference engines and optimization techniques such as KV Cache, Continuous batching, and FlashAttention.
- **Model Compression**: Post-training quantization (GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant, FP8), structured/unstructured pruning, knowledge distillation, and low-rank factorization.
- **Evaluation & Benchmarking**: Frameworks and test suites for assessing model accuracy, instruction-following capabilities, and inference performance.
- **Infrastructure & Localization**: Distributed AI frameworks (PyTorch, DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM), AI compilers (MLIR, TVM, XLA), and domestic hardware adaptation for accelerators like Huawei Ascend.

Intended users include AI engineers, researchers, and developers seeking practical guidance on LLM deployment and AI system engineering. Notable technologies include PyTorch, DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM, HuggingFace PEFT, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, and Triton.

name: SmartRefreshLayout
description: 🔥下拉刷新、上拉加载、二级刷新、淘宝二楼、RefreshLayout、OverScroll，Android智能下拉刷新框架，支持越界回弹、越界拖动，具有极强的扩展性，集成了几十种炫酷的Header和 Footer。
summary:
SmartRefreshLayout is an Android intelligent pull-down refresh and load-more layout framework designed to support all types of Views (such as AbsListView, RecyclerView, and WebView) and multi-layer nested view structures. Built by extending `ViewGroup` for enhanced performance, it supports multi-touch, nested scrolling with `CoordinatorLayout`, synchronization with `ListView`, automatic refresh and load-more triggers, custom rebound interpolators, boundary over-scrolling, and second-level refresh (Taobao-style two-layer layouts). 

The framework features modular architecture split into separate packages such as `refresh-layout-kernel`, classics and radar headers, material headers, and ball pulse footers. It supports custom Header and Footer implementations, sliding modes including translation, stretching, and fixed top/back layers, and AndroidX. Intended for Android developers building application user interfaces, SmartRefreshLayout provides flexible configuration options via Java code, XML attributes, or global application setups.

name: gin-vue-admin
description: 🚀Vite+Vue3+Gin拥有AI辅助的基础开发平台，企业级业务AI+开发解决方案，内置mcp辅助服务，内置skills管理，支持TS和JS混用。它集成了JWT鉴权、权限管理、动态路由、显隐可控组件、分页封装、多点登录拦截、资源权限、上传下载、代码生成器、表单生成器和可配置的导入导出等开发必备功能。
summary:
Gin-vue-admin is a full-stack, separation-of-concerns development framework designed to rapidly build admin panels and medium-to-small enterprise projects. 

Its main capabilities include JWT authentication, dynamic routing and menus, Casbin-based permission control, automated API documentation generation via Swagger, multi-point login restrictions using Redis, file chunk uploading with cloud storage integrations (Qiniu, Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud), a form generator, and a backend/CRUD code generator. 

The intended users are developers with foundational knowledge of Go and Vue seeking to accelerate application development by leveraging pre-built authentication, user management, role management, and menu configuration modules. 

Notable technologies used include Go, the Gin web framework, Vue, Element Plus, GORM, MySQL/MariaDB, Redis, Viper, FSNotify, and Zap.

name: labelImg
description: LabelImg is now part of the Label Studio community. The popular image annotation tool created by Tzutalin is no longer actively being developed, but you can check out Label Studio, the open source data labeling tool for images, text, hypertext, audio, video and time-series data.
summary:
LabelImg is a graphical image annotation tool designed for labeling objects in images with bounding boxes. It is intended for machine learning practitioners, researchers, and developers preparing datasets for computer vision tasks. The application supports saving annotations in PASCAL VOC (used by ImageNet), YOLO, and CreateML formats as XML or TXT files. 

Main capabilities include creating and editing rectangular bounding boxes, visualizing existing annotations, managing pre-defined classes, and flagging images as verified. It features a graphical user interface equipped with numerous hotkeys to streamline the labeling workflow. 

LabelImg is written in Python and utilizes Qt (specifically PyQt5) for its graphical interface, with `lxml` used for XML handling. It can be installed via PyPI, built from source across Linux, macOS, and Windows environments (including Anaconda distributions), or run via Docker.

name: pipenv
description: Python Development Workflow for Humans.
summary:
Pipenv is a Python virtual environment and dependency management tool designed to bridge the gaps between `pip`, `virtualenv`, and Python interpreters like `pyenv` or `asdf`. It automates virtual environment creation and manages project dependencies through a `Pipfile` and `Pipfile.lock`, enabling deterministic builds, hash verification for security, and dependency graph inspection. 

The tool is intended for Python application developers and users seeking a consistent working project environment across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Notable capabilities include automatically generating project files, supporting local environment customizations via `.env` files, checking for security vulnerabilities, and installing packages from version control systems like Git. Pipenv requires Python 3.10 and above and integrates shell completion powered by `argcomplete`.

name: PlotNeuralNet
description: Latex code for making neural networks diagrams
summary: PlotNeuralNet provides LaTeX and Python code for drawing architectural diagrams of neural networks for use in reports and presentations. The project's main capabilities include generating visual representations of networks such as FCN-8, FCN-32, and Holistically-Nested Edge Detection through a Python interface that outputs TikZ/LaTeX code. It is intended for researchers, developers, and writers who need to create publication-ready figures of machine learning models. Notable technologies used in the project include LaTeX, TikZ, and Python, with installation instructions provided for Ubuntu and Windows environments.

name: highlight.js
description: JavaScript syntax highlighter with language auto-detection and zero dependencies.
summary:
Highlight.js is a syntax highlighter written in JavaScript that operates in web browsers and on servers. It works with diverse markup structures, has no framework dependencies, and provides automatic language detection for over 180 languages in its core library. 

Intended for developers seeking to style and highlight code blocks in web pages or server environments, the project supports custom usage configurations, Vue.js integration via `highlightjs/vue-plugin`, and asynchronous processing via Web Workers. 

The library can be installed via npm or yarn using packages such as `highlight.js` or `@highlightjs/cdn-assets`, fetched through popular CDNs including cdnjs, jsdelivr, and unpkg, or built directly from source. Highlight.js is released under the BSD License.

name: pydata-book
description: Materials and IPython notebooks for "Python for Data Analysis" by Wes McKinney, published by O'Reilly Media
summary:
This repository contains materials and IPython notebooks for "Python for Data Analysis, 3rd Edition" by Wes McKinney, published by O'Reilly Media. It provides practical examples, tutorials, and code samples covering Python language basics, Jupyter Notebooks, NumPy arrays and vectorized computation, pandas data structures, data loading, storage, cleaning, wrangling, plotting and visualization, data aggregation, group operations, time series, and modeling libraries. 

The project is intended for readers and practitioners learning data analysis using Python. Notable technologies used include Python, pandas (specifically version 2.0.3), NumPy, Jupyter Notebook, and uv for package management and environment resolution. Setup instructions support both uv and Conda environments, and separate branches are available for readers of the 1st and 2nd editions.

name: games
description: Archived — A list of games, add-ons, maps, etc. hosted on GitHub. Any genre. Any platform. Any engine.
summary:
Games on GitHub is an archived, curated community-driven collection of open-source games, engines, frameworks, plugins, and development utilities. The repository catalogues thousands of projects spanning browser-based, native, and mobile platforms, covering diverse genres such as arcade, first-person shooters (FPS), role-playing games (RPGs), massively multiplayer online role-playing games (MMORPGs), strategy, racing, puzzles, and sandboxes. 

Intended for game developers, open-source contributors, and enthusiasts, the collection highlights numerous game development frameworks, physics engines, rendering libraries, chat bots, and toolsets implemented across a wide array of programming languages and technologies, including JavaScript, HTML5, WebGL, C++, Python, Java, and ActionScript.

name: chromium
description: The official GitHub mirror of the Chromium source
summary: Chromium is an open-source browser project that aims to build a safer, faster, and more stable way for all users to experience the web. The repository contains the source code for the browser and related products such as Chrome, Android WebView, and Ash. Intended users include developers and contributors working with the Chromium source code directory structure and documentation rooted in `docs/README.md`.

name: delve
description: Delve is a debugger for the Go programming language.
summary: Delve is a debugger for the Go programming language. Its primary purpose is to provide a simple, full-featured, and easy-to-use debugging tool designed to stay out of the developer's way during troubleshooting. Delve includes a command-line client, command-line options, an API, and support for plugins and GUIs, making it suitable for Go developers seeking to inspect and debug applications.

name: LSPosed
description: LSPosed Framework
summary:
LSPosed Framework is a Riru or Zygisk module designed to provide an ART hooking framework that delivers consistent APIs with the original Xposed. It leverages the LSPlant hooking framework and Magisk to allow users and developers to modify the behavior of the Android system and applications in-memory without altering APKs. 

Main capabilities include supporting in-memory modifications, enabling multiple modules to affect the same system or app parts simultaneously, and ensuring full compatibility with original Xposed modules. It supports Android versions 8.1 through 14. Intended users include Android power users and developers seeking to write or utilize Xposed-compatible modules. Notable technologies and projects utilized include Magisk, Riru, XposedBridge, Dobby, LSPlant, and the GNU General Public License v3 (GPL-3).

name: activepieces
description: AI Agents & MCPs & AI Workflow Automation • (~400 MCP servers for AI agents) • AI Automation / AI Agent with MCPs • AI Workflows & AI Agents • MCPs for AI Agents
summary:
Activepieces is an open-source, all-in-one AI automation and workflow builder designed as an extensible alternative to Zapier. It targets both technical and non-technical users within organizations seeking a secure, self-hosted integration platform. 

Main capabilities include an intuitive flow builder with loops, branches, auto-retries, versioning, HTTP actions, and NPM code execution. It features over 200 open-source integrations, native AI integration for experimenting with various providers and custom agents, human-in-the-loop approval workflows, and interactive chat and form input triggers. Additionally, all community and built-in pieces automatically function as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for LLMs via tools like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf.

The project is built using TypeScript, providing a type-safe piece framework with hot-reloading for local development, where integrations are structured as type-safe npm packages.

name: websocket
description: Package gorilla/websocket is a fast, well-tested and widely used WebSocket implementation for Go.
summary: Gorilla WebSocket is a Go implementation of the WebSocket protocol (RFC 6455). It provides a complete, tested, and protocol-compliant package with a stable API, passing the server tests in the Autobahn Test Suite. The repository includes examples for chat, command execution, echo (client and server), and file watching.

name: lucide
description: Beautiful & consistent icon toolkit made by the community. Open-source project and a fork of Feather Icons.
summary: Lucide is an open-source icon library and fork of Feather Icons that provides over 1,600 vector SVG files for digital and non-digital projects. Designed for developers and designers, the project offers official packages and integrations for JavaScript, React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact, React Native, Angular, Astro, and static SVG usage, along with a dedicated Figma plugin. The library is distributed under the ISC License.

name: firefly-iii
description: Firefly III: a personal finances manager
summary: Firefly III is a free, open-source, and self-hosted personal finance manager designed to help users track expenses, manage income, and gain insight into their budgets. Intended for privacy-conscious, tech-savvy individuals who prefer local server administration over cloud uploads, it features a double-entry bookkeeping system, recurring transactions, rule-based transaction handling, piggy banks for goal savings, financial reports, multi-currency support, two-factor authentication, data import tools, and a comprehensive REST JSON API. The software is distributed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3 and can be deployed via technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

name: Tasmota
description: Alternative firmware for ESP8266 and ESP32 based devices with easy configuration using webUI, OTA updates, automation using timers or rules, expandability and entirely local control over MQTT, HTTP, Serial or KNX. Full documentation at
summary:
Tasmota is an alternative open-source firmware designed for ESP8266, ESP8285, and ESP32 family devices. It provides entirely local control and easy configuration via a webUI, supporting OTA updates, automation through timers and rules, and communication via MQTT, HTTP, Serial, or KNX. 

Intended for smart home enthusiasts and developers, Tasmota integrates with platforms like Home Assistant, Domoticz, openHAB, Node-RED, and native Matter ecosystems, alongside cloud options such as AWS IoT Core and Azure IoT Hub. It supports over 150 sensors and peripherals, smart appliances, lighting controls, protocol bridging (including Zigbee, Bluetooth, IR, RF, Modbus, and DALI), displays with LVGL touch interfaces, and audio. The firmware also features the Berry scripting language, a DSL-based LED animation engine, and networking options like Ethernet, WireGuard VPN, and TasMesh. 

Written for PlatformIO, the project includes development tools and documentation to help users build custom firmware binaries and connect local smart devices.

name: cli
description: Command-line tool to customize Spotify client. Supports Windows, macOS, and Linux.
summary: Spicetify CLI is a command-line tool designed to customize the official Spotify client across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Its main capabilities include changing user interface colors, injecting custom CSS for advanced styling, injecting extensions to manipulate the UI and control the player, and adding custom apps. The tool is intended for users who want complete control over their Spotify client experience. Notable technologies utilized include Go (indicated by the Go Report Card) and code signing provided by SignPath.io and the SignPath Foundation.

name: EventBus
description: Event bus for Android and Java that simplifies communication between Activities, Fragments, Threads, Services, etc. Less code, better quality.
summary:
EventBus is a publish/subscribe event bus library for Android and Java designed to simplify communication between components. It decouples event senders and receivers, integrates with Activities, Fragments, and background threads, and avoids complex life cycle issues and dependencies. 

Main capabilities include fast event delivery, advanced features such as delivery threads and subscriber priorities, and support for an annotation processor with a subscriber index to prevent reflection-related problems. The library is tiny (approximately 60k), ships with embedded rules for R8 and ProGuard, and is available on Maven Central for both Android and Java projects. It is intended for Android and Java developers seeking a proven messaging solution.

name: RxSwift
description: Reactive Programming in Swift
summary:
RxSwift is the Swift-specific implementation of the Reactive Extensions (Rx) standard, serving as a generic abstraction of computation expressed through the `Observable<Element>` interface. It enables developers to easily compose asynchronous operations and streams of data, unifying asynchronous tasks, KVO observations, and UI events under the abstraction of sequences. 

The project's main capabilities include broadcasting and subscribing to values from observable streams, transforming and composing asynchronous work using a suite of operators, and supporting testing for reactive systems. It is divided into five components: **RxSwift** (core logic), **RxCocoa** (Cocoa-specific extensions for UI app development), **RxRelay** (wrappers around subjects), **RxTest**, and **RxBlocking**. 

Intended for developers building applications for iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and Linux, the project utilizes the Swift programming language and integrates via tools like Swift Package Manager, Carthage, XCFrameworks, or manual inclusion.

name: editor
description: Open-source 3D architectural editor with a local CLI, MCP tools, and practical workflows for humans and AI agents.
summary:
Pascal Editor is an open-source, local-first 3D building editor designed for architecture, home building, facility management, home services, and infrastructure. It runs in the browser or via a CLI and enables AI agent integration through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Main capabilities include 3D scene editing, hierarchical scene management (ranging from sites and buildings down to levels, walls, slabs, ceilings, roofs, and items), procedural geometry generation, collision detection, spatial queries, and capture extensions. It supports extensible plugin architecture for custom node types, panels, and renderers.

Intended users include developers, architects, builders, facility managers, and AI agents interacting through MCP workflows. 

Notable technologies used include React 19, Next.js 16, Three.js with WebGPU renderer, React Three Fiber, Drei, Zustand, Zod, Zundo, three-bvh-csg, Turborepo, Bun, and Node.js.

name: eslint
description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.
summary: ESLint is an open-source tool designed for developers to identify and report on patterns found in ECMAScript and JavaScript code. Its core capabilities include parsing JavaScript via Espree, utilizing an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) to evaluate code patterns, and offering a fully pluggable architecture where every rule functions as a plugin. It supports JSX syntax natively and can be configured through customizable rules and error levels. Intended for JavaScript developers and maintainers seeking code quality and static analysis, the project runs on Node.js and adheres to semantic versioning and the OpenJS Foundation Code of Conduct.

name: claude-skills
description: 380 Claude Code skills & agent skills & plugins (30+ Agents, 70+ custom commands, 380+ skills, customizable references, scripts)for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and 8 more coding agents — engineering, marketing, product, compliance, C-level advisory, research, business operations, commercial & finance, and your daily productivity skills.
summary:
This repository is an open-source library of 388 production-ready skills, plugins, and agent packages designed to provide domain expertise and workflows for 13 AI coding tools and platforms, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Hermes Agent, and Mistral Vibe. 

The project purpose is to augment AI coding assistants with reusable knowledge across 20 domains. Main capabilities span software engineering, DevOps, product management, marketing (including Answer Engine Optimization), security auditing, regulatory compliance, productivity workflows, academic research, enterprise Research Operations, business growth, and a full suite of C-level advisory personas and slash commands. It also includes an agent launcher and a markdown-to-HTML conversion stack.

Intended users include developers, technical founders, product managers, marketers, and researchers seeking structured, multi-platform prompt instruction and tool automation. Notable technologies featured include Python (providing over 700 standard library-only CLI tools), Playwright, GitHub Actions, Terraform, Helm, and support for the `agentskills.io` standard alongside specialized conversion and installation scripts for diverse development environments.

name: symphony
description: Symphony turns project work into isolated, autonomous implementation runs, allowing teams to manage work instead of supervising coding agents.
summary: Symphony is a project purpose-built to turn software project work into isolated, autonomous implementation runs, enabling teams to manage tasks rather than supervise coding agents directly. Its main capabilities include monitoring issue trackers such as Linear boards, spawning agents to handle assigned tasks, and providing proof of work including CI status, PR review feedback, complexity analysis, and walkthrough videos before safely landing accepted pull requests. The intended users are software engineering teams operating in environments that have adopted harness engineering. The project includes an experimental reference implementation built in Elixir, referenced alongside a formal specification (`SPEC.md`). Symphony is distributed under the Apache License 2.0.

name: 30-Days-Of-React
description: 30 Days of  React challenge is a step by step guide to learn React in 30 days.  These videos may help too: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC7PNRuno1rzYPb1xLa4yktw
summary:
This repository contains **30 Days Of React**, an educational programming challenge and step-by-step guide created by Asabeneh Yetayeh to help both beginners and advanced developers learn React. 

**Project Purpose:**
The guide is designed to teach users how to develop React applications, add interactivity to websites, and build mobile apps, desktop applications, and games. It aims to significantly improve participants' programming and problem-solving skills over a 30-day period.

**Main Capabilities & Topics:**
- Comprehensive daily modules covering JavaScript refreshers, React fundamentals, components, props, lists, keys, class components, states, conditional rendering, project folder structures, events, forms, controlled versus uncontrolled components, and component life cycles.
- Advanced topics including third-party packages, higher-order components, React Router, Fetch versus Axios, hooks, custom hooks, context, and refs.
- Hands-on coding exercises and practical projects built into the curriculum.

**Intended Users:**
The challenge targets both beginners and advanced JavaScript and React developers who possess intermediate-level skills in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

**Notable Technologies:**
- React
- JavaScript (ES6+)
- Node.js
- HTML & CSS
- Google Chrome & V8 engine
- Visual Studio Code

name: Wox
description: A cross-platform launcher that simply works
summary:
Wox is a fully native, open-source launcher designed for Windows, macOS, and Linux as an alternative to Raycast and Alfred. Positioned as a keyboard-first productivity tool, it facilitates local file searches, application launching, and quick actions through a focused input interface. 

The project features full native GPU rendering on all supported platforms without utilizing Electron or browser shells, and it maintains a low idle memory footprint of approximately 150 MB. Its capabilities are extended via an extensible plugin system supporting Node.js, Python, and custom script plugins, alongside a dedicated theme store. Intended users include developers and power users seeking a lightweight, background-resident desktop launcher. Installation is supported via package managers such as Homebrew, Winget, Scoop, Chocolatey, and the Arch User Repository (AUR).

name: mongoose
description: MongoDB object modeling designed to work in an asynchronous environment.
summary: Mongoose is an asynchronous object modeling tool designed for MongoDB, supporting Node.js and Deno (alpha). It provides a schema-based solution to model application data, featuring built-in type casting, validation, query building, business logic hooks (middleware), and schema-level default values, getters, setters, and indexes. Mongoose is built on top of the official MongoDB Node.js driver, automatically buffering commands until a database connection is established. It supports defining embedded documents, custom methods, statics, and pseudo-joins. The project also includes Mongoose Studio, a browser-based GUI for managing MongoDB documents, schemas, and queries.

name: Awesome-LLM
description: Awesome-LLM: a curated list of Large Language Model
summary: Awesome-LLM is a curated resource repository focused on large language models (LLMs), featuring foundational papers, benchmarks, open-source model checkpoints, datasets, and tooling. The project provides structured lists and guides covering LLM training frameworks, inference and deployment engines, evaluation benchmarks, and application development libraries. Designed for AI researchers, developers, and practitioners, the repository highlights state-of-the-art technologies and popular projects related to models like DeepSeek-R1, Llama, Qwen, and OpenAI GPT series. Key capabilities documented include 3D-parallelism training, RLHF, memory-efficient inference, and RAG application architectures.

name: kit
description: A standard library for microservices.
summary:
Go kit is a programming toolkit designed for building microservices and elegant monoliths in Go. It provides a comprehensive set of packages and best practices to solve common problems in distributed systems and service-oriented architectures, enabling developers to focus on delivering business value. 

The project's primary messaging pattern is RPC, supporting pluggable serialization and transport mechanisms rather than being restricted to JSON over HTTP. It is designed to operate within heterogeneous service-oriented architectures and existing infrastructures without mandating specific deployment, configuration, or orchestration tools. 

Go kit is intended for developers and organizations of any size building scalable Go-based backends and distributed systems. It is Go modules-aware while maintaining compatibility with non-modules environments.

name: Graphite
description: Community-built comprehensive 2D content creation appplication for graphic design, digital art, and interactive real-time motion graphics powered by a node-based procedural graphics engine
summary:
Graphite is a free, open-source vector and raster graphics engine designed as a procedural toolbox for 2D content creation. It features a fully nondestructive editing workflow that combines layer-based compositing with a node-based generative design core.
