Built similarly to a game engine, Graphite wraps its tools around a node graph to support user-friendly workflows for vector and raster graphics, with planned expansions for photo editing, motion graphics, digital painting, desktop publishing, and VFX compositing. 

The project is intended for artists, designers, graphics programmers, and Rust developers seeking a comprehensive, accessible content creation tool. Notable technologies and architectural aspects include a node graph core supporting nondestructive boolean operations, procedural patterns, and infinite scalability. The source code is implemented in Rust and dual-licensed under the MIT License and the Apache License 2.0.

name: agenticSeek
description: Fully Local Manus AI. No APIs, No $200 monthly bills. Enjoy an autonomous agent that thinks, browses the web, and code for the sole cost of electricity.
summary:
AgenticSeek is an open-source, voice-enabled AI assistant designed as a 100% private, local alternative to Manus AI. It operates entirely on user hardware without cloud dependencies, making it tailored for local reasoning models.

The project's main capabilities include autonomous smart web browsing (searching, reading, extracting information, and form-filling), an autonomous coding assistant capable of writing, debugging, and running programs in languages such as Python, C, Go, and Java, smart agent selection to automatically deploy the best agent for a task, and multi-agent task planning and execution. It also features experimental speech-to-text and text-to-speech voice interaction.

AgenticSeek is intended for developers, researchers, and privacy-conscious users seeking an independent AI automation tool that keeps all files, conversations, and searches on-device. It supports local LLM providers including Ollama and LM Studio (as well as OpenAI-compatible local servers like llama.cpp), alongside optional cloud-based API providers like OpenAI, Google Gemini, Deepseek, Hugging Face, TogetherAI, OpenRouter, and MiniMax. Built with Python and Docker, the repository integrates tools like SearxNG and Redis for search capabilities.

name: CS-Books
description: 🔥🔥超过1000本的计算机经典书籍、个人笔记资料以及本人在各平台发表文章中所涉及的资源等。书籍资源包括C/C++、Java、Python、Go语言、数据结构与算法、操作系统、后端架构、计算机系统知识、数据库、计算机网络、设计模式、前端、汇编以及校招社招各种面经~
summary:
This repository provides a curated collection of over 1,000 classic computer science electronic books, learning notes, and interview preparation materials. Its primary purpose is to serve as a comprehensive, centralized resource for computer science students and software engineers looking for programming and technical literature. 

The repository covers a wide range of subjects, including programming languages such as C, C++, Java, Python, and Go, alongside foundational topics like data structures and algorithms, operating systems, Linux, computer networks, databases, backend architecture, and machine learning. Additionally, it offers interview question banks, study notes, and career development guides tailored for campus recruitment and technical job seekers. 

The intended users are computer science undergraduates, fresh graduates, and experienced professionals (such as junior to mid-level backend engineers) preparing for job interviews or seeking to deepen their technical knowledge. The resource links utilize notable cloud storage services and platforms, preserving specific technical documentation, guides, and popular developer roadmaps.

name: Ehviewer_CN_SXJ
description: ehviewer，用爱发电，快乐前行
summary: EhViewer is an E-Hentai browser application designed for the Android platform. It provides users with capabilities to browse, search, and download galleries, manage download tasks with features like pause/resume and drag-and-drop sorting, handle local album and archive imports, view reading progress, and interact with comments and ratings. The app includes mechanisms for logging in through WebViews and handling Cloudflare verification. Notable technologies and libraries used in the project include Kotlin, Java, Gradle, jsoup, OkHttp, greenDAO, and libwebp. Intended users are Android device owners looking for an optimized client to access and read content from E-Hentai.

name: Daily-Interview-Question
description: 我是依扬（木易杨），公众号「高级前端进阶」作者，每天搞定一道前端大厂面试题，祝大家天天进步，一年后会看到不一样的自己。
summary: The repository contains a collection of daily frontend interview questions and detailed answers designed to help developers prepare for interviews at major technology companies. Intended for frontend developers and learners seeking technical advancement, the project provides regular coding challenges, algorithm problems, and conceptual questions covering JavaScript, CSS, performance optimization, and frameworks such as Vue.

name: axum
description: HTTP routing and request-handling library for Rust that focuses on ergonomics and modularity
summary:
Axum is an HTTP routing and request-handling library for Rust that focuses on ergonomics and modularity. Its main capabilities include routing requests via a macro-free API, declaratively parsing requests using extractors, providing a predictable error handling model, and generating responses with minimal boilerplate. 

Axum leverages the `tower` and `tower-http` ecosystem by utilizing `tower::Service` directly instead of a custom middleware system, allowing applications to integrate features like timeouts, tracing, compression, and authorization while sharing middleware with other libraries such as `hyper` and `tonic`. Built as a thin layer on top of `hyper`, the library ensures high performance with low overhead and is implemented in 100% safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). The minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) is 1.80.

Intended users are Rust developers building web applications and HTTP services who want a modular, extensible routing framework compatible with the Tower ecosystem.

name: underscore
description: JavaScript's utility _ belt
summary: Underscore.js is a utility-belt library for JavaScript that provides support for standard functional programming tasks such as each, map, reduce, and filter without extending any core JavaScript objects. The library is intended for JavaScript developers seeking functional programming helpers. It is an open-sourced component of DocumentCloud.

name: awesome-electron
description: Useful resources for creating apps with Electron [SUBMISSIONS ARE TEMPORARILY PAUSED BECAUSE I'M TIRED OF REVIEWING LOW-QUALITY STUFF]
summary:
Awesome Electron is a curated list of useful resources, applications, boilerplates, tools, components, and educational materials for creating desktop applications with the Electron framework. Electron combines the Chromium rendering engine and the Node.js runtime to enable cross-platform development using web technologies. 

The repository serves developers, designers, and creators looking for open-source and closed-source app examples (such as Visual Studio Code, Hyper, and WebTorrent), project boilerplates (incorporating tools like React, Vue, Angular, TypeScript, and Webpack), development and packaging tools (such as electron-builder, electron-packager, and Vite integrations), UI component toolkits, documentation, articles, books, videos, and podcasts.

name: hacker-laws
description: 🧠 Laws, Theories, Principles and Patterns for developers and technologists.
summary: Hacker-Laws is a reference repository and overview of laws, theories, principles, and patterns commonly discussed by developers and technologists. Its purpose is to compile well-known software engineering and socio-technical concepts—ranging from Amdahl's Law and Conway's Law to SOLID principles, the CAP Theorem, and Brooks' Law—providing concise explanations and real-world context without advocating for their absolute application. The project is intended for developers, engineers, and technical teams seeking a curated guide to software development realities, system design principles, and organizational patterns.

name: generative-models
description: Generative Models by Stability AI
summary:
This repository contains generative models and a modular, config-driven codebase developed by Stability AI for diffusion-based image, video, and 4D asset synthesis. 

Project Purpose:
The project provides official implementations, training scripts, and inference pipelines for state-of-the-art generative models including Stable Video 4D 2.0 (SV4D 2.0), Stable Video 4D (SV4D), Stable Video 3D (SV3D), Stable Video Diffusion (SVD and SVD-XT), SDXL-Turbo, and Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL base and refiner versions 0.9 and 1.0).

Main Capabilities:
- High-fidelity novel-view video synthesis, 4D asset generation from video inputs, and image-to-video 3D orbit generation.
- Text-to-image and image-to-image generation via ultra-fast and high-resolution diffusion architectures.
- Invisible watermark embedding and detection for generated visual media.
- Modular training pipelines supporting continuous-time and discrete-time diffusion models, flexible conditioning via `GeneralConditioner`, independent samplers, and custom noise-scaling/loss-weighting configurations.

Intended Users:
AI researchers, machine learning engineers, and developers looking to perform inference or train large-scale latent diffusion models.

Notable Technologies:
Python, PyTorch, PyTorch Lightning, WebDataset, Hugging Face Hub, and Streamlit.

name: planning-with-files
description: Persistent file-based planning for AI coding agents and long-running tasks. Crash-proof markdown plans, session recovery after /clear and compaction, per-turn re-injection against context rot, deterministic completion gate. Manus-style. Install from npm, the Claude Code plugin marketplace, or npx skills. Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, 60+ agents.
summary:
Planning with Files is a persistent file-based planning skill designed for AI coding agents and long-running agent tasks. Its primary purpose is to prevent context window loss, crashes, compaction resets, and `/clear` events from destroying active task state by maintaining durable markdown planning files on disk (`task_plan.md`, `findings.md`, and `progress.md`). 

Main capabilities include automated lifecycle hooks that re-inject active-plan context every turn, SHA-256 hash attestation to prevent plan tampering, parallel task isolation via slug directories, optional gated completion checking, a run ledger, and session recovery tools. Intended users are developers employing AI coding agents across multiple platforms who require long-running task continuity and robust workflow management. 

The project notably supports over 60 agents using the Agent Skills standard alongside native plugins for platforms such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Pi Agent, Hermes Agent, OpenCode, and DeepSeek Harness. Technologies utilized include Python, PowerShell, Bash, and the Agent Skills specification.

name: MusicFree
description: 插件化、定制化、无广告的免费音乐播放器
summary:
MusicFree is a customizable, plugin-based, and ad-free free music player designed for Android and Harmony OS. The project functions strictly as a media player without built-in audio sources; instead, it relies entirely on user-installed plugins to handle searching, streaming, album and artist details, playlist imports, and lyric retrieval. 

Main capabilities include local data storage for privacy, light and dark themes with custom background support, lyric association to link and display lyrics across multiple tracks, and support for both local and network-based CommonJS plugin installations. 

The software is intended for end-users seeking a customizable, ad-free listening experience who source or create their own offline music repositories and plugins. Notable technologies and formats utilized include Android, Harmony OS, CommonJS, JavaScript (.js), and JSON.

name: SwitchHosts
description: Switch hosts quickly!
summary:
SwitchHosts is an open-source application designed for developers and system administrators to efficiently manage and switch between different hosts file configurations. Its main capabilities include managing system, local, remote, group, and folder hosts entries; quick switching from the main window or system tray; syntax highlighting; find and replace functionality; scheduled or manual remote hosts refreshing; import and export of hosts data including backups from URLs; trashcan management; and preference controls such as custom write modes, proxies, post-apply commands, and a local HTTP API. 

Built for macOS, Linux, and Windows, SwitchHosts is developed using Tauri, React, Jotai, and Mantine, with Rust utilized for backend and build requirements.

name: iTerm2-Color-Schemes
description: Our next-generation, interactive app is currently in beta!  Come try it out at terminalthemes.com! Over 600 terminal color schemes/themes for iTerm/iTerm2. Includes ports to Terminal, Konsole, PuTTY, Xresources, XRDB, Remmina, Termite, XFCE, Tilda, FreeBSD VT, Terminator, Kitty, Windows, Visual Studio,, Ghostty, and dozens more
summary:
This repository provides a comprehensive collection of color schemes originally designed for iTerm (iTerm2), along with ported configurations for a wide variety of other terminal emulators, text editors, and operating systems. 

**Project Purpose:**
The project serves as a centralized hub for cross-platform terminal and editor color themes, allowing users to apply consistent styling across different environments. It includes generator and converter scripts to automatically translate base themes into numerous target formats.

**Main Capabilities:**
- Pre-generated color themes for iTerm2, Terminal, Konsole, PuTTY, X11 (XRDB/Xresources), Terminator, XFCE Terminal, FreeBSD vt(4), MobaXterm, LXTerminal, Windows Terminal, Visual Studio Code, Alacritty, Ghostty, Otty, Rio, Termux, Vim, and Ptyxis.
- Automated generation scripts using Python and Docker to compile theme variations, check WCAG color contrast, and generate visual screenshots.
- Built-in preview tools, including an interactive terminal truecolor previewer (`preview_theme.py`) and generic OSC 4 shell scripts.
- Machine-readable JSONL and YAML exports.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, system administrators, and terminal customizers looking to sync or apply custom color palettes across diverse terminal emulators and development environments.

**Notable Technologies:**
Python, Docker, YAML, JSONL, and truecolor ANSI escape sequences.

name: shields
description: Concise, consistent, and legible badges in SVG and raster format
summary: Shields.io is a service and open-source project that generates concise, consistent, and legible badges in SVG and raster formats for GitHub readmes and web pages. It supports numerous continuous integration services, package registries, distributions, app stores, social networks, and code coverage or analysis services. The repository hosts the frontend and server code for Shields.io, an NPM library named `badge-maker` for generating badges, and the official badge design specification. Intended for developers and open-source maintainers, the project is built using Node.js, utilizes Docusaurus for frontend development, and integrates with technologies like Sentry and Prometheus for self-hosted server monitoring.

name: libuv
description: Cross-platform asynchronous I/O
summary:
libuv is a multi-platform support library focused primarily on asynchronous I/O. Its core capabilities include a full-featured event loop backed by epoll, kqueue, IOCP, and event ports, as well as asynchronous TCP and UDP sockets, DNS resolution, and file system operations. It also supports file system events, ANSI escape code controlled TTY, IPC with socket sharing via Unix domain sockets or named pipes, child processes, a thread pool, signal handling, high-resolution clocks, and threading and synchronization primitives. 

Originally developed for Node.js, libuv is additionally utilized by projects such as Luvit, Julia, and uvloop. It follows semantic versioning and maintains a stable ABI across major releases under the MIT license. Supported building methods include autotools and CMake across multiple operating systems, with specific integration options via Homebrew, vcpkg, and Conan.

name: guizang-ppt-skill
description: AI-agent Skill for generating polished HTML slide decks: editorial magazine and Swiss layouts, image prompts, social covers, and a WebGL/low-power presentation runtime.
summary:
Guizang PPT Skill is an Agent-oriented web presentation and cover-generation skill designed for environments like Claude Code and Codex. It produces single-file HTML horizontal swipe presentations, presentation assets, and multi-platform covers, complete with a built-in rehearsal and presenter mode. 

The project features two distinct visual systems: **Style A (Electronic Magazine × Electronic Ink)**, which emphasizes narrative, personal expression, and editorial storytelling across 10 layouts and 5 ink color themes, and **Style B (Swiss Internationalism)**, which prioritizes grid-based design, high-saturation anchor colors, and strict layouts across 22 locked templates and 4 anchor color palettes. 

Intended for users seeking to generate offline sharing materials, AI product demos, and keynote presentations, the tool supports AI-driven image generation (using tools like GPT-Image 2.0 and GPT-M 2.0 for infographics, charts, and UI scenarios), CleanShot X-style screenshot framing, and multi-platform covers (such as WeChat 21:9 headers and 1:1 sharing cards). 

Notable technologies and tools include HTML/CSS, WebGL (with static fallback options), Playwright-based validation scripts, and local browser-based dual-screen presenter tooling. It is delivered as a standalone plain-text codebase with built-in deck validation, layout constraints, and quality checklists.

name: grok-build
description: SpaceXAI's coding agent harness and TUI. Fullscreen, mouse interactive, extensible.
summary:
Grok Build (`grok`) is SpaceXAI's terminal-based AI coding agent. It operates as a full-screen Terminal User Interface (TUI) designed to understand codebases, edit files, execute shell commands, search the web, and manage long-running tasks. The tool functions interactively, headlessly for scripting and CI pipelines, or embedded within editors via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). 

Written in Rust, the repository contains the source code for the `grok` CLI, TUI, and agent runtime. Main capabilities are modularized across components including `xai-grok-pager` for the TUI interface, `xai-grok-shell` for the agent runtime and headless entry points, `xai-grok-tools` for utility implementations, and `xai-grok-workspace` for host filesystem, version control system (VCS), execution, and checkpointing operations. Built using Cargo, the project relies on DotSlash for managing hermetic tooling and requires Rust and `protoc`. 

Intended for developers, the project supports macOS and Linux build hosts with prebuilt binaries available. First-party code is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.

name: quasar
description: Quasar Framework - Build high-performance VueJS user interfaces in record time
summary: Quasar Framework is an enterprise-ready and AI-ready cross-platform Vue.js framework. It enables developers to build high-performance, accessible Single Page Applications (SPAs), Server-Side Rendered (SSR) apps, Static Site Generated (SSG) apps, Progressive Web Apps (PWAs), browser extensions, hybrid mobile apps, and Electron desktop applications from a single codebase. The project provides offline documentation and APIs designed for AI coding agents. Notable technologies mentioned include Vue.js, Vite, and Electron under the MIT license.

name: awesome-low-level-design
description: Learn Low Level Design (LLD) and prepare for interviews using free resources.
summary:
This repository provides comprehensive resources for learning Low-Level Design (LLD), Object-Oriented Design (OOD), and concurrency to help engineers prepare for technical interviews. The content covers OOP fundamentals, class relationships, design principles (such as SOLID, DRY, KISS, and YAGNI), design patterns (creational, structural, and behavioral), and Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagrams. It also explores concurrency and multi-threading concepts, synchronization primitives, concurrency challenges, and concurrency patterns. 

Designed for software engineers and job seekers preparing for LLD and concurrency interviews, the repository offers a curated list of practice problems categorized by difficulty—ranging from easy systems like parking lots and vending machines to medium systems like LRU caches and elevators, and hard systems like ride-sharing services and movie ticket booking platforms. Additionally, it features multi-threaded programming problems such as thread-safe caches, concurrent hash maps, and blocking queues, along with recommended reading materials, books, courses, and external resources.

name: ace
description: Ace (Ajax.org Cloud9 Editor)
summary:
Ace (Ajax.org Cloud9 Editor) is a standalone, browser-based code editor written in JavaScript. It is designed to match and extend the features, usability, and performance of native editors such as TextMate, Vim, and Eclipse, serving as the primary editor for Cloud9 IDE and the successor to the Mozilla Skywriter (Bespin) Project. 

Intended for web developers and applications requiring embedded text or code editing capabilities, Ace can be easily integrated into any web page or JavaScript application as a textarea replacement or advanced code editor. 

Main capabilities include syntax highlighting for over 120 languages, more than 20 themes, automatic indent and outdent, support for huge documents up to 4,000,000 lines, fully customizable key bindings including Vim and Emacs modes, regular expression search and replace, code folding, multiple cursors and selections, live syntax checking, and full language client support via ace-linters. 

Notable technologies utilized in the project include JavaScript, Node.js, requireJS, and the dryice build tool with uglify-js for minification.

name: the_silver_searcher
description: A code-searching tool similar to ack, but faster.
summary:
The Silver Searcher (known as `ag`) is a code-searching tool similar to `ack`, built for high performance and speed. It is designed for developers seeking a fast command-line utility to search through source code repositories. 

The project's main capabilities include searching files in parallel across multiple CPU cores, automatically ignoring file patterns specified in `.gitignore`, `.hgignore`, and custom `.ignore` files, and performing both literal string and regular expression searches. 

To achieve high performance, The Silver Searcher utilizes several notable technologies and optimization techniques:
- POSIX Threads (Pthreads) for multi-core parallel searching
- `mmap()` instead of standard buffer reading
- Boyer-Moore string search algorithm for literal strings
- PCRE's JIT compiler and `pcre_study()` for regular expressions
- Pre-loaded, binary-searched arrays for non-regex ignore patterns rather than repeated `fnmatch()` calls

The tool integrates with text editors and environments such as Vim, Emacs, and TextMate.

name: tree-sitter
description: An incremental parsing system for programming tools
summary: Tree-sitter is a parser generator tool and incremental parsing library designed to build concrete syntax trees for source files and efficiently update them as files are edited. It aims to be general enough to parse any programming language, fast enough to parse on every keystroke within a text editor, robust enough to yield useful results despite syntax errors, and entirely dependency-free. Its pure C runtime library can be embedded into any application. The project provides bindings for Rust and WebAssembly (Wasm), alongside a command-line interface.

name: GDevelop
description: 🎮 Open-source, cross-platform 2D/3D/multiplayer game engine designed for everyone.
summary:
GDevelop is a full-featured, no-code, open-source game development software designed to build 2D, 3D, and multiplayer games for mobile, desktop, and the web. Intended for creators, developers, and teams of all skill levels, it allows users to make games using an event-based system, modular behaviors, and AI-assisted tools. 

The technical architecture comprises:
- `newIDE`: The game editor built with JavaScript, React, Electron, PixiJS, and Three.js.
- `GDJS`: The TypeScript game engine utilizing PixiJS and Three.js for 2D and 3D WebGL rendering.
- `Core`: C++ core classes defining game structure and IDE tooling.
- `GDevelop.js`: Bindings of `Core`, `GDJS`, and extensions to JavaScript with WebAssembly for IDE usage.
- `Extensions`: Built-in features, objects, behaviors, and WebAssembly-powered physics engines including Box2D and Jolt Physics.

name: react-virtualized
description: React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data
summary: React Virtualized is a library providing React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data through virtualization. Its main capabilities include performance optimization for extensive datasets via components like `List`, `Table`, `Grid`, `Masonry`, `Collection`, `InfiniteLoader`, and `AutoSizer`. The project is intended for web developers building performant React applications that handle substantial amounts of data or large collections. Notable technologies utilized include React, ReactDOM, ES6, CommonJS, UMD, Webpack, and CSS.

name: SteamTools
description: 🛠「Watt Toolkit」是一个开源跨平台的多功能 Steam 工具箱。
summary:
Watt Toolkit (formerly Steam++) is an open-source, cross-platform utility toolbox designed primarily to enhance the Steam gaming experience. Its core capabilities include network acceleration via local reverse proxies (using YARP.ReverseProxy) to speed up game website access and inject JS scripts, multi-platform account switching for services like Steam, Epic, and Uplay, and comprehensive Steam game inventory management (custom covers, playtime simulation, cloud save management, and achievement unlocking). Additionally, it provides a local authenticator supporting HOTP, TOTP, Steam, and Google tokens with batch trade confirmation, alongside game window utilities. 

The project is intended for PC and mobile gamers utilizing platforms such as Steam. It is built using .NET 7.0 and C# 11, supporting Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android operating systems, with development environments utilizing tools such as Visual Studio, JetBrains Rider, and VS Code.

name: vimium
description: The hacker's browser.
summary:
Vimium is a browser extension designed to provide keyboard-based navigation and control of the web in the spirit of the Vim editor. It is intended for users seeking efficient, mouse-free web browsing across supported browsers including Chrome, Edge, and Firefox. 

Main capabilities include page scrolling, opening and manipulating links and tabs, searching page content using find mode, navigating browser history, utilizing local and global marks, and executing advanced browsing commands such as focusing text input boxes and managing URL hierarchies. Vimium also supports command repetition, visual modes, and extensive custom key mappings via its options page, allowing users to remap or unmap default key bindings and add comments. An optional companion Vimium New Tab Page extension is available to enable functionality on all browser-opened new tab pages.

name: angular-cli
description: CLI tool for Angular
summary:
Angular CLI is a command-line interface tool designed to initialize, develop, scaffold, and maintain Angular applications directly from a command shell. It functions as a monorepo containing various packages and tools supporting the Angular ecosystem. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Workspace and project creation, configuration, and file structure management via commands like `ng new` and `ng serve`.
- Application building and bundling using the Angular Build System (`@angular/build`), Webpack (`@ngtools/webpack`, `@angular-devkit/build-webpack`), and specialized build tools (`@angular-devkit/build-angular`).
- Code generation and scaffolding using Schematics (`@angular-devkit/schematics`, `@schematics/angular`, `@angular/pwa`).
- Task execution and orchestration via Architect (`@angular-devkit/architect`).
- Server-side rendering support through Angular SSR (`@angular/ssr`).

**Intended Users:**
Web developers and software engineers building, maintaining, and scaling applications with the Angular framework.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Node.js and Node Package Manager (npm)
- Angular
- Webpack

name: cmder
description: Lovely console emulator package for Windows
summary:
Cmder is a portable software package and console emulator for Windows created to provide a usable and eye-pleasing terminal experience. Designed as a self-contained environment with no external dependencies, it is ideal for use on USB sticks or cloud storage. 

The project's main capabilities include running multiple shells within a single window using tabs—such as `cmd.exe`, PowerShell, and Bash—alongside custom prompt layouts, Monokai color schemes, alias management, and tab manipulation shortcuts. It features built-in support for context menu integration and directory tracking/shell integration with Windows Terminal. 

Cmder is intended for Windows users seeking a robust, customizable command-line environment with portable configurations. It is built on top of ConEmu and incorporates technologies such as Clink, clink-completions, a Monokai color scheme, and a vendored Git-for-Windows installation.

name: rethinkdb
description: The open-source database for the realtime web.
summary:
RethinkDB is an open-source, distributed NoSQL database designed for building realtime web applications. It stores schemaless JSON documents and offers high availability with automatic failover and fault tolerance. Its primary capability enables developers to instruct the database to continuously push updated query results directly to applications via changefeeds, eliminating the need for polling. 

Intended for developers building scalable realtime applications such as liveblogs, collaborative tools, and chat bots, RethinkDB features official drivers for JavaScript, Python, Ruby, and Java, alongside a wide ecosystem of community-supported third-party drivers for languages including C#, C++, Clojure, Elixir, Go, Haskell, PHP, Rust, and Scala. 

The project exposes the ReQL API for database queries and management. Built using technologies such as C++ (GCC or Clang), Protocol Buffers, jemalloc, and OpenSSL, the repository provides build instructions for Linux, FreeBSD, and Windows environments. RethinkDB is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license by the Linux Foundation.

name: developer-portfolios
description: A list of developer portfolios for your inspiration
summary: This repository provides a curated, alphabetical directory of developer portfolios intended to serve as inspiration for software engineers, full-stack developers, AI/ML engineers, mobile developers, and UI/UX designers looking to build or showcase their personal websites. Inspired by a widely shared developer community prompt, the collection spans thousands of entries categorized alphabetically from A to Z. Each entry links to an individual's personal portfolio website and typically highlights their specific technical focus, professional roles, or domains of expertise—ranging from frontend engineering, backend architecture, and DevOps to artificial intelligence, data science, and web3 technologies. The repository functions as an open-source resource where developers can discover diverse portfolio designs, layout concepts, and implementation styles by submitting pull requests via its contribution guidelines.

name: react-admin
description: A frontend Framework for single-page applications on top of REST/GraphQL APIs, using TypeScript, React and Material Design
summary:
react-admin is a frontend framework for building single-page applications running in the browser on top of REST or GraphQL APIs. Designed for frontend developers and engineers, it enables the creation of administrative interfaces, e-commerce apps, CRMs, and helpdesk tools. 

The framework is backend agnostic, connecting to any API via data provider adapters, and provides a comprehensive suite of building blocks including authentication, routing, forms and validation, datagrids, search and filters, roles and permissions, internationalization (i18n), and theming. Notable features include optimistic rendering, undo capabilities, saved queries, and complete component customization. 

Built using TypeScript, React, Material Design (Material UI), react-hook-form, react-router, and react-query, react-admin supports optional TypeScript usage, offers modular architecture, and supplies complete documentation alongside multiple example applications.

name: hashcat
description: World's fastest and most advanced password recovery utility
summary:
Hashcat is a free and open-source password recovery platform designed for GPUs, CPUs, and large distributed systems. Aimed at security professionals and researchers, it functions as a password cracker supporting over 590 hash modes and 10 attack modes, including wordlist, combination, brute-force, PCFG, table, hybrid, mask, generic plugin feeds, and association. 

Core capabilities include an in-kernel rule engine, a Brain feature to skip previously tried candidates, an assimilation bridge for adding hash modes in C, Python, or Rust, distributed cracking networks, automatic performance tuning, an integrated thermal watchdog, and encrypted plains support. It reads candidates from wordlists, stdin, or external programs, and utilizes Markov chain keyspace ordering. 

Hashcat operates across Linux, Windows, and macOS, utilizing backends such as CUDA, HIP, Metal, and OpenCL. Distributed under the MIT license, it supports multi-device and mixed-device systems, multi-hash cracking, interactive pause and resume, session restoration, built-in benchmarking, and keyboard layout mapping.

name: lottie-ios
description: An iOS library to natively render After Effects vector animations
summary:
Lottie for iOS is a cross-platform animation library targeting iOS, macOS, tvOS, and visionOS that natively renders vector-based animations and art in realtime with minimal code. The project is designed for developers and designers to load and render lightweight animations exported in the bodymovin JSON format from tools such as After Effects, Sketch, and Haiku. 

Main capabilities include playing, resizing, looping, speeding up, slowing down, reversing, and interactively scrubbing animations, as well as modifying keyframable values like colors and positions at runtime. 

Intended users are software engineers and UI/UX designers looking to ship complex animations without manual recreation. The library supports installation via Swift Package Manager, CocoaPods, and Carthage, and includes tools for automated formatting, unit testing, and snapshot validation using SwiftFormat and SwiftLint.

name: driver.js
description: A lightweight, dependency-free JavaScript library for guiding user focus across the page.
summary: Driver.js is a lightweight, zero-dependency, and highly customizable Vanilla TypeScript library designed to create product tours, feature introductions, page overlays, and focus shifters for web applications. Weighing around 5kb gzipped, it allows developers to highlight any element on a page, provide contextual help, display modals, and control interactions via keyboard across all major browsers. The project includes a powerful API and hooks for manipulating elements during highlighting, and features an Astro-based playground for local development. It is available under the MIT license.

name: onlook
description: The Developer Tool for Designers • An Open-Source AI-First Design tool • Visually build, style, and edit your code with AI • World's best, top-most agent recommended #1 Developer tool for Designers to design with Real Code.
summary:
Onlook is an open-source visual-first code editor and design tool built for AI-native designers and developers, specifically optimized for Next.js and TailwindCSS projects. It bridges the gap between design and code by enabling users to craft websites and prototypes through a browser DOM visual editor alongside real-time code editing and AI assistance. 

Key capabilities include visual Figma-like UI tools, real-time code-to-design preview, layer browsing, brand asset management, checkpoint restoration, and integrated AI chat for generating and modifying projects. The architecture loads code into a web container, serves a preview via iFrame, maps DOM elements to their exact source code locations, and supports tool calls for design iteration.

Intended users include frontend developers, full-stack engineers, and UI/UX designers looking to build and iterate on web applications visually and programmatically. 

Notable technologies used in the project stack include Next.js, TailwindCSS, tRPC, Supabase, Drizzle ORM, AI SDK, OpenRouter, CodeSandbox SDK, Freestyle, Bun, and Docker.

name: apollo
description: An open autonomous driving platform
summary:
Apollo is a high-performance, flexible open-source architecture designed to accelerate the development, testing, deployment, and commercialization of autonomous vehicles. It provides a comprehensive software framework and development cycle for autonomous driving developers, encompassing modules such as CyberRT, Localization, Perception, Prediction, Planning, Decider, and Control. 

The project targets autonomous vehicle developers, researchers, and partners working on self-driving technology. Key capabilities range from basic waypoint following (Apollo 1.0) and fixed-lane cruising with LiDAR (Apollo 1.5) to complex urban road navigation, 360-degree visibility, scenario-based planning, deep learning model integration, package management, and large-scale deployment toolchains like Dreamview Plus. 

Apollo integrates with hardware including by-wire equipped vehicles (tested on the Lincoln MKZ), minimum 8-core processors, 16GB memory, and GPUs utilizing CUDA (version 11.8+) or ROCm. It relies on technologies such as Docker, Ubuntu (18.04, 20.04, 22.04), LibTorch, and NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Distributed under the Apache-2.0 license, Apollo offers modular components, extension methods via plugins and packages, simulation tools, and model training services to support scalable autonomous driving applications.

name: hangzhou_house_knowledge
description: 2017年买房经历总结出来的买房购房知识分享给大家，希望对大家有所帮助。买房不易，且买且珍惜。Sharing the knowledge of buy an own house that according  to the experience at hangzhou in 2017 to all the people. It's not easy to buy a own house, so I hope that it would be useful to everyone.
summary:
杭州房产知识扫盲是一个旨在为购房者提供杭州房地产市场全方位参考与指导的综合性资料库。该项目汇集了杭州各行政区与板块划分、核心地段定位、地铁及交通规划、拆迁计划、土拍信息、学区划分以及商业综合体与医疗等配套设施分析。

项目主要内容涵盖：
- **板块与规划**：详细介绍主城区、各城市副中心及17个重点发展增长极的定位（如钱江新城、钱江世纪城、未来科技城等），并收录了大量官方控规文件与轨道交通远期规划。
- **购房核心概念**：系统科普土地性质、容积率、公摊面积、购房定金与诚意金区别、东边套与西边套优劣势等买房必备常识。
- **政策与市场数据**：整理了人才居住证办理指南、购房资格与首付要求、住宅用地供应中期规划及历年土地成交档案。
- **信息渠道汇总**：精选了官方网站、透明售房网等专业工具以及多维房产自媒体公众号和论坛。

本项目旨在帮助购房者、投资者及研究人员全面了解杭州城市建设与楼市动态，防范买房风险，适合所有关注杭州房产与城市规划的人士作为入门到深入求证的参考指南。

name: JCSprout
description: 👨‍🎓 Java Core Sprout : basic, concurrent, algorithm
summary: JCSprout (Java Core Sprout) is a Java core knowledge repository designed to help developers master fundamental and advanced backend engineering concepts. Its main capabilities encompass in-depth explanations, source code analysis, and practical guides covering Java collections, multi-threading, JVM internals, distributed systems, system architecture design, databases, data structures and algorithms, Netty, and networking protocols. The project targets Java developers and software engineers seeking to strengthen their technical foundation, prepare for technical interviews, and understand production troubleshooting and high-concurrency architecture practices. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced include Spring, Spring Boot, Spring AOP, Redis, Kafka, Guava, Netty, MySQL, and TCP/IP.

name: discord.js
description: A powerful JavaScript library for interacting with the Discord API
summary:
discord.js is a powerful Node.js module and multi-package repository designed to easily interact with the Discord API. 

The project provides comprehensive tools for developers building Discord applications, including the primary `discord.js` wrapper, `create-discord-bot` for scaffolding projects, and several specialized packages: `@discordjs/builders` for constructing API payloads, `@discordjs/rest` and `@discordjs/core` for REST API interactions, `@discordjs/ws` for gateway management, `@discordjs/voice` for the Discord Voice API, alongside utility packages like `@discordjs/collection`, `@discordjs/formatters`, `@discordjs/brokers`, `@discordjs/proxy`, `@discordjs/rpc`, `@discordjs/structures`, and `@discordjs/util`.

name: legacy-homebrew
description: 💀 The former home of Homebrew/homebrew (deprecated)
summary: Homebrew (Legacy) is a deprecated repository that has been split into two separate repositories: Homebrew/homebrew-core, which contains the Homebrew formulae and packages (formerly located in `Library/Formula`), and Homebrew/brew, which houses the Homebrew package manager itself.

name: gitflow
description: Git extensions to provide high-level repository operations for Vincent Driessen's branching model.
summary:
git-flow is a collection of Git extensions that provide high-level repository operations for Vincent Driessen's branching model. This repository is no longer maintained and has been succeeded by git-flow-next. 

The project's main capabilities include managing the complete lifecycle of feature, release, hotfix, and support branches through subcommands. Intended users are software developers and teams utilizing Git for version control who want structured management for development, production, and release branches. Notable technologies and tools associated with the project include Git, Bash, and ZSH (via community shell completion integrations).

name: DeepSpeech
description: DeepSpeech is an open source embedded (offline, on-device) speech-to-text engine which can run in real time on devices ranging from a Raspberry Pi 4 to high power GPU servers.
summary: Project DeepSpeech is a discontinued open-source Speech-To-Text engine that implements a model trained by machine learning techniques based on Baidu's Deep Speech research paper. The project utilizes Google's TensorFlow to facilitate implementation. It provides capabilities for speech recognition, with documentation, installation guides, usage instructions, training models, pre-trained models, and checkpoints available for users.

name: openapi-generator
description: OpenAPI Generator allows generation of API client libraries (SDK generation), server stubs, documentation and configuration automatically given an OpenAPI Spec (v2, v3)
summary:
OpenAPI Generator is an open-source tool that automatically generates API client libraries (SDK generation), server stubs, documentation, and configuration files from a given OpenAPI Specification (supporting versions 1.0 through 3.1). 

The project supports a vast array of programming languages and frameworks for API clients (such as Java, TypeScript, Python, Go, C#, PHP, Ruby, Rust, and Swift) and server stubs (including Spring Boot, ASP.NET Core, FastAPI, Express, and Gin), alongside various documentation formats like HTML, Markdown, and AsciiDoc. 

Intended for developers and organizations implementing API-first design and workflow integration, OpenAPI Generator helps streamline software development and maintain consistency across distributed systems. It can be utilized via command-line interface (CLI), Docker images, Maven and Gradle plugins, NPM, or pip, and integrates with CI/CD pipelines and popular IDEs. The project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 License.

name: pm-skills
description: PM Skills Marketplace: 100+ agentic skills, commands, and plugins — from discovery to strategy, execution, launch, and growth.
summary:
The PM Skills Marketplace is an AI operating system and plugin repository designed for product managers, founders, and teams using AI assistants such as Claude Code, Cowork, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, and Kiro. It provides 69 structured PM skills and 42 chained workflows across 9 plugins covering product discovery, strategy, execution, market research, data analytics, go-to-market, marketing/growth, toolkits, and AI shipping. 

The project embeds proven product frameworks from industry practitioners such as Teresa Torres, Marty Cagan, Alberto Savoia, and Ash Maurya into daily workflows. Skills offer domain knowledge and analytical frameworks, while slash commands chain these skills into end-to-end processes like discovery cycles, roadmap transformations, PRD writing, sprint planning, and AI codebase audits. Notable technologies and formats include markdown-based universal skill structures, SQL generation (BigQuery, PostgreSQL, MySQL), and static security and performance auditing for AI-built codebases.

name: clash-party
description: :electron: Another Mihomo GUI.
summary:
Clash Party is a graphical user interface (GUI) for Mihomo (Clash Meta). It is designed to provide an out-of-the-box user experience without requiring the Tun service mode. 

Key capabilities include one-click Smart Core rule overriding for AI-driven optimal node selection, built-in Smart and Mihomo (Clash Meta) kernels, support for modifying most common Mihomo configurations, multiple color themes, WebDAV-based configuration backup and restoration, advanced configuration overriding, and deep integration with Sub-Store for subscription management.

name: elixir
description: Simple from zero to scale
summary: Elixir is a programming language designed for building scalable and maintainable applications. Intended for developers and contributors building software within the Elixir ecosystem, the project relies on Erlang. The repository contains the source code, build utilities via `make`, and instructions for compiling from source, testing, reporting bugs, and proposing new features through the Elixir Core mailing list. The software is released under the Apache License 2.0.

name: gopeed
description: A fast, modern download manager for HTTP, BitTorrent, Magnet, and ed2k. Cross-platform, built with Golang and Flutter.
summary:
Gopeed (Go Speed) is a fast, open-source, and cross-platform download manager built with Go and Flutter. It is designed for general users and developers seeking a lightweight, high-performance solution across desktop, mobile, web, and self-hosted environments. 

The project supports concurrent multi-connection HTTP and HTTPS transfers, BitTorrent, magnet links, and ed2k resources. Capabilities include full-featured BitTorrent management (DHT, uTP, Web Seeds, selective file downloads, tracker tracking, and seeding limits), flexible task handling, and a native UI without Electron or WebView shells. It provides browser extensions, JavaScript extensions for custom download sources, automated scripts, webhooks, and a REST API and CLI. Additionally, Gopeed features an AI integration via an MCP endpoint enabling natural language task management. 

Technologies utilized include Go for the backend core, Flutter for the native front end, and Docker and QNAP for containerized or network-attached deployments.

name: chatterbox
description: SoTA open-source TTS
summary:
Chatterbox TTS is a family of open-source text-to-speech and voice cloning models developed by Resemble AI. Designed for developers, researchers, and creators building voice agents, localization workflows, and interactive media, the repository offers multiple model variants optimized for specific performance and deployment needs. 

The lineup includes **Chatterbox Multilingual V3**, a 0.5B general-purpose model supporting 23+ languages with improved speaker similarity and reduced hallucinations, alongside dedicated Single Language Packs for specialized regional dialects. For low-latency English voice agents, **Chatterbox-Turbo** utilizes a 350M parameter architecture and a streamlined single-step decoder with native paralinguistic tags like `[laugh]` and `[chuckle]`. For resource-constrained and on-device environments, **Chatterbox-Nano** provides a 110M parameter version capable of efficient CPU inference. 

Technologies utilized include PyTorch, Torchaudio, and Resemble AI's Perth Perceptual Threshold Watermarker for embedded audio watermarking.

name: nodemon
description: Monitor for any changes in your node.js application and automatically restart the server - perfect for development
summary:
Nodemon is a development tool for Node.js applications that automatically restarts a node process when file changes are detected in a directory. It serves as a replacement wrapper for `node`, requiring no additional changes to underlying application code. 

Intended for software developers and engineers working with Node.js and other script-based environments, nodemon monitors file modifications, supports custom executable mappings for non-node scripts (such as Python or Perl), and manages multiple watched directories, file extension watch lists, and ignore patterns. Notable capabilities include manual restarting via the command line, configuration via local or global `nodemon.json` files or `package.json`, delayed restarts, signal handling for graceful shutdowns, and event-driven automation. Technologies utilized include Node.js, Chokidar, and picomatch for file system monitoring and globbing. It is distributed under the MIT license.

name: haystack
description: Open-source AI orchestration framework for building context-engineered, production-ready LLM applications. Design modular pipelines and agent workflows with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory, and generation. Built for scalable agents, RAG, multimodal applications, semantic search, and conversational systems.
summary:
Haystack is an open-source AI orchestration framework designed for building production-ready Large Language Model (LLM) applications in Python. It enables developers to design modular pipelines and autonomous agent workflows with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory, and generation. 

Main capabilities include building scalable Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, multimodal applications, semantic search, question-answering systems, and production-ready agents equipped with lifecycle hooks, token tracking, and progressive skill discovery. It provides native asynchronous support, conditional routing, branching, loops, and a model-agnostic architecture compatible with major AI providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Mistral, Google, Hugging Face, AWS Bedrock, and Azure OpenAI, as well as local models. 

Intended users include developers, data scientists, and organizations across industries—such as technology, enterprise, public sector, and content platforms—seeking to build, customize, and deploy scalable AI systems. Notable technologies and tools integrated within the ecosystem include Hayhooks for exposing pipelines via REST APIs or MCP servers, Docker, and Python.

name: Unlimited-OCR
description: Unlimited OCR Works: Welcome the Era of One-shot Long-horizon Parsing.
summary:
Unlimited-OCR is an advanced optical character recognition and document parsing model designed for one-shot long-horizon parsing and multi-page document understanding. Built to push the boundaries of document analysis, the project supports both single-image parsing (with configurable "gundam" and "base" modes) and multi-page or PDF document analysis. 

The repository provides extensive support for running inference via multiple deployment frameworks, including Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang. It includes capabilities for batch processing, customized text generation with repeat-ngram handling, PDF-to-image conversion tools utilizing PyMuPDF, and post-processing utilities for evaluation benchmarks such as OmniDocBench. It is intended for researchers, developers, and practitioners working in computer vision, document intelligence, and optical character recognition. Notable technologies utilized include PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face, Docker, and Python.

name: PLFM_RADAR
description: Open-source, low-cost 10.5 GHz PLFM phased array RADAR system
summary:
AERIS-10 is an open-source, low-cost 10.5 GHz Pulse Linear Frequency Modulated (LFM) phased array radar system designed for researchers, drone developers, and software-defined radio (SDR) enthusiasts. It is available in two variants: the AERIS-10N (Nexus) offering a 3 km range with an 8x16 patch antenna array, and the AERIS-10E (Extended) providing a 20 km range with a 32x16 dielectric-filled slotted waveguide array. Both versions feature ±45° electronic beam steering in elevation and azimuth alongside 360° mechanical scanning.

The system relies on a modular architecture comprising a power management board, a frequency synthesizer board using an AD9523-1 clock generator, an STM32F746xx microcontroller for system management and sequencing, and an XC7A50T FPGA handling real-time digital signal processing such as pulse compression, Doppler FFT, Moving Target Indication (MTI), and Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detection. RF operations utilize LTC5552 microwave mixers, ADAR1000 phase shifters, and ADTR1107 front-end chips, with QPA2962 GaN amplifiers on the extended version. The platform integrates a GPS module, IMU, barometer, and a Python-based graphical user interface with map integration. Hardware files are distributed under the CERN-OHL-P license, while software and firmware use the MIT license.

name: dashy
description: 🚀 A self-hostable personal dashboard built for you. Includes status-checking, widgets, themes, icon packs, a UI editor and tons more!
summary:
Dashy is a customizable dashboard and homepage designed for self-hosters and homelabs. It serves as an application launcher and system monitoring hub, intended for self-hosters, home cloud users, and individuals managing personal servers.

Main capabilities include multi-page support, real-time HTTP app status and ICMP ping monitoring, dynamic widgets, instant search with hotkeys, UI-based theme and configuration editors, multi-language support, E2E-encrypted cloud backup and sync, and alternative view modes like workspaces and a browser startpage. It supports multiple application launching methods, authentication options including Keycloak and basic auth, and single-file YAML configuration.

Notable technologies used include Docker, Node.js, Yarn, Vue.js, Keycloak, and Cloudflare Workers with KV storage.

name: 12-factor-agents
description: What are the principles we can use to build LLM-powered software that is actually good enough to put in the hands of production customers?
summary:
12-Factor Agents is a methodology and guide for building reliable, production-grade LLM applications and AI agents. It addresses the limitations of monolithic AI frameworks by advocating for modular, software-driven design patterns. 

The project outlines twelve core principles—ranging from natural language tool calls and prompt/context ownership to structured outputs, stateless reducers, and human-in-the-loop tool integrations—designed to help developers construct scalable, maintainable LLM software. Intended for software engineers and technical founders aiming to deploy robust AI features to production customers, the project provides architectural concepts applicable across programming languages like TypeScript and Python.

name: fastText
description: Library for fast text representation and classification.
summary:
fastText is an open-source library designed for the efficient learning of word representations and text classification. The project's main capabilities include training word vectors using subword information (such as character n-grams), computing representations for out-of-vocabulary words, performing supervised text classification tasks like sentiment analysis, generating sentence and paragraph vectors, and model quantization to reduce memory usage. 

Intended for developers, researchers, and data scientists working with natural language processing, fastText provides a command-line interface as well as Python bindings. The codebase is implemented in C++ and utilizes C++11 features. Building the library requires a compatible compiler supporting C++11 alongside standard build automation tools like GNU Make or CMake. Python integration additionally relies on NumPy, SciPy, and pybind11.

name: darknet
description: Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Darknet is an open-source neural network framework written in C and CUDA, designed to be fast, easy to install, and supportive of both CPU and GPU computation. It serves as a foundational platform for state-of-the-art real-time object detection models, specifically hosting implementations, resources, and citations for YOLOv4, Scaled-YOLOv4, and YOLOv7. The repository provides research papers, wikis, and integrations targeting computer vision developers and researchers seeking high-speed and high-accuracy object detection capabilities on datasets like MS COCO. Notable technologies associated with the project include C, CUDA, PyTorch, OpenCV, and TensorRT.

name: MiniCPM-V
description: A Pocket-Sized MLLM for Ultra-Efficient Image and Video Understanding on Your Phone
summary:
MiniCPM-V and MiniCPM-o are pocket-sized multimodal large language model (MLLM) series built for ultra-efficient image, video, speech, and omnimodal understanding on mobile and edge devices. 

**Project Purpose:**
The project delivers compact, high-performance foundation models optimized for deployment across smartphones, local computers, and consumer hardware, providing capabilities comparable to much larger proprietary models while minimizing computation and latency.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **MiniCPM-V 4.6:** Efficient vision-language understanding across single images, multiple images, and video. Powered by the intra-ViT early compression technique from LLaVA-UHD v4, it cuts visual encoding computation by over 50% and supports mixed 4x/16x visual token compression.
- **MiniCPM-o 4.5:** End-to-end omnimodal interaction featuring full-duplex multimodal live streaming, concurrent streaming video/audio input with text/speech output, proactive interaction (e.g., proactive reminders), zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS), voice cloning, role play, and robust document OCR parsing.

**Intended Users:**
Designed for individual developers seeking local AI inference and quantized edge-device demos, enterprises requiring scalable production-grade server deployments, and researchers focusing on multimodal fine-tuning and model adaptation.

**Notable Technologies:**
Built using architectures such as SigLIP2, Qwen3.5, Qwen3-8B, Whisper, and CosyVoice2. Supported across inference frameworks including vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, FlagOS, and Hugging Face Transformers, alongside training ecosystems like LLaMA-Factory and SWIFT.

name: focalboard
description: Focalboard is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Trello, Notion, and Asana.
summary:
Focalboard is an open-source, multilingual, and self-hosted project management tool designed as an alternative to Trello, Notion, and Asana. It helps individuals and teams define, organize, track, and manage work. 

The project is available in two main editions:
- **Personal Desktop**: A standalone, single-user desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
- **Personal Server**: A standalone, multi-user server for development and personal use, utilizing SQLite.

Intended users include developers, individuals, and teams seeking self-hosted task and project tracking solutions. Notable technologies and tools referenced in the repository include Docker, SQLite, Make, npm, ESLint, Cypress, and platform-specific UI frameworks such as Windows WPF and WebKitGTK for Linux.

name: cool-retro-term
description: A good looking terminal emulator which mimics the old cathode display...
summary: cool-retro-term is a customizable, lightweight terminal emulator designed to mimic the look and feel of old cathode ray tube (CRT) screens for visual appeal. Its main capabilities include adjustable colors, fonts, and visual effects accessible through a context menu. The project is intended for users seeking a retro aesthetic on Linux and macOS. Built using Qt6, it utilizes the QML port of qtermwidget (Konsole).

name: deep-learning-for-image-processing
description: deep learning for image processing including classification and object-detection etc.
summary:
This repository provides a video-based tutorial series on applying deep learning to image processing, intended for students and learners in the field. The course covers network architectures, innovation points, and model implementation for training using PyTorch and TensorFlow (Keras). 

The tutorial topics span multiple computer vision domains, including:
- **Image Classification:** LeNet, AlexNet, VggNet, GoogLeNet, ResNet, ResNeXt, MobileNet (V1–V3), ShuffleNet (V1–V2), EfficientNet (V1–V2), RepVGG, Vision Transformer, Swin Transformer, ConvNeXt, and MobileViT.
- **Object Detection:** Faster-RCNN/FPN, SSD, RetinaNet, YOLO Series (V1–V5, YOLOX), and FCOS.
- **Semantic Segmentation:** FCN, DeepLabV3, LR-ASPP, U-Net, and U2Net.
- **Instance Segmentation:** Mask R-CNN.
- **Keypoint Detection:** DeepPose and HRNet.

Additionally, presentation slides for the lessons are provided within the `course_ppt` folder.

name: UniGetUI
description: UniGetUI: The Graphical Interface for your package managers. Could be terribly described as a package manager manager to manage your package managers
summary:
UniGetUI is a graphical user interface (GUI) designed to manage command-line package managers across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Created by Martí Climent and maintained by Devolutions, the open-source project allows users to discover, install, update, and uninstall software from multiple package sources through a single interface. 

Supported package managers include WinGet, Scoop, Chocolatey, Homebrew, APT, DNF, Pacman, Flatpak, Snap, pip, npm, Bun, .NET Tool, PowerShell Gallery, Cargo, and vcpkg. Its capabilities include bulk installation and removal, automated update checks and background maintenance, package metadata viewing, exportable/importable software lists, local and cloud backups via GitHub Gist, a system tray integration, command-line control, and a local automation API. 

The application is targeted at users seeking a unified management layer for command-line tools. Releases are compiled using NativeAOT across supported platforms, with packages distributed via the Microsoft Store, GitHub Releases, and native package managers.

name: nprogress
description: For slim progress bars like on YouTube, Medium, etc
summary:
NProgress is a minimalist progress bar library designed for slim, realistic loading indicators in Ajax-heavy applications, inspired by interfaces from Google, YouTube, and Medium. 

Main capabilities include starting, completing, incrementing, and setting specific progress percentages, alongside a force-done method and status retrieval. It supports integrations with Turbolinks and Pjax, and offers extensive configuration options such as minimum starting percentages, custom templates, easing strings, animation speed, trickling behavior, loading spinners, and custom parent containers. 

The project is intended for web developers looking to add subtle loading feedback to their applications. Technologies utilized include JavaScript, CSS, npm, Bower, and unpkg CDN.

name: Detectron
description: FAIR's research platform for object detection research, implementing popular algorithms like Mask R-CNN and RetinaNet.
summary:
Detectron is Facebook AI Research's software system designed to provide a high-performance, flexible codebase for object detection research. Intended for researchers and developers in computer vision, the platform enables the rapid implementation and evaluation of novel object detection algorithms. 

The software implements state-of-the-art object detection algorithms—including Mask R-CNN, RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, RPN, Fast R-CNN, and R-FCN—alongside backbone network architectures such as ResNet, ResNeXt, Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN), and VGG16. 

Written in Python and powered by the Caffe2 deep learning framework, Detectron also supports advanced capabilities like Group Normalization and includes a Model Zoo providing pre-trained baseline models.

name: Open-AutoGLM
description: An Open Phone Agent Model & Framework. Unlocking the AI Phone for Everyone
summary:
Open-AutoGLM is a phone assistant framework built on the AutoGLM models (`AutoGLM-Phone-9B` and `AutoGLM-Phone-9B-Multilingual`) designed to understand mobile screens via multimodal vision-language models and automate tasks using natural language instructions. 

**Purpose & Capabilities:**
- Translates natural language descriptions (e.g., "open Meituan and search for hot pot") into automated device actions such as launching apps, tapping, typing, swiping, and navigating.
- Supports sensitive operation confirmation mechanisms, manual takeover during login or verification codes, and remote debugging over WiFi or network.
- Compatible with over 50 mainstream Chinese Android applications and 60+ HarmonyOS NEXT applications.
- Integrated with Midscene.js for multi-platform UI automation.

**Intended Users:**
- Developers, researchers, and end-users looking to deploy AI-driven mobile GUI agents for testing, task automation, and hands-free interaction.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Vision Language Models (AutoGLM-Phone-9B series)
- ADB (Android Debug Bridge) for Android control
- HDC (Harmony Device Controller) for HarmonyOS control
- Inference frameworks: vLLM and SGLang
- Python, PyTorch

name: sst
description: Build full-stack apps on your own infrastructure.
summary: SST is an open-source framework designed to help developers build full-stack applications on their own infrastructure. It supports popular web frameworks and architectures, including Next.js, Remix, Astro, and APIs. Key concepts and capabilities include Live development, resource Linking, a Console, and reusable Components. The project supports JavaScript ecosystems via npm, pnpm, bun, and yarn, as well as global CLI installation methods. Local development and building of the CLI require Go and Bun.

name: baoyu-skills
summary:
baoyu-skills is a collection of over 20 productivity and content generation skills designed for AI agents like Claude Code and Codex to improve daily work efficiency. The project provides modular tools categorized into Content Skills, AI Generation Skills, and Utility Skills.

Main capabilities include generating Xiaohongshu image cards, infographics, SVG diagrams, article cover images, slide decks, knowledge comics, and article illustrations, alongside publishing tools for platforms like WeChat Official Accounts, X (Twitter), and Weibo. It also features AI image generation integrations supporting OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, DashScope, Z.AI, MiniMax, Replicate, Jimeng, and Seedream, as well as utility functions for downloading YouTube transcripts, converting URLs or X threads to markdown, translating documents, summarizing WeChat group chats, and extracting Electron app resources.

Intended users are developers, content creators, and professionals using AI coding agents who want to automate multi-step publishing and creative generation workflows. Notable technologies utilized include Node.js, Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), and various third-party AI image and language models.

name: fonts
description: Patched fonts for Powerline users.
summary:
Powerline fonts is a repository providing pre-patched and adjusted fonts for use with the Powerline statusline plugin. Its main capability is supplying a wide variety of modified font families—such as 3270, Anonymice Powerline, Arimo Powerline, Cousine Powerline, Droid Sans Mono for Powerline, Fira Mono for Powerline, Hack, Inconsolata for Powerline, Meslo for Powerline, Source Code Pro for Powerline, Terminess Powerline, and Ubuntu Mono derivative Powerline—equipped with the glyphs required by Powerline. 

The project is intended for users of terminal emulators, text editors, and shell environments who utilize the Powerline plugin, including specific configuration guidance for iTerm2 users and fontconfig adjustments for Linux distributions. Installation is supported via shell scripts (`install.sh` and `uninstall.sh`) and native package managers on Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, and Red Hat-based Linux distributions using commands like `apt-get` and `dnf`.

name: awesome-swift
description: A collaborative list of awesome Swift libraries and resources. Feel free to contribute!
summary:
Awesome Swift is a curated list of Swift-related frameworks, libraries, tools, guides, and learning resources. The project functions as an extensive directory covering various categories of Swift development, including user interface components, networking, data management, dependency managers, automated testing tools, architecture patterns, and server-side utilities. 

Its primary purpose is to help Swift developers discover open-source libraries, code style guidelines, boilerplates, and development tools to accelerate application development across Apple platforms (iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS) and Linux. The intended users are Swift and iOS/macOS developers of all skill levels, ranging from beginners seeking learning tutorials and style guides to experienced engineers looking for production-ready architectural frameworks, database drivers, and debugging utilities. 

Notable technologies and tools featured throughout the repository include SwiftUI, UIKit, Combine, Core Data, Vapor, Kitura, Alamofire, RxSwift, SQLite, Realm, CocoaPods, Carthage, and the Swift Package Manager.

name: go
description: The Open Source Data Science Masters
summary:
The Open Source Data Science Masters (OSDSM) is a collectively maintained, open-source curriculum designed to prepare students for entry-level data scientist roles through self-guided study. It focuses on foundational theory and applied skills using open-source materials and zero-cost resources comparable to reputable paid programs.

The curriculum is structured into four main components:
1. **The Core**: Covers foundational concepts, problem-solving heuristics, the scientific process and experimentation, data querying using SQL, mathematics (calculus, linear algebra, statistics), and Python programming with libraries like pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and matplotlib.
2. **Specialty**: Allows learners to choose two specialized areas such as causation, natural language processing, graph analysis, machine learning, data visualization, linear programming, convex optimization, or deep learning/neural networks.
3. **Doing Data Science**: Focuses on professional workflows, communication, teamwork, spec writing, and results presentations.
4. **Capstone Project**: A practical project where students formulate a hypothesis, write a specification, analyze a dataset of their choice using tools like Jupyter notebooks, and document their work.

Intended for self-directed learners aiming for careers in data science, the project incorporates technologies and tools including Python, SQL, Jupyter, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and networkx.

name: rollup
description: Next-generation ES module bundler
summary: Rollup is a JavaScript module bundler designed to compile small pieces of code into larger, complex libraries and applications using the standardized ES module format. It enables developers to write future-proof code by supporting ES modules and provides features like tree shaking—statically analyzing code to exclude unused imports—to minimize bundle size and eliminate bloat. Rollup can target modern browsers for faster native loading or compile code to legacy module formats such as CommonJS, AMD, UMD, and IIFE-style scripts to ensure compatibility with environments lacking native ES module support. It is intended for JavaScript developers building applications or libraries and can be operated via a command-line interface or a JavaScript API, supporting technologies such as Node.js, npm, CommonJS, AMD, UMD, and ES modules.

name: docker_practice
description: 最新Docker容器技术，从真实案例中学习最佳实践！| Learn and understand Docker&Container technologies, with real DevOps practice!
summary:
"Docker 从入门到实践" is an open-source technical book and guide designed to help readers systematically master Docker container technology, from core concepts and underlying principles to advanced practical applications. 

Based on Docker Engine v29.x, the book targets application developers, system administrators, DevOps engineers, and IT professionals with basic Linux knowledge. It provides structured learning content ranging from fundamental operations—such as images, containers, and registries—to advanced topics including Dockerfile, data and network management, Buildx, and Compose. Additionally, it explores underlying implementations, container orchestration systems like Kubernetes and Etcd, container security, monitoring and logging systems (Prometheus, ELK), and ecosystem projects such as Fedora CoreOS and Podman.

name: AiToEarn
description: Let's use AI to Earn!
summary:
AiToEarn is an all-in-one AI content marketing agent platform designed to help one-person companies (OPCs), creators, brands, and enterprises build, distribute, and monetize content globally across mainstream platforms. 

The project's core capabilities are organized around four main agent functions:
- **Monetize**: Sells content through merchant promotional tasks using result-oriented settlement models including CPS (Cost Per Sale), CPE (Cost Per Engagement), and CPM (Cost Per Mille).
- **Publish**: Distributes content with one click to over 10 platforms—including Douyin, Xiaohongshu (Rednote), Kuaishou, Bilibili, Channels, WeChat Official Accounts, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Threads, X (Twitter), Pinterest, and LinkedIn—and provides unified calendar scheduling.
- **Engage**: Automates platform operations via a browser plugin to handle likes, collections, follows, AI-generated targeted comment responses, conversion signal mining, and brand monitoring.
- **Create**: Streamlines content production by automatically orchestrating video and image generation models (such as Grok, Veo, Seedance, and Nano Banana) for batch creation and multi-channel distribution.

Intended users include solo entrepreneurs, digital creators, marketing teams, and developers. Notable technologies used include Docker, Node.js (v20.18.x), Electron, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and integration with various AI and social media relay services.

name: fe-interview
description: 前端面试每日 3+1，以面试题来驱动学习，提倡每日学习与思考，每天进步一点！每天早上5点纯手工发布面试题（死磕自己，愉悦大家），6000+道前端面试题全面覆盖，HTML/CSS/JavaScript/Vue/React/Nodejs/TypeScript/ECMAScritpt/Webpack/Jquery/小程序/软技能……
summary:
This project is a free, open-source public service repository featuring a comprehensive frontend knowledge question bank designed to drive learning through interview questions. It aims to help developers build solid foundations and maintain daily study habits in web technologies. 

The project provides thousands of questions across foundational topics such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and soft skills, as well as specialized subjects including Vue, React, AngularJs, ECMAScript, NodeJs, jQuery, mini-programs, and tools like webpack. 

Intended users are frontend developers, job seekers, and learners looking to continuously improve their technical knowledge through daily practice and problem-solving rather than cramming. Notable technologies and concepts covered encompass HTML, CSS, JavaScript, ECMAScript, Vue, React, Angular, Node.js, and webpack.

name: faas
description: OpenFaaS - Serverless Functions Made Simple
summary:
OpenFaaS is an open-source, serverless framework designed for developers to easily deploy event-driven functions and microservices to Kubernetes or alternative environments without repetitive boilerplate code. It allows users to package code or binaries into OCI-compatible or Docker images, yielding scalable endpoints equipped with metrics and auto-scaling capabilities, including scaling to zero. 

The project targets developers, hobbyists, and enterprises looking for serverless orchestration. Notable features include a UI portal, a template store supporting languages like Node.js, Python, and Golang, a command-line interface (CLI) utilizing YAML for function configuration, built-in queuing, background processing, and support for event triggers such as HTTP, Apache Kafka, and AWS SQS. OpenFaaS integrates with cloud-native technologies including Kubernetes, OpenShift, Istio, Linkerd, and Grafana.

The repository houses the OpenFaaS Community Edition (CE), written in Golang and governed by specific non-commercial and trial licensing terms, alongside commercially supported Standard and Enterprise tiers maintained by OpenFaaS Ltd.

name: spotify-downloader
description: Download your Spotify playlists and songs along with album art and metadata (from YouTube if a match is found).
summary:
spotDL v4 is a command-line music downloader designed to find songs from Spotify playlists on YouTube and download them along with album art, lyrics, and metadata. 

Main capabilities include downloading tracks, saving Spotify metadata without downloading, retrieving direct URLs, synchronizing local directories with Spotify playlists, updating song file metadata, and providing a limited-feature web interface. The tool sources audio from YouTube to achieve the highest possible bitrate (128 kbps for regular users and up to 256 kbps for YouTube Music premium users).

Intended users are individuals looking to manage, download, and sync music collections based on Spotify links. Notable technologies utilized include Python, FFmpeg, Deno, yt-dlp, Docker, and the PyPI ecosystem, with installation supported via pip, prebuilt executables, Termux, Arch User Repository, and Docker containers. The project is distributed under the MIT License.

name: vapor
description: 💧 A server-side Swift HTTP web framework.
summary: Vapor is an HTTP web framework designed for Swift. Its purpose is to provide an expressive and easy-to-use foundation for building websites, APIs, and cloud projects. It is intended for Swift developers seeking to construct web services and applications. Vapor utilizes Swift 6.0+.

name: testify
description: A toolkit with common assertions and mocks that plays nicely with the standard library
summary:
Testify is a set of Go packages designed to help developers write comprehensive test code and verify that programs behave as intended. Its main capabilities include easy assertions via the `assert` and `require` packages, mock object generation and expectation tracking via the `mock` package, and object-oriented testing suite structures via the `suite` package. 

Intended for Go developers writing unit and integration tests, Testify integrates with the standard `go test` runner. Notable technologies used include Go (golang), supporting Go versions 1.19 and onward, along with ecosystem tools like `golangci-lint`, `testifylint`, and `mockery`.

name: awesome-deep-learning-papers
description: The most cited deep learning papers
summary:
This repository provides a curated list of top 100 highly cited and seminal deep learning papers published between 2012 and 2016.
