Designed as a foundational starting point for researchers and practitioners, the collection emphasizes classic papers that offer valuable lessons and broad applicability across diverse domains rather than narrow application-specific studies. 

The catalog is organized into several key topics, including understanding, generalization, and transfer; optimization and training techniques; unsupervised and generative models; convolutional neural network models; image segmentation and object detection; general image and video processing; natural language processing and recurrent neural networks; speech recognition; and reinforcement learning and robotics. It also includes sections for older foundational papers, technical hardware/software reports, datasets, books, surveys, tutorials, and blogs. 

Notable technologies and frameworks referenced across the materials include TensorFlow, Theano, Torch7, MatConvNet, Caffe, and OpenAI Gym. The repository targets deep learning researchers, beginners, and practitioners seeking a structured overview of seminal works in the field.

name: LxgwWenKai
description: An open-source Chinese font derived from Fontworks' Klee One. 一款开源中文字体，基于 FONTWORKS 出品字体 Klee One 衍生。
summary:
LXGW WenKai (霞鹜文楷) is an open-source Chinese, Japanese, and Korean (CJK) font derived from Fontworks' Klee One. Designed with a Japanese textbook style that blends regular script (Kai) and Song script characteristics, the project aims to provide a high-quality open-source regular script font suitable for poetry, annotation, and medium-length texts. 

The font family supports Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Hangul, featuring multiple weights and Unicode Variation Sequences (UVS) for punctuation positioning. Notable variants include *LXGW WenKai Screen*, *LXGW WenKai Lite*, *LXGW WenKai GB*, *LXGW WenKai TC*, *LXGW WenKai KR*, and western-merged variants such as *LXGW Bright* and *LXGW Bright Code*. 

Intended for general users, developers embedding fonts into software, and designers seeking open-source CJK typography, the project is distributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (OFL 1.1). Technologies utilized include Python 3, make-based build pipelines, and various open-source font merging and deep learning tools for character generation.

name: Babylon.js
description: Babylon.js is a powerful, beautiful, simple, and open game and rendering engine packed into a friendly JavaScript framework.
summary: Babylon.js is a 3D engine and framework designed for building 3D experiences on the web. Its main capabilities include rendering 3D scenes, managing cameras, lights, and meshes (such as spheres and grounds), and handling render loops and window resize events. The project provides full typing support, ES6 packages supporting tree shaking, and modules available via npm. It also offers tools such as an online playground, sandbox, shader creation tool, and exporters for 3DS Max, Maya, Blender, and Unity. Intended users include developers and creators building 3D web applications. Notable technologies utilized include JavaScript, TypeScript, and glTF.

name: pumpkin-book
description: 南瓜书：《机器学习》（西瓜书）公式详解
summary:
南瓜书（pumpkin-book）是一个专门为周志华老师的《机器学习》（西瓜书）编写的配套学习资料与解析笔记项目。项目的主要目的是针对西瓜书中较为难懂的公式进行解析，并为部分公式补充具体的推导细节，帮助读者更好地理解书中的数学内容。

该项目的主要能力包括提供西瓜书全书公式的详细推导过程、本科数学基础视角的公式讲解、超纲数学知识的附录与参考文献引导，以及配套的PDF版本下载、勘误表和视频教程。 intended users（intended users）主要为机器学习领域的初学者以及在自学机器学习过程中需要查阅和推导公式细节的学生和研究者。

name: masscan
description: TCP port scanner, spews SYN packets asynchronously, scanning entire Internet in under 5 minutes.
summary:
Masscan is an Internet-scale asynchronous port scanner designed to scan the entire Internet in under 5 minutes from a single machine at rates exceeding 10 million packets per second. Its syntax, parameters, and output formats are similar to `nmap`. 

Main capabilities include simultaneous IPv4 and IPv6 scanning, custom TCP/IP stack implementation, banner checking across multiple protocols (such as HTTP, FTP, SSH, SMTP, POP3, IMAP4, SSL, SMBv1/v2, Telnet, RDP, VNC, and memcached), randomized target generation via encryption, and multiple output formats (XML, JSON, binary, grepable, and list). Intended users are security professionals, network administrators, and researchers conducting wide-range network discovery. 

Notable technologies and components used include an ad hoc user-mode TCP/IP stack, C90 standard C, `libpcap`, and optional support for high-performance network drivers like PF_RING ZC. It compiles using standard C compilers such as `gcc`, `clang`, or Microsoft Visual Studio, with primary support for Linux alongside Windows and macOS.

name: calibre
description: The official source code repository for the calibre ebook manager
summary: Calibre is a cross-platform e-book manager designed to view, convert, edit, and catalog e-books across all major formats. Intended for e-book readers and users managing digital libraries, Calibre communicates directly with e-book reader devices, fetches book metadata from the internet, and downloads newspapers to convert them into readable e-book formats. It operates across Linux, Windows, and macOS.

name: incubator-seata
description: :fire: Seata is an easy-to-use, high-performance, open source distributed transaction solution.
summary:
Apache Seata (Simple Extensible Autonomous Transaction Architecture) is a high-performance, easy-to-use distributed transaction solution designed for microservices architectures. It addresses data consistency challenges across multiple services and independent data sources by providing a global transaction framework. 

The core architecture consists of three main components: Transaction Coordinator (TC), which maintains global and branch transaction statuses and drives commits or rollbacks; Transaction Manager (TM), which defines global transaction scopes; and Resource Manager (RM), which manages resources for branch transactions and communicates with the TC. Its transaction lifecycle utilizes a globally unique XID propagated through microservices invocation chains to coordinate local branch transactions. 

Targeted at developers building distributed microservices applications, Apache Seata supports Java environments and integrates with Spring Boot via artifacts such as `seata-all` and `seata-spring-boot-starter`. The project ecosystem also provides GoLang clients, Kubernetes integration, and CLI tooling.

name: flux
description: Official inference repo for FLUX.1 models
summary:
FLUX by Black Forest Labs provides minimal inference code and utilities to run image generation and editing tasks using an extensive suite of open-weight models. The repository supports capabilities such as text-to-image generation, in/out-painting, structural conditioning (via Canny and Depth variants with optional LoRA), image variation, and in-context image editing. 

Intended users include developers, researchers, and commercial entities looking to perform local inference or integrate with the BFL API. The project features local installation procedures supporting standard Python environments as well as NVIDIA TensorRT configurations via Enroot containers. Notable technologies and frameworks utilized include Python, PyTorch, HuggingFace repositories, and TensorRT. Additionally, the codebase provides built-in usage tracking logic to facilitate commercial licensing compliance for the open-weight models.

name: feather
description: Simply beautiful open-source icons
summary: Feather is a collection of open-source SVG icons designed on a 24x24 grid with an emphasis on simplicity, consistency, and flexibility. Intended for developers and designers, the project can be used in web applications via client-side JavaScript, Node, SVG sprites, and a Figma component library. Notable technologies used include JavaScript, npm, and SVG.

name: A2A
description: Agent2Agent (A2A) is an open protocol enabling communication and interoperability between opaque agentic applications.
summary:
The Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol is an open-source project hosted by the Linux Foundation and originally contributed by Google. It provides an open protocol that enables communication, discovery, and interoperability between opaque generative AI agentic applications built on diverse frameworks. 

Main capabilities include capability discovery via "Agent Cards," modality negotiation, secure collaboration on long-running tasks without exposing internal states or memories, and support for synchronous request/response, streaming via Server-Sent Events (SSE), and asynchronous push notifications. The protocol handles rich data exchange including text, files, and structured JSON data.

Intended users include developers and enterprises seeking to connect multi-framework agents—such as those built using Google ADK, LangGraph, or BeeAI—into complex sequential, hierarchical, or multi-agent workflows. 

Notable technologies and technical terms utilized include JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP(S), Agent Cards, Server-Sent Events (SSE), and official SDKs provided in Python (`a2a-sdk`), Go, JavaScript, Java, .NET, and Rust.

name: zulip
description: Zulip server and web application. Open-source team chat that helps teams stay productive and focused.
summary:
Zulip is an open-source, organized team chat application designed for both live and asynchronous conversations through unique topic-based threading. Aimed at remote teams, Fortune 500 companies, open-source projects, and organizations of all sizes, it combines the best elements of email and chat. 

The project can be self-hosted on Ubuntu or Debian Linux, via Docker, or deployed using prebuilt images for DigitalOcean and Render, and is also available through Zulip Cloud hosting options. Zulip is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: crawlee
description: Crawlee—A web scraping and browser automation library for Node.js to build reliable crawlers. In JavaScript and TypeScript. Extract data for AI, LLMs, RAG, or GPTs. Download HTML, PDF, JPG, PNG, and other files from websites. Works with Puppeteer, Playwright, Cheerio, JSDOM, and raw HTTP. Both headful and headless mode. With proxy rotation.
summary:
Crawlee is a web scraping and browser automation library designed to help developers build reliable scrapers that bypass modern bot protections. Written in TypeScript, it provides a unified interface for both HTTP-based and headless browser crawling. 

Main capabilities include a persistent URL queue, pluggable tabular and file storage, automatic resource scaling, integrated proxy rotation and session management, lifecycle hooks, configurable routing, error handling, retries, and ready-to-deploy Dockerfiles. For HTTP crawling, it features HTTP2 support, browser-like header generation, TLS fingerprint replication, and HTML parsers like Cheerio and JSDOM. For real browser crawling, it supports JavaScript rendering, screenshots, human-like fingerprint generation, and automated browser management via Playwright and Puppeteer across Chrome, Firefox, and Webkit.

Intended for developers building web scrapers and automation solutions in JavaScript or TypeScript (requiring Node.js 16 or higher), the library integrates smoothly with the Apify platform and is also usable via a dedicated CLI.

name: difftastic
description: a structural diff that understands syntax 🟥🟩
summary:
Difftastic is a structural diff tool that compares files based on their syntax rather than operating purely on a line-by-line basis. It understands programming language syntax, distinguishes significant whitespace from indentation changes, handles reformatted code, and supports over 30 programming languages. The project is designed for human consumption, providing a side-by-side display and compatibility with version control systems such as Git and Mercurial. It also supports merge conflict markers and can check if two files share the same Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) without generating a full diff. 

Difftastic treats structural diffing as a graph problem utilizing Dijkstra's algorithm and integrates tree-sitter parsers. It falls back to a line-oriented diff with word highlighting for unrecognized file extensions or parse errors. Non-goals include generating patch files for later application and performing AST-based merging. Known issues involve performance scaling on files with heavy changes, memory usage, and potential confusion in side-by-side displays.

name: simple-icons
description: SVG icons for popular brands
summary: Simple Icons is a collection of over 3,400 SVG icons representing popular brands, designed for developers and designers. The project provides direct SVG downloads via its website, CDN hosting (supporting customizable colors and dark mode variants), and native packages for Node.js, TypeScript, and PHP. Numerous third-party extensions and wrapper libraries exist for frameworks such as Angular, Astro, Blazor, Django, Flutter, React, Svelte, and Vue.

name: github-profile-readme-generator
description: 🚀 Generate GitHub profile README easily with the latest add-ons like visitors count, GitHub stats, etc using minimal UI.
summary:
GitHub Profile README Generator is a web application designed to help users easily create and customize GitHub profile READMEs through a minimal user interface. The project purpose is to simplify adding popular features and metrics without manual editing.

Main capabilities include generating Markdown and providing a live preview based on user inputs such as name, tagline, developer platform usernames, and portfolio links. It supports uniform dev and social icons, visitors counter badges, GitHub profile stats cards, top skills, streak stats, dynamic blog integrations (Dev.to, Medium, RSS feeds, Hashnode), Wakatime stats, and a Buy Me A Coffee button. 

Intended users are developers looking to build or update their GitHub profile pages quickly. The application is built using Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lucide React, and React Hook Form, and incorporates Google Analytics 4 with privacy-first configurations and IP anonymization.

name: dbx
description: 25 MB lightweight cross-platform database client for 100+ databases, including MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, DuckDB, SQL Server, and Dameng. Built-in AI, MCP Server, CLI, desktop and Docker. | 轻量级跨平台数据库管理工具，支持 MySQL、PostgreSQL、SQLite、Redis、MongoDB、达梦等 100+ 数据库，提供桌面端、Docker、CLI、内置 AI 助手和 MCP。
summary:
DBX is a lightweight, cross-platform database manager and developer tool supporting over 100 databases, message queues, and middleware in a single binary. Its primary purpose is to provide a fast, zero-bloat environment for database management, data operations, schema analysis, and AI-assisted SQL generation across desktop, Docker, CLI, and web deployments.

Main capabilities include a CodeMirror-based query editor with autocomplete, a high-performance virtual-scrolled data grid, schema browsing, ER diagrams, schema comparison, data import/export, file preview via DuckDB, specialized browsers for Redis and MongoDB, and consoles for message queues and middleware such as Kafka, RocketMQ, RabbitMQ, Pulsar, MQTT, Nacos, Consul, ZooKeeper, and etcd. It also features a built-in AI SQL assistant compatible with Claude, OpenAI, and local models, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI coding agents, and an extensible sandboxed plugin system. 

Intended users include software developers, database administrators, and AI developers seeking a unified database console. Notable technologies used include Tauri 2, Vue 3, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, CodeMirror 6, Rust, sqlx, Tiberius, redis-rs, and the MongoDB Rust driver.

name: Kingfisher
description: A lightweight, pure-Swift library for downloading and caching images from the web.
summary:
Kingfisher is a pure-Swift library designed for downloading and caching web images asynchronously in applications built for iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS. 

Main capabilities include URLSession-based and local data loading, a multi-layer hybrid memory and disk cache with customizable expiration and size limits, cancelable downloading, content prefetching, low data mode support, live photo caching, and built-in transition animations. It offers extensible image processors and filters, customizable placeholders and indicators, and method chaining via the `KF` builder and `KFImage` for SwiftUI. It also provides framework extensions for `UIImageView`, `NSImageView`, `NSButton`, `UIButton`, `NSTextAttachment`, `WKInterfaceImage`, `TVMonogramView`, and `CPListItem`.

The intended users are Swift developers building Apple platform applications who need an efficient, lightweight system for remote image handling and caching. Notable technologies utilized include Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit, AppKit, URLSession, and Swift Concurrency.

name: awesome-flipperzero
description: 🐬 A collection of awesome resources for the Flipper Zero device.
summary:
This repository is a curated collection of resources, databases, applications, firmwares, graphics, hardware modules, and guides for the Flipper Zero device. Designed for enthusiasts, developers, and ethical hackers, the project provides comprehensive tools and documentation spanning Sub-GHz, NFC, RFID, Infrared, BadUSB, GPIO integrations, and Bluetooth capabilities. 

Key capabilities include accessing community databases and dumps, installing custom firmwares such as Unleashed and Momentum, downloading plugins and games, managing device animations, and constructing hardware modules or 3D-printed cases. The repository also compiles off-device utilities, development bindings (such as Rust crates and C/C++ SDKs), file converters, debugging scripts, and repair references. Notable technologies and protocols referenced throughout the project include ESP32, ESP8266, NRF24, CC1101, KiCad, Python, and VSCode extensions.

name: whisperX
description: WhisperX:  Automatic Speech Recognition with Word-level Timestamps (& Diarization)
summary: WhisperX is an automatic speech recognition (ASR) tool that provides fast, batched inference with word-level timestamps and speaker diarization. Designed for developers and researchers working with audio and video transcription, the project utilizes a faster-whisper backend for high-speed processing and integrates wav2vec2 for accurate forced phoneme alignment. It also features Voice Activity Detection (VAD) preprocessing to reduce hallucinations and pyannote-audio for multi-speaker identification and labeling. Notable technologies include PyTorch, torchaudio, CTranslate2, and Hugging Face models.

name: pkg
description: Package your Node.js project into an executable
summary:
`pkg` is a deprecated command-line interface and API that packages Node.js projects into standalone executables capable of running on target machines without requiring Node.js or npm to be installed. 

Project capabilities include cross-compilation for multiple platforms and architectures (such as Linux, macOS, and Windows with support for various Node.js versions), automated dependency traversal, bytecode generation via V8, asset and native addon (`.node` file) bundling, compression algorithms (Brotli or GZip), and the creation of self-extracting installers or commercial evaluation versions. It manages a virtual snapshot filesystem at runtime and allows runtime options to be baked into executables.

Intended users are Node.js developers looking to distribute commercial apps without exposing source code, deploy single-file deployments, or test applications across multiple Node.js versions. Notable technologies utilized include Node.js, V8 bytecode compilation, QEMU, and Rosetta 2 for cross-architecture builds.

name: argo-cd
description: Declarative Continuous Deployment for Kubernetes
summary: Argo CD is a declarative GitOps continuous delivery tool designed for Kubernetes. Its main purpose is to automate, audit, and simplify application deployment and lifecycle management by ensuring that application definitions, configurations, and environments are declarative and version-controlled. The platform is targeted at developers, platform engineers, and operations teams managing Kubernetes workloads and multi-environment GitOps workflows. Notable technologies associated with the project include Kubernetes and Git.

name: eShopOnContainers
description: Cross-platform .NET sample microservices and container based application that runs on Linux Windows and macOS. Powered by .NET 7, Docker Containers and Azure Kubernetes Services. Supports Visual Studio, VS for Mac and CLI based environments with Docker CLI, dotnet CLI, VS Code or any other code editor. Moved to https://github.com/dotnet/eShop.
summary: The eShop sample application repository is now a read-only archive, with active development moved to the updated official .NET eShop repository (https://github.com/dotnet/eShop) as of November 2023. Historical code remains accessible via the dev branch.

name: Roo-Code
description: Roo Code gives you a whole dev team of AI agents in your code editor.
summary: Roo Code is an AI-powered developer extension for the Visual Studio Code editor designed to serve as an in-editor development team. It enables users to generate code from natural language specifications, refactor and debug existing code, write and update documentation, answer codebase questions, automate repetitive tasks, and utilize MCP servers. The project adapts to user workflows through specialized operational modes, including Code Mode, Architect Mode, Ask Mode, Debug Mode, and Custom Modes. Intended for developers seeking AI assistance within their editing environment, the repository notes that the extension was shut down on May 15th, pointing users to community alternatives such as ZooCode and Cline. It is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: index-tts
description: An Industrial-Level Controllable and Efficient Zero-Shot Text-To-Speech System
summary:
IndexTTS is an industrial-level, controllable, and efficient zero-shot text-to-speech system designed to clone voices from a single reference audio clip. The project supports Chinese, English, Japanese, Spanish, and Arabic. Its main capabilities include cross-lingual voice cloning, fine-grained emotion control (via emotional reference audio, explicit emotion descriptions, emotion vectors, or text-derived emotion analysis), speaking speed adjustment, and pronunciation control through Pinyin, CMU phonemes, and Japanese Kana. 

Intended for developers, researchers, and content creators looking for expressive and multilingual voice synthesis, the repository offers both a Python API and a WebUI. Notable technologies utilized include PyTorch, DeepSpeed, vLLM for production serving, and `uv` for environment and dependency management.

name: electron-react-boilerplate
description: A Foundation for Scalable Cross-Platform Apps
summary:
Electron React Boilerplate is a foundation for building cross-platform desktop applications. Its purpose is to provide a pre-configured development environment that streamlines writing, building, and packaging applications for local platforms. 

Main capabilities include starting a development environment with live reloading, generating production-ready bundles, previewing production builds locally, packaging installers using electron-builder, and executing smoke tests to verify app startup and IPC preloads. 

Intended users are software developers and engineers building desktop applications using web technologies. 

Notable technologies integrated into the project include Electron, React, React Router, electron-vite, React Fast Refresh, Node.js, and Vite 7.

name: windows95
description: Windows 95 in an app. Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
summary: The windows95 repository hosts an Electron application that runs the full Windows 95 operating system. Built primarily in JavaScript, the project leverages the v86 x86 virtualization library by Fabian Hemmer to execute Windows 95 on desktop platforms, including Windows, macOS, and Linux. The app functions as a functional emulator capable of running legacy software and DOS games, featuring preinstalled games and support for custom disk images via QEMU. It is intended for educational purposes.

name: gson
description: A Java serialization/deserialization library to convert Java Objects into JSON and back
summary:
Gson is a Java library designed to convert Java objects to their JSON representation and vice versa. Its primary purpose is to support serialization and deserialization for arbitrary Java objects, including pre-existing or unmodifiable objects without source-code access, without requiring Java annotations. 

Main capabilities include providing simple `toJson()` and `fromJson()` methods, extensive support for Java Generics, handling arbitrarily complex objects with deep inheritance hierarchies, and allowing custom object representations. It is targeted at Java developers, though it can work with other JVM languages and supports JPMS module descriptors. 

Technologies mentioned include Java, Maven, Gradle, ProGuard, R8, and optional JPMS modules such as `java.sql` and `jdk.unsupported` (`sun.misc.Unsafe`).

name: Paddle
description: PArallel Distributed Deep LEarning: Machine Learning Framework from Industrial Practice （『飞桨』核心框架，深度学习&机器学习高性能单机、分布式训练和跨平台部署）
summary:
PaddlePaddle is an industrial deep learning platform and core framework featuring advanced technologies, basic model libraries, end-to-end development kits, tools, components, and service platforms. Designed for industrial applications across sectors such as manufacturing, agriculture, and enterprise services, it enables developers, researchers, and enterprises to build, train, and deploy models. 

Key capabilities include unified dynamic and static graphs with automatic parallelism for distributed training, integrated training and inference for large models, high-order automatic differentiation and complex number operations for scientific computing, a neural network compiler for computational flexibility and performance optimization, and a heterogeneous multi-chip adaptation solution supporting multiple hardware types through a pluggable architecture. Released under the Apache-2.0 license, PaddlePaddle provides extensive English and Chinese documentation, guides, APIs, and an active open-source community.

name: gaussian-splatting
description: Original reference implementation of "3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering"
summary:
This repository contains the official implementation of "3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering," a method designed for real-time (≥30 fps) novel-view synthesis at 1080p resolution from multiple photos or videos. 

The project purpose is to enable high-quality radiance field rendering while maintaining competitive training times. Its main capabilities include optimizing 3D Gaussians starting from sparse Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points, interleaved optimization with anisotropic covariance density control, and a fast visibility-aware rendering algorithm supporting anisotropic splatting. Additional integrated features include training speed acceleration, depth regularization, exposure compensation, anti-aliasing via EWA filtering, OpenXR support for VR, and an interactive SIBR-based Top View.

Intended users include researchers and practitioners in computer graphics and computer vision working on novel-view synthesis and radiance fields.

Notable technologies and frameworks used include PyTorch, CUDA, OpenGL, OpenXR, COLMAP, ImageMagick, and the SIBR framework. The codebase comprises a PyTorch-based optimizer, a network viewer for training progress, an OpenGL-based real-time viewer, and conversion scripts for processing custom datasets.

name: p5.js
description: p5.js is a client-side JS platform that empowers artists, designers, students, and anyone to learn to code and express themselves creatively on the web. It is based on the core principles of Processing. Looking for p5.js 2.0? http://beta.p5js.org
summary:
p5.js is a free, open-source JavaScript library designed for accessible creative coding, acting as a web-based interpretation of Processing. Created as an exploratory tool and inclusive platform, it enables artists, designers, educators, beginners, and developers to treat web pages like sketchpads. 

The library provides a full suite of drawing tools and supports the creation of audio-visual, interactive, experimental, and generative works for the web. Notable technologies and graphics capabilities include WebGL and WebGPU. Users can extend the core library with community-created libraries and utilize the p5.js web editor. The project prioritizes accessibility, inclusivity, and community support, maintained primarily by volunteers with backing from the Processing Foundation.

name: ramda
description: :ram: Practical functional Javascript
summary:
Ramda is a practical functional programming library for JavaScript programmers, designed specifically to support a pure functional programming style. Its main capabilities include creating functional pipelines with immutability, side-effect-free functions, and automatic currying with parameters ordered specifically to facilitate currying. The library uses plain JavaScript objects and arrays as its basic data structures while prioritizing a clean API and high performance. 

Ramda is intended for JavaScript developers seeking an elegant, functional approach to coding. Notable technologies and ecosystems supported include Node.js, Deno, Webpack, Rollup, TypeScript, and Flow.

name: happy
description: Mobile and Web client for Codex and Claude Code, with realtime voice, encryption and fully featured
summary:
Happy is a mobile and web client for Claude Code and Codex that enables users to remotely monitor and control AI coding agents from anywhere with end-to-end encryption. The project provides a CLI wrapper to start AI sessions, push notifications for permission prompts or errors, and instant device switching between computer, phone, and desktop. 

The intended users are developers and engineers who want to track the progress of their AI-assisted coding tasks while away from their keyboards. 

Notable technologies and components include:
- **Happy CLI**: A command-line interface installed via npm (`happy claude` or `happy codex`).
- **Happy App**: A web UI and mobile client built with Expo (supporting iOS and Android).
- **Happy Desktop**: A native macOS application.
- **Happy Agent**: A remote agent control CLI.
- **Happy Server**: A backend server utilized for encrypted synchronization.

name: mihon
description: Free and open source manga reader for Android
summary:
Mihon is a full-featured reader application designed for Android devices running Android 8.0 or higher, enabling users to discover, read, and organize manga, webtoons, and comics. 

Main capabilities include local reading, a configurable reader with multiple viewers and reading directions, library organization using categories, light and dark themes, scheduled library updates for new chapters, local and cloud backup creation for offline reading, and tracker support for platforms such as MangaBaka, MyAnimeList, AniList, Kitsu, MangaUpdates, Shikimori, Bangumi, and Hikka. The application does not host any content and has no affiliation with content providers.

name: laravel-crm
description: Krayin CRM is Free & Open Source CRM Built with Laravel for Customer, Lead, and Sales Management.
summary:
Krayin CRM is a free, open-source customer relationship management framework designed for SMEs and Enterprises to manage the complete customer lifecycle. It features a descriptive admin panel, an admin dashboard, custom attributes, email parsing via SendGrid, and a modular approach. The platform supports extensions for Multi-Tenant SaaS, WhatsApp CRM integration, and VoIP CRM integration. 

Intended for e-commerce businesses, developers, and administrators, Krayin CRM is built using Laravel, PHP, and Vue.js. System requirements include Apache 2 or NGINX, PHP 8.3 or higher, Composer 2.5 or higher, and MySQL 8.0.32 or higher or MariaDB 11.4 LTS or higher, alongside at least 3 GB of RAM.

name: prefect
description: Prefect is a workflow orchestration framework for building resilient data pipelines in Python.
summary:
Prefect is a Python-based workflow orchestration framework designed for data teams to build, automate, and monitor resilient data pipelines. It enables users to turn scripts into production workflows featuring scheduling, caching, retries, error handling, and event-based automations. 

Intended for data practitioners and engineering teams, Prefect uses `flow` and `task` decorators to manage complex dependencies and branching logic. Workflow activity can be observed locally via a self-hosted Prefect server UI or managed through Prefect Cloud. The framework requires Python 3.10+ and supports installation via `pip` or `uv`. A lightweight `prefect-client` package is also available for communicating remotely with Prefect servers or Prefect Cloud in ephemeral execution environments.

name: security-audit-skill
description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
summary:
The `security-audit` project is a coding-agent skill that transforms AI agents into security auditors, originating as the single-repo starting point for Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness. It orchestrates isolated agents to perform structured security audits across target codebases. 

The project executes a six-phase workflow: Reconnaissance, Coverage-led hunting, Candidate validation, Structured output, Independent record verification, and Target-neutral reporting. It uses specialized hunting classes covering attack surfaces such as memory safety and binaries, AI and LLM implementations, web protocols and auth, client-side code, supply chains, cloud deployments, RPC and messaging protocols, resource exhaustion, data isolation, and desktop or mobile IPC. 

Intended users include developers and security engineers leveraging AI coding agents for automated vulnerability discovery, penetration testing, and code security reviews. 

Notable technologies and tools used include Node.js for zero-dependency validators (`validate-findings.cjs`, `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs`), JSON schemas, and markdown documentation files. The skill requires an OS-enforced sandbox with external networking disabled, resource limits, and strict write controls to safely execute target builds, tests, and fuzzers.

name: navidrome
description: 🎧 Your Personal Streaming Service
summary:
Navidrome is an open-source, web-based music collection server and streamer that lets users listen to their personal music libraries from any browser or mobile device. 

Main capabilities include handling very large music collections, streaming virtually any audio format, utilizing curated metadata, supporting compilations and multi-disc box sets, and maintaining a multi-user environment where each user manages their own play counts, playlists, and favorites. It automatically monitors libraries for changes, supports multiple lyric formats (including embedded tags and sidecar files like LRC and TTML), features on-the-fly transcoding with Opus encoding support, and offers compatibility with Subsonic, Madsonic, and Airsonic clients. 

Intended for music enthusiasts seeking a self-hosted streaming alternative, Navidrome runs on macOS, Linux, Windows, and Raspberry Pi, and is provided as Docker images. The project features a low-resource design with a modern, responsive, and themeable web interface built using Material UI.

name: Public-APIs
description: 📚 A public list of APIs from round the web.
summary:
Public-APIs is a curated, categorized collection of web APIs gathered from across the internet, designed for developers seeking resources for consumption and application integration. The repository organizes diverse services into a comprehensive Table of Contents spanning categories such as advertising, analytics, cryptocurrency, finance, machine learning, natural language processing, social media, transportation, weather, and videogames. 

Intended for software developers, engineers, and designers, the project provides references to both commercial and open-source APIs—including tools leveraging technologies like GraphQL, REST, JSON, XML, and WebSockets. It highlights resources across major platforms like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft, as well as specialized services for tasks such as file storage, image manipulation, authentication, mapping, and payment processing. Distinctive names and technical standards like Swagger and OpenAPI are supported to aid in API design and discovery.

name: DSA-Bootcamp-Java
description: This repository consists of the code samples, assignments, and notes for the Java data structures & algorithms + interview preparation bootcamp of WeMakeDevs.
summary: This repository hosts a Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) and interview preparation bootcamp. The project purpose is to provide educational resources for technical interview readiness, featuring a lecture playlist, a course website, and programming assignments with solutions available on LeetCode. Intended users include students and software engineering candidates preparing for technical interviews. The notable technologies and languages specified include Java and YouTube.

name: lexical
description: Lexical is an extensible text editor framework that provides excellent reliability, accessibility and performance.
summary: Lexical is an extensible, framework-agnostic text editor framework designed for reliability, accessibility, and performance. It features a plugin-based architecture, an immutable state model supporting time-travel with built-in undo and redo, real-time collaborative editing via Yjs, and serialization capabilities for JSON, Markdown, and HTML. Lexical supports rich content types such as tables, lists, code blocks, images, and custom nodes. Written in TypeScript for type safety, the project provides official React bindings alongside vanilla JavaScript support, targeting modern web browsers including Chrome 86+, Firefox 115+, Safari 15+, and Edge 86+. Intended for web developers building text editing applications, Lexical offers WCAG-compliant accessibility out of the box.

name: Vundle.vim
description: Vundle, the plug-in manager for Vim
summary: Vundle (Vim bundle) is a plugin manager for Vim designed to help users track, configure, install, update, search, and clean Vim plugins and scripts directly within the `.vimrc` file. It automatically manages runtime paths and regenerates help tags for installed scripts. Main capabilities include executing management actions through a single keypress in an interactive mode, searching available Vim scripts, and supporting plugins hosted on GitHub, other Git repositories, local machines, or specific subdirectories. Intended users are Vim developers and system administrators seeking a streamlined plugin workflow. Notable technologies utilized include Git, Curl, and Vim 7.3 across OS X, Linux, and Windows platforms.

name: SuperClaude_Framework
description: A configuration framework that enhances Claude Code with specialized commands, cognitive personas, and development methodologies.
summary:
SuperClaude Framework is a meta-programming configuration framework designed to transform Claude Code into a structured development platform through behavioral instruction injection and component orchestration. It provides developers with systematic workflow automation, intelligent agents, and extensive tooling across the complete software development lifecycle.

Main capabilities include 30 slash commands (covering planning, development, testing, project management, and research), 20 specialized AI agents (such as PM, Deep Research, and security engineer roles), 7 adaptive behavioral modes (including token-efficiency, brainstorming, and orchestration), and integrations with 8 Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Notable technologies and integrations include Tavily for web search, Playwright for browser automation, Context7 for documentation lookup, Sequential-Thinking for multi-step reasoning, and Serena for memory persistence. 

The framework is intended for developers and contributors seeking structured, token-efficient, and accelerated AI-assisted software engineering. It is distributed under the MIT License and installable via `pipx` or direct Git cloning.

name: MagicMirror
description: MagicMirror² is an open source modular smart mirror platform. With a growing list of installable modules, the MagicMirror² allows you to convert your hallway or bathroom mirror into your personal assistant.
summary: **MagicMirror²** is an open-source modular smart mirror platform designed to convert a standard mirror into a personal assistant. The project focuses on a modular plugin system backed by a growing list of installable modules. It is built using **Electron** as an application wrapper, eliminating the need for separate web server or browser installations. MagicMirror² targets makers and developers looking to build customized smart home displays with a community-driven ecosystem.

name: ncnn
description: ncnn is a high-performance neural network inference framework optimized for the mobile platform
summary:
ncnn is a high-performance neural network inference framework optimized for mobile, embedded, and desktop deployment. It operates with no third-party runtime dependencies and features a pure C++ implementation with C APIs and Python bindings. The framework provides CPU optimization (including ARM NEON and multi-core scheduling) and Vulkan GPU acceleration across platforms such as Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, WebAssembly, and HarmonyOS. 

ncnn includes the `pnnx` tool to convert PyTorch and ONNX models into ncnn format, alongside support for quantization, fp16/int8 arithmetic, custom layers, and model optimization tools like `ncnnoptimize`. It accommodates multi-input, multi-output, and multi-branch graphs for tasks spanning image classification, object detection, segmentation, face recognition, pose estimation, and speech recognition. Intended users are developers deploying deep learning models efficiently onto edge devices, phones, PCs, and browsers. Notable projects utilizing ncnn include Tencent applications such as QQ, Qzone, WeChat, and Pitu.

name: FizzBuzzEnterpriseEdition
description: FizzBuzz Enterprise Edition is a no-nonsense implementation of FizzBuzz made by serious businessmen for serious business purposes.
summary: FizzBuzzEnterpriseEdition is a satirical software project that implements the classic FizzBuzz game according to the rigorous, high-quality standards, architecture design principles, and customizable, extensible solutions characteristic of enterprise software. The repository demonstrates how an interview programming assignment—traditionally solved with basic loops and conditional statements for numbers 1 through 100—can be built with extreme enterprise-grade complexity. Intended users include software engineers and developers looking for programming satire that parodies over-engineered corporate software design.

name: CV
description: ✅（已完结）超级全面的 深度学习 笔记【土堆 Pytorch】【李沐 动手学深度学习】【吴恩达 深度学习】【大飞 大模型Agent】
summary:
This repository provides a comprehensive deep learning notes and tutorial collection covering computer vision (CV), natural language processing (NLP), large language models (LLMs), and Agent technologies. The materials incorporate instructional video content and corresponding notes from prominent lecturers including Tu Dui, Mu Li, Andrew Ng, and Da Fei, complemented by shared datasets. 

The project is designed for self-learners, students, and job seekers looking to master artificial intelligence, offering structured guidance ranging from foundational frameworks to advanced commercial-grade projects. Key technologies and frameworks featured throughout the notes include PyTorch, Jupyter Notebook, and Anaconda. In addition to technical learning materials, the repository provides community support channels, paper tutoring, resume editing, interview preparation, and job referral opportunities across major technology and enterprise companies such as Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, ByteDance, and Huawei.

name: best-of-ml-python
description: 🏆 A ranked list of awesome machine learning Python libraries. Updated weekly.
summary:
Best-of Machine Learning with Python is a curated and ranked list of open-source machine learning and data science projects built for Python developers, data scientists, and researchers. The repository aggregates hundreds of libraries grouped into 34 specialized categories—including machine learning frameworks, natural language processing, computer vision, data visualization, time series, graph data, geospatial analysis, reinforcement learning, recommendation systems, and hyperparameter optimization. Projects are automatically scored and ranked based on metrics collected from GitHub and package managers. 

Notable technologies and frameworks highlighted across the list include general-purpose and deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, Keras, XGBoost, JAX, and PaddlePaddle; specialized NLP tools such as Hugging Face Transformers and spaCy; and distributed computing or hardware-acceleration ecosystems like Ray, Dask, cuDF, and CuPy. The project serves as a comprehensive discovery tool for finding and comparing libraries to build, track, optimize, and deploy AI and machine learning workflows.

name: Awesome-Nano-Banana-images
description: A curated collection of fun and creative examples generated with Nano Banana & Nano Banana Pro🍌, Gemini-2.5-flash-image based model. We also release Nano-consistent-150K openly to support the community's development of image generation and unified models(click to website to see our blog)
summary:
This repository is a curated collection of task scenarios, examples, and prompts for Google's image generation and editing models, specifically Nano-banana and Nano-banana-pro. It showcases multi-image fusion, creative editing, and specialized visualizations gathered from platforms like Twitter/X and Xiaohongshu. 

Additionally, the project introduces Nano-consistent-150k, a high-quality dataset exceeding 150k entries built on Nano-Banana to maintain character identity consistency across diverse and complex editing scenarios. The repository also references related projects such as Editable-Design, a design skill combining coding agents with image generation models. 

Intended users include AI practitioners, prompt engineers, researchers, and creators interested in advanced image generation, character-consistent editing, and multimodal data construction. Notable technologies mentioned include Blender, Cinema 4D, PyTorch, Unreal Engine 5, and Hugging Face datasets.

name: CosyVoice
description: Multi-lingual large voice generation model, providing inference, training and deployment full-stack ability.
summary:
CosyVoice is an advanced large language model (LLM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) and speech synthesis system designed for zero-shot multilingual speech generation, cross-lingual voice cloning, and streaming applications. Its main capabilities include multi-lingual speech synthesis across 9 common languages and 18+ Chinese dialects/accents, pronunciation inpainting for Pinyin and CMU phonemes, instruction-following controls (emotions, speed, volume, language, and style), built-in text normalization, and bi-streaming support (text-in and audio-out) achieving low-latency outputs. 

Intended for developers, researchers, and production environments requiring expressive, high-consistency speech generation, the repository provides Python scripts, FastAPI and gRPC servers, WebUI demos, Docker configurations, and runtimes optimized with vLLM and NVIDIA Triton TensorRT-LLM. Notable technologies utilized include PyTorch, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Fastapi, and WeTextProcessing.

name: mostly-adequate-guide
description: Mostly adequate guide to FP (in javascript)
summary:
This repository contains a book and learning guide focused on the functional programming (FP) paradigm using JavaScript. The project aims to teach functional programming principles—such as algebraic data structures, functors, monads, and categorical constructs—through a widely used mixed-paradigm language, allowing developers to apply concepts immediately to real-world programs. 

Intended for developers looking to learn or transition to functional programming without immediately adopting purely functional languages, the guide features in-depth examples, runnable chapter exercises, and a supporting npm module (`@mostly-adequate/support`). The repository includes instructions and build scripts for generating PDF and EPUB versions of the book using Node.js and Calibre's `ebook-convert`. Notable technologies and environments referenced include JavaScript, Node.js, Gitbook, Calibre, nvm, Scala, Haskell, PureScript, and Swiftz.

name: system-design-interview
description: System design interview for IT companies
summary:
This repository provides a systematic guide and curated resource collection to help software engineers prepare for system design interviews at IT companies. It outlines a structured interview approach covering user cases, constraints, high-level architecture, component design, and object-oriented design (OOD). 

The project aggregates core study materials, including articles on basic system design concepts (such as scalability, CAP theorem, consistent hashing, and distributed systems fallacies), real-world engineering blog references from major tech companies, architectural overviews of notable products and systems, and practical reference solutions for frequent interview questions like designing a CDN, search engine, key-value database, or recommendation system. It also recommends technical books and design pattern resources. 

The intended users are software engineers and developers preparing for technical interviews. The repository references various technologies and distributed systems concepts, including MapReduce, Bigtable, Dynamo, Memcached, Cassandra, HBase, MongoDB, Redis, Apache Storm, Apache ZooKeeper, Apache Kafka, and Erlang.

name: vanna
description: 🤖 Chat with your SQL database 📊. Accurate Text-to-SQL Generation via LLMs using Agentic Retrieval 🔄.
summary:
Vanna 2.0 is an enterprise-ready framework designed to turn natural language questions into data insights, SQL queries, interactive tables, Plotly charts, and natural language summaries. It features a modern web interface centered around a pre-built `<vanna-chat>` component that supports real-time streaming responses and integrates with React, Vue, or plain HTML.

The platform is intended for developers, data analytics teams, multi-tenant SaaS applications, and enterprise environments requiring secure, user-aware permissions. Notable capabilities include role-based and row-level security, identity tracking via custom `UserResolver` implementations (supporting cookies, JWTs, or OAuth tokens), audit logs, and rate limiting. It also provides lifecycle hooks, LLM middlewares, conversation storage, observability, and custom tools.

Vanna 2.0 works with major LLMs (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, Azure, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, and Mistral) and numerous databases (including PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, SQLite, DuckDB, and ClickHouse). It integrates cleanly into backend frameworks like FastAPI and Flask.

name: age
description: A simple, modern and secure encryption tool (and Go library) with small explicit keys, no config options, and UNIX-style composability.
summary:
age is a simple, modern, and secure file encryption tool, format, and Go library. It is designed with small explicit keys, post-quantum support, no configuration options, and UNIX-style composability. 

Main capabilities include encrypting and decrypting files using age public keys, SSH public and private keys (`ssh-ed25519` and `ssh-rsa`), passphrases, and hybrid post-quantum keys. It supports multiple recipients, recipient files, passphrase-protected identity files, PEM-encoded armor output, and inspecting encrypted file metadata without decryption. Hardware PIV tokens like YubiKeys are supported via plugins.

Intended users include developers, system administrators, and anyone requiring straightforward and secure file encryption. 

Notable technologies and formats include Go, a C2SP specification format, and implementations or integrations in Rust (rage), TypeScript (typage), and YubiKey plugins.

name: brave-browser
description: Brave browser for Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows.
summary: The Brave Browser repository serves as the central hub for issue tracking, release management, and documentation wiki for the Brave Browser. Note that the actual source code and core contributions are maintained separately in the brave-core repository. The project targets developers, administrators, power users, and general users seeking bug reports, feature requests, software releases, and developer documentation.

name: BongoCat
description: 🐱 BongoCat — A cross-platform interactive desktop pet that brings fun to your desktop!
summary: BongoCat is an interactive desktop companion application for Windows and macOS that features an on-screen Live2D cat. The project's main capabilities include tracking mouse movement, reacting dynamically to every pressed keyboard key, mouse button, and gamepad button, and supporting custom Live2D models. Designed for desktop users looking for a customizable screen pet, BongoCat operates fully offline with no network access required, ensuring user privacy and data security through its open-source codebase.

name: ruby
description: The Ruby Programming Language
summary:
Ruby is an interpreted, object-oriented programming language designed for web development, plain text processing, serialized file handling, and system task management. Created by Yukihiro Matsumoto (Matz), Ruby is simple, straightforward, and extensible. 

Its main features include simple syntax, normal and advanced object-oriented features such as mix-ins and singleton methods, operator overloading, exception handling, iterators and closures, automatic garbage collection, dynamic loading of object files on supported architectures, and high portability across Unix-like and POSIX-compatible platforms, Windows, and macOS. The project is intended for developers and programmers seeking a versatile scripting and application development language.

name: iview
description: A high quality UI Toolkit built on Vue.js 2.0
summary:
iView is a high-quality UI toolkit built on Vue.js, designed to provide developers of all skill levels with dozens of useful and beautiful components accompanied by extensive documentation and demos. 

Main capabilities include a friendly API, server-side rendering (SSR) support, TypeScript integration, and compatibility with Nuxt.js and Electron. Most components support modern browsers and Internet Explorer 9 and above. 

Intended for web developers building applications with Vue.js, the project provides integration options via npm, global script tags, a Vue CLI 3 plugin, and a starter kit. Notable technologies used include Vue.js (versions 1.x and 2.x), JavaScript, CSS, TypeScript, Nuxt.js, and Electron.

name: validator.js
description: String validation
summary: validator.js is a library of string validators and sanitizers designed exclusively for string inputs. It provides a comprehensive set of validation methods for checking formats such as emails, URLs, IP addresses, dates, numeric ranges, credit card numbers, JWT tokens, cryptocurrency addresses, and localized identifiers, alongside sanitization utilities like escaping, trimming, blacklisting, and normalizing email addresses. Intended for JavaScript developers working on server-side and client-side applications, the package can be installed via npm, yarn, pnpm, or bower, and supports ES6 imports, tree-shaking, and AMD loaders. Notable technologies and formats supported include JSON, Base32, Base58, Base64, ISO standards, and various regional locale specifications.

name: pure
description: A set of small, responsive CSS modules that you can use in every web project.
summary: Pure is a set of small, responsive CSS modules designed as a starting point for every website or web app. Its main capabilities include a customizable responsive grid, a solid base built on Normalize.css for cross-browser compatibility, consistently styled buttons, vertical and horizontal menus with dropdown support, form alignments, common table styles, and an extremely minimalist look that is easy to customize. Pure is responsive by default with a non-responsive option and features an extremely small file size of 3.7KB minified and gzipped. It is intended for web developers looking for lightweight CSS styling modules. The project utilizes Node.js and npm for building from source and is distributed under the Yahoo! Inc. BSD-3-Clause license.

name: beekeeper-studio
description: Modern and easy to use SQL client for MySQL, Postgres, SQLite, SQL Server, and more. Linux, MacOS, and Windows.
summary:
Beekeeper Studio is a cross-platform SQL editor and database manager built for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Designed with a focus on modern user experience and speed, it provides an uncluttered, high-performance workbench for developers and database administrators to interact with multiple databases. 

Key capabilities include an autocomplete SQL query editor with syntax highlighting, a tabbed interface for multitasking, table data sorting and filtering, query run-history, saved queries, data import/export, and backup/restore functionality. It supports a wide array of relational, NoSQL, and analytical databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Amazon Redshift, CockroachDB, MariaDB, TiDB, Google BigQuery, Redis, Oracle Database, Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Firebird, LibSQL, ClickHouse, DuckDB, SQL Anywhere, MongoDB, Trino/Presto, SurrealDB, DynamoDB, and Snowflake. 

The project is structured as a monorepo built with Node.js, Electron, and Vue.js, offering a Community Edition licensed under the GPLv3 alongside commercial paid editions.

name: listmonk
description: High performance, self-hosted, newsletter and mailing list manager with a modern dashboard. Single binary app.
summary: listmonk is a standalone, self-hosted, feature-rich newsletter and mailing list manager distributed as a single binary. Designed for high performance, it uses a PostgreSQL database as its data store. The project is intended for users seeking a self-hosted solution to manage mailing lists and newsletters. Notable technologies utilized include Go for the backend and Vue with Buefy for the frontend UI. Installation is supported via Docker using Docker Compose or through standalone binary execution. The software is free and open-source, licensed under the AGPLv3.

name: timescaledb
description: A time-series database for high-performance real-time analytics packaged as a Postgres extension
summary:
TimescaleDB is a PostgreSQL extension designed for high-performance, real-time analytics on time-series and event data. It provides advanced data management capabilities including hypertables for time-based data partitioning, columnstore storage with compression, continuous aggregates for incremental pre-aggregation, and time-bucket functions. 

Intended for developers, database administrators, and organizations handling heavy data workloads, the project is commonly applied in domains such as IoT, financial markets, logistics, application event logging, and AI applications. Notable technologies utilized include PostgreSQL, Docker, and companion tools like pgvector, pgvectorscale, and pgai.

name: flutter-go
description: flutter 开发者帮助 APP，包含 flutter 常用 140+ 组件的demo 演示与中文文档
summary: FlutterGo is a paused-maintenance Flutter project that previously provided developer resources and community engagement opportunities. Intended for Flutter enthusiasts and developers, the repository includes team contact information for resume submissions via email and a DingTalk QR code for direct connection, though no active technical capabilities or technologies are currently detailed due to suspended maintenance.

name: Archon
description: The first open-source harness builder for AI coding. Make AI coding deterministic and repeatable.
summary:
Archon is an open-source workflow engine and harness builder designed to make AI coding deterministic and repeatable. It functions like a software development equivalent of Dockerfiles or CI/CD pipelines, allowing developers to encode software engineering processes—such as planning, implementation, validation, code review, and pull request creation—as structured YAML workflows.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Deterministic Workflows:** Combines rigid structure (bash scripts, tests, git operations) with AI intelligence at designated steps.
- **Git Worktree Isolation:** Automatically runs workflows in isolated git worktrees to enable parallel task execution without conflicts.
- **Workflow Automation (SDLC pack):** Ships with workflows for triage, investigation, planning, implementation, validation, code review, PR creation, and maintenance.
- **Flexible Interactions:** Supports loops, human approval gates, and fresh-context execution per iteration.
- **Multi-Platform Access:** Operates via CLI, a Web UI (`archon serve`), and chat platform integrations including Telegram, Slack, GitHub Webhooks, and Discord.

**Intended Users:** Software developers and engineering teams utilizing AI coding agents (such as Claude Code) who want to enforce consistent, repeatable development processes across their repositories.

**Notable Technologies:** Built using TypeScript/Bun with support for SQLite and PostgreSQL databases, integrating with Claude Code and GitHub CLI.

name: osquery
description: SQL powered operating system instrumentation, monitoring, and analytics.
summary:
osquery is a SQL-powered operating system instrumentation, monitoring, and analytics framework available for Linux, macOS, and Windows. It exposes an operating system as a high-performance relational database, allowing users to write SQL-based queries to explore and monitor operating system data such as running processes, loaded kernel modules, open network connections, browser plugins, hardware events, and file hashes. 

SQL tables are implemented using a plugin and extensions API. Queries can be performed on an ad-hoc basis using the `osqueryi` shell, executed via a scheduler using `osqueryd` to monitor state across a set of hosts, or launched from custom applications using osquery Thrift APIs. The project is intended for system administrators, security professionals, and developers seeking to analyze and monitor host infrastructure.

name: angular-styleguide
description: Angular Style Guide: A starting point for Angular development teams to provide consistency through good practices.
summary: The Angular Style Guide by John Papa provides an opinionated set of conventions, syntax rules, and structural guidelines for building Angular applications. Endorsed by the Angular team, the project is designed to help teams establish consistent development practices based on real-world experience, presentations, and training courses. The repository contains multiple versions tailored to different versions of Angular, specifically including guides for Angular 1 and Angular 2. The intended users are developers and teams working with the Angular and AngularJS ecosystems who seek guidance on application architecture and clean code practices.

name: livewire
description: A full-stack framework for Laravel that takes the pain out of building dynamic UIs.
summary: Livewire is a full-stack framework for Laravel that enables developers to build dynamic user interface components using PHP without needing to write extensive JavaScript. Designed for Laravel developers, the framework streamlines frontend development by keeping application logic on the backend while maintaining reactive interfaces. The project utilizes PHP, JavaScript, Composer, NPM, and ChromeDriver for local development and testing.

name: docz
description: ✍ It has never been so easy to document your things!
summary:
Docz is a tool designed to help developers write and publish interactive documentation for their code. By utilizing MDX files, Docz transforms code showcases into live-reloading, SEO-friendly, and production-ready static documentation sites. 

Main capabilities include running a local development server for live previews, generating static build assets for deployment on any static hosting provider, and supporting interactive components like code playgrounds and property tables via MDX integration. The project is intended for software developers and teams looking to streamline code documentation. It leverages notable technologies including GatsbyJS, Gatsby theme shadowing, React, and MDX, while supporting custom configurations and styling solutions such as styled-components, Sass, Less, and CSS Modules.

name: oh-my-posh
description: The most customisable and low-latency cross platform/shell prompt renderer
summary: Oh My Posh is a cross-platform, highly customizable, and extensible prompt theme engine for any shell. It serves as a shell-agnostic and platform-agnostic prompt utility designed to be fast and configurable. Its main capabilities include support for secondary prompts, right prompts, and transient prompts. The project targets developers and command-line users seeking to personalize and enhance their shell environments. Notable technologies and languages associated with the project include Go, PowerShell, and various shell environments.

name: compose-samples
description: Official Jetpack Compose samples.
summary:
The Jetpack Compose Samples repository contains a collection of individual Android Studio projects designed to help developers learn Jetpack Compose. Intended for Android developers, the repository provides hands-on demonstrations of various use cases, complexity levels, and APIs through sample applications such as JetNews (a blog post viewer), Jetchat (a chat app focusing on UI state patterns and Material 3), Jetsnack (a snack ordering app with custom design systems), Jetcaster (a podcast app featuring Redux-style architecture and dynamic themes), Reply (an email client demonstrating adaptive design and Material 3), and JetLagged (a sleep tracker showcasing custom layouts and graphics). 

The samples highlight notable capabilities including custom layouts, animations, dynamic theming, downloadable fonts, adaptive UIs for phones, tablets, foldables, desktops, wear, and TV devices. Key technologies and libraries utilized across the projects include Jetpack Compose, Material Design 3, Architecture Components (Navigation, Fragments, LiveData, ViewModel), Coroutines, Room, WindowInsets, and Window Size Classes.

name: fasthttp
description: Fast HTTP package for Go. Tuned for high performance. Zero memory allocations in hot paths. Up to 10x faster than net/http
summary:
Fasthttp is a high-performance HTTP implementation for Go, designed specifically for high-throughput edge cases where servers and clients must handle thousands of small to medium requests per second with consistent low-millisecond response times. 

Main capabilities include fast HTTP server and client operations optimized for zero-memory allocation in hot paths, byte slice buffer reuse, and support for connection hijacking and streaming options via custom request handlers (`RequestHandler` and `RequestCtx`). It is intended for advanced Go developers and high-load production environments requiring extreme throughput and minimal garbage collection overhead, whereas standard library alternatives are recommended for general use cases. Notable technologies and related concepts include Go, TCP, Unix sockets, and integrations with third-party routers and frameworks such as Fiber, Atreugo, and fastws.

name: RAG-Anything
description: "RAG-Anything: All-in-One RAG Framework"
summary:
RAG-Anything is an all-in-one multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework built on top of LightRAG. It aims to process and query diverse document formats containing mixed content modalities—including text, images, tables, mathematical equations, audio, and video—within a single integrated architecture. 

The project's main capabilities include an end-to-end multimodal pipeline for document ingestion, parsing, and query answering, universal document format support (PDFs, Office documents, images, text files, and media), specialized content analysis for visual, tabular, and mathematical elements, and automated multimodal knowledge graph construction with cross-modal relationship discovery. It supports multiple parsers such as MinerU, Docling, and PaddleOCR, alongside direct content list insertion and flexible hybrid retrieval mechanisms. 

Intended users include researchers, developers, and organizations working on academic research, technical documentation, financial reporting, and enterprise knowledge management involving rich, heterogeneous documents. Notable technologies used in the project include Python, PyTorch, OpenAI APIs, MinerU, Docling, PaddleOCR, faster-whisper, and PySceneDetect.

name: intro.js
description: Lightweight, user-friendly onboarding tour library
summary: Intro.js is a user onboarding and product walkthrough library designed to help developers create step-by-step guides, introductions, and hints for web applications. The library enables step presentations to be applied to HTML elements using attributes such as `data-intro`, `data-step`, and `data-hint`, and is initiated via JavaScript using the `introJs().start()` function. It provides Right-to-Left (RTL) language support through dedicated stylesheets and includes various framework wrappers. Built using Node.js and npm, Intro.js can be integrated via local cloning, yarn, npm, or CDN services like jsDelivr and ccdnjs.

name: streisand
description: Streisand sets up a new server running your choice of WireGuard, OpenConnect, OpenSSH, OpenVPN, Shadowsocks, sslh, Stunnel, or a Tor bridge. It also generates custom instructions for all of these services. At the end of the run you are given an HTML file with instructions that can be shared with friends, family members, and fellow activists.
summary:
Streisand is an automation tool that sets up censorship-resistant Virtual Private Network (VPN) services and anti-censorship tools on cloud servers. Intended for users with Unix command-line experience, the project aims to bypass network blocks imposed by ISPs, telecommunication companies, politicians, and corporations. 

Streisand automates the configuration of various services and add-ons, including OpenSSH, Tinyproxy, OpenConnect, Cisco AnyConnect, OpenVPN, Stunnel, Shadowsocks with the V2ray-plugin, Tor bridge relays with obfs4 (Obfsproxy), and WireGuard. It generates a private website containing configuration instructions and client software for the deployed services. 

The project supports deployment on major cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Digital Ocean, Google Compute Engine (GCE), Linode, and Rackspace, as well as fresh Ubuntu servers via advanced installation methods. Installation requires a Unix-compatible system, including Linux, BSD, macOS, or Windows 10 via the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).

name: saleor
description: Saleor Core: the high performance, composable, headless commerce API.
summary:
Saleor is a GraphQL-native, API-first e-commerce platform designed for scalable, composable, and headless commerce. It provides a technology-agnostic backend where APIs are the sole mechanism for interaction, configuration, and extension. 

Main capabilities include a native multi-channel architecture supporting multi-currency, multi-language, and multi-warehouse operations, alongside robust product and content management, flexible order and customer tracking, a promotion engine, payment orchestration, and advanced cart management. Extensibility is achieved through webhooks, attributes, metadata, apps, subscription queries, API extensions, and dashboard iframes, separating custom logic from the core to improve reliability, performance, and independent scalability. 

Intended for developers, enterprises, and high-traffic brands requiring high availability, the platform integrates with a decoupled user-friendly dashboard (`saleor-dashboard`) and sample storefronts built with technologies like Next.js, React, TypeScript, GraphQL, and Tailwind CSS. Deployment options include Docker Compose, Saleor Cloud, and a CLI tool (`@saleor/cli`), with code linting maintained via Ruff.

name: jdk
description: JDK main-line development https://openjdk.org/projects/jdk
summary: The JDK repository provides the source code and development materials for the Java Development Kit, managed by the OpenJDK Community. Its primary purpose is to develop, build, and maintain the JDK. The repository directs users to comprehensive building instructions available in HTML and Markdown formats within the documentation. Intended users include developers and contributors participating in the OpenJDK ecosystem. Project resources, community information, and issue tracking are hosted externally via openjdk.org and bugs.openjdk.org.

name: rxdb
description: The local-first database that runs on every JS runtime and replicates with your existing backend - no vendor, no lock-in - https://rxdb.info/
summary:
RxDB is a fast, local-first, reactive NoSQL database designed for JavaScript applications. It enables developers to query current database states as well as subscribe to state changes on queries, documents, or individual fields, making it well-suited for realtime UI-based applications and multiplayer environments. 

The project features a flexible storage layer supporting pluggable engines such as LocalStorage, IndexedDB, OPFS, LokiJS, Dexie.js, SQLite, FoundationDB, DenoKV, and in-memory storage. It also provides a built-in replication sync engine with plugins for GraphQL, CouchDB, Websocket, WebRTC, Supabase, Firestore, NATS, and Google Drive. 

Intended for frontend and full-stack JavaScript developers, RxDB runs across diverse environments including web browsers, Node.js, React Native, Capacitor, NativeScript, Flutter, and Electron. Notable technologies and capabilities include schema validation, key compression, migration, encryption, conflict handling, and CRDT support.

name: TelegramGroup
description: 2026最新悄咪咪收集的10000+个Telegram群合集，附全网最有趣好用的机器人BOT🤖【dianbaodaohang.com】
summary:
This project is a comprehensive Telegram directory and navigation guide featuring over 10,000 curated Telegram groups, channels, and bots. It provides categorized indexes and functional links covering search tools, group and channel management utilities, media downloaders, translation bots, AI and ChatGPT helpers, cryptocurrency wallets, financial resources, VPN and proxy configurations, RSS feeds, and official Telegram resources. 

Designed for users seeking to explore and utilize the Telegram ecosystem, the repository includes usage tutorials—such as bypassing sensitive content restrictions on iOS clients, troubleshooting verification issues with +86 numbers, and requesting Telegram APIs. It also aggregates popular Chinese-language communities spanning programming languages, tech discussions, Apple and Android ecosystems, and financial markets. Notable technologies and tools referenced throughout the navigation include Telegram API, MTProto, Node.js, Python, RSS, and various proxy protocols like Shadowsocks and Clash.

name: backtrader
description: Python Backtesting library for trading strategies
summary:
Backtrader is a feature-rich live trading and backtesting platform written in Python. It is designed for quantitative traders and developers looking to test, analyze, and execute trading strategies. 

Main capabilities include support for multiple data feeds, multiple strategies, and multiple timeframes simultaneously, with integrated resampling and replaying. It offers built-in indicators, support for *TA-Lib* indicators, and straightforward custom indicator development. The platform features integrated broker simulation supporting various order types (such as *Market*, *Limit*, *Stop*, *OCO*, and bracket orders), slippage, volume filling strategies, commission schemes, analyzers (like Sharpe Ratio and SQN), automated staking via sizers, schedulers, trading calendars, and plotting via *matplotlib*. Data can be sourced from CSV files, online sources (including Yahoo Finance), *pandas*, and *blaze*. Live trading and data feeds are supported for *Interactive Brokers* (via *IbPy*), *Visual Chart*, and *Oanda*. 

The platform supports Python >= 3.2, *pypy*, and *pypy3*, and is self-contained with minimal external dependencies.

name: AeroSpace
description: AeroSpace is an i3-like tiling window manager for macOS
summary:
AeroSpace is an i3-inspired, tiling window manager for macOS designed for advanced users and developers. Its core purpose is to provide a fast, keyboard-centric workflow with proper multi-monitor support and rapid workspace switching without animations. 

Main capabilities include a tree paradigm for window management, custom emulation of virtual workspaces to bypass native macOS Spaces limitations, a CLI-first interface with manpages and shell completion, and plain-text configuration (TOML). It utilizes macOS public accessibility APIs and avoids requiring users to disable System Integrity Protection (SIP).

Targeted at developers and power users seeking a practical, text-configured window management solution, AeroSpace minimizes GUI use and avoids complex visual styling features like animations or window borders. Notable technologies used include Swift, Xcode, Homebrew for installation, and the macOS Accessibility API (`AXUIElement`).

name: chalk
description: 🖍 Terminal string styling done right
summary:
Chalk is a zero-dependency terminal string styling library designed for Node.js and browser environments. It provides an expressive, chainable, and nestable API to color and style terminal output. 

Main capabilities include automatic color support detection, support for 256 colors and Truecolor (16 million colors) via RGB, HEX, and ANSI-256 models, custom theme definition, string substitution compatibility, and separate configurations for standard output and standard error streams. It supports a wide array of text modifiers, foreground colors, background colors, and underline styles.

Intended users are JavaScript and TypeScript developers building command-line tools or terminal-based applications who require reliable, performant, and feature-complete string formatting.

name: chinese-programmer-wrong-pronunciation
description: 中国程序员容易发音错误的单词
summary:
This project provides a comprehensive reference list of English vocabulary, technical terms, software tools, and programming languages commonly mispronounced by Chinese programmers. Its purpose is to correct pronunciation errors by supplying British and American phonetic symbols, audio links, common mispronunciations, and Chinese definitions for terms such as `access`, `Apache`, `Array`, `Git`, `Kubernetes`, `Nginx`, `SQL`, and `Vite`. 

Intended for Chinese-speaking developers, software engineers, and technical professionals, the repository aims to improve professional communication. Ecosystem tools provided include a web-based word list, a Chromium browser extension for real-time pronunciation lookup without page navigation, and a companion iOS application.

name: maui
