description: .NET MAUI is the .NET Multi-platform App UI, a framework for building native device applications spanning mobile, tablet, and desktop.
summary:
.NET Multi-platform App UI (.NET MAUI) is a cross-platform framework designed for developers to create native mobile and desktop applications from a single shared codebase. Evolving from Xamarin.Forms, the framework enables the development of apps targeting Android, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and Windows. 

Project capabilities include building high-performance applications using a unified SDK, base class libraries, and a toolchain. Developers can utilize Visual Studio productivity tools and emulators to accelerate the development process. The framework supports integration with modern ecosystems and toolkits, including the Syncfusion Toolkit for .NET MAUI, the .NET MAUI Community Toolkit, and the MVVM Toolkit.

Intended users are software developers and engineers building applications that target a wide range of modern mobile and desktop devices. Notable technologies used within the ecosystem include C#, XAML, .NET, and Visual Studio.

name: matplotlib
description: matplotlib: plotting with Python
summary:
Matplotlib is a comprehensive Python library designed for creating static, animated, and interactive visualizations. It produces publication-quality figures across various hardcopy formats and interactive environments. 

The library's main capabilities allow it to be utilized in Python scripts, Python and IPython shells, web application servers, and multiple graphical user interface toolkits. It serves developers, data scientists, and researchers seeking robust plotting tools in Python ecosystems.

name: IOPaint
description: Image inpainting tool powered by SOTA AI Model. Remove any unwanted object, defect, people from your pictures or erase and replace(powered by stable diffusion) any thing on your pictures.
summary:
IOPaint is a free, open-source, and fully self-hosted inpainting and outpainting tool powered by state-of-the-art AI models. Designed for users seeking advanced image editing capabilities via a web UI, command-line interface, or 1-click installer, it supports CPU, GPU, and Apple Silicon hardware. 

The tool utilizes various erase models (such as LaMa) to remove unwanted objects, defects, watermarks, and people from images, alongside diffusion models (including Stable Diffusion, Stable Diffusion XL, Realistic Vision, DreamShaper, BrushNet, PowerPaintV2, AnyText, and Paint-by-Example) for object replacement, text drawing, and outpainting. Additionally, IOPaint features integrated plugins for interactive object segmentation using Segment Anything, background removal via RemoveBG and Anime Segmentation, super-resolution with RealESRGAN, and face restoration using GFPGAN and RestoreFormer, accompanied by a built-in FileManager for browsing and saving outputs.

name: eng-practices
description: Google's Engineering Practices documentation
summary: The Google Engineering Practices Documentation repository provides public access to Google's generalized engineering best practices developed across various languages and projects. The primary content consists of Google's Code Review Guidelines, which are divided into The Code Reviewer's Guide and The Change Author's Guide. These documents aim to benefit open-source projects and external organizations by sharing collective software development experience. The intended users are software developers, code reviewers, and change authors seeking guidance on effective code review and engineering workflows. Distinctive internal terminology used throughout the documentation includes "CL" (changelist, referring to a change, patch, or pull request) and "LGTM" ("Looks Good to Me," used by reviewers to approve a changelist).

name: sops
description: Simple and flexible tool for managing secrets
summary: SOPS (Secrets OPerationS) is an editor of encrypted files that supports YAML, JSON, ENV, INI, and BINARY formats. It encrypts data using AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, HuaweiCloud KMS, age, and PGP. Originally launched at Mozilla in 2015, SOPS is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox project.

name: octotree
description: GitHub on steroids
summary: Octotree is a proprietary browser extension designed to enhance GitHub code review and exploration by providing a file tree sidebar. Available for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Brave, and Opera, the extension improves navigation for developers working within GitHub repositories. This repository contains the old source code of a very limited version of Octotree, with complete copyright owned by the Octotree team.

name: jaeger
description: CNCF Jaeger, a Distributed Tracing Platform
summary:
Jaeger is an open-source distributed tracing system originally created by Uber Technologies and hosted as a graduated project by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). Its purpose is to monitor and troubleshoot microservices-based distributed systems through end-to-end distributed tracing. 

Main capabilities include collecting traces, processing query requests, managing storage backends, and providing a web-based user interface. It integrates with the OpenTelemetry SDK, accepting traces via OTLP over gRPC and HTTP. 

Intended users include developers, operators, and organizations running cloud-native applications who need to trace requests across complex service architectures for development debugging or production monitoring. 

Notable technologies and components used within the ecosystem include Docker, Go, OpenTelemetry Collector, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Apache Cassandra, and ClickHouse.

name: vorssaint-utils
description: Free and open-source macOS menu bar toolkit.
summary:
Vorssaint is a free, open-source, local-first macOS menu bar utility designed to replace multiple paid Mac apps. It consolidates a wide array of tools into a single customizable hub that lets users install, reorder, or completely disable individual features as needed.

Main capabilities include:
- **Audio & Sound:** Per-app volume control with volume boosting past 100%, per-app output routing, output switching, and microphone management.
- **System Monitoring:** CPU, GPU, memory, and temperature trackers, history graphs, fan control, customizable menu bar readouts, network traffic stats, and system alerts.
- **Windows & Dock:** Live-preview app/window switchers, window snapping layouts, Dock previews, window management shortcuts, and quit-protection prompts.
- **Keyboard & Mouse:** Text snippet expansion, smooth and linear scrolling, mouse acceleration controls, focus-follows-mouse, and customized key/mouse button bindings.
- **Clipboard, Files & Links:** Clipboard history with search/pins, plain-text pasting, a temporary file/text shelf, Finder shortcuts, URL cleaning, and disk image installers.
- **Everyday Productivity Tools:** A simulated or native Dynamic Island integration, AI agent monitoring (Claude, Codex, OpenCode), a command bar search field, a radial menu, a markdown scratchpad, and a screen-cleaning mode.
- **Capture & Create:** Screenshots, screen recording, local text recognition (OCR), QR code reading, color picker, and local media/video conversion tools.
- **App Management:** An application updater, cache cleaner, app uninstaller, Homebrew manager, and port manager.
- **Energy & Display:** Keep-awake timers, display brightness adjustments, HDR headroom controls, and Bluetooth sleep toggles.

The project is built for macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer running on Apple Silicon, requires no user accounts or unnecessary telemetry, and is licensed under the GPL-3.0-or-later license.

name: lens
description: Lens - The way the world runs Kubernetes
summary:
Lens is a Kubernetes IDE developed by Mirantis designed for developers and DevOps engineers. It provides an intuitive context-aware user interface for managing and troubleshooting Kubernetes workloads, boosting team productivity, and supporting cloud-native development. Lens serves over 1 million users globally, ranging from startups to enterprises. 

The repository contains the legacy source code for the retired open source version of Lens Desktop on its 'master' branch, released under the MIT license. While Lens Desktop remains actively developed and supported by Mirantis, contributions to the core product are now made through extensions using the Lens extension API.

name: RedisDesktopManager
summary: RESP.app (formerly RedisDesktopManager) is a GUI for Redis designed to offer the Redis community an improved developer experience and increased productivity when developing with Redis. The repository provides a graphical user interface application for managing and interacting with Redis databases.

name: ds4
description: DeepSeek 4 Flash and PRO local inference engine for Metal, CUDA and ROCm
summary:
DwarfStar is a small native inference engine designed to run selected large language models efficiently on consumer and personal hardware. Its primary target models include DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 PRO, GLM 5.2 and 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and Qwen3.8 Flash Next, supporting both text and experimental vision capabilities. 

The project is purpose-built and self-contained rather than functioning as a general GGUF runner, relying on specific GGUF files and built-in project tools for imatrix, quantization, quality, and speed evaluations. Supported hardware includes Apple Silicon Macs (via Metal), NVIDIA CUDA systems (such as DGX Spark and Ada Lovelace multi-GPU setups), and AMD ROCm on Strix Halo systems. It incorporates advanced memory and execution strategies such as SSD streaming for running models larger than available RAM, RDMA tensor parallelism across multiple machines, pipeline parallelism, compressed KV caches, and optional speculative decoding (MTP).

Designed for developers, researchers, and power users, DwarfStar provides a command-line interface, a native interactive coding agent (`ds4-agent`), an HTTP server (`ds4-server`), and integrated capability regression testing (`ds4-eval`). The software adapts kernels and quantization layouts from the `llama.cpp` and GGML ecosystem.

name: phoenix
description: Peace of mind from prototype to production
summary: Phoenix is a web development framework designed to provide rapid prototyping and production-ready performance. Its main capabilities include building rich, interactive web applications and APIs, supporting real-time features, and offering project scaffolding via the `phx.new` Mix task. Intended for developers building web applications, the framework integrates with technologies including Elixir, Phoenix.js, and the Mix build tool. It is distributed under the MIT License.

name: Sentinel
description: A powerful flow control component enabling reliability, resilience and monitoring for microservices. (面向云原生微服务的高可用流控防护组件)
summary:
Sentinel is a flow control and reliability framework designed to guarantee reliability and resilience for microservices. Its core capabilities include flow control, traffic shaping, concurrency limiting, circuit breaking, and system adaptive overload protection. It also features real-time monitoring of single nodes and clusters, extensible rule management via SPI, and a dashboard for real-time configuration and metrics visualization. 

Sentinel is intended for developers and architects building distributed systems and microservices who need traffic governance and fault tolerance. It provides out-of-the-box integrations for common frameworks and libraries such as Spring Cloud, gRPC, Apache Dubbo, Quarkus, Spring WebFlux, and Reactor. The project offers polyglot support with native implementations in Java, Go, C++, and Rust.

name: skyvern
description: Automate browser based workflows with AI
summary:
Skyvern is an open-source automation platform designed to execute browser-based workflows using Large Language Models (LLMs) and computer vision. Rather than relying on brittle, code-defined XPath selectors or traditional DOM parsing, Skyvern utilizes Vision LLMs and a swarm of autonomous agents to visually comprehend websites, plan navigation, and reliably complete multi-step actions despite layout changes.

Main capabilities include AI-powered page interactions, structured data extraction, file downloading, form filling, automated authentication with multi-factor authentication (TOTP) support, and a no-code workflow builder. It provides Python and TypeScript SDKs extending Playwright with natural language page commands (`page.act`, `page.extract`, `page.validate`, `page.prompt`), as well as browser tunneling and remote debugging integration (`CDP-connect`).

Intended users include technical and non-technical professionals seeking to automate repetitive browser tasks such as invoice downloading, job applications, form submissions, and insurance quote retrievals. Notable technologies integrated or supported include Playwright, Python, TypeScript, Docker, PostgreSQL, SQLite, liteLLM, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and major model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Gemini, Azure, and Ollama.

name: distroless
description: 🥑  Language focused docker images, minus the operating system.
summary:
The Distroless project provides minimal container images that contain exclusively an application and its runtime dependencies, omitting package managers, shells, and standard Linux distribution programs. Designed for secure production environments by improving vulnerability scanner signal-to-noise ratios and reducing image sizes (with static images starting around 2 MiB), the project targets developers and organizations containerizing applications. 

The images are based on Debian 13 (trixie) and are available in various language runtimes and configurations, including Java, Node.js, Python, and static variants. Notable technologies used to build and verify the project include Bazel, Docker, and Cosign for keyless image signing. Distroless images can be integrated via multi-stage Docker builds or Bazel container rules (`rules_distroless` and `rules_oci`). The project also provides specialized tags such as `nonroot` for running securely without root privileges and `debug` variants containing a BusyBox shell for troubleshooting.

name: winboat
description: Run Windows apps on 🐧 Linux with ✨ seamless integration
summary:
WinBoat is an Electron-based desktop application designed for Linux users to run Windows applications and full Windows desktops with seamless integration. The software uses a containerized approach, running Windows as a virtual machine inside a Docker or Podman container via tools like dockur/windows. It communicates with the guest environment using the WinBoat Guest Server and leverages FreeRDP with Windows's RemoteApp protocol to composite applications as native OS-level windows. 

Main capabilities include automated installation workflows, local filesystem integration (mounting the Linux home directory inside Windows), smartcard passthrough, and resource monitoring. The project is intended for Linux users seeking to run Windows applications natively within their desktop environment. Notable technologies used in its development and execution include Electron, Docker, Podman, FreeRDP, Go, and Bun.

name: anubis
description: Weighs the soul of incoming HTTP requests to stop AI crawlers
summary: Anubis is a lightweight Web AI Firewall Utility designed to protect upstream web resources and communities from scraper bots and AI company request floods by issuing connection challenges. Positioned as an alternative to Cloudflare for origin protection, it allows administrators to configure bot policy definitions to explicitly allowlist specific traffic, such as known good bots.

name: vibe-coding-cn
summary:
Vibe Coding 指南是一个将想法通过 AI 结对编程转化为现实的终极工作站与方法论项目。其核心目的是提供一套以规划驱动和模块化为基础的开发流程，帮助开发者避免 AI 失控并高效构建项目。

主要capabilities包括提供成体系的提示词工具链（如用于约束 AI 行为边界的 system_prompts、涵盖需求澄清与计划执行的 coding_prompts）、支持 Excel 与 Markdown 互转的 prompts-library 工具、本地快照备份脚本，以及完整的文档、教程和项目架构模板。项目还整合了多语言入口与丰富的外部提示词及技能库资源。

该项目intended users主要是希望利用 AI 进行高效辅助编程、应用开发或游戏开发的开发者、工程师以及技术爱好者。

 notable technologies and tools mentioned include Claude Opus 4.5, gpt-5.1-codex.1-codex, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Visual Studio Code, Neovim, LazyVim, Warp, Ollama, Mermaid Chart, and Docker-like terminal utilities such as tmux.

name: marimo
description: A reactive notebook for Python — run reproducible experiments, query with SQL, execute as a script, deploy as an app, and version with git. Stored as pure Python. All in a modern, AI-native editor.
summary:
marimo is a reactive Python notebook environment designed to be reproducible, git-friendly, and executable as pure Python scripts or deployable web applications. It aims to replace traditional JSON scratchpads by offering a deterministic, reactive execution model where running a cell or interacting with UI elements automatically updates dependent cells and state without hidden variables. 

Main capabilities include synchronized interactive UI components like sliders and tables, built-in SQL querying, interactive dataframe filtering, native package management, dynamic markdown, and AI-native coding assistance. It is intended for data scientists, developers, researchers, and educators who work with Python and data visualization. Notable technologies integrated into the project include Python, SQL, WASM, pytest, Ruff, and integrations with major editors such as VS Code, PyCharm, and Neovim.

name: system-design-notes
description: Notes of the book System Desgin Interview - An Insider's Guide
summary:
This repository contains study notes based on "System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide" (Volumes 1 and 2 by Alex Xu). The project serves as a structured educational resource for software engineers, developers, and technical candidates preparing for system design interviews. It covers fundamental scaling concepts, back-of-the-envelope estimations, and a standard system design framework, alongside architectural breakdowns for various real-world applications and services. 

Specific system designs detailed across the chapters include rate limiters, consistent hashing, distributed key-value stores, unique ID generators (such as Snowflake), URL shorteners, web crawlers, notification systems, news feeds, chat systems, search autocomplete, YouTube, Google Drive, proximity services, nearby friends, Google Maps, distributed message queues, metrics monitoring and alerting systems, ad click event aggregation, hotel reservation systems, distributed email services, S3-like object storage, real-time gaming leaderboards, payment systems, digital wallets, and stock exchanges. The notes also provide supplementary technical resources and references citing architectures from major platforms like Amazon Dynamo, Apache Cassandra, Google BigTable, Discord, Slack, and Netflix.

name: chartdb
description: Database diagrams editor that allows you to visualize and design your DB with a single query.
summary:
ChartDB is an open-source, web-based database diagramming editor designed to instantly visualize database schemas, customize diagrams, and export SQL scripts without requiring installations or database passwords. 

Main capabilities include instant schema import using single smart queries that retrieve database schemas as JSON, AI-powered export for DDL script generation to facilitate database migrations across different dialects, and interactive schema editing. 

Intended users include developers, database administrators, and teams seeking efficient ways to visualize, document, and migrate database structures. Supported databases comprise PostgreSQL (including Supabase and Timescale), MySQL, SQL Server, MariaDB, SQLite (including Cloudflare D1), CockroachDB, and ClickHouse. 

Notable technologies used in the project include Node.js (`npm`), Docker, OpenAI API, and custom LLM inference endpoints (such as vLLM). The software is released under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0).

name: magic-wormhole
description: get things from one computer to another, safely
summary:
Magic Wormhole is a Python library and command-line tool (`wormhole`) designed to safely transfer arbitrary-sized files, directories, and short text pieces between computers. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Endpoints are connected using short, human-pronounceable, single-use "wormhole codes" generated by the sending machine and entered on the receiving machine.
- Supports tab-completion on codewords for the receiving side.
- Relies on a separate mailbox server and transit relay for connection facilitation.

**Intended Users:**
- Users and developers needing a secure, straightforward method to transfer data between two computers.

**Notable Technologies:**
- Written in Python (compatible with Python 3.10 through 3.12).
- Distributed under the MIT license.

name: NekoBoxForAndroid
description: NekoBox for Android / sing-box / universal proxy toolchain for Android
summary: NekoBox for Android is a universal proxy toolchain and Android GUI application powered by sing-box, requiring Android 5.0 (API 21) or higher. Designed for users seeking advanced network routing capabilities on Android, the application supports a wide array of proxy protocols including SOCKS, HTTP(S), SSH, Shadowsocks, VMess, Trojan, VLESS, AnyTLS, ShadowTLS, TUIC, Hysteria 1/2, WireGuard, and plugin-supported protocols such as Trojan-Go, NaïveProxy, and Mieru. Additionally, it parses popular subscription formats like Shadowsocks, ClashMeta, v2rayN, and sing-box outbounds to resolve node information while ignoring diversion rules. Built using core technologies and UI concepts derived from SagerNet, sing-box, shadowsocks-android, and Yacd-meta, NekoBox for Android serves as a comprehensive client solution for managing and utilizing diverse proxy networks.

name: Self-Hosting-Guide
description: Self-Hosting Guide. Learn all about  locally hosting (on premises & private web servers) and managing software applications by yourself or your organization. Including Cloud, LLMs, WireGuard, Automation, Home Assistant, and Networking.
summary:
The **Self Hosting Guide** is a comprehensive reference repository designed to help users establish and manage private, on-premises servers and self-hosted environments. It provides curated lists of software applications, architectures, hardware platforms, and management tools as privacy-friendly alternatives to commercial Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) subscriptions.

The project covers a wide variety of domains and capabilities, including:
- **Containerization & Orchestration:** Docker, Docker Compose, Podman, Kubernetes, Portainer, and Nomad.
- **Networking & Remote Access:** WireGuard, Tailscale, Netmaker, PiVPN, OpenVPN, SSH, and reverse proxy solutions like Nginx Proxy Manager.
- **Storage & File Management:** Nextcloud, MinIO Object Storage, Synology, ZFS, Btrfs, and various backup utilities.
- **Databases:** Relational and NoSQL solutions including PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, and Redis.
- **AI & Large Language Models (LLMs):** Tools for running local LLMs and AI services, such as llama.cpp, LocalAI, Ollama, and ChatGPT UI kits.
- **Home & Media Automation:** Home Assistant, Homebridge, ESPHome, Plex, Jellyfin, and various video surveillance solutions.
- **Development & DevOps:** Git hosting (Gitea, GitLab), CI/CD platforms (Drone, Woodpecker), and configuration management systems like Ansible.

Intended for homelab enthusiasts, developers, systems administrators, and privacy-conscious users, the guide provides detailed setup guides, tutorials, and ecosystem classifications for both single-board computers like the Raspberry Pi and enterprise-grade hardware.

name: NLP-progress
description: Repository to track the progress in Natural Language Processing (NLP), including the datasets and the current state-of-the-art for the most common NLP tasks.
summary:
This repository tracks the progress of Natural Language Processing (NLP) by providing an overview of state-of-the-art (SOTA) results and benchmark datasets across common and traditional NLP tasks. The project covers languages including English, Vietnamese, Hindi, Chinese, French, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, Korean, Nepali, Bengali, Persian, Turkish, German, and Arabic. 

The main capabilities include tracking performance on tasks such as automatic speech recognition, dependency parsing, intent detection, slot filling, machine translation, named entity recognition, part-of-speech tagging, question answering, sentiment analysis, summarization, and language modeling, among others. The repository is intended for researchers and practitioners looking for a quick reference on NLP benchmarks, datasets, evaluation metrics, and pointers to public leaderboards and code implementations. Structured data can be exported into a machine-readable JSON format, and the documentation site can be built locally using Jekyll.

name: chi
description: lightweight, idiomatic and composable router for building Go HTTP services
summary:
`chi` is a lightweight, idiomatic, and composable HTTP router designed for building Go services and large REST APIs. Built on the Go standard library's `net/http` and `context` packages, it features 100% compatibility with standard handlers and introduces zero external dependencies. 

The project focuses on maintainability, modularity, and developer productivity by utilizing a Patricia Radix trie routing tree. Key capabilities include sub-router mounting, inline middlewares, route groups, URL parameter parsing, and context value chaining for request-scoped timeouts and cancellations. It also includes an optional `middleware` package providing utilities like logging, rate limiting, compression, request ID injection, panic recovery, and secure client IP resolution. Additionally, subpackages like `docgen` facilitate automatic documentation generation from source routes. 

Intended for Go developers building robust HTTP servers, microservices, and REST APIs, `chi` is optimized for structuring large codebases into manageable, modular components.

name: MaxKB
description: 🔥 MaxKB is an open-source platform for building enterprise-grade agents.  强大易用的开源企业级智能体平台。
summary:
MaxKB (Max Knowledge Brain) is an open-source platform designed for building enterprise-grade AI agents, intelligent customer service solutions, corporate internal knowledge bases, and academic or educational systems. 

Main capabilities include a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline supporting direct document uploads, automated online document crawling, text splitting, and vectorization to reduce large model hallucinations. It features an agentic workflow engine with a function library and MCP tool-use capabilities for complex business scenarios, zero-coding integration into third-party systems, model-agnostic support for private and public models (such as DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and MiniMax), and native multimodal support for text, images, audio, and video. 

Intended users include enterprises, developers, and organizations seeking to integrate smart Q&A and AI workflow orchestration into their business systems. The technology stack utilizes Vue.js for the frontend, Python with Django for the backend, LangChain for the LLM framework, and PostgreSQL with pgvector for data storage.

name: yjs
description: Shared data types for building collaborative software
summary:
Yjs is a CRDT (Conflict-free Replicated Data Type) framework that exposes internal data structures as shared types like `Map`, `Array`, `Text`, `XmlFragment`, and `XmlElement`. These types enable automatic change distribution and conflict-free merging among peers. 

The framework is network-agnostic and supports P2P setups, offline editing, version snapshots, undo/redo management via `Y.UndoManager`, and shared cursors. It features built-in bindings and utilities for rich text editors and frameworks such as ProseMirror, Quill, CodeMirror, Monaco, Slate, React, Vue, and Svelte, alongside multiple connection and persistence providers (including WebSockets, WebRTC, IndexedDB, and MongoDB). Alternative language ports exist in Rust (`yrs`), Python, Ruby, C#, Swift, and Go.

Intended for developers building real-time collaborative web applications, document editors, and decentralized knowledge bases, Yjs scales well with an unlimited number of users and large documents. The codebase is distributed under the MIT license.

name: ratatui
description: A Rust crate for cooking up terminal user interfaces (TUIs) 👨‍🍳🐀 https://ratatui.rs
summary: Ratatui is a Rust crate designed for building terminal user interfaces (TUIs). It provides a simple and flexible library to create text-based interfaces for command-line applications, dashboards, and interactive console programs. Originally forked from the `tui-rs` crate, Ratatui targets Rust developers looking to construct console applications using widgets and frames, with integration support for tools like `cargo-generate` for rapid project scaffolding.

name: Iosevka
description: Versatile typeface for code, from code.
summary:
Iosevka is an open-source sans-serif and slab-serif typeface family offering both monospace and quasi-proportional designs, specifically tailored for writing code, terminal usage, and preparing technical documents. 

The project provides multiple subfamilies, including 6 monospace variants across 9 weights (Thin to Heavy), 2 widths (Normal and Extended), and 3 slopes (Upright, Italic, and Oblique), as well as 2 quasi-proportional subfamilies named Aile and Etoile. Key capabilities include extensive character support across hundreds of languages, customizable stylistic sets, character variants, and built-in support for ligatures and language-specific ligation sets through OpenType features. 

Intended for developers, programmers, and technical users, the typeface can be installed via GitHub releases, package managers on major operating systems (including macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD), or built from source.

name: spiderfoot
description: SpiderFoot automates OSINT for threat intelligence and mapping your attack surface.
summary:
SpiderFoot is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) automation tool designed for both offensive reconnaissance (such as red team exercises and penetration testing) and defensive exposure analysis. It enables users to target entities including IP addresses, domain names, hostnames, network subnets, ASNs, email addresses, phone numbers, usernames, person names, and Bitcoin addresses. 

The application features over 200 integrated modules utilizing a publisher/subscriber model for maximum data extraction—such as subdomain enumeration, threat intelligence queries, dark web searches, social media profiling, and bucket scraping—along with a YAML-configurable correlation engine featuring 37 pre-defined rules. It provides both a web-based user interface via an embedded web server and a command-line interface, with support for CSV, JSON, and GEXF exports, custom SQLite querying, and Tor integration. 

Intended for security professionals and researchers, SpiderFoot is written in Python 3.7+ and licensed under the MIT License. It also includes capabilities to invoke external tools like Nmap, Whatweb, DNSTwist, and CMSeeK, and supports Docker-based deployments.

name: core
description: An Emacs framework for the stubborn martian hacker
summary:
Doom Emacs is a configuration framework for GNU Emacs tailored for users seeking high performance, stability, reproducibility, and a modern aesthetic. It provides a modular organizational structure, a declarative package management system powered by straight.el, an extensible command-line interface, and optional Vim emulation via evil-mode. 

Intended for Emacs enthusiasts and power users looking for curated opinions and sane defaults without excessive overhead, Doom supports LSP integration (via lsp-mode or eglot), project search and management utilities (powered by ripgrep and ivy or helm), isolated workspaces, and extensive programming language and development tool configurations. 

Key technologies used include GNU Emacs, Git, ripgrep, and fd. Prerequisites require GNU Emacs (versions 27.1 through 31.1), Git, and ripgrep.

name: livewire
description: A full-stack framework for Laravel that takes the pain out of building dynamic UIs.
summary: Livewire is a full-stack framework for Laravel that enables developers to build dynamic user interface components using PHP without needing to write extensive JavaScript. Designed for Laravel developers, the framework streamlines frontend development by keeping application logic on the backend while maintaining reactive interfaces. The project utilizes PHP, JavaScript, Composer, NPM, and ChromeDriver for local development and testing.

name: MaaAssistantArknights
description: 《明日方舟》小助手，全日常一键长草！| A one-click tool for the daily tasks of Arknights, supporting all clients.
summary:
MAA (Maa Assistant Arknights) is an automated assistant tool for the game Arknights designed to complete daily tasks automatically. Its main capabilities include combat automation with drop recognition and uploads (supporting Penguin Stats and YiTuLiu), smart infrastructure roster scheduling and shift changes, automated public recruitment with high-star and high-qualification recognition, operator and material inventory exports, friend interactions, credit store management, and rogue-like automated farming. It also supports automated combat via JSON operation scripts (Copilot) and runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS (including a CLI mode).

Intended users include Arknights players seeking to automate routine tasks and developers looking to integrate automation capabilities or build custom workflows.

Notable technologies and libraries used include C++20, OpenCV, PaddleOCR, FastDeploy, ONNX Runtime, and DirectML for GPU acceleration. The project provides comprehensive API integration interfaces and sample bindings for C, Python, Java, Rust, Golang, Dart, TypeScript, and Woolang.

name: v86
description: x86 PC emulator and x86-to-wasm JIT, running in the browser
summary:
v86 is an x86-compatible hardware and CPU emulator designed to run machine code inside web browsers and Node.js environments by translating it to WebAssembly modules at runtime. It emulates an x86-compatible CPU (Pentium 4 level with SSE3 support, excluding 64-bit and multicore extensions), an FPU powered by Berkeley SoftFloat, a VGA card with SVGA and Bochs VBE extensions, an IDE disk controller, a PCI network card, SoundBlaster 16, virtio devices, and standard legacy hardware like PS/2 keyboards and mice, programmable interval timers, and interrupt controllers. 

Intended for developers and enthusiasts looking to run legacy or modern operating systems—such as various Linux distributions, FreeDOS, MS-DOS, Haiku, KolibriOS, and Windows versions ranging from 1.01 to 2000—directly within web technologies. 

The project is built using WebAssembly, Rust, and JavaScript/TypeScript. It can be embedded via `libv86.js` or through an official npm package (`v86`), supporting local development and testing workflows via Make, Docker, and Dev Containers.

name: oh-my-posh
description: The most customisable and low-latency cross platform/shell prompt renderer
summary: Oh My Posh is a cross-platform, highly customizable, and extensible prompt theme engine for any shell. It serves as a shell-agnostic and platform-agnostic prompt utility designed to be fast and configurable. Its main capabilities include support for secondary prompts, right prompts, and transient prompts. The project targets developers and command-line users seeking to personalize and enhance their shell environments. Notable technologies and languages associated with the project include Go, PowerShell, and various shell environments.

name: deepface
description: A Lightweight Face Recognition and Facial Attribute Analysis (Age, Gender, Emotion and Race) Library for Python
summary:
DeepFace is a lightweight Python-based face recognition and facial attribute analysis framework. Designed for developers and researchers, it wraps state-of-the-art face recognition and detection models to handle end-to-end pipelines including face detection, alignment, normalization, representation, verification, and database-backed search.

**Main Capabilities:**
- **Face Verification & Recognition:** 1:1 verification and 1:N folder or database-backed search (supporting backends like PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Neo4j, pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, and Milvus with approximate nearest neighbor support).
- **Facial Attribute Analysis:** Predicts age, gender, emotion, and race/ethnicity, alongside face anti-spoofing detection.
- **Vector Embeddings:** Extracts multi-dimensional vector embeddings and computes similarity metrics (Cosine, Euclidean, Euclidean L2, Angular).
- **Real-Time Stream & API:** Provides webcam-based real-time video analysis as well as a REST and gRPC API (plus Docker and cloud integration).

**Notable Technologies:**
- **Models:** VGG-Face, FaceNet, OpenFace, DeepFace, DeepID, ArcFace, Dlib, SFace, GhostFaceNet, and Buffalo_L.
- **Detectors:** OpenCV, SSD, Dlib, MTCNN, Fast MTCNN, RetinaFace, MediaPipe, YOLO, YuNet, and CenterFace.
- **Backends/Runtimes:** TensorFlow, PyTorch, and ONNX Runtime.

name: compose-samples
description: Official Jetpack Compose samples.
summary:
The Jetpack Compose Samples repository contains a collection of individual Android Studio projects designed to help developers learn Jetpack Compose. Intended for Android developers, the repository provides hands-on demonstrations of various use cases, complexity levels, and APIs through sample applications such as JetNews (a blog post viewer), Jetchat (a chat app focusing on UI state patterns and Material 3), Jetsnack (a snack ordering app with custom design systems), Jetcaster (a podcast app featuring Redux-style architecture and dynamic themes), Reply (an email client demonstrating adaptive design and Material 3), and JetLagged (a sleep tracker showcasing custom layouts and graphics). 

The samples highlight notable capabilities including custom layouts, animations, dynamic theming, downloadable fonts, adaptive UIs for phones, tablets, foldables, desktops, wear, and TV devices. Key technologies and libraries utilized across the projects include Jetpack Compose, Material Design 3, Architecture Components (Navigation, Fragments, LiveData, ViewModel), Coroutines, Room, WindowInsets, and Window Size Classes.

name: notable
description: The Markdown-based note-taking app that doesn't suck.
summary:
Notable is a markdown-based note-taking application designed to avoid vendor lock-in by storing notes and attachments directly on the local disk. Intended for users seeking a lightweight, extensible note-taking solution with no proprietary formats, the project features a powerful Markdown editor that supports GitHub Flavored Markdown, KaTeX expressions, and Mermaid diagrams. 

Main capabilities include a VS Code-derived editor with multi-cursors, syntax highlighting, and a minimap, alongside a split editor, a multi-note editor for bulk actions, a dark theme, a minimalist Zen mode, indefinitely nestable tags, Evernote note importing, and global search and replace. The application is keyboard-friendly and utilizes standard files that can be edited externally, synchronized via services like Dropbox, or managed with Git. Notable integrates technologies such as KaTeX and Mermaid, and provides a customizable user interface through built-in Devtools.

name: fasthttp
description: Fast HTTP package for Go. Tuned for high performance. Zero memory allocations in hot paths. Up to 10x faster than net/http
summary:
Fasthttp is a high-performance HTTP implementation for Go, designed specifically for high-throughput edge cases where servers and clients must handle thousands of small to medium requests per second with consistent low-millisecond response times. 

Main capabilities include fast HTTP server and client operations optimized for zero-memory allocation in hot paths, byte slice buffer reuse, and support for connection hijacking and streaming options via custom request handlers (`RequestHandler` and `RequestCtx`). It is intended for advanced Go developers and high-load production environments requiring extreme throughput and minimal garbage collection overhead, whereas standard library alternatives are recommended for general use cases. Notable technologies and related concepts include Go, TCP, Unix sockets, and integrations with third-party routers and frameworks such as Fiber, Atreugo, and fastws.

name: eza
description: A modern alternative to ls
summary:
eza is a modern, small, fast command-line file-listing utility designed as a featureful alternative to the traditional Unix/Linux `ls` command. Built as a single binary, it provides enhanced defaults, color-coded file types and metadata, symlink awareness, extended attribute handling, and Git repository integration. 

Main capabilities include grid and tree views, recursive directory listing, hyperlink support, mount point details, SELinux context output, human-readable relative dates, recursive directory sizing, and customizable themes via `theme.yml` or standard environment variables. It also features robust filtering options such as glob-based ignoring, git-ignore integration, and various sorting parameters, alongside detailed long-view metrics like binary file sizes, inodes, hard links, and custom timestamp styles. 

Intended for developers and terminal users on Linux, macOS, and Windows, eza extends functionality beyond the legacy `exa` project with fixes for layout bugs, brightness controls, and security updates. The project uses Nix for builds and packaging.

name: intro.js
description: Lightweight, user-friendly onboarding tour library
summary: Intro.js is a user onboarding and product walkthrough library designed to help developers create step-by-step guides, introductions, and hints for web applications. The library enables step presentations to be applied to HTML elements using attributes such as `data-intro`, `data-step`, and `data-hint`, and is initiated via JavaScript using the `introJs().start()` function. It provides Right-to-Left (RTL) language support through dedicated stylesheets and includes various framework wrappers. Built using Node.js and npm, Intro.js can be integrated via local cloning, yarn, npm, or CDN services like jsDelivr and ccdnjs.

name: react-redux
description: Official React bindings for Redux
summary: React Redux provides official React bindings for Redux, offering performant and flexible state management capabilities for React applications. It is designed for React developers building applications with Redux, requiring React 18 or later for version 9.0. The project integrates with module bundlers and package managers such as npm, Yarn, Webpack, and Browserify, and supports setup via Vite and Next.js templates utilizing Redux Toolkit.

name: slim
description: Slim(toolkit): Don't change anything in your container image and minify it by up to 30x (and for compiled languages even more) making it secure too! (free and open source)
summary:
Slim (SlimToolkit), formerly known as DockerSlim, is a free, open-source CNCF Sandbox project designed to optimize, secure, inspect, and debug container images. It enables developers to reduce container image sizes by up to 30x while removing unnecessary components to shrink the attack surface, all without requiring changes to original Dockerfiles, base images, package managers, or workflows. 

The toolkit offers comprehensive capabilities through commands such as `xray`, `lint`, `build`, `debug`, `run`, `merge`, `images`, `registry`, `vulnerability`, and `appbom`. It performs both static and dynamic analysis to understand application behavior, automatically generating security profiles including Seccomp and AppArmor. It also supports HTTP probing, crawling, and API specification testing to detect dynamically loaded components.

Slim is intended for software developers and DevOps engineers working with containerized applications. It supports diverse application stacks including Node.js, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, Elixir, PHP, and Haskell running on base distributions like Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, Alpine, and Distroless. Notable technologies and ecosystems associated with the project include Docker, Kubernetes, OCI registries, and integrations with CI/CD platforms such as Jenkins and GitHub Actions.

name: jdk
description: JDK main-line development https://openjdk.org/projects/jdk
summary: The JDK repository provides the source code and development materials for the Java Development Kit, managed by the OpenJDK Community. Its primary purpose is to develop, build, and maintain the JDK. The repository directs users to comprehensive building instructions available in HTML and Markdown formats within the documentation. Intended users include developers and contributors participating in the OpenJDK ecosystem. Project resources, community information, and issue tracking are hosted externally via openjdk.org and bugs.openjdk.org.

name: rxdb
description: The local-first database that runs on every JS runtime and replicates with your existing backend - no vendor, no lock-in - https://rxdb.info/
summary:
RxDB is a fast, local-first, reactive NoSQL database designed for JavaScript applications. It enables developers to query current database states as well as subscribe to state changes on queries, documents, or individual fields, making it well-suited for realtime UI-based applications and multiplayer environments. 

The project features a flexible storage layer supporting pluggable engines such as LocalStorage, IndexedDB, OPFS, LokiJS, Dexie.js, SQLite, FoundationDB, DenoKV, and in-memory storage. It also provides a built-in replication sync engine with plugins for GraphQL, CouchDB, Websocket, WebRTC, Supabase, Firestore, NATS, and Google Drive. 

Intended for frontend and full-stack JavaScript developers, RxDB runs across diverse environments including web browsers, Node.js, React Native, Capacitor, NativeScript, Flutter, and Electron. Notable technologies and capabilities include schema validation, key compression, migration, encryption, conflict handling, and CRDT support.

name: backtrader
description: Python Backtesting library for trading strategies
summary:
Backtrader is a feature-rich live trading and backtesting platform written in Python. It is designed for quantitative traders and developers looking to test, analyze, and execute trading strategies. 

Main capabilities include support for multiple data feeds, multiple strategies, and multiple timeframes simultaneously, with integrated resampling and replaying. It offers built-in indicators, support for *TA-Lib* indicators, and straightforward custom indicator development. The platform features integrated broker simulation supporting various order types (such as *Market*, *Limit*, *Stop*, *OCO*, and bracket orders), slippage, volume filling strategies, commission schemes, analyzers (like Sharpe Ratio and SQN), automated staking via sizers, schedulers, trading calendars, and plotting via *matplotlib*. Data can be sourced from CSV files, online sources (including Yahoo Finance), *pandas*, and *blaze*. Live trading and data feeds are supported for *Interactive Brokers* (via *IbPy*), *Visual Chart*, and *Oanda*. 

The platform supports Python >= 3.2, *pypy*, and *pypy3*, and is self-contained with minimal external dependencies.

name: tools
description: Unified developer tools for JavaScript, TypeScript, and the web
summary: Rome is a unified toolchain written in Rust that acts as a formatter, linter, bundler, and more for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, HTML, Markdown, and CSS. Designed to replace tools such as Babel, ESLint, webpack, Prettier, and Jest, Rome aims to provide a cohesive experience for processing code, displaying errors, parallelizing work, caching, and configuration with minimal setup. The project features strong conventions, first-class IDE support via a sophisticated parser providing full-fidelity source text representation, and top-notch error recovery. Rome is MIT licensed and serves as the predecessor to Biome.

name: AeroSpace
description: AeroSpace is an i3-like tiling window manager for macOS
summary:
AeroSpace is an i3-inspired, tiling window manager for macOS designed for advanced users and developers. Its core purpose is to provide a fast, keyboard-centric workflow with proper multi-monitor support and rapid workspace switching without animations. 

Main capabilities include a tree paradigm for window management, custom emulation of virtual workspaces to bypass native macOS Spaces limitations, a CLI-first interface with manpages and shell completion, and plain-text configuration (TOML). It utilizes macOS public accessibility APIs and avoids requiring users to disable System Integrity Protection (SIP).

Targeted at developers and power users seeking a practical, text-configured window management solution, AeroSpace minimizes GUI use and avoids complex visual styling features like animations or window borders. Notable technologies used include Swift, Xcode, Homebrew for installation, and the macOS Accessibility API (`AXUIElement`).

name: wechaty
description: Conversational RPA SDK for Chatbot Makers. Join our Discord: https://discord.gg/7q8NBZbQzt
summary:
Wechaty is a conversational Robotic Process Automation (RPA) SDK designed for chatbot makers. It functions as a universal interface to build and manage chatbots across multiple messaging platforms, including WeChat and WhatsApp. 

The project's primary capability is enabling developers to write bot logic once using a simple API and run it across various platforms and protocols—such as Web, iPad, Windows, and mock providers—via pluggable puppet providers. Wechaty supports cross-platform execution on Linux, Windows, macOS, and Docker. 

Intended users are chatbot developers, operations teams, and engineers seeking to automate messaging workflows, manage group chats, handle contacts, and process media files. Wechaty is natively available in TypeScript and JavaScript, with multi-language wrappers and community ports provided for Python, Go, Java/Kotlin, Scala, PHP, and .NET (C#). Notable technologies and tools integrated into the ecosystem include Node.js, Docker, ES Modules, and various puppet implementations like PuppetPuppeteer, PuppetWorkPro, and PuppetPadLocal.

name: api-guidelines
description: Microsoft REST API Guidelines
summary: The Microsoft REST API Guidelines repository provides a collection of documents and related materials supporting the Microsoft REST API Guidelines initiative. Its purpose is to foster dialogue and learning within the API community and encourage organizations to develop their own standards. The repository includes targeted companion documents and pattern catalogs for specific internal development groups, namely Azure service teams (referencing the Azure REST API Guidelines and Considerations for Service Design) and Microsoft Graph service teams (referencing the Microsoft Graph REST API Guidelines). The intended users are developers, API designers, and service teams—particularly within Azure and Microsoft Graph—building or modifying RESTful APIs.

name: bend
description: Bend 2: a fast language that blocks AI mistakes via proof. Install: curl -fsSL https://bend-lang.com/install.sh | sh
summary:
Bend is a high-performance programming language designed to communicate precise intents to AI systems, featuring built-in mathematical proof checking and parallel execution. It targets developers and AI agents operating in post-AGI environments where code correctness is critical. 

The project's main capabilities include mechanical verification of mathematical proofs via `LAWS.bend` files to block AI-generated mistakes, automatic multi-core CPU and GPU parallelization via divide-and-conquer structures, and compilation speeds comparable to C and CUDA. Its syntax blends Python-like constructs with affine dependent types. 

Notable technologies and formats used include Lean (for kernel formalization), C, CUDA, Metal, JavaScript, and WebAssembly/Node.js ecosystems. Bend runs best on back-end Linux and macOS environments.

name: maui
description: .NET MAUI is the .NET Multi-platform App UI, a framework for building native device applications spanning mobile, tablet, and desktop.
summary:
.NET Multi-platform App UI (.NET MAUI) is a cross-platform framework designed for developers to create native mobile and desktop applications from a single shared codebase. Evolving from Xamarin.Forms, the framework enables the development of apps targeting Android, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and Windows. 

Project capabilities include building high-performance applications using a unified SDK, base class libraries, and a toolchain. Developers can utilize Visual Studio productivity tools and emulators to accelerate the development process. The framework supports integration with modern ecosystems and toolkits, including the Syncfusion Toolkit for .NET MAUI, the .NET MAUI Community Toolkit, and the MVVM Toolkit.

Intended users are software developers and engineers building applications that target a wide range of modern mobile and desktop devices. Notable technologies used within the ecosystem include C#, XAML, .NET, and Visual Studio.

name: matplotlib
description: matplotlib: plotting with Python
summary:
Matplotlib is a comprehensive Python library designed for creating static, animated, and interactive visualizations. It produces publication-quality figures across various hardcopy formats and interactive environments. 

The library's main capabilities allow it to be utilized in Python scripts, Python and IPython shells, web application servers, and multiple graphical user interface toolkits. It serves developers, data scientists, and researchers seeking robust plotting tools in Python ecosystems.

name: qwerty-learner
description: 为键盘工作者设计的单词记忆与英语肌肉记忆锻炼软件 / Words learning and English muscle memory training software designed for keyboard workers
summary:
Qwerty Learner is a word-memorization and typing-muscle-memory training software designed for keyboard workers and programmers whose primary working language is English. The application combines English vocabulary retention with keyboard typing practice to help users strengthen English input muscle memory and prevent input errors by requiring correct spelling before progressing. 

Main capabilities include built-in dictionaries for standardized tests (such as CET-4, CET-6, GMAT, GRE, IELTS, SAT, TOEFL, and graduate entrance exams), programmer-focused word lists, programming language API drills (including JavaScript, Node.js, Java, C#, and Linux commands), phonetic transcriptions, audio pronunciations, chapter dictation modes, and real-time speed and accuracy metrics. 

Intended users are keyboard workers, developers, and individuals preparing for English examinations who want to improve typing fluency and vocabulary simultaneously. Built using React and Node.js, the project is available as a web application and a VSCode extension.

name: github1s
description: One second to read GitHub code with VS Code.
summary:
GitHub1s is a browser-based code explorer built on VS Code that enables users to browse files, search code, switch branches, inspect commits, and review pull or merge request diffs without cloning a repository. By inserting `1s` after `github` in a repository URL (or using gitlab1s.com for GitLab repositories and npmjs1s.com for npm packages), users can immediately explore public repositories without signing in, or access private repositories by supplying authentication tokens. 

The platform features built-in GitHub1s AI chat integration, allowing users to connect their preferred model endpoints to receive repository overviews, explain files or selections, and look up implementation details. The remote repositories are read-only, and search capabilities depend on upstream services. GitHub1s is licensed under the MIT license.

name: eng-practices
description: Google's Engineering Practices documentation
summary: The Google Engineering Practices Documentation repository provides public access to Google's generalized engineering best practices developed across various languages and projects. The primary content consists of Google's Code Review Guidelines, which are divided into The Code Reviewer's Guide and The Change Author's Guide. These documents aim to benefit open-source projects and external organizations by sharing collective software development experience. The intended users are software developers, code reviewers, and change authors seeking guidance on effective code review and engineering workflows. Distinctive internal terminology used throughout the documentation includes "CL" (changelist, referring to a change, patch, or pull request) and "LGTM" ("Looks Good to Me," used by reviewers to approve a changelist).

name: sops
description: Simple and flexible tool for managing secrets
summary: SOPS (Secrets OPerationS) is an editor of encrypted files that supports YAML, JSON, ENV, INI, and BINARY formats. It encrypts data using AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, HuaweiCloud KMS, age, and PGP. Originally launched at Mozilla in 2015, SOPS is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox project.

name: octotree
description: GitHub on steroids
summary: Octotree is a proprietary browser extension designed to enhance GitHub code review and exploration by providing a file tree sidebar. Available for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Brave, and Opera, the extension improves navigation for developers working within GitHub repositories. This repository contains the old source code of a very limited version of Octotree, with complete copyright owned by the Octotree team.

name: jaeger
description: CNCF Jaeger, a Distributed Tracing Platform
summary:
Jaeger is an open-source distributed tracing system originally created by Uber Technologies and hosted as a graduated project by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). Its purpose is to monitor and troubleshoot microservices-based distributed systems through end-to-end distributed tracing. 

Main capabilities include collecting traces, processing query requests, managing storage backends, and providing a web-based user interface. It integrates with the OpenTelemetry SDK, accepting traces via OTLP over gRPC and HTTP. 

Intended users include developers, operators, and organizations running cloud-native applications who need to trace requests across complex service architectures for development debugging or production monitoring. 

Notable technologies and components used within the ecosystem include Docker, Go, OpenTelemetry Collector, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Apache Cassandra, and ClickHouse.

name: lens
description: Lens - The way the world runs Kubernetes
summary:
Lens is a Kubernetes IDE developed by Mirantis designed for developers and DevOps engineers. It provides an intuitive context-aware user interface for managing and troubleshooting Kubernetes workloads, boosting team productivity, and supporting cloud-native development. Lens serves over 1 million users globally, ranging from startups to enterprises. 

The repository contains the legacy source code for the retired open source version of Lens Desktop on its 'master' branch, released under the MIT license. While Lens Desktop remains actively developed and supported by Mirantis, contributions to the core product are now made through extensions using the Lens extension API.

name: RedisDesktopManager
summary: RESP.app (formerly RedisDesktopManager) is a GUI for Redis designed to offer the Redis community an improved developer experience and increased productivity when developing with Redis. The repository provides a graphical user interface application for managing and interacting with Redis databases.

name: source-code-hunter
description: 😱 从源码层面，剖析挖掘互联网行业主流技术的底层实现原理，为广大开发者 “提升技术深度” 提供便利。目前开放 Spring 全家桶，Mybatis、Netty、Dubbo 框架，及 Redis、Tomcat 中间件等
summary:
This repository provides source code analysis and explanations of mainstream frameworks and middleware used in internet applications to help developers enhance their technical depth and breadth. It targets software developers seeking to understand underlying implementation principles. 

The project covers detailed notes, personal understandings, and design patterns extracted from reading the source code of prominent technologies, including Spring (IoC, AOP, SpringMVC, Spring Transaction, SpringBoot, Spring Cloud, SpringSecurity), MyBatis, Netty, Dubbo, Tomcat, Redis, Nacos, Sentinel, RocketMQ, and JDK 1.8 foundational classes, collections, and concurrent programming utilities (such as JUC and AbstractQueuedSynchronizer).

name: skyvern
description: Automate browser based workflows with AI
summary:
Skyvern is an open-source automation platform designed to execute browser-based workflows using Large Language Models (LLMs) and computer vision. Rather than relying on brittle, code-defined XPath selectors or traditional DOM parsing, Skyvern utilizes Vision LLMs and a swarm of autonomous agents to visually comprehend websites, plan navigation, and reliably complete multi-step actions despite layout changes.

Main capabilities include AI-powered page interactions, structured data extraction, file downloading, form filling, automated authentication with multi-factor authentication (TOTP) support, and a no-code workflow builder. It provides Python and TypeScript SDKs extending Playwright with natural language page commands (`page.act`, `page.extract`, `page.validate`, `page.prompt`), as well as browser tunneling and remote debugging integration (`CDP-connect`).

Intended users include technical and non-technical professionals seeking to automate repetitive browser tasks such as invoice downloading, job applications, form submissions, and insurance quote retrievals. Notable technologies integrated or supported include Playwright, Python, TypeScript, Docker, PostgreSQL, SQLite, liteLLM, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and major model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Gemini, Azure, and Ollama.

name: distroless
description: 🥑  Language focused docker images, minus the operating system.
summary:
The Distroless project provides minimal container images that contain exclusively an application and its runtime dependencies, omitting package managers, shells, and standard Linux distribution programs. Designed for secure production environments by improving vulnerability scanner signal-to-noise ratios and reducing image sizes (with static images starting around 2 MiB), the project targets developers and organizations containerizing applications. 

The images are based on Debian 13 (trixie) and are available in various language runtimes and configurations, including Java, Node.js, Python, and static variants. Notable technologies used to build and verify the project include Bazel, Docker, and Cosign for keyless image signing. Distroless images can be integrated via multi-stage Docker builds or Bazel container rules (`rules_distroless` and `rules_oci`). The project also provides specialized tags such as `nonroot` for running securely without root privileges and `debug` variants containing a BusyBox shell for troubleshooting.

name: stackedit
description: In-browser Markdown editor
summary:
StackEdit is a full-featured, open-source Markdown editor built on PageDown, the Markdown library used by Stack Overflow and other Stack Exchange sites. 

The project provides capabilities for creating and editing Markdown documents, with an ecosystem that includes a Chrome app, a Chrome extension, and `stackedit.js` for embedding StackEdit into any website. It is designed for users seeking a versatile Markdown editing environment. 

Notable technologies used in the project include PageDown, npm, Helm, and Kubernetes.

name: grpc-go
description: The Go language implementation of gRPC. HTTP/2 based RPC
summary: gRPC-Go is the official Go implementation of gRPC, a high-performance, open-source, general remote procedure call (RPC) framework designed with mobile and HTTP/2 support in mind. It allows developers to build connected systems and services in Go by importing `google.golang.org/grpc`, leveraging Go module support for dependency management. The project is intended for Go developers building distributed applications, microservices, and network communication layers. Notable technologies and protocols utilized include Go and HTTP/2.

name: go-micro
description: A framework for building agents and services
summary:
Go Micro is a Go framework for building distributed services and AI agents. Its core foundation provides pluggable interfaces for service communication—including RPC, discovery, pub/sub, registry, client/server, broker, transport, codec, and store. Expanding on this architecture, Go Micro enables developers to construct independent services, integrate AI models via a common interface, deploy autonomous agents that interpret requests and utilize tools, and coordinate repeatable sequences of work through workflows. 

The framework is intended for Go developers building service-backed applications, AI agents, and microservice architectures. Notable technologies and components mentioned include Go (version 1.25 or newer), OpenAI as an AI provider, and an optional command-line interface (`micro`) supporting features such as chat, service generation, hot reload, and deployment.

name: winboat
description: Run Windows apps on 🐧 Linux with ✨ seamless integration
summary:
WinBoat is an Electron-based desktop application designed for Linux users to run Windows applications and full Windows desktops with seamless integration. The software uses a containerized approach, running Windows as a virtual machine inside a Docker or Podman container via tools like dockur/windows. It communicates with the guest environment using the WinBoat Guest Server and leverages FreeRDP with Windows's RemoteApp protocol to composite applications as native OS-level windows. 

Main capabilities include automated installation workflows, local filesystem integration (mounting the Linux home directory inside Windows), smartcard passthrough, and resource monitoring. The project is intended for Linux users seeking to run Windows applications natively within their desktop environment. Notable technologies used in its development and execution include Electron, Docker, Podman, FreeRDP, Go, and Bun.

name: n8n-mcp
description: A MCP for Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Windsurf / Cursor to build n8n workflows for you
summary:
n8n-MCP is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects AI assistants like Claude, VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf to the n8n workflow automation platform. It provides deep, structured access to thousands of n8n workflow nodes, node properties, operations, official documentation, and pre-built workflow templates. 

Designed for developers, engineers, and automation builders, the project features core discovery and validation tools alongside advanced n8n management tools for workflows, executions, credentials, data tables, and AI agents. It supports deployment via npx, Docker, and Railway, and integrates with AI-powered development environments. Notable technologies and protocols include the Model Context Protocol, LangChain nodes, and n8n's public and instance-level APIs.

name: Cap
description: Open source Loom alternative. Beautiful, shareable screen recordings.
summary:
Cap is an open-source screen recording and collaboration platform designed as an alternative to Loom. It provides fast screen, camera, and microphone capture with two primary workflows: Instant Mode for immediate link sharing during recording, and Studio Mode for local editing with background, zoom, trimming, and caption tools. Intended for teams, developers, and individuals needing async communication, Cap supports product demos, bug reports, and tutorials. 

Key capabilities include team workspaces, viewer analytics, automated Cap AI transcriptions and summaries, comments, and the ability to import existing Loom videos. Cap emphasizes data ownership and privacy by allowing users to store media locally, connect custom S3-compatible buckets (such as AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, or MinIO), use custom domains, or self-host the full platform using Docker Compose, Railway, or Coolify. 

The repository is structured as a Turborepo monorepo utilizing macOS and Windows desktop apps built with Tauri v2, Rust, SolidStart, and Next.js, alongside a MySQL database managed with Drizzle ORM, Tailwind CSS, and Effect for HTTP APIs.
